text:
As-salamu alaykum.

Ah, Faris Sahab! How are you? Are you well?

Alhamdulillah, your prayers. How are you? How is everything on your side?

Allah's grace.

Yes, yes, we are well, Alhamdulillah, we are fine. The month of Rajab, many, many congratulations. Remember us in your prayers.

Yes, many congratulations. Remember this faqir well in your prayers.

Surely, surely, surely. Insha'Allah, Insha'Allah. And how are your parents?

They are all well, Alhamdulillah.

Yes, yes, Alhamdulillah. How is the weather there?

It's become very good, very good, here these days. In your... what is it called... hospital... Alhamdulillah, it's become very good, yes, yes.

It feels very good. After many days, I got the chance to speak with you again.

Yes, yes, yes, yes, yes, yes, yes, Alhamdulillah, Alhamdulillah. I am also happy.

I, Ansar Bhai, was thinking... I was actually just thinking yesterday that I... pretty much every day I read something or the other from my religious knowledge. So I feel that when I read, it's like climbing a staircase, like a person climbs stairs. But when I talk to you, I get the feeling of being in a lift [elevator], that I... the lift... I learn so much from one discussion. Otherwise, I would have to learn very slowly...

This is your love, Bhai. Yes, yes, yes, yes, yes. This is your love, Bhai. God's generosity is with you, Alhamdulillah.

It's Allah's grace, Bhai. Allah has been so kind to give me such a good means (*wasila*). Ansar Bhai, I will present my questions to you now.

Yes.

Yes, yes, yes, yes. These questions are a bit... they are, I mean, not on a sequential topic, because I have been collecting them for a long time. They are from various... I mean, random, like random questions.

Ah, ah, ah, yes, yes.

So, right now, I am listening to some lessons of Hazrat Ibrahim that took place recently in Karachi, you know, these... uh... *Shu'al al-Anwar* and uh... *Asas*.

Ah, ah, ah, yes. So...

Yes, yes. Those lessons were... they took place in front of us, in our presence.

Yes, yes, yes, absolutely.

Yes, yes. So, in that connection, some questions have arisen, so I wanted to ask you that... ah, ah... Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim. Yes, yes, yes. They said that this... in the story of Habil and Qabil, the mention of the crows, that where they... a... two crows came, they fought, killed each other, then dug a pit... ah, ah, ah, ah, ah... so you... ah, ah... can you tell me something about that, who were those crows? What was their... Hazrat alluded to it, but he didn't explain that who were those crows, what was their reality behind it?

Okay. These... they were... they were individuals (*ashkhas*) of vile nature (*khabith*). The crow is among the vile animals, isn't it? Yes, yes. Yes. Vile animals, it eats filth (*khabasat*). Yes. Yes, so these were vile people. Yes, yes. But, now through them... now understand, it's as if... a... they had to be taught a lesson. Yes. So that... this... one killed the other, and in this way, it dug a hole and buried it. Yes. Now when Qabil killed Habil, he couldn't understand what he should do. Hmm, hmm. What path should I take for this? So, nature, through them, taught him a lesson.

Okay. But those two...

Yes, yes, yes.

...were vile.

Okay, because in the story of Habil and Qabil, Habil is good, Qabil is bad. So I was thinking, was there something similar with the crows, that one is good, one is bad?

No, no, that's not the case. In the case of the crows, both were bad. Okay. In the case of the crows, both were vile. Yes, yes.

Okay, Ansar Bhai...

But now, through that, God had a purpose to teach him. Yes, yes. And that was from the vile group. But what happens is that nature, even from such people, takes some work so that the believers... or other people... can learn a lesson from it. So Qabil, who was actually, he was from within the *hudud* (ranks) of Mawlana Hunaid's *da'wat* (mission). Yes, yes. He had not come from outside.

Habil?

From the *hudud* of the *da'wat*.

Ah, Qabil.

Okay. Qabil, yes. Yes, Qabil. He was... Mawlana Hunaid's *da'wat* had *hudud*. So he was a brother.

Okay. So their real brother...

No, he was not a biological brother. Yes, yes, yes, yes. He was not a biological brother. He... from the twelve *hudud* of Mawlana Hunaid... the twelve *hudud* that are before the Imam, he was one of them. The ones that Hazrat... in Azad-i Imamiyyah, he was also one of them, this Qabil. Hmm, hmm, hmm. Yes. So when... Adam alayhis salam, he... appointed a *na'ib* (deputy), appointed his *wasi* (successor), to his one... *hadd* (rank-holder), whose name is Habil. Another *hadd* who was... him... he was overcome with envy (*hasad*). Hmm. Yes. Now if you relate this to our Prophet's time, I will bring you there. Yes, yes. The very same thing. Yes. The very same thing. Ali was the Prophet's cousin, he wasn't a real brother. Yes. Yes. Now, by Allah's command, the Prophet... Rasulullah appointed Ali as his caliph. Yes. So... it became difficult for Umar to bear. That is Qabil. Okay. In our time, in the Prophet's time, he is Qabil. It was difficult for him to bear. That why was Ali made [the caliph]? Yes. Yes, we were more capable, or Abu Bakr... he didn't object, he was more capable. Yes, yes. Why was Ali made the... Prophet... his caliph? Yes, yes, yes. He had envy towards them. So he fulfilled that envy and... as if... he removed Ali and made Abu Bakr the caliph. Yes. Meaning, in a way, he killed Ali. Yes. The *batini* (esoteric) killing. Yes. Do you understand this? Yes. The *batini* killing. Yes. So here too, he... this... as for Qabil, now from this example, you will get the full picture. Yes, yes. You will understand the whole thing, the whole... yes... that this Habil, who is... he was also from the *hudud* of Adam alayhis salam's *da'wat*, he was from the high *hudud*. And Qabil was also there. Yes. But Qabil didn't have the merit (*liyaqat*). Hmm, hmm, hmm. Habil had the merit, the capability. Therefore, Adam alayhis salam, by the command of Mawlana Hunaid, appointed Habil as his caliph. Right. Yes. So the other *hadd* who was, Qabil, he was overcome with envy. And he... committed an offense. And in a way, he did a *batini qatl* (esoteric killing). Yes. Yes, removing him from his position. Right. And he did not succeed in it. Yes. Yes. So now, this analogy that I have made, you have understood the whole picture from it. Yes, yes, absolutely. Very good. Subhan Allah. Yes, yes, yes. Alhamdulillah. Ansar Bhai, if a person has the disease of envy (*hasad*), what is the cure for it?

Yes. The cure for it is... what else is the cure for it? It's to control one's *nafs* (self). Yes, there is... there is. Yes, yes, yes, yes. There is a *du'a* of Mawlana Ali, *Du'a daf' al-hamm wal-ghamm* (The Supplication for Repelling Anxiety and Grief). Yes. In it, you... this... the part of the *du'a* is... in it, these words come: *a'udhu bika Allahumma min al-kufri wal-faqri wal-hirsi wal-hasadi*. (I seek refuge in You, O Allah, from disbelief, poverty, greed, and envy.) Okay. There are these phrases that come. Yes. *min al-faqri wal-faqati... wash-shakki wan-nifaqi was-su'i... was-su'il akhlaq*. (from poverty and indigence... and doubt and hypocrisy and evil... and evil character.) Yes. I mean, so many things come in it that corrupt our character. Yes. Yes. Yes, yes. So that... the one for repelling anxiety and grief. Yes. In that, this *du'a* comes. So you keep reciting that *du'a*. Insha'Allah. And besides this, in the *Ratib*, the final *du'a* that we recite, yes, in that, at the very end, these words come: *wa khallifna bi-akhlaqin Natiqatin Malakiyyah*. (And replace for us with the ethics of the Angelic Natiq.) Yes, yes, yes. O Allah, your ethics... make them like the ethics of the Natiq-i Malakiyyah, that is, make them good ethics. Yes. And good ethics, noble ethics, what are they? That in which there is sincerity, truthfulness, truth, good dealings, obedience, submission. Yes. And there is no envy, no greed, no avarice. Yes. And... one does not go against the commands of the elders. One does not act against the commands of the *shari'ah*. All these things are included. So, *wa khallifna...* we should ask for this in the *Ratib* every day. *Wa khallifna bi-akhlaqin Natiqatin Malakiyyah*. (And replace for us with the ethics of the Angelic Natiq.) Right. Yes. So this... so you... day and night, you... recite the *du'a* of the *Ratib*. Insha'Allah. So, Insha'Allah, by Allah's blessing, this... this flaw will be removed. Insha'Allah. And recite this *du'a daf' al-hamm wal-ghamm*, in which there is *a'udhu bika Allahumma min al-kufri wal-faqri wal-hirsi wal-hasadi wal-kibri wa 'adhab al-qabr*. (I seek refuge in You, O Allah, from disbelief, poverty, greed, envy, pride, and the torment of the grave.) This is in our *Bada Sahifa*, isn't it, this *du'a*? It's in the *Bada Sahifa*. It's at the very end, this *du'a*. At the end. I will look, Insha'Allah. Yes, at the end. It's after the *nafl* prayers. Thank you. Or rather, it's after the *munajat* (intimate prayers). An edition was made to it, it wasn't there before. Yes, yes. But later an edition was made, so it was placed at the end after the *munajat*. Okay, Insha'Allah, I will read it. Yes. The *du'a...* its name is... it has another name, it's also called *Du'a Nasiri*. Okay. And in the *Sahifa*, its name is written as *Du'a daf' al-hamm wal-ghamm*. Hmm, hmm, hmm. It's a very magnificent *du'a* of Mawlana Ali. Insha'Allah. A very magnificent *du'a*. You should recite that daily. For sure. Thank you, Ansar Bhai. So, Insha'Allah, by its blessing... Okay, Ansar Bhai, the aquatic animals, the predatory ones like sharks and others of that kind, which rank do they belong to? Ah, ah, ah. The fourth rank. So in the water... The fourth rank. The fourth rank is of the aquatic kingdom, isn't it? Okay. So the term *wahshi janwar* (wild/predatory animal) is used, then *wahshi janwar* of the third rank, it means the *charind* (land animals), *parind* (birds), *darind* (beasts), all three which are predatory, it's about all of them. Yes, the third rank is that. Because birds have a separate rank, but among those birds, there are good birds and there are predatory birds. So those predatory birds... Yes, all of them. In the ranks, there are both good and bad. Yes. But in the fourth... For example, the hawk is a predatory bird. As there is the rank of animals, yes, yes, in that, there are *halal* (permissible) animals and *haram* (forbidden) animals. Yes. There are cows and goats, and there are lions and tigers. Yes, yes, yes, all of them are included in it. Yes. But among them, they are segregated. That these have been made *halal* animals, so their spiritual progress will happen, but they have to perform some services. Yes. They have to endure hardships. Yes. That they have to be of use to humans. Right. That... the goat, the cow, etc., they will give milk. And they will become food for humans. Yes, yes. And when the time comes, when they have to come under the knife, they will be sacrificed. Right. They have to perform all these services. So nature is making them do this. Now whatever is happening, it's a state of compulsion. They have to do it. Right. They have no escape from it. Because... This is a state of compulsion. Because they did not do it in the realm of free will. Yes, that's right. That's right. They were absent from the realm of free will. Okay. So now they have to go through these things in a state of compulsion, and then they will get on the path of spiritual progress. Spiritual progress has to be made by everyone. Yes. Every single thing in the world has to do it, from the smallest thing... Yes. ...it too has to make spiritual progress. Yes. Right. Thank you. Okay, Ansar Bhai, the *Ahl al-Saqar*, the people who are from there, about them I... there is something I am not understanding. That, granted that they... the duration that has been stated for them, the people of *Ahl al-Saqar*, is for one *kawr-i a'zam*. And then the painful punishments of *Saqar*, those are described in great detail in *al-Anwar al-Latifah*. So, I... this much I can understand, that yes, they opposed great Imams and they caused trouble for great *Awliya Allah*. But Ansar Bhai, one *kawr* means 16,000 crore years. So, for such a long... such a long period of punishment... although they did such a thing, but the thing they did, they did it in a life of 50 or 60 years, they caused trouble. But nature has set the punishment for this for one *kawr-i a'zam*. So this... such a long... its length... I don't understand its length, that... I mean, this is a bit too much... Do you understand my question? Yes, I understood, I understood. A good, good question you have. Now, this is... since the beginning of the *dawr al-sitr* (cycle of concealment), yes, since the *dawr al-sitr* has begun, yes, since then, this Iblis, who became Iblis, yes, and the vileness (*khabasat*) that came into him, that vileness has been accumulating, it kept moving forward. Yes. And in every era, this vileness continued, it kept moving forward. Yes, yes. And it grew and grew, and in the time of Nuh, this vileness came, and in the time of Ibrahim it came, in the time of Musa it came as Pharaoh, in the time of Ibrahim it came as Nimrod, and in the time of Isa it came, and in the time of the Prophet, it came in the forms of Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman, Muawiya, Yazid. Yes. Now, after the Prophet, there is no other prophet. Yes. Yes. So now, the chains will continue, now the... the *da'wat* will move forward, it will move forward through the Imams, and when the Imams are concealed, it will move forward through the *du'at*. Yes. So, this vileness that has happened, and these events that have happened, this vileness, from the beginning of the *dawr al-sitr*, has kept increasing. It became greater and greater. Yes, yes. So now, these people... now they have to... the punishment that has to be given, is that these... Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman, Muawiya, Yazid, all such people, or later on in the *da'wat* there came people like Ibn Qutub, so these people became a complete collection of vileness. Yes. Just as with Ali, there was a collection of all the best qualities. Yes. They became the *rabb al-dawr* (lord of the cycle). So, all the luminous qualities were collected in Ali. Yes. All the Imams and... Prophets and Messengers, etc., who have been, their entire collection is gathered with Ali. Yes. All the *awsia* (successors), their collection is gathered with Ali. Yes. And all the Prophets and Messengers, their collection is gathered with the Prophet. So the good qualities are gathered with the good people. And in this way, the bad qualities are gathered with these bad people. Right. So now... yes, so now these people who have good qualities gathered in them, they will... in the future, now... now what will happen? After the Prophet, the chain of prophethood is finished. Yes. The chain of succession (*wasi-ship*) is finished. Now whatever the situation is, we have to see the era of the Qa'im. We have to see the matter of the Qa'im's appearance. So when the Qa'im appears, Ali will be in his form of *haykal*, the Prophet will be at the station of the mind, all these matters, all the good matters will be there. So now, the people who have to receive punishment, they too have done very bad things, and the chain has been going on until now. Yes. And just as Iblis had asked for respite from Allah, that grant me respite. So Allah Ta'ala had said, "Alright, *waqtin... ila yawm al-waqt al-ma'lum* (until the day of the appointed time)." "I will give you respite until the appointed time." Then he said that I will mislead them, I will mislead my entire community. This comes at the very end of Surah Rum. That he said that... "I will mislead everyone." Yes. Except for the sincere servants. "*illa 'ibadaka minhum al-mukhlisin*" (except for Your chosen servants among them). Yes. "Among them, your sincere servants, I will mislead everyone except them." So he tried his best. And nature gave him the full opportunity. Go on, do what you have to do. In the end, when you come to me, then your punishment... you are deserving of punishment anyway. Right. So when you... your entire... your respite is over, at that time I will seize you. Hmm. Yes. I won't seize you immediately. It's not necessary that punishment comes immediately. Right. Yes. Sometimes it is delayed for a hundred years, two hundred years. A thousand years are delayed. Right. And when the time of reckoning comes, then they are caught. Yes. It is not necessary that enemies are immediately... punished. Like Muawiya. So he... Muawiya also committed so much oppression. But he lived, didn't he? He was alive even after Ali, right? The one who had Ali killed was Muawiya, but he was alive even after Ali. So, the one *kawr* of punishment that is being given to them, is it for the entire past... the entire *dawr al-sitr*? Yes, for the entire... entire... all of it... the entire collection of all this vileness is gathered with these people. Okay. So after the Prophet... all... yes... So it is not for the duration of one person's life, it is for the duration of the collective. The collective... the entire collective has gathered in one place. It has gathered in Abu Bakr, it has gathered in Umar, it has gathered in Uthman, it has gathered in Muawiya, it has gathered in Yazid. So, Ansar Bhai, for example, just as... just as Muawiya came, now, as you said, that Mawlana... Muawiya is from the opposites (*azdad*) of... Hazrat Ali... of Hasan... of Imam Hasan. Abu Bakr and Umar and these people are from the opposites of Mawlana Ali. So, just as Umar came, the body that came, Umar himself was what he was, but his body... just as Ali's *nasut sharif* (noble physical form) was a reflection of all the noble people and the luminous qualities... it was a reflection of them, of different... of the preceding Sadiq Imams. So Umar's body was also a full... I mean, vile... which had been coming from the past eras, it was a reflection of that. Absolutely, absolutely. That's how you should understand it. Subhan Allah! That's how it is. Yes. It was only then that he was capable of confronting Mawlana Ali, otherwise who had the audacity to... Yes, absolutely, absolutely, absolutely. Okay, okay. That's right, that's right. Subhan Allah! What a state of knowledge! Okay, Ansar Bhai, this... this is a bit of a difficult... the matters of *'Ayn* and *Mim*, which are a bit difficult... particularly the matters of the *hijabat* (veils) that come. So, in that, I was having a question, that on *Yawm al-Ghadir*, it has been stated that Mawlana... Rasul Akram gave Mawlana Ali the entire... *nasut kulli* (universal physical form), he bestowed it upon you, he entrusted all the collections to you. And there, it has also been said that their veils were exchanged. *Mim* took the veil of *'Ayn*, and *'Ayn* took the veil of *Mim*. And Ali passed away in the veil of *Mim*. And then after that, the veil of *Mim* that was working after that, that was... the veil of the Prophet... sorry, the veil of Ali that was working, which... after that for 30 years, which fought the wars and all, the veil of the Prophet was working there. So, this... but in the stories... in the *sirat* (biography), it is mentioned that even when the Prophet handed over all the collections to Ali, some things still remained. Like some things you obtained through tears, some were your last breaths that were upon your hand, then... you know, various things like that. But at that time, the veils had already been exchanged. So then at that time... I mean... was *Mim* acquiring from *'Ayn*? This... this... these are matters of... these are matters. Yes. That I can explain to you in detail. I cannot explain them over the phone. These are not matters to be discussed over the phone. Yes, you're right. So I cannot explain it to you. Yes, yes. So for this, we need to have a face-to-face meeting. For sure, for sure. So there I can explain it with examples and in some detail. Insha'Allah, may Allah grant this opportunity too. Yes, Insha'Allah, surely. This is a matter of mutual give and take. The trusts (*amanat*) that were with Ali, he gave them. Some trusts that were with the Prophet, the Prophet gave them to Ali. Okay, okay. The matters of mutual give and take continued. For example, the Prophet had some of Ali's... of... some trusts of Mawlana Muhammad al-Baqir alayhis salam. Hmm, hmm, hmm. These are all... Mawlana Muhammad al-Baqir, meaning... Mawlana Husayn's son, Mawlana Ali. Their son. Mawlana Ali's son, Mawlana Muhammad al-Baqir. The one to whom the Prophet sent greetings. The one who... the one who was supported... the one to whom it was conveyed through greetings. So when was it conveyed? After 100 years of the Prophet's passing. After that, then... this matter... through Hazrat Jabir ibn Abdullah al-Ansari, that "O Jabir, you will see my son's son's son." Yes. "And when you meet him, convey my greetings to him." "And tell him that 'your ancestor, this is a trust for you'." Hmm. So... this... Mawlana Jabir... Jabir conveyed the greetings. When? After approximately 50-60 years had passed. Mawlana Ali had also passed away, then Mawlana Husayn came, the events of Karbala happened. What a long life Mawlana Jabir had. Yes, yes. Yes. And after that, then that... Mawlana Ali Husayn Zayn al-'Abidin's time passed, and after that Mawlana Muhammad al-Baqir came. And to him, Jabir ibn Abdullah al-Ansari... they conveyed the greetings, meaning some of the Prophet's trusts, the Prophet... through them, conveyed them. Jabir ibn Abdullah al-Ansari is from the *babul abwab* (gate of gates) of Mawlana Muhammad al-Baqir. Yes. Through him, it was conveyed. So these matters happen. This give and take of trusts happens. When was it given? How much was given? What was given? So all these are very deep matters. Hmm, hmm. So... I've heard that... that whosever... whichever Imam's name is Muhammad alayhis salam, they will surely receive something from the Prophet. Whoever's name is Ali... Yes, absolutely, absolutely. So he... For this reason, you see, in all the chains of the Imams that have been, up to now, the names of the Awliya and Imams, among them you will mostly find Muhammad or Ali. Muhammad will be there, Ali will be there. Yes, yes, yes. Yes. Or Hasan will be there, or Husayn will be there. Hmm, hmm. Besides these five blessed names, you will find other names very rarely. Maybe one or two... Isma'il's name is a bit... Isma'il's name is a bit different among the names of all the Imams. I mean, this is a... Yes, yes, yes, I am saying that sometimes, somewhere you will find an exceptional case. So Mawlana Isma'il is also among the Imams, isn't he? Yes. Ibrahim had two sons, one of them you appointed to Imamah and Wasayah. Hmm, hmm. And the other, Isa, you gave him Nubuwwah and Risalah. So the chain of Imamah and Wasayah continued from Isma'il. That is why there were those issues. Right, right. That is why Isma'il's name came, and with him were the matters of Isma'il's Imamah and Wasayah. Okay, so to him... Yes, yes, yes. Mawlana Isma'il ibn Jafar, isn't he? Yes, yes, yes. Yes. Their matters are also very profound. How Imam Jafar al-Sadiq handled matters with them. Yes, their passing... their passing... their *fida'* (sacrificial double), their *fida'* was created, Khuraj ibn Anak. Yes, yes, yes, yes. Yes, and his appearance was just like Mawlana Isma'il's. And Mawlana Isma'il, he left Kufa and went to Basra. Hmm. He was sent far away. So many such matters are there, to save him from enemies. So his *fida'* was also created. So these are... matters happen. Okay. Okay, Ansar Bhai, it has been read that Hind, when she... Hamza... Hazrat Hamza's liver... she chewed it and it... so for that, it was said that if Hamza's... a drop of his blood had entered Hind's stomach, Paradise would have become obligatory for her. Yes. So... this is a matter of the *shari'ah*, isn't it? But it is stated that she could not chew it. In history, it is said that she chewed the liver. Okay. But she could not swallow it, the liver. It's a matter of Hind's... what kind of... it's a... a... such a thing... that she had someone killed through deception. She sent her good slave. Yes, yes. Yes, a good slave... she had him killed through deception. Yes. And she had... taken an oath... she had made a vow. Yes, yes. That in the Battle of Badr, her... relatives were killed. They were killed by Ali's hands and Mawlana Hamza's hands. Hmm, hmm. So she had taken an oath that until I chew his liver, I will not rest. Hmm. And I will not eat good food. But you are saying... And Hind is the wife of Abu Sufyan. No, she couldn't swallow it. According to the accounts... the truth is... what the Imams have said is that it was such a blessed thing, how could a vile... Hazrat Hamza alayhis salam, he is... he has received the title of *Sayyid al-Shuhada* (Master of Martyrs). Yes. He is *Sayyid al-Shuhada*. Mawlana Rasulullah gave him the title of *Sayyid al-Shuhada*. Yes. And later this title was given to Mawlana Husayn. Yes. When he was martyred in Karbala, after that this title of *Sayyid al-Shuhada* became associated with him. Yes, rather, it is said that when... I mean... among the Prophet alayhis salam's assembly, his form was the highest, but then after that, when Janab Jafar al-Tayyar was martyred, then he became elevated. Yes. So... okay, Ansar Bhai, just now, since Janab Jafar al-Tayyar's name came up, his... those... one... the Prophet alayhis salam said a strange thing about him, didn't he? That "your two hands have reached Paradise before you." Yes, that is when, while fighting, your two hands were martyred. Just as what happened with Hazrat Abbas... two individuals... Just as here too, that is... No, it's not about individuals, it's not about individuals. No, no, no, no, no. While you were fighting, your first... your left arm was cut, or your right arm was cut, and then you took the sword in your left hand, so your left hand was also cut off. Hmm, hmm. And then you were martyred. So it is said that the angels gave you a *ghusl* (ritual bath). And you... you were taken to Paradise. And you were given two wings. In place of the two hands, you were given two wings. That is why he is called Jafar al-Tayyar. *Tayr* means... *tayr* means bird. Yes. So Jafar al-Tayyar, meaning the flying one. That is why they call an airplane a *tayyara*, don't they? Yes, yes, yes. In Arabic, they call an airplane a *tayyara*. Hmm, hmm. So this is Tayyar. Jafar al-Tayyar, that is why he is called that. Okay. And this happened in the early days of Islam, in the time of early Islam, you... fought a battle, by the Prophet's command, you did jihad, and in that you achieved this martyrdom. This is an event from the Battle of Mu'tah. Yes, yes, yes. From the Battle of Mu'tah. This is an event from the Battle of Mu'tah, yes. So in that, these events happened. Yes. So for this reason, his rank is also considered very high. Okay. Okay, Ansar Bhai, in Shu'al al-Anwar, when Hazrat Ibrahim... he... mentioned Nuh alayhis salam, you said that... "What do you know about Nuh alayhis salam, how high his rank is," you said something like that. Right? So now they are saying that there is no such thing. This jo naadimin, they are saying that the group of musirr wa mustakbirin, a faction of this became naadim, a faction of this became shaak, and its last faction remained the same as the original. Meaning they... Absolutely, absolutely, a wrong conception. A completely wrong conception. He is saying that the naadimin... The Saahib-e-Anwaar has explained in detail that... ...that groups were formed. 70 groups were formed. There are 15 types of naadimin. And tell me about the types of naadimin too. From which forms were what things made? These kawaqib were made, the falak-e-muhit was made, the falak-e... all the aflaak were made, and all the matters that occurred. So 8-10 factions from the naadimin remained above. Yes. And we are at the fourth or fifteenth station. We have come into this world, we are enduring these troubles etc. He is saying that... And the faction of shaak wa mutahayyirin is separate. The one of musirr wa mustakbirin... That is why, that is why the Rasul said that my ummah will have 70 factions, 72 sections. So this, this is all talk of truth, man. He is saying that the naadimin are actually the taab-u-bi-tawbati. And the group below that is lubb-un-nida. He is saying this. And then the rest of the lower part, the falling group of musirr, in that, an upper section is of naadim, the middle one is of shaak, and... so much confusion... Just go on, I knew that... Absolutely, absolutely, today, completely reject today's conception. And the truth of the da'wat is that the naadimin, the musirr-mustakbirin are 15... ...the shaak wa mutahayyirin, they were formed right there, formed in the Alam-e-Ruhani. Yes. Absolutely, clear, the same. And they, at that time, until that time, they only had thoughts. Then they tried to break free on their own. When all these matters happened and the decree of Aashir was also revealed, so from the side of the first creation, matters occurred, so they tried to break free on their own. So in trying to break free, first length was created, yes, then breadth was created, then depth was created. Meaning length, breadth, and depth. Right. This was created. And the outward form took on wujud (existence). And in the Alam-e-Ruhani, there is no such thing as a body. Right. There wujud, but such things happened. Such, such volume was created. And then from there above, the command came from above that now these people are no longer fit to live here. Right. Now for them, make another place for them, where these people can be cleansed. Right. So they were cast down. Right. And this, this very thing has been explained in detail in the Qur'an-e-Majeed, and the verses of Surah al-hamd point to this very thing. Yes. 'Sirat alladhina an'amta 'alayhim' (The path of those upon whom You have bestowed favor). Yes. That O Allah, make me walk on the path of those upon whom You have bestowed favor, meaning the naadimin-mustakbirin. Right. 'Ghayril maghdubi 'alayhim' (Not of those who have evoked [Your] anger). And do not make me walk on the path of those upon whom Your wrath has descended. Right. Meaning the shaak wa mutahayyirin. Right. And not 'wa lad-daallin' (nor of those who are astray). And not on the path of those who are misguided, astray, meaning the musirr wa mustakbirin. With such detail, with such clarity, all things have been explained, and then they say that from the musirr wa mustakbirin these came out, those came out, these are completely wrong things. The very conception is becoming wrong. Hmm. Okay, Alhamdulillah. Jazakallah, Ansaar bhai, thank you very, very much. You have given me a lot of peace, clarifying all these things with you. And I will submit this to you, I will request that you do not read the asbaaq of Sadullah Mian. Yes. Absolutely. This should not go out in my name. No, no, no, absolutely. I understand completely. Because if there is so much confusion, then it is better not to know, that is better. It is better not to know than to know something wrong. Yes. Because all these things I am hearing for the first time from your mouth. Yes. I will to you... I will tell Zahid bhai about this, next time when you go to Hyderabad, I will tell you, give you this recording, this is a special recording which we, Javid bhai has also kept separately, I have also kept separately. In it, he has said all this. You can listen to it yourself. Oh, what will I, what will I do by listening to such things, man. Yes, you have a point too. I, I, I don't even want to listen. That's right. Absolutely right. Why should I spoil my tasawwur? Absolutely right. Alhamdulillah. Please do not take my name. Ansaar bhai, you don't worry at all. I to anyone... you, you don't know anything. You, no one even knows that you... I only... I am only saying this for the sake of your love, that your tasawwur should not be spoiled. If a mo'min's tasawwur is spoiled, then everything is finished. All, absolutely, I now will not... Please wait while we connect your call.

In the name of Allah, all our madaris and taqarir, etc., are finished. And I am starting the series of sabaq today. Although there are very few days, I have until the 13th, and inshallah, I will have to depart from here. And the visa and the time is long, so time is short. So, it is clear that whatever the…

I will pass through the main roads. It is not possible to go into the side streets. And even from the main roads, one has to pass very quickly. For this reason, in some way, these lessons… that you may be able to reach... and the falsafa of Aale Muhammad, alayhis salatu was salam, that you may be able to understand it, that we, on which din we are, and how pure our din is, and which of all these matters our din contains.

The very first and most fundamental thing, as I have said before and have explained in this gathering, is the tasawwur of God. Because the matter, everything that begins, begins with the zikr of Allah Ta'ala. And the tawhid of Rabb al-'Alamin, meaning, to consider Allah Ta'ala as one, is the greatest of all 'ulum. Meaning, among the 'ulum, the knowledge that is greater than all is the tawhid of Allah Ta'ala. To consider Allah Ta'ala as one. You will say that considering Allah Ta'ala as one, what kind of 'ulum is this? And how is this matter so vast? How is there such breadth in it that Allah Ta'ala should be considered one? Just consider Him one, and it's over. Then in considering Him one, how did such breadth emerge that we refer to it as 'ulum, and we interpret tawhid through 'ilm?

So the matter, in fact, is that we understand that one seed, when it is sown, is a small, ordinary seed, but when it brings forth its fruit, you see how large and mighty a tree it becomes. It has branches, and... In the same way, we are understanding this, but when you see its breadth, you will realize that the zikr of Allah Ta'ala and the tawhid of Allah Ta'ala, to affirm His Oneness, is not an ordinary matter. There is a very vast expanse in it that you will find.

I have told you before this that the world's civilization, in what way it has taken turns, and we have passed through an era on the surface of the earth when the people of Rome and Greece had divided God into lakhs of gods. And they had deities of different gods, and they used to perform puja-path of them. This is something everyone knows. But an era also came, which is called the Renaissance, when civilization took a turn, and that thing... was nullified, and Hinduism was born. And in Hinduism, this thing happened, that they said that, well, 'ubbad al-asnam (idol worship) is better to be called; that is, the puja of sanams should certainly be done, the parastish of but (idols) should certainly be done, but for but-parasti, so many buts are not needed. If you take a select few buts, that will be better. So they... 365 days are in a year, they made 365 gods, and each day they began to do puja-path with one god. And these were the buts that... whose puja they used to do where most of all? In Makkah Mu'azzama. The Arabs living in Makkah Mu'azzama are the very first, fundamental Hindus who started Hinduism. It is done. And Makkah Mu'azzama, Khana-e-Ka'bah Muqaddas, is their very first deval, where they had placed the buts. You must have heard this.

So those buts were placed there, and they saw that it is difficult to bring and place 365 buts at the Khana-e-Ka'bah, so they had divided them into three buts, and had brought and seated three buts there, whose names were Lat, Manat, and 'Uzza. Lat, Manat, and 'Uzza. This was it. And in some places, it has also been mentioned that 'Uzza, in fact, was a temple built in Ta'if, where this goddess was worshipped, the 'Uzza goddess. And with Lat and Manat was Hubul. So Lat, Manat, and Hubul, these three deities were made, and they were kept there. And a strange thing is that when Hinduism was finished, and when its great philosophers, who are of Hinduism, such as Radhakrishnan and Jawaharlal Nehru and the great philosophers who have passed of Hinduism, they considered that no, this is not an appropriate thing, that we should be called worshippers of 365 gods or worshippers of buts. It is better that we too divide these 365 into three, that would be good. So they... even today, if you take out and see their philosophy, the Puranas and these Vedas and their old books, if you see them, then in them you will get hints that the three gods they were believing in, those three gods were what? Shiv, Vishnu, and Brahma. These were their three deities. One who creates, one who destroys, one who sustains. These were the three deities whom the Hindus used to worship.

Well, these three were there, and besides that, 365 gods were with them. But the era passed so much that after this, that period came when Hazrat `Isa Masih` came to the world and he gave the teaching and you explained taslis. And the teaching that Hazrat `Isa` was giving, who was Ruhullah, who was a nabiyy of God, a respected nabiyy, who was a high-ranking nabiyy, after Hazrat Adam, Nuh, Ibrahim and Musa, Hazrat `Isa` had come. So you can imagine that 124,000 nabiyys had passed, and every nabiyy in his place had given the call to Allah, whose central idea which they had presented was the parastari of the One God. So it is clear that in the parastari of the One God, the matter of three cannot be included. How could Hazrat `Isa` explain three? But it was the misfortune of his followers, who were affirming him, that those who were the followers of Hazrat `Isa`, and especially his hawaari as they were being called, they also went on this wrong path. And what was that? That they, these three things: Father, Son, Ruh al-Qudus. Father, Son, and the Holy Ghost. In these three things, their trinity came, and they became the affirmers and believers of taslis.

So in reality, it was not so. Hazrat `Isa` was not giving such a teaching. But when Hazrat `Isa` used to call out, "Father, Father, listen to me," the people used to understand that they are calling out to a father, so they must be sons. And they used to say that Jibril is coming to me and bringing me this message, just as prophets used to say in their time. So when `Isa` used to say this in his time, and people used to say that, O `Isa`, who came to you and who brought and delivered this message? He would say the Ruh al-Qudus brought it. So the Ruh al-Qudus brought it, so these people established the Trinity: Father, Son, and Ruh al-Qudus. So in this way, these followers of theirs, those who were their followers, had made this kind of taslis. Otherwise, he, na'udhubillah, na'udhubillah, was a worshipper of tawhid, and he was doing the parastari of the One God.

Well, the era of taslis also came, and his followers divided it into three, three gods. But after this, an era came when in Iran this idea was born that this taslis and all these 365 days of a year and dividing them among gods, all these things are wrong. In reality, we see that in this world there are only two things: good and evil. Good or evil. Whoever does anything, some work will be good or some work will be bad. Good and evil, heaven and hell, virtue and vice. We see only these two concepts, of good and evil. For this reason, we think that in the world there can only be two things, only two deities can exist, only two gods can exist. And who are they? Ahraman and Yazdan. Ahraman and Yazdan, they named it. The Iranians. And Ahraman and Yazdan. That is, the god of evil is Ahraman and the avatar of virtue is Yazdan. So they presented the concept of Ahraman and Yazdan. And taking that concept, they moved forward. This was the era of jahiliyya, which is famous as the jahiliyya of the Arabs. And what should I describe to you about that jahiliyya? You know that the Arab had become an abode of every kind of evil. And all evils were present in them. There was no such defect of the world that was not present in those Arabs before the arrival of the Sarwar-e-Kainat. When the zuhur of the Sarwar-e-Kainat happened, your sacred zuhur, and you, Sarwar-e-Kainat, came into the world, at that time this was the situation. And you, `huwa alladhi ba'atha fil-ummiyyina rasulan` (He it is Who sent among the unlettered a Messenger from among themselves), when this verse came and you were made a nabiyy, then the very first thing you did was this, that look, it is not so, O people, because the example was being given before you, of taslis too, and of many gods too, and the closest matter that was coming was of two gods. The matter of the two gods of Iran was coming. So the Prophet said that look, my Quran, the word of Allah, has come down upon this, and what does this word say? You think and understand, use your intellect, and think, and do not fall into such disgrace. These two gods, three gods, all these things are wrong. God, His being is one, and it should not be divided in this way.

To explain this, you presented this verse of the Quran Majeed: `law kana fihima alihatun illallahu lafasadata` (If there had been in them any gods except Allah, they would both have certainly been in a state of disorder). If there were two gods, O people, then remember this universe would have been ruined. There would be destruction, and complete destruction would occur. One god would say, "Let it rain," the other god would say, "Don't let it rain." Today, just as is the condition of your sheikhs, the situation of squabbling, at that time what the condition of the gods would have been, you can imagine. So in this way, if it were so, then the whole system… one would say that I will make the sun rise from the east, the other would say I will make the sun rise from the west. One would say that the sun has been given heat and the moon has been given coolness, the other god would say, no, from today the moon has been given heat and the sun has been given coolness. What would happen then? It would become a matter of great chaos. So na'udhubillah, these concepts are extremely nonsensical concepts. And the Prophet, alayhis salatu was salam, refuted them and explained that look, leave all these things and you people have fallen into misguidance. And you people, consider that one institution cannot have two directors. One scabbard cannot hold two swords. One place cannot have two masters. How do you accept two gods? `law kana fihima alihatun illallahu lafasadata.` And he refuted it and you said that no, it cannot be, you must believe in one God.

When the Prophet, alayhis salatu was salam, was presenting this thing, the Muslims, who were they? They were but-parast. They were worshippers of Lat, Manat, and Hubul. They were those who had many wives; the situation was that some had 100, some 200, some 300 wives. Whatever they were, and how they were, they ate these animals, and what animals did they eat, you know? They ate crocodiles. Along with eating goat meat, they would also roast and eat the goat's skin. They ate crocodiles. They ate elephants. They drank blood. So this was their condition. The state of their evil habits was this, and the state of the tribes' savageness was this, that a man, after killing an enemy, would remove his skin and drink wine in his skull. Women would dye their clothes with his blood. And the situation was such that for target practice, to aim correctly, they would use children, placing children and then aiming. So this was the peak of barbarism. Such barbaric people, such uncivilized Arabs, of which you all are having a good experience. Beyond this, nothing more can be said. Such Arabs, whom the Sarwar-e-Kainat, the Mercy to the Worlds, was setting right, and you are seeing that today 65 Muslim states are glittering with Islam. This wave of Islam that spread, the Sarwar-e-Kainat spread it. And what must have been your efforts? What effort must not have been made? You can imagine, they were being put on hot sand, entrails were being thrown on your head, you were being beaten, you were called mad, called a poet, you were given all the bad titles of the world. Your name was Muhammad, and you were called Muzammam. Muzammam is being said. That is, the reviled one is being said. Muhammad means the praised one, not, but Muzammam is being said. So the Prophet endured all the taunts. For what? For guidance. And you used to say, O Lord, save my community from misguidance. And like Nuh, you did not curse that my community should be destroyed. Like Hazrat Ibrahim, you did not do that. Just like Hazrat Adam or Musa and `Isa`, but you endured it, and after enduring it you said that, O Lord, they do not know, if they understand, it would be very good. Do not send down Your punishment upon them, O Lord. Do not send down punishment upon them. So this was the Mercy to the Worlds.

So the Prophet, alayhis salatu was salam, used to teach this. But what happens is, the real point is this, that the people who are attached, attached how? You will think, being attached by the hem, meaning sitting very close, they became attached. Or, if a person living is very far away, but his heart is connected, then even if he is a lakh of miles away, he is near. And if you are sitting very near, and your heart hates him, then you are very far. So this is a simple matter. In the same way, those who were sitting near the Prophet of God, you must be thinking that they must have received mercy and they must have understood all things well from the Prophet of God. No. It is dark right under the lamp. It is dark right under the lamp. You cannot see light under it. So it was the same situation. I mean, those sitting with the Prophet of God, among them was his uncle Abu Lahab, Abu Jahl was also there. These kafirs were also there. So everyone came. So did they all become pure? Did they become Muslims? Was there true Islam in their hearts? Nothing was there. So you will say, they used to sit and stand with the Prophet of God day and night. So I am telling you that this is guidance. Whoever got it, got it. It is guidance for whoever wants to take it. He who moved forward, took guidance. He who stayed back, did not find guidance.

So the Prophet of God was giving this guidance to everyone, that look, the very first thing I teach you is to practice tawhid of Rabb al-'Alamin, recite the kalimah of la ilaha illallah. There is no god worthy of worship except Allah. What happened then? People came and wanted to give gold equal to Jabal Abi Qubays. A mountain. A mountain of gold. And they said, we will provide you with a legion of the most beautiful women. You take all this. And we will give you the government of the entire Arab world in your hands, you can rule as you wish. The Prophet said, I need neither wealth, nor beauty, nor government, nor gold. I don't need anything, O people. So they said, this Prophet is strange. He is not ready to take anything and be persuaded. So how to convince him now? So the last resort that exists, the first is targhib, the second is tarhib. The first is targhib, after that is tarhib, after that is tarkib. What happens in targhib? Giving temptation. They gave temptation to the Prophet, he didn't accept. And after that, they started tarhib. Tarhib means beating and killing. Calling you names, calling you mad, calling you a poet. They inflicted so much pain that these words came from the Prophet's mouth: `ma udhiya nabiyyun mithla ma udhitu` (No prophet was harmed as I was harmed). What pain must not have been inflicted? All this pain. But they saw that despite giving pain, this nabiyy is patient and grateful. Then they got tired.

Now they used a third resort. What was that resort? Tarkib. And what is tarkib called? Compromise. This is the strategy of Satan. Compromise. What does compromise mean? You believe some of our things, we will believe some of yours. You bend a little, we will bend a little. This is what happens. So to make a compromise, they told the Prophet that, O Messenger of Allah, we will do this, we will make some compromise with each other. This very compromise Allah Ta'ala has described in the Surah of `qul ya ayyuhal-kafirun` (Say: O you disbelievers). You read that Surah, you will find out. Otherwise, they finally told the Prophet that, O Messenger of Allah, they are not going to agree. Allah Ta'ala says that they will never agree. Because what had they done? This Surah came down at the time when they came before the Prophet and said, look, Messenger of Allah, let's do one thing, so that you are also happy and we are also happy. You don't speak ill of our gods, we won't speak ill of your God. We, we will worship our gods, you worship your god. We will also... and if you insist a lot, we will also include your God among our gods. There were 365 gods, what's the delay in them becoming 366 gods? But you do this one thing. So the Prophet said, no, what is the point of accepting this? So they, the others said, that such a Prophet will not agree, we have to be a bit cunning. So they were cunning. What did they do? They said that, O Messenger of Allah, all this is acceptable. We accept everything of yours. Do one thing. Don't make us recite this kalimah of `la ilaha illallah`. These were Arabs. You understood? These were those Arabs, those uncivilized Arabs, who came before the Prophet and said this. Leave this kalimah, and you kindly change this kalimah by one kalimah. And that kalimah should be this: `Allahu ilahun` (Allah is one among the gods). That `la ilaha illallah` which is causing a big commotion, which is piercing the heart, is causing us great pain. You, please change this to `Allahu ilahun`. The matter was the same. What was its meaning? `Allahu ilahun` means that God is one among the gods. Meaning, the Prophet was being told that among all the gods, your God is also one. It was the same thing. The Prophet said, no, this cannot be. I am trying to say that I am negating the godhood of all gods, as if wiping them out with a wrong pen, and establishing my God. And you are saying that... no. You must do the parastari of the One God.

So you made the parastari of the One God... to make them understand, you said that you all recite the kalimah of `la ilaha illallah`, you will become pure. When you said this, and when some people... who were they? Only one woman, who came forward, she was Hazrat Khadijah al-Kubra, your wife. And only one boy, who was eight years old, who was `Maula-e-Kainat` `Amir al-Mu'minin` `Ali`. And only one man, who came forward later, who was Hazrat Abu Bakr. That's it. So all this happened and they became Muslims. But no virtue is established from this. If virtue were established, then they would have also kept Islam properly. They did not keep Islam properly.

So the point is that when the Prophet made them recite this kalimah, after making them recite the kalimah, they began to say, "Look, I am telling you, but... its explanation... telling is my job, explaining is not my job." Just listen to this point. Telling is my job, explaining is not my job. For explaining, this Ali is sitting. This is my mubayyin, my musharrih, this is the one who explains, this is my wasi, this is my wazir, this is my brother, this is the one who explains all things. Ali is the one who explains everything. You listen from me, and understand from Ali. My job is only to tell, Ali's job will be to make you understand.

Now the situation was such that if they had become attached to Amir al-Mu'minin, then correct knowledge would have come to them. We tell you that look, among you, in your view, `shi'an-e-Ali` is famous. Who are `shi'an-e-Ali` called? The party of Ali. People of Ali's party. Today, there are hundreds of thousands of Shias present. Did the Shias who are connected to Hazrat `Ali`, did they get that explanation of the Prophet? If the Shias had gotten that explanation today, then today their condition would not be with the Sunnis. So it turns out that one who has no history, what would he have gotten from Ali? Because we... there were only a handful of people, who could be counted on fingers. Amir al-Mu'minin, with whom they used to be attached, and from whom they used to learn things, they were a few who... with whom, in reality, we have been attached, they were Hazrat Salman al-Farsi, they were Hazrat Miqdad ibn al-Aswad, they were Abu Dharr al-Ghiffari, they were 'Ammar ibn Yasir, they were... these great personalities, Hudhayfa al-Yamani, these were those great personalities of religion, they were the shining lamps of Islam, they were the mountains of knowledge, who, in the court of Amir al-Mu'minin and in the court of the Prophet, alayhis salatu was salam, used to sit, used to listen, and they used to learn. And those attached to them were our ancestors, attached to them were our A'immah, attached to them were our du'at, attached to them were we. We became attached to these du'at, because of which this 'ilm came to us, and this became our wirsa.

So now you imagine how reality is reached. So the Prophet had said that look, my job is only to convey the kalimah, and this... you... look, I will tell you a special thing about it. The Prophet said that `man qala la ilaha illallah dakhala al-jannah` (Whoever says 'There is no god but Allah' will enter Paradise). Whoever recites the kalimah of `la ilaha illallah`, he will enter paradise. And after that, you turned towards Amir al-Mu'minin and smiled, looked at him, and then said, `man qala la ilaha illallah mukhlisan dakhala al-jannah` (Whoever says 'There is no god but Allah' with sincerity will enter Paradise). Whoever recites the kalimah of `la ilaha illallah` with sincerity, he will enter paradise. So with sincerity... now people were astonished that just now the Prophet has said that whoever recites the kalimah will enter, then again... so you explained that, "O people, I am saying and I am also explaining it, that with sincerity." People said that, "O Messenger of Allah, what is that sincerity?" You said that, "Whatever you have to understand, understand from Ali." Listen from me and understand from Ali. So it turns out that the one who explains sincerity is Ali. So what happened? That those who were attached to Ali, they understood tawhid correctly. The Prophet, alayhis salatu was salam, those attached to him were who? Muslims. These all Muslims, they had heard the Prophet say this, and they said, "That's it, we have heard tawhid from the Prophet, we will go to paradise." And they went away, and reached their tribes. And they got involved in the same life of comfort and pleasure. And they said that we have heard it. Now because we have accepted the Prophet, accepted Islam, so let's believe in the One God, `la ilaha illallah`... just as today you see the condition of Muslims, that they recite the kalimah of `la ilaha illallah` one lakh times, recite it two lakh times, recite it so many times that their heart starts to race. They recite it so many times that boxes of custard apple seeds are prepared, that this is of two lakhs, this is of three lakhs, such boxes of seeds are brought and kept, and on them, two lakh times the kalimah of `la ilaha illallah` is recited. So does the kalimah of `la ilaha illallah` pass down the throat by reciting it two lakh, three lakh times? Hey, reciting the kalimah just once is enough, but it has to be recited with sincerity. You recite it two lakh, three lakh times, who has told you to? So just as Muslims are doing today, the Muslims of before have also done this. These are their descendants. These are their descendants. Who have turned their faces away from the Prophet in this manner... close the door. Who have turned their faces away from the Prophet in this manner, and they have done wrong.

Hazrat `Ali ibn Abi Talib` was the one who explained the true meanings and subtleties, and he explained that look, reciting the kalimah with sincerity is this, that you believe this... अरे, you, if all Muslims, even today, I am saying that, that all Muslims today, you pick up any book, take any thing, take any tafsir, you will see that among them this thing is written, that God is one. God is one. Is God one? It is wrong. You will say, what? God is not one? Hey, we have been hearing this since childhood that God is one. The matter, in fact, is this. There is a difference between speaking and understanding. Hazrat `Ali ibn Abi Talib` said that look, this kalimah of the Prophet is explaining that God is one, this is not it, but it is explaining that God is `ekta` (unique).
