So it is known that man is with his concept. And he cannot get out of this world of concepts. So this fluctuation that happens, because of that this has to be believed, that you are `ekta` in your own place. And the other believer, he is `ekta` at his own level. You will say, "No, there is some difference, it is like this, it is like that." So you, inshallah, in the next lesson you will find out how this difference was created. All things will come. And that is what is called the `tartib` of `musafa`. "Hey, brother, everything is fine with us, but this `tartib` of `musafa`, I don't understand. So-and-so sir is much younger than me, how is he going on top? I don't understand." This is very... it is against the spirit. That one who is going up, this thing I don't like. Everything else is fine, this `musafa`... The other gentleman says that what you have put in this `tartib`, I don't like `musafa` at all. "Hey, why? What is this, listening to the hand? I don't understand. What is this `musafa`, `musafa`?" So this `musafa` will also come, the `tartib` of `musafa` will also come, inshallah, and its details will also come before you, inshallah.

So what I was saying is that in terms of concept, our state is different. So Amir al-Mu'minin explained that you should consider the high and low orders as `ekta` in their own respective places, this in reality is `tawhid`. This is the `tawhid` he explained. `Tawhid`'s first part is `tawhid`. It is a part and also a division. The second thing is `tanzih`. `tanzih` means to purify. Meaning, Allah Ta'ala, na'udhubillah, is impure, so pour buckets of water and purify him? No, it's not like that. Impure means that the words that are attached to him, you snatch all of them from him. He needs to be purified. And what are those? These things that you have said, `Quddus`, `Mu'min`, `Muhaymin`, `Muhaiman`, these `nawwad o nunam`, snatch them from him and apply them to his creation. They are not befitting of him. This is called `tanzih`. `tajrid` is said for skinning a goat's hide. This is a daily observation, especially in Arabia, goats are slaughtered day and night. So you see, the skinning of a goat's hide is called `tajrid`. `tajrid` is said for... to establish `tajrid` for Allah Ta'ala, you do this, that all the creations, all the beings that exist, all the creation, from that entire creation, you take one thing, that to create from nothing, no one has the power. No one has the courage to create from nothing. You snatch this thing from everyone and reserve it for Allah Ta'ala, that only God's work is this, that he created from nothing. To do this is... you have said that this is `tajrid`. And you have said that whoever does `tawhid`, `tanzih`, and `tajrid`, he is a `muwahhid`. He is the one who does the `tawhid` of Allah. So in reality, who is the one who does `tawhid`? That `muwahhid` is the one who does `tanzih`, `tajrid`, and `tawhid`. The one who does `tawhid`, `tanzih`, `tajrid`, in reality, he is a `muwahhid`.

This is what Amir al-Mu'minin explained to us. Do the Muslims have this thing? No. The Muslims, they consider Allah as one, they do not consider Allah as `ekta`. And if they even say the word `ekta`, they do not accept it. They... from a philosophical perspective, they do not see it in that way. So it is clear that for the Muslims, they neither do `tajrid`, nor `tanzih`, nor `tawhid`. How will you consider them Muslims? How will you do `tawhid`? Because they had only heard from the Prophet, said `amanna billah`, accepted Islam, recited the `kalimah` of `la ilaha illallah`. And they apparently became Muslims. You may call them Muslims, but in their hearts, that Islam did not shine in the right way. It could not.

Well, I will end with this. After this, inshallah, I will describe to you that the Lord of the worlds, how He did the creation, how the `ruhaniyyat` came, and this `nawwad o nunam`, for whom it can be befitting, how were those creations created? And how did Allah Ta'ala create the spiritual world? This will be described tomorrow.

Now, what are those five things? These five fundamental beliefs which I have explained, they are five. They are the work of the heart. The work of the heart that I previously enumerated. After that are the acts of worship. The acts of worship, as you know, are *ṭahārah* (purity), *namāz* (prayer), *roza* (fasting), *zakāt* (alms), *ḥajj* (pilgrimage). But everything is at its own time. You will perform *jihād* when the *imām* appears. You will perform *ḥajj* once in a lifetime when you feel the need. If you have the means, you will have the capacity, you will have peace of mind, there will be no trouble, then you will make arrangements for your wife and children. You will fulfill the rights of your parents. You will perform *zakāt* when 40 rupees have accumulated with you, then one rupee from that you will give, or if you have 2.5%, you will pay the *zakāt*. When you have that much money. And in this way, you have to do it in such a way that you aren't fasting every day. No, only during Ramaḍān Sharīf will you fast. Allow Ramaḍān Sharīf to come, and get ready for fasting. What preparation? The preparation for *iftārī*. You prepare for *iftārī* for the fast. That's all. Whatever it is, you make preparations. Ramaḍān Sharīf is passing, and you are going to be people who fast, *alḥamdulillāh*, *alḥamdulillāh*. You have already prepared for it. The fasts will take place, Ramaḍān Sharīf will come, you will fast. Similarly, if you are *nāpāk* (ritually impure), you will perform *ṭahārah* (purification). If you have a minor ritual impurity, you will perform *wuḍū'*. If you have a major need, you will perform *ghusl*. But the thing that is always with you, the only thing, the only *farḍ* (obligation) from Allah is the five daily prayers. And that too, what has Allah done? He has kept such a time for it, that the first is the time of dawn. It doesn't happen that it's suddenly the time for *Fajr*. No. You know, you sleep late at night, now how will I pray *Fajr*? So Allah has said, don't worry, sleep, get up at two, three o'clock, what's the hurry? The time for *Ẓuhr*, it's a very good time. And during that time all the work is done, you get half an hour, and that too Allah has arranged in such a way that what will you eat? Okay. And similarly, the time for *'Aṣr*, for *Maghrib*. What a time. The time for *'Ishā'* is when everyone has had their dinner. So the five prayers are there. And in our religion, what has been done is that this has been divided into three prayer times. That is, *Maghrib* and *'Ishā'* can be prayed together, and *Ẓuhr* and *'Aṣr* can be prayed together. The three prayer times, pray this prayer. And a clarification has been given, a *sunnah* has been stated. Some people have made *Ẓuhr* separate and *'Aṣr* separate. When you pray *Maghrib* prayer, I will also pray *Maghrib* prayer. What about *'Aṣr*? I will pray *qaḍā'* (missed) prayer. May Allah protect us! They say, I will pray *qaḍā'* prayer. What happened, sir? It wasn't on time. I am performing the obligation. So when you are performing the *qaḍā'* prayer, it is also a compulsion. When you see the hadith, what is written in the hadith? It says that for the one who prays *qaḍā'*, there is destruction. God destroy the one who prays *qaḍā'* prayer. You are praying *qaḍā'* prayer, should you pray *qaḍā'* prayer? When a curse has been invoked for the one who prays *qaḍā'* prayer, what will happen to the one who does not pray? You can estimate that. You have the choice. Now, this is the situation. So, *farḍ* is *farḍ*. If you don't fulfill it here, you will have to fulfill it. One thing is that you are, for example, tied in a procession, in a relay, in a race. If you don't support your companion, if you don't run, what will happen to you? You will have to run, in any case, with force. And if you cannot run, then you will be dragged, they will drag you away. They will drag you away. So the matter is exactly like this, that without fulfilling these *farā'iḍ* (obligations), there is no choice. If you did not do it here with happiness, how much time does it take to do *wuḍū'*? And how much time does it take to pray? If you have spent your life with some laziness, then in the grave, your heights, which are so tall and wide, now there, a dead person cannot even get up, nor can they turn on their side. There is constriction, there is darkness, and there is no question of getting up from there. Now, there you will pray. Now when you pray, Allah will make you pray with more severity. Be certain of this. You will have to face more hardship than if you pray to Allah with happiness now, that would be much better. So that hardship will be much more, and because those who are our elders, who are our teachers, this trouble is also going to come upon them, because they often say, "Brother, for God's sake, pray *namāz*." So both are involved, one who guides and one who is guided. Both are there. For which you are urged to pray *namāz*. This is why there is so much emphasis. What was the last word? *Namāz*, *namāz*, *namāz*, *namāz*. And if there is no *namāz*, then there is nothing. If there is no *namāz*, he is not ours. If there is no *namāz*, he is not our friend. If there is no *namāz*, he is not our brother. If there is no *namāz*, then he is nothing. He has no relation. The one who leaves the five prayers, the Prophet says that he is a *kāfir* (disbeliever) and a Muslim has no connection with him. The one who leaves the five prayers. Now you will say that we, since becoming Bāwājī, how many prayers have gone? The prayers that have gone is another matter, but from the moment you have heard, you should be bound. You should become bound. You know, they call me Vijulā'ī. I am not worthy of being Vijulā'ī. But Vijulā'ī, those who were before you used to be like this and those who were after them used to be like this. But you were bound by it, and you will have to be bound by it. If you don't do it, then... One *farḍ* of Allah, and that too a *farḍ* that comes to you in 24 hours. If you had been given 50 prayers, what would you have done? If it had been said that these seven *farā'iḍ* all come at once, and Ramaḍān Sharīf also comes, and *zakāt* also has to be given at once, then look, you would join hands and say, "I am leaving." That's it. It would happen, wouldn't it? So Allah Ta'ālā has divided five things for you. He has given you ease. He has made you prosperous, and he wants you to fulfill just one *farḍ*, and you are negligent even in that. Anyway, Muslims think that we, by performing the *farā'iḍ*, by performing *ḥajj*, by praying *namāz*, by giving *zakāt*, have fulfilled the seven *farā'iḍ*. Hey sir, you are putting up lights at the butcher's shop, and this lamp is putting a very big filter on it, and I am sitting here watching that the strings of lights are being put up, and how beautiful it is, how big it is, and it is glittering, and people are... from here there is everything. And here you are putting up a small bulb from the butcher's, where there is no electricity, and here there is electricity. Which one will you appreciate? The one where there is light, you will appreciate that one. But where is the light? Because there is no *jān* (life/soul) in it. As someone said, a child was born, 10 pounds. You are very happy, there will be a party, 10 pounds child. The celebration is tomorrow, what happened? The child died. So the same is the case here, that everything is there, but the situation is that it is death. Everyone's life is death. What is the issue? That the foundation of *walāyah* is not there, which is the first obligation. There should be the love of 'Alī. There should be the desire for 'Alī. Now you are also involved in the love of 'Alī. Hey sir, in the same way that there is an expression of love, in the same way that there is an expression of love, love in that way. Your love for 'Alī means that you love 'Alī, you believe in 'Alī, so believe in 'Alī's words. Believe in 'Alī's actions. Follow him. Act in that way. That will be believing in 'Alī, that will be believing in the Prophet. Otherwise, you don't believe. So it became known that without *walāyah*, this is not the case for Muslims. That's why all their actions are useless. It becomes like scattered cotton, it becomes like scattered dust. It becomes like dust. All their deeds will be thrown in their faces, and they will be struck with them. So there is no result of action without *walāyah*. Now don't create sorrow in your heart that, O, the sorrow of the whole world is in our liver, what will happen to us Muslims, and they sit down and think. One time, a phone call came late, at 11 o'clock at night. I was worried, it was 11:15, 11:30. It was 11:15, 11:30 or 12:15. And I picked up the phone. I was worried, my wife was sleeping. Whose phone call is this? It was some reality that a sister was telling me, and she had phoned me, saying, "Please give me an answer." I was worried, what happened to you? "It's nothing." Because she lives alone, she lives far away, and she is poor. And the thing is, she doesn't have money, but she is poor. And she said... Now I was worried, what is the matter that at such a late hour... She said, "I am sitting here on a chair, and I am watching the river flowing. When will this river be cleaned?" This big river, when will it be cleaned? I said, "For God's sake, now you look at your own matters, for God's sake, leave the cleaning of the river. Now you, you look at this." So this is the situation. If we create sorrow in this way and sit down, it will be very difficult. That thing... The worry that one gets is about one's own affairs. What about others? So as I was telling you, this system, Allah Ta'ālā, this divine government, this divine system and arrangement, He has established it in such a way that for everyone, `li-kulli qawmin hād` (for every people a guide), a guide kept coming. No nation can claim that a prophet did not come to it. But what kept happening? That `wa takhadhu rusuluhu huwwā`. Oh, what a pity. I used to send prophets, the Qur'ān says. I used to send prophets, but you made a joke of them. You threw stones at them. You called them insane, you called them magicians. Alright, alright. Now get ready for the retribution. And my blow will be such that you will know. What will you do in taking revenge on someone? At most, if you take revenge, you will strike with a dagger, you will kill. That's it. Your revenge is this. Hey, the divine revenge starts from here. When you understand what divine revenge is, there is no sound in its blow. There is no sound in its stick. And its blow is severe. You will not even know, like a leaf you will fly away. What is your status, you are a worthless speck in the universe. What is your standing? But your situation is that you sit down to count your own standing, then you become equal to Allah. So I was saying that the divine system was established, and guides kept coming to us. And this chain remained established. In every era, in the time of Ādam, in the time of Ibrāhīm, in the time of Nūḥ, in the time of Ibrāhīm, in the time of the *A'immah*, all of them, whether it was Mūsā or 'Īsā, or our Prophet, peace be upon them, the chain of prophets continued in the universe, the chain of *A'immah* continued to be established. They kept coming, they kept giving guidance, which was their work of guidance, and they kept delivering guidance, and they kept doing their work and going. But those who had to take guidance, took it, those who did not have to take guidance, did not take it. They prepared the provisions for their grave. Those who did not, they will suffer in the grave forever, they will suffer torment. This is a permanent thing. This is a temporary thing. This life is for a few days, it will pass, and this, this intoxication will wear off. This face of ours, as you were seeing your face in the mirror, while looking, you are startled that your black hair is turning white. Then you see that there are wrinkles on my face. Then you see that the face has changed. And you are getting scared of your own face. You have not yet seen your real face. Your real face is to be seen at the time of the last gasp. What a face it will be. So in that face, may Allah protect our honor, and may Allah protect our dignity. May the Lord of the worlds give us salvation for the sake of His *A'immah*. This is salvation. Otherwise, what is this salvation that we have made provisions for? Anyway, I was saying that these *A'immah* kept doing their work. When they, just as we have day and night, in their religion too, there are nights and there are days, which are called *satr* (concealment) and *kashf* (manifestation). And in *satr* and *kashf*, what happens? Sometimes the *imām* is manifest, sometimes he is concealed. The time of concealment came. He went into concealment. Just as it is night now and it is also ending. So the time of concealment came, he went into concealment. And what did he do by hiding? It doesn't happen that Allah has hidden the sun, so now he has made you dark. No, he has given you the moon. Take its light. He has given you the stars, take their light. And if you need a lot, then light a lamp in your house, you will get light from that. In the same way, the system remained established for us. The *dā'ī* is present, your elders are present. So they keep this system going. And from there, Allah Ta'ālā, the *Imām* (peace be upon him), this is not our power. This is not some elder's doing. Whichever speck the sun shines upon, it starts shining. Otherwise, it has no capacity. It is a worthless speck. But when it shines, it shines. When it becomes, then its obedience becomes obligatory. And it gives guidance. And taking guidance is your job, giving guidance is its job. So this guidance, this chain is going on in its place. This era of the master of the universe came, when the pride of all existence, Aḥmad al-Muṣṭafā, Muḥammad al-Muṣṭafā (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) came to his place, and this world was illuminated. And the ignorance of the Arabs became disbelieving, and after the darkness was removed, the light of dawn appeared. The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) came. He spread Islam. He spread the religion. He taught everything, explained everything. But, just as you had to come at a certain time, as a human being, you were being presented. So you, as a human being, also had to become sick, you had to tie a stone to your stomach, you had to be hungry, you had to have a fever, you had to laugh, you had to cry. Exactly a human life had to be presented before us. Otherwise, we would not see him as a human, but we would see him as something else. So he had to be presented before us as a human, so that we too could shape our lives according to his example. So when the Prophet was about to pass away, whom did he appoint in his place? It is obvious that when you were about to depart from the world, you said that now in my place... people said, "O Messenger of Allah, we used to see you and fast, we used to see you and do *iftār*, we used to see you and do good deeds, we used to see you and do this and that." Now, what do they know? Pay attention to early Islam, in that era, they used to say, "We used to see you and do everything." He said, "Whatever you used to do by seeing me, now do it by seeing 'Alī." So he made a will, he established his successor. Whom did he do it to? Amīr al-Mu'minīn 'Alī. How did he establish him? What was the incident? This incident is a great incident that comes in the explanation of Ahd-e-Sharīf. And since this incident comes in the explanation of Ahd-e-Sharīf, I will briefly narrate it to you. The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him), when Masjid al-Qubā', a large mosque in Madīnah Munawwarah is Masjid al-Qubā'. This very mosque is mentioned in the Holy Qur'ān: `ussisa 'alat-taqwā` (founded on piety). The foundation of which was laid on piety, this is that mosque. This mosque is a very blessed mosque. There are many signs in it. And in the niche of that mosque, the Prophet was standing. The Sūrah *Idhā Jā'a* was revealed. Jibrīl Amīn descended, and you got the good news that your demise is about to happen, it is near, and with it, this good news was given that Makkah will be conquered, and after that, the time of your demise is near. Allah Ta'ālā wants to meet you. The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) turned. He said to the people, "O people, the time is near that I should go. And now there is a need that before separating from you, I should explain some things to you." People started crying. They said, "O Messenger of Allah, what are you saying? Your separation is a great sorrow for us." He said, "It will happen, but what to do? We have to go, in any case. And Allah is our master. And before going, I want to fulfill the last obligation of *Ḥajj*, so that you can see once how the rituals of *Ḥajj* are performed. I will also perform it, you also see it and understand." When the obligation of *Ḥajj* was mentioned, people happily agreed. If he had said that I am going to tell you something else, then these Muslims, these weak-minded Muslims, those who had malice in their hearts, those whose minds were rusted, whose hearts were filled with filth, whose hearts were filled with hatred for 'Alī, they would never have agreed, nor would so many have gathered. A crowd of two hundred thousand gathered. It was the occasion of *Ḥajj*. And now these Bedouin Arabs were thinking that goats will be slaughtered, camels will be slaughtered, food will be available, and we are with the Prophet. What kind of fun it is, and what kind of things happen. The entire gathering of two hundred thousand was with him, and the honorable Prophet was going. He reached Makkah. There, you... Makkah had been conquered. After the conquest of Makkah, you purified Makkah. That is, the idols that were there, you had them thrown out. Through whom were they broken? They were broken through 'Alī. And after that, you performed *Ḥajj*. After performing the entire *Ḥajj*, because after a long time the Prophet got a chance to perform *Ḥajj*, because Makkah, Ka'batullah, was in the hands of the disbelievers, the idolaters, the Quraysh. When you conquered Makkah and performed its *Ḥajj*, after performing *Ḥajj*, now you said that I am returning. I am going from the station of Juḥfah towards Madīnah. There was a path in those days. People thought that the Prophet had come by one path and was going by another path. Just as it is said for the Friday prayer that one should come by one path and go by another. It is better. We will keep changing paths, will we build two or three paths to the mosque? It's not like that. Anyway, the Prophet returned by another path. People were thinking that the Prophet has taken this path. It was called the path of Juḥfah. And the station came, and on the station of Juḥfah, this verse was revealed, which I recited before you. `Yā ayyuhar-rasūlu balligh mā unzila ilayka` (O Messenger, announce that which has been revealed to you). Whatever has been revealed to you, convey it. The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) paused. For a moment, he waited. Jibrīl descended again. He said, `balligh`, O Messenger, `mā unzila ilayk`, `wa in-lam taf'al fa-mā ballaghta risālatah` (convey what has been revealed to you, and if you do not, then you have not conveyed His message). If you have not conveyed it, it is as if you have not conveyed the message. You have not done any work. See what a threat it is, how severe the verse is. What kind of tone it has, what kind of mood the verse is showing. When this verse was revealed, three times Jibrīl descended. Now the Prophet was helpless. And he looked towards the sky. Jibrīl descended and said, "O Messenger of Allah, why do you worry? Perhaps you... perhaps you are worried that they should not cause any harm to you, that people should not create any trouble over this announcement." `wallāhu ya'ṣimuka minan-nās` (and Allah will protect you from the people). Allah will protect you from the people. Their evil will not work at all. You announce. Don't worry, do whatever you want. Did the Messenger of Allah have any worry? No. The matter is that in praise of Amīr al-Mu'minīn, the Prophet wanted a promise to be revealed from Allah, so that people may see. Because when love is born, every aspect of the beloved is adorned. Everything is said, and sometimes it needs to be said with exaggeration. Here there was no exaggeration. But praise was necessary. And the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) was praising him. And what did Allah Ta'ālā do? That `Allāhu ya'ṣimu...` Allah will protect you from the people, will protect you from their evil. The Prophet, at that very moment, what did he do? You had reached that place which is called Ghadīr Khumm. *Ghadīr* means a pond. It was a pond, a pit, there. You had reached there, the name of which was Khumm. You had reached the place of Khumm, and there you stopped. And after stopping, you said, "Those who are coming, stop them. And those who have gone ahead, call them back." Everyone was called back, everyone came. And after that, you said, "This desert, in this desert, there are many thorny trees. Remove these thorny trees." People immediately got ready. It was the command of the Prophet. Someone took a pickaxe, someone took a spade, and they removed all the thorns from there. Hey, the Prophet was not giving an outward command. In fact, the thorns that were in their hearts, the jealousy that was in their hearts, he was removing those. Anyway, the ground was cleared. And the desert was vast. And the thorns were not fitting even in the clothes. Now, what a celebration it was, that the sky, as long as it exists, and as long as it has existed, it was yearning for this celebration. That its eyes may see this celebration. This celebration. And this was the occasion of the celebration. It was the occasion of the greatest Eid, Eid-ul-Akbar. The Prophet said that I want to give a sermon before you. Immediately, the saddles of the camels, the saddles of the camels were brought and placed there. A pulpit was made from them. Otherwise, where would a pulpit come from? This was made into a pulpit. The Prophet came upon it. And after coming, he said, "Assalamu alaykum." You said salaam. After that, he said, "`Alastu awlā bikum min anfusikum?`" (Am I not more worthy of you than your own selves?). Are you... am I not greater than your own selves? "O people, am I not greater than you?" They said, "`Qālū balā yā Rasūlallāh`" (They said, "Yes, indeed, O Messenger of Allah!"). "Indeed, you are greater than us, O Messenger of Allah. And our parents be sacrificed for you." He said, "Did I not tell you about heaven and hell? Did I not warn you about hell and give you the desire for heaven? Did I not tell you about prayer, fasting, zakat, etc.? Did I not teach you everything? You were lying somewhere, from where I took you out. You were lying in misguidance, in ignorance. Look at your ignorance. In what evils you were lying. From all the evils, I took you out or not?" They all said, "O Messenger of Allah, indeed, our parents be sacrificed for you. You took us, we were like animals. We were animals." When he took this confession, when they said, "Yes, we were like animals. You made us human. You taught us everything." Then what did he do? He said, "Look, since you believe in me and acknowledge it in this way, that I am greater than you, I am greater than your own selves, then remember that now I am saying that I am your master. And being the master, I am saying that `Man kuntu mawlāhu, fa-hādhā 'Alīyyun mawlāhu` (Of whomsoever I am the master, this 'Alī is also his master). Of whomsoever I was the master, from today, 'Alī is his master." You, in that gathering, there would have been 30-50 'Alīs. It's a gathering of two hundred thousand. So 'Alī, what if the Prophet had just said this much and stopped? Then any Tom, Dick, or Harry would have been caught and made 'Alī, and the name 'Alī would have been given. Or whichever 'Alī it was, he would have been caught and brought, and a garland of flowers would have been put on him, and he would have been seated in the Prophet's place. This is what Muslims were like. This was the public's voice. You know how mob mentality is. So the Prophet did not do that. Rather, he took Haḍrat 'Alī ibn Abī Ṭālib, took him and raised him with both hands, raised him up and said, "This is 'Alī. `Man kuntu mawlāhu, fa-hādhā 'Alīyyun mawlāhu` (Of whomsoever I am the master, this 'Alī is also his master). Of whomsoever I was the master, from today, this 'Alī is his master. The entire nation is entrusted to him. And now obey him." He prayed, "`Allāhumma...` I... if 'Alī... befriend him who befriends 'Alī. And humiliate him who humiliates 'Alī. Love him who loves 'Alī." He said all this and says, and what a strange statement, and all these statements are present with the Muslims. After that, he says, "`Adir al-ḥaqqa ma'ahu ḥaythu dār`" (Make the truth revolve around him wherever he turns). O Allah, make it so, O Lord of the worlds... see, he is praying, the Prophet. That make it so that the truth follows 'Alī. 'Alī wherever he goes, the truth should go there. He did not say that 'Alī should follow the truth. Did you understand? That wherever 'Alī goes, the truth should be there. After saying this, you prayed two rak'ahs of prayer, and Amīr al-Mu'minīn also prayed. After that, he sat in the tent. First Abū Bakr came, then 'Umar came, then 'Uthmān came. They all came. "`Bakhin bakhin laka yabna Abī Ṭālib, asbaḥta mawlāya wa mawlā kulli mu'minin wa mu'minah`" (Congratulations, congratulations to you, O son of Abī Ṭālib! You have become my master and the master of every believing man and woman). They were saying that congratulations, congratulations, O son of Abū Ṭālib! You have become our master and the master of all. They kissed his hand, gave their allegiance, and all the companions came, Ṭalḥah came, Zubayr came, all these accursed ones came and after congratulating 'Alī, they left. And the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) was smiling and watching. He was smiling and watching who was congratulating, what they were doing. After that, he said, "O people, the hypocrites among you, the two-faced ones, the two-hearted ones, who have hatred for 'Alī in their hearts and show love on the outside, if I want, I can identify each one of them. I can identify each one of them. It's not that I don't know. But I don't like to tell. But I am telling you, so remove this hatred. Cleanse your impurities and love 'Alī, be devoted to 'Alī. And if you are desirous of heaven, then love 'Alī. Follow 'Alī. And if not, you will go to hell." He said this, after that the matter ended. You returned. You came. And the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) became ill. After that, you had a deathly illness. And the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) passed away from the world. Haḍrat 'Alī ibn Abī Ṭālib's lap was where the Prophet's head was. And at that time, your last breath that you took, the Prophet, he wiped it. And the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) passed away. Haḍrat 'Alī was the guardian of the shrouding and burial. You gave the *ghusl*. And on the command of the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him). And there, when all the Ahl al-Bayt were in an uproar, everyone was grief-stricken. The master of the universe had left the world. The mercy to the worlds had left the world. What would not happen? Could there be a greater sorrow than this? You tell me. There cannot be a greater sorrow in the world than the master of the universe leaving the world. It was not a small thing. But what was the situation? That here, the matter of shrouding and burial was going on. There, Abū Bakr and 'Umar, and the Muhājirūn and Anṣār, they all gathered together, and there, at Saqīfah Banī Sā'idah, a place, today that place, that cursed place exists. Where they went and sat, and started consulting, that now who will sit in the Prophet's place? Hey brother, what the Prophet was saying his whole life, did you not hear that? Did you not see that he appointed 'Alī? Did you forget the incident of Ghadīr Khumm? No, all that was gone from their minds. No, such a big task the Prophet has entrusted to us. Such a big property, such a big government, such a big task, after all, if we don't do it, who will? This task we have to do. There, the Muhājirūn started fighting. We are Muhājirūn. We are the ones who lived with the Prophet. We spent our lives in Makkah with the Prophet. There, the Anṣār started fighting. We gave refuge to the Prophet in Madīnah. We have the right. We should become the caliph. There, if I were to narrate this to you now, hours would pass. Such fights happened. Abū 'Ubaydah was a sensible person, he was wise. There, the leaders of the Anṣār's tribe stood up. There, the leaders of the Muhājirūn's tribe stood up. Anyway, whoever's influence was working, he was moving forward. Haḍrat 'Umar was working with a lot of force. And he saw this, that if I take the lead and take the upper hand, the matter will be spoiled. This is because perhaps these people will not listen to me. But it is better that right now, I make Abū Bakr the caliph. And make him the caliph, so that then he will make me the caliph. They made this kind of trickery. And they grabbed Abū Bakr's hand and kissed it, and said that from today, the caliph is Abū Bakr. There were long, drawn-out situations. Big, big speeches were made there. And after that, 'Umar did this trickery. And he said that my sword will cut and throw away whoever comes forward. I am kissing Abū Bakr's hand, he is the Caliph of the Messenger. Well, he became the Caliph of the Messenger. After that, what happened? That now, he had said in the ears of Abū Bakr, "I am making you, but take care of me. As you go, make me. It shouldn't be that you forget me. I am making you the caliph for this very reason, that you make me the caliph. If you don't make me, then just as I am scaring people with the sword, I can also break the caliphate into pieces." So Abū Bakr nodded his head and said, "'Umar, don't worry, *in shā' Allāh*." When there were gestures between them, he said, "Brother, just take care." That's it. Now all this has happened. After it happened, drums started beating. Just as in the old days, the announcers would beat drums and make announcements. "Look, so-and-so has happened, this has happened." It's an old era. Beating drums, they are speaking, the announcement is happening. And that announcement, Abū Bakr himself wrote the message. Why? Because his father was present. And to inform his father, he wrote that I have been chosen as the caliph and I have become the Caliph of the Messenger, *alḥamdulillāh*, and this and that is the matter. He sent that letter with someone. That Abū Quḥāfah was on his rooftop. He was very old. He was sitting on some high place. And the messenger came and gave the letter, saying, "Your son has given this." He said, "Brother, my eyesight is weak, I can't see. What is written, what is it?" He said, "Sir, please come closer and read it, because it is a very special letter. He told me to give it into the father's hand." The letter arrived, and Abū Quḥāfah took it and read that letter. And in the letter, it was written that I have become the Caliph of the Muslims. Sometimes he writes Caliph of Allah, sometimes... Now he is reading, he is not understanding what he is writing. Sometimes he writes Caliph of Allah, sometimes he writes Caliph of the Prophet, sometimes he writes Caliph of the Muslims. And in the end, the signature is exactly my son's. He asked, "What has happened?" And when he read it, he understood that he has sat in the place of the Prophet. My son has sat in the place of the Prophet. He asked the messenger, "What is the matter? Why did people make my son the one? After all, what did they see in him that they made my son the caliph? Was 'Alī ibn Abī Ṭālib not there? Did people not hear that `anā madīnatul-'ilmi wa 'Alīyyun bābuhā` (I am the city of knowledge and 'Alī is its gate)?" Who is saying this? Abū Quḥāfah is saying it. Abū Bakr's father. So he is saying, "What happened that my son was chosen?" The messenger said, "Sir, the real matter was that your son was the most senior. *Mā shā' Allāh*, he had a long beard, and he was the most senior, he was a companion of the Prophet, he was with him in the cave. He had so many great qualities." He said, "Hey brother, if it was because of seniority, because of being older, that he was made, then the father is me. Why was I not made?" I am his father, sitting here. Why was I not made? Anyway, there are many jokes, and there are many such stories. Anyway, it passed, it passed. And what befell the master of the universe, only Allah knows best. The pain you had was for your son. Just as I will tell you, two mothers came fighting to Haḍrat 'Alī. Two mothers came fighting. In this era, a mistake cannot happen in a hospital. Before, in maternity hospitals, a lot of mistakes... What was a hospital? The house itself was the maternity hospital. Now there, a mistake happened. They used to live, tribal people used to live, and Bedouin people, you know very well how they live. Because you have lived with them. Now, what happened was that by chance, at the same place, two children were born to two mothers. And what happened? That... one child passed away. Now the other mother saw that my child has passed away. What did she do? She snatched that child and said, "This dead child is yours, this child is mine." Now both were fighting that the living child is our child. Now both of them reached Haḍrat 'Alī. The Caliph of his time. They reached him and said, "O 'Alī, decide that this child is ours." She said that the child is ours. What did you say? You called Qambar, your servant. "Qambar, bring the sword." He brought the sword, Qambar. You said, "This child, from the middle, exactly, see, don't make a mistake. Exactly from the middle, cut it in half. Half a child to you, half a child to you." Now the real mother, she cried out, "O 'Alī, what a disaster you are doing! For God's sake, don't give it to me, but let it live." You did this. You said, "This mother is a liar, this mother is truthful. Give the child to her." So what was the matter? The pain for Islam was with 'Alī, because it was his child. This Islam was 'Alī's child, it was a thing of their house. 'Alī had the pain for Islam. What pain would anyone else have? When a messenger reached the Caesar of Rome and he did not get an answer, what of it? And when the Negus of Abyssinia did not get an answer, what of it? If you are being asked about some verse in the Qur'ān Sharīf, then it is being asked, "Is this verse in the Qur'ān Sharīf?" The Caliph is sitting. And you... see, pick up their books and read. There are not one, there are thousands of stories. Not one, there are hundreds of stories. Now, for whom will you mourn this? For the Muslims? Or for the Caliph-makers? Or for the Caliphs? Anyway, there is a lot. We have nothing to do with it. We don't have to humiliate anyone, nor do we have to do anything. Anyway, we look at ourselves. So the real mother, she had the pain for Islam. That's why what did she keep doing? She saw that there should be no bloodshed in my Islam, so she remained silent for 30 years. But when the Caliphate came to her door, and they said to 'Alī, "'Alī, now take the Caliphate." At that time, what was 'Alī ibn Abī Ṭālib doing? He was sitting and mending his shoes. He was mending his torn shoes. So people entered his house and said, "'Alī, now take charge. Haḍrat 'Uthmān has been martyred. The Caliphate is over. There is no one else. Who should we appoint besides you? Ṭalḥah and Zubayr, who were there, they have also gotten into some trouble. They are fighting with each other. It is better that you take the Caliphate. This is your right, and you..." You smiled and looked at them. First, he kept getting angry. When he saw that these people are not listening, they are doing this, he said, "O people, why are you making such a commotion at my door? My door is weak, my house is weak. If you make a commotion, my house will also fall. I live in a weak house, O people. And why are you making a commotion? And you see what work I am doing." They said, "O 'Alī, what work are you sitting and doing? You are sitting and doing the work of a cobbler. You are sewing shoes." So you said, "O people, what would be the price of my shoes?" They said, "O 'Alī, your shoes are so torn, torn from all sides, and you are trying to sew them, you are patching them. What value does it have? No value." You said, "O people, by God, the value of these shoes in my eyes is more than your Caliphate." Did you see? This was the sarcastic reply of 'Alī. This was a slap on the face of the nation, on their assembly, on their democracy, on their republicanism. That you... you count people, you don't weigh them. You don't weigh. You are those people who... 200 sheep... 200 goats, from these people, if you gather a little bit of their intellect, can the intellect of one human be formed? Can the intellect of one human be formed by gathering a little bit of the intellect of 200 sheep? Your system is exactly like that. You have chosen someone by joining heads. Your choosing is different, God's choosing is different. This is the divine system. How did you choose? If you confess that yes, we are leaving the system in our hands, then I will accept. You... you do not have the right to appoint. Hey, when God and the Prophet have appointed me, how... That's why when 'Alī went and took the Caliphate, and they confessed that yes, God and the Prophet have appointed you, we are not appointing you. Then you said, "Confess." When they confessed, you reached the mosque. And at that time, your condition was that you were wearing ordinary clothes, and when you came to the pulpit for the Caliphate, your condition was that you were getting up, you were sitting among the people. People were getting up. So people did what? They took you by one hand, another person took you by the other hand, and they sat you down. "Hey old man, where are you getting up?" They are saying to 'Alī. See, people had become so ignorant. They had even stopped recognizing 'Alī. Now they said, "Hey, O old man, where are you getting up? 'Alī is coming." "Hey, I have heard his name a lot. He is a great rider, he has innate knowledge. Hey, he is a great rider, he won the Battle of the Trench, and he won Tabūk, and he won Badr, he won Uhud. Hey, he was the Prophet's special man. Hey, he was a brother, he was a successor. Hey, just think, what are you doing? 'Alī is about to come. Sit down in your place." He said, "O people, the 'Alī for whom you are saying this, I am that very 'Alī. Leave me, O people. Let me go and sit on the pulpit." This was 'Alī. There was no grandeur of kingdoms, nor were there forts, nor were there curtains of gold and jewels. All things were thrown away. There was an ordinary cloak, a black turban, a stick in his hand. Amīr al-Mu'minīn was coming after 30 years, to that very pulpit of the Prophet. And you came and, stumbling, when you went and sat, you sat in the Prophet's place. The custom had become that when Haḍrat Abū Bakr came, you sat one step lower. And people said, "O Abū Bakr, why are you sitting lower?" He said, "To sit in the Prophet's place... this is a place of respect. Who can sit? Who will sit in the Prophet's place?" So he sat lower. The second gentleman came, when Haḍrat 'Umar became the Caliph, he left Abū Bakr's place, he took a step lower. 'Uthmān came, he left that step. Now they were descending one step at a time. Now, in the time of Hishām ibn 'Abd al-Malik, a discussion arose, that this commotion that happened, why did they descend these steps? When Haḍrat 'Alī came, what did you do? He went straight ahead, stumbling, and sat in the Prophet's place. People said, "Why did you not maintain the custom? You should have also taken a step lower." You gave a slap of a reply. "What a foolish thing you are saying! I am the one who will sit in the Prophet's place. The Prophet sat me here. I will sit in the same place." This is sitting in the right place. Now what happened? In the time of Hishām ibn 'Abd al-Malik, a discussion started, whether this was right or wrong. Hishām said, "Brother, whether it was right or wrong, leave that, but 'Alī did a great favor to us. If the Caliphs had kept descending one step at a time, it would have gone into a well. The pulpit would have become a well, and one step would have descended. It would have become a joke." So, anyway, this was the Caliphate of the Muslims. This was our Caliphate. 'Alī's. And it was the day of Ghadīr Khumm, and the appointment was for Amīr al-Mu'minīn. And you were the Caliph of the Prophet. But after becoming the Caliph, what work did you do? The same work of the Prophet, that `mā ātākumur-rasūlu fa-khudhūhu wa mā nahākum 'anhu fantahū` (what the Messenger gives you, take it, and what he forbids you, refrain from it). What the Prophet gives, take it. What the Prophet forbids, stop from it. This was also 'Alī's work. Amīr al-Mu'minīn, as soon as he came, he said, "Beware, when the time for prayer comes, it should not be that the prayer is not done." And "Beware, do not even look at such a thing." It is a wrong thing. One should not even look at a wrong thing. One should not eat it, one should not drink it. And the thing from which I am stopping you, stop. The thing from which I am not stopping you, don't stop. And what things did he stop from? You think that Islam has placed many restrictions. No. Only in plants, the plants that we have, in those plants, there is only one thing that you have been stopped from. And we are not even aware of that. We are so ignorant. We say we are Sulaymānī, Mu'minīn, etc., we take the name of hadith, but we don't know. In plants, there is one thing not to eat. You will say, "What's in plants?" What do you know, sir? What reality are you aware of? You are not even aware of your own reality. Tell me, the one you keep calling your own, your own, your own hand, your own head. Are you aware of any reality? Your... in your stomach, inside you, what treasure is running in your body, what is happening, can you tell now? No. When you put a machine on, you will know. How much is the pressure, you will know. Sir, with a machine... Sir, you look inside yourself, it is your world. Look into your world. So you are aware of something, how can you say? Anyway, in plants, one thing is forbidden by Allah, and that is mushroom. Mushroom is forbidden. It is haram. Its soup, etc. You will say it has so many varieties, etc. Those varieties are all hellish. This is hell. It should be avoided. Don't touch it with your hand. You will say, "We have drunk so much of it until now, so much..." All that is wrong. It is a wrong thing. Mushroom is haram. If you are a follower of 'Alī, don't touch it with your hand. Don't even look at it. If a new thing is created, what do you do? I ask you, there are seven colors, aren't there? You will say, "Yes, there are seven colors." If there was an eighth color, what would it be like, tell me. Hey, I am asking a simple question, tell me the eighth color. Hey sir, there isn't one, so what can I tell you? No, tell me. You have created a sixth sense. So here, bring an eighth color. Why don't you bring it, sir? You have created a sixth sense. Just give it a name. Sixth sense's name should also be... "No sir, it's just XYZ." Hey, what is this XYZ? Give it a name. Why don't you give it? You don't give it. So in the same way, you should understand that what is haram is haram. In plants, it is this one thing. And in animals, the pig. *Na'ūdhubillāh, na'ūdhubillāh*. That animal that feeds only on filth. You just look at it, look at its face, look at its mouth. Look at its form. *Na'ūdhubillāh*. The pig is a pig. And some people say, "What difference does it make? It's just meat. You can eat anything." The one who eats filth, you eat him? When you stop the water, it is obvious that when you stop the water, you should not bring a single drop of water here. Stop all the water. You will say, "How will I stop it like this, brother?" When I build a dam, some water will remain, and then it will dry up. So what happened later was that the water remains and then dries up. In the same way, the rules of slavery came. In the same way, these Arabs who were addicted to wine, the Bedouins who lived in the desert, where there was no water, who were in great difficulty, they did not get water for miles, so they used to drink this wine. It was in their blood. So the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him), Allah Ta'ālā, used this wisdom, that if he had declared it haram at once, they would have been very shocked. They would have had a great problem. That's why He... He induced a desire in them for it, and the verses for wine came gradually, so that they could be stopped and explained. And look at it from a psychological point of view. From a psychological point of view, it happens that you go to a doctor. You go to the doctor. And why do you go to the doctor? When you are sick, you go. You don't just go to the doctor like that. Unless he is a friend, then you go, that's a different matter. If he is a relative, you go. Otherwise, when you are sick, you will go. When you go to the doctor sick, what do you say to the doctor? "Sir, I have this problem, this illness. Please treat me." And that doctor will check your pulse, etc. After seeing everything, he will say, "You have this illness, etc." But what will the doctor say? It is obvious that a doctor is wise, and he is a physician. So obviously, first of all, he will tell you prevention. And you know that this saying is famous in the world, and we are bound by it: Prevention is better than cure. Prevention is better than cure. So, prevention first, treatment later. No, you will not see such a doctor who tells you the treatment first and the prevention later. No. First, he will tell you the prevention, and that too with emphasis. Then he will say, "Take these pills, drink this syrup, or take this injection." So the doctor will treat you in this way. And how will he treat you? That first of all, he will make you sit and he will read out a list to you, that you will have to abstain from these things. Now you are sitting in the doctor's office. Just imagine the scene. The doctor is also here, and the patient is also ready. Now the patient went, and both of them said to the doctor, "Doctor, this is the disease, and please treat it." And the doctor saw it. After seeing it, he said, "Look brother, you have a lot of cold, you have bronchitis, and you will have to abstain from such and such things." Now he started listing the names before you. He started listing so-and-so name, so-and-so thing, so-and-so thing. "Brother, don't eat this vegetable, don't eat brinjal, don't eat potatoes, don't eat pumpkin, don't eat this thing." You don't even like those things. You kept listening quietly. He kept reading out the list. And you kept listening. And while listening, when he named such a thing which you are very fond of, and you drink and eat a lot of it, then you said, "Doctor, this too?" Why? Until now you were not startled. Why did you jump from your chair? You immediately jumped from your chair and said, "Doctor, this too?" And the doctor was also surprised, "O God, this man will kill me, what will he do? Now should I tell him or not? And in reality, it is poison for him. But now how to explain it to him?" So he also used great wisdom. First, he read out the list which you did not like. Whatever strange things he read out, you said, "I don't eat those things anyway." You said, "I have left everything." The doctor said, "That's good." "No problem." He said, "No problem." And the doctor kept listing things, and you showed no reaction. "No problem, no problem," you kept saying. As soon as he named that thing, the color of your face changed. "Hey doctor, this too?" The doctor said, "Hey, not wine!" The physician of the nation, our doctor, the doctor of doctors, the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him), when he named this thing, you were startled. "Hey, wine! Hey, hey, wine! Now that too is not allowed? Hey, first there is no water in the desert. And now we used to live by drinking this. Now wine is also not allowed?" Now, if you think, that doctor is wise, so he will try to explain it to you gently. "Hey, wine... for God's sake, son. Look, it's not good for you." He will explain it with such coolness. If he had said, "It is poison for your nose. You will die." Then... you would have left that doctor and gone to another doctor. "This doctor, shoot him." You would have gone to another doctor. So it became known that the matter becomes difficult. This is the psychology of a human. That where you forbid, there you have a desire. And the things whose list he gives, there you are startled, because you have a desire for it. So this physician, our physician of the era, and the physician of the nation, the leader of the mystics, the leader of the prophets, he, how did he work with wisdom? He, through the Qur'ān, Allah and the Prophet were united. They were not separate. Whatever the Prophet said, Allah said, whatever Allah said, the Prophet said. `wa mā yanṭiqu 'anil-hawā` (Nor does he speak from [his own] inclination). So the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) conveyed the command of Allah in such a way that he did not use the word haram. If he had used the word haram, the heart of this Arab would have broken. "Oh, haram!" Like that... So he explained it with coolness. "Look brother, in this, it is a satanic act. It is this thing." So there, he gave them a warning by revealing different verses, he scared them first. And the other things he mentioned, "You can eat this, you can do this," he made them happy. And then he brought one thing and said, "Leave this, brother. Just leave this." But what advantage did they take from it? "Look, the word haram is not there, so come on, drink." So this subtlety, do you know who did it? The second Caliph. The second Caliph, he was the first to make it permissible. He said, "The light wine, which has a little intoxication, like beer, what's the harm in drinking that?" Come on, drink. When he drank, the third Caliph was very pious. He said, "The Caliph Awwal and the Caliph Thānī are drinking, what's the harm in drinking a little?" He also drank. So this custom started from there. So, anyway, when he was forbidden, he had to stop. And for this reason, this is the prohibition. So don't fall into the illusion that the word haram has not come. This is wrong. One should not fall into illusion. So, anyway, one has to stop from these five things. And in intoxicants, these are the things. And other intoxicating things, you will say, "What about... tobacco..." Oh, tobacco, today they are saying cancer, cancer. Hey sir, they are saying cancer. Our Prophet, 1400 years ago, had said that this is a cancer for your soul. Now why are you concerned about the cancer of the body? This is a cancer for your soul. If you smoke a pipe, you will be destroyed. If you smoke a cigarette, your heart will burn. And if you do anything, you will be ruined. What was said was said, it is a line on a stone. No, sir. "We... we are permitted to smoke a cigarette. And for that, we have this... and our fast is accepted from this." "The next day, you can fast." You should ask. "What is the connection between fasting and a cigarette?" "But if you smoke a cigarette, you can fast." What could be more foolish than this? And "My mind starts working. My mind starts working, this factory, from what?"

In the context of Tawhid Rabb al-'Alamin (the monotheism of the Lord of the worlds), I had explained to you what the Tawhid of Iman (faith) is. Tawhid is the name for Tanzi'ah (transcendence) and Tajrid (abstraction). Tawhid is to keep the Khutut 'Ali (high lines) and Khutut Dani (low lines) within their respective limits. Tanzih is to purify Him from all Sifat (attributes), and Tajrid is to deem the attribute of creating from where there was nothing as worthy only for Allah Ta'ala. To perform these three tasks is what? It is Tawhid. And what has the 'Alam-e-Islam (Islamic world) or the world done? They have accepted a Dair-e-Khuda (realm/temple of God). In this regard, I had presented before you Shirk (polytheism), Kufr (disbelief), Irtad (apostasy), and all these things. The real matter is that a materialist who keeps an eye on matter, the way he views the world, if you were to sit and examine it in that way, you would find that there are only two... there is only one ideology that leads to Allah Ta'ala. What is it? That Sabab (cause) and Musabbib (causer), Athar (effect) and Mu'aththir (effector), 'Illat (cause) and Ma'lul (effect), cause and effects, we measure the world by these. And... by this, we examine that in order to see the conditions of the world, that every thing has an effect, and it has a cause. There is an effect, and it has a Mu'aththir (effector). Or there is an 'Illat (cause), and it has a Ma'lul (effect). If there is a Ma'lul, it has an 'Illat. In this same way, if you keep examining all things... for example, you saw smoke somewhere in the distance. What did you understand? That there must be a fire there. Fire... in the same way, you saw rain, so you immediately understood its cause, that this rain came because of the clouds. And what was the cause of the clouds? They were caused by vapors. How were the vapors caused? The heat of the sun on the river caused it, and from that, the vapors rose. So in any case, from 'Illat and Ma'lul... In this way, we see that all things find their place, and we, the entire world, has understood the 'Illat, the final 'Illat, as what? And the final Mu'aththir, the one who casts the effect, they have understood that as God. And as I told you, they understood the final cause as God. In this same way, if you look at numerical numbers, one, two, three, four, five, if according to these numbers, they understood one as God. Whereas one was not God, but rather, the one who counts one... the counting that happens, the counter of the counting is one... so there was a difference between 'Aad (the counter) and 'Adad (the number). And 'Aad is the one who counts, and the one who counts is God. In this same way, in 'Illat and Ma'lul, 'Illat was God, cause was God, and the Mu'aththir, the one who casts the effect... So, what they, what the world understood was this. What was the reality? That just as you consider the counter of the counting to be God, in the same way, cause and effect and whatever else, the maker of this... the one who made it is God. So, in our Tawhid and the Tawhid of the entire world, there is such a clear difference. In our view and in the view of the entire world, such a clear difference and Imtiyaz (distinction) has arisen. Are you understanding? That they call the final... the one who creates the final cause, God. They call the final Mu'aththir God. We call the one who created that Mu'aththir God. So, in this way, a clear difference has arisen between our ideology and their ideology. And I had told you, in the context of committing Shirk, that there is a Shirk-e-Khafi (hidden polytheism) and a Shirk-e-Jali (manifest polytheism). Shirk-e-Khafi, I had told you that we, just as, are afraid of something, or we watch some spectacle and we like it a lot and we don't say Subhanallah, and we like it and... some divine things, we associate them with it. If, although in our hearts we associate something or other, then this thing that we associate, what will that be? It is Shirk-e-Khafi. And what is Shirk-e-Jali? That in a completely manifest way, just as 'Isa 'alayhi al-salatu wa al-salam (Jesus, peace and blessings be upon him) was considered the son of God. Or 'Uzayr (Ezra) was considered the son of God... Jali. So, to be saved from Shirk-e-Jali, Shirk-e-Khafi, all these things... So, as I have told you, Allah Ta'ala has... al-salatu wa al-salam, for this very reason, that Allah Ta'ala, who is the Creator, the creator of the cause, the creator of the Mu'aththir, the creator of the 'Illat, the one who counts, He can never be counted, He can never be enumerated. He cannot be enumerated. That is why the Prophet of the Lord of the worlds has said what? "Man 'arafa nafsahu faqad 'arafa Rabbahu" (He who knows himself knows his Lord). The one who recognized his own self, he recognized his Lord. To recognize the Lord, if you want to, then look at your own self. If you do not find your self, you will not find God. So it became known that to look at one's own self... that is why it came in the Qur'an Sharif: "Wa fi anfusikum afala tubsirun" (And in your own selves. Will you not then see?). O people, why do you not see within your own Nufus (selves), in your own beings? The way your being has come, you do not reflect upon it. And what is the reality? I will... the series is still long... and I will tell you that this Jan (life/soul), the entire world is Anjan (unaware) of it. They are unaware of the Jan itself. It is not known what the Jan is. You will say, "Such a radiant thing, a walking, moving human being"... is because of this Jan. But the reality is that they are unaware of this very Jan. They do not know what the Jan is. So this was the Lutf-o-Karam (grace and generosity) of Allah Ta'ala, this was the Ihsan (benevolence), that... Tawhid was bestowed upon us in the correct manner, and we were connected with such Awliya' Allah (friends of God), their Daman (hem of the garment) came into our hands, because of which we were able to practice the correct Tawhid. And who are the ones who taught that correct Tawhid? Mawla-na al-Mu'minin, Hazrat 'Ali ibn Abi Talib 'alayhi al-salatu wa al-salam (Our Master, the Commander of the Faithful, Hazrat 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, peace and blessings be upon him), who, in his explanations, made rivers flow. And in his Khutbat 'Aliyat (Sublime Sermons), he decided this and he told us clearly and manifestly... So I was telling you that in reality, this entire Khalf-e-Shar (confusion), why did it happen? As the poets say, one of our... Jigar's teacher, Asghar Gondvi, his couplet is: "Lau-e-Shama'-e-Haqiqat ki... Fanus ki gardish se kya kya nazar ata hai" (The flame of the candle of reality... what all is seen from the revolution of the lantern). So they remained in this revolution. All the people of the world remained in the revolution and they understood it within the revolution of the lantern, and they could not reach the reality. And even Allama Iqbal says... "Kabhi aye Haqiqat-e-Muntazar, nazar aa libas-e-majaz mein, ke hazaron sajde tadap rahe hain meri jabin-e-niyaz mein" (O Awaited Reality, appear sometime in the garment of metaphor, for thousands of prostrations are writhing on my forehead of supplication). So what is this Haqiqat-e-Muntazar (Awaited Reality) that was awaited? What is that Haqiqat-e-Muntazar? Iqbal, too, like all the lakhs of Muslims, like a Mard-e-Mu'min (man of faith), held this ideology that when our Intiqal (passing away) happens, we will meet with Allah Ta'ala, we will meet with the Rab (Lord), and we will... that Haqiqat-e-Muntazar... But what are our distances? Now you will understand all those things and the realities will come before you, and you will find out how far this philosophy is. That Iqbal is not seeing from so close. Only one thing about him is that he was indeed a Falsuf (philosopher), a great Hakim (wise man), and he said some couplets in a strange manner. And especially, Iqbal's philosophy of Khudi (the self), as I told you, that our individuality, that... if you want to prove and state the Infaradiyyat (individuality) of God, and He is a unique being, Ahadiyyat (oneness), then He was Ahad (the One), He was Ekta (one), He created Ekta in us too, and what will be the thing that shows this Ekta? It is Khudi. So this was the philosophy that Iqbal presented. In any case, the world remained in this confusion and could never get out of it. From here, about the Dhat-e-Ahadiyyat (Essence of Oneness), various thoughts arose, various matters arose, and because of these chaotic conditions, and because of not having the correct Idrak (perception) of Dhat-e-Ahadiyyat, and because of not being Halqa-ba-gosh (subservient) to Islam, what happened? They made such an उलट-फेर (topsy-turvy mess) in this matter that they became atheists. They went towards atheism and became Mulhid (heretics) against God, they began to do Inkar (denial) of God. They said that Maddiyat (materialism) is everything, this matter is everything. So, I am telling you how the world is being corrupted, and we are becoming the cause, Muslims are becoming the cause of its corruption. They did not guide correctly. And they did not tell them in the right way. Otherwise, if they had been told in the right way and guided in the right way... they did not want to see, nor did they want to tell, whatever you may think. In any case, they were to remain astray, and astray they became. So I was saying that to know the reality of that Lord of the worlds is among the impossibilities. And it is such a thing about which the Prophet, 'alayhi al-salatu wa al-salam, has clearly stated: "Idha balaghtum ila Allah, fa-skutu" (When you reach [in thought] to Allah, then be silent). When you reach Allah, thinking, then be silent, be careful. You are not to walk here, O Salik (traveler), O one who walks, stop. Now your step will not move forward, and you become silent. For the Dhat-e-Ahadiyyat, you just acknowledge this much, that He is... he taught to call upon Him, he taught us to understand, in what manner we should call upon Him, in what way we should call upon Him, what was taught? "Shahid Allahu annahu la ilaha illa hu" (Allah bears witness that there is no god but Him). Allah has given witness that there is no Ma'bud (one to be worshipped) but... Remember this. Never forget this verse, that "Shahid Allahu annahu la ilaha illa hu." I told you that generally the meaning that is given to this, the meaning that is given, what meaning is given? That Allah has... Waraq (paper/leaf) except Allah. And this statement cannot be correct. For this reason, that Allah Himself should give His own testimony... अरे (hey), a testimony is one that someone else gives. Should one give one's own testimony for oneself? You will say, "It was the Dhat-e-Ahadiyyat, it was the being of Allah Ta'ala, and it was the matter of that Lord of the worlds"... But despite that, the matter does not settle. So the one who gives the testimony, among the beings created by him, the highest being is the one who gave the testimony and said that there is no Ma'bud... And how did he give the testimony? He said "Hu" (He). So just as he said "Hu," we also have to say "Hu," we also have to point with just "Hu," which our... what name did he use to refer to it? Mubdi'. He referred to it by the name Mubdi' or Ghayb al-Ghuyub (the Unseen of the Unseen). He gave them two words, to them... to us, for understanding. It is not its name. What are its names? Those are the ninety-nine names, the ninety-nine names that have come in the Qur'an Sharif. And from those same attributes... In reality, what happens from a name? As I have explained, it is that by which a thing is recognized. The manifestation of God are those ninety-nine people who, in reality, are His created beings. They have become Raziq (the Provider), they have become Qadir (the Powerful), they have become 'Alim (the Knower), whom we call 'Alim-e-Mutlaq (the Absolute Knower). Otherwise, what will happen? It will become Shirk. If we consider that Lord of the worlds to be 'Alim-e-Mutlaq, then we too are a little knowledgeable, even if it is 1% so. But we are. We are also knowledgeable and He is also knowledgeable. For this very reason, look, the knower of the unseen... "Ma ya'lamu"... Allah Ta'ala who is... in the Qur'an Sharif it is clearly stated that no one is a knower of the unseen except Allah. Right? No one is a knower of the unseen except Allah. When no one is a knower of the unseen except Allah, then why did Allah Ta'ala say this, "Wa al-rasikhuna fi al-'ilm" (And those firm in knowledge). And those people know who are firm in knowledge. So it is known that there are some people of Allah who are indeed knowers of the unseen. So when they are knowers of the unseen, then it is obvious that this statement which is generally made is not correct. The knowers of the unseen are intermediary beings. They are Wasita (intermediaries). And the details of those Wasita will come before you. And I will tell you how those Wasita are, how the knowers of the unseen are, how they are Wasila (means), how the Ahl al-Bayt are... But I am telling you this, that the Lord of the worlds, from His grace, from His generosity, from His munificence, did this, that the need was that His... Now you will say, "Was he in need of servitude?" From our perspective. Meaning, it was such a necessary thing that His servitude should happen. That is why it came in the Qur'an Majid that... "Ma khalaktu al-jinna wa al-insa illa li-ya'budun" (And I did not create the jinn and mankind except to worship Me). We have not created the jinn and the ins (humans) except for His 'Ibadat (worship). So it is known that His 'Ibadat is the Ghayat (ultimate purpose), it is the essential thing, and it is the intended Maqsad (objective). So this thing, you should tie it in a knot, that the purpose for which the Lord of the worlds has created is His 'Ibadat. So for His 'Ibadat, for His 'Ibadat, what did He do? He created everyone, the jinn and the ins, everyone. Now, if you consider that all the Muslims of the world... this Qur'an... those who believe in the Qur'an, who interpret this to mean that He did not create the jinn and ins except that... Allah Ta'ala, for His own 'Ibadat. Now, before them, I will present one verse, and they should explain its meaning. That verse is, "Ma tara fi khalqi al-Rahmani min tafawut" (You do not see in the creation of the Most Merciful any inconsistency). Is there anyone who will translate this? "Ma tara fi khalqi al-Rahmani min tafawut." Allah Ta'ala says, "O... O Prophet," or it is an address to all Muslims, "O people of faith..." He has already said that the jinn and the ins are for His 'Ibadat. He has said this first. And after that, he says, "Wa ma tara fi khalqi al-Rahmani min tafawut." That in the creation of the jinn and the ins, O people, you will not see any Tafawut (discrepancy). And the situation is that jinn are hidden and ins are manifest. The Qur'an came upon humans, prophets came, the book came, everything came. And for the jinnat, we don't even know what came. The Surah Jinn, however, is present in the Qur'an Sharif. Is it? Do you people meet with the jinn? You will say... to meet with humans is a blessing. A person meets another person, but the heart rarely meets with anyone. So here itself... so what will we do by meeting the jinn there? What kind of love is going to increase? But you see this, that when this Tafawut... Allah Ta'ala says that there is no Tafawut. So it is a challenge to all of Islam. Just bring it... the meaning of this verse. আরে (Hey), we see Tafawut. An extreme amount of Tafawut. Someone is up, someone is down, someone is small, someone is big, someone is tall, someone is fat, someone is thin, someone is black, someone is yellow, someone is white, someone is... someone is in a state of cold, someone in a state of heat, someone has some condition, someone has another condition... अरे (hey), there are thousands of Tafawut. There are thousands of Tafawut. In the children of one set of parents, there is Tafawut among the children. There is Tafawut among all the children who are born. In twins... Now what more can you take than this? So the creation that has been born, the Makhluk (created beings) that are there, Allah Ta'ala says you will not see any Tafawut in the Khilqat (creation). This is Allah's claim. And the claim we are seeing, what are we seeing? Are you all understanding? Are you getting it? That he will not see any Tafawut. And the Tafawut is that someone is thin, someone is fat, someone is wealthy, someone is a pauper. Look at the condition of some, they don't have enough to eat. Look at the condition of others, it is so abundant that it is beyond description, that he doesn't even have time to count it... Look at the condition of the Agha Khan. A lot... there are many in the world. Look at the condition of the Amir of Kuwait. So it is known that the Tafawut is immense. And there is so much Tafawut that it is beyond description. And this is Allah Ta'ala's claim. So how can this claim be true? Are you understanding? So the claimant is Allah Ta'ala and the verse is revealed in the Qur'an. "Ma tara fi khalqi al-Rahmani min tafawut." That you will not see any Tafawut in the creation. And we are seeing that there is immense Tafawut, a great deal. And there is so much Tafawut that it is endless. So then how is this? It should also be that our... and Allah's word will remain foremost. Why would it not? Because Allah Ta'ala is saying it. And how can it be wrong? "Sadaqa al-Sadiqin" (The truthful have spoken the truth), "Sadaqa al-Qa'ilin" (The speakers have spoken the truth). How can it be wrong? What was it? That Khilqat (creation) is the one which He created... that is a Ruhani Khilqat (spiritual creation), which I am beginning to mention. In that Ruhani Khilqat, you will not see any Tafawut. That Lord of the worlds created from where there was nothing. From a non-existent non-being. Meaning, if you describe even nothingness, that there is something in its result which is... a non-existent being, and it is not existent. From a non-existent being, Allah Ta'ala created. How many did He create? Two, four, eight, ten, a thousand, twelve... how many? Countless, innumerable. He created innumerably, with abundance. How did He create? He created Ashbah (forms), He created Qudsani (holy ones), He created 'Aql (intellect), He created Nafsani (souls). He created countless ones. You cannot count even its thousandth or lakhth part. আরে (hey), counting the hairs on the head, even for that... for those ancient jungle dwellers, it would have been a difficult matter. Today you can define an area and count the hairs. So can you... an हिस्सा (part) and count it? This is Allah Ta'ala's claim. For this, what claim is He making? And he is stating this very thing: "Wa ma ya'lamu junuda Rabbika illa hu" (And none knows the soldiers of your Lord except Him). Allah's army... this... who is this army? We ask the Muslims. The Muslims give this very answer, that... these are the Muslims. They are Allah's army. We have become Allah's army. Neither a sword in hand, nor a pistol with us, and ready to fight, and "junud" (soldiers). Allah Ta'ala says they are an army. And this is the state of the army. And its census does not happen? Hey, every country has its count, its census is done. So it is known that that 'Alam-e-Ruhani (spiritual world), that 'Alam-e-Qudsani (holy world), which were Nufus (souls), Ashbah (forms), were spirits... understand this, all this is for understanding. I am telling you, otherwise the words... spirit doesn't fit correctly. Understand Ashbah. Understand shadow. Understand Nafs (self/soul). Understand 'Aql (intellect). That is why they say in the Du'a for it, "'Aqlan kullun, Basaran kullun." That they, from head to... just as we are sitting with a body, if you did not have an eye, would you see? I put my hand over your eye... for a long time your eye has done the work of seeing. Now you give the command, you are the king of this kingdom of the body, you just give the command to your hands to see a little. Will your hands see? They cannot see. Those who were there were made entirely of eye. They were made entirely of nose. They were made entirely of hands, senses. They were made entirely of 'Aql. Such Ashbah were created, in which there was not even a... that there should be a difference of 19-20, it is not so. They were all identical. They had one quality, one nature, one essence, one... of one kind. They were 'Aql, they were Nafs, they were Shibh (likeness), they were Qudsani, they were Ruhani. They were Zat (essence). And the Zawat (essences) were separate. How many were there? ... there were no groups, no tribes, they had no community, no name. They were created countless. It is not that one group was created at one time, and after that Allah Ta'ala... If He had created again, He would not remain God. Now you will say... this is a long discussion. If He had created again, He would not remain God. For this reason, that... na'udhu billah (we seek refuge in Allah), God would become a tyrant. You created them first, and those who came later say, "O Allah, how did you create these first, and why did you create us later? You are a tyrant." Na'udhu billah. So just as today the Muslims... that regarding Hazrat Adam, Allah Ta'ala says, "La taqraba..." addressing Janab Adam and Hawwa (Eve), "La taqraba hadhihi al-shajarah... min al-qawm al-zalimin" (Do not approach this tree... lest you be among the wrongdoing people). If not a hundred, then at least fifty. If not fifty, then at least five. Five should have come out. Why did one come out?" This has to be explained. Why did one come out? For example, you should conceive of freedom. Freedom... conceive it. It's a bit difficult. Conceiving of freedom is not easy. Conceive of freedom. That you are completely free. How will you conceive this? For example. For instance, if you are made free, then it will be seen what is what and what is not. A person came to Hazrat 'Ali and said, "O 'Ali, am I free or am I compelled?" He said, "Lift one foot." Look, he was a Bedouin, but it was Mawla-e-Ka'inat. He said, "Lift one foot." He lifted it. After that, he said, "Now lift the other foot." He put that foot down and lifted the other. "No, no," he said, "lift the other foot while that foot is still up." He said, "Sir, how can I lift it? I will fall." He said, "You are this much free and this much you are compelled." This was freedom and compulsion. Did you see? This is the lesson of freedom and compulsion. So here too, conceive of freedom. And to explain the concept of freedom, I will give you an example. For instance, you see the railway tracks. On the railway tracks, there are two tracks, completely parallel, placed before you. And on both tracks, you place engines. Of the same weight, same pressure, and same thing. The same, not even a particle's difference should be there. The fuel should also be put in equally. The same weight, the same pressure, the same matter. And you start both of them there at the same time, on the same line. What will happen? How will the two go? They will go parallel, or will one go ahead? It won't go ahead. Why won't it go ahead? They have equality. It's not equality. The real matter is that one should go forward and one should fall behind. This is what I want. But it won't go. They will both go equally. Why? Because you have tied their feet, sir. If you had freed their feet, you would have seen that one goes ahead and one falls behind. Did you understand? You have tied their feet with the force of gravity and all these things. Remove this force, then you will see. Similarly, another example of a gun. Take a gun.
