You know this, that your trigger, when it works, it hits with one pound or two pounds, whatever it is. That's its impact. And you have the bullet. Now you hit the bullet. As soon as you hit it, what will happen? The molecules of that bullet, the molecules that are inside that bullet, all those molecules, with that pressure, with that impact it has received, they will go together in a straight line for a mile if the range is a mile. There can never be a difference in it. But as soon as the pressure is gone, freedom is gained, you will see, one falls here, one falls there, one falls here, one falls there. So it is known that freedom is needed. Then they can move forward, they can go ahead and behind. So in the same way, there, they were created free, not slaves. Their feet were not tied. So since they were created free, whoever had the thought, had the thought. One had the thought. So what can be done about it? And if one had not had the thought, then in the world, counting would not have started from one. It's possible that it would have started from ten, or fifty, or a hundred. And you would say, "I don't understand this." But since you, from your childhood... from history, you have been seeing that counting starts from one, so it doesn't even come to your mind that counting does not start from one. That is why you count from one. So it is known that that one being, Allah's... he did Tawhid, and from Tawhid Rabb al-'Alamin, what did he do? He obtained that virtue which he had to obtain. And in that respect, what is he called? 'Aql-e-Awwal (the First Intellect). The first 'Aql. Now I will tell you what happened after this. Now the series has begun, and you will find out that this 'Aql-e-Awwal, as soon as it became 'Aql-e-Awwal, the work that it had to do, when it did that work, at that very moment, from Allah Ta'ala's side, that thing was received. What thing was received? 'Ilm-e-ma-kana-wa-sa-yakun (knowledge of what was and what will be), Qudrat-e-Tammah (complete power), and Hayat-e-Abadi (eternal life). Sarmadi (everlasting). Now Hayat-e-Abadi and Sarmadi was received, he became for ever and ever. He became active, he did not remain passive. And Qudrat-e-Tammah was obtained. And he got 'Ilm-e-ma-kana-wa-sa-yakun. You will say, "Did Allah Ta'ala throw it from behind a curtain? Did he take it out of his pocket and give it?" No. There is no need to give it. I say that you brought a sword... I go to a swordsmith and I see a piece of iron, and I will tell him, "You have to make a sword from this." He will say, "This is a piece of iron, what are you saying?" "No sir, you just see." He will do the cycle, and after doing the cycle, he will show you the sword shining before you. You will say, "How did it become shining? How did the sword get its edge?" He will say, "I have brought it out from this very thing. The result of the cycle is that the sword has been made." So did he put it in his pocket? Did he put the cycle in his pocket? Did he put the sharpness in his pocket? No, it came out from within it. In exactly the same way, those things, those powers emerged from within. 'Ilm-e-ma-kana-wa-sa-yakun was obtained, Qudrat-e-Tammah was obtained, and Hayat-e-Abadi wa Sarmadi was obtained.

This... when he was created, and the state in which he was created, the name given to that state was this: that his manifestation was upon *surur* (joy), upon *hubur* (delight), and upon *musarrat* (happiness). Meaning, Allah was in a state of happiness... and in happiness... now, you cannot apply the complete physical attributes there. And what can you even apply to God? But for our understanding, we use these words: that his manifestation was upon happiness, upon *inbisat* (joy), upon *musarrat* (delight), and Allah Ta'ala had created him with happiness, and his existence was upon happiness. Not upon *gham* (sorrow). Today, the entire *aalam* (world) of ours accepts this, that the *makhzan* (source), *mabda'* (origin), and *sar-chashma* (fountainhead) of everything is *gham*. *Gham* is considered the origin, even though it is the most useless thing. Allah Ta'ala had created upon *hubur*, upon *musarrat*, not upon *gham*. So, the Lord of the worlds created the entire world, the *aalam-e-ruhani* (spiritual world), in a state... for our understanding... what was that state (*kayfiyat*)? It was of *inbisat*, of happiness. So, the foundation of the *aalam-e-ruhani* was upon happiness, and everything was created upon happiness. And obviously, the expression of happiness that occurs, how did Allah Ta'ala express it? He created them by giving them the jewels (*jawhar*) of *'ilm* (knowledge), *qudrat* (power), and *hayat* (life). And these were the jewels in which all other jewels were contained. There was nothing of the world that was not in it. You, if you... *diyanat-dari* (righteousness), *iman-dari* (honesty), *sachcha'i* (truthfulness), *tawazu'* (humility), *inkisari* (modesty), etc., whatever words there are, whatever *akhlaq* (morals) there are, if you gather all those morals, they will fall into just three things: *'ilm*, *qudrat*, and *hayat*. So it was understood that all things were divided into these three things: *'ilm*, *qudrat*, and *hayat*. And all virtues, all happiness, all jewels, all morals were gathered into these three things: *'ilm*, *qudrat*, and *hayat*. Just as in this world, which is the abode of action, the abode of the body, the abode of God's wrath, the house of God's anger, here you will see all evils gathered into what? Three evils. And which three evils are they? Speak up. *kibr* (pride), *hasad* (envy), and *hirs* (greed). And its foundation was laid... when? In the time of Adam, alayhi al-salam. It was laid. Otherwise, in reality, its foundation is much earlier than that. But it appears to us because a chain started with Adam, alayhi al-salam, so even before that Adam, alayhi al-salam, you will find these things. How so? What came from Shaytan? *Kibr* came. *khalaqtani min nar wa khalaqtahu min tin* (You created me from fire, and him You created from clay). That I was created from fire, and Janab Adam is made of clay, he is inferior to me. This... he showed this pride. Where did *hirs* arise? When the command came in the Quran, *la taqraba hadhihi al-shajarah* (do not approach this tree), that Adam and Hawwa should not go near this tree, and Hawwa went and that fruit... and the very thing they were being stopped from, a greater desire arose to break it. And they broke it. This is *hirs*. And where did *hasad* arise? In Habil and Qabil, in the two brothers, in the progeny of Janab Adam, that one's sacrifice was accepted and the other's sacrifice was not accepted. Habil had also offered, and Qabil had also offered. Habil's, Janab Habil's sacrifice was accepted, and Qabil's was not. So what did Qabil do? He took a stone and struck him, and Janab Habil passed away. He achieved martyrdom. So this was *hasad*. So, *hasad*, *kibr*, and *hirs*—all three of these things arose right here, in the time of Adam. And these three are evils, which are called *ummuhat-e-ma'asi* (the mothers of sins). From this, all evils take birth from its womb, are born from this womb. So this is the root of all evils. This root of all evils is *kibr*, *hasad*, and... is *shirk*... and... *kibr*, *hasad*, and *hirs*. In the same way... Come... So this root of all evils is *kibr*, *hasad*, and *hirs*, which we find in this world, which the world... what is it? It has taken on *jismaniyyat* (physicality), it has taken on *maddiyat* (materiality). ...where there is a reflection, not that state, but rather it is an abode of sorrow (*gham-kadah*). The abode of happiness, and the abode of *surur*, the abode of *musarrat*, that was the *aalam-e-ruhani* (spiritual world). And the *aalam-e-ruhani* contained three things... The *aalam-e-ruhani* contained three things. And what were those things? *'Ilm*, *qudrat*, and *hayat*. Their mission was upon *'ilm*, *qudrat*, and *hayat*, and they were created. Now, the thing that remains is that the Prophet, alayhi al-salatu wa al-salam, said at one place that *jannah* (paradise) is that house where *ma la 'aynun ra'at wa la udhunun sami'at wa la khatara 'ala qalb bashar* (what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and what has not crossed the heart of man). That the Prophet says that *jannah* is that thing, that place, regarding which you... those things have not occurred to your heart, nor have your ears heard its sounds, and nor have your eyes seen those things. *ma la 'aynun ra'at wa la udhunun sami'at wa la khatara 'ala qalb bashar* (what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and what has not crossed the heart of man). Nor has it occurred to any human heart. So it is understood that there are three things that are the things of that place... Now, if you take these three things and see... that in reality, it is that this *jannah* is being mentioned which is the *aalam-e-ruhani*. Which is the greatest *jannah*. And you might ask, are there other *jannah*s? Yes, there are other *jannah*s. Just as our gaze has stopped at a certain point, we call that the sky. And if you reach there, then what you see above that, that becomes the sky for you. In the same way... ...you will have to accept that the place where you attain all comfort, all happiness, that is your *jannah*. Jannah is not what is described in the Quran Majid, that there are such gardens, such delights, such rivers, such... such trees, on which there is the Tuba tree, on which fruits... jewels are hanging in the form of... or there are fruits, and with whatever intention you take the fruit, you will get its taste. There are rivers flowing, there are young boys, there are houris. All these things that contain physicality, why were they mentioned? So that the ignorant would develop an inclination towards *jannah*. Just as for the ignorant, this is a miracle. The Prophet, alayhi al-salatu wa al-salam, and the 124,000 prophets, the miracles they performed, they were not for us. They were for the ignorant. For us is knowledge. For the ignorant are the miracles. A miracle, which is something that incapacitates, is a very ordinary thing. They are its effects. And they are its characteristics, of prophethood, which do not become the proof of prophethood. The proof of prophethood is something else. So these things they did and showed... ...the book that was presented before us, the miracles they told of, that iron in someone's hand became like wax, and birds in the air, flying, stopped at the melody of Janab Dawud, or the flow of water, flowing, stopped. These miracles that happened, or pebbles in the Prophet's hand started speaking, or trees started to prostrate, or the moon began to split, or the sun started to turn back, or a staff became a python. All these things that were, they were ordinary things. Extremely ordinary things, just as the messengers were commanded that... `kallim al-nas 'ala qadr 'uqulihim` (speak to people according to the level of their intellect), speak according to their intellect, not more than that. In exactly the same way, this was being presented for the ignorant. In exactly the same way, this scene of *jannah* that is being presented in the Quran Sharif, which Muslims are taking and swaying to, and saying that they will get houris, young boys, and this will happen and that will happen, taking these things—this is for those ignorant Muslims. It is for the ignorant. It is not for the learned. For the learned, we will have to understand what *jannah* is. So the true definition of *jannah* is what the Prophet gave: `ma la 'aynun ra'at wa la udhunun sami'at wa la khatara 'ala qalb bashar` (what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and what has not crossed the heart of man). That neither eyes have seen, nor ears have heard, nor has it crossed the human heart. So those are the delights of *jannah*. And where are they? In the *aalam-e-ruhani*. The *aalam-e-qudsani*, the *aalam-e-ruhani*, which is the world of intellects, which is the world of *inbisat*, the world of *hubur*, upon which Allah Ta'ala made the designation and Allah Ta'ala formed it and created it, He created those countless intellects in the world of happiness. He created them with *musarrat*. And how did he create them? By giving them *'ilm*, *qudrat*, and *hayat*. He created them in a passive state. He created them in a state of potentiality, not actuality. In a state of potentiality, all the intellects were created. No one was greater than another, no one was lesser than another. There was not even the slightest difference in anyone. When you have accepted that there was no slight difference in anyone, then now... everyone could think. Everyone could think. And within everyone, this capability existed that they could... accept this matter, a good matter, think about a good matter, affirm the *tawhid* (oneness) of God, accept the Lord of the worlds. This was in everyone. You will say, "Well, at least 50 or 100 should have done it, a thousand or two thousand should have done it, or there were so many, what is the matter that all of them just kept sleeping there? Not a single one woke up? No one said 'Labbayk' to the divine call? No one affirmed the *tawhid* of the Lord of the worlds? What is the reason for this?" So, our *du'at*, alayhim al-salatu wa al-salam, are explaining just this, that they didn't do it, so they didn't do it. What happened, happened. Fact is fact. And what happened? That from among all those souls, one soul reflected upon its own self. The first one. It reflected upon its own self: have I come into being by myself? Meaning, have I created myself? He said this is my powerlessness, I cannot create myself. Then he saw among his own kind, around him, the entire *aalam-e-ruhani*. And seeing it, he began to say, "Has this entire *aalam-e-ruhani* created me?" He said, "No, this is also not possible." Have I created all of them? He said, "This is an even more impossible matter." With that, the thought came: the one who created us all, me and everyone, is a third one. Who is completely untouched, separate, not among us. He is completely separate from us. He does not have these eyes, nor these ears, nor this power, nor this knowledge and power, nor does he have these limbs, nor is he from the luminous apparitions, nor from the holy ones, nor is he gentle, nor spiritual, he is not beyond reason, nor beyond senses, he cannot be contained in anything. He is separate from all of us. And He is a self-sufficient being. And that being has created us. The moment he did this, what happened to him? The passive became active. The passive became active, and what did *'ilm*, *qudrat*, and *hayat* become for him? They became exalted. They became dynamic. And they came from a passive state to an active state. And I am saying that the first relation he established... Look, listen carefully... The first relation he established was that he looked at himself. He looked at himself, and after looking at himself, he said, "Have I been created by myself? Have I come from myself?" Our *du'at*, alayhim al-salatu wa al-salam, say about this: *ila dhatihi, nisbatun ila dhatihi* (to his self, a relation to his self). This is his relation to his own self. He related to his own self... ...the first relation he established... It was said in the world that `naqsh-e-sani behtar az naqsh-e-awwal` (the second impression is better than the first). Why was this said? Because the second impression is indeed better. Did you understand? So, the second impression, what was it? It was this. So now, these two relations that were established, and he acquired *'ilm*, *qudrat*, and *hayat*, and he became the source (*makhzan*) of happiness. That happiness which he received was so great, so much, and such was the state of *hubur*, that the grace he received from *mubda'-e-ta'ala* (the exalted originator), the gift he received... that *mubda'-e-ta'ala*, which we call what? *ghayb al-ghuyub* (the unseen of the unseen). Which we call *mubda'-e-ta'ala*. Which, in the final word, we call what? *Hu* (He). That being of *huwiyyat* (He-ness)... that *huwiyyat-e-muta'aliya* (exalted He-ness) as it is called... that *muta'aliya huwiyyat*... that *huwiyyat-e-muta'aliya* gave him a *kalima* (word). The *du'at* say a *kalima*. A *kalima* is a meaningful word. But its meaning is that it's not that some Allah Miyan is sitting and a series of prophethood is continuing, and it's being given. All this is for understanding, `taqriban lil-afham` (to make it easier to understand). It is for our understanding, for speaking, but there is nothing to be done. Whatever Allah had to give, He had given it there. It was to be refined within them. Those powers were present within them, and those powers emerged. The moment the powers emerged... ...the emergence of that power is called the receiving of the *kalima*. The emergence of those powers is called the attainment of *kamal-e-sani* (the second perfection). And what was the attainment of *kamal-e-sani*? That he became filled with *musarrat* (delight). And he attained so much *musarrat*... Just see, when someone comes first in something, in some game, just ask them. 'What can I say, sir, I got so much delight.' 'Even if I get... my breath was short, my condition was bad...' ...I had to take three injections, all that. But whatever happened, happened for the best. I achieved the lead (*sabqiyat*). I became the first. And I won that prize. So, whether it's some race, or something else, or some game, in whatever thing the one who runs, look at his state and ask his delighted heart, 'You...' And this is the very first being of the spiritual world, not just the world. The very first soul, the very first *nafs* (self), the very first intellect, that is succeeding there. So, his state of *hubur*, his state of *musarrat* was such that he became filled with *musarrat*. And having filled with *musarrat*, what happened? That within him, the two relations are swimming. Both relations are present within him: *ila dhatihi* (to his self) and *ila man huwa wujuduhu* (to the one who is his existence). You'll say, 'Did this relation become a part of him?' No, it is part and parcel of it. You cannot separate it. Can you separate the shape of this stool from the stool itself? Can you? Tell me. In the material world, you cannot separate it, so what will you separate in the spiritual world? So this... this is spirituality. So when he was filled with *musarrat* and in his place, he is swaying with joy. And it is a state of *inbisat*. Spontaneity has descended. And Allah's grace has arrived. *'Ilm*, *qudrat*, and *hayat* have been received. So when he was in such a state, at that time, from among all those spirits, from among all those apparitions, from among all those holy souls, two souls... ...two souls came forward. You'll say, 'From where did they come? Were they standing together? Were they close friends? Or were they completely separate? Or did he come from that class, and this from that class?' No. There was no class, nor this, nor that, nor that. Nothing. Just understand that two souls arose. If you say 'place', then location comes. If you say 'time', then era comes. If you say 'state', then attributes come. So there are no attributes, no place, no time, nothing. What is there? Two souls arose. And both souls, at the same time, saw his intellect. This one that arose, how did he arise? He arose by himself, for himself. He arose without a teacher. He arose without a guide. He arose without anyone giving revelation. He arose without anyone giving a sign. Oh, his glory was something else. Individuality was individuality. Oh, it was a commotion, a commotion. And can anyone even describe its state? Oh, can any era contain it? Oh, can any writer even write about it? The Quran would sway over it. Allah would be sacrificed for it. He became Allah. Are you understanding? He became Allah. The one about whom one is bewildered, the one for whom one yearns, is called Allah. Oh, that *huwiyyat-e-muta'aliya* (exalted He-ness)... ...no one knows it, no one recognizes it, there is no yearning, no bewilderment, no knowing, no coming. Our feet are broken, everyone is tired. The mind has sat down. One cannot go there, cannot reach there. The matter is finished there. This is everything. This one has become God, has become the God of the time, has become Allah. He has become God. And he is swaying in his place. And watching his state were two souls. You'll say, 'Why not three? Why not four? Why not eight?' They just weren't. What will you do about it, that only two arose? No soul arose from among them. And the two souls started to watch. There were two souls, two *nafs*, two apparitions. They, who were created... ...innumerable, countless. From them, only two arose. Only then did one and two happen. Two arose. And what did the two do? They saw this one and seeing him, they began to say, 'What a light! What brilliance! What splendor! What *surur*! What a state!' Are you seeing? Just as in our case, if someone comes wearing a new garment, then... we are stunned, and everyone's gaze starts to circumambulate them, thinking, 'From which shop was this beautiful thing bought?' So it's exactly the same state. That from where has this *musarrat* come? The state of both was such that both had made this one their target. Both had made this one their center. They had made this one the Kaaba of their gazes. And they were swaying, having made it the Kaaba, and were looking at it. But in their looking, both of their gazes slipped. One's gaze took the lower relation (*nisbat-e-adna*), and one's gaze took the higher relation (*nisbat-e-a'la*). Because the lesson was such: the higher relation and the lower relation. Because of this, what happened? One's gaze went to the lower relation. The other's gaze went to the higher relation. Are you understanding the matter? What the First Intellect (*'aql-e-awwal*) had laid the foundation for, the impression it had made, the effect it had left—that is, of `ila dhatihi`—that was its lower relation. Towards this lower relation, one went. And towards the higher relation, another went. Or you could say, one saw the conduct (*sirat*), and one saw the form (*surat*). One saw the light, and one saw the cause of the light. One saw the form, one saw the conduct. One saw the external, one saw the internal. Are you understanding? So, there was a clear difference in the gazes of both, a difference of heaven and earth. The one whose gaze was the highest... ...whose gaze was on the cause, 'What is the cause of this light?' 'What is the cause that this *inbisat* has descended upon it? What is the cause that it has become luminous? What is the cause that *'ilm*, *qudrat*, and *hayat* have manifested in it? What is the cause that it has become active?' 'What is the cause?' The one who was reflecting on this was superior to the one who was reflecting, 'How luminous it is!' 'How holy it is! What a form! What a state!' This was the difference between the two. The one whose vision was lesser, was lesser. The one whose vision was higher, was higher. Are you understanding? The one whose vision was higher, was higher. The one whose vision was lesser, was lesser. Now, obviously, here, no thing was an obstacle. Who became their teacher? See, the first person, whom we call the *mubda'* (originator), the *'aql-e-awwal* (first intellect), whom we call the *nafs* (self), whom we call the *lawh* (tablet) and *qalam* (pen)... ...so this person, who was the first, what had he done? He had done it by himself, for himself, without a guide, without a teacher, without a master. And how were these two? Who was their master? The First Intellect. Oh, that first being had become their master. They had become disciples by looking at him. And these two became disciples, but there was a big difference between the disciples. One took the lower relation, one took the higher relation. You'll say, was someone stopping them, holding one's hand saying 'take the lower relation', and holding the other's hand saying 'you take the higher relation'? No. Whoever wanted what, took it. As one wishes, one takes. Oh, both could have taken the higher relation. But they didn't take it. What can you do about it? By not taking it, what happened? One mistake costs a hundred years of piety. Do you understand? So now, this state of theirs, in this state... it is as if two horses are running, one horse has moved ahead, it has taken the lead. And the two horses that are coming behind it, those two horses, by the time they reach the target, what happens? One moves ahead and one is left behind. One moves a little ahead, and one is left behind. And the one who moved ahead was ahead, and the one who was left behind was behind. Now, these two, which are intellects, what do we call them? The Second Intellect and the Third Intellect. Or we call them *mub'athayn* (the two sent forth). *Mub'athayn* in Arabic means 'the emerging ones'. Those who emerge by seeing someone are called *mub'ath*. To be a *mub'ath* is to emerge. Seeing the First Intellect, they were becoming *mub'ath*. These two were emerging, and for this reason, they are called the two *mub'athayn*. These two were *mub'ath*, but in becoming *mub'ath*, what was the state? That the higher relation and the lower relation, or the *ashraf* and *adn* relation, was established. The higher relation was in its place, the lower relation was in its place. Now, here, they were given complete knowledge, they were given power, they were given strength, they were given everything. There was no need to ask for anything. If there was a need to ask, then the one who bestows, Allah Ta'ala, would not remain God, and these who ask would not be beggars. Neither were they beggars, nor was He the giver. There was nothing, in its place. They had to understand, and especially who had to understand? The one with the lower relation. He had to understand that this companion of mine is greater than me. But this did not happen. Look, understand this properly, well. This is a very big point I am settling. This matter, that both had emerged, and the second one had to understand that my companion is greater than me, and I am lesser. Why? No one needed to tell him. He understands it himself. He himself has knowledge, he himself has power, he himself has eyes, he himself has a self... ...he himself has a hand, he himself has a foot, he himself has sight, he himself has vision. There was no need for anything. He had to understand it himself. But he did not understand. And by not understanding, what happened? 'No. I and he... we are both equal.' This thought came that my companion, I and he are both equal. This is what is called, 'He fell, but kept his leg up'. And when they fall, what do they say to save their strength? 'Even the best horsemen fall in the field of battle.' But what happened here? He fell, and this is the matter of keeping the leg up. And now, this is an example, to explain. But anyway... ...what happened there? That he had to understand, he had to think, his power of perception was perfectly fine. And there was no need for anyone to explain it. He would have understood himself. But he did not understand. By not understanding, he said, 'No. I am his equal.' The illusion of equality (*wahm-e-musawat*) arose. The illusion of equality arose. He considered himself on the same level. 'We are both equal.' 'We both rose at the same time. We are students from the same school, and we are indebted to the same teacher.' The moment he thought this, evil was created. Did you see? Why did Allah Miyan create Shaytan? So that we do all these bad deeds... Did you get the answer? Now you won't say Shaytan. Why did Allah Miyan create Shaytan, that all the evil came into the world? If this Shaytan didn't exist, he wouldn't tempt us, and we wouldn't have to seek refuge from him, and we wouldn't do these troublesome things, and all the chaos and corruption of the world wouldn't exist. There would be no hijacking, nor any other thing. Nothing would happen. All evil would be finished, and he would have been... [unclear]. So this, sir, is the foundation of evil. Are you understanding? Where is evil being created? Evil is being created here, in the assumption of equality (*zann-e-musawat*). The moment he presumed it, evil was created. Evil was created. Now, see, this evil that was, this evil became the foundation, it became the source, and this evil, everything... it became the source of evil. And this is the storage of evil. Where? With whom? With the Second *Mub'ath*, or the Third Intellect. Now, the one who was the Second Intellect, that Second Intellect was very exalted, and in his own view, he was very high, he had gone towards the higher relation. And as soon as he had to do the work, he did it. The giver's hands are large. And He never stopped His hand of generosity. He bestowed generosity upon him. And what was that? That the same thing was placed in him. Just as Allah Ta'ala here gives every child the potential and creates them, 'You bring forth your potentials. If you want to become an educationist, become one. You want to become a certain thing, become one. You want to become a poet, become a poet. You take training in a certain thing, you become that thing.' 'As you wish to become, so God is. As one is, so is the other.' Are you understanding? How is God? As one is, so is the other. And as you wish to become, you become. So, as God had made him, there, this one who was to become, what did he do? He made himself in that way. And as soon as he did that work, which the First Intellect had done first, his master, the guide, had shown him... now, 'showing' doesn't mean he was sitting and teaching him, or the master came into his class, or... No, not telling... He learned from him, so he became the master. He became the disciple. So he became the master, he became the disciple. He became the first, he became the second. And two had risen, but one succeeded. And as soon as he succeeded, Allah's hand of generosity could not stop. And what happened to him? He became active. He got *'ilm*, *qudrat*, and *hayat*—all three things. He too attained knowledge of 'what will be', he got complete power, and he got eternal and everlasting life. He became eternal. And as soon as he got these three things, what happened? The same world of happiness came to be, but that happiness could not be attained which the First Intellect had. The being of the First Intellect is different, its happiness is different, its... to wave its flag... he is second, after all. A sort of consolation. Give them a consolation prize. In our case, they give prizes for third and fourth place, here the consolation prize started at second place. That first one had the lead. He was first, he was the first intellect, he was the pen. He became the tablet. He became second after him. He was abased, he was exalted. Now, as these things began to happen, what did the First Intellect do? As soon as the First Intellect attained perfection, the second perfection, which I call the second perfection. And similarly, he attained the second perfection, which is called *kamal-e-sani*. Now both have received it. What more is there to ask? One is called *sabiq* (the preceding one). The other is called *tali* (the following one). You understand Arabic. *Tali* means... not this *tali* (clap). *Tali* means the one who comes after. He is the *sabiq*, this is the *tali*. He is exalted, he is abased. He is the first, he is the last. He is... ...the First Intellect, he is the Second Intellect. And now, our elders explain that when two met, they started clapping. But this is a subtle hint, meaning that when the two met, they said, 'We two are enough, let's go and explain to this world...' ...to all these apparitions, to all these souls, to all these holy attributes, let's explain to them, 'Brother, why are you sitting silent? Why don't you turn towards the spiritual world? Why don't you come towards the *tawhid* of Allah? Why don't you affirm the *tawhid* of the Lord of the worlds? Let's go and explain.' The two of them joined hands. Listen carefully. The two of them joined hands—meaning, there are no hands, what hands are they joining? I am saying this to explain, `taqriban lil-afham`, there are no hands, no feet, no eyes, no limbs, no ears, no head. Oh, the two of them joined hands, meaning they came together, they united, and the two said, 'No, we have to give the call (*da'wah*).' And as soon as they started to call out, 'Come to the call of Allah.' This is our *Da'wat-e-Sharif*. Sulaymaniyyah, Ja'fariyyah, Alawiyyah, Muhammadiyyah, this *da'wah* of ours, its foundation stone was laid there. Are you seeing? Where was the foundation stone laid? You are seeing where the foundation was laid. This is the *Da'wat-e-Sharif*. Now, don't start with the *Da'wat-e-Sharif* from the common folk. Or don't start the *Da'wat-e-Sharif* from Adam, alayhi al-salam. Oh, I will show you thousands of Adams, insha'Allah. I will acquaint you with thousands of Adams. So anyway, the point is that this... the foundation of the very first *da'wah* was laid here. And when the two of them started to call out... *da'wah* means to call. You might think that a *da'wah* means being called for biryani, that is a *da'wah*. To be called to eat *halwa* in a... No. So *da'wah* is this too. And it is a knowledgeable *da'wah*, and this is a spiritual *da'wah*. This is a spiritual *da'wah*. And how was this *da'wah*? It was a holy *da'wah*. And they were called, they were summoned. And as soon as they called... ...the entire world. The two of them together. The two of them said, 'Oh, what is it, my brothers? You are our companions, you are with us. This... this is all `taqriban lil-afham`, these are not the words from there, these are not the matters from there that I am narrating. I am narrating to explain, forgive me. Those are not the words from there. That was a spiritual world. How was it... just as it happens here in the world, I am making a copy of it so that we can understand. The callers called, the summoners summoned... ...and these two did it, because it is from two that positive and negative work. Lightning flashes from positive and negative. A clap is made with two. A hand joins another hand, then there is a clap. Now the *da'wah* started, and the two of them began to call, began to summon. And when they started summoning, what was the state? First of all, on whom should the effect have been? On the third intellect. On the third intellect, whom we call what in our terminology? The Second *Mub'ath*. The effect should have been on the Second *Mub'ath*... ...it should have been influenced by it, that he should have understood first. Do you understand? Here, you brush your teeth, yes, you take the brush and brush, but only where there is dirt will it become clean. The teeth that are already shining are shining. Where there is dirt, it will become clean there. You brush all your teeth, but where there is dirt, it will be cleaned. So their purpose and aim was with that third one... ...who had laid the root of evil, who had become the source of evil, of malice. And they wanted to remove that very malice of his. They said, 'Listen, accept the divine call, accept the divine revelation, and abandon the assumption of equality.' 'This is useless, your thought. And leave all these things and come to the divine voice, affirm the *tawhid* of the Lord of the worlds, come to the relation, come to the higher relation, and save yourself.' 'Become active, you too will get *'ilm*, *qudrat*, and *hayat*, you too will attain the second perfection, so that you too become worthy of living in this spiritual world.' This was the purpose of the *da'wah*, the final aim of the *da'wah*, the objective of the *da'wah*, which is still the objective of our *da'wah* today. What is the purpose of our *da'wah*? Today, our *da'i* who is giving the *da'wah*, what is the meaning of the *da'wah* we are giving? The purpose of the entire *da'wah*... I will tell you later because right now these things are elementary, these things have not come yet, so they won't be clear. But the point is that the meaning of all these things is transformation, *tabdili-e-mahiyyat* (change of essence). To adopt spirituality from physicality. This work is being done. Spirituality from physicality. You'll say, 'What spirituality? After dying, we'll become spirits anyway.' Oh, you don't know the valleys yet. I will tell you about many valleys, insha'Allah. You will come to know... ...that even after dying, what kind of state we are in. What before dying, what at the time of dying, what after dying. This 'life after death' is just empty talk. But the real matters, I will tell you. Do you understand? And matters which your heart and mind will accept, such will be the matters. So anyway... don't be afraid of talk of death, but the thing is... ...I was talking about life. I was talking about that spiritual world, I was talking about the holy world. Death, we have imposed upon ourselves. We have left that and imposed death. So the First Intellect and the Second Intellect called, and they made countless calls. Now you'll say, did they use a loudspeaker, did they not use one? Did the voice reach everyone or not? Oh sir, there the question of reaching or not reaching doesn't arise. Everyone is intelligent, but still, some people need to be told. How many are there... ...they have intellect and everything, but despite that, you have to shake them to make them understand. Children, Allah has given them hands and feet... ...He has given them a tongue, He has given them taste, but parents have to feed them with a spoon... So anyway, the callers of the *da'wah* gave the call, otherwise they did not need the *da'wah*. They themselves should have come. But when the need for *da'wah* arose, and the callers called them... ...but the sad thing is that they are all listening... the *da'wah* that happened... ...it is not that it was happening towards some direction, towards the north, towards the south, towards the east, towards the west. No, there was no direction. It was happening to everyone there. Not a single individual was left out, not in front, not behind, not above, not below. They were all spiritual, they were holy, they were in a state of first perfection, they were given *'ilm*, *qudrat*, and *hayat*. They had to attain the second perfection. And to attain that perfection, this *da'wah* was being given, they were being called. And when they were being called, how? They were being called with great zeal and fervor. Why? Because these ones had become powerful, these ones had eaten their fill. And their souls had become rich. And they were in a state of *inbisat* and *hubur*, in a state of *musarrat*. Veils upon veils had been placed. And in this state, they were being called. They were being called with great *musarrat*. 'Come, come to the court of Allah, and affirm the *tawhid* of the Lord of the worlds.' But to affirm the *tawhid*... ...on whom was their main purpose and objective? On... ...just as parents advise all their children about dressing, wearing, writing, doing, reading, everything, but the child who is slow, the parents' attention is more on him. But it should not have such an effect on him that he falls prey to what is called an inferiority complex. So what do they do to prevent him from becoming a victim of that? They make it general for everyone. They tell all the children so that that child also gets more attention. So it was just like that. Here, the one who had become a victim of the inferiority complex was who? The Third Intellect. That third intellect was the one who had become a victim of the inferiority complex. Or you may think, 'Does the father's heir get an inferiority complex?' No, sir. We are using all these words for understanding, I am telling you. That was a spiritual world, it was not a physical world, those attributes were not physical. He needed it, but he hasn't done it, so what can be done about it? So their purpose was that he should learn, but sadly, he did not learn. But sadly, he did not learn. He was not ready to accept. And what happened? Now the entire world that they have started to call, now see how the world accepts it. So anyway... He made his *hijab* (veil), he made his helper, he made his assistant. Whom did he make? That Second Intellect. When the Second Intellect and the First Intellect met, and the *sabiq* and *tali* met, then the clapping started. Now the *da'wah* to Allah started... ...and they started to call their own kind, 'Come to the call of Allah! What has happened? You are conscious, you have understanding, you have also been given *'ilm*, *qudrat*, and *hayat*... ...you are also an inhabitant of that same spiritual world, you are seated on this pinnacle of the world, you are seated on the throne. Despite having everything, why don't you come? What is the matter? What is this lethargy? But they are sitting. Now when they started calling them, then obviously, it was their job to listen, so they listened. It wasn't that... and there, it's not like here where I say, 'Did you listen to the lesson?' 'Yes, I was listening to the lesson, but your mic was bad.' Now look, the whole mic has been broken. Because of the fear that when they ask, what will I say? Or, that what you said, those who sat in front heard it. 'What to do, sir, we were sitting at the back, we couldn't hear.' Here, people get ahead or behind, lethargy can set in. You will say, 'Sir, we've come tired from the whole day, what do you know, we haven't even eaten, we came straight here... ...now we'll go and eat.' But what... ...so there is hunger, or there is some matter of food, or lethargy, or illness, or sickness—all these things are obstacles here, but there, there was no such thing. They were not ahead or behind. They were not above or below. They were not exalted or abased. There was no order of precedence. That, 'He should go first.' 'No, sir... first the elders will go, then we will go. What should we do, sir?' There was no such order. There was an opportunity for everyone, a chance for everyone, and the caller had called everyone. And what actually happened is that they gained sense. And sense means to bind. *'aqala* means... ...as the Noble Prophet said, and taking this word from the dictionary, he said that an intelligent person (*'aqilmand*) is one who... ...first ties the feet of his camel and then protects it. If you leave the camel loose and then protect it, what kind of protection is that? So, to tie. That is why it is called *'aql*. *'Aql* means to bind. To bring yourself into a boundary (*hissar*). Allah has created you free, but you bind yourself. Bind yourself with some principles, with some morals, with some things in such a way that you remain obedient to them, you keep to your commitments. So it is understood that they did the work of the intellect, and they were called intelligent, and those intellects were called intellects. And what did they do? They said, 'Yes, yes, we accept.' But in this accepting, what happened was, just as it happens in a class, that a boy gets up and his state is such that he says to the teacher, 'I have to go drink water, I am thirsty.' So as soon as he gets thirsty... man is a social animal. Look, how many people start asking for water from the Quran? 'Sir, I have to go too, I have to go too.' Especially, look at the state of the children's classes, like KG. That they all get up. So in the same way... ...there, as soon as one person took the initiative and said, 'This is the *tawhid* of Allah, they are calling towards the *tawhid* of the Lord of the worlds, and I have accepted.' The moment he accepted... ...a group... now if you say a group, you will say, 'Was it a splinter from this side or that side, or did it come from the middle? Was it the right wing or the left wing, or did it come from behind?' That was not the case. There was no right wing, left wing, or its... there was no such thing. Whoever got up, from wherever they got up. That became a group. As I had said about the *jama'at*, you might remember, at the gathering in... that a *jama'at* is one that, however scattered they may be, in the north and south, east and west, but if they are of one creed, one way, one thought, then they are a *jama'at*. But if there is a crowd (*hujum*), a crowd, then it will not be called a *jama'at*, even if there are many of them, because they are scattered. So in the same way, those whose hearts are united... their hearts were not scattered, but their hearts were all united, and if they were of one creed, one way, then they are all called a *jama'at*. So this entire *jama'at*, how was it? That they... that third intellect... the second intellect had already been formed, you know. The first and second intellects. And this... a whole group is moving forward, following one intellect. You'll say, 'Was a monitor appointed? Was he designated there? Was it declared that this would be the third intellect?' Nothing. No one was declared, no one was made. But whoever took the initiative, whoever came forward towards the *tawhid* of Allah Ta'ala, the moment he came forward, with him... ...the steps that were taken forward, all of them became his *jama'at*. This was exactly like when an *imam* moves forward, his followers, the worshipers, move forward behind him. This is why, because this form had emerged in the spiritual world, otherwise would you ever think? You would be afraid to say such a thing, that brother... it's not understood that such a prayer as *namaz*, the worship of the One True God, and in the *namaz*... ...what is the state? That a person greater than us stands... even if he is very capable, very learned... not like the rich, that... that's not the case. So... the people who stand before you are decent people. Anyway, despite that, your conscience doesn't accept... ...that a person is praying ahead of me. After all, such a large row is being formed. How did he move ahead? Your objection is completely justified. He cannot move ahead. He cannot move ahead. But why did he move ahead? Because this form was created in the spiritual world. In the spiritual world, this form was created. The one who was to move ahead, moved ahead there. And the ones who were to follow, followed there. Whom the elders, alayhim al-salatu wa al-salam, say that `nazaru bi nazarihi` (they saw with his sight). That they too saw with his sight. `nazaru bi nazarihi` (they saw with his sight). They saw with his sight. The one whose sight met his sight, they became his followers. They became his *ummah*, they became his *muqtadi* (followers in prayer), they became those who stayed behind him, they became his worshipers, he became their... `ihtimam`... he became their *muqtada* (one who is followed), he became their *qasban* (protector). He became their leader, and he became their *imam*. Iqbal says, 'There is no *imam* in the beads of your prayer-counter (*daana-e-tasbih*).' There is no *imam* in your prayer-counter beads. That if it's a prayer-counter bead, you don't count the *imam* bead in it. They say, 'Oh, that's just for holding.' Do you understand? So this... to a certain extent of speech, it's all correct in its place. But what will they understand? What will they understand of *imam* and *imamat*? And what following are they doing? They won't understand. Anyway, whatever that *tasbih* is, to become the beads of that *tasbih*... what is that? That is from the spiritual world. In the spiritual world, the one who became the third intellect, who took the initiative, he became the third intellect. And with him, those whose gazes met, that became his circle. And how big was that circle? Uncountable. Innumerable souls. It wasn't that they could be counted... or that a tenth or a hundredth part of those who got left behind could be counted. No. They absolutely could not be counted. The third intellect moved ahead, and a circle formed with it. And what was that circle like? That... ...the 19th was above the 18th, but below the 17th. So in this way, one must count, that one above, one below. In this way, just as the order of our *masabi* is. That is why this order of *masabi* was established among us. Now, here, when you are seeing that this order has been established... ...in the same way, you will also have to understand that these, in their place, in what capacity and in what state were they established there? The capacity and state they had there, in the spiritual world, was this: that one had feet, and the other had a head. The one who was above, his foot and the one who was below, his head were joined. Are you seeing? When a circle is formed, you have to form the circle in such a way that someone's foot, your head. Someone's foot, your head. Your foot, someone's head. They were joined in this way. That is why in the world of Islam, the Prophet, alayhi al-salatu wa al-salam, established the practice of *qadam-bosi* (kissing the feet). Otherwise, the practice of *qadam-bosi* would not have come. Otherwise, Iqbal says, 'Even the *qalandar* was shamed by this, that when he bowed, neither his mind nor his body bowed before another.' But what would Iqbal know? But if we take Iqbal in this way, then he is definitely saying, 'I will say to Iqbal, you speak of 'before another' (*ghayr ke aage*), it is absolutely correct.' If you bow before another, then neither your mind nor your body will remain. But you will have to bow before your own. If one did not have to bow before one's own, then the Prophet, alayhi al-salatu wa al-salam, would not have established the practice of *qadam-bosi* himself. And he would not have said that if I were to make prostration (*sijdah*) permissible for anyone after Allah, for whom would I make it permissible? For the wife, to prostrate to her husband. That if it were so, for whom would he order to prostrate? For the wife, to prostrate to her husband. So this prostrating, or bowing, or kissing the feet, this practice that was established in the *da'wah*, it came from there. The link is from there. This is not a slavish mentality, nor is it a custom that has come from the Hindus. Get this idea out of your head. This practice that is there, it is a purely faith-based practice, which our master, our elders established, and its reason is this. By this, one is not humiliated, God forbid. Because one is not bowing before another (*ghayr*). 'Even the *qalandar* was shamed by this, that when he bowed, neither his mind nor his body bowed before another.' So what did they understand? Bowing before another. This is not before another; rather, this is before one's own. These are one's own. And those 'own' are the ones by whose sight he rose. Now you will say, 'What was the reality?' That they were happening one after the other there. If they had not happened one after the other... you will say, 'Look, the *da'wah* to Allah was happening, everyone was calling out...' '...everyone close the lesson tomorrow,' and everyone called out and said, 'Yes, close it.' Go on. How nice, everyone spoke with one voice. No, it won't happen like that. Look at the spiritual world as something very different from your own. Different. So, there, when the call was made and they were summoned, the callers, when they called, the responders, the ones who accepted the call, when they accepted... ...so when they were accepting, they were accepting in the capacity of a circle, that they were not just accepting their leader, but they were accepting the one who came before him. That the 'queue system' as it was happening... there was no queue system there, but they were establishing it themselves. So, the one who came before them, who accepted, after him you accept, he becomes your supreme leader. He is above you. His number was placed first, and you came after. Now his foot became your head. Nature arranged it so that his foot would touch your head. And this very practice, in the entire world, I will show you. Insha'Allah, when the Pure Earth, the Straight Path, and the Straight Signs and the Levels of the Imams and the Ranks of the *Da'is* come, and this world is established, and I will tell you about the physical world... ...then I will tell you how it happens and how it has remained established. Anyway, this method I was telling you, that two friends of ours have just arrived, that its link and its foundation, where was it laid? In the spiritual world. Anyway, in the spiritual world, this third intellect was established, and with the intellect, its circle was also formed. When the circle was formed, then now... ...the last member of the circle... so what happened? He... the last member became one who... when the call to *da'wah*... for example, an exam was given, in which all the papers were given... ...and your answer sheets were taken. And afterwards... you'll say, 'Now from the answer sheet, you add the students together.' 'No, sir.' ...it will come in February or January. So, just as there is a difference here, in the same way, the callers of the *da'wah*, the First Intellect and the Second Intellect, when they gave the first call... ...the group that accepted, that group is called the third intellect and its circle. Then everyone was called, and when they were summoned, what happened again? Another person arose. You'll say, 'This was a well-thought-out, a pre-planned program.' No, it was not a pre-planned program. What happened, happened. One moved forward, and a group moved forward with him. And the people who moved forward with him, that became his circle. So now, who are they becoming? The third intellect and its circle have been formed. The fourth intellect and its circle have been formed. Now... ...after that, he called again, so the fifth intellect arose, and its circle was formed. Then the sixth intellect moved forward, its circle was formed. Then the seventh intellect moved forward... the *da'wah* is happening continuously. They are being called continuously, they are being summoned, and they are coming. And their circles are being formed. So how did they become? That the... if we speak of prayer beads... ...seven prayer beads are hanging like this... one prayer bead in another, the second in the third... so seven prayer beads, as they are strung, in that way the circles kept forming. The First Intellect, the Second Intellect, then came the Third, the Fourth, the Fifth, the Sixth, the Seventh. This... these seven intellects were established. Seven and two, how many did that make? Nine. The First Intellect and the Second Intellect, and the seven intellects. But now we have to understand these intellects. That the first, the third circle that was established... ...the third intellect and its circle... so the last member of this circle, for example, let's say, this is a supposition, that if there are a thousand in the circle... a thousand souls... ...a thousand apparitions, a thousand souls, then that thousandth one was greater than whom? Than the leader of the fourth intellect. The one who was called the fourth intellect, who became the leader, he was greater than him. Similarly, the last member of the circle of the fourth intellect was greater than whom? ...The fifth. From the leader of the fifth intellect, from the one who was leading, he was greater than him. And so much greater was he... ...that his was the foot, and his was the head. His was the foot, and his was the head. The *imams* were joined to their followers. Now these circles, forming and forming, where did they end? Seven circles were formed. And above them are two. Who are they? The First Intellect and the Second Intellect. Now, there are two things to understand: that this system was established in this way, but the Second Intellect... ...at the time when he accepted the call to Allah, when he went from passive to active, from potentiality to actuality, and when, seeing the First Intellect, he created the higher relation, I have explained the higher and lower relation in great detail. So, the one whose gaze was higher, not lower, who was seeing the conduct and not the form, who was seeing the internal and not the external... ...that one, who was seeing the cause and not the effect, his gaze was higher. And that is why he became the Second Intellect, and he received *'ilm*, *qudrat*, and *hayat*. But when he established this, when he turned his gaze... when he saw the First Intellect with the higher relation, at that time, there were some souls who also became his circle. You will say, 'Then why did you leave it out?' So there are some reasons. There was a reason, which is why I left it out. But he also had a circle. You will say, 'Were those also countless souls?' No, it was not like that. A matter of coincidence. You will say, 'So many coincidences are happening!' All are coincidences. If they were not coincidences, then you could count the souls. But some souls were not counted. Innumerable. That is why Allah Ta'ala said what? That `wa ma ya'lam junud rabbika illa hu` (And none knows the soldiers of your Lord except Him). Except Allah, no one knows his soldiers. So, innumerable. But the souls that were with the Second Intellect were counted. Were they counted for a special reason? No. The people whose gazes met, they were 28. There were 28 souls, 28 intellects, 28 holy forms, *'alawi* states... souls, who had met his gaze with their gaze, and they too had become successful. So it is understood that 28 were his above, and the one who became the third intellect, under whom was he? Under those 28. Obviously, whatever the principle is, it should be according to the principle. Now, these 28 that became his, since this was the first soul... and the first soul that is... ...see, any motor that is made in a factory, or any thing that is made first, how much value it has and how it is advertised. In exactly the same way... ...this was the first soul, because the First Intellect had no circle, it was a unique being, it had distinction, and it was unique. But the Second Intellect had a circle. That is why its circle has great importance. And this important circle was how many? 28. These 28 souls that were his... ...they, for the entire world, for the remaining world, for our world, for all the worlds, and for as long as the world will last, until then, they became symbols. And the measure of everything, by which... you have a measure, a scale, with which everything is weighed, so that you can measure things with it, or weigh them. So, if all of Allah Ta'ala's things are to be measured, and if they are to be weighed, it will be from these 28. Meaning, if you take any thing in the world and start counting, it will always come out to 28. It will come out to 28. The elders have counted and shown many things. And in one of our *manasib* (rites)... ...Mawlana Ji 'Ali Khan Muqaddas was such an elder who created a rare point in this. He said that not only am I seeing the 28 mansions of the moon... ...and I am seeing the 28 letters of the Arabic alphabet, and I am seeing the *hudud* of our *da'wah* divided into 28. That there are 24 *hudud*... ...which have 24 *rak'ahs* that we pray in the east. Twelve *hudud-e-layli* (nocturnal) and twelve *nahari* (diurnal). So that's 24. And three are *ma'dhun*, *mukasir*, and the gate (*bab*). So this... ...the three that are separate are *hudud* who are in the presence of the Imam. In this way, the 28th... So the system of 28 that is running, he explained that if you take the names of the great elders... ...if you take the names of the great elders, their original names... ...many names are derived (*mustaq*). So, like 'Abd al-Muttalib... ...'Abd al-Muttalib means 'slave of Muttalib'. So in 'Abd al-Muttalib, you have to remove *'abd*... ...you only have to take Muttalib. So in this way, if you count the letters of the name properly, with health and rhythm... ...counting the letters of each week, how many will you get? 28. So you tell me... ...the names of the great elders were not thought of and kept beforehand. Even in them, you will find 28. So it is understood that all the spiritual things of Allah Ta'ala that you are hearing, and the things of the universe that are being weighed, are all based on 28. It is a system of 28. You'll say, 'Tell me about the 28 in our universe.' There is the sun and the moon. And... as... ...I said that the Prophet stated that if you put the entire universe on one side and the *kalima* on the other, the *kalima* will weigh more and the universe will not. So this *kalima*... ...even in it, there are 28. Why? How are there 28? *La ilaha illa Allah*. First *la ilaha* is negation (*nafi*), and the second is affirmation (*isbat*). And if you want to see three things in it, alif, lam, and ha. It is made of these three letters. These are its three jewels. And if you want to see four, then *la*, *ilaha*, *illa*, *Allah*. These are the four places where our pen breaks. And if you count its disjointed letters (*muqatta'at*), they come out to seven. In *la ilaha illa Allah*, if you count, they come out to seven. And if you count all its letters, you will get 12. So 12, 7, 4, 3, and 2, if you add them up, it becomes 28. The entire universe is based on this 28. Six directions... you see... four... east, west, north, south... ...sun, moon, and if in this way... day and night... everything will come out as two, or three, or four, or seven, or twelve. So in this way, things will start to happen. So the reality is that its link is where? Its foundation was laid there. The foundation stone is there. So the foundation of 28 was laid there. And there, these 28 of Allah Ta'ala were, which are called *Hazirat al-Quds* (the sacred enclosure). This is called *Hazirat al-Quds*. A special name was given to this circle. The elders gave it for some reasons, which, insha'Allah, you will get in due time. It is called *Hazirat al-Quds*. Anyway, so I was saying that the First Intellect happened, the Second Intellect happened, its circle of 28 was formed, then the third happened, the fourth happened, the fifth happened, the sixth, the seventh happened. And these seven and two together, how many did that make? Nine. Nine intellects have arisen. But everyone got intellect, but the third one, whose relation was not higher but lower, was...

The one who was looking at the form, looking at the apparent, was not looking at the inner character, and the one who was looking at the effect and not looking at the cause, who was he? The Tenth [Intellect]. That was the third intellect, which you may call `munba'ith-e-awwal` (First Emanation) or `munba'ith-e-thani` (Second Emanation). `Munba'ith-e-thani`, `munba'ith-e-awwal` became the second intellect. Now, of the two that were to rise and emerge, the one that was left behind as a laggard, that remained last, is standing in its place. So, the entire world became illuminated and radiant. If anyone remained, who was it? Only one intellect remained, but with its circle (`dā'irah`). With its circle. Who is the circle? Did someone draw a circle there? I have said, and I say it repeatedly, that no circle was drawn. `Nazarū bi-nazarihi` (They saw with his sight). Those who thought along with him, who met his gaze, they were the ones in his circle. And who were those in the circle? Countless souls (`nufūs`). There were countless souls, for whom there is no limit or count. For his companion, 28 emerged. After that, it could have been 29, 30, 32, 35, but it did not happen like that. It happened as it happened. There were 28 there, but with this one, there were countless; what can one say? And among those countless ones was also our countless one. We were also there. We were also sitting in that circle. We were also in that same circle. He said, "I don't accept," so we also said, "When you don't accept, we certainly don't accept." Simply like this. They bowed their necks, so we too bowed our necks. They said, "No," we also said, "No." So, it's just been going on like this. Now, what will happen in the future? God alone knows. So, what will happen? We have done what we have done. What can be said about that? So, there, when he said this and gave the call to God (`da'wat ilā Allāh`)—who? The First Intellect and the Second Intellect. So, the one who did not accept, who was he? The previous ones had accepted. The one who did not accept was that third intellect. If he had been successful, he would have become the second. And if he had not been that successful, he would have at least become the third. But he became neither the second nor the third. And at the very least, he would have taken some place—he would have become the fourth, the fifth, the sixth, the seventh. There were chances, but nothing came of it. Until what happened? Now the nine intellects came, their circles were formed, and all of them became pure and clean. From passive to active, they became active. `Kamāl-e-thāni` (secondary perfection) came, `'ilm`, `qudrah`, and `ḥayāt` (knowledge, power, and life) were granted to them. They became `azali` (pre-eternal), `abadi` (post-eternal), `nurani` (luminous), and `qudsani` (holy). They became part of that realm and became the splendor of God. All of them became eternal and successful. Now who was left? That `'Aql al-'Āshir` (Tenth Intellect). That intellect to which intellect did not come, and with it, us. All of us people. And how many were we? Countless and limitless. We were innumerable. Countless. And we were also not… we were also not ready to accept. Now what happened? There, all these people who were calling, who were inviting, then here, where there are slow people, who are, you know, students who study less, you see the teacher pays more attention to them. He scolds them more, and he tries harder to explain and teach them. So in the exact same way, more attention started to be paid to us. Whose attention? That of the First Intellect and the Second Intellect. It happened, and the call became continuous (`mutawātir`). Not just once, but they began to call continuously. They began to call again and again. And they began to call in such a way, just as we read the Holy Quran where? Standing in prayer. And we recite Surah al-Hamd. Without Surah al-Hamd, the prayer is not accepted. And in Surah al-Hamd, which verse? `Ihdināṣ-ṣirāṭal-mustaqīm` (Guide us to the straight path). Meaning, O Allah, guide us on the straight path. Guide us, O Allah, we are on the straight path. We are standing on the straight path, praise be to God. You are a follower of the Sulaymani, Ja'fari, 'Alawi, Ismaili path. You believe in the true religion (`dīn-e-ḥaqq`). Then what is it? You have achieved everything. But then why do you need to read `Ihdināṣ-ṣirāṭal-mustaqīm`? Brother, by just standing on the straight path, the destination is not reached. To stand on the straight path, one also has to walk. One has to reach the destination. It won't happen just by taking a covenant (`aḥd`); after taking the covenant, one must also uphold the covenant. One must also fulfill the condition. So one will have to walk. That was the situation. And what was the condition? That there, we were not ready to take the covenant, nor were we ready to walk. Meaning, not ready to listen. Not ready to listen. And who were we looking at? That third intellect. We were looking at that third intellect, who was of a lower (`adnā`) level, and we were listening to what he was saying. Now, the situation was that while listening to that third intellect, what happened was that those of us who were sitting, they say, you know, what is gained from sitting idle? So some people, what do they do? They even keep a book in the bathroom to read. That is, the etiquettes of that place, you should read them properly. `A'ūdhu` should be read. Without reading it, you cannot even say Bismillah. So first, `a'ūdhu` is to be read, and then Bismillah. That is why with us, first are the etiquettes of entering the lavatory, after that come the etiquettes of the mosque. It was understood that first is purification (`ṭahārat`). And you are going to perform purification, and you are reading. This is not right. Or you are lighting an incense stick. Here. Is there a place for lighting something? The place for this fragrance is here. There, you should just put phenyl. So, since this precedent has been set, I say that we should refrain from this. In such a place... because what do they call `'adl` (justice)? What do they call `zulm` (injustice)? `Waḍ' al-shay' fī ghayri maḥallih` (Placing a thing in its improper place). If you place a thing in its wrong place, it becomes an injustice. If I put this hat on my feet, then you will say, "Sir, what is this?" You are putting the hat on your head. You placed the hat on your head, that was justice (`'adl`). If you put it on your feet, it became an injustice (`zulm`). So, whatever thing is meant to be somewhere, it should be there. Not everything fits everywhere. So, the etiquettes of a place... understand? That... and whoever has these etiquettes, may they be blessed. But these are not our etiquettes. These are not our etiquettes. We have to cover our head and go. You will say, "Sir, do we cover our head to go to the bathroom?" What can I tell you? There are underlying reasons (`'illah`) for this. There are many underlying reasons. If I get the chance, God willing, I will explain this too. There are many underlying reasons. Without some wisdom (`ḥikmah`), nothing has been established. So, anyway, what I was saying was that there, when that third intellect and its circle did not accept, what happened? While sitting, while sitting silently, a thought occurred to them. What was the thought? Some of the people among those who were refusing, they started to reflect on their refusal and said, "We should refuse with more intensity (`shiddat`)." Someone did not. Someone said, "No, we should refuse with intensity." And what happens? The orators who are born, very great speakers are born, they are from among us. So, from among them, two or four people stood up. Not two or four, but rather two stood up, you could say. One stood up, the other said, "I will support you. I am your helper." Here. "I will support you. You please deliver a great speech." So he stood up and started to speak. On this side, Rahman was calling. On that side, Shaytan was calling. Do you see? On this side was the call of Rahman (`Raḥmāni da'wat`). On that side was the satanic call (`shayṭāni da'wat`). On this side was the call of Allah Ta'ala, the Rahmani [call], and on that side was the satanic call, the call of the master cavalier (`shahsawāni da'wat`). And how was it? Just as much force here, that much force was there. They said, "We also have power. We also have... God has also given us an eloquent tongue. We will also speak." "Go on, speak." "Speak." And here, Allah Ta'ala, meaning the First and Second Intellects, are giving the call, and here, that third intellect, whatever it did or didn't do in its place, is now sitting silently, but these two stood up. The one who stood up first is called Iblis. And the second one who supported him is called Shaytan. Now you must have understood. They say, "Allah Ta'ala..." "Sir, what a calamity this is, we don't understand this matter. If Shaytan had not been created, then all this evil would not have come, we would not have been misguided, and all these things would not have happened. It would have been best if Shaytan had been finished off. Why did Allah Miyan create him?" This is the biggest mistake that Allah Miyan has made, God forbid, God forbid, that he created Shaytan. Was he created, or did they become so themselves? They became so themselves. Allah had created them in the pre-eternal realm (`'ālam-e-azalī`). And He had made them luminous (`nurani`) and holy (`qudsani`). They became Shaytans by themselves. And in becoming Shaytan, how? They said, "No, now our claim must be greater. It should be an innovation from the servant (`bande kī ījad`)." So what is the servant's innovation? That now the refusal is this: that we will not accept that Exalted Originator (`Mubdi' Ta'ālā`), that is true, but go, we will not accept you either, nor those below you, nor anyone. We will not accept anyone. This. This intensity (`shiddat`) was created. Now this intensity was created, and they started to call in this manner, and they said... Now what happened? If a mad person stands and speaks in Hyde Park, listeners gather. If you start a new religion, you will surely find some followers. You can see the Aga Khanis, among whom there is a one-minute prayer and also a one-hour prayer. But the situation is that prayer can be done while sitting with a picture in front, but the followers accept an Imam who plays derby and drinks alcohol. But despite such things, they are blind to intellect, stones are on them, but they still accept. So it is known that people accept; in the world, everything is accepted. So anyone can take up a religion and start it. As they say, "Brother, this is such a place, here in Bombay, it's a place where any business can take off." So this also took off. It took off. It took off. So, in the same way, they started to speak. And they said, "No, we don't accept." "Go on." "We don't accept." And their words, just as people stand in the park and speak in their own tongues, here, they started to speak, and people started to listen to them. And as they listened, it started to have an effect. As the effect grew, it started to spread. As it spread, their group started to grow. And the group was already formed, but now it started to become stronger. "Go, it's absolutely, absolutely right." Now they will not accept. Now, that idea that was formed, it began to be imprinted (`murtasim`). Now the impression (`naqsh`) that was set, the second impression (`naqsh-e-thāni`) was better than the first impression (`naqsh-e-awwal`). Meaning, it started to become even firmer. Now it became firm. It became so firm, don't ask. Adamant in its place. Now what happened here? The First and Second Intellects are calling. They are calling out to countless souls, calling, continuously calling. "Look, come towards the Oneness of the Lord of the Worlds (`tawḥīd Rabb al-'Ālamīn`)." "Come towards the Oneness of the Lord of the Worlds." But now, a difference began to arise in the calling. And what was that difference? The thing is that when a person's children, their sons, become ready and come alongside them, they say, "Brother, now I want to rest a bit. I have become very tired. Whatever I had to do, I invested the capital, opened the shop, did all the work. Now you are ready, you are my right arm (`bāzū`). Go, now you manage the shop, I will rest a bit." So it is. So, just as it happens here, in the very same way, the First and Second Intellects said, "Enough is our call." They called a lot, they called out a lot. "It is better now that the third, fourth, fifth, sixth, and seventh should call, as they are now successful. They have now achieved secondary perfection (`kamāl-e-thāni`). `'Ilm`, `qudrah`, and `ḥayāt` (knowledge, power, and life) have come to them. Now there is no deficiency of any kind. It is certainly better that they call now." They should call. And the last individual (`ākhirī fard`) of the ninth intellect's circle began to call out. And he began to call. Whom? This third intellect. And he is calling countless times. Not just he is calling, but the ones above are also giving him support, and he is calling. Why? Just as the burden falls on the young one, it also fell on him. The last individual of this circle began to call them, and began to call continuously, but the non-acceptors... they were not about to become acceptors. The non-understanders were not about to become understanders. Why? That was... you will say, "Sir, was it possible?" It was possible. It was `'adm-e-khārijī` (external non-existence), it was `'adm-e-ghusānī` (deficient non-existence). There was understanding. Nothing was obstructing them. No verse had come down. Nothing was ahead or behind. They could have accepted. When everyone else accepted, there was no harm in them accepting too. But when they decided not to accept, they did not accept. And in this non-acceptance, the thing that became helpful was what? That affair of Iblis and Shaytan. The one who was first, and the one who supported him, supported him, and who had spoken at length and misguided him. And against the call of the Merciful (`da'wat-e-Raḥmāni`), the call of Satan (`da'wat-e-shayṭāni`) had begun. He gave him the contract and said, "Go on. If you don't accept, then don't accept. We will not submit to this." So now, for how long was their refusal, their conflict? The clash of the call of the cavalier/master (`shahsawāni da'wat`) with the call of the Merciful (`Raḥmāni da'wat`) has been the established order in the world to this day. `Ṣirāṭ al-mustaqīm-stīz shanār-e-bū-lahabī` (The one who opposes the straight path is the spark of Abu Lahab's nature). This has always been the conflict. The battle between good and evil will always remain. So this is from pre-eternity (`azal`). What `ṣirāṭ al-mustaqīm` and `bū-lahabī` will we see? O Iqbal, just look at how the realm of souls is. It began from there. The foundation was laid there. And what happened? And they laid this foundation, "Go, we do not accept you, nor those above you. We do not accept the Exalted Originator (`Mubdi' Ta'ālā`) either." Meaning, in their simple-mindedness, they thought they were performing a great feat. So they did not accept. And in this non-acceptance, they remained firm in their place, and a harshness (`ta'aṣṣub`) came into them. Meaning, a hardness came into their nature. And they became firm in their place and said, "We will not submit." And they took the words of the Quran, the luminous words, for themselves and upon you. And what are they? "We will not perform obedience. `Lā nuṭī'uhum` (We will not obey them). We will not obey. We will not accept." And this is what... in the court of Allah Ta'ala, their harsh... what was it? It was a reprimand, or it was the gravest disobedience that they were committing. And the Lord of the worlds, who is Merciful and Gracious, that Being was silent and watching. So how many were there? The First Intellect (`'Aql-e-Awwal`) and the Second Intellect (`'Aql-e-Thānī`). And after the Second Intellect, I had told you there were 28 souls, which we call `Hazrat al-Quds`. That circle (`dā'irah`) is small, blessed, and first. It is given precedence, which is why we call it `Hazrat al-Quds`. After this `Hazrat al-Quds`, how many were there? How many? Seven. Seven and two became nine. From these nine, the entire world had been divided. All had become pure and clean. Whether someone was ahead or behind, they had accepted. Whether one came into the ninth circle or the seventh or the sixth or the third, they were divided, and the whole world became clean. Now which world was left? That world remained. That world remained, of the third intellect, who had emerged with the seventh one, who had walked with the seventh one. Whose? With the Second Intellect. The one who emerged with the Second Intellect, he... in that, in that, the weakness he showed in his sight and his reluctance to accept the word, the `tawḥīd` of the Lord of the Worlds, he was left behind, and his group was left behind. Those who `nazarū bi-nazarihi` (saw with his sight), those who had met his gaze, all of them were left behind. Now, I had told you a little preface for the newcomers, that those who were left remaining from that group, that entire group was obeying the word of its leader.
