Meaning, once a leader is accepted, a superior is acknowledged, then people continue to follow in his footsteps. This is the established principle of the world. "We will die at whose feet? We will stumble at his doorstep." This is the way of the world. You cannot change it. A long time ago, in `alast`, we drank the cup of love; what can we do now? So, what happened there, happened. So, now, those who were following him, they followed him, and with great conviction. When he said "no," they said "no." And to strengthen this "no," to make it firm, and to give it support, what did he do? From among them, two souls (`nufūs`). That group that was with the third intellect, was of countless souls. Countless. Now you will say, "Sir, if the ones before him had 28, then after that, maybe 50 would have come out, or 49 would have come out." No, there's no question of it. They were countless. There's no point in counting. They were countless. But from among all those souls, two stepped forward. And what did they do? They tried to explain why we should say "no." To strengthen [the resolve]. It was the same situation, like, to give an example, they say that there was a fox whose tail was cut off, so it went about getting everyone's tail cut off. It's a bad example, but it's like that. Because these two had gone astray, they saw that everyone else should not reform. If they remain astray, it is good. Because their purpose was also that they remain astray. Now you will say, why did they want them to remain astray? What did they get? They got it. So they, in this way, organized and, in this way, started to call out and, in this way, started to invite, just as the call of the Merciful (`Raḥmāni da'wat`) was being done by the First and Second Intellects. Their call became a satanic call (`shayṭāni da'wat`). `Satīzah kār rahā hai azal se tā imrūz, chirāgh-e-muṣṭafawī se sharār-e-bū-lahabī` (The conflict has been ongoing from pre-eternity until today, between the lamp of Mustafa and the spark of Abu Lahab). These two are fighting each other. The struggle between good and evil, its seed, its beginning, started from there. Now, what you say, that if Allah Ta'ala had not created Shaytan, the whole affair would have ended. The very seed of the matter would have been destroyed. Evil would not have come into the world at all. But when did Allah ever create him, sir? Allah did not create him; he is self-created. An elder got so angry at the word "Shaytan" while reading the Quran, he was beating [the book], saying, "You are so wicked." Shaytan is wicked. Rahman wants to make [us] good, and here is Shaytan. He crossed out everything and wrote his forefathers' names. He said, if I write the names of the elders, it would be better. But what can be done? It's a blind following. Now, what happened there, happened. What can be done about it? So anyway, Shaytan, in his place, was giving the call of the master cavalier (`da'wat-e-shahsawāni`), the satanic call. On this side, the Rahmani call was happening; on that side, the satanic call was happening. But there too, as I said, there was one who took the initiative and one who was his supporter. The supporter is always a man of mischief, a cunning man, like 'Amr ibn al-'As. He is a man of a very strange disposition. Iblis is a rather simple-minded type; he is quick to raise his hand, but he doesn't think or understand that much. So, Iblis was... there, those who became Iblis, became. The names were not given. The names are not mentioned anywhere in our books. It was placed, the one who became, became. And the one who supported him, became. Now, just as I said, they give speeches, and where freedom is given, there all kinds of people speak, and listeners for everyone are also born. So, there were listeners for them too, and that was their entire group, because we had already said "no." They started listening to them. "Brother, they are saying the right thing. Let's go." And as they listened, the situation was that they listened with their heart. "Wow, what a great thing he said. What a great thing he said." Now, there, the First and Second Intellects, the call they had, what did they do? They handed it over to the last individual of the ninth intellect's circle. They said that it's a matter of... just like in any office, the clerks do most of the work. They say, "Sir, the director just signs. What can I do? I have to do everything." And it happens somewhat like this. They bear the responsibility, but the work, the labor, is done by the lower ones. So, the ninth intellect's circle was entrusted with this. The First and Second Intellects entrusted them with the task that "you must carry out this work." To guide them. So they started the call. And their call now became one-directional. The call was going in one direction, and they were calling, they were calling out, they were explaining. To whom? The third intellect and its circle. And they were saying repeatedly, "For God's sake, accept. Understand. Become right." And they were not ready to accept. Now, when they were not ready to accept, then they had to be called many times. Just as the First and Second Intellects had to struggle to illuminate this entire world and to explain, and to give them secondary perfection, in the same way, they also had to do it for the last individual of the ninth intellect's circle. They called a lot, they called out a lot, they explained a lot. But his voice was being drowned out. It is always the case that goodness is suppressed, and the voice of evil is very loud. You know, that is the nature of evil's voice. And Shaytan, with his full force and power... now you'll say, "Sir, how did such a satanic nature..." Allah Ta'ala does not oppress anyone. Everyone has freedom. They were also free to explain their case. They were calling equally, explaining equally, and saying, "We will not accept." When this stage began to arrive, then the third intellect, which was the `munba'ith-e-thāni`, which had seen the First Intellect with the `munba'ith-e-thāni`, if he had become successful, he would have become the second intellect. And if not, then at least he would have been the third intellect. If intellect had come to him, he would have become the third intellect. And if that hadn't happened either, then at least he would have been counted in some circle. And if he was counted, he would have become wise (`dānā`). He acted with ignorance (`nādānī`). And the situation was that now the last individual of the ninth intellect's circle, even his [call] was falling short, and but this certainly happened, that the result of that call began to be impressed upon him, and guidance began to work. Water, by dripping, began to make an impression on the stone. And he was startled and began to think about his mistake. And it is seen that when a great person makes a mistake, he does not accept it easily. Rather, he has to be approached with twists and turns to be made to accept it. And what does he do? He asks someone else, "Did I make a mistake? Did some error happen?" Now, this is called `tajāhul-e-'ārifāna` (feigned ignorance of one who knows). And what did he do? Now, those who had gone, now to ask his companion, for whom he had committed the mistake, to ask him, they wanted to ask him, but now the whole world was in between. Why? Secondary perfection had come in between. If it were the state of primary perfection, then everyone was together, no one could meet anyone. There was no question. In secondary perfection, all became... a hierarchy was established, a distance was established. One's station and another's station became high and low. A hierarchy was established. The matter was finished. So now he had to go to the last individual of the ninth intellect's circle and ask him, "Brother, what mistake did I make, and what slip occurred from me?" You understand? The last individual of the ninth intellect's circle, he asked him, "What mistake did I make, and what error happened from me?" So he said, "Your mistake was this very thing, that you did not acknowledge your superior. The sight of whose, your sight was less sublime than, and your sight was lower. You saw the form (`surat`), he saw the inner character (`sirat`). You saw the apparent, he saw the inner. He was greater than you, and you stopped acknowledging him." So he said, "But I acknowledged the Exalted Originator (`Mubdi' Ta'ālā`)." He said, "Love me and love my dog." If you are to love God, you should have also accepted the people of God. So you were ready to do `tawḥīd` of God. Shaytan, in the time of Adam, what did he do? He said, "I am greater than him." "I am the teacher of the angels, I am the one who does the best `tawḥīd`. I was the best practitioner of `tawḥīd`." In reality, he was. Shaytan was the best `muwaḥḥid` (practitioner of `tawḥīd`). The best `tawḥīd`-doer. In the very same way, he had done `tawḥīd` of Allah Ta'ala, but he had not accepted the First Intellect and the Second Intellect in the way he should have. Rather, he had accepted the First Intellect, but he had not accepted the Second Intellect. He had not accepted his superior and elder. As soon as the one who was saying this said it to the one who was saying, and the one who was understanding understood it... I told you before that there was no thing that was hidden there, or any ignorance. There was no hindrance. He himself should have understood, and he himself was understanding. Despite that, he asked. Upon asking, the one who was telling told him, he understood it. Understanding, he said... "I have certainly made a mistake. And I repent." And his repentance was presented. Now, the repentance that he presented, now the repentance has started to travel. From whom? From the circle of the ninth intellect, his repentance started to travel. The circle of the ninth intellect started to turn, that first, say, it was the thousandth, so after a thousand, it reached 999, and after that, it reached 998. Now this ladder is climbing. Climbing, climbing, it reached where? It reached the circle of the Second Intellect. And from the circle of the Second Intellect, it emerged and reached the Second Intellect. The second intellect, which was, it reached him, this repentance. `Fa-talaqqā Ādamu mir-rabbihi kalimātin fa-tāba 'alayh, innahū huwa-t-tawwābu-r-raḥīm` (Then Adam received from his Lord [some] words, and He accepted his repentance. Indeed, He is the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful). When towards the side of our master Adam, Allah sent some words (`kalimāt`). And when our master Adam took the support of those words, what happened? His repentance was accepted. Indeed, Allah is the great acceptor of repentance. That Adam was this one of ours. This third intellect is Adam. This is the first Adam. Among a thousand Adams, this is the first Adam I am telling you about. This was the first Adam who repented. And when his repentance reached, what was sent? Words (`kalimāt`). What are words? `Kalimah` means a meaningful word. Meaning, all these principles, because they had become active from passive, secondary perfection had been achieved, so all of them are now meaningful words. They are not meaningless words. They are meaningful. So these... Allah Ta'ala calls them words (`kalimāt`). He calls them `kalimāt`. So when he took the support of these words and took their intercession, and presented his repentance, then `fa-tāba 'alayh` (He accepted his repentance). Repentance was accepted. `Innahū huwa-t-tawwābu-r-raḥīm` (Indeed, He is the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful). Allah is the best acceptor of repentance. Who is the `Tawwāb al-Raḥīm`? The Second Intellect. The Second Intellect accepted his repentance. It is obvious that when the lower one accepted it, the First Intellect accepted it. When the First Intellect accepted it, then our intellect says, our heart says, our logic says, that the Exalted Originator (`Mubdi' Ta'ālā`) also accepted it. When it was accepted, the whole affair was over. And he was granted `ilm mā kān wa mā yakūn` (knowledge of what was and what will be), `ḥayāt-e-abadī wa sarmadī` (eternal and everlasting life). But a great upheaval (`qiyāmah`) occurred. The great upheaval was that the entire world became pure and clean, and after that, his turn came. And when he repented, and with his repentance, his turn came, his number was fixed. So, his own leader repented, and with him, those who had met his gaze, that entire group of his, from that group, some were wise, some were such that they had met his gaze. `Nazarū bi-nazarihi, tābū bi-tawbatihi, khalṣū bi-khalṣatihi` (They saw with his sight, they repented with his repentance, they were saved with his salvation). Meaning, they found salvation with him, they met his gaze with him, they repented with him. So, those who repented in this way, all of them became his group, and they also achieved secondary perfection. `Ilm mā kān wa mā yakūn` was granted, `qudrat-e-tāmma` was achieved, and `ḥayāt-e-abadī` was granted. Now, this group has formed. Now, this group that has been formed, we, just as we leave the seven groups as they are, we do not leave it like that, but we say that this now, which intellect is it becoming? The tenth intellect is being formed, which is called `'Āshir`. This is `'Āshir`. And the circle of `'Āshir` and the circle is called `Tābū bi-Tawbatihi`. `Tābū bi-Tawbatihi`. A certain poet has said, this couplet he wrote in gold letters on the niche and pulpit. He wrote this couplet in gold letters on the niche and pulpit, that "The ignorant (`nādāñ`)…" on the pulpit… yes, that "The ignorant fell into prostration when it was time to stand (`qiyām`)." "The ignorant fell into prostration when it was time to stand." Brother, when he was rising, they fell into prostration. Now, what was the situation? The `minus Tābū bi-Tawbatihi`, their situation is that they are sitting in their place. They are seeing that the light has come to all their companions, secondary perfection has been achieved, `ilm`, `qudrah`, etc., all has been received, but this group, the `minus Tābū bi-Tawbatihi` group, is fixed in its place. Now what happened? The `Tābū bi-Tawbatihi`… the group of `'Āshir`, on this, the last individual of the ninth intellect's circle passed on, handed over the work of the call, to whom? To `'Āshir`. And `'Āshir` handed it over to the last individual of its circle, whom is called the last individual of `Tābū bi-Tawbatihi`. He, who came to the station of `'Āshir`, meaning, he took charge of the station of `'Āshir` and he started the call. To whom? To the remaining ones, who are `minus Tābū bi-Tawbatihi`. Are you understanding? Are you understanding properly? Okay. So, when the call was made, the satanic call was also happening, but the listeners of the Rahmani call also emerge. The people of God, at least in Ramadan Sharif, repent. They say, "Brother, Shaytan is chained." So... just as we see here, exactly the same way it happened, that from that group, a few souls, a few people were there, a few souls, their number has not been given, but those souls, what did they do? They said, "Alright, we submit." Now see, when `'Āshir` repented, and at that very moment, those who met his gaze, they were the `Tābū bi-Tawbatihi` group. They, with him, achieved the class. With him, they achieved the rank. And their group that is being formed, it is being formed upon the call of the last individual of `Tābū bi-Tawbatihi`. Are you understanding? It is being formed upon the call of the last individual of `Tābū bi-Tawbatihi`. And with that, what did they do? This remaining group, which was the group of `'Āshir` that was lying there, from that group, some souls said, "We..." upon your call, your voice that is coming, to that we say `labbayk`. And we say `labbayk` just as we say `labbayk, Allāhumma labbayk` (Here I am at Your service, O Allah, here I am at Your service) in Hajj. `Labbayk, labbayk, Allāhumma labbayk`. As soon as they said `labbayk`, at that very moment, they too became successful, and they became pure and clean, and they too achieved secondary perfection. And this group was named `Labbu-Nidā`. `Nidā` means call, you know, and `Labbu` means those who said `labbayk` to them, those who accepted them. So, the `Labbu-Nidā` was the group that came after them. So, now see, first was the First Intellect, after that was the Second Intellect, after that were the seven intellects (`uqul`), and with the seven `uqul`, their circles. And after the seven `uqul` was `'Āshir`, and with `'Āshir` was one circle, which is called `dā'irah-e-Tābū bi-Tawbatihi`. And after that, the circle that was established was whose? `Labbu-Nidā`. Now, the last individual of `Labbu-Nidā` was entrusted with the task: "Now you make the call to God (`da'wat ilā Allāh`)." Who entrusted it? The last individual of `Tābū bi-Tawbatihi` said, "Now it's not my job. Now you have also become successful. Now you should teach." "You should explain." So, just as he entrusted it to him, now the last individual of `Labbu-Nidā`... the `Tābū bi-Tawbatihi`'s last individual entrusted it to `Labbu-Nidā`. The last individual of `Labbu-Nidā` has now started the call to God. To whom? To the remaining ones who are unsuccessful and who are stubborn, who are arrogant, who are not ready to accept, who are not ready to listen to the call. To them, he was calling. The last individual of `Labbu-Nidā` was calling. Now, what happened was that a delicate moment came. That this one, as he was calling... who? The last one of `Tābū bi-Tawbatihi`. No, the last one of `Labbu-Nidā`, when he was calling the remaining ones, and inviting them towards the `tawḥīd` of the Lord of the Worlds, so when he started calling them repeatedly, calling out repeatedly, then this group, its situation was that it remained in a state of some hesitation. "Should we accept?" "Should we accept?" "Look, how good a call it is. Our call is satanic." The satanic call was on one side. The Rahmani call was on one side. The call of the Merciful was strong, and the call of Satan was strong. Why? Because from the beginning, they were not the accepting type. You will say, "Sir, had they joined the `Tābū bi-Tawbatihi`, or had they joined the `Labbu-Nidā`?" No, no, these were the Shaytans. Their name was coming up that they were still doing their satanic acts. They had not accepted. So, when the God of God and all things were not ready to be accepted, then now, the First Intellect saw, "This is too much." "The water has gone over the head." "The water has gone over the head. And there is a limit to everything, and there is a boundary." Now, there is a boundary to explaining, to calling, to inviting, and now the boundary has been reached. Now, these are not the ones who will reform. They are not capable of living in this world. This is a spiritual world, a holy world, a world of justice. It is not a world of density, it is not a physical world, it is not a world of movement. Here, this is holy, completely germane, and of a quality... of this kind, in which there is delay, there is defeat, this is not that kind of world. So, in such a world, a pure, clean, and sanctified world, they are not fit to live. "Enough is enough. I have acted with a lot of forbearance. Now, send them out of the community." "Expel them from the community." "There is a need to remove them from their circles. There is a need to get them out." He issued the order. Who? The one in whose hand was the administration, in whose hand was the command, and in whose hand the Lord of the Worlds had given everything. Now, whatever there was for that world, he was it. Who? The First Intellect. Everything was given to the First Intellect. He, with his perfection and his... he reflected and... who is his helper? The Second Intellect. With the Second Intellect... now you'll say, "Sir, there must have been consultation, a consulting committee must have been formed." Now all these things are what... but anyway, he thought this and he had this thought, that these are not capable of living in this world. It cannot be that the good and the bad live together. Just as your sense of discrimination does not accept that you take clothes from a dirty place and arrange them in your wardrobe with your good clothes. Your sense of discrimination does not accept it. So just as the sense of discrimination discriminates everywhere, in the same way, he said, "These need to be sent to the laundry." "These need to be washed." "These need to be beaten." "They will not reform here. Put them in." "Remove them." And he issued the order. Now, this order, as soon as it was issued... and that order, the Quran states, `inṭaliqū ilā ẓillin dhī thalāthi shu'ab` (Proceed to a shadow with three branches). "Go, you, to the three-pronged shadow." To the three dimensions. And in the same way, the command `ihbiṭū` (descend/fall) which the Quran states, `ihbiṭū`, "Fall down." The command to fall down came. Now, this command that was issued, what can be said? This is that Being that on one side says `Kun` (Be), and on the other, `fa-yakūn` (and it is). On one side, he said it, and on the other, it happened. There is no question of any hesitation. So as soon as the command was issued by the First Intellect, this command traveled. It reached the Second Intellect. From the Second Intellect, it reached `Hazrat al-Quds`. From `Hazrat al-Quds`, it went into the `dā'irah` of the third. It reached the third intellect's `dā'irah`. From that `dā'irah`, it emerged and reached the fourth intellect. The fourth intellect gave it to its `dā'irah`. The `dā'irah` gave it to the fifth intellect. The fifth intellect gave it to its `dā'irah`. From the fifth intellect's `dā'irah`, it emerged and reached the sixth, from the sixth to the seventh, from the seventh to `'Āshir`. It reached `'Āshir`, and `'Āshir` gave it to its `dā'irah`, `Tābū bi-Tawbatihi`. And from its `dā'irah`, it emerged and reached `Labbu-Nidā`. When it came there... with their hands... now you'll say, "Sir, there must have been a paper there, a sanction was coming from above." No, this is all a matter of understanding. This is a divine revelation, and a divine command. And it was descending from there, flowing, coming. And this light was descending, this command was being revealed. In what form it was, how it was, we can only read it in the words of the Quran, nothing else. And I have read that to you. `inṭaliqū ilā ẓillin dhī thalāthi shu'ab`. Now, that command descended, descended, descended, and reached where? The last individual of `Labbu-Nidā` became the executive instrument. The `mutadabbir` (governor) of the entire `inkisārī` (subservience), and their subservience and our subservience, there is a world of difference. Why? The `Tābū bi-Tawbatihi` were those who had joined their sight with the sight of `'Āshir`. And the `Labbu-Nidā` were those who had accepted the call from his circle. This... `Labbu-Nidā`. And the call of `Labbu-Nidā` was happening, but they were accepting the call then, at that moment, they were accepting the call when the decree was coming. They were a bit... what will you say? Just as Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq said that there are three types of prayer. According to those who pray, I make a distinction, that some who pray do so because they, in the greed of paradise and to be saved from hell, pray. And this is the worship of merchants (`tājirāna 'ibādat`). And the second worship, what kind of worship is it? Out of fear. The worship of fear. That God knows what will happen to us. Meaning, out of fear of hell, or say, for some other fear, that what punishment will befall us, what will happen, what accident will happen. Out of fear, they worship. This is the worst. The second is the merchant-like worship, as I said, they worship with the hope of paradise. And there is one worship of the free (`aḥrār`), of the free people, there is a worship and devotion, and what kind of worship is it? They do it purely for God's sake. That He created us, and we have been created, we must bow down. We must bow down before him. That's it. So these, the third ones, are in reality the worship of the free, of the free people, a devotion. So, in the very same way, this group that was worshipping, that was doing `tawḥīd`, that was accepting, that was repenting, what kind of repentance was theirs? It was in a servile mindset. And some had a merchant-like mindset. It was a mix of both mindsets. Why? Because it was not the worship of free people. They were afraid, "The command has come." "God knows what is written in the command. Brother, accept it." "Now what will happen to us?" But anyway, understand that some such quality was there. I just gave an example. If we say in an example that Ram is like a lion, then you don't take his claws and nails and mustache and face and everything and apply it to Ram, but you look for the point of comparison, that in bravery, Ram is like a lion, that's why he is being called a lion. So, I have given a similar example. Don't apply the example to everything. I just meant to say this, that those who were there were very pure and clean people. They were such that, don't ask, and for their purity and cleanliness, God is the witness. They are so pure and clean. But when did they become so? That is a moment to think about, a moment of reflection. When is it happening? It is happening at that time when the command has been issued. The command was issued from here, and they repented from there. Now, when they repented, and they... their... their repentance was presented to Allah Ta'ala's court through various means, these who repented were minus-ed again from that group. It wasn't that the entire group became pure. It didn't happen like that. Rather, some from that group became pure, and they are called `Kallamam`. This should be remembered. It should be completely memorized (`ḥifẓ`). Just as you remember your name. If I wake you from your sleep, you will say your name. It should be memorized. `Kallamam`. They are called `Kallamam`. `Lamam` means a small bit. A small mistake. The one from whom a small mistake occurred, his subsequent name has been kept as `Kallamam`. They are called `Kallamam`. And the affair of these `Kallamam` has been settled. And for them, a small mistake occurred. Now, what was that small mistake? It was this mistake, that they said "yes" after saying "no." They accepted after refusing. If they had accepted, they would have been successful long ago. If they had accepted, they would have at least come into the `Tābū bi-Tawbatihi`. And if they had accepted, they would have become the `Labbu-Nidā`. But they accepted late. They were late in accepting, but they did accept. And with their acceptance, what did their count become? They became counted among the `Kallamam`. This `Kallamam` is a very great entity, and its gnosis (`ma'rifat`) is very difficult to explain. What I want to say is that Allah Ta'ala... in the workshop of power, in the workshop of pre-eternity, He gave to each what seemed appropriate to Him. So, this was the divine plan (`taqdīr-e-ilāhī`), to place everyone in their station. To place them in that very place. This was what justice (`'adl`) demanded, and this was what equity (`inṣāf`) demanded. And just as the Lord of the Worlds was just, in the same way, you have seen that all were organized, and all were established in succession, and everyone's ranks were fixed in their places. One after the other, they were established in succession, and being established, where did the matter reach? It reached the `Kallamam`. And these `Kallamam` were those, as I said, who said "yes" after saying "no." Or they had accepted after refusing. And that small... and what is that mistake called? It is called a small mistake (`zarā sī bhūl`). If your clothes are white, completely white, completely, so if a little black comes on it, a tiny speck, yet what will happen? It will be very visible. It will be very visible. Why? Because you are completely white. If your clothes were multi-colored, or dirty, then nothing would be visible on it. But if the whole thing is completely white and fair, then there, a little blackness is very visible. So, in the very same way, these who were, were pure and clean entities. A small blemish came upon them. A small thing came. So, that small thing, its ratio, that proportion, you should see from this perspective, that they were completely pure and clean. Meaning, whether secondary perfection (`kamāl-e-thāni`) had been achieved or not, that I will say now. But what I am saying is, they are `qudsāni` (holy), `Raḥmāni` (of the Merciful), `ilm`, `qudrah`, and `ḥayāt` (knowledge, power, and life) are with them in their primary state. And they are endowed with all attributes. And they are living in that spiritual realm. They are those beings. Although they have heard some different calls, they have, through their actions, shown at the last moment... that is why they say, `inna-l-a'mālu bi-l-khawātīmihā` (Indeed, actions are judged by their endings). That every action's outcome is what matters. The ending will be seen. That is why they say, "May Allah Ta'ala grant a good ending." What does it mean, a good ending? Meaning, it will be seen whether at the time of your death, at the time of your departure from the world, on what religion you were. Did your ending happen with good or not? Did your ending happen on the divine religion, on Islam, on faith, or not? So, this was the main thing. This was the last thing. So, in the very same way, these all were sanctified beings, blessed beings, luminous beings, holy people. But a small spot came on them, and that spot was a very strange spot, that they said "yes" after saying "no." So the Lord of the Worlds, what did He do? He counted them in such a way that now two things happened for them. And what were those two things? That now, `qudrat` (divine power) wants... `qudrat` meaning? The last individual of `Labbu-Nidā`. Now, `qudrat` means the last individual of `Labbu-Nidā`. He also wants to punish them, and he also wants not to punish them. Now both things should happen. Now, how can both things happen in one being? And that he should get punishment and not get punishment. How can that be? So, you see that just as there is a small thing, for example, there is a page and a pencil mark is made on it, you can erase it with an eraser. It is erased and becomes clean. In the very same way, it had to be erased. This was its punishment, that it had to endure so much there. So, `qudrat` put them in a dual trial, how to give them punishment and not give them punishment. And the desire of `'Āshir` is this, and the desire of the First Intellect and the Second Intellect and all the intellects is also this, that they should be punished and not punished. It's a very difficult stage. For `qudrat`, a very difficult stage had come. And at this stage, he, who is the last individual of `Labbu-Nidā`, he began to look with longing at his heavens above. His higher ones, who were, those `qudsāni` and `nurani` and principles, towards all of them he began to plead, that "It is better that you suggest. I don't understand what to do with them now." "What to do with them, and what... should I give them punishment or not, and how should I give it, and if I give it, then how?" Now you'll say, "Sir, did he not understand?" The thing is that when a major issue comes up, you don't use your own pen. Rather, your wisdom is in taking advice. That is why the Prophet was commanded, `wa shāwirhum fi-l-amr` (and consult them in the matter). What did he do? He started entrusting it to the ones above. Now the chain went up. It reached the First Intellect. And all of them, he sought their help. `Iyyāka na'budu wa iyyāka nasta'īn` (It is You we worship and You we ask for help). We worship only Him, and we seek help only from Him. This is it. This is the true meaning of `iyyāka nasta'īn`, that seeking help is this. You, in this world, the matter of help and worship is there, but the word for help (`istiyānat`) began from here. So, help was sought from him. And the matter of help went up through all the circles, that "They need help. They need to be guided. They need to be done. They need to be told what they should do now, how they should do it, and how they should be judged." This was a great stage that had come. For whom? For the last individual of `Labbu-Nidā`. Now, this last individual, who is made `'Āshir`, he saw that all these souls, for them, what should happen? When all of them, with their insights, with their analyses and syntheses, and dialogues, saw, and with all their spiritual insights, they cast them. On whom? On `'Āshir`, who is the last individual of `Labbu-Nidā`. So, it was suggested to him. This perfection reached him, it was suggested that it should be done in such a way that neither should they be kept with the bad people, nor joined with the good. Rather, they should be given a middle form. That is why the Prophet said, `khayru-l-umūri awsaṭuhā` (The best of affairs is the middle way). `khayru-l-umūri awsaṭuhā`, that the best of affairs is the middle way. You understand? So, at what stage has he said this? We see moderation as good in everything, but at what extreme has this been said, the Messenger of God is saying. Now, you can enjoy this `ḥadīth`. So, this, placing them in the middle, was the command. It was suggested, it was advised. And the work that had to be done, who had to do it? The last individual of `Labbu-Nidā` and `'Āshir` had to do it. `'Āshir`, what did he do to them? He said, "Brother, you, although you have said 'yes' after saying 'no', and accepted after refusing, yet, you cannot be punished with everyone. You cannot be put into the three dimensions. And nor can you be placed in this spiritual world. You cannot become intellects, nor can it happen here that you are put into this progeny, into this physical world. And you are hanged in this gallows. Neither can you be in this place, nor in that place. Rather, we will place you in the middle." And what was that middle form? It was that of the Prophets (`anbiyā`), and `awliyā`, and `a'immah`, and `aṣfiyā`, `atqiyā`, `khulafā`, `aṣḥāb`, `abdāl`, `awtād`, `shuhadā` (saints, imams, the pure, the pious, caliphs, companions, substitutes, pegs, martyrs). All our guides. All our `du'āt` (summoners), `alayhimuṣ-ṣalātu was-salām`, and all our perfect guides who have passed, one hundred and twenty-four thousand. All of them. This number, one hundred and twenty-four thousand, that is coming along, do not go by this number. You will say, "Sir, their number must also have been one hundred and twenty-four thousand." No. This one hundred and twenty-four thousand is a number that the Prophet mentioned in one place, but that one hundred and twenty-four thousand, when its exegesis comes, I will tell you where one hundred and twenty-four thousand is established. But for now, just understand that they are countless, innumerable. And all of them are, and all of them have been stopped in the middle. They have been stopped. Neither are they fit to go to that world, nor to this spiritual world. They have been stopped in the middle. And the place where they have been stopped... now you'll say, "Sir, was there a place there?" Neither was there a place, nor was there time, nor was there space. I have already told you that space is where there is support. Time is what is called where there is the motion of the sun and moon. And where there is neither ahead nor behind, neither first nor last. That is the state. So, all those people, in the state in which they were stopped, that is called `Tāmūr`. Got it? `Tāmūr`. That is called `Tāmūr`, that is called `markaz` (center), that is called `Ka'ba-e-rūḥānī` (the spiritual Kaaba), that is called `markaz`. That is called the celestial sphere... the gate of the world of holiness. And that is also called the workshop of spirituality (`kārkhāna-e-rūḥānī`). The entire workshop of spirituality was established. The real Kaaba was made. It became the center of everything. Everything was made, so what was made? This. `Tāmūr`. The `Tāmūr` was made. Now, this is... so this is called the Active Field. Now, these who came to this Active Field were all the Imams, they are the Prophets, they are the `awliyā`, `aṣkiyā`, `atqiyā`, all the beings are, the `du'āt` are, everyone is. Now, do not connect from here to there yet. As I will later explain in `bāzūn`, how to connect them. Because in connecting, there will be a mistake. So, but anyway.

This group that is *Kal-lamam*... who in reality is that group of *Kal-lamam*? That very group is our *Anbiya* (*'alayhim al-salatu wa'l-salam*), our *Awliya*, our *A'imma*, our *Du'at*. They are our *Asqiya*, our *Asfiya*, our *Sayya*, our *'ubbad*, our *Zuhhad*. These are all the things. Right now you do not have the spiritual understanding of this. You only understand that there is a *Nabi* and there is a *Rasul*. The matter stops at the level of *Nabi* and *Rasul*. If it goes a little further, then the spiritual understanding goes up to the level of *Imam*. So, other than the three terminologies of *Imam*, *Nabi*, and *Rasul*, we do not take a third term. Come, I will now count out some ranks (*darajat*) for you. When a *Momin* traverses the ranks and progresses, it is so that you may know how many heavens are stacked one upon another. When we first take the *'ahd-e-sharif* (sacred covenant), at that time, at the moment of taking the *'ahd-e-sharif*, the condition of our *nafs* (soul) is such that... the *Du'at* describe that condition by saying that we are *Mustajib* (responders), those who accept the *da'wat* (call). So, it is the state of a *Mustajib*. From *Mustajib* we become *Momin* (believer). From *Momin* we become what is called a *Mukasir*. From *Mukasir* we become *Ma'dhun*. From *Ma'dhun* we become *Da'i al-Mahsur*. From *Da'i al-Mahsur* we become *Da'i al-Mutlaq*. From *Da'i al-Mutlaq* we become *Da'i al-Balagh*. From *Da'i al-Balagh* we become *Hujjat*. From *Hujjat* we become *Bab*. And from *Bab* we become *Imam*.

So you have seen these ranks. But count them for a moment. The *Mustajib* is one. It is a single rank, just one. And after that, as soon as he steps into the rank of *Momin*, when he enters the circle of *iman*, he has to traverse ten ranks there. To say it, everyone is a *Momin*, no doubt. But someone is in the first rank, someone in the second, someone in the third, someone in the fourth, someone in the fifth, and someone in the tenth. And if someone completes their tenth rank, then just as in a college or school, after succeeding, you are not made to sit in the old class—that is a matter of humiliation—you are made to sit in a higher class. So, *Qudrat* (Divine Power) will arrange it such that as soon as your soul is elevated, you are given the rank that is above. So you will step into *Mukasarat*.

You reach the rank of *Mukasarat*. You... the apparent way we are given opportunities and so on, do not go into those things. My point is this: you should examine and see this from an academic (*'ilmi*) perspective. You reach *Mukasarat*; there are ten ranks there. When you traverse those ten ranks, you reach the rank of *Ma'dhun*. When you traverse the ten ranks of *Ma'dhun*, you reach the rank of *Da'i al-Mahsur*. Now, it is a different matter of spiritual knowledge what a *Da'i al-Mahsur* is, what a *Da'i al-Mutlaq* is, what a *Da'i al-Balagh* is. This is a separate discussion. I will digress from the topic, so I am leaving it for now. Now, after *Da'i al-Mutlaq* there is *Da'i al-Balagh*, after *Da'i al-Balagh* there is *Hujjat*, after *Hujjat*... all of them have ten ranks each.

So, just as this is, in the same way, you have to understand the ranks of the *'Aalam-e-Ruhani* (Spiritual Realm). The very first and lowest rank is that of *Nubuwwat* (Prophethood). A *Nabi* (Prophet) is at the most ordinary rank. The most insignificant, the lowest rank, the first rank, at the threshold, right at the entrance—that rank is called *Nubuwwat*. And when a *Nabi* completes that task, when he accomplishes the task of *Nubuwwat* and resolves its many responsibilities, then from *Nubuwwat* he comes to *Risalat* (Messengership). He becomes a *Rasul*. He will not be called *Ya ayyuha'l-Nabi*, he will be called *Ya ayyuha'l-Rasul*. And above *Risalat* comes... the rank of *Imamat*. And upon *Imamat* comes... tell me... the rank of *Wasayat*. Upon *Wasayat* comes the rank of *Nutq-e-Ilahi*. And *Nutq-e-Ilahi* has three degrees: *Jaddiyyat*, *Fathiyyat*, and *Khiyaliyyat*. After traversing these degrees, the rank that comes is that of *Hujjiyyat* or *Imamat-e-Ruhaniyya*. Upon *Imamat-e-Ruhaniyya* comes *Nutq-e-Ilahi*. In *Nutq-e-Ilahi* come three degrees... *Jadd*, *Fath*, and *Khiyal*. Upon that comes *Hujjiyyat*. Upon *Hujjiyyat* comes *Hijabiyyat*. Upon *Hijabiyyat* comes *Anzariyyat*. Upon *Anzariyyat* comes *Ahadiyyat*. Upon *Ahadiyyat* comes *Samadiyyat*.

Are you understanding the ranks? These are the ranks. And the one who is called a *Nabi* is at the very initial rank. Now, for now, do not trouble yourselves. Do not start judging our Prophet (*'alayhi al-salatu wa'l-salam*) and others. If I have given you a scale, do not start measuring immediately, please. Just understand that these are the ranks. This many ranks have to be traversed. So now, who has traversed how many ranks and what, I will explain this to you later. For now, what you have to understand is that these are the steps of the *'Aalam-e-Ruhani*, and these are its ranks. And *Nubuwwat* is the initial rank. Now, you see that there, all those who were of the *Kal-lamam*... they were of the *Kal-lamam*, those who had said "yes" after saying "no," who had affirmed after denying—all of those people, all those lofty souls (*nufus-e-'aliya*), those personalities of saintly attributes (*qudsi-sifat*), what did they do? They did say "yes" after saying "no," but... in changing their "no" to a "yes"... in turning their "no" into a "yes," they took on two relations (*nisbat*s).

Now you will say, what kind of relations? The very same relations that the *'aql-e-awwal* (First Intellect) had left behind. Because such relations were created with the *'aql-e-awwal*... just as... what happens? When you live here in the city, you get very big, wide roads. But if you go to a village for a moment and see in the village how there are footpaths (*pagdandi*s). Why are they called footpaths? It is because near the fields there are very small paths, paths for just one person to walk on. So you walk on that footpath. How is that footpath formed? That footpath is formed... the poor farmer, to plow his field and to bring his bullocks and so on, when he walks on a path, then on his... his... footsteps, and on his very footprints, people walk, and a path begins to form. And a footpath is made. So, in exactly the same way, a mark was left by the *'aql-e-awwal* of two relations, which are called *nisbat-e-adna* (the lower relation) and *nisbat-e-'ala* (the higher relation). I had told you that the two intellects that arose after seeing this *'aql-e-awwal*, the vision of both of them was more or less different. One's vision was... was on the exoteric, one's was on the esoteric. One's was on the effect, one's was on the cause. One was looking at the inner character, another was looking at the outer form. These conditions that existed, these two separate conditions, why were they created? It was because the *'aql-e-awwal* had performed its profession of the monotheism of the Lord of the Worlds with two relations. I had told you that one relation was *ila dhatihi* (towards its own self), meaning it was towards its own self, that it looked at itself and then it looked at all those of its own kind, and thought, "Did I create them, or did they create me?" It said, "No." But then it said that "It must be that there is a creator of all of us." This relation was the higher relation, and its own relation was the lower relation. So these two relations that the *'aql-e-awwal* had left, that very track was of use. Here, those relations were running, and from this very relation all the intellects (*'uqul*) were becoming more or less similar. And these very relations, descending lower and lower, upon reaching the *Kal-lamam*, became even more divided. And how were they divided? The *Kal-lamam*'s group, which is an innumerable group, that group, what did it do? Some people, some souls, accepted that relation which was more noble (*ashraf*). Some souls accepted that relation which was lower (*adwan*).

Now, the question remains, who were those who accepted the *ashraf* relation? And who were those who accepted the *adwan* relation? Those who accepted the *adwan* relation became the *Du'at* and the *Anbiya*. All the *Anbiya* and all the *Du'at*, all of them accepted the *adwan* relation. I mentioned the *Anbiya* in this regard because we are very familiar (*ma'nus*) with them. A human being is most familiar with their mother. But the superiority of the father has been stated by Allah Ta'ala everywhere. In the Quran, there is the superiority of the father. So, the point to be made was that these... who are the *anbiya-e-kiram* (noble prophets), all of them are in the *nisbat-e-adna* (lower relation). They are in the *nisbat-e-adna*. And who became part of the *nisbat-e-'ala* (higher relation)? The Imams became part of it. Whom the *duniya-e-islam* (world of Islam) does not know at all. Well, it neither knows the *'Aalam-e-Ruhani*, nor does it know any of these things. In fact, it does not even know these terminologies, what the difference is between an Imam and *Nubuwwat* and what these things are. For them... for them, even someone who has written four books can be an Imam. This terminology of Imam has become so common that everyone becomes an Imam. But becoming an Imam is not easy. An Imam is a *Hadi* (guide) and a *Rahbar* (leader), but what kind? He is one who possesses the *nisbat-e-'ala*. Where did the *nisbat-e-'ala* begin? From *Imamat*, from *Wasayat*—all these are of the *nisbat-e-'ala*. And where is the *nisbat-e-adna* from? From the *Du'at*, from *Nubuwwat*, from *Risalat*, from all... from the *Wasayat* here—all these relations are *adna*.

Now, when those souls were divided between *nisbat-e-'ala* and *nisbat-e-adna*, then their station (*qiyam*) and their residence also became... since we are helpless servants (*'ajiz*) and we discuss in terms of physical realities (*jismaniyyat*), and without that, we do not understand, for this reason, the explainers have explained it this way. Although there are no places there, there is no station, no one is ahead or behind. But the explainers have told us in such a way that if they are of the *nisbat-e-'ala*, the *A'imma*, then they are all above. And if they are of the *nisbat-e-adna*, then they are all below. Why? Because they are their slaves. The *A'imma* are the masters (*aqa*), the owners (*malik*), and all the *anbiya-e-kiram*, they are all slaves. They are all their... their... fostered ones (*parwarda*), their slaves, subservient (*ta'be'*) to them. They are subservient to the commands of the Imam (*ahkam-e-imam*). So, *Imamat* is lofty, it is exalted, it is of the *nisbat-e-ashraf* (more noble relation). *Nubuwwat* is of a lower station (*dheeley*), *Nubuwwat* is of the *nisbat-e-adna*, and it is much lower (*niche*).

Now, if you were to see this here, how should we understand it here? Since I am telling you that the place where they all gathered and stopped, that very place we call the *Ka'bah*. That is what we call the *Ka'bah-e-Ruhani* (Spiritual Ka'bah), the *Markaz* (Center), the *Qalb* (Heart). That is what we call the *Ta'mur*, that is what we call the *Dakhil-e-'Aalam-e-Ruhani* (Entrance to the Spiritual Realm), and that is what we call the *Bab-e-'Aalam-e-Ruhani* (Gate of the Spiritual Realm). So, since that is the *Bab-e-'Aalam-e-Ruhani* and the *Ka'bah-e-Ruhani*, you must have some relation to this *Ka'bah-e-Ruhani* through this Ka'bah. So, come to this Ka'bah. Let's reflect within this Ka'bah on what their station (*maqam*) would be. Meaning, reflect here and understand it over there. You have to reflect here and understand it there. You have to reflect here. You have to understand it there. That of this *Ka'bah-e-Ruhani*, the one that is the *dakhili Ka'bah* (internal Ka'bah)... the inner part of the Ka'bah, this Ka'bah is... what shape is it? It is of a conical (*makhruti*) shape. It is not square (*chaukhut*). It is not like this, with four sides made in this way. The Ka'bah is not like this. The Ka'bah is such that a wall comes from here, and this wall is called the *Hateem*. Its name is also *Hijr-e-Isma'il*. If you were to include this and draw a circle (*da'irah*), you would realize that a conical shape is formed.

So, the shape of the Ka'bah is conical, and the conical shape is that of our heart. This is the heart. The heart of the entire world (*jahan*) is the Ka'bah. And inside this Ka'bah, just as our heart has three membranes (*parde*), in the same way, it has three membranes. It has three parts (*hisse*). Of that Ka'bah. Because... now you will say, "If we dig the earth there and see..." You won't see anything by digging the earth. These are all spiritual matters. So, it has three parts. And these three parts are just like the chambers or membranes in our heart. So, absolutely... those parts of the heart, obviously their importance is much greater compared to the limbs that are attached to the heart or the veins that are attached to it. Their importance will not be as great as that of the things inside the heart. So, in exactly the same way, inside the Ka'bah, the cavities (*tajawif*)—they are called *tajawif* in our terminology, *tajawif* means chambers (*khanon*)—so the *tajawif*, the parts, the membranes, in that place were the *A'imma*. All the Imams were there. All the Imams resided there. And the outer parts, where we perform circumambulation (*tawaf*), which is called the *mataf*, where the *Maqam-e-Ibrahim* is, and from where you perform *tawaf*, that... that is, every... this is a wall, draw an arc here. This is... this is called the *bittiqah-e-shumali* (northern section), that is called the *bittiqah-e-junubi* (southern section), this is called the *gharbi* (western), and this is called the *sharqi* (eastern). So these are all *bittiqah*s, *bittiqah* means sections.

These are things that require a lot of understanding. In any case, I am telling you that the *tajawif* have more importance than the *bittiqah*s. So, who were the ones who came to the *bittiqah*s? They were the *Anbiya-e-kiram*. They were the *Anbiya-e-kiram*. And just as this our Ka'bah is the factory (*karkhana*) of life, that all of life that is being distributed and arranged is all from here. The fragrance is spreading from here. Seventy winds are blowing from here. Whether it is *dabr* or *qubur*, whose names have been mentioned, all the winds blow from here. The incidents (*hadithat*) come from here. All matters of life and death (*hayat-o-mamat*) are related to this very Ka'bah. And whatever things are coming into the world, whether it is raining or various incidents are occurring, the connection of all things, the connection of life and death, is with this very factory of the world (*karkhana-e-'alam*). With this very manifest Ka'bah.

This needs to be understood, how it is. So, just as this is a factory in which there are thousands of things and a tremendous work is being done. And what are its great pillars (*sutun*)? Its great pillars are the very things I mentioned to you: its *tajawif*, its *batayiq*, its *ma'e sa'id*, and its *azwa*, *anwa'*, its *hawaiyya*, and its... *Maqam-e-Ibrahim*, its *Maqam-e-Mimbar*, and *Maqam-e-Zamzam*. These are not ordinary things. This water and this... আরে, you will say that this is a living miracle (*mu'jizah*) of Islam, that since then until today, this well has not been able to dry up. But you are looking at the exoteric; I am looking at the esoteric, that the things that are being plundered from there, the grace (*faiz*) that is flowing, can never be stopped. From that spiritual Ka'bah. It cannot be stopped even from this physical Ka'bah. So, when this physical Ka'bah has these capabilities (*salahiyatein*), what will be the state of the spiritual Ka'bah?

Now are you understanding? So that spiritual Ka'bah, where all those souls were made to stop... were placed. And they were not included in the *'Aalam-e-Ruhani*. They did not receive *'ilm ma kana wa ma yakun* (knowledge of what was and what will be), they did not attain *qudrat-e-tammah* (complete power), they did not get *hayat-e-abadi* (eternal life). Meaning, they did not attain *kamal-e-thani* (second perfection). They did not attain it. And it's not that they were cast into this physical world either. "No, you neither go here nor go there, but remain suspended (*mu'allaq*) in between." And the place where they were made to stop, and the manner in which they were made to stop, that is what is called the *qalb-e-'alam* (heart of the world), that is what is called the *qalb-e-ruhani* (spiritual heart).

So, in this *qalb-e-ruhani*, how they were stationed, that is what I was telling you. That their arrangement (*tartib*) was in such a way that those above were all the *A'imma-e-kiram* (noble Imams), and those below, who were they? All the *anbiya-e-'izam* (great prophets). Now, among the *A'imma-e-kiram*, who all? I... I cannot list everyone's names, but I will tell you that there is Amir al-Mominin Ali, there is Janab Hasan, there is Janab Husayn, there is Imam Ali Zayn al-'Abidin, there is Janab Muhammad al-Baqir, there is Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq. There is Janab Mu'izz, there is Janab Mustansir, there is Janab... all these are the manifest Imams (*Imam-e-zahir*). This entire chain of Imams is running. If you go higher up, there is Janab Ibrahim, there is Janab Isma'il. You will see that in the Quran Majid, wherever Allah Ta'ala has mentioned the *Anbiya*, whenever a *Nabi* was mentioned, all the prophets were mentioned. So our Hazrat Ibrahim Khalil al-Rahman, was he mentioned? He was also mentioned there. And he was mentioned quite a bit.

whenever a *Nabi* was mentioned, all the prophets were mentioned. So our Hazrat Ibrahim Khalil al-Rahman, was he mentioned? He was also mentioned there. And he was mentioned quite a bit. Whose? Hazrat Ibrahim Khalil al-Rahman, who was a friend of Allah, who had performed the sacrifice (*zabhiyyat*) of his son, Janab Isma'il. Indeed. The mention of Janab Ibrahim was made, but in what way was the mention made? That he is the one and only *Nabi* about whom it is stated—Allah Ta'ala says in the Quran Majid—*waj'alnahu li'l-nasi imama* ("And We made him an Imam for the people"). "O Ibrahim, We will make you an Imam for the people." So it became known that this was a special quality (*khususiyyat*) of Janab Ibrahim, that we consider him a *Nabi*, but he holds the rank of *Imamat*. He is an Imam.

So, just as, to explain a special quality, I told you, so now the *Anbiya*... these were the *A'imma-e-kiram*, who were takers of the higher relation, who were of the *nisbat-e-ashraf*, or who were the personalities residing above. Now, below... the personalities who came below, who were they? Our Prophet, Hazrat Muhammad Mustafa (*sallallahu 'alayhi wa sallam*) was there, and Janab... Janab Dhul-Kifl was there, Janab Shu'ayb was there, Janab Yusuf was there, Janab Daniyal was there, Janab Ayyub was there, Janab... Sham'un was there, Janab Dawud was there. There is an army (*lashkar*) of 124,000 prophets. It is a very large army. All were there. Now see, they have all been established. Now they are all established, and the Lord of the Worlds (*Parwardigar-e-'Alam*)—which Lord of the Worlds? ...'Ashir. That one who holds the administration in his hand. And who is that? The last individual (*fard*) of *Labbu nida'*. The last individual of *Labbu nida'* has now done what? To them... he told them... before giving a punishment, a word is spoken. In the same way... their condition was that they were in agony. They were feeling grief for their companions. And just as our human nature (*fitrat*) works here, there it was working even more intensely. And these people started to call out, started to explain, and began to say, "Believe it, understand it. What is it, brother? We have now become correct. See how successful we have become. You too, at least, become successful, and you too believe. And listen to the divine voice, accept the divine call (*da'wat-e-ilahi*). আরে, become *Sulaymani* (followers of Sulayman/submissive)!" This is what they were saying. And when the call was being given, that group to whom the call was being given, what did that group do? It started to listen. But what was the situation? How was the call being given? I want to explain that. Please understand.

The call was not being given in the way that the *'aql-e-awwal* was giving the call, or the *'aql-e-thani* was giving the call, or the third intellect was giving the call, or the last individual of its circle, 'Ashir, was giving the call, or the fourth intellect, or its... or 'Ashir, the tenth one, was giving the call, or the last of *tabu' batuti* was giving the call, or the last individual of *Labbu nida'* was giving the call. It was not a call like that. That was an individual call (*infradi da'wat*). It was the call of one person. Although he was receiving knowledge from everyone, he was receiving spirituality (*ruhaniyyat*), he was receiving grace (*faiz*), but it was one call. He was giving the call alone. He was giving the call alone. The entire administrator (*mudabbir*) was giving the call. The entire Universal Intellect (*'aql-e-kull*) was giving the call. But now the call that was being given, what kind of call was it? Team work. Now, it is to work together, unitedly. "We will all work together. Our community will work. We will work under the name *Hizb al-Iman* (The Party of Faith)." There you have it. Now this *Hizb al-Iman* that is working, this community of faith that is being established, what was it like? It was of all the *awliya Allah* (friends of God). It was of the *A'imma*, who were of the *nisbat-e-ashraf*, and it was of all the *Anbiya*, who were of the *nisbat-e-adna*.

Is it clear to you? Is it perfectly clear? So it was like this for *nisbat-e-'ala* and *nisbat-e-adna*. And all of them, all of them were giving the call. To whom were they giving the call? I told you that those who are minus *tabu' batuti*, minus *Labbu nida'*, minus *Kal-lamam*, who are left behind, they are giving the call to them. And who is sitting among them? Among them, we poor ones are also sitting. We are also sitting. But our rebellion is established. Our rebellion is established, and we were not ready to accept. That's why we were sitting there. Now, the group... our group was also divided. How many were with us? Countless. There were many. There were many of everything. Meaning, there was no deficiency of any kind. There were very many. There were also those who were absolutely not ready to believe. There were also those who were stuck in doubt and astonishment. There were also those who were moving towards a little remorse. They were there with this kind of state of being.

Now this state, which Allah Ta'ala has described... their condition was such that, just as the Quran Majid describes it, a remorseful person, the *nadim*, his state is such that if he is touched even a little, if he is provoked even a little, then look, he will completely... they say, "Oh brother, they've gone, they've become Allah Miyan's cow." But that "Allah Miyan's cow" is very good. We give it this name, "Allah Miyan's cow," or "shift-light," or that he bows his head, he does this or that. We think one should come with some pride, with some understanding, with some... this is nothing. So, the remorseful person has this capability within him, that if he is explained even a little, it is more than enough. Just the support of a finger is enough for him. He will grab hold of it. So this is the leaven of remorse. This is the remorse that is speaking to him, and he becomes ready to accept immediately.

So I was saying that the remorse that was happening there, what kind of remorse was it? It was that we were thinking in various ways. That there was a variation in remorse, there was a state of astonishment, there was insistence. But various were our states. Now, among these *Anbiya* and *Awliya*, first let me talk about their... my masters. What was the state of all these *Anbiya* and *Awliya* who are there? This is something to understand. And it is a very important thing. There, just as I told you, the points were established, and the order was established. And how was the order established? It was established on their remorse. On the leaven of their remorse, on their repentance, this order was established. And what was the order? It was that the very first being, if there was one, who was it? The coming *Qa'im al-Qiyamah*, *'alayhim al-salatu wa'l-salam*. Are you understanding? The coming *Qa'im al-Qiyamah*, *'alayhim al-salatu wa'l-salam*'s being was present there, and he was greater than all, he was there. Now you will say, "Greater in what way?" I will tell you. In what way he was greater, I will tell you, but for now, establish the order. This was there, and after him, if there was anyone in the order, it was Amir al-Mominin, Ali ibn Abi Talib, *'alayhi al-salatu wa'l-salam*. Did you understand? Now you must be understanding what the station of Ali is. They call Ali God, and rightly so, that's the truth. So now it was Ali's station. And after Ali there were Hasan, Husayn, and so on. Now this chain was established and continued, and a complete line was formed. Now, how was this order established? That is what I am going to tell you about how the order was established. What happened was that there, everyone was given the initiative, everyone was given the right to "give the call to Allah." "It's team work. You should also call, you should also call, you should also call." Look, when the noble month of Ramadan comes, there are lessons here, there are lessons there. The people of Allah sit in the mosque, and the beloveds of Allah come and they recite. They are reciting here, they are reciting there. There is a lesson here, there is a lesson there. Even today, in Jamia Azhar, where I went and saw, that mosque where Sayyidna Qadi al-Nu'man used to teach, its platform has been made and elevated out of respect. But in other places, lessons happen, and in the same seating arrangement of the school, lessons happen. And all the different groups, as they sit, they do. So, just as the opportunity arises, in the same way, the lessons will be established. Absolutely the same situation happened. Everyone took their own lesson and sat down, and everyone began to make their own call, to call out. And everyone is calling.

If you say that since the *A'imma* were greater, and since they were elders, of the *nisbat-e-ashraf*, they should have been the only ones to call. They should have stopped this lower call, "What need is there for the *Anbiya* to speak? What need is there for these *Du'at* to speak? Be quiet. We are the ones calling, that is more than enough." No, it wasn't done like that. Since they were remorseful, they were *Kal-lamam*, everyone was given the right to speak. "You should give the call. This group that is unsuccessful and are deniers, they should be called." When they were given this full right, they were all giving the call. So now, they began to look at one another there, "Brother, I am giving the call, but let me see what call the other one is giving." Just as we have a habit here, that if there is, say, a cooking competition, from one pot, people will quickly leave and look at the other to see if they have added the spices or not, or if they have done this or that. So just as it happens here, or in an examination hall, one looks at another's paper to see... "Oh, he's getting up early." If he got up early, then one feels worried, "Come on brother, his is finished, we are sitting here until late, so we will get more marks." So now, just as there is a strange state, just as it is here, a somewhat similar state... there, such things don't happen, but there was a similar state, that they all, all of them who were watching... the inclination of all of them... the focus of all the *A'imma*... was on Amir al-Mominin, Ali ibn Abi Talib, *'alayhi al-salatu wa'l-salam*. Everyone's gaze, the center of their gaze, had become... who? Mawla-e-Ka'inat, Mawla-e-Mushkil Kusha, Amir al-Mominin, Hazrat Ali ibn Abi Talib, *'alayhi al-salatu wa'l-salam*, had become the center. And everyone's center, the Ka'bah... he had become the Ka'bah. He had become the spiritual Ka'bah for everyone. Everyone's gazes were fixed there. "Oh brother, what call should we give now? The call..." Janab Fatimah is also observing, Janab Hasan is also observing, Janab Husayn is also observing, everyone is observing, and they are all observing that "No, if a call is to be given, one needs to learn from Ali ibn Abi Talib. If there is a call, it should be like this."

But what happened? Ali ibn Abi Talib, *'alayhi al-salatu wa'l-salam*, accepted the call, and he looked at the call of whom? Of Hazrat Qa'im, *'alayhi al-salatu wa'l-salam*, the coming one who will establish the Qiyamah. His gaze was on his call. Now what happened? If all of you are looking at me, and I start looking at the chandelier, what will you do? You will think that there must be some matter that his gaze has gone there, so we should also look. Come on. Naturally, while looking at me, you will start looking at the chandelier, because I looked at the chandelier. You were looking at me. So, in exactly the same way, everyone was looking at Ali. Ali was looking at Janab Qa'im. Everyone's gaze went to Janab Qa'im. Did you understand? Everyone's gaze went to Janab Qa'im. All the Imams of the Era of the Qa'im were called. The Era of Muhammadi and the Era of Qa'imi were called. All of them, all the Imams became attached to him. Are you understanding? All of the Imams became attached to whom? To Hazrat Qa'im, *'alayhi al-salatu wa'l-salam*. Now, the being of Janab Qa'im became what? It is obvious that if you keep praising me, I will surely rise. From anyone's praise, a person... they say that he starts to fly. That state happens. So this is the state of a servant. Now, what happened there was that when everyone's gaze started to fall upon him, everyone started to learn, the state of Janab Qa'im became very lofty. The coming one, the establisher of Qiyamah, *'alayhim al-salatu wa'l-salam*, *'ala dhikrihi al-salam*, his state became very lofty, and he became the Ka'bah for everyone. For all the *A'imma*. But what was the situation? Since everyone had first made their Ka'bah whom? Mawla-e-Ka'inat, Hazrat Ali ibn Abi Talib, *'alayhi al-salatu wa'l-salam*. For this reason, now when the gaze started to go towards Janab Qa'im, it started to go while stumbling a bit, that it is also seeing Ali, and also seeing Qa'im. It is also seeing Ali, and also seeing some of Qa'im. This state began to happen there. So, the gaze of all the *A'imma* was now where? On Janab Qa'im and also on Janab Ali. The gaze was there, and everyone was learning from Janab Ali. Are you understanding?

Now, what happened below? The one who was below, who was of the *nisbat-e-adna*, who were the *Anbiya*, like Janab Shu'ayb, Dhul-Kifl, and Janab Dawud, Sulayman, and all the *Anbiya*, as many as are mentioned in the Quran and as many as are not mentioned, all the *Anbiya*, Sham'un, Ayyub, Yusuf, Daniyal, all... as many *Anbiya* as there are, all of those *Anbiya*, *'alayhim al-salatu wa'l-salam*, within them... this state occurred, that everyone's gaze was falling upon Janab Ibrahim, *'alayhi al-salatu wa'l-salam*. Understand? Everyone's gaze was falling upon Hazrat Ibrahim. And Hazrat Ibrahim's gaze was falling upon Hazrat Muhammad, *'alayhi al-salatu wa'l-salam*, *fida-hu ummi wa abi*, the master of the universe, the pride of all existence. His gaze was falling upon him, Hazrat Ibrahim's. And what happened? The gaze of all turned towards the master of the universe. All the prophets' focus, all the prophets' center became who? The master of the universe. The pride of all existence became everyone's center, and everyone's gaze is clashing there, and everyone is learning. "Oh brother, if we have to learn, we should learn from here. The method of the call is from here. The call will only come from this. What call do we know how to give? What the call is called, we don't know. What... we are doing it, but the correct way, the way the call has to be given, that has to be learned from the Prophet." So all are in the discipleship of the Prophet, all are learning a lesson from you, are learning. So this was the state, and Hazrat Prophet, *'alayhi al-salatu wa'l-salam*, everyone had made him their Ka'bah.

Suddenly a revolution came. What is fact is fact. The revolution that came was this: these relations were in their own place. Those of the noble relation were in their own place, those of the lower relation were in their own place. Suddenly an earthquake came, a great tremor came, a revolution came in the spiritual world. And it was this: Hazrat Ali ibn Abi Talib, *'alayhi al-salatu wa'l-salam*, moved from his place. Now, I have to say all this because we are sitting in the physical realm. There, there is no place, no moving, no coming, no going. But for the sake of understanding, it is *taqriban li'l-afham* (an approximation for understanding). That the Prophet, *'alayhi al-salatu wa'l-salam*, began to look down, thinking, "No, brother... the great thing is, the courageous thing is, to learn even from one's subordinate. If he is below, he should not be ignored." His gaze went to where? To those below. And he said, "Let's see what kind of call he is giving." When he turned his gaze to give the call, what was known? That among them, one is shining like the universal sun. And is so luminous that it is beyond description, and its rays are dazzling, and it is a very astonishing state, and its guidance is extremely tremendous. Who felt this? Ali ibn Abi Talib, *'alayhi al-salatu wa'l-salam*, who is in the noble relation. In the higher relation. The moment his gaze fell upon Janab Prophet, he said, "*Amantu*" (I believe). "I have brought faith." Meaning, the moment he brought faith, and the moment he accepted that "No, if there is a way, it is that of the master of the universe." So what happened? The gaze of one from the noble relation fell upon the master of the universe. Now, the gaze of the entire world, whether above or below... are you understanding? Whether in the noble relation or the lower relation, whether they are *A'imma* or *Awsiya* or *Hujjat*s or *Qa'im* or anyone below, whether *Anbiya* or *Awliya* or *Asfiya* or *Asqiya* or *Du'at*, the center of everyone's gaze became the Mercy to the Worlds (*Rahmatun li'l-'Alamin*), Hazrat Muhammad Mustafa (*sallallahu 'alayhi wa sallam*). You became the soul of the spiritual world. And in this way, your state became.

Now, this state of yours that happened, the entire world shrank and gathered around you. And the master of the universe is shining in it as the sun of guidance. You see? But what is it? He is in the lower relation. Your occurrence, your beginning, your coming was in the lower relation. The Prophet, *'alayhi al-salatu wa'l-salam*'s. And there, Ali is in the higher relation. Keep this in mind. Now what happened? Divine Power began to see that a great revolution has come. अरे, the one of the higher relation is doing this before the one of the lower relation, and the one of the lower relation is truly very lofty, which is why he has become the center of everyone's gaze. And the center of everyone's gaze has become him. There must be something in him. So, the moment Divine Power felt this... Divine Power... the last individual of *Labbu nida'*. The moment he felt this, he began to raise the throne. The Prophet, *'alayhi al-salatu wa'l-salam*'s point (*nuqta*) was sent forth (*mab'uth*). And the master of the universe, who is being sent forth, you are being raised higher. This is the essential *Mi'raj*. You see? What will these Muslims tell of the *Mi'raj*? What will they tell of the *Mi'raj*? I will explain to you in full what the *Mi'raj* is. The true, essential *Mi'raj* of the master of the universe is this, that you were lifted from this throne. You were lifted from this floor and brought to the throne. You were brought to the throne. So now, who are the lifters? अरे, they are the *A'imma*. Those who are of the noble relation, they are lifting. Whose throne? Hazrat Muhammad Mustafa (*sallallahu 'alayhi wa sallam*)'s throne. They lifted your throne and brought it, and after bringing it, they placed it in the higher relation. "No, no Prophet, how can you stay in the lower relation? You are in the noble relation. अरे, you are our most noble. How can you stay in the lower relation?" So this that happens, a... understand that if, say, he has not studied and passes the exam with a first class, then you look at him with great astonishment. So the Prophet who was coming, he had come in the lower station. अरे, he had come in a very low state, the Prophet, but he did not remain low. So how? Through his own excellence, through his own capability, through his own effects, through the characteristics of his prophethood, the Prophet won. And having won, he is now going where? His throne is rising higher and higher. Going on and on, the Prophet, *'alayhi al-salatu wa'l-salam*, came into the higher relation. Now, after coming into the higher relation, now don't you ask. Now it is spring upon spring. That spiritual world's state, what can I describe of it? That in that spiritual world... if they have all become fresh flowers, if they have become the suns of guidance, if they have become luminous lamps, then who? The master of the universe. Except for the master of the universe, the lamp of all is extinguished. All are dim. Why? Because Ali is circumambulating around you. And all the *A'imma* are circling. Everyone's gaze is circumambulating him. So this sun of guidance, who was it? It was the being of the master of the universe, that Prophet, *'alayhi al-salatu wa'l-salam*.

This is the very reason that the Prophet, *'alayhi al-salatu wa'l-salam*, this should not be said right now, but I will tell you in great detail later, that when he came into this world here, what did you do? Hazrat Ali ibn Abi Talib, *'alayhi al-salatu wa'l-salam*, you were seven or eight years old. When the occasion of *wa andhir 'ashirataka'l-aqrabin* (And warn your nearest kindred) came, you invited all your relatives over a pound of meat and a bowl of milk. And the Prophet said, "In my mission, in my work, in spreading Islam, who is ready to help me? People, is there anyone ready to become my helper?" So Janab Ali gets up and says... a seven-year-old child, what do you see? And he comes and says, "O Messenger of Allah, I am ready to become your helper. I am your brother, I am your supporter, I am your helper." So the Prophet says, "Yes, yes, O Ali, you are my supporter, you are my minister, you are my helper, you are my everything." You saw? This... this matter, what does it indicate? People have seen it in this light, whereas the world of Islam sees it in what light, I am telling you. Because there is animosity towards Mawla-e-Ka'inat, Amir al-Mominin, so they saw it in this light, that they said, "Janab Prophet, *'alayhi al-salatu wa'l-salam*, had said... 'Brother, I need a helper.' What else? A child, in his innocence, he was a naive, innocent child, what would he know of the world? Without understanding anything, he raised his hand, just as some children raise their hands in class. In that way, he said yes." আরে brother, if Ali was a child, and was speaking out of incomprehension, the Prophet, *'alayhi al-salatu wa'l-salam*, was not a child. How did the Prophet accept Ali's call? How did the Prophet accept Ali as his supporter and his helper? The Prophet was accepting for this very reason, that he knew who Ali was. He understood Ali's personality. And there was no one who could read this gaze. If there was anyone there who could read it, it was Janab Salman, Janab Abu Dharr al-Ghaffari, Janab 'Ammar ibn Yasir, Janab Miqdad ibn Aswad. These were the personalities who were reading the gaze of prophethood, or were reading the gaze of Amir al-Mominin, who knew the secret. There were only a few, a handful of people who knew. Not everyone knew. अरे, the situation was, the spiritual knowledge of the Mawla was such, it has been told, that one time Hazrat Ali ibn Abi Talib, *'alayhi al-salatu wa'l-salam*, the house he lived in... his house is still present in Kufa today. And in that house, Khatun-e-Jannat also lived there, Hazrat Fatimah al-Zahra. And you... often, you would go out for your labor. You would come back, you would rest, it would be nighttime. Qanbar, who was your slave, of Amir al-Mominin, he came one time. And just as Allah has commanded, that "when you enter a house, enter with permission." "May I come in?" So Janab Fiddah, who was Janab Fatimah al-Zahra's maidservant, she said, "Come, Qanbar, come. You can come." He entered. Upon entering, he said, "Where is my Mawla? My master and my lord, Amir al-Mominin, where is he? I need him, where is he?" So Janab Fiddah felt like making a joke. Janab Fiddah joked and said, "Mawla-e-Ka'inat, you are asking about him? You are asking about Hazrat Ali?" He said, "I have been asking the same thing since the beginning, where is Hazrat Ali?" So she said, "He must be in the heavens." "Heavens?" "He must be in the constellations. In the twelve sections that are there, he must be there. He must be in the sun, in Saturn, in Mars, in Jupiter. He must be in the sky, in the stars, in this, in that." Now she started saying strange things, Janab Fiddah, and Janab Qanbar was perplexed, bewildered. He said, "What are you talking about? I don't understand anything." So it became known that Hazrat Fiddah was more knowledgeable than Janab Qanbar. Although she was Fatimah's maidservant, he was Ali's slave. So Ali's slave was weaker in knowledge, but Janab Fatimah's maidservant was greater, that she understood, and she began to describe Janab Ali's conditions. So now, what were these conditions? अरे, the one in whose hand is the key to the spiritual world, who is the focus of the spiritual Ka'bah, who has become the center, what will we say about him? He was the center of gazes. He was the center of the *A'imma*. So, when everything had happened there, then what... Prophet, *'alayhi al-salatu wa'l-salam*, after knowing your states, could he make any deficiency? No. He could not make any deficiency. And he had to entrust that thing to you. When I... when I speak of the chain of *Imamat* and *Nubuwwat*, etc., in this world, and I will speak from Adam until this day, at that time I will explain it to you, you will enjoy it. If I speak now, you won't understand, and you won't enjoy it either. And that pleasure will not be there, the pleasure I want to create. So, the Prophet, *'alayhi al-salatu wa'l-salam*'s appointment at Ghadir and on other occasions is a matter of great importance, a momentous event, and I will prove and tell you what the inner secrets were, and what was happening. अरे, the Prophet was giving the rightful one his due.
