Obviously, Paradise... the grass of Paradise, and then the ram of Paradise, and how much it must have grazed. It must have been so fatty, like the ones here in Kuwait. It must have come. We get so much to eat, but the goat doesn't get fat, but its life is taken. Here in the desert, but the ram is fat. It came, and Janab Ibrahim sacrificed that ram. So this fatty ram... and this... where from? It had been grazing in Paradise for 40 years. In reality, it was not that the ram was a ram, nor was Paradise Paradise, nor was grazing grazing. And in reality, it was this: that Hazrat Lut, the prophet, who among all the prophets is the highest prophet, meaning after Janab Ibrahim, if the greatest prophets are counted, it is Lut, the prophet, 'alayhi al-salatu wa-salam. Your being is very high, very great, of great majesty. And this you have achieved merely through your own effort (*kasb*), because you were sent to such a people who were steeped in misguidance. And you extricated them from great degradation (*zalalat*). Because of this, your rank became high. And that Hazrat Lut, the prophet, 'alayhi al-salatu wa-salam, he was similar to that ram. In reality, that ram was meant to be Janab Lut, who in Paradise, meaning in the knowledge of the Hazrat-e-Imami, had been studying for 40 years, and he was sent, that "sacrifice him." Meaning, grant him prophethood and so on. Now, don't look towards Ishaq yet. Here, Janab Lut came, and you sacrificed Janab Lut, meaning you entrusted him with *risalat* and *nabuwwat*. But when you were entrusting *risalat* and *nabuwwat*, a sign came from the Imam towards you, "Look, Ibrahim, you are giving it, but make him a trustee (*mustawda'*). Make him only a trustee (*amanat-dar*) for your son Ishaq."

This... but it is that Ishaq could not receive prophethood and *risalat* until Lut received it, because he had achieved that greatness. So these were those rams, which Janab Ibrahim sacrificed. And after that, *wa fadaynahu bi-dhibhin 'azim* (and We ransomed him with a great sacrifice). This was the great sacrifice which Janab Ibrahim fulfilled. And Allah Ta'ala said, *inna hadha lahuwa al-bala'un mubin* (Indeed, this was the manifest trial). This was a very severe trial, which... meaning, it was a battle between two sons, and Allah's... not a sent prophet, but the Imam of the time faced a great dilemma, as to whom to give prophethood and *risalat*, and to whom to give Imamat and apostleship. This dilemma arose. Indeed, this was a great trial for an Imam, but you came through this trial very successfully, and you distributed what you had to. You gave it to Janab Isma'il, but making whom a trustee? Janab Lut, who was in place of the ram. And you entrusted everything to him. After that, what did you do for Janab Ishaq? From Janab Lut's side, that thing was a trust (*amanat*). That trust... trusteeship is trusteeship. Even if they sit with the money, the trust has to be handed over. He handed over that trust to whom? To Hazrat Ishaq. This Hazrat Ishaq, Janab... whose... Janab Ayyub's father. Janab Ayyub, whose father? Janab Yusuf's father. And the chain continued, of father and son, for some time, and the chain of prophethood continued in this way for some time, and in the progeny of Janab Ishaq, prophethood continued. There, prophethood and *risalat* continued, and here, Isma'il, the Imam, 'alayhi al-salatu wa-salam, whom Janab Ibrahim, after him, his younger son, honored with Imamat. Now, along with honoring with Imamat, what happened was that a story from your childhood is that you were still young, this incident had not even occurred yet, that Janab Hajra took you and left, and where did you reach? Nature wanted these wonders to keep happening in the world, and you reached Mecca the Honored. Who? Hajra, with Janab Isma'il. Now, this is all written in the *Tiskar-e-Ibrahim* (Memorials of Ibrahim). That there were some relics of Hazrat Ibrahim, these are his memorials, these are his miracles, these are his signs, because of which this Hajj came into being in the world of Islam. What Hajj came, brother? That she brought Janab Isma'il, Janab Hajra, and there it was a desert, a barren valley (*wadi ghayr-i dhi-zar'*). There was no sign of water there, a desolate, barren land, and Mecca the Honored. And after arriving there, Janab Isma'il became thirsty. He became so thirsty that Janab Hajra became restless for her child. A mother's love awoke, and you started looking to see if any water was visible. For that, you climbed a small hill. The name of that hill was Safa. And from that hill, she saw if any water was visible. She saw that it was not visible. She ran and went to another hill, its name was Marwa. And reaching Marwa, she looked again, and again, that there is no water. In this way, she made seven rounds, and despite making the rounds, no water was found. Exhausted and disheartened, she came to her son and saw that from the rubbing of his feet, a spring was gushing out from the ground, and so much water was flowing that the water would not stop. And that child was quenched with water, but even after that, it would not stop. So Janab Hajra said, "Zam, zam" (stop, stop). And as soon as she said "Zam, zam," the water stopped. But to this day, that miracle of Islam is apparent. There are many miracles of Islam, and among them, one miracle is this, that today that small well... look today, that people from all over the world are quenched from it. Since when? From Janab Adam's time until now, they are being quenched. You will say the story of Ibrahim is starting. No, it starts from there. That water which has never finished is always flowing and has always been available. And the world has been quenched. So, this... and this running that she did, Allah Ta'ala instituted the *sa'i* (ritual running) because of it, that "you too, just as my pure wife, Hajra, ran, you too run." And in this way, she performed the *tawaf* (circumambulation), so you too perform the *tawaf*. And that Janab Ibrahim and Isma'il... *tahir baytiya lil-ta'ifina wal-'akifina wal-rukka'i al-sujud* (purify My House for those who circumambulate and those who are devoted and those who bow and prostrate). For them, we... this House has been purified. Janab Ibrahim and Isma'il built it. You circumambulate this House. These things were not like this. अरे, this House, as you know, *inna awwala baytin wudi'a lil-nasi lalladhi bi-bakkata mubarakan* (Indeed, the first House [of worship] established for mankind was that at Bakkah - blessed). This was God's first house. Are, Kamru-te-Azam was born here. And its glory and majesty was that the first point of the *Tamur* came here. It's not as the Shi'a say, that because 'Ali was born here, the Ka'ba gained honor. No, no. Of course, in its own place, this honor is very true, but 'Ali being born in the Ka'ba is an honor because the first *ibda'* (origination) was born there, he was born there, Janab 'Ali. This is certainly an honor, there is no doubt in it. But along with that honor, this thing is also necessary. So, the world of Islam took it that this... what is Hajj? It is the memorials of Ibrahim. Janab Ibrahim, when he was taking Janab Isma'il for sacrifice, Shaytan met him on the way. And I always tell you that Shaytan's biggest job is what? To stop. To stop from a good deed. He said, "Ibrahim, what are you doing? You are going to cut your beloved son? You are going to kill him? What is this? What are you doing?" At that time, you picked up a stone and threw it, and said, "May Allah's curse be upon you. You stop me from a good deed." Then he went further, another Shaytan came, you threw a stone at him too. A third Shaytan came, you threw at him too. So they say, look, three Shaytans had come, that is why three Shaytan pillars were made, and stoning those idols in this way became a memorial of Ibrahim. Apparently, it is certainly correct, but in the inner (*batin*), there are great depths. These are manholes. All the corrupt things that are going on in the world, you don't open the entire sewer, you open the manhole and look. So this, in their respective places... whatever doubts arose in the time of Nuh, in every era, the three who have been, Qarun and Haman and Fir'awn, you see them in their place. There is mention of these three. In this way, all who have been, in their own place, these are their residual bodies, their dirty bodies' locations. And when you throw a stone at them, reciting the prayer, then you should be certain that nature does this: that the bullet that you will fire from a gun will not have that effect which that pebble will have, whether it hits or not, but it will have an effect. It will have an effect, and nature... at that time, when it is meant to be hit, it is like a living human being, that idol is standing there. You see it as a stone pillar, but in reality, it is alive. And the blow lands on it, and it feels the blow. And nature wants it to be hit. And the blow lands. So anyway, the matters of Hajj are different. What to go into those details for. In any case, all this happens. So, it happened in the apparent, and it happened in the inner. And this was the kind of incident with Hazrat Ibrahim, and Janab... Hazrat Isma'il. And then Janab Ibrahim, searching for his son, reached there. So, reaching the Baytullah, you took Janab Isma'il and you, taking him there, in building this House... *li-l-ta'ifina wal-'akifina wal-rukka'i al-sujud*. Allah Ta'ala says, "*Tahir baytiya* (Purify My House)..." Meaning, they built this House for Allah. *Wa idh yarfa'u ibrahimu al-qawa'ida min al-bayti* (And [mention] when Ibrahim was raising the foundations of the House). They raised the House high. They built that House, Janab Ibrahim. And for whom did they purify the House? For all those who perform *tawaf*, who bow, who prostrate, for their sake, it was purified and cleaned, and built. Even today, that place where Janab Ibrahim stood and built, where the marks of his blessed feet are, that is the Station of Ibrahim (*Maqam-e-Ibrahim*). It is a great sign (*mash'ar-e-'izam*). And today, the entire world of Islam that is misguided... misguided... the state of the world of Islam is that that Baytullah, which is Allah's most blessed House, there Allah Ta'ala has kept only one grave. And whose grave is that? Hazrat Isma'il's. The grave of Hazrat Isma'il, Zabihullah (the one sacrificed to Allah), is right there. And where is that grave? It is in that arch, which is under the *mizab* (waterspout). That is why the *tawaf* is done from the outside, but despite that, Muslims enter inside, they recite prayers there, they trample the grave with their feet. That is why it is forbidden for us to... from inside... only at the time of Hajj, to make the intention under the *mizab-e-rahmat* (waterspout of mercy) is allowed. Otherwise, it is not, because that is the grave of Janab Isma'il. That small crescent, that part which is between the *rukn-e-shami* and *rukn-e-'iraqi*, that arch that is built, that crescent, inside that crescent, Hazrat Isma'il is buried. You understand? So in any case, these wonders happened, many such wonders. And it happened in this way. And Hazrat Ibrahim, 'alayhi al-salatu wa-salam, distributed his spiritual lights (*anwar*) in such a way that he gave this to Janab Ishaq, and he gave that to Janab Isma'il. But you wanted that just as all these things are being given by me, you, in your own time, also wanted to acquire them in the same way. One thing that happens is that you think an Imam, whether a child or an adult or whatever, an Imam is an Imam, what need is there for him to read or write? No, no. Just as nature desires, in the same way, a child will have to read, he will have to write, he will have to learn. The entire process will be the same as it is for our children. Why so? Because he has to present the character of a human being before us. He has to present the character of a human being. That is why, when I will mention the Prophet of Allah, sallallahu 'alayhi wa-sallam, the biggest misguidance in the world of Islam is regarding the Prophet, that they call the Prophet the *nabi-e-ummi* (the unlettered prophet). Na'udhubillah, na'udhubillah (God forbid), they call him an ignorant prophet. They say that this is the greatness of the Prophet, that the Prophet, 'alayhi al-salatu wa-salam, despite being ignorant, taught all the people, the entire world of Islam. So they consider this a sign of greatness, but they don't understand that this is a great insult. Na'udhubillah, it is to be insolent in the honor of the Prophet. The Prophet, 'alayhi al-salatu wa-salam, was a tremendous scholar. And what can be said about the knowledge of the Prophet? Whose knowledge can compare to the Prophet's knowledge? And the Prophet's knowledge, how was it? He had learned it. There are teachers, there is a school, there is a madrasa, everything, Insha'Allah, when the mention of the Prophet comes, I will tell you. Where he read and where he learned, who the teachers were, what was the age, what he was learning. It will all come. But in the same way, Hazrat Ibrahim, the ancestor of the Prophet, the Prophet's grandfather, he also learned in the same way. In the same way, you also received education, and how did you receive that education? You, at that time, you received education in such a way that you... first of all, as the Qur'an-e Majid mentions, that at that time, because *kahanat-parasti* (soothsaying-worship) was very prevalent, at that time, *sitara-parasti* (star-worship) was very prevalent. So in the story of Hazrat Ibrahim, it comes in this way, that you saw the star, and said, "*Qala hadha rabbi* (He said, 'This is my Lord')." "This is my Lord." *Fa-lamma afala qala la uhibbu al-afilin* (But when it set, he said, "I do not love those who set"). When that star set, he said, "I don't like those who set." *Fa-lamma ra'a al-qamara bazighan qala hadha rabbi* (And when he saw the moon rising, he said, "This is my Lord"). When he saw the moon, he said, "*Hadha rabbi*. This is my Lord. It is absolutely certain. This big moon is surely my God." *Fa-lamma afala qala la uhibbu al-afilin* (But when it set, he said, "I do not love those who set"). "I don't like those who set." The Qur'an is mentioning this. *Fa-lamma ra'a al-shamsa bazighatan qala hadha rabbi hadha akbar* (And when he saw the sun rising, he said, "This is my Lord; this is greater"). When he saw the sun, so bright and so luminous, he said, "*Hadha akbar* (This is greater). This is very big." And he said that this... this is surely God. And after that, he says that *la-in lam yahdini rabbi la-akunanna min al-qawm al-dhalimin* (if my Lord had not guided me, I would have been among the erring people). "If my Lord does not guide me, I will be among the wrongdoers." Now you should laugh and cry at the state of the world of Islam. Whatever you do, but the entire world of Islam says that this Janab Ibrahim, according to the custom of that time, he called the star God, and when it set, he left it. Then he called the moon God, and when it set, he was disillusioned. Then he called the sun God, but it also... but then what? In this way... but Janab Ibrahim could not understand, and such things happened to him as was the talk of that time. And so Janab Ibrahim's state was also like that, and he remained misguided, but then Allah Ta'ala guided him, because he had to be made a messenger, a prophet, that is why Allah Ta'ala kept guiding him. All these things are not so. And for God's Imam to have such things said about him, it is not so. Are, this is presenting the nature of a human being, Allah Ta'ala is. And Hazrat Ibrahim's matters are being presented, how his education and upbringing was in his childhood. You, when you first saw the star... this star is Janab Hud. The great personality of that time, whose name was Hud. That Hud, when he came as a teacher to you and began to teach Janab Ibrahim, you began to say that this teacher... just as these incidents happen to you and me, that we consider the teacher an angel. "What a teacher we have, he is a treasure trove of all knowledge, and how excellently he knows." Just as we form a conception about our teacher, in the same way, Janab Ibrahim's conception for Janab Hud was that he is everything. *Fa-lamma afala*, when they set, meaning when Ibrahim became proficient in that knowledge and reached the level of his teacher's knowledge, and Janab Ibrahim saw that "Are, this is nothing, there are many scholars above him. This is like the camel who saw its own height under the mountain. Now what is his status? Are, this..." *Fa-lamma afala*, they set. So he said, "I don't like those who set." Meaning, "I don't like those who limit knowledge. I want knowledge to soar." Allah Ta'ala says, "*fawqa kulli dhi 'ilmin 'alim* (And above every possessor of knowledge is a Knower)." Above every scholar, there is another scholar. So in this way, above every scholar, there is another scholar. So that meant exactly this. That Janab Ibrahim, what did he do after that? He saw the moon. What is the moon? That is Janab, who were the great personalities of your time, whose name was Salih. That great personality was your teacher, and he started your education and upbringing. Now he started their education. And when their education was finished, he said, "Brother, I was thinking that he is everything. Now he is also finished. He was a great teacher, and that great teacher is also finished." So he said, "But I was thinking that he is everything, but he has also set." And after that, the sun of the universe shone. This is Janab Salih. Janab Salih's... who? Your own father. Your own father. Janab Salih is teaching and bringing you up. And when he finished teaching you, he said, "Ibrahim, now you have acquired everything." So after that, he says that if Allah Ta'ala at this time... all this has been acquired... now he too... this sun of the universe, I thought that he is everything, but my father has also taught me whatever he had to, I have understood everything. At that time, you say that if my Lord does not guide me, I will be among the misguided people. So it is known that, na'udhubillah, what the world of Islam gives the fatwa on, that Hazrat Ibrahim was going towards disbelief (*kufr*), and Allah Ta'ala saved him, did this, it was not like that. If it was a matter of *kufr*, as other great scholars of Islam have applied this word to Janab Ibrahim, have done this injustice, that he was going towards *kufr*, it was not like that. If he was going towards *kufr*, then why did Allah Ta'ala present the words of Janab Ibrahim, *la-in lam yahdini rabbi la-akunanna min al-qawm al-dhalimin*? That "if I... if I... if my Lord does not guide me, I will be among the wrongdoers."

These matters were all of teachers and of his studentship. And after that, you received guidance, and you were honored with Imamat. So these were matters of education and upbringing, which were stages you had completed. Janab Ibrahim. Just as the ancestor of the Prophet, Hazrat Ibrahim Khalil al-Rahman, completed it, in the same way, our Prophet, 'alayhi al-salatu wa-salam, also, when those incidents befell him, you also completed them. And you fulfilled them completely. When the mention of the Prophet comes, I will tell you how you completed them. But nature wants that just as a life story is presented, the entire life story should be presented. There should be war and battle, there should be struggles, there should be illness, there should be travel, there should be migration, one should also be beaten, one should also be whipped, everything should happen. There should be comfort, Gabriel should also descend, there should be a Mi'raj, everything should happen. A life story should be presented. And there should also be miracles, that you are left at a crossroads, wondering what kind of personality this is. So, for the life story to come before us, it was presented in this way, and every prophet left his life story in this way, so that it would be a source of guidance for us. If only those from the Tamur had come here to the world and had come in that state only, in a spiritual state, in an intellectual state, and had given a call, "Come, O people, and accept our guidance," then you would see that if such a voice came here, what would happen? The entire group here would leave the house. "Oh brother, it seems there is some problem here." And the matters that are seen are different. The matters that are seen are different. Voices are coming from here and there. "What kind of thing is this? We have never heard such a voice. We are not ready to learn such a lesson." So you would neither learn the lesson nor would he give guidance. So the matter, in fact, is that Allah Ta'ala did not keep the method of giving guidance in this way. He sent them in human form so that we, as human beings, can take complete guidance from a human being, and understand and comprehend. And he also, before us, presents the same kind of life story. There is war, there is battle, there is illness, there is sickness, he laughs, he cries, there is assembly, there is poetry, all the incidents happen in the same way. Husayn is coming running, the court of the Prophet, 'alayhi al-salatu wa-salam, is assembled, and coming, the dates that are kept in the dish, and Janab Husayn comes and takes the dates and eats them. He is a child. And all the people are watching, saying that Husayn is a small child, he came, an innocent child, and took the dates and ate them. It is a completely innocent manner, a gesture. He must have eaten. But the Prophet, 'alayhi al-salatu wa-salam, says, "O Husayn, look, charity (*zakat*) is forbidden (*haram*) for us. What have you done? How did you put this in your mouth?" Although he is a child, the Prophet is saying so... but if the Prophet said this, why? Because he wanted to inform the Ummah, so that this thing is noted, and it is told, "Look, *zakat* is forbidden for the Ahl al-Bayt." And you put your hand in his mouth and took out the date with the saliva and threw it, saying, "No, this is forbidden for us." So, did Husayn not know this? अरे, Husayn knew. He knowingly came and ate, and this was all a complete understanding between them. This is all a matter of understanding. That "we will eat, and you will take it out." So that such a precedent is set in the world, such a thing happens, so that all the people know that such and such a thing happens. When Janab Mufaddal... Janab Mufaddal, who is the Babul-Abwab of Janab Ja'far al-Sadiq, 'alayhi al-salatu wa-salam, who is the highest personality, you are coming with whom? With Janab... with Janab Ja'far al-Sadiq, 'alayhi al-salatu wa-salam... he was the Babul-Abwab, but you were the *kalb* (dog/servant), but you were the Babul-Abwab of Maulana Zain al-Abidin, 'Ali Zain al-Abidin. You come, Maulana 'Ali Zain al-Abidin is performing Hajj. As soon as he is performing Hajj and circumambulating, what happens? First of all, you kiss the Hajar al-Aswad (Black Stone). As soon as you go to kiss it, the people part like moss, just as moss parts on water, they part like that, and he goes. Hashim bin 'Abd al-Malik is standing there and watching with great amazement. And he recognized that this is Imam 'Ali Zain al-Abidin, the son of Imam Husayn. The son of the Imam is the Imam. These are the grandsons of Janab 'Ali. He understood, Hashim bin 'Abd al-Malik. But because of the pride of his state, he asks his courtiers, "The king of the time... he asks his courtiers, 'Brother, who is this? Who is this?'" See the pretended ignorance. "And... who is he, what is this? He is being given so much respect. What is this?" So at that very moment, Farazdaq, the poet, was there. And Farazdaq, the poet, could not bear it. He came forward and says, "O Hashim, you don't know him? अरे, *hadha alladhi ta'rifu al-batha'u wat'atahu wal-baytu ya'rifuhu wal-hillu wal-haramu* (This is he whose footstep the valley knows, and the House knows him, and the sacred and the profane precincts). Are, this... you don't know this personality? Are, him... the Ka'ba knows him. And him... the place which is lawful (*hill*) and the place where one has to wear the *ehram*, they know him." And the ode (*qasida*) that Farazdaq began to recite, what can be said of that ode? *Zahabiya*, which is written with golden water, meaning the golden ode, it is called. And he recited tremendous verses. So when he started reciting the verses, he says while reciting, that these are the personalities from whose mouths the word *la* (no) has never come out. The word *la*, meaning 'no', has never come out. To refuse a supplicant is not in their nature. These are people of generosity and bounty (*jood-o-bakhshish*). Their hands have always been open. So, *ma qala la qattu illa fi tashahhudihi lawla al-tashahhudu kanat la'uhu na'amu* (He never said 'no' except in his Tashahhud; were it not for the Tashahhud, his 'no' would have been 'yes'). They never said 'no'. And in the *tashahhud*, if the word *la* in *la ilaha illa allah* did not come, they would have never said the word *la* in their entire lives. Did you see what a verse he recited? He said that in the *tashahhud*, if... if in reciting the Kalima Tayyiba, the word *la* did not come, they would have never uttered the word *la* from their mouths in their lives. So he was startled. And he said, "Farazdaq, you are my stipendiary (*wazifa-khwar*), you are from my courtiers, but you have never written such an ode in my praise." He said, "Brother, I am certainly, O king, your stipendiary, I am everything. You too, develop those qualities in yourself that are in the Ahl al-Bayt. I am ready to write that ode for you too." Develop those qualities. At that time, he was imprisoned. And after that, as soon as Maulana 'Ali Zain al-Abidin found out, you sent a sum of money with a slave, that... the slave kissed his feet, Farazdaq's, and said, "But I have recited the ode in the praise of the Imam. I have not said it for the sake of money." Anyway, he did not accept the gift and placed the Imam's letter on his head. So these incidents happened. At that time, Mufaddal was also with you, and Mufaddal was circumambulating. While circumambulating, look, this is an incident to be heard with great attention. Since it is an incident of Hajj, and it is connected to Ibrahim, I am mentioning this incident. Now, Janab Ibrahim... Janab 'Ali Zain al-Abidin is circumambulating. The Imam is circumambulating. Are, the one who is the intended of the Ka'ba, he himself is the Ka'ba. He himself is the Ka'ba. The Imam is the intended of the Ka'ba. You are circumambulating. But why are you circumambulating? Because this is the Ka'ba which is the station of Kamru-te-Azam. Do you understand? That is why he also has to be given respect. So the Imam is circumambulating, and behind him, Janab Mufaddal is also circumambulating. While circumambulating, he says, "O Maula, so many people are circumambulating. This *haram* (sanctuary) is full. And this Kalima that they are reciting, *ashhadu an la ilaha illa allah wa ashhadu anna muhammadan rasulullah*... these countless people, this vast crowd (*jam'e ghafir*), and this outward appearance of Muslims, this outward appearance, this devoted manner, this Muslims' heart is bowed, and towards Allah's Ka'ba, and everyone is seeking their forgiveness and praying. Can we... O Imam, can we call them misguided? All these Muslims, all these Muslims who have come to this pure House of God with pure intentions, seeking their forgiveness, can we call them misguided, O Imam?" You said, "O Mufaddal, if you call them pure and clean, then where will Allah's justice (*'adl*) and fairness (*insaf*) be? Where will Allah's justice be? How will Allah dispense justice? What justice will there be for the believers (*momineen*)? Those who have received instruction sitting on the sackcloth of the believers, who have passed their time in great difficulties, who, with 'Ali, ate the barley bread (*sattu*), and who used to break it on their knee, that 'Ali, Amir al-Momineen, and who used to put it in water and eat it. And the difficulties they endured, for their entire lives they endured difficulties and kept the name of Islam high. There are thousands of such incidents which I can tell you. And you know them." So all these incidents... then what, after all, Maula? Will these Muslims be dealt with in this way? So you said this, "Look, Mufaddal, it's not that Allah Ta'ala closes his doors on anyone. But whoever is to be given a place, that place is given. Allah's justice is in its place, established and flowing. You just close your eyes." And this was a moment of قیامت (judgment/greatness) which Janab 'Ali Zain al-Abidin said to Janab Mufaddal. He said, "Maula, you command and I will close my eyes." "Yes," he said, "just close your eyes." He closed his eyes, and he said, "Alright, O Mufaddal, now open your eyes." He opens his eyes and sees that there are camels, there are goats, they are all roaming around. He said, "Maula, what is this?" He said, "Just, Mufaddal..." And then he placed his hand on his eyes again, and then removed it. Again he sees that the same crowd is present. Did you see? What was the matter in fact? That you were explaining that "as you are, so is God." "As you are, so is God." Whether they come to the *haram*, so what? Whether they read the Qur'an, so what? Whether they become a Hafiz, so what? Whether they wear the cloak of paper, so what? Whether they bathe in Zamzam, so what? Nothing happens. Without the love of 'Ali and the progeny of 'Ali, not even a leaf moves. The people of Tamur will have to be accepted. And that entire chain will have to be accepted. If even one link is missing, then there will be no name of salvation from anywhere. So you are understanding the chain from the beginning. So the chain is from there. The poet says, "The world is not a vegetable garden. The people of the Prophet are the people of 'Ali, the people of 'Ali are the people of God." "The people of the Prophet are the people of 'Ali, the people of 'Ali are the people of God." So that was the reality of the matter. And these... the matter was, in fact, this: that these were not just the memorials of Ibrahim, but in them were Allah's great signs (*ayat*), great miracles (*bahirat*), the great symbols of Allah (*sha'a'ir-e-'izam*), as the Qur'an calls them. That in these are great, great signs. These are our great signs. Do not consider these things ordinary. So what are this Safa and Marwa? In them are great events hidden. What can I explain to you about Safa and Marwa? And in between this running, what can I tell you? And this Baytullah, and the key of Baytullah, that *miftah*, which is called the Hajar al-Aswad, is a great event. What can I tell you, what is in that *miftah*? That the essence of the entire Baytullah is right there. The entire key is that Hajar al-Aswad. For which Hajar al-Aswad I have told you what was done to it. The same was done as was done to 'Ali. What was done to 'Ali in the apparent, the same was done to the Hajar al-Aswad. This, instead of being in the Baytullah (House of God), was in the *bayt-ul-khala* (toilet). It has been in the *bayt-ul-khala*. It has been tied in the *hammam* (bathhouse). And it has been hit with a catapult (*ghofan*), it has been broken. Otherwise, this stone was one piece. And this blackness that it has today, why is it? These are the deeds of the Ummah. Their all black deeds, because of which it is a mirror. And in that mirror, their deeds are being reflected, due to which it is black. Otherwise, when the Dour-e-Kashf (Era of Unveiling) comes, it will become like a white stone, like snow, and will shine. In the Dour-e-Kashf, it will be that shiny. But today that black stone that is made, it is our reflection falling on it, our sins. It is our sins that are reflecting on it and making it black. So this, you have to make a covenant there. You have to shake hands with it. I mean, you read the prayers, at least translate them. You have to stand near it and pray, and all that. I am telling you that for every person who kisses it, there are different curtains for him. There are different covers for him. Different shutters are falling. You have so many wonders of electronics in the world, what will you say about the electronics of nature? What will you say about that greatness, which has given you this power, has given you a jewel like intellect, because of which you are doing so many miraculous things? Then that Lord of the Worlds, the chemistry He must have done, the factory of the universe He must have created, and His factory of life, Mecca the Honored, and His Ka'ba the Sacred, and the Hajar al-Aswad He must have made, what great events must be hidden in it? Tell me. And do you consider this pillar (*rukn*) an ordinary pillar? Do you consider these walls of stone and lime? Or Janab 'Umar, as he came and said, "O stone, you neither give benefit nor harm. The Prophet kissed you, so I will also kiss you." Do we also, na'udhubillah, say the same? No, it cannot be so. It cannot happen. So in any case, so you have seen, you have received some guidance and some light, and your mind has started working. That that *hatim* is also something. Are, that *hatim*, that *hijr-e-isma'il*, *hijr-e-isma'il* you have said, but you haven't understood what it is. That *hijr-e-isma'il*, why was that crescent made? You pass by all places, but you have to go from outside that crescent, not past these walls. Because the grave of Isma'il is there. The grave of Janab Isma'il is kept there. Why is it kept there? There must be some reasons for it, which nature wanted, and it did. The relics of Janab Ibrahim are kept there, which is called the *Maqam-e-Ibrahim*, where you have to pray two rak'at, otherwise your *shawk* (desire/effort) is not accepted, the *tawaf* is not accepted. You have to perform two rak'at of prayer. And in this way... and then you have to come to the place of Zamzam and drink two sips. So all these are great signs, great depths. And among these depths, one great depth is that *mizab-e-rahmat* (waterspout of mercy). That waterspout, although since it is of the Ka'ba, you have said that since it is of the sacred Ka'ba, it should be made of gold. No, no, nature also wanted that this most magnificent waterspout... its greatness should be manifest in the world as well. Nature wanted it, and people also wanted that waterspout to be made of gold. It was made of gold, and it matched its greatness, and that waterspout has great importance. It is not an ordinary waterspout. That waterspout has great importance, and it is under it that we have to make the intention for Hajj. It is under it that we have to make the intention. And this *mizab-e-rahmat*... people's condition is what? The Prophet had said to understand its inner meaning, what this *mizab-e-rahmat* is, and after all, why was this *mizab* made? What is meant by this *mizab-e-rahmat*? And they left that, and what did all the Muslims do? Now they are sitting, waiting in the rainy season, leaning against the wall. I have also seen many people sitting there. "Brother, why are you waiting?" "The clouds have come, so we are sitting." "So what, the clouds have come, so you are sitting? The Ka'ba is open at that time." "The clouds have come." "No, brother, we are waiting for the water, for it to rain, so we are sitting." So I said, "What if it rains, what's the big deal?" Meaning, if it rains, mercy will come, otherwise mercy will not come? "No, no, that's not the point. The point is that the water on top of the Ka'ba should collect, and after collecting, it should fall from this waterspout. And when it falls, we should bathe in it, so it will be as if all our sins have been washed away." Washed away, became pure and clean. There you go. Did you see? So bathing under the waterspout means what? Washed away from sins. One is that, and one is the *Jabal-e-Rahmat* (Mountain of Mercy). If you descend from it, then, the Prophet had said, all sins will be cleaned. Our all sins have been shed and cleaned. They have fallen off like leaves fall in autumn. The Prophet had certainly said it, but he had not said that the major sins (*kaba'ir*) would also be washed away. The major sins, which I have counted as five sins, those sins are not easily removed. These are scratches that have occurred. To remove these scratches, you will have to fast. To remove these scratches, you will have to give expiation. To remove these scratches, you will have to give charity. You will have to kill your ego. If you don't want to kill it and expect the color to be bright... no, it can't happen like that. You will have to do it, and if you do, you will be successful. Allah Ta'ala is certainly *Tawwab-ur-Rahim* (the Most Forgiving, the Most Merciful), but forgiveness is with the conditions of the seeker. Forgiveness must also be sought in that way. So, it is apparent that in this way, one should seek forgiveness. So in any case, I was saying that these memorials of Janab Ibrahim were not just that, but they were Allah's great... in them were great purposes hidden, and great majesty was hidden in them. Insha'Allah, if I get a chance, I will talk about it in the context of Hajj. But for now, the story of the prophets is ongoing. So I was saying that Hazrat Ibrahim Khalil al-Rahman, the Imam, after him, to whom did he entrust the Imamat? To his son, Janab Isma'il, who was the younger. To his younger son, Janab Isma'il, he gave the Imamat, whose son was who? Janab Qayzar. And whose son was Janab Finhas. And whose son was Janab Salamat. And whose son was Janab Hamaisa'. And after that, the chain continued uninterrupted, of the ancestors of the Prophet. There was Qusayy, there was Kilab. In any case, the chain continued, the chain of Imamat remained. This is the chain of the Imams. They are the masters of the universe. They are not just of the universe, but of all the universes, they are the masters, whom God has entrusted His divinity to. And the chain of prophets also continued in the same way. The messengers who, taking the apostleship, or as ambassadors from them, who were taking the apostleship from them, who were becoming prophets, they were also in their own place, fulfilling the duties of prophethood and apostleship. There was Ayyub, there was Yusuf, all these prophets in their own place were established, and the chain continued in this way.

Last time I had stated that regarding Hadrat Ibrahim Khalil al-Rahman, his status was not only that of a Nabi (prophet), but he also had the status of an Imam. And his father, Maulana Salih, had established him. And he himself established a Nabi and Rasul (messenger) whose name was also Ibrahim. And the Quran Majid refers to this when it says, *"rajulun yuqalu lahu Ibrahim"* (a man called Ibrahim). This was Janab Ibrahim. And you heard all his stories. And the Imam, 'alayhi al-salat wa al-salam (peace and blessings be upon him), after him, raised his son, Janab Isma'il, and honored him with the Imamat. From the son of Janab Ibrahim, Janab Isma'il, then Ayyub, Ya'qub, Yusuf... this chain continued. And this continuing chain reached where? It reached Maulana Uz. A thousand years had passed. And then Allah Ta'ala said, just as a thousand years after Adam, Janab Nuh was established. And who established him? Janab Hud. And similarly, after a thousand years, Maulana Salih came, and Maulana Salih established Janab Ibrahim. And Janab Ibrahim, in his place, established whom? A Nabi whose name was also Ibrahim. In the same way, a thousand years of Janab Ibrahim 'alayhi al-salat wa al-salam had passed. And the people who were performing bay'ah (pledge of allegiance) with you were very few, but those who were not performing bay'ah, who were not accepting Janab Ibrahim, who had not brought faith in the qawl (word) of Ibrahim, what was their state? They were... as it is said, *"Ma hadhihi al-tamathilu allati antum laha 'akifun"* (What are these statues to which you are devoted?). What has happened to you that you worship idols and are engaged in but-parasti (idol-worship)? Kahanat-parasti (worship of priests), but-parasti, sitara-parasti (worship of stars)... all these things and tawahhumat (delusions) were being created in great numbers. And the disease was spreading and growing. And this condition, growing and growing, made great progress in a thousand years. And the time of Hadrat Musa came. And at this time, among the offspring of Janab Ibrahim, such as Janab Isma'il... Janab Isma'il's son was Janab Finhas; he is an Imam. And Janab Ya'qub... Ishaq's two sons were Janab Ayyub, Ya'qub, etc. This is the chain of Ambiya' (prophets). This is the chain of A'immah (Imams). The chain of Imams, after Janab Isma'il, continuing... and from Finhas, continuing, reached where? Janab Uz. Alif Dal, Uz. Maulana Uz, salawatullah 'alayh (blessings of Allah be upon him), was the Imam-e-Waqt (Imam of the time). And he saw that now a time has come for me to send a Nabi-e-Mursal (sent prophet). It is necessary to send a Nabi-e-Mursal and give them a book, so that they may take that book and work in the world as a natiq nabi (speaking prophet) and perform the duties of risalat (prophethood), and establish the shari'ah. So they, Janab Uz, indicated for Janab Musa 'alayhi al-salat wa al-salam, that now Janab Musa should be honored with nubuwwat (prophethood). Now, before selecting Janab Musa, it is a strange work of qudrat (divine power) that the stories of Hadrat Musa 'alayhi al-salat wa al-salam himself are so vast and extensive that in the Quran Majid, if you pick up any para' (part), you will see that the story of Hadrat Musa is present. Some mention or other is there. Hadrat Musa is dominant throughout the Quran Majid. So he was so jalil al-qadr (of great stature). This means he became a prophet of very great stature and surpassed all prophets. It's not like that, but his stories are many. And the second thing was that there was great haybat (awe) in Janab Musa. His jalal (majesty) was tremendous. And for this reason, this aspect was very pleasing to Allah Ta'ala. The Lord of the Worlds narrated his stories with great detail in the Quran Majid. All the details are present in the Quran Majid. But what had happened was that this child, whose name is Musa, who was born in the house of 'Imran... his father's name was 'Imran. This son, Musa, was born to Hadrat 'Imran. And when this boy was born to them, it so happened... it so happened that at that time, the rule of the Fara'inah (Pharaohs) was in place. The rule of the Pharaohs of Egypt was ongoing. And the Fir'aun (Pharaoh) of that time, his name was Walid ibn Mus'ab. Walid ibn Mus'ab. Mus'ab was his father's name, his own name was Walid. Walid ibn Mus'ab was the king at that time. And he had a great belief and trust in nujum (astrology). As I told you, the entire nation was in misguidance. Ramal, Jafr (forms of divination), and these things that are coming to us today, this is the demand of the time. Because the era is ending, so sitr (concealment) is coming. And within sitr, fitrat (nature/disposition) is coming. Fitrat, meaning the lamp, when it is about to be extinguished, it flickers brightly before it goes out. That is our condition. Now misguidance is increasing more. So in the same way, in that era, misguidance was slowly increasing. And who was the first victim of that misguidance? The king himself. Because he had money, kingdom, treasures... he had everything. So he was the first victim. And he, Fir'aun, called the astrologers and asked, "What is the matter? Look in the stars about me, whether I will have a son or not. I have been desiring a son for a long time, but I have not had a son." They said, "O King, what desire for a son are you holding? We are seeing..." They told Fir'aun, whose name was Walid ibn Mus'ab. The astrologers told him, "O King, we are seeing that a boy will be born in your kingdom who will destroy your kingdom. He will ruin your kingdom, and such a person is coming, we are seeing this in the stars." Fir'aun became very upset. "How can this be?" So he could only think of one thing, and his advisors gave him this advice: to carry out a massacre of all the children. So he ordered a massacre, that any child born this year should be killed and finished. So, a massacre began. Whichever house had a boy, they started killing them. What can you ask of a king's command? The massacre started. The mother of Hadrat Musa became very worried. And taking permission from Janab 'Imran, she left with her child. And after leaving, she had not even named that child yet. Pay attention. She had not even named her child yet. The order was issued, and she became worried, the mother of Janab Musa. And coming, she saw that she couldn't understand what to do. So she said, "O Allah, what should I do for my child? You alone guide me." Allah Ta'ala sent a wahi (revelation) to Janab Umm-e-Musa (Mother of Moses) and said, *"an iqdhifihi fi al-yamm"* (Cast him into the river). Cast him into the Nile. O Mother of Moses, this was a wahi. To the mother of Janab Musa. So it became known that wahi also comes to the honeybee, it comes to many people, it comes to the mother of Musa. Wahi is not a special characteristic [of prophets alone]. It does come to prophets, to every prophet and messenger, but the wahi that came to you [Prophet Muhammad] was in the most excellent way. But wahi is always a divine path, a divine method. [unclear] made arrangements for the police, etc. and Janab Musa got the news of it, and he left from there. And he left straight away. And it was destined by Allah that you would become a prophet of Allah. So leaving from there, you went straight on, took another path, and went far from the palace. When you went far from the palace, there you met a person. You met a person, about whom it is said, *"wa fajadna... 'abdan min 'ibadina ataynahu... rahmatan minna... min ladunna rahmah"* (And We found a servant from among Our servants whom We had given mercy from Us). Allah Ta'ala says that they, Janab Musa, found a man from among the servants. *"fa-wajada 'abdan min 'ibadina ataynahu rahmatan min 'indina wa-'allamnahu min ladunna 'ilma"* (and he found a servant from among Our servants to whom We had given mercy from Us and had taught him knowledge from Our own presence). That We had given him mercy from Our presence and We had bestowed knowledge upon him. Now, regarding this personality, all the mufassirin (exegetes) write that it was Khidr, 'alayhi al-salat wa al-salam, whom Janab Musa met. Although it has nothing to do with Khidr. Hadrat Musa... the Hudud-e-Da'wat (Ranks of the Mission) who were there, Janab Uz, who is the Imam-e-Waqt, from his da'wat (mission), he met a hadd (rank-holder). Who... Janab Musa was already a din-dar (religious person) from birth. Obviously, such a jalil al-qadr personality, how could he not be religious? He was a din-dar. As soon as you found a person who could give you some talqin (instruction), you said, "Brother, you seem to be a great scholar. Give me permission to stay with you and learn and study with you." He said, "O Musa, I... find you to be a good person. I am surely ready to keep you with me. But it seems to me, *"lan tastati'a ma'iya sabra"* (you will not be able to have patience with me). You will stay with me, but you will not be able to have patience. The things I will do, you will not be able to be patient with them." This is the incident which is narrated in detail in the Quran Majid. Now, Hadrat Musa joined him. He set a condition that he would have to be patient. He said, "I will be patient." And Musa, however, was unsuccessful in his patience. Now, he, with that hadd-e-'ali (high-ranking person), who was called Khidr, Janab Musa went. As they were going, the hadd-e-'ali who was with you, he boarded a boat. He boarded a boat. He asked, "Brother, are you traveling on the river?" He said, "Yes, I am traveling on the river." "Alright, wherever you go, I am ready to go with you." Musa joined him. And going forward, after the river journey ended, as soon as they disembarked at a place and reached the shore, they saw some children playing. Many children were playing together like this. From among them, he caught one child. Who? That hadd-e-'ali caught the child and after catching him, killed him. These are all stories from the Quran Majid. Now, as soon as he killed him, Hadrat Musa became worried. Seeing the murder, he said, "What is this? You have committed a terrible act! This child was playing, and you caught him and killed him. What is this matter?" He said, "Look, Musa, I told you before that you will not be able to be patient. And yet you objected. Although I was going to tell you everything." Now, you see. After that, he said again, *"lan tastati'a ma'iya sabra"* (you will not be able to have patience with me). You will not be able to be patient with me again. Now Musa again pleaded and said, "Keep me with you." He joined him again. They went forward. After going forward, what happened was that when they reached a place, they saw that there was a house, but it was in a dilapidated state. The wall was somewhat standing, somewhat falling. It was lying in such a state. Hadrat... Janab... Khidr, who was your hadd-e-'ali, he... ...took some clay and lime and started building the wall, placing stones. And he told Musa, "Musa, help me." He said, "Brother, if you are sitting here doing this work, neither has anyone appointed you, nor are you doing it for wages, nor do you take wages. Why are you building this after all?" He said, "Then you objected again. Now, *"hadha firaqu bayni wa baynika"* (this is the parting between me and you). Now there is parting between me and you. Now go, Musa. Your path is separate, my path is separate. You... But..." Musa said, "Brother, alright, this is the third time it has happened. Now what greater mistake can I make? It has become a very big mistake, but at least tell me why you did all this." At that time he said, "Alright, I will tell you the ta'wil (inner meaning/interpretation) of this, Musa." So look, the entire Muslim world believes that the Quran Sharif does not have a ta'wil. This is such a great story of Hadrat Musa, and qudrat (divine power) itself narrates its ta'wil. Through whose tongue? Through the tongue of Khidr. And he says, "O Musa, that boat which I damaged, it was because on its shore, there was a king who used to seize the boats of these poor people in a usurping manner and take them. And I wanted a defect to appear in it so that he would see the defect and leave it alone. So that he would not usurp their boat." "Well, that child whom I killed, you object to me that murder is for murder, and you have killed an innocent person for no reason. You think he is innocent. Hey, I know more than you. I am seeing his reality, where he has come from, where he is going, who he himself is. I am seeing all this. And Musa, you don't know, his parents are mu'min (believers). Both his parents are believers. And they have immense faith, their faith is very strong. But this child of theirs is a kafir (unbeliever). And he wants to bring his parents also towards kufr (unbelief). And the poor parents are so weak that due to his coercion, they will also spoil their faith. I am afraid of this. So, to save their faith, I said that it would be better if this kafir is finished." And I... The one who had the authority, the one who had authority with qudrat, he used that authority. Just like the case of 'Ubaydullah al-Shi'i, whom the Imam, Maulana Mahdi Billah, salawatullah 'alayh, had killed. And you then led his prayer. So that incident, I am pointing towards that, that this was a similar matter, and you killed him. "Oh," Musa said, "Is that so? This was the matter." "Well, what about that wall you raised without wages? What was that?" You said, "Look, beneath it, there was the treasure of two children." There was some capital of two orphan children, and because the wall was dilapidated, that orphan children's treasure was coming out, and people would loot it, and those poor orphan children would not get their capital. That is why I raised the wall. "So that for some time, until they become adults, the wall provides support, and they get their things." So Musa said, "If only I had that much understanding, otherwise I would have stayed with you." He said, "No, now there is no question of it. You did not have patience, and this is the result, that you must go." So, this was the limit of the tarbiyat (training) of Janab Musa, and this training was happening. And Hadrat Musa was learning this training. That you, after that, you started receiving talqin, and you continued to travel, and you started receiving intellectual things. Tawhid (monotheism) and all these things, after understanding them well, you gained a good command over tawhid. And how to practice Allah Ta'ala's tawhid and what it is... all these things, since he was to be honored with nubuwwat, he was learning all this, and he was coming under the training of Allah Ta'ala and learning the training. So during this learning process, you passed by... this is also a strange incident that happened, that you were passing through a jungle. And in your hand, there was always a thick staff ('asa). And taking that stick, you were going through the jungle, and you saw that a shepherd was sitting under a tree. And he was combing the hair of his goat with his hands. And he was saying, "O Allah Miyan, O Allah Miyan, you also come. I will also, just as I am taking out the lice from this goat, I will also take out the lice from your hair and keep them. And I also love you very much, and I will also clean you of all the lice and make you very nice and good." When Janab Musa heard this, he was very surprised. "Hey, what kind of talk is this person doing? He thinks of God like his goat. And along with that, not just a goat, but he thinks there are lice in God's hair just like in the goat's hair. And he talks about taking them out." He got into a state of jalal (majesty), Janab Musa, and taking his staff, he went and stood furiously in front of him. And started saying, "What were you saying?" First, he got scared, "Who are you?" He said, "Brother, I am asking you, what is this you are babbling? This is kufr (unbelief). Why are you... This is kufr. What kind of kufr are you babbling? And what kind of blasphemous things are you saying?" He said, "What? What I was saying, was it wrong?" He said, "It is absolutely and completely wrong. Have you understood God to be like a goat? And on top of that, you even imagine lice in his hair. What kind of thought is this?" He said, "Is Allah Miyan not like my goat?" So what happened was that in that love and affection, he was engrossed in the love of Allah. And he was one who loved Allah very much. But he tore his collar and, just as a lover runs away, he also started running. Into the jungle. "I thought, O Allah Miyan, you would also be very beloved like my goat." And his entire universe was just the goat. "But you turned out to be something else." This state that happened, that the wahi that was coming to Janab Musa... ...the grace of Allah Ta'ala that was coming, the gazes of Janab Uz that were there, and the attention that Janab Uz was giving to Janab Musa, all of that attention broke. When it stopped, Musa became worried. "What happened? The talqinat that were happening, all that was happening, the knowledge I was getting, the teacher I was getting... all this guidance... all these things have stopped. What is the matter? Why has the wahi stopped?" He became worried and then pleaded towards Allah. Now where is he turning? He is turning towards Janab Uz. "O my Master, what is the matter that there is no emanation upon me? These blessings are not upon me. What is the matter?" He said, "Musa, a servant of mine, my beloved servant, he was remembering me in some form or another." Look, here the purpose is not from Uz. Here it is from that Allah Himself. That Lord who is not there, who creates from there. "He was remembering his God in some way, but he was remembering, wasn't he? He was remembering me in some form, wasn't he? But you stopped him from that remembrance." So, this act was not pleasing to God. And the wahi to Janab Musa stopped. So, one who is absorbed in the love of Allah cannot be stopped. He was loving for the sake of Allah. He was doing it for the sake of Allah. So he was... How much was his intellect after all? O Musa, how much was his intellect? His entire capital... he was a shepherd. His entire capital, his universe, was all these goats. And he understood God to be like his goat, so what can you do? You wanted to give him such a great intellect, so what would happen? That is why the Prophet said, *"kallimu al-nasa 'ala qadri 'uqulihim"* (Speak to people according to their level of understanding). Whatever you say to people, say it according to their intellect. If you say more than their intellect, it will become a problem for them, they will not understand the burden. You will not be able to make them understand. So this was the matter of Janab Musa. And Musa was going through such experiences. Now, experiencing these things, now Musa... you were commanded by Janab Uz to go towards our Shu'ayb. You were commanded to go to Shu'ayb Nabi, by Janab Uz, the Imam of the time. And at that time, the last prophet... among the very last prophets of Hadrat Ibrahim Khalil al-Rahman was Janab Shu'ayb. And he was commanded to go towards Shu'ayb. Who? Janab Musa. Hadrat Musa 'alayhi al-salat wa al-salam said, "Okay, I have been commanded to learn. I am going and I will go to Shu'ayb and learn from him." So Shu'ayb Nabi used to live in a village at one place. He reached there. As soon as he reached there... first of all, in a village, you know, when one goes to a village, there is a well (bawli) or a water-place (panghat). So there too, a well came. And as soon as he reached the well, Janab Musa thought, "Let me also drink some water." But he saw that there was a line there. Every... some girls were standing. All of them were taking their goats to make them drink water. Now, Hadrat Musa saw that two girls had been standing for a long time, but they were not getting a chance. And other people were making their goats drink water and leaving. These poor girls were just standing there. And they were in a difficult situation and not getting water. He explained to the people, and somehow got water for their goats and gave it. And both of them, those two girls, made them drink the water. Their goats. After giving them water to drink, these two girls went to their father. In reality, they were the two daughters of Janab Shu'ayb. They were the two daughters of Hadrat Shu'ayb Nabi. And both of them went to their father and started narrating, "Father, a strange incident happened today." He asked, "What's the matter? You have come very early today. What is the matter? It usually takes you a long time to water the animals, but today you have come very early." They said that such and such an incident happened. We saw a man, and due to his kindness, we were able to water them quickly, and this is what happened. So Janab Shu'ayb said, "He must be a good man, that's why you got the water quickly and so on." So the younger daughter, who was very clever, said, "Father, what's the matter that you just call him a good man and become silent? Hey, a person who is so good, he should be given a reward (ajr)." *"Hal jaza'u al-ihsani illa al-ihsan?"* (Is the reward for good [anything] but good?). It is the command of Allah Ta'ala that the reward for a good deed is a good deed. "He should get some reward for it. He did so much work for us, he should get some reward for it." This was an indication. And what did Janab Shu'ayb do? After that, he sent for Janab Musa. Hadrat Musa was also a seeker. He came and reached Janab Shu'ayb. Now when he met Shu'ayb, Janab Shu'ayb said... "I want to marry my daughter to you." Their father, Shu'ayb, saw this indication from the younger daughter and married his younger daughter to you. Now, there was no wedding here, no nikah (marriage contract), no goat, no water, no nothing, no panghat. The matter, in fact, was that this was the madrasa (school) of Janab Shu'ayb, and these two daughters were the teachers and instructors there. They were men. They were teachers. And these goats were their students. And Janab Shu'ayb, he himself was the prophet and teacher of that time. You can understand him as the one who managed everything. And what Janab Musa did, "sharab kiya" (made to drink), meant that these girls wanted to impart knowledge but were unable to, meaning they couldn't answer their students. Hadrat Musa, with the knowledge he had acquired, with that knowledge, he "made them drink water" (quenched their thirst for knowledge), meaning he gave them knowledge. He gave them knowledge and answered them. So they were very surprised and came and mentioned it to their father, "Today we met such a person who gave very good answers to our questions, and such and such things happened." So Janab Shu'ayb sent for him. He was a seeker of meeting Janab Shu'ayb. The meeting with Shu'ayb also happened. And Shu'ayb, what he did was he "married" them, which means he joined them together. Meaning, that student of yours, he told him, "Now you must support Janab Musa and be his Hujjat (proof) and stay with him, and you have to work with him. And to spread the da'wat." So this was the incident, and what did the world understand it to be? That Janab Musa's wedding was happening, to whose daughter? To the younger daughter. You see, what the matter was, what the Quran says, and what the incident actually is. All such stories are like this. All stories are of this kind. They are all matters to be understood. Otherwise, if incidents were like this, then, God forbid, God forbid, what would they be? They would be just tales. These are stories and tales. No, no, it was not like that. They were matters of wisdom. And Janab Musa, after that, stayed with Shu'ayb, and much education and training took place with Janab Shu'ayb. And after that, he started saying... from Musa... Musa took leave from Janab Shu'ayb, "Now you give me permission, so that I may travel." Otherwise, the reality is that Janab Musa did have a wife, you were married, and the woman you were married to, what was her name? Safura. This was an invalid wife of yours. This Safura was a very bad wife. And just as someone's son is bad, someone's wife is bad, someone's friend is bad, anyway, this wife was also very bad, your Safura. Anyway, whether she was bad or whatever she was, she was his wife. You took Safura and left. And your first child was expected. And you left and were going, Janab Musa. And the mountain of Tur was visible from a distance. And you were passing by the foot of the mountain of Tur. And Safura, at that time, started to feel the need for fire. "I need fire, because my condition is that of pregnancy, and it would be better if I could get some fire." *"Anastu naran"* (I perceive a fire). Janab Musa said, "I am seeing some fire on that mountain. And I feel its warmth. You wait here now, I will go to the mountain and bring fire." Hadrat Musa climbed the mountain. And seeing that fire, he climbed up. And going there, he got that fire. But there, as he went... ...and he saw that there was a strange scene. And what is it? The divinity of God became visible. A mountain and such a beautiful valley and all this. So he said, *"tarani"* (Show me Yourself). "O Lord of the Worlds, you show yourself to me." So Allah Ta'ala said, *"lan tarani"* (You will not see me). "You cannot see me, O Musa." See, that is why he is called Kalimullah (the one who spoke to Allah), because he had a conversation with Allah Ta'ala. There was a conversation. which the Quran Majid has taken. Now, you say, *"tarani"* (Show me Yourself), "O my Lord, show yourself to me." Allah Ta'ala says, *"lan tarani"* (You will not see me). "You cannot see me." Now this conversation was between Janab Musa and whom? It was of Uz. He was going towards Hadrat Imami. And he wanted to meet Janab Uz himself and gain benefit from him. So Janab Uz said, "O Musa, why have you come to me to gain benefit? Hey, between me and you, there are still many. So you should benefit from them. What are you trying to benefit from me for? You think that if I am found in the river, you will acquire from me? No, it doesn't happen like that." Sometimes a thought comes that if we meet someone very great, like Taiyib Sahab or so-and-so, we will get the entire treasure of knowledge. This is all wrong thinking. You, your vessel, for example, it's like this: you want to take water from your tap, but you don't want to take it from there. Instead, you yourself want to go where the water comes from, to the lake, and take from the lake. Alright, go to the lake. But even at the lake, what will you do? When you go to take it, what will happen? You will bend down and take it in your two hands. So it became known that it is that same hadd-e-'ali and the hadd-e-'ali of the hadd-e-'ali through which you got the water. You will not drink from the water like an animal with your mouth in it. So the matter, in fact, is that qudrat has kept these intermediaries. That without an intermediary, you are not going to get anything. So Hadrat Musa wanted all the knowledge to come to him from Maulana Uz himself. Now you will say, "Why not, just as other prophets like Janab Salih and others were given signs, why wasn't Janab Musa given them?" Qudrat did not want it. Now you may want it, but qudrat did not want it. Now this was the seeing of God and not seeing God. Now we are sitting with this, that God who is the Mubdi' Ta'ala (the Exalted Originator), and we are seeing this God and that God. Where is the matter going, where is it being applied, and where are the Muslims understanding it? So this call was from Janab Uz that, "O Musa, *"lan tarani"* (You will not see me). You cannot see me. *"Unzur ila al-jabal"* (Look at the mountain)." "Just look at the mountain. This bush that is visible on the mountain, just look towards it." Meaning what? That "meet with 'Adnan." That bush was 'Adnan. That was his name. And "meet with him. And acquire knowledge from him. You will find out the matter." Just seeing 'Adnan is enough. And when Janab 'Adnan... when he saw him, Hadrat Musa... And when he saw his knowledge, sitting there to acquire it... he was so astonished. *"fa-kharra maghshiyyan 'alayh"* (he fell down unconscious). That he fainted and fell, Janab Musa. Meaning, the apparent story is that Musa looked at that bush, and upon looking, he could not bear its light and splendor, and you fainted and fell. Apparent. In the inner meaning, what? That Janab 'Adnan... His knowledge was so lofty, and his intellectual depth was so great, that Janab Musa could not bear its splendor, and you fainted. Fainted means he could not keep his senses intact. "Oh, what kind of things are you saying? This is such a lofty and high-level matter." So, the Imam had told him correctly, "Hey, just acquire from 'Adnan. Coming to me is a distant matter. First, climb the steps." So this was the story of Janab Musa's *"lan tarani"*, that "you cannot see me." So *"lan tarani, lan tarani"* became [a phrase], that if someone starts arguing, they say, "He is doing a lot of *lan tarani*." He is doing *lan tarani*. So the matter, in fact, was this. And Janab Musa... People and... a poet has also written a couplet about it, "You go to get fire, and you find a prophet." Hadrat Musa went to get fire, and he got prophethood. But what was the reality? You are understanding and seeing. That Janab Uz is showing favor to him, being kind to him, and he has made him a student of Janab 'Adnan. And after becoming a student of 'Adnan, he, Janab Musa, got up. When he came out of that unconsciousness, meaning that amazement he was in, the चक्र (chakra/whirlpool) of knowledge he had entered... "This knowledge and this brilliance and this power and this matter..." When he came out of that amazement, Janab Musa... ...at that time, Janab Musa was commanded, "O Musa, now I am choosing you, making you a prophet." "I am making you a prophet, O Musa." This voice started coming from the mountain. Janab Uz is the one who is speaking, and he is addressing Musa, "O Musa, We have chosen you for risalat and nubuwwat." And Musa said, "What other burden have you put on me?" He said, "No, the talqin you have done, you should acquire it. And the discipleship you have undertaken, this is its fruit that you are receiving. Now you go. *"Idh-hab ila Fir'awna innahu tagha"* (Go to Pharaoh, for he has transgressed). O Musa, now go to Fir'aun. He has rebelled. He has rebelled in this land and established a rival mission (da'wat-e-zidd). He has established a mission against us, which is a rival mission. And it is necessary to deal with him." "Walid ibn Mus'ab." "And go to him." Janab Musa said, "O Allah, O Maulana Uz, I am ready to go, but give me a helper (mu'in) and supporter (madadgar). What will I do alone, O Allah? I am very worried, I am alone. What can a single person do? There should be someone for companionship." So he was asked, "Musa, what do you want after all?" He said, "My eyes are on my brother, O Master. Whose name is Harun." "My brother Harun." *"wa-shrah li sadri"* (and expand for me my breast). You pray, "O Lord, expand my breast, and make my brother Harun my supporter and my helper. *"Haruna wa si'an waziri"* (Harun, my... and minister). Make Harun my minister, make him my partner." And all this. This was the same prayer which the Prophet, 'alayhi al-salat wa al-salam, made on an occasion for Amir al-Mu'minin. Anyway, here, when you are reading the story of Musa, then listen to that. That Janab Musa prayed this and said, *"wa-hlul 'uqdatan min lisani"* (and untie the knot from my tongue). "O Lord, do this favor also, make Harun my partner, my helper, my supporter, and there is a knot in my tongue. Meaning, some stutter has come into my tongue. Untie this stutter so that I can explain properly. And I can praise and glorify you, and I can explain the sciences. I have fallen into a great difficulty, O Lord. Please get me out of this." Janab Uz consoled Janab Musa, "Alright, go, we have made your Harun a Wasi (successor). And we have accepted him as your khalifa (caliph), as your Wasi. Now both of you go quickly. And Fir'aun has rebelled greatly in this land. Bring this matter to a conclusive end." Janab Musa was already majestic. What more can one ask? Now he got nubuwwat, he got risalat, and then he got a brother like Harun. After getting brother Harun, Janab Musa, who you had already seen, could dismiss someone with one slap. Now he went to slap whom? Fir'aun. Now he reached the court of Fir'aun. And Fir'aun's court is decorated. And he, after going there, said, "Fir'aun, you abandon rebellion and arrogance and accept faith, and all these things..." And he was proud. Fir'aun. Of his astrologers, of his magicians. And at that time the greatest magician was Samiri. The magic of Samiri was tremendous. And he was doing magic. He was proud of his Samiri. And he said, "Musa, what magic are you carrying on with? Which god are you talking about? I don't believe in any of this. And if you want to compete, then do it." What happened was that when Musa was about to leave, and with Janab Harun... and he was descending from Tur, at that time Allah Ta'ala said, "You... Musa, as you go, take two of our signs with you. You put your hand inside your pocket." "Inside your pocket" means put it inside your bosom, in your collar. As Janab Musa put his hand in, he said, "Now take it out." As soon as he took it out, it shone like the sun. He said, "Take this sign of ours with you. Secondly, you throw down this staff that you are holding in your hand, this big staff you are carrying, this stick, throw this stick." He threw it, and it became a snake. And Musa got scared. He was told, "Musa, there is no need to be scared. Pick it up in the name of Allah, and it will become a staff. We will return it to its original state, its first state. *"ala suratihi al-ula"* (to its former state). We will bring the snake to its first state. Don't worry." Janab Musa picked it up, and it became a stick again. He said, "Take these two signs and go. It will be enough for you." And there he reached, and he had to face Samiri. And over here, Fir'aun ordered, "Samiri, you and your magicians throw the ropes. Let Musa know how ropes become snakes." Samiri prepared all the magicians. Everyone threw their ropes, and they became snakes. And it was magic. There is no denying sorcery. That is why we believe in sorcery, that sorcery exists in the world. And I am telling you, one thing you must remember, is that all these things that happen, which our intellect does not understand... ...and the things that appear confounding to us, they are all just one thing. What is it? Surat-e-Khabith (The Evil Form). All the miracles are of the Surat-e-Khabith. What we call ghosts, spirits, jinn, and all these worldly things, it is all that one thing. Anyway, sorcery is also the name of that thing. And in different ways, in different forms, it manifests itself. So, those people threw the ropes, and the ropes became snakes. And what did Janab Musa do? He had already been commanded, and it had been told to him. He threw his stick. When he threw the stick, it became a huge dragon and swallowed the small snakes. It swallowed the small snakes. And this feat that was performed, Fir'aun was left watching, "This is a disaster. The snake of my magicians has been swallowed." This is the apparent story, and it also had an inner story. The meaning was that Samiri, who was the scholar on his side, threw many questions. And all those questions were answered by Janab Harun. On behalf of Musa, Harun gave the answers. With the answers, he was stunned, Fir'aun. And he started saying, "What is this? He is answering all these things. What do I... I am just watching." So, it happened in the apparent and also in the inner meaning. And this was the mission of misguidance, and Fir'aun at that time became very afraid. And started saying, "No, now this Musa must be killed." Just as it happened with every prophet. Someone, like Janab Ibrahim, they picked up and threw into the fire. So here too, you... ...an army was sent to capture him. And Janab Musa fled from there, and you went straight to the Nile, and you struck the Nile with your staff. And a path was made, and you went out. And what happened there? That the army entered, and the two... its waters met, and all were drowned. So the tyranny of Fir'aun was washed away. And over here, you escaped. This was the apparent matter, and the inner matter was that his mission was annihilated. And Janab Musa 'alayhi al-salat wa al-salam continued to rely on his Janab Harun. And he made Janab Harun his Wasi. Now, what a marvel it was that when he got salvation from all these pharaohs, he reached his mission and wanted to run an institution of nubuwwat and risalat. So when he wanted to run it, a strange thing happened. That the people of the da'wat all became opposed. Whose? Of Hadrat Musa. They said, "Musa, we believe in everything of yours. We have seen your majesty since childhood. What is the extent of your majesty? A person dies from a single slap. What greater majesty can there be than this? We have seen your great miracles, your great things, your great knowledge and depth. We believe in everything, but our heart cannot understand this Harun business. The heart believes everything, but it does not accept Harun. We are not ready to accept your Wasi." So what happened? This is... this is called Surah al-Baqarah. This long chapter that there is, Surah al-Baqarah, which you read in the Quran Majid, this is that Surah al-Baqarah. That Hadrat Musa said that the Quran narrates it like this. "Look, Allah has commanded me, O people, that I should sacrifice a cow. And I want to... there is a cow in my sight, I want to sacrifice it." So everyone raised a hue and cry and said, "Musa, it cannot be like this. That you will slaughter whichever cow you want, it cannot be like that. We will tell you which cow you have to slaughter." So Musa said, "Alright, brother, you tell me. But I..." "So which cow will you bring? Bring the cow, and I will slaughter it." They said, "Musa, that's correct, we will bring the cow. But just tell us, which cow is in your sight? What are its signs?" It's this, that "we will be the ones to bring the cow." This is one thing. But along with this, look at the attitude of the people of the da'wat. That they are also asking, "Just tell us, what kind of cow did you want to slaughter?" Hadrat Musa said, "One that passes urine and stool in secret, in the darkness, and is very modest and shy. I would like to slaughter such a cow. And one that is black. And one that *"tasurru al-nazirin"* (pleases the onlookers), that pleases those who see it. Seeing it, they say, 'Wow, what a cow!'" So the Quran Majid narrates all these kinds of things. Now, Muslims are sitting with this, that this was the sacrifice of the cow, and your people were not agreeing, and Janab Musa told them its signs, and all the people brought a cow. And that cow, which Janab Musa in reality wanted to sacrifice, was that same cow. So the matter, in fact, was that "cow" is Hujjat. Hadrat Musa had twelve nuqab (chiefs), nuqaba. That is what Allah Ta'ala is saying, "O Musa, just see that this staff of yours, this stick you have, it is not an ordinary stick. Just strike with it." As soon as he struck, *"fa-nfajarat... ithnata 'ashrata... nahran"* (and there gushed forth... twelve... springs). From it, twelve springs began to flow, says the Quran. So what is the reality of this? That it was the miracle of Janab Musa, that your twelve nuqaba were ready. So out of the twelve nuqaba, out of the twelve du'at (missionaries), out of the twelve hujjats (proofs), you wanted to appoint one as your successor, as your wasi. And these people were saying that "we will choose." See, this election which happened with the Prophet, its beginning is here. And the foundation of democracy was laid here with Hadrat Musa. They said, "We will have an election. Meaning, we will choose. Meaning, we are also something, after all. We also have this much intellect. We have sense and understanding. Are we completely useless? No, we also have an opinion. We also have intellect." So they told Janab Musa. So this was the whole matter. And what happened was that as he told them the signs, that my hujjat should have such and such signs, whom I want to appoint as my successor and wasi. And they, taking those signs, when they pondered and made a choice, whom did they choose? They came bringing Harun. They came, and they brought that same Harun. And Janab Musa also wanted the same. *"Ma kunna nabghi"* (What we were seeking). Allah Ta'ala says, Janab Musa said, "Hey, this is what we wanted. This is what we wanted, and you also wanted the same. It's good that you are also happy, and we are also happy." Their word was also kept, and Janab Musa made Janab Harun his wasi. And after making him a wasi, now he started to live with Janab Harun. And Musa was very happy that my brother has been made my wasi, O Lord. What greater happiness can there be for me than this?
