That the one who explains everything, the one who does everything, the one who answers, is my brother, my Harun. That is why he answered Fir'aun and his people. And he was very proud of Janab Harun. Who? Hadrat Musa 'alayhi al-salat wa al-salam. So in this pride and this state, you were going. And the situation was such... that now the final time is coming. And Janab Harun separated from you and he said, "O Janab Musa, give me permission, that I want to go for some recreation or some work." You would not separate Janab Harun. But when he asked for permission, you said, "Alright. When you want to go to a certain place, then go." This Janab Harun departed from there. Now, when he departed, there, when he was passing through that jungle, from that place where he wanted to go, he saw... that there are some people who are digging a grave. They are digging a grave. Seeing the grave being dug, Janab Harun stopped there and started saying, "Brother, for whom is this grave being dug? Who has died? And for whom is this grave being dug?" So... So Janab Harun said, "He must indeed be such a good person for whom such a good grave is visible to me. And if you people give permission, I would like to lie down and see." And Hadrat Harun, with their permission, entered that grave and lay down. As soon as he lay down, the Angel of Death descended and captured his soul. The apparent story is this, and after the soul was captured, they filled in the earth, and Harun passed away. In this way, Harun's death occurred. And... Now, apparently these are the matters, but what is the inner meaning? That is a matter of the rihiyat (spiritualities). Which I told you about, how the rihiyat are gathered. That is... that is still some intellectual matters which you will not understand now. But there were some things which were meant for Janab Harun to depart. And that time had come. So Janab... Their death is not death. Their life is not life. Their illness is not illness. Their murder is not murder. The Quran is giving evidence for this. So when you believe and understand this matter, then you should understand that this too was something similar. And Janab Harun's departure also happened in this way. And Janab Musa, now when he saw... when he got the news of Janab Harun's death, then you... his son, Janab Harun's son, whose name was Finhas, you chose him. "Now, to keep nubuwwat and risalat going, I choose Finhas, Harun's son." But Finhas was of a young age. So when they saw that Janab Musa... that Finhas is very young now, how should he be... an 'ataliq (tutor) was appointed. Just as Sayyidna Sulayman appointed Ja'far... Sayyidna Ja'far was appointed, but when he saw that he was very young... he had appointed him from birth. But when he saw he was young, he appointed Sayyidna Muhammad as his 'ataliq and mustawda' (trustee). In the same way, here too, a mustawda' was appointed. Whom? Yusha' bin Nun. Yusha' bin Nun, whose grave is in Baghdad. There, he... you appointed him, Janab Yusha' bin Nun, as his 'ataliq and mustawda'. And Yusha' bin Nun continued to handle the affairs, until Finhas grew up, and then he... nubuwwat and risalat. This chain, what I am calling the preliminary one, of the ghulams (servants), or the safirs (emissaries), or the viceroys, or the ones who handled the nubuwwat and risalat, this started running in its place. From where? From Janab Musa to Harun, and from Harun to Janab Yusha' bin Nun, and after him Janab Finhas. This chain went on here. And up above, the chain that went on from Janab Uz... that Uz, 'alayhi al-salat wa al-salam, who are the Imam-e-Waqt, who are the Master of the time, the Lord of the time, the God of the time, they... their son 'Udhadh. Their son, his name was 'Udhadh. His name was Uz, and his son's name was 'Udhadh. He appointed him. 'Udhadh, after him, appointed his son. This chain of imamat went on like this, from son to father. Here the chain is not from father to son. This chain started to run here. So, anyway, the story of Hadrat Musa does not get completed. If some more things which are related to the story of Hadrat Musa... are said. Since I don't think that in the stories of Hadrat Musa, any other such thing remains. Except for one thing. And that thing is that in your time, great hukama' (sages/philosophers) were born. Yours was such an era in which Allah Ta'ala created great hakims (sages). The greatest hakim who came into the world... was Luqman Hakim. About whom Allah Ta'ala says that "We gave him wisdom." To Hadrat Luqman. So wisdom... The meaning of hikmat became Luqman, and the meaning of Luqman became hikmat. Such wisdom was given to Luqman. And Janab Luqman's stories... there are not many stories in the Quran Majid, but there is one piece of advice of yours which you gave to your children. "O child, after me, you should live like this." He gave advice, which is in the Quran Majid. Read it. It is very interesting and worth reading and understanding. In it, one of the pieces of advice is, *"wa la tamshi fi al-ardi maraha"* (and do not walk upon the earth with insolence). "O children, look, when you walk on the earth, walk very softly. Don't stamp your feet. Otherwise, the earth trembles and shakes. [unclear] You will be surprised, the earth... So, these are great words of wisdom that are related to Janab Luqman. In my reading, it has also come in a book, though it is not mentioned in the Quran Majid, that Janab Luqman, the advice he gave to his children... he gave some tablets, and he gave them some writings. Just as, understand it, he gave a book. And when he gave the book, the children saw it was a plain book, completely empty. They saw, all the pages were unwritten, completely plain. And they were worried, "What did father give us? There is nothing written in it. What advice is this? And what advice does father want to give?" But they saw that on one page, in a corner, only this much was written. "You keep your head cool and your feet warm." Only this much was written, "Keep your head cool, and keep your feet warm." Meaning, the head is the repository of all things. If you keep your head cool... meaning, emotions, feelings, all these things, if you do them with coolness, then no illness will come upon you. [unclear] Because disease is created from thought, from imagination, and from all these things, from mental things. So you gave this advice, "Keep your head cool." "Feet warm" means always be engaged in striving. Always be engaged in striving. So, anyway, these are great, excellent pieces of advice present in the Quran Majid. This was Hadrat Luqman, who was born in that era. Not only this, hey, Aristotle, whom they call Aristoteles, who are counted among the teachers of Alexander, Hadrat Aristotle... He was also from that same era. Not only he, but Hippocrates was there, Socrates was there, Plato was there, Galen was there, all these great, great sages were coming, of Greece, and they were from the same era as Janab Musa. Whose mention we have with great detail. With details. And these were those lofty personalities who... were not made subject to Musa. All these were lofty. All these sages who were there, Janab Hippocrates, Socrates, etc., they were greater than Musa. Why, brother, when they were greater, why wasn't he made Musa? Why wasn't he made a prophet? We think in this small way. No. "The beloved of the Beloved is the one whom He chooses." Understand it like that. The matter here is something else. They were certainly muwahhidin (monotheists) in their own place, great believers in tawhid. What can one say about them, Hippocrates and Socrates? They sounded the trumpets of reason. They wrote such books that the intellect is astonished. Even today, those things... Plato's Dialogues, read them. All these things are available. And who will stand against the sages of Greece? But for this reason, they were muwahhidin. And they did not come under the shari'ah of Musa. They were not made subject to Musa. And they were kept separate, and they were like that. And in the time of Janab Musa, among the incidents, there is the descent of manna and salwa. The misbehavior of the people of Bani Isra'il with you. All these incidents happened. And the descent of manna and salwa is a great matter. Manna and salwa are sciences. which were sent down to Janab Musa. Now if you look up manna and salwa in the Quran Majid, then its meaning is given as quail and partridge. Quail and partridge. It's good, very good. At least let the quail and partridge come. The meaning of it is given as quail and partridge. Quail and partridge. Even after reading it, one feels like laughing. That at that time, quails and partridges became very abundant. Meaning, to eat, there was plenty of quail and partridge to eat. So this is manna and salwa. Manna and salwa... They were great blessings from Allah Ta'ala. They were sciences, sciences that were sent down. And they understand this to be manna and salwa. So what will the literalist Muslim understand of these matters? So, anyway, they understood it in this way. So, anyway, my point was that the era of Hadrat Musa 'alayhi al-salat wa al-salam continued for a thousand years. And in that period, such great, great sages continued to come. And not only all these sages came... ...but in your time, there was a king who passed away, whose name is Qarun. Qarun was a king who passed away, whose wealth was to such an extent... ...that the keys to his treasures were carried on forty camels. The one whose treasure keys were carried on forty camels, what would his treasure be like? So, anyway, Qarun also passed away. And... ...and Qarbun also passed away. So, anyway, this... Qarbun, he was a strange king. Who had great enmity with the people of wila' (devotion) and the people of truth. And at that time, Allah Ta'ala... ...wanted to save the Ashab al-Kahf (Companions of the Cave), and he saved the Ashab al-Kahf. And he told them, "Go into this cave." And when they went into the cave, Allah Ta'ala made sleep overtake them. From which, the Surah al-Kahf of the Ashab al-Kahf came down. You read Surah al-Kahf. So that... When they reached the cave, sleep overtook them there, and they slept. Now, *"rajman bi-l-ghayb"* (guessing at the unseen). Allah Ta'ala says that some say there were eight, some say that the ninth was their dog, some say there were seven, the eighth was their dog. *"Rajman bi-l-ghayb"*, meaning all this is guesswork. But Allah has its knowledge. So the reality is that if you see the exegeses of the Quran regarding the Ashab al-Kahf, they have taken countless names. Sometimes one name, sometimes another name. In some exegesis, other names are given, in some exegesis, other names are given. But correctly and in reality, the names they had... those Ashab al-Kahf, they are those Ashab al-Kahf whom... ...we have such blessed names of theirs, that if any calamity befalls, earthquakes come, storms come... ...then we, facing the qibla, if we take their names, then we can be saved from it and be safe. So our elders of the faith have also clarified their names, who they were and what they were. And a strange coincidence, a gentleman was going... I have also visited the Ashab al-Kahf two or three times. But he... when I was leaving, before that, there was a Bohra gentleman, but I had seen that person before, who was a great scholar. ...and he started asking me, "Brother, I have to go there too. Whose ziyarat (visit) is there?" So I said, "There is also the Ashab al-Kahf." He said, "I want to visit the Ashab al-Kahf." I asked, "Do you know the Ashab al-Kahf?" So I told him the names. And after going there, he saw that those same names were written on the graves. He was very surprised. He said, "Brother, this thing... I asked our mullah ji, but he didn't have it. How did you get these names?" So, anyway, those names are, Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim, Jamliqa, Kashutat, Kashafat, Yunus, Yawanis, Bus, 'Adhar, and their dog's name was Qitmir. So these are those Ashab al-Kahf. And who were there, upon whom sleep was made to descend, and whose story is mentioned in the Quran Majid. All this is within the era of Hadrat Musa, this thousand-year period that passed. All these things have come within that era and have happened. And after that, when the time of Hadrat 'Isa started to come, at that time also some people came. And how? That these... Zarathushtra of the Parsis, he has also come. He has come, about whom I will narrate, Insha'Allah, to you. And this era of Hadrat Musa lasted for a thousand years. And this chain of Janab Musa continued with your Harun, and after Janab Harun with Janab Finhas and Yusha' bin Nun. Over here, the imamat continued from Janab Uz. And until the chain reached where? It reached Maulana Khuzayma. Now, this is the time when 'Isa, 'alayhi al-salat wa al-salam, was to descend. It was Hadrat Uz who had bestowed the Taurat upon Janab Musa. And the Taurat came down, meaning it is not that from above the heavens Allah Ta'ala is sending it down. It is not like that. The Taurat was an inspired book that was coming. And all these things came. And Janab Musa, taking that book, established the shari'ah. And he made his people follow that same shari'ah. [End of lecture]

First of all, to understand this, I had explained a little bit, but before understanding it, there is a foundational matter that should be well-seated in the mind and understood. That matter is that the `as̲h̲ir-i mudabbir-i ḥakīm` (the wise demiurge, the Tenth Intellect)—that `as̲h̲ir` who was the last individual of the `maqtū' nizā'` (the interrupted lineage), the one who came after the `kalamm`—that `as̲h̲ir-i mudabbir-i ḥakīm` saw how the salvation of this realm would come about. This realm which is taking on `tajassum` (corporeality), taking on matter, to bring that realm from `tajassum` towards `rūḥāniyyat` (spirituality), to bring it into a reasonable state, what sort of condition must it be passed through? How should it be passed? This too was in his thought. Indeed, I told you that he had three purposes, which I explained to you. And he also, all the `uqūl`, from the First Intellect down to the lower intellects, saw this thing: that they should be imprisoned in the `'ālam-i tajassum` (world of corporeality). This was also one thing. That was there. But the question of how the rungs of progress should be, how progress should happen, how one should come from this `jismāniyyat` (corporeality) towards `rūḥāniyyat` (spirituality)—when he began to contemplate this, when he began to ponder, only two things came to his mind. You see, as I had told you, the two relations (`nisbatayn`) that were formed, those relations are visible to you everywhere in their different forms and different ways. You saw it in the `kalamm`, you saw it in the state of the `'aql-i awwal` (First Intellect), and you also saw it in the `tābūt-i tawbah` (Ark of Repentance). These states, the states of the two, the dual states, will be visible to you everywhere. In the same way, when he thought about the salvation of this realm, he found two states. One is that they should progress in a `lāhūtī` (divine) manner. This entire realm must progress. Who thought this? The `as̲h̲ir-i mudabbir-i ḥakīm`. That for this realm to progress, to move away from this matter and take on a spiritual form, it has to progress in two ways; there will not be progress in just one way. And how will those two types of progress happen? One through `lāhūt` (the divine realm) and one through `nāsūt` (the human/physical realm).

Now, what is this thing `lāhūt`? What is this thing `nāsūt`? This is something to be understood. I will tell you. But in his mind, two things came. One is `nāsūt`, meaning that in which the `jism` (body) and `jismāniyyat` (corporeality) remain while it progresses. And `lāhūt` is when the body does not remain in corporeality but rather, in its entirety, totally, takes on `rūḥāniyyat` (spirituality) and then progresses.

So you have seen, just as there is one thing, that as the world is revolving, it is revolving on its own axis and also revolving around the sun. So there were two ways for it to rotate. In the same way, there were also two rungs of progress: progress through the physical, and our spiritual progress as well. Allah the Exalted willed this both types of progress. And which Allah? The `mudabbir-i ḥakīm`, `as̲h̲ir`. The `as̲h̲ir-i mudabbir-i ḥakīm` willed this, for which the Holy Quran said, `Wa tabārak Allāhu aḥsan al-khāliqīn` (And blessed is Allah, the best of creators). Blessed is that Allah who is the best of creators.

Meaning, all the `uqūl` had the potential to bring this human into this `tajassum` and imprison him in cages, but the way the Lord of the Worlds, the `mudabbir-i ḥakīm` and `as̲h̲ir` did it in this manner, Allah the Exalted Himself praised it. Who praised it? The `'aql-i awwal` praised it. The `'aql-i awwal` praised it, saying that this is the best of creators. Meaning, the human's stature, his `tajassum`, the flexibility within him, the faculties within him and the intuition, the states, his mental state and his feelings, and his heart's connections, and the balance (`mīzān`) that Allah the Exalted has placed within his entire body—this state that was placed within a human, the Lord of the Worlds praised it greatly, that there could not have been a better state than this. Better than this... those who were the `uqūl`, who were united in knowledge, power, and life, in omnipotence and life, who were described by perfect qualities, and who were created without time and space—now, if there can be any form for them, it can be a human form in which they are imprisoned. The one in which we are imprisoned today.

His sight was working in this way, and he thought of imprisoning us. But as I said, along with imprisoning, he was also searching for a way out. `See before you leap.` The same thing, that "brother, we are going, but after that, how will we get out?" The thought of getting out was also coming to his mind, and the thing that was coming to his noble thought, the matter that was coming to his noble mind, what was it? It was `nāsūt` and `lāhūt`.

What is this thing `nāsūt`? And what is this thing `lāhūt`? To understand this is a great task. And these are indeed deep mysteries. As I told you, `nāsūt` is a thing that has `jismāniyyat` (corporeality), despite the fact that it is a thing that has `jismāniyyat`, but it is like a reflection (`kas-i war`), it is like a spirit (`rūḥ`), despite the fact that it has physicality. And `lāhūt` is entirely `rūḥ` (spirit), and it is entirely... the forms that are there, it is a state that resembles them. And both of these are the rungs of progress, on which the things in this realm that are to progress, do progress. Now, how is this, how is `lāhūt` formed, and what is `nāsūt` made of? This thing will become clear to you on its own in my intermediate lesson, and you will understand what `nāsūt` is and what `lāhūt` is. But I was telling you that our one image (`shabīh`), the one that was falling from there, in that `malakūtī` (angelic) realm, in that `lāhūtī` (divine) realm, in that sacred and spiritual realm, the states we had, when we were in the state of `uqūl`, when we fell from that state, then every falling entity had a different intention (`niyyah`). I was saying that its intention was also different. Not only was the intention of every single person different, but even within one person, there were different intentions, because of which its... its parts took on separate portions.

And I had explained this to you in detail, that if one person is divided into 100 cells, then which cell accepted first, that became number one; the one that accepted second, became number two. So the balance (`mīzān`) of each one will not remain the same. And when this thing was happening, I told you that every person's `conception` there, their `concept`, at the time of falling, that thing was his final thing, and his intention had become frozen (`munjamid`), and Allah the Exalted had placed that intention of his in the record room.

For example, the `shākk-o-mutaraddid` (doubters and waverers) were in a state of doubt, and their intentions were of doubt, and their... their perception, their mind, was filled with doubts. Now, for any... I mentioned their types, they had 20 types according to them. And the `musirr-o-mustakbir` (obstinate and arrogant) were divided into 35 types, and they... their... similarly, they had types. But within a `momin` (believer) too, among those who believe, there were also 15 types, the first of which were the `kalamm`.

The first type were those who said 'no' and then said 'yes', who accepted after denying. And they are our Imams, our Prophets, our Messengers, our `muqtadā` (exemplars), our `rahbar` (guides), our `du'āt` (missionaries), our... these... all who were from there, who became the guides of the religion, they all belong to that world and are related to that thing. So anyway, this... I said... So when we were falling... now, set the `kalamm` aside, because they are the first type and will remain there. But we who were falling, and whom I was saying that the gaze was most upon us, because this child had some life in it. It was crying, it was repenting. This was a class of Sulaymanis who were repenting, whose tears nature was watching.

And for this very reason, what did nature do? That just as... whoever intended in a certain way, they were given that same fruit. So since we had repented there, here nature caught our hand first. `Thumma nunajjī alladhīna ittaqaw wa nadharu al-ẓālimīna fīhā jithiyyā` (Then We will save those who feared Allah, and We will leave the wrongdoers within it, kneeling). Those who adopted `taqwā` (piety), we will pull them out of this realm, but those who are `ẓālim` (wrongdoers), meaning those who are not going to do justice, who place things in the wrong place, we will leave them in this very realm. What do we care? If the number of prisoners in a prison increases, a prison is a prison. Let the prisoners remain in the prison, what difference does it make? Let them remain until... as long as, `mā dāmati al-samāwātu wa-l-arḍ` (as long as the heavens and the earth endure).

Allah the Exalted said this to complete a period (`muddat`). Otherwise, what is the reality? That this too must have a duration, for after all, in what duration will these things end? And which duration is it for them to end? As I have said, it is a `qawr-i a'ẓam` (Great Cycle). 360,000 multiplied by 360,000. In one `qawr-i a'ẓam`, the alteration of this universe completely... it becomes from top to bottom and bottom to top. The period of that alteration is one `qawr-i a'ẓam`. And the period in terms of progress is one `mawr-i a'ẓam` (Great Epoch). Remember. The period in terms of progress is one `mawr-i a'ẓam`.

A `dawr`... what do they call a `dawr`? A period of 400,000 years is called one `dawr`. And in such a `dawr`, night comes seven times and day comes seven times. The night is of 7,000 years, the day is of 50,000 years... actually it is 47,000 years, 3,000 years are for its... for the twilight and dawn. So that is, a day with Allah is 57,000 years. And seven such days together make one week, which we call a `dawr`. And a `qawr` consists of 400,000 such `dawr`s. And a `mawr` consists of 400,000 such `qawr`s.

If you calculate it, it is... it is very difficult to calculate. I tried to do this at the Dhahran Petroleum University, but there it just started giving powers, that you should put 25 dots, you should put 24 dots, that many upon it... this is how it comes out. So, as it is, our calculation becomes very difficult. But for your understanding, you should understand this, that a `dawr` is of 400,000 years, a `qawr` is of 400,000 such `dawr`s, and a `mawr` is of 400,000 such `qawr`s.

For this universe to end, to turn its page again, to renew this universe, which duration has Allah the Exalted set? One `qawr-i a'ẓam`. And to be free from the universe, to get out of this realm, to go from spirituality... from corporeality towards spirituality, whoever is going, for them the duration that is set, whose is it? It is of one `mawr`. One `mawr`. For this reason, Allah the Exalted has stated in the Holy Quran, that where He addresses the jinn and mankind, `In-ḥall istaṭa'tum an tanfudhū min aqṭāri al-samāwāti wa-l-arḍ fa-nfudhū lā tanfudhūna illā bi-sulṭān. Fa-bi-ayyiālā'i Rabbikumā tukadhdhibān` (O company of jinn and mankind, if you are able to pass beyond the regions of the heavens and the earth, then pass. You will not pass except by authority. Then which of the favors of your Lord will you deny?).

Do you, O mankind and jinn, want to get out of the confines of this heaven and earth? Alright, try to get out. See how the Lord is asking. `Fa-nfudhū`... just try getting out and show me. `Fa-nfudhū lā tanfudhūna`... you can never get out... `illā bi-sulṭān` (except by authority). Now, for the meaning of this `sulṭān`, commentators have said strange, strange, nonsensical things. Strange, strange... whatever came to their minds, they said those things. In reality, who is the `sulṭān`? He is the `ṣāḥib-i mawr` (Master of the Epoch). The `ṣāḥib-i mawr` who will come, the `qiyamah` (resurrection) of `qiyamah`s, the `qā'im` who will come, that `ṣāḥib-i mawr` is the one who will take the entire `haykal` (temple/structure) with him. Anyway. Now you have to understand `haykal` too, and you have to understand `nāsūt` too. So, to explain the `haykal`, and to explain `nāsūt` and `lāhūt`, these introductions were necessary, and you are understanding that matter. So I was telling you that a `momin` falling from there... a `momin` falling, when he made an intention (`niyyah`), then in the act of his making an intention, some of his things were spent. Meaning, you... when you think, you say, "why do you burn yourself by thinking, brother?" So now this word you are saying, you are saying it with understanding. In reality, you have burned your blood by thinking and thinking. And when you burned your blood, you diminished yourself. Your blood is a part of your body. So it is known that thought consumes a thing. So your... your `ṣūrat` (form) that was made there, the angle from which you repented there, that act of repentance consumed one of your portions. And I had explained this very thing, that one surface of water is... that one part of it is becoming gas and rising, one is becoming water and remaining, and one is becoming ice. An intelligent person would call all three things water. But it takes on three forms. So in exactly the same way, the thing that... that there, our... we... through thought (`taṣawwur`), we consumed ourselves, that thought of ours was preserved in the record room, which our `du'āt` call the `'umūd-i nūr` (Pillar of Light). In the `'umūd-i nūr`, the record of ours that remained, that record of ours that has remained, that is one part of us that was finished.

The second part, that was... after that, was the intention that we had made of repentance. And I called that `ḥissiyyah`. The sense (`ḥiss`) that is in us, the smelling of the nose, the seeing of the eye, the touching of the hand, the hearing of the ear, this sense that we have, the `ḥawāss-i khamsah` (five senses), the external and the internal, these that are working, they are working from this very `ḥissiyyah`.

The third thing that was there, and that thing, what was it? `Nāmiyah`. What is `nāmiyah`? To grow. The power to grow that is in us, that we become tall, long, wide, that every part of us develops, that is the power of `nāmiyah`. So there were three powers into which we were divided in the beginning. And after that, the thing that was made of ours there, what was that thing? The heart. Although I said 'heart' first in some context. So that was correct in its context because it is the king of this realm. In that sense. So it was the heart, and after the heart, then the liver was formed, and the brain was formed, and the liver was formed, and in this way, all the organs began to be formed, then the nails and hair also, in the end, came and... so if you take the division of the body and sit with it, our body, the `du'āt` divide it into six parts: hard bones, soft bones, veins and fibers, muscles, and hair and nails. In these six parts, our `du'āt` have divided our body... that is, it has been divided.

Now, I told you that some part of ours became `nāmiyah`, some part of ours became `nāṭiqah`, some part of ours became `ḥissiyyah`. The `nāṭiqah`, I am telling you, where did its center for residing become? It went into the record room. It became related to the `'umūd-i nūr`. What was the second thing? Our `ḥissiyyah`. That `ḥissiyyah` was given to the sun. The sun is a very big platform. Many things work there. I had said that one is its dense parts (`kasā'if`), which we call `sīp` (mother-of-pearl), the shiny things. After that are its subtle parts (`laṭā'if`), which are the things inside it. And after that are its spiritual parts (`rūḥāniyyāt`), which are even deeper inside it. So these things that were there, those things... the sun took care of those things, of our `ḥissiyyah`. And our `nāmiyah` was preserved entirely by whom? The moon preserved it. Now, we... when our time came in the universe, and nature wanted to bring us onto the stage of manifestation, I told you that the `shākk-o-mutaraddid`, `musirr-o-mustakbir`, and `nādim-o-mustaghfir` were divided. The `shākk-o-mutaraddid`, `musirr-o-mustakbir`, and `nādim-o-mustaghfir`. The `nādim-o-mustaghfir`, I had told you, became the ethereal world. The entire shining celestial world, whether it is the constellations (`burūj`), whether it is the all-encompassing sphere (`falak-i muḥīṭ`), whether it is the sphere of the moon, or the sun, or Jupiter, Mars, Venus, Mercury, these... all the stars of these spheres, and their spheres, everything that was there, all of it was the treasure of the `nādimīn` (repentant). And after that, the sphere of ether, the sphere of air, the sphere of water, and the sphere of earth—these four spheres, how were they made? They were prepared from the `shākk-o-mutaraddid`. And below that, what we call the crust, what we call the earth, the hard part, the solid part, this `jawf` (interior) of the earth, this inner part of the earth, that entire thing, how was it made? It was made from the `musirr-o-mustakbir`. And especially from the `musirr-o-mustakbir`, and particularly from the `musirr-o-mustakbir`, which thing was made? Hell (`jahannam`) was made. Hell is beneath this very earth, which they call the central core. In the language of science, they call it the central core. That is the middle part of the earth, which science to this day has not been able to investigate. It says, `whether it may be in liquid form or gas form`. So it is in gas form or liquid form. So in reality, it is neither in gas form nor in liquid form, but rather they are proper valleys, they are proper cities, they are proper... its... its length, what is it? Its breadth, what is it? Its... what is the heat (`ḥarārat`) there? What is the heat in the first layer? What is the heat in the last layer? What are the names of its layers? All these things are known and understood. But it is all there. I had told you that there are 70 valleys. There are 70 valleys of Hell. And it has four mouths, and those four mouths are... they have come out in different places. I had told you that three are on land and one is in the water. And the one that is in the water, it is in the Atlantic Ocean.

So anyway, now this... the mouths of Hell for exiting are separate, and the mouths for being thrown in there are separate. The mouths for entering Hell are separate, the mouths for exiting are separate. Anyway, now I had to tell you this, that the `musirr-o-mustakbir`, `shākk-o-mutaraddid`, and `nādim-o-mustaghfir` were divided in this way. Now, after being divided, the Lord of the Worlds wants that... in this world, every thing should create its existence, come with its existence, and come into the world as a human with intellect and wisdom, and with their respective intentions. If he is a `musirr-o-mustakbir`, he will come as an atheist. And if he is a `shākk-o-mutaraddid`, he will come as a `shākk-o-mutaraddid`. If he is a `nādim-o-mustaghfir`, he will come as a `nādim-o-mustaghfir`. But what? If he just remains a `shākk-o-mutaraddid`, then there would be no point. If he just remains a `musirr-o-mustakbir`, there would be no point. That is why what happens? If water continuously falls on a stone, then sooner or later it makes a hole. So the guidance of the prophets, the guidance of the messengers, sooner or later it will bring about a change. And after taking blows again and again and again, he moves from number 20 to 19, from 19 to 18, from 18 to 17, and in this way, he will come to number one and sometimes even cling to the feet of a `momin`. And by clinging, slowly, slowly, he will start coming into the 15 categories of the `momin`.

So, this is the state that happens. And sometimes this also happens in nature, that sometimes a `musirr-o-mustakbir` comes out and doesn't even have to climb the rungs of the `shākk-o-mutaraddid`, but rather comes straight into the category of the `momin`. This also happens. But these are all exceptions, and with every general rule, there is an exception. And in this way, these states happen. But I told you that nature wanted every person to come to this stage and play their part. The part that you have been given, you may have been anything in your reality. You may be children of the same class, your classmates are all with you, but if you are given the part of an uncle, you will become an uncle; if you have to become a nephew, you will become a nephew. If you have to become a woman, you will become a woman; if you have to become a man, you will become a man. On the stage, the work you have to do, you will come and accomplish that work. So on this stage of manifestation, when you were brought, every person started coming according to his intention. This is what the Prophet, peace be upon him, was saying: `Kullu mawlūdin yūladu 'alā fiṭrat al-islām fa-abawāhu yuhawwidānihi wa yunassirānihi wa yumajjisānihi` (Every child is born on the natural disposition of Islam, then his parents make him a Jew, a Christian, or a Zoroastrian). Now what will happen? If he is a Jew or a Zoroastrian by his... his... his nature, then first he will be born on the `fiṭrat al-islām`. He will come on Islam. Coming on Islam doesn't mean this Islam. It doesn't mean our Islam. It means he will be born on a temperament of obedience. He will be an obedient child. Now, however you teach a child, if he goes towards Hinduism, he will become a Hindu; if he goes towards Sikhism, he will become a Sikh. So the Prophet said it in this way. Anyway, the point was that every person will act here according to his intention. And after acting, what will happen? The prophets who come, they... now you have to pay a little attention. The prophets who come, the righteous messengers who come, when they come and call you, "Come, `Qūlū lā ilāha illā Allāh tufliḥū` (Say, there is no god but Allah, and you will be successful). O people, say `lā ilāha illā Allāh`, you will find salvation." Now, the sound of this messenger, whose ears is it hitting? Everyone is hearing it. But some are stones who are hearing it. And some are animals who are hearing it. But in human form. And there are very few who are human, who are hearing it and saying `Sami'nā wa aṭa'nā` (We hear and we obey). Who are they, who are saying this? Those who obeyed right there. Those who obeyed there, the moment they heard it here, they said, "we obeyed." And those who didn't obey there, they will have to think a little. Of course. And they have the right to think. Because they didn't obey there, they won't obey here either. But these prophets, through their preaching, their teaching, their examples, their full intelligence, and for the `juhalā` (ignoramuses), who are the most worthless class, remember, who are completely crude, whom they call ignorant, whom we call `ignorant`, for their sake, what did the prophets have to do? They had to show miracles (`mu'jizah`). A miracle is not proof of prophethood for us. The entire Islamic world places miracles on a pedestal. We... for us, a miracle has the lowest status. It is one of the signs of prophethood, and it is only for making the ignorant understand, so that... that it is possible that this might create some life within them. This is the massage of the heart, that some spark might be created, some life might be created. Otherwise, a miracle is not the real thing. The real thing is teaching, the real thing is knowledge, the real thing is its understanding. She works from this understanding. So I told you that now you are seeing that everyone is coming to this stage of manifestation, but everyone's death is not the same. Now what is happening? There is a clear difference between the death of a `momin`, the death of a Muslim, and the death of a non-believer. There is a clear difference. The death of a Muslim... the death of a `momin`, how it will be, first you understand that, then you will understand a lot about how ordinary people die. And what happens before death? What happens at the time of death? What happens after death? And after that, what rungs are there? All those things will, Insha'Allah, come in the lesson. So the first thing I told you is that a human's death, when it occurs, then what happens? We think that... you... sometimes you... from your mouths the words come out that, "brother, as long as there is breath, there is hope" (`jab tak sāns, tab tak ās`). This is a sentence that is common among the elite and the common folk. As long as there is breath, there is hope. So what does it mean? It is a reality. We say it without understanding, but it is a saying of wisdom. The fact is that all our breaths... the number of breaths we have to take, its counted breaths have been recorded there in the oxygen layer, which I had told you about, that our... the sphere of ether, below the sphere of ether is the sphere of nitrogen, and below that... after that is the sphere of air, and in the sphere of air, there is the oxygen layer. In that oxygen, your breaths are... counted breaths are present. If you take that last breath, then your ration of breaths is not there, your action is finished, so let's go, your matter here is finished. Now, the common conception is... what is it? A section of Muslims has this common conception, that in paradise, there is a tree called Shajar-e-Tuba. That Shajar-e-Tuba has various... branches, and it has crores, countless leaves. And the state of those leaves is that when a leaf falls, a person here dies. That leaf is a symbol, that the leaf fell, so... what is a leaf falling? If some wood hits it, or say the wind blows, then a calamity has come, meaning we have passed away. There is no such matter. A leaf breaking or a leaf turning yellow or falling does not mean you fall here. And things don't happen. But for this very reason... now you... in many things... this is also a very complex thing, which is very troubling for the human mind, that a human's... see, this is a very big point I am saying, but I will not explain it now. The explanation will come later. But I am saying that a human's, when death... he assumes that it is possible his death was written, brother, now through suicide, but he has died. It is not like that. This is an offense. Offense against God. He has violated His law. That his death was appointed for a certain time, it comes at that exact time and will come at that time. `Yudrikukum al-mawtu wa law kuntum fī burūjin mushayyada` (Death will overtake you even if you are in lofty towers). If you are even inside a fortress, death will reach you. It is going to reach you. So that is a certain thing, about which all the wise men have used the word `yaqīn` (certainty). Death is called `yaqīn`. It is a thing that will come. But this certainty... the thing that is to come, for that, one must understand that this suicide... the one who brings his death early, since he has broken that law, now what will happen? That the relations that have been established related to him, there are millions of relations he has. He has a relation with plants, with parents, with relatives, with air, with water, with food, with the earth, with burial, with the shroud, he has a relation with the country, he has thousands, millions of relations, one man. And he has broken all those relations by breaking one law. As soon as he broke this law, what will nature do to him? It will give him full punishment. Just as you do not live here without being punished, in the same way, nature will also punish him, and Hell is his punishment. The punishment for one who commits suicide is Hell. The punishment for one who commits suicide is Hell. So it is known that this is a very big... the biggest sin, which... if... although you are taking your own life. So if you are saving your own life, then in the same way you should consider that if you are saving your own life, then it is obvious that you are profiting that much, you are gaining that much of a great benefit, you are doing that much of a good deed. If you are saving yourself. And if you are saving all your limbs, then it is obvious that all those limbs will testify for you on the Day of Judgment, not against you, but in your favor.

...these are such high personalities that don't even ask. Umme Salma is a very high personage, but she comes and says, "O Messenger of Allah, include me in this cloak, so I too can be among the Ahl al-Bayt." He replied, "`Anti 'alā al-khayr` (You are upon goodness). O Salma, you are on a good path, but it cannot be that you are included among the Ahl al-Bayt." "I will not include anyone besides these five." But the Prophet included two in these five. One, the spiritual teacher, whom they call `Sayyid al-Malā'ikah` (Master of the Angels), Jibril Amin. To him it was said... in Janab Imam Husayn's final sermon there is a line that says, "Jibril is our sixth." So the sixth of your *panjatan* is Jibril. These are all things to understand. How he is Jibril, what he has become, how he was included. And physically, the one who was included was Mawlana Salman al-Farsi, `salawatullah 'alayh`. That Janab Salman, who was the highest personality of the Prophet's era. That Salman-e-Pak was included. In this way... So why are they Ahl al-Bayt? Because they were from *there*. The Prophet was looking at the connection from *there*. ...if you cut the second hand, the life is not diminished. Why didn't he die? And why is the life not diminished? It is a moment for reflection. But when you cut the head, he dies. So it is known that the connection of life (`jān`) is with the head. The connection is only with the head. It is not with the hands and feet. The hands and feet are instruments through which the faculty (`quwwat`) acts. It is the faculty that acts. And what is that faculty? I had said that when that faculty's image emerges, that image finds life. This image that you have been making for ages, what are you doing? For your entire life, religion (`dīn`) is the name of portraiture, the name of making your own image. And the image you have made, you... at the time of death... that image will be presented to you. `Fa-wajadū mā 'amilū ḥāḍirā wa mā rabbuka bi-ẓallāmin li-l-'abīd` (And they will find what they did present [before them]. And your Lord does no injustice to [His] servants). Now, upon being presented, what will happen? The Prophet says that the death of a `momin` is a cause for happiness. Because he will see his image and be very happy. He is very happy that what a good image, what a good thing I have made. So since it is his own creation, he likes it anyway, but since it was made in obedience to God and His Messenger, he is even happier looking at that image. Now, along with being happy, what will happen? That in this image, in this happiness, he will remain engrossed, and his `nafs-i ḥissiyyah` which is inside him... "Inside him" means what? The faculties are all external. Meaning, the machinery on which it acts is inside. And what is that machinery? It is the heart, the brain, the liver. These are its centers where they act. The `ḥissiyyah`, `nāṭiqah`, and `nāmiyah` act on these things. And the `ḥissiyyah`... this image will pull the `ḥissiyyah`. It will pull it and join it to itself. Now, when it joins, how will it be? How will it join? In the way that this cushion that is placed before you... this... this cushion that is placed, its shape and the cushion, just separate them for me and show me. Its shape and the cushion, separate them and show me. They cannot be separated. So in exactly the same way, they will join. Our `ṣūrat` (form/image) and our... our `ḥissiyyah`... and `ḥissiyyah` and our `ṣūrat`, in the same way, will become one. When they become one, then as soon as they become one, the `'umūd-i nūr` will come into action. That `'umūd-i nūr` that has gone from top to bottom, where the forms are recorded, it will pull our... our form and what will it do? The one who is one step ahead of you, whose number, if yours is 18, then his is 19, it will give it to him. It only has to do this much work. Even you will not know that someone has come to you. Just as an uninvited guest arrives, in the same way, they will have arrived. So what will happen? That... that... that form will come. So in this way, to every `momin`, the other `momin`'s... in this way it will keep happening, shunting will be happening. And how is this happening? To millions at once. Just as a computer separates and divides things, our intellect cannot even comprehend it. So in exactly the same way, nature's computer will start working, and that thing will be separated, and whichever form your form is inferior to, even a little, it will be handed over to that one. This is called `ḥadd-i 'ālī`. You will go to your `ḥadd-i 'ālī`. That `ḥadd-i 'ālī`, if you knew in life who it was, you would lick their soles. You would prostrate to them. And for every blessing, you would first offer thanks to them, then offer it to Him. For this very reason, the Prophet hinted, "If I were to make prostration permissible, I would tell the wife to prostrate to her husband." So what was the meaning? He was telling the beneficiary to prostrate to the benefactor. This was the Prophet's meaning. It was a matter of understanding. Anyway, the point was that in this way, they will start joining, they will join. But what happens? In the `da'wat-i ḥaqq` (the true mission), in the `da'wat-i Sulaymāniyyah Ja'fariyyah`, just as you see, there are `ḥudūd` (ranks). Brother, we don't have the ruling of `ṣallū khalfa kulli barrin wa fājir` (pray behind every righteous and sinner), that you can pray behind anyone. He is righteous, he is a sinner, a liar, a drinker, a gambler, but you put him forward... you say Bismillah... you stand up... Allahu Akbar... Brother, this is also a method. You know he is a sinner, a transgressor, how can you pray behind him? So it is known that every thing happens with `idhn` (permission). For this very reason, the Rasul was told, `Dā'iyan ilā Allāhi bi-idhnihi` (as one who invites to Allah by His permission). Did you see? That `Dā'iyan ilā Allāhi bi-idhnihi wa sirājan munīrā` (as one who invites to Allah by His permission, and as an illuminating lamp). That one who calls towards Allah by His command, and you are an illuminating lamp. So it is known that every thing includes Allah's command. It must be `bi-idhnihi`. Until there is permission, it does not happen. So it is known that here too there is permission. So it must be with permission. So now what happened? That thing was established with permission, and you... from here... you left and went to your `ḥadd-i 'ālī`. After reaching the `ḥadd-i 'ālī`... now, what happens? That in any `da'wah`, the `ḥudūd` that are established, the one who establishes the `ḥudūd` sees this, that their excellence, their temperament, their `taqwā` (piety), their purity, he examines everything. Otherwise, he is responsible (`mas'ūl`). The question will be asked of him. The one he is elevating... the question will be for the one who elevates. So the one he is elevating, understand that he will only elevate those who have that capability. And what does capability mean? What, will there not be a `ḥadd-i 'ālī` among the `mominīn`? There will be, undoubtedly. There will be countless. There can be. Undoubtedly. One `momin` can be the `momin` of many people. He can be the `ḥadd-i 'ālī` of many. He can be. Everything is correct. But where the `ḥadd` is established, that "brother, this is the `mabsūṭh`." Wherever the word `mabsūṭh` has come, understand that some matter has happened. Now what does it mean? That the circle has started to shrink. The `ḥudūd` were established, that they are the milestones. Now the milestone that was made, it started to gather many things, and the circle started to shrink. So now, such a milestone, if you start to gather them, then above them will be the `ma'dhūn`... the `mukāsir`, above them will be the `ma'dhūn`, above them will be the `dā'ī-i maḥṣūr`, above them will be the `dā'ī-i muṭlaq`. The one who is the master of the `jazeera` (island/region), everything will gather with him. When everything gathers with the master of the `jazeera`, and it is destined for all of them to gather with him, it is destined for them to come to that point, then if you call him `mālik` (master), what is wrong with that? For this very reason, we call our elders `mālik`, so why do we call them that? We call Sayyidnā `mālik`, so why do we call him that? We call him that for this very reason, that he is the master. When our... our `ṣūrat` is released, it will surely come to him. This is a certain and conclusive thing. So when it comes to him, it is known that he is the master. He is the master. So it is obvious that when he is the master... now the one who is his master, who is that? The one who is the master of three `jazeera`s. Or the one who is the master of twelve `jazeera`s. So now the circle is shrinking, see. A large circle into a smaller one, a smaller one into an even smaller one, an even smaller one into an even smaller one, and what has happened? Now it is concentrated at one point. What is that point? That `nuqṭah-i parkār` (center of the compass), what is it? It is the `dā'ī`. Now the `dā'ī-i 'aẓīm` (Great `dā'ī`) has come before you as one point, after which you either understand the Imam or the `nā'ib-i Imam`, so you have only that. After that, there is no other personality. But in reality, what is it? The number of ranks between you and the `dā'ī` is the same as the number of ranks between the `dā'ī` and the Imam. Are you understanding? The number of ranks between us and the `dā'ī`, these are all spiritual matters. In the same way, between a `dā'ī` and an Imam, there are ranks. For example, above a `dā'ī` will be a `dā'ī-i balāgh`, above a `dā'ī-i balāgh` will be who? The `ḥujjat`. Above the `ḥujjat` will be the `bāb`. And above the `bāb` will be the `ḥujjat-i Imam`. And above the `ḥujjat-i Imam` will be the Imam. These are the ranks that must exist in every era. They cannot be removed. This... this is the quorum, this is a completely fixed thing, it is a program of action on which work continues, it is an eternal thing. It is a completely unchangeable thing, an eternal and necessary thing. Now what will happen? That circle shrinks and shrinks and goes to the `dā'ī`. Now when the `dā'ī` passes away, he... all his `haykal`... what are those `ṣūrat`s? They are all being shunted. They are meeting and separating, meeting and separating. Meaning, from where to join them, where to join them, and how to join them, these are all things to understand. Anyway, happening and happening, what will that form be? It will be the form of a human. Its name is `haykal`. That... the `ṣūrat`s will all join together. When a `dā'ī` is passing away, if only our eyes could see, that the one who is passing away is passing away, but that one passing away, what thing is he taking? He is taking that great `haykal` which is taking on a human form, and all the `ṣūrat`s are finding their composition in it. And this entire `haykal` resides where? In the sacred Ka'bah. It resides in the sacred Ka'bah, in which the minimum number of `ṣūrat`s is 100,000. For this very reason it has been said that if someone performs one `rak'ah` of prayer in the sacred Ka'bah, what reward will he get? He will get the reward of 100,000. Because there, 100,000 `ṣūrat`s are watching you, so you got the reward of 100,000. So it is obvious that the most sacred place in the physical world, if there is one, is the sacred Ka'bah. And the `haykal` has to reside there, so it will reside there. But the Imam can be anywhere. The Imam will be anywhere, but his sight will be there. Meaning, you switch it on, and the... where will the effect be? It will be in the sacred Ka'bah. So it is obvious that it will be. Now, in this way, the `ṣūrat`s shrink and shrink and come where? They come to the `bāb`... to the `dā'ī`. Now from the `dā'ī`, they go to the `dā'ī-i balāgh`. From the `dā'ī-i balāgh`, progressing, they go to the `dā'ī`... to the `ḥujjat`. When they progress from the `ḥujjat`, then this is the stage of `sidrat al-muntahā` that comes, which is called `bāb al-abwāb`. When they reach the `bāb al-abwāb`, that `bāb al-abwāb`, which is called the gate of gates. The Imam has many gates, but the gate of gates is the `bāb al-salām`, the gate which has been referred to as `bāb-i ẓāhir` (the external gate) and `bāb-i bāṭin` (the internal gate). That is the real gate. So, just as I can tell you, that if all the `ṣūrat`s were coming to the Prophet, then at that time, the `bāb al-abwāb` for all the `ṣūrat`s, for the entire Islamic world that had spread, if there was a gate for it, then who was it? It was Salman al-Farsi. Salman al-Farsi was that `bāb al-abwāb`. He was the gate. But who did the Prophet, peace be upon him, call the gate? He called Janab Ali. "I am the city of knowledge, and you are the gate of that city of knowledge." So the gate you are calling him, you are calling him in a spiritual sense, in the sense of knowledge. But in reality, what is it? The indication is towards Salman al-Farsi. It is not towards Janab Ali. The gate is... so in the same way, every Imam has a `bāb al-abwāb`, who is made a gate. And these are the esoteric knowledges... there are thousands of books on these knowledges. There are thousands of books. To acquire these knowledges, about these `ḥujjat`s, `bāb al-abwāb`s, who is the `bāb` of whom, and which of the `bāb al-abwāb`s is external, internal, or is it a `silsil` (chain) or an `inbi'āthī` (emanation), whether it is the `ḥāfiẓ` of the station of Moses or the `ḥāfiẓ` of the station of the prophets, to understand all these things... these are such deep matters that to explain them is also a difficult thing for you to understand. So anyway, these are many things. So anyway, all this... this is just an indication, these are alleyways. These are particulars (`juzīyyāt`), there are many. There are countless particulars, believe me. So anyway, that `bāb al-abwāb` is the one who handles that `haykal`, about which the Lord said, `jannat al-ma'wā 'indahā sidrat al-muntahā` (The Garden of Abode, near it is the Lote-tree of the Farthest Boundary). `Jannat al-ma'wā` is that near which is `sidrat al-muntahā`. `Sidrat al-muntahā` is the person of the Imam. Now you have arrived. I was saying that one Imam's... see, remember my words. A little... the time will be a little more. For one Imam to give birth to his child... for one Imam to give birth to his child and for one Imam to spread his `da'wah`, both are equal. Did you understand? Now, how are they equal, I will explain to you. For one Imam to give birth to his offspring, and for one Imam to spread the noble `da'wah`, both are completely equal things. How is it? That an Imam who is spreading the `da'wah`, what is he doing? He is irrigating, he is cultivating. Meaning, he is irrigating the `ṣūrat`s so that their forms become good, so that all the good `ṣūrat`s gather with him. There should be no waste (`kachrāpan`) in them, no crookedness in them. All the `ṣūrat`s should come in a good state. Their character should be good, their conduct should be good, their character should be good, their this thing should be good, their knowledge should be good, their practice should be good. Why do the `du'āt` say this? Why do the lower ranks say this? Why do they keep exhorting for good deeds? For this very reason, that the one who dies will die, and it is obvious that the `ṣūrat` will separate, but the `ṣūrat` should not come in a wretched state. Every parent wants their child to be fresh, healthy, handsome, and with sound limbs. It shouldn't be that he is born with deficient limbs. No parent is happy with a deficient child. They will hold the child to their heart because it is their child, but they will not be happy. So in exactly the same way, the `ṣūrat`s that come to an elder, he wants them to be good, so he will keep advising, will keep teaching, assemblies will keep happening, and their characters will... they will keep refining their characters, so that those `ṣūrat`s become good and come to him. Now, all these `ṣūrat`s have gathered where? With an Imam. And I am telling you that a `bāb al-abwāb`, when he passes away, when does he pass away? His time of death is fixed. The passing of the `bāb al-abwāb` is in his own control. In the world, only one personality... the Imam's matter is separate... that matter is not here... I am telling you that he is from the `kalamm`. Leave that aside. This is from the `kalamm` it is related. Imams, prophets, messengers, etc., to consider them human is... it is a thing that has fallen from humanity. God forbid, God forbid. They are `kalamm`. They have cast a reflection. And if anyone is achieving the pinnacle of humanity, it is only one person, who is the `bāb al-abwāb`. The pinnacle of humanity that is being achieved, it is not by the prophets, it is by the `bāb al-abwāb`. The `bāb al-abwāb` is the one who achieves the pinnacle of humanity. And how does he achieve the pinnacle of humanity? That he... when... it is given into his control... as they say, "God asks the servant, 'Tell me, what is your will?'" That is the `bāb al-abwāb`. He is what? `Man shā'a shā' Allāh, mā shā' Allāh shā'nā` (What we willed, God willed; what God wills, we will). These are those servants, the `bāb al-abwāb`, whose life is so pure that just consider that for a `momin` to progress and reach the rank of a `dā'ī`, what efforts it will take. And from a `dā'ī`, to leave and... I am telling you, climbing the same number of ranks, if he reaches the rank of a `bāb al-abwāb`, then this is the state that if he says, "it shouldn't rain," it will immediately stop raining. He says, "the wind shouldn't blow," the wind will stop blowing. Because they are obedient. All the elements of nature are obedient to him. They are obedient to the `bāb al-abwāb`. Now, the matter of the Imam is something to be left aside. The `bāb al-abwāb`, whatever he says, motions are happening. The elements, as many as there are in nature, they are all obedient to him. So now death is also in his hand. And he passes away when? When the Imam is four days, 40 days, or four years old. This period is fixed. Four days, 40 days, or four years is the age of the Imam. So he has a connection with Imam, peace be upon him. From these periods, he chooses one period. Four days, 40 days, or four years. This is the period. Now you will not understand what subtleties are in it, what subtle matters are in it. And there are subtleties in it, and he chooses a period from it and after choosing it, his death occurs. "Death occurs" means what? He himself wills his death, and his death occurs. And when he dies, what happens? That entire `haykal`, the carrier of all those `ṣūrat`s becomes he himself. And he becomes the `qalb-i haykal` (heart of the `haykal`) of that entire `ṣūrat`. Now I will tell you how those `ṣūrat`s are gathered. If I take a large mirror, an `a'inah` (mirror), and place that `a'inah` before you, you will look into it and say, "what a good, clear, crystal mirror." And everything is perfectly visible in it, just like a mirror. And I drop that mirror and break it, and I make a thousand pieces of it. Now you see, if you pick up one piece from it, will you not see an image in it? You will see it. And if I join all those pieces, will you not see one image again? So in the same way, although you see one `bāb al-abwāb`, he is divided into thousands, into millions. Although you see one Imam, he is divided into millions. This is what it is, "different aspects of nature," which the world has spoken of with foolishness, we are speaking of it with wisdom. That this is the wonder of nature, that he... this is why when a person came to Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq and said, "Is this the Imam? I heard so much praise for the Imam. Is this the Imam?" He... he read his thoughts. The Imam was there, what would he not read, what thing would he not see? What particle is there that is hidden from them? He said, "Just scratch my back." He... he removed the cloth and when he started scratching, he said, "What is this? The Imam's condition?" The entire back is completely afflicted, full of boils. "Is this the Imam?" He was astonished. And he fell into more confusion, that "this Imam is like this?" He went and sat down. Then he called him again. He came again. He said again, "Brother, it's itching." Now the whole court is filled, he can't refuse either. He said, "This is a strange thing. Look at the Imam's condition. The back, all afflicted. How can he be such an Imam?" He came again. He said, "What I was thinking was absolutely correct." Now when he puts his hand, he sees the back is completely clear. "This is a strange thing." He said, "This is a strange miracle." Then he went and sat down. Then the Imam said, "Come again." When he came again, now when he puts his hand, he finds neither a back, nor a head, nor what he finds, nor this he finds, he finds nothing. So he is `al-ān kamā kān` (now as he was). He is from *there*. "The one in whose grasp is the divinity, I am that servant." These are those personalities. So anyway, this Imam's `haykal` is established in this way. And an Imam's spreading the `da'wah` and giving birth to a child are one and the same. I will explain this matter, Insha'Allah, in tomorrow's lesson, how they are the same. And I told you this, that the `haykal` that is formed, how is it formed? A person's `nāṭiqah` (rational soul), which is his thought (`taṣawwur`), that `taṣawwur` plus his... his `ḥissiyyah`... that `ḥissiyyah`, which has performed worship and piety for ages, it joins together, both things join together and become one, which we call a `ṣūrat`. And those `ṣūrat`s all gather, and after gathering, they... they leave and... they gather at one place at the `bāb al-abwāb` and become a `haykal`, and that `haykal` goes to the Imam. This is called `imāmat`. If the Imam does not receive this `haykal`, he is not an Imam, for us. `Imāmat` is this very thing, that `naṣṣ` (designation) is done. This `naṣṣ` is done at this very time. For us, `naṣṣ` means this. The written `naṣṣ` is separate, the paper is separate, the ink is separate, the pen is separate, the time is separate. And the thing that is written, it means that the `ṣūrat`s are counted and handed over to you. This is called `naṣṣ`. And when they are handed over, he becomes responsible for them. Insha'Allah, I will tell you that at the time of death... you have only seen the `ḥissiyyah` leaving, meaning a little bit... in tomorrow's lesson I will tell you... how the `ḥissiyyah` joins with the `nāṭiqah` to become a `ṣūrat` and then a `haykal`. And how the `nāsūt` is formed, meaning how the `nāmiyah` comes out. And after that, how an Imam giving birth to a child is the same as spreading the `da'wah`, this I will, Insha'Allah, explain in detail tomorrow.

I was telling you that in the matter of *namiyah*, *hissiyah*, and *natiqah*, I had said that these are three *nafs* (souls/selves). We have understood that the ones who are given to us by Allah Ta'ala (the Exalted) as *nafs*, and these three *nafs* I had told you, what is their *makr* (base), and where is their *source*, and where is their *palat* (return), and when are they received? These three or four things I had clarified for you. I had told you that the highest *nafs* is the *nafs al-natiqah* (the rational soul). After that is the *nafs al-hissiyah* (the sensate soul), and the third *nafs* is the *nafs al-namiyah* (the vegetative soul). What are their powers? *Nafs al-namiyah* is from *numu* (growth), from growing, and the power of growth is called *namiyah*. *Hissiyah* is what is called sensation, whether it is the external senses or the five external or five internal senses. This is what is called *hissiyah*. *Natiqah*, the power of *nutq* (speech/reason), is what the world calls *natiqah*. In reality, it is not the power of *nutq*. This is just the external manifestation. The internal power of *nutq* is that the *nafs* of a human, the *'uluww-e-manzilat* (high station) it had attained, there, at the time of falling, the angle at which its fall occurred, and the *niyyah* (intention) that it made at that time while falling from there, and its *concept* that was there—to attain that is called *natiqah*, which we call *zamir-e-nadamah* (the conscience of regret). We have several words for it. There is *zamir-e-nadamah*, there is *sabiqah* (antecedent), and we, and there, it is a matter of "there," and our concept is from "there." Our thought is what we did there. So, I was telling you that what is the *makr* (base) of these three *nafs* like? It is that these three *nafs* are born from what? They are a part of our *shabih* (image/likeness). What we are thinking is a part of us, it is our one *part*. And the thought we had there, that thought of ours was preserved, and that same thought is given to us here upon taking the *'ahd-e-sharif* (noble covenant). This is what is called the receiving of the *natiqah*. And upon taking the *'ahd-e-sharif*, what happens? That same *tasawwur* (conception) of ours is presented before us, and we move forward carrying that *tasawwur*. And the amount of *nadamah* (regret) we felt, to that same extent, *qudrah* (Nature/Power) makes us reach [our goal]. And with it, we keep moving forward. And `laysa lil-insani illa ma sa'a` (and that man can have nothing but what he strives for). Striving for a human is nothing but what he has striven for, meaning striving now becomes necessary. But *qudrah*, to the extent that he has made the *niyyah*, to deliver him to that point is the work of *qudrah*. After that, what happens? He moves forward with his own effort. Now, at which point his effort from "there" ends and his effort from "here" begins, no one can estimate this. These things have been hidden, and they have been hidden for his own betterment. And the second thing I had said was *hissiyah*. And *hissiyah* is what? It is also a thing from "there," it is *nadamah*, which was the position after that, and as I had explained to you, one was a gas form, and this is a liquid form. And one which, and this liquid form, which is called *hissiyah*, what is its *makr*? It is the *aftab* (sun). The *aftab* is such a thing that when a human is born here, it is given to him, and through it, he is born as a living being. And the third thing it had was *namiyah*. And *namiyah* was its third thing, which is a thing of growth, a thing of power, this is its *nafs*. This is also a thing of the *nafs*. And when is this received? After the *nutfah* (sperm-drop) emerges from the loins of the father and settles in the mother's womb, at that time it is received, and this is the very thing that causes growth. So, there are three souls (*jan*) in a human. In a common human, there are two souls, and in a *Sulaymani* or a *mu'min* (believer), there are three souls. The first soul is that the settling in the *shikam-e-madar* (mother's womb) is born from the *madah* (substance), and what is its name? It is the settling of the *nutfah*, and it is called *namiyah*. When it comes out of the *shikam-e-madar*, then it is called the receiving of *hissiyah*, and from the *aftab* that thing is given to it. Its thing is given to it, and this happens. And when is *natiqah* received? When he becomes *baligh* (mature), understanding, intelligent, becomes *baligh*, becomes understanding, then at that time, if he takes the *'ahd-e-sharif* at the hand of some *ataliq* (tutor/guide), then from the time of the *'ahd-e-sharif*, his own thing is given to him. No new thing is being received. But this is neither a thing to be seen, nor is it a thing to be seen, but all three *nafs* are obtained by him. Now, after taking the three *nafs*, what happens? The reality is that all his things, meaning all the *fuzlat* (superfluities) that were there—he had tough sinews, soft sinews, muscles, nails, hair, and tough bones, soft bones—these six things are called *fuzlat*. So, the process of all these things was that they all had to be obtained and had to progress to become *natiqah*. But because they did not become *natiqah*, but the procedure was such that they kept getting more or less, they kept happening, they kept happening, and they came into a state of *tajassum* (corporeality). Now what will happen? Emerging from all this *tajassum*, everything has to do what? It has to become *natiqah*. Until they become *natiqah*, they will not become *'aql* (intellect). If they do not become *'aql*, they will not go into the *'alam al-'aql* (world of intellect). This is a necessary matter. But what did *qudrah* do? For this, it has appointed a duration, that one *shabih* (image) that is falling from there to here, for that *shabih* to come into the *'alam al-'aql* again, if a duration is required, it is 360,000 multiplied by 360,000. Meaning, until he spends the duration of one *dawr-e-a'zam* (grand cycle) here in the world, he will not progress. Now if we understand that for one *'aql*, one *shabih* that has come into this world, for this *shabih* to progress and go back into the *'alam al-'aql* again, if a duration is required, then what is it? It is one *dawr-e-a'zam*. Now you see this. Just listen properly to my words, that I am saying that for one *shabih* that has fallen from there to here, a punishment has occurred, and after falling, for it to progress, the duration required is one *dawr-e-a'zam*. And you know about *dawr-e-a'zam*, as I had explained that the duration of one *dawr* is 400,000 years, and one *dawr-e-a'zam* is of 400,000 such *dawrs*. Only after spending the duration of one *dawr-e-a'zam* will it progress. When I am saying that one *dawr-e-a'zam* must be spent, then you will fall into the thought, "Then what is good, and what is bad?" When progress is to happen only after a *dawr-e-a'zam*, within the duration of one *dawr-e-a'zam*, then what is the benefit? What is to be gained by running more? We have to reach it in that same duration. Walk slowly, slowly. Time has to be passed in any case. What will be, will be. So, what is the real matter? The wise person will be the one who completes his journey with success and goes to his destination and rests. That person will not be counted as wise who, being a *saliq* (traveler on the path), keeps the destination far away and sits with this hope that, "Come on, the destination is bound to be reached someday." No. The wise one is he, the good one is he, who quickly completes his destination. That, of the *du'at* (callers/missionaries), of others, the ranks that are elevated for us, who do their *tazkiyat* (purifications), *tasfiyat* (clarifications), who make their progress, the meaning of that is just this, that we, on our spiritual level, should purify ourselves, cleanse ourselves so quickly, so that we cleanse ourselves before the full duration of that *dawr-e-a'zam*. You will say, "Alright, you have cleansed and you have become pure, everything has happened, but the duration required is still the same." A lot is required, but your state is the state of a successful one, and after facing that success, you cannot imagine that unsuccessful state, of one who is still moving, crawling. So, there is a very big difference. But you see this, that if that duration is fixed as one, then he is in a state of *tashbih* (likeness) and *tahleel* (dissolution), and he has reached God's mercy, and he is a very successful person. And that person is not successful who is progressing slowly, slowly. So anyway, this is the difference between the two that I have told you.

When 'Ashir al-Mudasir made a plan (*tadbir*), and *nasut* and *lahut* came to his mind, and he established the chain of *Imamah* (Imamate), now he himself cannot stop this chain. Because this method he created for the progress of the world, and which was sanctioned by *'aql-e-awwal* (the First Intellect), now he himself cannot change that thing either. That is why it was said that, [unclear Arabic phrase related to God's will and Imamah], that the *mashi'ah* (will) of Allah is current in everything except *Imamah*. So, what is the meaning? That the chain of *Imamah* cannot be stopped. That chain continues on. As the Shi'a say today, that after Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq, جناب (Mr./His Eminence) Isma'il was indeed the Imam, but since he passed away, his brother Musa Kazim became the Imam, because Mawlana (our master) Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq did what? He made him the Imam. We do not believe this at all, because *Imamah* cannot be reversed. After the father, it will go to the son. If Isma'il was the Imam, then his son would have been the Imam, whose جناب (name) was Mawlana Muhammad, whom they call Mawlana Muhammad al-Maktum. So, the matter, the chain, will continue on from father to son, and this chain will never end. There will be millions of Imams, countless Imams, and the chain of *Imamah* will continue on. Insha'Allah (God willing), I will, in the future, when these topics are finished, I will also tell you some of the chains of the prophets and the Imams.

These were the things I had told you. That *namiyah*, *hissiyah*, *natiqah*. *Namiyah*, *hissiyah*, *natiqah* are the three *nafs*. And these three *nafs* are a part of the *shabih* (image/likeness) that is with God in the *'alam al-arwah* (world of spirits) in its original form, in the form of a *shabih*, in the form of a soul. It is one part of it, a *part*. It is the *nafs*, and also a part of it. And *nafs al-namiyah*, *nafs al-natiqah*, *nafs al-hissiyah*—why are these three called different *nafs*? On the basis of their *nadamah* (regret). The one among them who had the most *nadamah* became *natiqah*. The one who had less *nadamah* became *hissiyah*. The one who had even less *nadamah* became *namiyah*. The one who had even less *nadamah* became an animal. The one who had even less *nadamah* became a plant. It became a mineral, it became soil. In this way, happening, happening, in the end, it reached up to here in our hair. Because human hair does not grow. So, it was known that this is the matter of *nadamah*. So, the most excellent of things will be what? It will be *natiqah*. And *qudrah* (Nature/Power) did what to *natiqah*? It was such a supremely high thing that it did not send it into this world at all. It kept it on its own *'arsh* (throne). It kept it in the *'umud al-nur* (pillar of light), which we call the place of refuge. The *natiqah* of each one, because it has regretted, its regret has a particular angle. That regret is on some angle, on some corner. And that angle is preserved in some place. It remains. Now, this, which is the light of regret, and it has been placed. Now, how does this happen, and how is regret received from there? This is a thoughtful matter.

Someone had asked a question that upon the death of a *mu'min*, what is the state of his soul? So, to know that, it is necessary to first understand these stages: what is *nafs-e-nadamah*, and how does *zamir-e-nadamah* (conscience of regret) work? As I was explaining, this, the one who is falling from there, his *zamir-e-nadamah* is preserved. That is constantly preserved, and this is the very thing that is received here, and it is received in the form of regret, and that is called receiving the *natiqah*. And when is *natiqah* received? When he takes the *'ahd-e-sharif* (noble covenant). After taking the *'ahd-e-sharif*, he receives the *natiqah*. And with this *nafs*, what work does he do for his whole life? He purifies it his whole life with *'ilm wa 'amal* (knowledge and action), with worship, and purifying it, purifying it, he makes it big, and he makes it strong, and he makes it capable, so that it becomes capable of progressing from that world.

As I was saying, that there is one's *nasi*, which is that *lahut* (divine realm) and *nasut* (human realm). And regarding *lahut*, I had told you in detail that this is the very thing that becomes a part of *lahut*—it is our *nafs al-natiqah*. When our *nafs al-natiqah* departs, then upon departure, the *nafs al-natiqah* kicks the *hissiyah* and leaves. And after kicking the *hissiyah*, it leaves, and after going, it, at its *hujjat*'s (proof's) place, and he at his *hujjat*'s place—in this way, it passes through *hujjat* after *hujjat*, and from the *hujjat* to the *juzr*, and from the *juzr* to the *tali*, and from the *tali* to the *hujjat-e-layl*, and from there it reaches the *bab al-abwab* (gate of gates), and from the *bab al-abwab*, after staying for four years, four months, and forty days, it passes away and reaches the Imam, peace be upon him. This entire procedure that is happening with our *natiqah*, this whole procedure is what is called *lahut*. You understand? This is all called *lahut*. And the procedure that is of our *hissiyah*, our *hissiyah* became separated with whom? With the *natiqah*. As I said to you before, who is the one who takes our *hissiyah*? It is a pilot. Always remember that when you go to some island, when you reach the harbor, then what happens there? Your captain separates, and the pilot from there comes to steer and take the ship. So, in exactly the same way, this *natiqah* is a thing from "there." Until it comes, your *hissiyah* will not be capable of leaving from here. So, the *hissiyah* will become capable and will leave from here. Now what thing is left? *Hissiyah* met with *natiqah*. *Natiqah* has completed its purification of *'ilm wa 'amal*. And these three things became one, "three in one." *'Ilm wa 'amal*, worships, all things, all came under *'ilm wa 'amal*. And *hissiyah* was in its place. And you did purification with knowledge. These all things became one, and that, included in the *zamir-e-nadamah*, it, the *surah* (form) as we call it, that *surah* progresses, and progressing, it reaches the *bab al-abwab* passing through *hujjat* after *hujjat*, and from the *bab al-abwab* it goes to the Imam, peace be upon him. And the Imam takes that *haykal* (form/temple), and after taking that *haykal*, it is called *Imamah* (Imamate). An Imam cannot be an Imam until that *Imamah* comes to him. Now, imagine that, a supposition is that in this whole journey, there are 100,000 people. So, 100,000 people are there, and let's assume 100,000 people are dying. Suppose.
