So, the 100,000 people who are dying, their *surah*—as soon as I say *surah*, you should understand: *natiqah* plus *hissiyah* plus *'ilm wa 'amal*—these three things reach the Imam, passing through *hujjat* after *hujjat*. How much time it takes, what time it takes, what dangers it faces, what obstacles it faces, all these things are a separate matter. Anyway, it has to reach the Imam through the *bab al-abwab*. I will say a little more about this later. But for now, understand that this is one procedure, this is one path you have seen. The second path I am telling you is that now what remains? That body from which he is dying, its *hissiyah*, *natiqah*, after all these things have left, now what thing is left? Only *namiyah* is left. And *namiyah*, when it departs, when does it depart? There are very few such believers who are such pure souls, such pure and clean, that upon death, their *nafs-e-namiyah* leaves and it progresses. But not everyone's *namiyah* leaves; rather, they remain in the grave, and inside that grave, they have to be included. And until when do they have to be included in the grave? And for a *mu'min*, this is the restriction, that if his *namiyah* is also imprisoned in his body, it is not for more than three days. So, there is a three-day imprisonment for them. Now obviously, in three days, he will be buried. Whether he is buried or not, anyway, after being buried, on the third day you do the *ziyarah* (visitation), the *fatihah* you read, the Qur'an you read, the good deeds you do, what is the purpose of all that? The purpose of that is that in some way, the *namiyah* should be released. The *namiyah* should progress. This is your purpose. It is done in three days. After three days, from the grave, that *namiyah* in the form of *rihiyya* (gaseous substance) emerges, and the moon pulls it with its rays, and for fifteen days it does the work of absorbing, and for fifteen days it does the work of giving. That is why from a crescent, it becomes a full moon, and from a full moon, it becomes a crescent. And taking this, what does it do? It hands it over to Mercury. Mercury hands it over to Venus. Venus gives it to the Sun. In the Sun, after being washed, after being cleaned—they are washed in Mercury too, they are washed in Venus too, there are separate tasks for them everywhere—and in the Sun, after its polishing is done, those *rihiyya* which are now completely transparent, have become pure, their impurities have been removed, their sediments have been removed, now those things come back to whom? To the moon. And the moon, through four fruits—either dates, or apples, or grapes, or pomegranates—through these, they fall upon them like dew, and the *hujjat*'s (proof's) supplications and that fruit, which he purifies, it is absorbed into it, and that thing, the Imam, peace be upon him, the angels bring it to his court. It is brought by some hand or the other. No other person can touch it. All the angels keep protecting it, and when it reached the Imam, and the Imam and his wife, the *zawjah mutahharah* (purified wife), when they eat, and from their union and marriage, the birth of a child is completed, that child's body and the nourishment of the body, what are they formed from? They are formed from those *rihiyya*. Meaning, it is not one apple or one pomegranate, but the foods that are received after that, the milk, the foods, all of those are the same *rihiyya* which had ascended from the graves of the believers in the form of *namiyah rihiyya*. So, it became known that who constitutes the body of an Imam? The final *ruh* (spirit) of a *mu'min*. The lowest *ruh* of a *mu'min* is what the body of an Imam is made of. So, what is the situation? That just as we have power and authority over our clothes, that whenever we want, we can change them, do as we want, whenever we want, we can do it, in the same way, they have power over the body. Whenever they want, whenever they wish, they can manifest it, change it, show it, hide it, and show their manifestation as they wish. They have complete power, authority over the body. And these powers of theirs are very vast, and to what extent they are vast, these are all things that are beyond count. It's not that there are only one or two incidents, no, but their numbers are countless, that how many miracles they can show, how many things they can be divided into, what is there, what is not, and how are their forms, how are their places of residence, how are their manifestations. Anyway, there are many details for an Imam. So, it was known that our *nafs-e-namiyah* that was broken, it became capable of forming his body and came to use. So, I was actually telling that the essential thing, the most noteworthy, the most important thing is the heart of this sphere and earth, and which heart is that? The heart that has been made for all the spiritual and physical worlds is the *Tamur*. The *Tamur* is the actual field which is doing the real work, and there, the chain of Imams that is established, the *Imamah* is current from that chain. So, the Imam who becomes an Imam in his place, what will he do? He will cast his *athar* (effect/trace) here. He will only cast an *athar*. And how is the *athar* established? I'll tell you, like a bottle of perfume, if you empty out all the perfume from it, you will say, "Is there anything left in it?" You will say, "No, I have emptied out all the perfume." Even if you try a million times to empty it, the fragrance will remain. So, in exactly the same way, they cast an *athar* here, and that *athar* establishes a body, and that body is requested from us. The Imam requests a body from us, so that he can be seen in the physical world. So that he can be seen like us, and can present a character like ours, can present a life-story like ours. For this reason, we are pleased with our kind of human. Just as if you see any animal doing things like humans, you see a parrot doing various kinds of tricks, doing things, so why does it appeal to you? Why do you like it? You don't like it because it is doing a strange thing, but because it is doing work like one of your own. So, you like it because it is doing work like one of your own. Absolutely, you also do the same kind of work, and that same action is there, it is of the angels. So, it became known that our real...are our pure Imams, who one after another, in the higher realm or the lower realm, keep getting established in the *Tamur*, whose succession is established there. So, the real Imam who is to be established is established where? In the *Tamur*. As soon as its bulb lights up in the actual field, or that point emerged, or in the *Bayt al-Ma'mur* (Frequented House) that point shone, and he came to his service, at that very moment his *hijab* (veil/manifestation) was established here, that this is Imam Hasan, peace be upon him. Now, this is Imam Husayn, peace be upon him. Or, this is Imam Zayn al-'Abidin, peace be upon him. You are calling him جناب (Mr./His Eminence) 'Ali Zayn al-'Abidin, but in reality, that 'Ali the high who is sitting there, he is the real 'Ali, and the one who is here, he is his *hijab*. So, he became the *muhtajib* (the veiled one), and this became the *hijab*. He became the *muhtajib*, this is his *hijab*, and in this way, the work is being done. I have said a very deep and important thing to you, I hope you have understood, that the *hijab* and the *muhtajib* are the most important things. It is in this way that there, he is the *muhtajib*, here is his *hijab*. The *muhtajib* is what? The *muhtajib* is a thing of "there," they are from "there," and they are established there, and they do not need to come into this world. But at the time when they cast their *athar* here, how is that *athar* established? It is that from us, the *namiyah* things that emerge in the form of *rihiyya*, those *rihiyya* are collected, they take the form of a statue, and they take a body, and that body of the Imam is what? It is the *hijab*. I hope you have understood. He is the *muhtajib*, this is the *hijab*. That is why the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said that I... look! That is why he is saying, that I, in the world, am Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him. My name is Muhammad. And my name in the heavens is Ahmad. Why did he say this? Because in that actual field, your name was Ahmad. And here your name is Muhammad. In the same way, the successor of the Prophet, Amir al-Mu'minin 'Ali, who is in the higher realm, his name there is [unclear], and here it is 'Ali. So, in this way, every Imam will have a *muhtajib* and a *hijab*. And the *hijab* here is what? It is an *athar*, and I am telling you that he himself does not come here, but he establishes an *athar*. Just as the *athar* of the *shabih* from "there" is falling on you, which is called the soul (*jan*), because of which you are walking around. If this soul is not there, you are a corpse. So, in the same way, their life, whatever it is, is from the *athar*. And that whole body which they have taken and are sitting before you, that is "us." It is us ourselves. The 100,000 individuals who died, their *namiyah* that rose from their graves in the form of *rihiyya*, the moon took it, and through Mercury and Venus, it was given to the Sun, and the Sun then gave it to the moon, and the moon threw it down here, and the fruit took it, and the fruit came into the food, and that food, it was the settling of the *nutfah*, and the child that was born was the Imam, peace be upon him. So, it was known that the relationship between the body and the soul that is ours, that relationship of theirs is that our highest soul is their lowest soul. The power that we have over our clothes, they have over their bodies. So, this difference you should have clearly understood. When you have understood that the relationships of the Imam are like this, then you will have to understand that this *namiyah* of ours which remains in the grave, this three-day prison that you endure sitting idle, how is this prison? Although it is a natural thing, it is a natural thing, but you see that a higher-ranking *mu'min* than him is one whose *nafs* is released upon death. He is the highest-ranking *mu'min*, whose *namiyah* also left, *hissiyah* also left, *natiqah* also left. He is the best one to die, whose *namiyah* also was released, *hissiyah* also was released, *natiqah* also was released. Meaning, *hissiyah* plus *natiqah*, which in the form of a *surah* became part of the *haykal*, and what remained was *namiyah*, *namiyah* also left. And after *namiyah* left, what happened? The moon's rays pulled it, but from where? From the body itself. From the body itself. There was no need to go into the grave and wait for three days. So, one *mu'min* whose *namiyah* is being released after death, and another *mu'min* whose *namiyah* is being released after going into the grave for three days, there is a big difference between the two. And the responsibility for all these things, the release, the *salvation of the soul*, or *mukti* (liberation), or our *najat* (salvation), or the attainment of the hereafter, all these things depend on what? On the *'ahd-e-sharif*. The basis of all these things, meaning the basis of the entire religion, is that hand in hand for ten minutes, the covenant you took, that whole basis, the summary of your life is that. The summary of the whole life is that, that at the time when the one giving [the covenant] said "In the name of Allah," and the sword was struck, and here the *'umud al-nur* came into motion, and he handed over that *tasawwur* to you. This is our belief, and that *tasawwur* was your own. God is as He is. You, meaning, it cannot be that someone else's *tasawwur* is given to someone else, God forbid, this cannot happen. The *tasawwur* that was yours was given to you. You continued doing *'ilm wa 'amal* (knowledge and action) taking that *tasawwur*, and in the world, you were busy with your hereafter. So, it was known that your *'ahd-e-sharif* is a basic thing, a fundamental thing. It is the *nuqta-e-bikar* (compass point), and the whole thing is revolving around it. And what is this *'ahd-e-sharif*? This is the *zamir-e-nadamah*. This is the *sabiqah*. And this is the weeping, the lamenting, the mourning, this is the worship, this is the *khushu'* (humility), this is the *khuzu'* (submissiveness), this is the asking for forgiveness and repentance in the court of God. The name of all of this is the *'ahd-e-sharif*. If you have taken the *'ahd-e-sharif* from the heart and have done everything, then everything will happen. You can understand it like this, the one who takes the *'ahd-e-sharif* and the one who does not take the *'ahd-e-sharif*, what is the difference between them? A train is there, and they are traveling, two...let's say two travelers are sitting on a train and are traveling. So, both of them reached, and one person did what? In some way or another, he took a lot of luggage. With how many bags and baggage he came, that he has winter luggage, summer luggage, new clothes, with several trunks and boxes he has boarded the train, and he has made full arrangements for his comfort. He has arranged for everything—eating, drinking, living, everything—and is boarding the train. And boarding, he is looking at his destination, and saying, "Well, I am going to the destination." And another person is there, who is coming, who is traveling, neither his clothes are proper, nor his luggage is proper. He doesn't have a single thing, but his clothes are also tattered. His clothes are tattered. In such a state, in a miserable state, he is traveling, but that poor fellow has a ticket. So, you tell me, will the one who has the ticket, the one who has taken the *'ahd-e-sharif*, reach the destination, or will the one who has boarded with so many bags and baggage, will he reach the destination? He will not reach the destination. After doing so much... "Oh, we had written hundreds of books." "We had been writing all our lives." "We had been working on Islamic studies all our lives." "We had been taking the name of the Prophet all our lives." "Oh, we had been reciting the *kalima tayyibah* (the good word) all our lives." "All our lives we have been reciting the *kalima*." No thing will be of any use. `Haba'an manthura` (like scattered dust). This is, look, the evidence from the Qur'an. Let me give you the evidence from the Qur'an. `Hal ataka hadith al-ghashiyah, wujuhun yawma'idhin khashi'ah, 'amilatun nasibah, tasla naran hamiyah` (Has there come to you the story of the Overwhelming [Event]? [Some] faces, that Day, will be humbled, Laboring [and] weary. They will [enter to] burn in an intensely hot Fire.). Allah Ta'ala says that how many faces there will be... he is remembering the people by their faces. How many faces there will be, how many people there will be, meaning in this one part, the whole meaning is being expressed. As a part for the whole. How many faces there will be on the Day of Judgment, who are performing *khushu'*. Performing *khushu'*, meaning God Himself is giving them testimony of *khushu'*. Performing *khushu'*, performing *khuzu'*, prostrating to their Lord, and offering prayers. Offering such prayers that a mark of prostration falls here first. The effect of prostration... Allah Ta'ala said that the effect of prostration should be known, the meaning was that by prostrating, so many prostrations have been done in the court of God that the forehead becomes luminous. It did not mean that we should rub and rub and get marks here. This was not the meaning. So, these Muslims thought that getting marks on the forehead is the effect of prostration. This was not the meaning. So, what was the meaning of doing all this? That by doing all this, from all things, the situation was that somehow our result should come out, and... Now, if suppose all this was done, with full luggage, he is going laden. He has performed many worships, kept many fasts, all these things. Allah Ta'ala says, performing *khushu'*, performing *khuzu'*, offering prayers... `tasla naran hamiyah`, "Oh, Our fire will burn them." O Lord, what are You saying? Just explain a little. God's Qur'anic verse is there. `Tasla naran hamiyah`, "We will throw those faces into the fire." We will kill them, and we will put them in the fire. "Oh, what is this matter?" "O Allah, why are you putting these praying ones, these forgiveness-seekers, these performers of *khushu'* and *khuzu'* in the fire?" Because they do not have the love of 'Ali. That *nuqta-e-bikar* (compass point) that was there, that *Tamur*, the regret that had to be done there, the regret that was supposed to be done, that regret is not with you, that ticket is not with you, that *'ahd-e-sharif* is not with you. So, go. `Tasla naran hamiyah`, for you, there is nothing but fire. There is only fire. So, for them, there will be no salvation. A person is sitting with a ticket, has taken the *'ahd-e-sharif*, he has such a ticket that he will reach his destination, but he is shivering all along the way. He is enduring cold all along the way, enduring heat, enduring troubles. So why is he shivering? Because he has not done the *'amal* (deeds). He has not taken the provision of *'amal*. *Khayr al-zad al-taqwa* (the best of provisions is piety). Piety was the best provision for the hereafter. Since he has not taken the provision for the hereafter, he is suffering troubles all along the way. So, if we suppose that we do not suffer troubles all along the way, we should also do its *'amal*, and also take the ticket, then what is there to ask? The hereafter is ours, only ours. And a Muslim who is doing everything, but since he does not have the ticket, that *'ahd-e-sharif* is not there, so nothing can happen. If you say that today there are so few Shi'a, so few who love 'Ali, what about them? You see, in the world, the saying is famous, "Love me and love my dog." If you love me, then love my dog too. So, if you love God, then you should not only love the people of God, meaning 'Ali, but also the people of 'Ali, the Ahl al-Bayt (People of the House), meaning the people of the *Tamur*, you should love them all. Here, what is your situation? That if you believe in 'Ali, you don't believe in the lineage of 'Ali. If you believe in 'Ali, you don't believe in the way 'Ali should be believed. You either believe him as the fourth, or the third, or the second, or not even the first, and what is the situation? You have made 'Ali the Imam. As the Shi'a believe. They believe 'Ali is the first Imam. Oh, a person who has become a Ph.D., if you call him a matriculate, it is an insult. He is a matriculate, so he is, he was at some time, brother, but now he is a Ph.D. At least call the poor fellow a doctor. And you are calling him a matriculate. So, that will be a wrong thing. So, what do the Shi'a do with their understanding? They believe he is the first Imam. This is the greatest misguidance, a deviation. The 'Ali who became the Imam of Imams, whom the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said in his own text. What did he say? That `al-Hasan wa al-Husayn sayyida shabab ahl al-jannah, imaman qama aw qa'ada, wa abu-huma khayrun min-huma` (Hasan and Husayn are the masters of the youth of Paradise, they are Imams whether they rise or sit, and their father is better than them). Hasan and Husayn are both true Imams, and their father is better than them. So, if the Prophet, suppose, had to say that all three are Imams, he would have said, "'Ali, Hasan, Husayn are all three true Imams." He could have said that. Why did he say, "better than them"? So, to say "better" indicates that there was something else which the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, was saying was better. That which was better was the *wasayah* (successorship). That 'Ali who was going to the *wasayah*, if you call him an Imam, it is a matter of insult. So, the one who is at whatever rank, keep him there, that is the right thing. If you wear your hat on your foot, this is not a human thing. To place something in an inappropriate place is injustice. The place where it belongs, it fits there. If you remove it from its place, this is injustice. So, it was known that this was true love, that love meant this. That is why the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said repeatedly, all his life he kept saying, sometimes praising 'Ali, sometimes spreading the cloak and saying, `Allahumma ha'ula'i Ahl al-Bayti` (O Allah, these are my Ahl al-Bayt). O Allah, these are my Ahl al-Bayt. Oh, what had happened to this Prophet that he was telling about his family members, his family members? He was telling because these are the family members of "there." They are not of "here," they are of "there," they are of the *Tamur*. He was telling this. That is why he was spreading the cloak and telling, that these are the Imams. These are your Imams. These are the ones for whose sake you regretted there. If you regret for them, then you will be successful. If you love the people of power, if you regret for them, if you obey them, or if you consider them the king, or consider them the rulers, then your chain will never connect. So, accept this chain, these are the Ahl al-Bayt. By *bayt* (house), it meant the *Tamur*. These are the people of "there." This was the indication of the Prophet, that you should understand the people of "there." So, it was known that the *'ahd-e-sharif* is that essential thing because of which salvation occurs. Now, if suppose he took the *'ahd-e-sharif*, and after taking it, he did not do *'ilm wa 'amal*, did not do worship, was deficient in fasting, deficient in prayers, deficient in this, deficient in that, deficient in character, deficient in this, then what will happen? The first thing, as I told you, is that his *namiyah* will not leave. No matter how much of a *mu'min* he is, the *namiyah* will not leave. And if the *namiyah* does not leave, what will happen? The torment of the grave will occur. The torment of the grave for how many days? But since he is a *mu'min*, respect was shown, that for three days, the torment of the grave will be upon him. Now, if the torment of the grave is upon him, this is what is called the torment of the grave. The torment of the grave, the torment of the grave, what is it? Oh, the one who is dying has died, the one who is departing has departed. These decaying bones, this body that is going to rot and decompose, after burying it in the ground, now Munkir and Nakir are coming and asking questions, and Munkir and Nakir are asking for your account. From where did Munkir and from where did Nakir come? All is correct, but from a scholarly perspective. What is meant by Munkir and Nakir? It is that the angels who are appointed over your *namiyah* and *hissiyah*, they will ask, "With what actions are you bringing your *hissiyah* and *natiqah*?" This is Munkir and Nakir. And what is the torment in the grave? It is that your *namiyah*, until it reaches its destination, its name is the torment of the grave. What suffering does the *namiyah* face? What suffering does the *namiyah* face? That suffering... you see, I have clearly told you that *hissiyah* is that thing which feels. The five external and internal senses, the one that carries them is a *nafs* whose name is *hissiyah*. Seeing, tasting, smelling, touching—these qualities are the qualities of *hissiyah*. Obviously, your *hissiyah* has gone. *Hissiyah* has gone, *natiqah* has gone, minus... a *nafs al-natiqah*—now what thing is left? Only *namiyah*. *Namiyah* has been buried inside your body. And *namiyah* has the power of growth. Now, I am telling you, the torment of the grave should have some meaning, some concept. What is the concept? It is that this *namiyah*, which for 50, 60, 70, 80, 90, 100 years of life was with you, along with *hissiyah*, so what happened? Some qualities of *hissiyah* developed within it. A little bit of awareness came. Some sensation came into it. Inside *namiyah*, some sensation came. That sensation that developed within it, that *hissiyah* of sensation that it took a little bit of, that *namiyah*, now when you are burying that *namiyah*, what will be the situation? That *namiyah* will start to feel some things. That is why the Prophet said what? "Look, don't use too much hot water for the funeral bath." "Look, lay him in the grave like this." "Look, observe this propriety." If you observe all these proprieties, then you have had mercy on that *namiyah*. The real thing is *namiyah*. The guest, whatever it is, is all *namiyah*. What's the matter with the body? The body is nothing. The real thing is *namiyah*. Now, if the *namiyah* is inside your body and has gone into your grave, then for three days, the suffering it faces, that suffering, God and God's messenger have described the torment of the grave in this way, that if he is a *mu'min*, he will face suffering of this extent, just as you fall in a dream. What happens in a dream? You see that you have climbed a big mountain and you are falling from it, and your state is such that when you wake up from your dream, you are drenched in sweat. Why, sir? Have you rolled off the bed? But you felt that you fell from a mountain. So, this feeling that is there, that same feeling your *namiyah* has in the grave. In the grave, that *namiyah* feels, and to reduce that feeling, what has to be done? We read the Qur'an, or read Surah Yasin, we do feeding, and we do *fatihah*, we do good deeds for him, what is that? It is that the *namiyah* of that person should be released from its bonds. The *fiqaq*... *fiqaq* means to open. There are three things by which the bonds of our *nafs* are broken. The first *fiqaq*, the second *fiqaq*, the third *fiqaq*. These are three *fiqaqat*. The first *fiqaq*, whose amount is fixed at 250, and adding its [unclear], 261. 161. And its double is the next one, and its double is the third one, meaning the total comes to 1127. How has this amount been determined? It is based on very extensive calculations that you will not understand. For now, you cannot understand, anyway, it is based on these calculations. Now, what happens with this? That you gave that amount, and you were freed from its bonds. Now you will say, "Why were the bonds put on the *nafs* in the first place, that it has to be freed?" "Why the bonds?" So, I ask the world of Islam, please pay attention. Any person should answer me with a cool mind, that the entire world of Islam, which today has so many, crores, countless Muslims, are all their children born as pure and Muslim? Do they not need to have the *darb* (ritual strike) applied? And do they not have to be made Muslim? Why do they make them Muslim? If *qudrah* had already created them as Muslims, and this necessity of surgery did not arise here, then how good it would have been. Why was this kept? When it is known that *qudrah* keeps it and wants us to cut here, we should do the surgery, and that is called "making a Muslim." Look, "making a Muslim." So, it was known that this happens, *qudrah* puts some bonds, and we have to make them Muslim. In exactly the same way, some bonds come upon our *nafs*. There is a bond on *namiyah*, there is a bond on *hissiyah*, there is a bond on *natiqah*. To be freed from that bond, it is `min ma tuhibbun` (from that which you love), that wealth which you love very much, spend it. And this money is used for such a thing that in its reward, what does *qudrah* do? It frees that *nafs* from those bonds. You will say, "By doing what, what happens?" But what to do? Until you spend, you will not attain that thing. Just as you do *tazkiyah* (purification) with *zakat* (alms), you purify your wealth, in the same way, these are *fiqaqat*, and by paying them, these things are released. So, you gave *sadaqah* (charity), you did *qurbani* (sacrifice), you did the feeding for *ziyarah*, you recited the Holy Qur'an, you read Yasin for him, you prayed for his forgiveness, and along with doing all this, you paid the *fiqaqat*, then the *nafs al-namiyah* will also be released, and the restrictions that are upon it, it will get release from those chains. And what kind of chains are they? They are all spiritual things, what will you understand? Although it is physical, it is a spiritual bond. And freed from those bonds, it will be released. And you will say, "Well, after three days it has to be released anyway, so what is the need to give? What is the need to do?" But you see, with what trouble that released prisoner comes out. After three days, he is released for sure, but with how many troubles he is released. To give him relief, if you do this little bit, what will you lose? Today, you are sacrificing your life for him, weeping and wailing, so you should do this so that he is released. When he is released, then as I have told you, the *namiyah* after being released goes into the moon, and the moon, this, from crescent to full moon, and from full moon to crescent, it happens for this very reason. It is the *rihiyya* of the believers, the *namiyah*, which are shining, and this is becoming the moon and shining, the *rihiyya*. These are the *rihiyya* of the believers which are shining. And these, through Mercury and Venus, go to the sun and are washed, and then they come to use in forming the body of the Imam, as I have explained to you in detail. So, when you have seen that this is the matter with *namiyah*, and with *hissiyah*, it is that it went with the *natiqah*. So, when *hissiyah* went with *natiqah*, we call that a *surah* (form). And when a *surah* met with a *surah*, and *surah* after *surah* started to connect, the circle, in a small circle, a small circle in a smaller circle, it started to join, and happening, happening, the *du'at* (callers), and after the *du'at*, the *hujjat* (proof), after the *hujjat*, the *bab* (gate), and after the *bab*, they reached the rank of *bab al-abwab*. And there, all the forms took one human form. Look, everything will be in human form. A human's thought is also a human. Look, today Hindus and others, whatever gods or idols they make, they will either make them in the form of a human, they cannot make them otherwise. They will make them a bit crooked, but they will make them in the form of a human. Or if not, they will make them in the form of an animal. So, just in the same way, *qudrah* has kept it that the best stature is that of a human. That *haykal* (form/temple) which will be formed of those forms will also be in human form. Meaning, a place for the head, a place for the ear, a place for the nose, a place for the hand. Just as, whatever one's rank is, that form will be adjusted there, and it will be a *haykal* in the form of a human. And the place for this *haykal* to reside is, as I have told you, the Ka'bah. And who is the one who keeps it there? It is the Imam of the time. By the command of the Imam, that *haykal* moves, and that *haykal* always resides where? In the Holy Ka'bah. And in that *haykal*, how many forms are there? At least there are 100,000. That is why the reward for one *rak'ah* (unit of prayer) is 100,000. It is equal to 100,000 *rak'ahs* to offer one *rak'ah* of prayer in the Haram, in the Baytullah (House of God). So, when you have learned that all this is there, then you pay attention that our *namiyah* that has emerged from the grave, that *namiyah* which emerged from the grave after three days, and after all the bonds were released, and after being washed and cleaned in all those things, after being cleansed of all filth and dirt, after the impurities and dross were removed, it came into this world, and after coming into the world, and coming upon some fruit, and the Imam eating it as food, and it being capable of becoming his son, what does it mean to become a son? The body. Only the body. And the *nafs* of that boy is what? It is the *athar* (effect/trace). The point that is to come in the *Tamur*, that is its *athar*. So, the origin is in the *Tamur*, which I call, there the name is Ahmad, and here it is Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him. So, you have to understand this, that this kind of... The Prophet said one thing and clarified the whole matter. So, when this kind of matter has been understood by you, then it was known that this is the state, and there are *hijab* and *muhtajib*, and this is the situation. So now, when you have understood this, that the *athar* of the *Tamur* happens, so this *nafs-e-hissiyah* of ours that emerges, that *hissiyah* also, when it ascends in the form of a *surah*, it also has some bonds, it has some restrictions. To free it from those restrictions and bonds, you also have to pay *fiqaq*. And along with paying *fiqaq*, you have to do your deeds. But the reality is that the matter is not so straightforward, that the road is also right, your motor is also right, its parts are also right, the petrol is also full. All things have to be accounted for and arranged. In the same way, the journey of the hereafter is also not a solitary matter. All things have to be considered. The character should also be correct, the worships should also be there. Although you have not performed worship all night long, but you have performed the five daily prayers, you have shown respect, you have also fasted, you have also given *zakat* (alms). So, all these things should be there to some extent, so that your journey can pass with moderation, with a middle path. And if, suppose, this does not happen, then valleys will come, and you will face difficulties. There are difficulties for the soul, and there are difficulties for the body, that we think our leaving the grave is easy. Oh, it is very difficult. I am saying it for the sake of speaking, that he is a *mu'min*, so his *namiyah* also leaves. But who knows, if suppose there is a *mu'min*, and there is another *mu'min*—one *mu'min* is there who offered prayers, gave *zakat*, did this, did that, did Hajj, performed worships, had good character, did all things. And another *mu'min* is there, who engaged in major sins. Who committed sins against God, who, the greatest sin is *shirk billah* (associating partners with God). I have continuously explained to you about *shirk*, how *shirk* happens. If, God forbid, we have committed *shirk*, God forbid, and after that, lying is the greatest sin. The situation is such that lying has become such a habit for us that it is like honeyed milk. And it is the greatest sin. Here you told a lie, there your *surah* (form) started to become dark. And an effect started to fall on it. This is a matter of giving with one hand and taking with the other. This is not a matter of delayed payment. And after that, the greatest sin is wine, and after that is adultery, after that is murder. These are the five great sins that I have mentioned before you. If any person has committed these sins, then one *mu'min* who is walking straight, and another *mu'min* who has committed all these things, there will be a big difference between the two. There will be a big difference between the two, and what kind of difference will it be? The difference will be that this *mu'min* who has engaged in major sins, who has committed such great sins of God, which are called *kaba'ir*, about which the Prophet said, "Even if you perform Hajj, all things will be forgiven, `illa al-kaba'ir` (except the major sins)." Except for the major sins. Yes, if he repents for the major sins, performs `tawbah al-nasuh` (sincere repentance), asks for forgiveness, then the Lord of the worlds is the one who forgives. But if he does not want to, and if this is the matter, then obviously he has fallen into trouble. He has fallen into trouble, so what has happened? The *namiyah* is far from being released, some of the *hissiyah* also remains. You understand? The matter of the *namiyah* being released is a distant thing, if some part of the *hissiyah* also remains... some part, not all. Some part of a *mu'min*, if it remains, then what a severe torment it is, just tell me. It is the same matter as if you are burying a living person. What a torment it is, what a calamity it is. God forbid, God forbid, through the grace of our Auliya Allah (Friends of God), may our state not be like this. But I am telling you that even believers are subject to this trial. Now, apart from them, the people who are there, what will be the state of their death, and what state of their death will you see? That their death does not even happen. They think the departure of the *nafs-e-hawaiyah* (aerial self) is death. Oh, where did the death happen? The departure did not even happen. Departure is what is called when *namiyah* has also left, *hissiyah* has also left, *natiqah* has also left. There is no *natiqah* at all. The pilot is not there to pull the *nafs*. *Hissiyah* remains with them as *hissiyah*, *namiyah* with them as *namiyah*. I will explain in detail in tomorrow's lesson, but today I only have to explain about the *mu'min*. And some other things of the *mu'min* are still remaining. I have to tell you that if the *namiyah*, *hissiyah*, and *natiqah* of a *mu'min* progress, then minus *namiyah*, minus *hissiyah*, minus *natiqah*, now the thing that remains, what is that thing? Six parts remain. I said tough bones, soft bones, tough sinews, soft sinews, muscles, and hair, nails. These six parts are called the six *fuzlat* (superfluities) which are buried in the grave of a *mu'min*. Now, the one who is being buried is being buried with the six *fuzlat*. If the *namiyah* has left, then that *mu'min* is what? Minus *namiyah*, minus *natiqah*, minus *hissiyah*. Now he has gone in total, and now he is buried with only the *fuzlat*. Now what is the state of these *fuzlat*? That now they have entered the *dawlat-i 'alam* (state of the world). What is *dawlat*? It is a mill, which in our terminology is called *mizaj-i mu'tadij* (tempered disposition). Remember, the name of this mill that works in nature is *mizaj-i mu'tadij*. This, the clouds and rain and the rain that comes, and the vegetation that grows, the process of all these things is called *mizaj-i mu'tadij*. So, *mizaj-i mu'tadij* is a very big procedure, to explain which a lot of time is needed. And that, anyway, understand that the formation of stratified clouds, and the falling of rain, and from it the growth of vegetation, and that vegetation becoming food for some animal, and those foods, being slaughtered under a knife by some halal animal, that slaughtered meat coming into our food, and eating that food, and from that food, the formation of the *nutfah*, and it being the cause of the settlement for some child, and that child emerging from it in the form of a human. So, now this happens in this way, and through a very long procedure... God forbid, God forbid, it is not like what the Hindus have, that life after life, or *awghaman* (transmigration). That, God forbid, is not there, which they call rebirth or reincarnation. Curses upon our *du'at* for such a thought. It is not like that. And if this coming again was not to happen, then God would not have said this in the Holy Qur'an: `minha khalaqnakum wa fiha nu'idukum wa minha nukhrijukum taratan ukhra` (From it [the earth] We created you, and into it We will return you, and from it We will extract you another time.). "Oh, from this grave, We had taken you out. Into this grave, We are putting you. From this grave, We will have to take you out." `inna alladhi farada 'alayka al-Qur'ana la-raddika ila ma'ad` (Indeed, He who has ordained the Qur'an for you will [surely] bring you back to a place of return.). Allah has made the Qur'an obligatory upon you so that you may be returned to your place of return. All these things, most of the verses are indicating that your *'awdat* (return) happens, our return happens, our coming back happens. `wal-akhiratu khayrun laka min al-ula` (And the Hereafter is better for you than the first [life].). "Oh, your hereafter is better than your first." Meaning, your first life and the life that is to come, there will be a big difference between this life. In this life, if you have acted with understanding, with comprehension, then you have prepared for the coming life. The hereafter is the coming life. This life is the first life. So, these are all indications in the Holy Qur'an which are telling that we will have a return. And we, this is what Mawlana Rumi has also said, that we have to come into this universe countless times. Now look, what is the reality? The one who came, never came. You understand my point? The one who came, never came. And the one who went, went forever. Now I am proving this to you. For example, suppose there is an 'Amr. 'Amr's *nafs al-natiqah*, his *nafs al-hissiyah*, his *nafs al-namiyah*, and he passed away. After passing away, *nafs al-hissiyah* joined with *nafs al-natiqah*, reached the *hujjat*, and it became part of the *haykal*. Now tell me, who is the one being released? It is only the *nafs al-natiqah*. It is the one who was joined with the *hissiyah*. When it was released, it is the same one who was saying "I, I." The one who was calling himself "I" all his life, that was only the *natiqah*. Which was released, and after being released, now what remains? *Namiyah* remains. So, *namiyah*, along with its body, is going to remain in this universe. And until it does not create it in the form of a *natiqah*, it will not be released. Now you will say, how will it create it? In exactly the same way that the *natiqah* was created there from your own body. Just as one *shabih*, by regretting there, created your *natiqah* for you, in the same way, you here, your *namiyah*, you will make it into *hissiyah*. You will make *hissiyah* into *natiqah*. And how will you make it? You will make it through these same worships. You will make it through these same spiritual exercises. You will make it through this same love for Amir al-Mu'minin. You will make it through this same monotheism of the Lord of the worlds. These same beliefs, these same ethics, these same worships, these same dealings. From these, you will progress. From these, you will... If you think that you can achieve spiritual progress from physical progress through some other procedure, you cannot. The procedure for achieving spiritual progress from physical progress is only this. That you will have to walk in this way, then this is the straight path, and you will have to pass through this straight path. From this path. So now what is it? That that *natiqah* which... that when it was released from you, now it is part of the *haykal*. And your *namiyah* which was released... please pay attention. Your *natiqah* which was released, that is part of the *haykal*. And the *haykal* has been formed where? At the place of the *bab al-abwab*. And at the place of the *bab al-abwab*, it has been formed in the shape of a human. Suppose that you, one number, two number, three number, four number, let's say I give numbers. Number one there takes the place of the eye. Number two takes the place of the ear, some take the place of the nose, some take the place of the head, some take the place of the hand. Suppose. Whoever took whatever according to their own account, they took it. That *haykal* has been formed. So, the place that you take in the *haykal*, then in the state of *namiyah*, your *namiyah* that has emerged in the form of *rihiyya*, and after being washed has come, and has become the body of the Imam, then in the body of the Imam too, it will take the same place which it had taken in the *haykal*. I hope you understood. The place that you took in the *haykal*, if you took the place of the eye, then in the *nasut* (human realm), meaning in the body of the Imam too, you will come in the place of the eye. And you are what? The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, has given the command for *wudu'* (ablution) to perform the prayer. Common Muslims will say, "How good it is, we stay in dust and dirt, and how good it is that purity is achieved, we do *istinja* (ritual cleansing), purity is achieved, and becoming pure and clean, washing our hands and feet, all the parts that are external, after washing them clean, we go and stand in the court of God, how good it is." That's it, the matter is over. Oh, this was not the thing. The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, the Seal of the Prophets, he did not just tell about *wudu'* for this reason. Oh, he has encompassed millions of things, the Seal of the Prophets. Among those countless things, the most important thing was this, that when you sit down to do *wudu'*, here you said "Bismillah" (In the name of God), there the *haykal* started to move. And that in the noble *nasut* also, the movement started. Oh, there are many other things that have started to move. Many things have started to move. Here you said, `Allahumma... Muhammad al-Nabi ka`, here you rinsed your mouth and read the supplication. And you read the supplication which the Prophet and the progeny of the Prophet and the Ahl al-Bayt have told. If you read the Qur'an, that will have no effect either. You will have to read the same supplication that has been told to you. Here you read that supplication, there what will happen? That in the place of the mouth, whatever is in the *nasut*, that will come into motion. And in the place of the mouth, whatever is in the *lahut*, that will come into motion. And they will look towards you. So, what does it mean? That your *wudu'* will start to become complete. And your transformation will begin. So, the transformation that you have, it happens at every single moment. Its beginning is where? It is from *istinja*. It is from *istinja*. Now, there are great points, if I were to open them, it would become too much, but it is very difficult, it is possible that it will be heavy on your intellect. That is why I do not want to open those things. Otherwise, I would tell you why *qudrah* gave such organs, and why it made them lower things. Why was the practice of *istinja* kept? I would tell all these things. But the reality is, you understand, that these are all our illusions, this is our corrupt illusion, which we, with the Tenth, and the Ninth, had said, "No, no, we do not believe, and we will not believe anyone." The denial that we did, that denial has fallen to this extent here. And it has made us fall so much that today we are hiding our own flaws. We are covering our own faults. Why did this covering of flaws happen? It is because of "there." The covering of flaws came, and we started to cover our flaws. So, it became a matter of shame. So, it was known that it is all a matter of "there." And in the same way, when you do its purification, then this purification happens. And how does the purification happen? Until you say, `Ashhadu an la ilaha illallah, ashhadu anna Muhammadan rasulullah` (I bear witness that there is no god but God, I bear witness that Muhammad is the messenger of God), until then purity cannot happen. The purity of anything will not happen until you recite the *kalima tayyibah*. Now, you have recited the *kalima tayyibah*, and if you have started to recite the *kalima tayyibah* in a long and drawn-out way, as has been told, commonly among the Muslims as it has been told, then what will happen? That *kalima tayyibah* will also become deficient. The milk is a lot, oh, the pot is full, but with henna in it. What will you do? If a drop of urine falls, what will happen? So, it all became impure. So, in the same way, if you have recited the *kalima tayyibah*, and after that, you said, `al-khayru wa al-sharru min Allah ta'ala` (good and evil are from God, the Exalted). "Good and evil, whatever there is, is from God." God forbid, God forbid. Oh, He is pure good. He wants only good. He wants to take you from physicality to spirituality. He wants to clean you right there. You did not get cleaned there, and you came here, and on top of that, you are blaming God, that evil is also from God. Some gentlemen had come, it was the early days. And they told me... my zeal was a bit more, so I gave him a slap. So, those gentlemen were very displeased, that you are saying this, you are doing that. I said, "Brother, you are reciting the *kalima tayyibah*, `al-khayru wa al-sharru min Allah ta'ala`." That goodness is there, badness is there, whatever there is, is from God. Now, the slap that has reached you, it has reached you from God. What can I do? I am helpless. So, eat the slap. So, anyway, although it is a joke, but very many points emerge from it. If we were to explain this saying, `al-khayru wa al-sharru min Allah ta'ala`, the whole of Islam would be torn to shreds. The whole of Islam would be torn to shreds. No thing will remain. It will be shattered into pieces. Just give me the proof for that. Oh, He is pure good. He is the origin of all. He is the total intellect. From there, you take blessings. From Him, you ask for everything from the true giver. And you are saying that whatever evil is reaching is from Your side. Wow. You do the evil, and you curse Satan. You do the deed yourself, and you curse Satan. Can this be? It cannot be. So, Satan does mislead, but why do you get misled? Why do you get misled? So, the fault is actually ours. And this is the thing, remember, that God is as He is. He is *'adil-e-hakim* (Just and Wise). And with Him is justice. With Him is not injustice. So, it was known that the way that 'Ashir al-Mudasir had set for *lahut* and *nasut*, that is the same way for *lahut* and *nasut*, by which our progress will happen. And the death of a *mu'min* is not just the departure of the *nafs-e-hawaiyah* (aerial self), but it is the departure of the *namiyah*, and the departure of the *hissiyah* by joining with the *natiqah*. This is the reality of death. Now, the six parts that are left are buried. Now, after being buried, as I said, for these six *fuzlat* to be cleansed, 300 years are needed. 300 years are for the cleansing of the grave. And I have told you that the things that emerge from his body, when the cleansing of the grave is done in 300 years, this is a wash house. The grave is what? It is a procedure. This is done. Now, the second procedure starts, of the spheres and the constellations. When they go into the constellations, then the 12 constellations I told you about, in each constellation for 60 years, and according to 60 years, if you calculate for 12 constellations, 720 years, take out 20 years from that, 700 years. 700 and these 300 years, 1000 years. The duration is 1000 years, after that your return happens, and that *mu'min* comes into the world. That *mu'min* is born again at someone's house. At whose house he has to be born, these are all things that who will be the siblings, what is there, what is fate, what is plan, what is predestination, what is free will, all these things are to come. But I am just telling you that his return happens, and he comes into the world. When he comes into the world, then obviously now the one who is coming, who is he? Although you may call him by his name, you may call him Zayd, you may call him whatever, but in reality, who is that Zayd? It is the *hissiyah*... no, but the *namiyah*. The *hissiyah* has gone. The *namiyah* has now come as *hissiyah*. You are calling that *hissiyah* Zayd and so on, because that is the soul. Because now it has been replaced. Now it has moved forward, that the *namiyah* took the place of the *hissiyah*, the heart took the place of the liver, the brain took the place of the heart, the liver took the place of the brain. Now, happening, happening, happening, what will happen? That one part of it will be reduced. And which part will be reduced? The foot. The part of the foot that was reduced, the part of the sole that was reduced, that part which is lying in the universe, that treasure that is lying upon it, meaning the human who is whole, he is not one whole *shabih*. He is one part. Within that one part, the account that has been kept for collecting, the part of yours that has been kept in the spheres, from there you will be taken out and joined. In this way, becoming better and better, you, coming again and again, passing through this world again and again, what will happen? You will have to progress within one *dawr-e-a'zam*. One *dawr-e-a'zam*, I have explained to you in detail. Now, how many returns one has to make, there is no need to tell this, anyway, their returns are also fixed, that a *mu'min* has to make how many returns. But it is not necessary that after 1000 years he must come. No. It can be that two or three thousand years pass in between, and God holds you back, then brings you. This is in the hands of *qudrah*, and it will be according to your accounts, that when you have to be brought, you will be brought, when you do not have to be brought, you will not be brought. And in this way, coming, coming, what will happen? One day you will be completely released. So, how will you be completely released? That at the time when you will start to end... in exactly the same way that a lamp is burning, a flame is burning, a wick is burning, a lamp is burning, so now look at it, that the lamp that is burning, your attention will always be on the flame, on that lamp, you will not look at the oil that is being consumed to light it. So, that lamp, you are looking at it, that for how long it has been burning, but you are not looking at the oil, that how many tons and tons of oil is being put into it. So, in exactly the same way, you are a *shabih*, a form, a human, as a human you are manifest, and from beneath you, how much is coming and how much is going, you do not know. But what happens is that burning, burning, burning, when you will be about to be extinguished, when you will be completely cleaned from here, then what will happen at that time? That the part that is reduced, that part will be joined with what? With the highest-ranking part of the *Saq-i-Mutahhid* (United Trunk). The highest-ranking part of the *Saq-i-Mutahhid*, which has become deserving of faith, will be joined with you. And when it is joined, then some flexibility will be created in your nature, some shock, a jolt will be created. Now you will say, why was I needlessly joined with this, that this shock was created? Why did this happen? So, this is the arrangement of *qudrah*. If a shock was created, then there are your accounts with it too. There is a give and take, because of which it was joined. It will not be joined just like that. With whom the joining is made, the joining is made with understanding. The joining, whoever's it may be, will be made with understanding. And that joining will start to form from it. And in this way, gradually, a *mu'min* will keep progressing, and he will, the *nafs-e-hissiyah* will progress with the *natiqah*, then *namiyah* will progress by becoming *hissiyah*, then the lower parts will keep increasing. Happening, happening, happening, all the *natiqahs*, all the ones that have been released, are all included in the *haykal* of the Imams. All these mirrors have been joined to become a big mirror, and that mirror has become a *shakhsiyyat* (personality), which is equal to *'aql* (intellect), and you have become capable of progressing from here. And that progress cannot happen... `fa bi-ayyi ala'i rabbikuma tukadhdhiban` (Then which of the favors of your Lord will you deny?) `la tanfudhuna illa bi-sultan` (you will not pass except by authority.). You cannot get out of this *dawlat-i 'alam* (state of the world) without the authority of a *sultan*. And who is that *sultan*? It is the *Sahib-i-Mawr* (Master of the Cycle). When the *Sahib-i-Mawr* comes, he will take all these things and ascend, and now countless things have gone, countless people have gone in one *dawr-e-a'zam*. Because one *dawr-e-a'zam* has passed in the world. One *dawr-e-a'zam* has passed. We, in the 399th *dawr* of the second *mawr*, in the first *dawr* of the 400th *dawr*, in the *dawr-e-sitr* (cycle of concealment), we are sitting here. This much of the world's duration has passed. Now, how much will pass, for this, nothing can be said, because it is our choice, that we become clean quickly, it is our choice that we take a long time to become clean. But this is certain, that every single particle of the world has to become clean.

I have explained to you the state of a believer's death. I believe you must have understood that how a believer's death occurs. And I had told you that we have three souls, three types of *nafs*: *nāmiyah* (vegetative), *ḥissīyah* (sensory), and *nāṭiqah* (rational). A human does not have one soul. Just as the idea is prevalent throughout the world that a human has one soul and when that soul departs, that's it. It is not so. A human has three souls. And *nāmiyah* is separate, *ḥissīyah* is separate, and *nāṭiqah* is separate. The virtues of the *nāmiyah*, its powers, its functions, its matters—they are completely separate. *Mawlā-i-kā'ināt Amīr al-Mu'minīn* mentioned in his sermon where he discussed the *nāmiyah* in detail, and he also spoke about the *ḥissīyah*. In the same way, he spoke about the *nāṭiqah*. If you... if you read your master's sermons, you will certainly find all these things in his sermons, in his sayings, in his pronouncements. You will find all these things are present. But we need to... that book, *Nahj al-Balaghah*, which is second only to the Book of God in rank for us, to understand it is a great thing. It should be part of our study. There are two things which I always say, and *Sayyid al-Mālik* stated this with great severity. And that is, the books that should be by our bedside are two. One is the *Qur'an al-Majeed*, which we should be reciting day and night. It should be read. And the second thing which we must always read with discipline is *Da'ā'im al-Islām*. *Da'ā'im al-Islām*. What is it? The seven pillars (*da'ā'im*): *walāyat*, *ṭahārat*, *namāz*, *rūza*, *ḥajj*, *zakāt*, and *jihād*. This book on the seven pillars that we have was written by the order of the Imam. And it was written... *Qāḍī al-Nu'mān* wrote this book, and its authenticity (*sanad*) was given by *Mawlānā Mu'izz, ṣalawātu-llāhi 'alayh*. And this is an authentic (*mustanad*) book that we have. And this authentic book, the *du'āt* give it such importance that every single page, every single line needs to be read and absolutely memorized. So we should always... now, praise be to God, its translation into Gujarati and its translation into Urdu have all been done. The translations are available, and you can buy the translation, read the translation, and you can also read the Arabic. So we need to... we should read *Nahj al-Balaghah*. This is because it is the word of *Mawlā Amīr al-Mu'minīn*, who had said, "*naz-zilūnī min ar-rubūbīyah wa qūlū lī kull shay'*" (Bring me down from divinity, and then say whatever you wish about me). "Lower me from divinity, O people, do not make me God (*Rabb*). Lower me from divinity, and then say whatever comes to your heart about me." Meaning, you can praise as much as you can, you can say as much as you can. The Prophet, *'alayhi-ṣalātu wa-s-salām*, said the same thing for Amīr al-Mu'minīn, that in praising Janāb-i-Alī, you can say whatever you wish. If someone says something you think is a lie, don't deny it. Did you see? If there is something in praise of *Mawlā* that you consider a lie, do not deny it; you might just not be able to understand it. So tell me, in the realm of possibility (*imkān*), if a picture of the Creator could be drawn, it would be *Mawlā-i-kā'ināt*. Just as Allah Ta'ala is the manifestation of oneness (*waḥdānīyat*) in His place, in the same way, in the realm of possibility, the manifestation of oneness is *Mawlā-i-kā'ināt Amīr al-Mu'minīn*. And you people are understanding all these realities. You are seeing, and you have understood *tāmūr* well, which is called *Bayt al-Ma'mūr*, and how *tāmūr* was formed, how the *nisbat-i-a'lā* and *nisbat-i-adwan* were formed. You know all these things, so you should understand all these things. So anyway, this is a moment for reflection, that you must adhere to the *sharī'at* (religious law) of the *da'ā'im*. Because before learning the *ḥaqā'iq* (realities), adherence to *sharī'at* is absolutely necessary. And *ḥaqā'iq* are not given without explaining the *sharī'at* and without explaining *ta'wīl* (esoteric interpretation). This is... understand that here, the situation in the *Jazīrah* of Hindustan, the functionaries (*manāṣib*) who have passed through here, from their experience, they saw it in such a way that they agreed to give it. Otherwise, believe me, *Sayyid al-Mālik* does not approve of it. That the *ḥaqā'iq* be given? No. There is no need to give them now. First, teach them *sharī'at*, teach them *ta'wīl*. After that, we will see, at that time we will give them a verdict. Now you imagine that all the students (*talamidhah*) there... I recently went there to Najran, and I saw that education takes place in closed rooms, and there are approximately 2,000 students. 2,000 students benefit, and the vast majority are kept at the level of *sharī'at* and *ta'wīl*. The *ḥaqā'iq* are told to very few people, and that too in closed rooms they are told, and only special people are taught. It is not taught to other people. So why this restriction? It is due to its importance. Due to its importance. So we should understand its importance. And when, alhamdulillah, all things are becoming clear to you, and everything is being explained, then you should have the same desire to know the *sharī'at*. Understand the *sharī'at* as well, because "*bazr al-ḥayāt al-abadīyah*" (the seed of eternal life)... this is the seed of eternal life. If we are not aware of the *sharī'at*, we are nothing. *Amīr al-Mu'minīn* once said that if a believer comes to me who is unaware of the *sharī'at*, I will crush his nose. Please pay attention. *Mawlā-i-kā'ināt* is saying this, so he is saying it for a reason. He became so displeased that he said, "I will just crush him." So it is clear that studying *sharī'at* and studying law is very necessary. This is the philosophy of law that you are learning, how the law was codified, how it was made. So anyway, I have... in my series of talks, what I had explained was about the death of a believer. I had explained about the three *nafs*—what their centers are, where they came from, where they were placed, and when we received them here, and after receiving them, what their repositories (*makhzan*) became. The brain is a repository, the liver is a repository, the heart is a repository. These are their repositories. And when death occurs, how the *nāmiyah* separates, how the *ḥissīyah* exits, how the *nāṭiqah* becomes separate. I have explained the detailed death of a believer to you. And I said that the *nafs al-ḥissīyah*, along with its form, that which is the pilot, which is a thing from "there," which was its concept, which was its system of administration (*niẓāmat*) there, which was its administrative plan (*tadbir-i-niẓāmat*), and for which it cried when it fell, and left its antecedents (*sawābiqah*), upon those antecedents it has to work here. And the form it creates through knowledge and action, all those things that happen, what are they? They are called its *sūrat* (form). And this *sūrat*, joining with the *ḥissīyah*, becomes three-in-one. *Ḥissīyah* plus deeds (*a'māl*) plus that concept that came from there. So all these three things, after combining, become one form and reach *Bāb al-Abwāb* (the Gate of Gates), passing through stages. It is called a *haykal* (spiritual body). And at whichever station that *haykal* is, its *nāmiyah* also comes to that same station in the body. This is a spiritual state, and that is a physical state. What is the spiritual state? A *haykal* is formed in the shape of a human, and where does that *haykal* reside? In the *Khāna-i-Ka'ba-i-Muqaddas* (the sacred house of Ka'ba), and it is by the Imam's order. And an Imam, when he appoints (*nass*) his son, what does he do? He entrusts the *haykal*, which is the essence of that *da'wat*, of the spirits (*arwāh*) of all believers. Meaning spirits (*rūḥ*) here means what? Those forms (*sūrat*). The essence of those forms is handed over to him. This is called doing *nass*. *Nass*. And this *nass* is called Imamate. Until he receives Imamate, he is not an Imam. And in this way, he became Imam upon receiving *nass*. And which child was it? That child is the one who is the same believers who passed away, and after three days from the grave, their *nafs al-nāmiyah* came out. Or if they were very good believers, their *nāmiyah* came out earlier. And after coming out, what happened? It went to the moon, and mixed in Mercury and Venus, and after being in the sun, it came back to the moon via Venus and Mercury. And the moon threw this, and the fruits absorbed it, and that fruit came into the food, and those foods became sperm (*nuṭfah*), and they were used in the formation of the child. And these foods, slowly mixing, the child's formation began, and it became the body of the Imam, *'alayhi-ṣalātu wa-s-salām*. Just as we have power over our clothes, they have the same power over their bodies. They have the same power over their bodies, that they can bend it, make it disappear, or show it whenever they want. And similarly, you see that one time the Prophet, *'alayhi-ṣalātu wa-s-salām*, was present. It was the occasion of Eid, either Eid al-Adha or Eid al-Fitr. And all the people were coming, and all the tribes, after coming, were offering congratulations for Eid in the court of the Prophet. So the Prophet, *'alayhi-ṣalātu wa-s-salām*... you will say, did they not pray the Eid prayer with the Prophet? So many people, the whole of Arabia, how could they pray? Each person prayed in their own place and came. Well, when they came and said, "O Messenger of Allah, we have come to offer you congratulations for Eid." So the Prophet said, "O people, you have come to me to offer congratulations for Eid. Tell me, with whom did you pray the Eid prayer? Who led your prayer (*imāmat*)?" So there, there were tribes... you tell me, it was the assembly of the Master of Both Worlds, the court. So many tribes were seated. He asked one tribe, and its leader replied, "O Messenger of Allah, we... the prayer... it was *Amīr al-Mu'minīn*, Hazrat Ali, who led us in prayer." They prayed under his leadership. He asked the second, he also said the same. He asked the third, he also said the same. Whoever he asked, they all took Ali's name. And Hazrat Ali was sitting next to the Prophet with his head bowed, he was sitting there. And the Prophet, *'alayhi-ṣalātu wa-s-salām*, kept asking and smiling. And after asking everyone, he turned towards Hazrat Ali, and after turning, he placed his hand on the head of Janab-i-Ali and said, "If there is a *Ḥablullāh al-Matīn* (the strong rope of Allah), that rope which *Wa 'taṣimū bi-ḥabli-llāhi jamī'ā* (And hold firmly to the rope of Allah all together) commands you all to hold, that is Ali and his progeny." So, the main point was to show this, that look, if he wishes to show manifestations, he can show thousands. That is why he became *Maẓhar al-'Ajā'ib wa-l-Gharā'ib* (the Manifestation of Wonders and Marvels). There is no personality in history who can compare to Ali, to be called *Maẓhar al-'Ajā'ib wa-l-Gharā'ib*. His state was such that when he walked, they would call him *Maẓhar al-'Ajā'ib wa-l-Gharā'ib*. That the one who manifests wonders is going. "Look, the one who manifests wonders is going." So his state was such that people had forgotten his name and called him by the name *Maẓhar al-'Ajā'ib*. Why? Because his state was such that when he walked on the path, pebbles would bow and greet him, voices of salutations would come from there, an animal would come and greet him, a tree would prostrate, it would go into bowing (*rukū'*), it would bow and greet. So seeing these states... and the miracles of Janab-i-Ali were such that there was a miracle at every step, so what must the state have been? They were seeing all this, but the world (*dunyā*) is very bad. The world is very bad. Just as even today, we understand many things very well, but our hearts are not inclined. We do not become that good. Similarly, the people there, because they were from the *shāk-i-muṭahhir* and *nasl-i-mustakbir*, what happened? They could not be inclined. They could not bring Islam. They could not believe in Ali as he should have been believed in. That is why *Amīr al-Mu'minīn* said, "If I give all the wealth of the world to my enemy, he will not be ready to believe in me. And if it is my lover (*muḥibb*), even if I crush him, even if I kill him, he will not leave my feet." So the real matter was that in the pre-eternal world (*'ālam al-azal*), those who loved, loved; those who hated, hated. That is why the Prophet said, "*al-arwāḥu junūdun mujannadah, fa-mā ta'ārafa minhā-'talaf wa mā tanākara minhā-'khtalaf*" (Souls are like conscripted soldiers; those whom they recognize, they get along with, and those whom they do not, they disagree with). We were a troop. Because it has been explained to you that of the countless souls that were created, those who showed remorse (*nadāmat*) there, did so, and those who did not show remorse, did not. To show remorse is to accept the whole chain. To accept the *bay'at* is to accept the *Ahl al-Bayt*. This is the chain, and one must accept the chain. Today I want to say that you have seen the salvation of a believer, how his salvation occurs. And I had told you that the final reward of his salvation is his body, which consists of six humors (*fuzlāt*), which is buried in the grave. And after being buried in the grave, what happens? These noble humors... as Chakbast said, "What is death? The dispersal of the elements." But the point was, is this dispersal a problem? It is a matter of concern. It's not like that. The dispersal of elements is not just like that. It is that "*in kullu nafsin lammā 'alayhā ḥāfiẓ*" (Verily, over every soul there is a watcher). An angel is present to protect every single part. So the Lord of the Worlds, who can send an angel for every drop of rain, will He not protect this? He will protect everything. So those noble humors, what happens to them? I said 300 years is the duration in the grave, and 60 years are in the worms, then 700 years here and 300 years there, in 1000 years, its return (*'awdat*) happens, and it comes back and returns. But it is not necessary that it comes back in every thousand years, because it is a long duration. The period that is set is for a span of a human generation, in which there is purification. Just as the general Muslims (*'āmmat al-muslimīn*) believe, the moment one dies, there are only two paths: either paradise (*jannat*) or hell (*dūzakh*). And see their resurrection (*qiyāmat*). What kind of scene of resurrection do they paint? Do you know? The scene of resurrection they paint is that the sacrifices we make in Eid al-Adha... for this sacrifice, a fat goat should be brought, a rather good one should be brought, spend a little extra, but because the reward is great. What is the reward? The reward is that it will be ridden. So it is clear that if you bring a skinny one, it will be a problem. It should be rather good and fat and healthy, so that we can ride it. Where? On the *pul-i-ṣirāṭ* (the bridge over hell). That path which is sharper than a sword and thinner than a hair, on that *pul-i-ṣirāṭ*, the ride is happening on what? On that goat which they are sacrificing. And they are mounted on it. And if they slip a little, it's hell, and if they reach straight, it's paradise. It seems as if life has become a balancing act. This is just buffoonery. These are all absurdities. These are things that are incomprehensible. These are nonsensical things. They are not things that can enter anyone's intellect. Who will understand? Who will explain? Who will make these fools understand what is what? They think there is a scale in the east and west where all things will be weighed. Brother, those are weighed in the scale of intellect (*mīzān-i-'aql*). It's not some such thing that a grocer is sitting with a scale and weighing. So all these things, all these points, are to be understood, to be comprehended. It's not that they are such things. They... here, the Muslims say that the trumpet of Israfil is in such a state that it is a big horn that has stretched from east to west, and who knows how many angels are lifting it or not, but Israfil is blowing it. Israfil, who is an angel, who is among the great angels, the chief of angels, he is blowing. And what happens when he blows? In it, there are as many holes as there are people. When air comes out of a hole, that trumpet sounds, and from here, people start rising from their graves, shaking off their shrouds. This is some... is this some game, some spectacle? Rising from graves, and that's why they place twigs and make a chamber for them... These are all nonsensical things. None of this is true. If there were no knowledge, no core (*lubb*), no rationales (*ma'qūlāt*), and no knowledge of the Quran, all this would become absurd. There is no such thing. It's not that a person dies when a leaf falls from the Sidrat tree, nor does a person become alive when air comes out of the holes of a horn. None of it is true, it is not so. But all of them are things to be understood from a knowledgeable perspective. Because there are countless things to understand. That's why, in terms of moving away from my main topic, I am leaving them and moving forward. I was saying how your humors progress, and how, along with their return, you come back to the world and you progress. But when a believer progresses, then regarding the progress of a believer, I had said that there is a difference between the progress of a believer and a sinful believer (*momin-i-muqassir*). Who is a *momin-i-muqassir*? One who is a sinful believer. You will say, who is not a sinner? All are... you can easily understand the difference between a sinful believer and a non-sinful believer. One who commits major sins (*kabā'ir*) will be considered a sinful believer. I have listed the major sins for you. The believer who commits major sins is the one who will fall into trouble, and he will not be saved easily. And the first punishment he will get is that he will have to endure three days of confinement in the grave for his *nāmiyah* to be released. For three days he is imprisoned, and the *nāmiyah* cannot be released easily. He has to endure the torment of the grave for three days, but not more than three days. And the believer who is pure and clean, he passes away and his *nāmiyah* is released. The *ḥissīyah* also goes, and the *nāṭiqah* also goes. The pilot has taken all the things. Now, what is the need? See, if there is a train, and the horsepower of the engine is considered. If the weight is high, but the horsepower is more, the engine will pull it. So, either our knowledge should be so vast, so comprehensive, so dominant, so strong, that it can pull all the garbage-filled wagons. Meaning, if there have been some sins, if there are garbage in our body, and we are tainted by sins, then it should be pulled by the power of knowledge. That is why Allah Ta'ala said about the virtue of knowledge: "*yarfa'i-llāhu-lladhīna āmanū minkum wa-lladhīna ūtū-l-'ilma darajāt*" (Allah will raise those who have believed among you and those who were given knowledge, by degrees). The exaltation of ranks is based only on knowledge, not on deeds. So why are deeds put behind? For this very reason. Now you see, either make the engine powerful enough to pull the heavy wagons that are tainted with sin, or keep reducing the sins so that even a light engine, one with less power, can pull it. Both options are before you. That is why *Mawlā-i-kā'ināt* preferred this more: that not every person has the capacity to acquire knowledge, to be able to delve into knowledge, to master all sciences, and for his life to be sufficient, for him to find a true teacher (*mu'allim-i-ṣādiq*), and for books to be available. All these things are not possible. So at the very least, do this: by abstaining from sins, filter your body, purify it, so that when the puller pulls, it doesn't have to exert force. That is why he said, "*takhaffafū talḥaqū*" (Be light, and you will catch up). This is a single sentence of *Mawlā-i-kā'ināt*. He says, "*takhaffafū talḥaqū*." "Be light, and you will catch up." This does not mean to diet. It does not mean to make yourself thin. No, no. By reducing sins, you have to purify yourself so that you can catch up. So that is why *Mawlā-i-kā'ināt*... at the time when he fought the battle... of... your... the battle that was fought of the camel, that which... so, that very great battle that was fought, in the final sermon of that battle which he gave, in that sermon he said this, that "*takhaffafū talḥaqū*." "You become light, and you will catch up." This is called the Battle of the Camel (*Jang-i-Jamal*). So, anyway, I have explained to you that a believer is purified in this way. But now, besides a believer, now, in "besides," everyone else is included. See, the religion tells us that "*wa mā ba'da-l-ḥaqqi illā-ḍ-ḍalāl*" (And what is there after truth except error?). After truth, if there is anything, it is misguidance. Now you will say, isn't there some middle path? No. You fall from the peak of a mountain and get stuck in the valley. Now there is no stopping place on the way. Now you will say, no, tell us of some step where we can rest, where something can happen. Well, Inshallah, I will tell you. I am saying that after misguidance from the truth, after leaving the truth, there is nothing but misguidance. But despite that, the mercies of Allah Ta'ala, His bounties, His... His favors are very, very many, countless. What can be said of His mercy? Now see, the condition of the general Muslims, that condition is, of course, different from that of the infidels (*kāfir*). They recite the *kalimah* of monotheism (*tawḥīd*), they follow the Prophet of Islam. At the very least, they perform the outward prayers, fasting, etc. They worship Allah, they prostrate, they believe in the monotheism of the Lord of the Worlds, they recite the *kalimah Lā ilāha illā Allāh*. Although it does not enter their hearts, they do not recite it with its true meaning, but they do recite it. So it is clear that there is a difference between them and the infidels. But along with the difference, if they did not do the work that was meant to be done, then what will happen? All that they have done will become like scattered dust (*habā'an manthūrā*). The state of a pot of milk will be ruined by a single drop of urine. The very same will be the situation. And what is that? If someone is a *Nāṣibī*... if someone from the Muslims is a *Nāṣibī*, meaning one who has enmity with Ali and the followers of Ali, who is hostile, he is finished. His end has come. And calamity will befall him. Now, on this, you might quickly conclude that the Shī'ān-i-Alī will be saved. No. They will be in even more trouble. Now you will ask why? They love Ali and the followers of Ali very much. No, they do not love the followers of Ali completely. That is why they are in trouble. They neither understood Ali, nor the followers of Ali. This is that Shia. The chain that was to be followed, if they had followed that chain today, all these sciences would be with them. They did not follow it. And most of all, see, the proof of misguidance and error, what is it? To check if rice is cooked in a pot, you press a couple of grains.
