They will say that the one-minute 'ibadat is very good. "Brother, let's go. We have very little time. This is very good, this is a cheap mazhab. Accept this mazhab, it is very good. A one-minute 'ibadat." They sit down, perform the 'ibadat, and leave. What is it? They have to recite a tasbih (rosary), and after reciting the tasbih, they are free from their obligation. Or, while reciting the tasbih, what should they do? They should keep a picture of their Imam in front of them. The Imam's picture is placed in the jamatkhana, they sit there, and that is their jamatkhana, that is their masjid (mosque)—everything is right there. Just looking at the picture and reciting the tasbih is enough, and after reciting the tasbih, their duty is finished. And it is such a cheap mazhab that the tasbihs given by their muftis are very strange and peculiar. They give them very strange and peculiar tasbihs. Sometimes they give `Ya Hayyu Ya Qayyum`, sometimes `Ya Wadud`, sometimes something else, sometimes `La ilaha illallah`. Well, they do give some good words, but the issue is that first, they are Khojas, and then their tongues falter, and then they are in such a state of zalalat (misguidance) and gumrahi (straying), being a perfect embodiment of it, that they neither think nor understand. They say whatever comes to their mind, and the listeners understand it as they please, and so it goes on. Regarding this, there is a famous story of a "Gudgudiya" which has been narrated in detail by Mawlana, and it is also present in the roznamchas of our revered father. It was a strange story that a Khoja old woman was on her deathbed, and when she was close to dying, she wanted to say that the ta'wiz (amulet) given to her by her elder, the Imam—that is, the Imam of the Khojas—she had been reciting it her whole life. Now that her death was imminent, she wanted to present this ta'wiz to him and have it cut open. So, their Mukhi sahib (community leader) was present, and when he was present, it was opened. Inside, there was a considerable sum of money, and that money was presented to the Imam sahib. But when she was asked, that old woman, "What tasbih were you reciting?" she replied, "Ya doodh, ya roti" (O milk, O bread). That poor, frail old lady had no teeth, and her stomach was also not good, so what could she eat? She would soak some bread in milk and eat it. That's what she remembered: "Ya doodh, ya roti." They were perplexed as to what this "doodh ya roti" was. Later, it was found out that the person who told her, what he had given her was "Ya Wadudu, Ya Ra'ufu" (O Loving, O Kind). `Ya Wadudu, Ya Ra'ufu` became "Ya doodh ya roti." She started reciting `Ya Wadud, Ya Ra'uf, Ya Wadud, Ya Wadud` so quickly that it turned into "doodh aur roti," and the poor woman spent her life on "doodh aur roti." So, such are the conditions. In any case, what can be done? This is the state of the Khojas, the state of the Dawoodis, the state of the 'Aliyyas is something else entirely. Theirs is a qiyamah (calamity) in itself. The situation is that there is nothing to take from them, not even a speck of 'ibrat (lesson). They have no lata'if (subtleties) from which we could... They are kasa'if (densities). But the thing is, for us Mu'minin, it is a place of 'ibrat. When we go to their gatherings and get a chance for ziyarat (visit), I also had an opportunity and reached there... A sahib, and the 'Aliyyas who are called that, the group that split from the Dawoodis. And they started reciting Sadaqallah. When they started reading the Sadaqallah, after `Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim`, they started `Sadaqallah`. They went on and began to say: `Qul Huwallahu Ahad` (Say, "He is Allah, the One"). Then after that, they paused, and then said `Qul Huwallahu Ahad`. They paused, then said `Qul Huwallahu Ahad`. They said `Qul Allah` three times, so `Qul Allah` was said. They didn't even read the surah, and by saying `Qul Allah, Qul Allah` three times, they finished it. And where the word `hayhat lima tu'adun` comes, they spread their hand like this and said, "hay hath" (this is the hand), meaning "hayhat lima tu'adun". This, this is zalalat (misguidance), this is gumrahi (straying). What can be said? It's a cascade of falsehoods. This is one thing; there are many thousands of such things. It's not one or two things, but thousands of things. When their 'aql (intellect) is stoned, they start doing puja (worship) of stones. Such people, despite being human, despite having intellect, despite being sa'insdan (scientists), despite being very 'aqlmand (intelligent) and danishmand (wise), despite being aware of 'ulum 'aqliyyah (rational sciences), despite living in this world of water and clay, where rivers of 'ilm (knowledge) are flowing, and in today's atomic age, what do they do? You see. What are they doing these days? The situation is that they are being taught in their houses of worship to offer namaz (prayer) in our name as well. Our elders are commanding, "Don't forget to offer namaz in my name," so they offer namaz in their name. Brother, namaz is for God, lillah (for Allah). Besides Allah, who else's... "No, but they say to offer namaz." "And do this and that." They do it. So, we do not have such andhi taqlid (blind following), na'uzubillah, na'uzubillah (we seek refuge in God). Nor do our elders ever teach us such things. But you see how they misguide, how they lead astray, and a whole group is following them in this state of misguidance. And they keep accepting them and following. So, the situation here is that those who were close to the truth and got separated, their condition is this. So don't even ask about the condition of the 'alam-e-islam (Islamic world). Their condition is extremely dire. It is very much worse. That is why, as I said to you in this tasalsul-e-bayan (continuity of discourse), yesterday I explained to you that the 'azabat that occur—which are naqs, raqs, 'aqs, waqs, naqs, raqs—these are seven darakeh (levels), seven abwab (gates) of jahannam (hell), where they are taken. And they have to suffer 'azab. The first darakah is of the Habshis (Ethiopians), and after that, the four darakeh are for what? They are for siba', that is, for darindon (predators). After that are the hashrat al-arz (insects of the earth), and after that, what are they for? After them are the tuyur (birds). So, in this way... the fourth... the first darakah is of the Habshis, the second darakah is of the bear and the monkey, and after that is the siba', of the darindon. The fourth is... and after that, the darakah is of what? Yes, after them, finally, come the tuyur. And after the tuyur, there are the nabatat (plants), and after the nabatat, the seventh darjah (level) is of ma'daniyat (minerals). They have to traverse all these darajat, and they are given punishment, and these darakat are called 'azab-e-adna (the lesser punishment). This is called the punishment of the gates of jahannam. And they are given 'azab. And for each darjah, for the condition of each darakah, for its circumstances, we have 25, 25 ayats (verses) written. The Quran Majid is the very soul of haqa'iq (realities). It is not that some ayat does not present a dalil (proof) regarding this. The Quran Majid is the main thing. For everything, a dalil, a muhkam (firm) dalil exists. And it will not happen that we can deviate from the Quran Majid, na'uzubillah, na'uzubillah, never. It cannot happen. For all the darakat, the darajat, the darakat, everything is mentioned in Allah Ta'ala's muhkam book, and that is everything. Well, they traverse these darajat. As I told you: `kunu qiradatan khasi'in` (be apes, despised), "You become monkeys now and fall into a state of transformation." Why did Allah Ta'ala say this? And `ja'alahum qiradatan wa khanazir wa 'abdat al-taghut` (He made them into apes and swine, and worshippers of the false deity). We made them apes, we made them worshippers of the false deity, that is, worshippers of asnam (idols). So, what is all this? He is giving them punishment according to their 'azab, and He is mentioning the darajah and the darakah. So, in this tasalsul-e-kalam (continuity of discourse), I told you that our Du'at have arranged it and shown that look, after this comes this darjah, after that comes this darakah, after that, this is the state of jahannam. So, first, the hisb (sensation) is taken away, then the namiya (growth) remains. The namiya is also slowly taken away until they reach a state of junun (madness). And passing through all these conditions, they traverse these darakat. To traverse these darakat, this 'azab, which is called adna, although before this there is another 'azab, which is called 'azab-e-qabr (punishment of the grave). The Du'at do not even count the 'azab-e-qabr. The 'azab-e-qabr is in its own place, what has been called 'azab-e-qabr, 'azab-e-qabr, it is in its own place. And that 'azab-e-qabr, as I told you, how is that 'azab-e-qabr received? It is due to the hisb and namiya which were lost in his body. Now, when he died, that nafs (soul) did not leave his body. Which nafs? Namiya and Hisb. Why? Its pilot to take it away is not there, so where will it leave from? It spread throughout the body, and they took his body and buried it, or took it and burned it, or, as the Parsis do, they feed it to the birds as charity. They made it into charity. So, it was torn apart by birds of prey, or eaten by the earth, or swallowed by fire. In some way or another, they became fana fillah (annihilated in God). But do you think they were annihilated? No. They were afflicted by 'azabat, and they will have to endure all those 'azabat consecutively. Nothing is fana in this world. Only the hai'at (form) changes. Only the surat (shape) changes. Nothing becomes fana in this world, nothing is fani (perishable). Nothing becomes fana, the surat changes. So I told you that they have to traverse these darakat. This is a small punishment. But the point is that when Hazrat Qa'im 'Alayhissalatu wassalam comes and the 'adalat (court) is established before him, and his darbar (court) is set up, and the 'adalat is held in his hands, and after the darbar, his judgments are announced, the judgments of the entire world will be before him. You will see that all the people... all the judgments of the people will be before the Qa'im. A chair will be placed for him, and how will the judgments happen? It is all an intellectual matter, and it is also a matter of understanding. Indeed, it is not so difficult if you understand it from an 'ilmi (knowledge-based) perspective. They are going to give judgments that are perfectly just. And the judgments of everyone will certainly be done. But whose judgments will they be? The judgments of those will be presented who have been the mudda'iyan-e-waqt (claimants of the time). Those who have opposed the anbiya, the awliya, the a'immah—such people will be presented. It is for them that this great court is held. They are the Chief Justices. It is for them that this great session is held. What is the question of hama shuma (you and me) there? Will every individual of the world be made to stand there and have their judgment passed? This is not the point. Their judgments will have already happened. And the judgments of hama shuma will happen in what way? They will be in the darakat, as I have told you. This is their qudrati (natural) judgment that is present. They will be taken into the darakat, into the seven levels, into the gates of jahannam. And there, they will have to be thrown in. And those seven zirah (armors) and in that zirah, the seven kadiyan (links), which I said are the qamis (shirts), they will have to wear. And I said that whenever they change their qamis... or perhaps I explained it to you, at that time they are given a choice, and they are told what punishment they are being given. But when the punishment is given, it is not told for what matter the punishment is being given. When the punishment is given, just as here, the sentence is read out to the person, that you are being punished for this reason, what it is, etc. In exactly the same way, when the qamis changes, he is told who he is, why he has come, for what he has received punishment, for what he has already been punished, and to which place he is going now. That's it. But when he is receiving the punishment, he is not told who he is or what he is. So this is the way of the 'Adil, the Hakim. And in this way, jabr (compulsion) and ikhtiyar (choice) have been joined by Allah Ta'ala. So, in this kind of situation, he traverses his darakat. But those who are to be presented before the Qa'im, they are such mujrim (criminals) who are very formidable criminals, who opposed the anbiya, the a'immah, who came and clashed with great mountains. And such people will be presented there, and what will happen to them? For them, it is "sentence to death." Which is called, for them, rigorous punishment. And what kind of punishment will that be? They will be given the death penalty, just as it is given here in this world. The death penalty means the ultimate punishment is given. The punishment that they will receive, within that punishment, the first punishment will be that they will be given 'azab-e-atraf (punishment of the extremities), and after the 'azab-e-atraf, 'azab-e-sijjin (punishment of the lowest prison) will be given. What is 'azab-e-atraf? I will explain 'azab-e-atraf a little bit, because I don't need to go into its details right now, because the 'azab-e-atraf is the punishment of the polar region, of the poles. The North and South poles that we have, where there is extreme cold and extreme heat, and where an immense amount of snow falls and causes great suffering. There, they are punished in this region, in this place. And when is this punishment given? When they have already suffered the 'azab-e-adna and are such that they are also destined to receive the 'azab-e-saqra (punishment of the scorching fire). There are two conditions. Such people who have been sentenced to death, that is, they are also to receive the 'azab-e-saqra, then they are given the 'azab-e-atraf. And it is given to those who, having suffered the 'azab-e-adna, have now come, having completed their entire journey, and now they have to suffer the 'azab-e-atraf. Are you understanding? That is, whoever is to be cast into saqar, it is necessary for them to endure the 'azab-e-atraf. Those who are not being cast into saqar, they will only endure the 'azab-e-adna and be sent back. This is the way of the shari'at. And in this way, the 'azab-e-atraf is given only to those who are to go to saqar and whom the Qa'im 'Alayhissalatu wassalam will put to the sword. And they will be cast into saqar. And before casting them into saqar, they will have to endure the 'azab-e-atraf in this very world. And since the period of Qa'im 'Alayhissalatu wassalam, of our dawr (era)... I told you that 399 qawr (cycles) have passed in the second mawr (aeon), and we are in the 400th qawr, at the end of the first dawr. That is, what is it now? The Qa'im of the dawr is coming. The Qa'im of the dawr who is coming, the judgment will be in his hands. And when the judgment happens, then it is clear that now, those who are in the polar regions, on them the punishment is being suffered. And because of this, what happens? Very large skeletons have been found, very large carcasses have been found, and their bones have been found, of animals, which are very enormous animals. They are several elephants in size for one animal. What is this? It is the power of Allah Ta'ala that those who are being punished are joined together. They are put into a single form, into a single cage, and in the form of these large, large animals, they suffer punishment. And they suffer punishment in such a state that for months, snow is falling on them, they cannot even turn their necks, they cannot even move, and they are such enormous animals, and they have to endure this extreme cold and that. And after that, when they finish this matter, then again, they have to take on a human form in that same state, through what? Through the mizaj mu'tadil ki charkhi (the wheel of balanced temperament). I explained to you before, remember that wheel. The ilahi charkhi (divine wheel) and the tarbiyat ki charkhi (wheel of nurturing) is what? The mizaj mu'tadil. That is, becoming abr-o-baad (clouds and wind), raining down, becoming a plant, that plant being eaten, that food coming into the diet, that animal eating that food, and after eating, being slaughtered, and a person eating the meat of that animal, and from that, a nutfah (sperm-drop) is formed, and from that nutfah, a human is born. This is called the sayr (journey) of the charkhi. And in this charkhi of mizaj mu'tadil, after coming into it, it can be good or it can be bad. That is, just as you grind wheat in a mill, and you can also grind very bad things, in the same way, this mill is useful for both. But the mill is from the side of nature, it is of mizaj mu'tadil. So, this is how it will be. We do not, na'uzubillah, na'uzubillah, have beliefs like awagawan or reincarnation or rebirth. We do not hold such ideas or conceptions. If we believe in a janam (birth), that is, that our second coming into the world will happen, it will be through the mizaj mu'tadil. And our method is what? That after 1,000 years, 'awdat (return) happens, but only if nature also wills it. If, for example, nature wills that no, his 1,000 years are up, but he needs to be kept here for now, then he will be kept for quite some time, and then after that, he will be made to appear. These are their circumstances. Everyone has their own accounts, their own circumstances. But if he is deserving, he will appear again. But he can also be held back due to his circumstances. So, as I told you, this 'azab-e-atraf is given only to those who are also to receive the 'azab-e-saqra, and who are to receive the 'azab-e-saqra, and that is a matter for later, because first, the judgment of Janab-e-Qa'im has to happen. But I am telling you that if Allah Ta'ala has established these 'azabat, for what reason did he establish them? So that the shaare'-e-shari'at (lawgivers of the sacred law)—those anbiya-e-kiram (honorable prophets), those mursalin (messengers), those rasulan-e-barhaqq (true apostles) who came into the world and did their work, and their shari'ats (laws) were accepted by those who accepted, but those who did not accept, who became murtad (apostates), who denied them, who stood before them as Fir'awn, as Namrud, as Haman, as Qarun, as Fir'awn, and appeared and opposed them—this is for them. So why did those shari'ats come? They came for guidance. If there was no intention of giving guidance, then Allah Ta'ala would have, na'uzubillah, become a zalim (tyrant). The Lord of the Worlds has not created us just for nothing. He created us and kept guidance with us. And how did He give guidance? I have told you in detail before, that He gave it through the Tabur. In the Tabur are those people, those individuals who were your sathi (companions), who were like you, who were exactly your hamsath (peers), but what happened with them? They, instead of "no," said "yes." After denial, they made iqrar (affirmation). And they became pak-o-saaf (pure and clean). But you did not feel nadamat (regret) until you were surrounded by the sulasah-e-abad (three eternal dimensions), until you came into the condition of hayyula (prime matter) and surati (form). Until then, you did not feel nadamat. We felt nadamat, and as a result, the firqah-e-najatwala (the saved sect) was formed. We became Sulaimani. But despite all this happening, the judgment will certainly happen. We fell into this world of... which is the house of gusse (wrath). This is what the Du'at have said, this world, which Mawla-e-Kainat, Hazrat 'Ali ibn Abi Talib 'alayhissalatu wassalam, kicked three times and said, "`Tallaqtuki thalath`" (I divorce you thrice). I divorce you three times. What is the meaning of talaq (divorce)? Was she a woman whom he was divorcing? No, it means I am leaving you. And he kicked it. And when you, to restrain the duldul, got down, you kicked the mountain. In this way, you kicked the earth and said, "O earth, and O world, you adorn yourself and come before people with zeenat (beauty), but I curse you and do this to you." So, it is the house of God's wrath. It is a kaid-khana (prison). In a prison, you will say, "I should get biryani, I should get all these things, I should get means of adornment, I should get all comforts." No, sir, not here. You will get ara'ish (adornments), you will get zeba'ish (beautifications), you will get happiness, but with wrath. That is, with gham (sorrow). You have not yet received a moment of happiness when sorrow comes. You have not yet received happiness when sorrow comes. So, this is a house of sorrow, a gham-kada (abode of grief). Here, there is wrath, and here, you will have to bear the wrath of Allah. Here, happiness will come with sorrow. So, since it is a kaid-khana, you cannot hope for goodness here. That is why it is called the Bait al-Ghazab al-Ilahi (the House of Divine Wrath). It is called the house of God's wrath. It is a dar-e-'amal (realm of action), the house of God's wrath, and here you have to do your deeds. What do you have to do? You have to act with piety, following the shari'at-e-barhaqq (the true sacred law), taking the tawassul (intercession) of your prophet, you have to determine your own path. This is the correct path. That is why what did Allah Ta'ala do? He told that Tabur to stay right there, but their hijabs (veils) should be established, and they should be established in order and give guidance, and the chain of guidance should remain established in the world. The chain of guidance continued on this side, but Shaytan, you saw, was standing right there and playing his shaytanat (tricks). And what kind of shaytanat did he play? What kind of shaytanat did he play? As I said, like the speakers in Hyde Park who give speeches, and anyone can go and start yelling at a wall, and people start listening. In the same way, that masukh (transformed being) grew, and he was shouting, and people were listening. And they were listening to the voice of this Shaytan. Was this Shaytan some entity that had been created, had a label, had been made? Na'uzubillah, nothing of the sort. He was from among them, from the group of 'ashir (the tenth), he was one of them. But it just occurred to him that he should create opposition. He created opposition. The result of creating opposition was that he became Shaytan. And when he became Shaytan, what happened? He appeared here first. And he came, and when he came, he came in the form of Shaytan. And all his followers, all those who followed him, all those who did not believe, his entire zariyyat (progeny)... That is why, when we say `a'uzu billahi minash shaytanir rajim` (I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Shaytan), we seek refuge from whom? From all those surat-e-khabisah (evil forms) about which you have heard. They are all his zariyyat. Any surat-e-khabisah will be attributed to him. Now, I want to tell you how Allah Ta'ala arranged the means of guidance. And I told you... Now, leaving this topic, because the final mention is of the judgment of Janab-e-Qa'im, so to bring up that mention, I want to first briefly mention the shari'ats, how the factory of guidance was established here. I will also briefly touch upon that before you. That is why I... at least the nutuqa... the mention of 124,000 nabi (prophets) cannot be done. There are detailed stories about them. The stories are not just those that you read in Qasas al-Anbiya or in the books of Muslims. No, no. These are prophets, righteous prophets, givers of guidance. They are not humans like us. Understand? Na'uzubillah, na'uzubillah, the way Muslims have considered them to be humans just like any other human. No, they are much higher than us. What is the difference between us and them? ...'alam-e-paak... No, these are anbiya, these are rasul, these are givers of guidance, these are the people of the Tabur, they live in the bait al-ma'mur (the Frequented House). What have we to do with them? No, these are givers of guidance, and in the givers of guidance, there is a difference like heaven and earth. So Janab Yunus, Yusuf, Ya'qub—the story of each one is worth understanding. Each one is full of hikmat (wisdom). All their matters are worth knowing. Each and every thing. Did this Zulaikha and Yusuf's qissa (story), this ishqiya (love) story, did the Quran narrate it? Na'uzubillah, na'uzubillah, which Muslims take as a love story and make a big fuss about, saying "This Ahsan al-Qasas is a rangin (colorful) narrative." This is a colorful story of the Quran. Na'uzubillah, na'uzubillah, the Quran Majid and portraying its prophet in this manner? No, no, it is not like that. It is a matter of great understanding. Who was Zulaikha, who was Yusuf, what was happening, who was Ayyub, who was Ya'qub—all these are things to understand. Anyway, I will mention a few people before you for this reason, that those who were the nutuqa, in our tradition, the anbiya-e-kiram who came as natiq (speaking) prophets, at least I will mention those five or six nutuqa so that you will get an idea of what the sirat (character) of our anbiya is and how they give guidance and how guidance is given. So that you can understand the sawab (reward) in contrast to this 'azab, and along with that, you can understand that those who are to be sentenced to death, they are these people who opposed the anbiya, the awliya, the a'immah. Those who opposed them, they are to be sentenced to death, and their judgment will be at the hands of the Qa'im. Will Karbala just pass like that? No, it won't. Will the 30 years of silence of Mawla-e-Kainat just pass like that? No, it won't. Will the poisoning of Janab-e-Hasan be forgotten? No, it won't. Every single thing will be answered for. `Az maast ki bar maast` (What is upon us is from ourselves). `Hai yeh gumbad ki sada, jaisi kahe waisi sun` (This is the echo of the dome; as you say, so you shall hear). As you did, so you received. Receiving it is certain. If you did good, good. If you did bad, bad. `faman ya'mal mithqala dharratin khayran yarah, waman ya'mal mithqala dharratin sharran yarah` (So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it, And whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it). He who did good, saw it. He who did bad, saw it. Not that he did good and it went into the water, or did bad and it went into the water. No, it will not happen like that. This is not the law of nature. You see that if you touch fire, fire is fire. Ice does not become a ball of fire, and if you take ice, fire does not form. And if you take tamarind, it doesn't become mango, and if you take mango, it doesn't become tamarind. When the law of nature doesn't change, then this law of nature also doesn't change. As is Allah, so it is. So when nature established the shari'ats, first of all, I told you, and I want to refresh your memory, that let's go back to the lesson I taught you, where the qa'imrud-e-a'zam was established on the rasikh (firmament), when the world found its tartib (order), the world was first created, and I had said that Hazrat Adam 'alayhissalatu wassalam, who is called Adam-e-Qa'imrud, where did he come? He came to Lanka. He came to Lanka, where 27 individuals were gathered, and he was the 28th. And from them, he propagated the da'wat. And how? 12 became layl (night), 12 became nahar (day), one was a mazur, one was a mu'akhkhir, and one was a babu. And in this way, there was a taqsim (division) of 27, and he himself was the 28th. And in this way, the silsilah (chain) of imamat (leadership) began from the Imam. And what happened? Now his sons who became Imams... Remember that it is a qa'idah-e-kulliyah (universal principle) for imamat that only the son of an Imam will be an Imam. This is our iman (faith). And it is the qawl-e-faisal (decisive statement) of the Prophet 'alayhissalatu wassalam that `mashiyatullah yadullahi sha'in illa fil imama` (The will of God is the hand of God in nothing except in the Imamate). The will of God... that is, God's will is as God wills. This is the i'tiqad (belief) of all the Muslims of the world, all of this is there. But our i'tiqad is slightly different. And what is that? We say that God is as He wills, `innal-laha 'ala kulli shay'in qadir` (Indeed, Allah is over all things competent). Allah Ta'ala has power over everything, but there is one thing over which He does not have power. You see? Allah Ta'ala does not have power over one thing. He does not have power over that thing which Allah Ta'ala Himself has said, "I have established it, and now I am not going to change it." `la tabdila li khalqillah` (there is no changing the creation of Allah), Allah Ta'ala says in the Quran Majid. There will be no change in this. `la tabdila li sunnatillah` (there is no changing the way of Allah). There will be no change in the way of Allah. For what is He saying this? For the imamat. This chain of imamat that Allah has started, there will be no change in this. Any law can be changed because it is in Allah's hands, in His power, everything. But the Parvardigar-e-Alam, who has also done this, the way He has arranged the 'ashir and the mudabbir, now there will be no change in this. After an Imam, only an Imam will come, the son of an Imam will be an Imam. And you have understood well why the son of an Imam is the Imam. It is for this reason that propagating the da'wat and giving birth to a son are equivalent matters. You have understood. Propagating the da'wat and giving birth to a son are equivalent matters. That is why I say that if you miss even one lesson, it will be difficult. Propagating the da'wat, that is, whatever samra (fruit) of the da'wat comes, it is clear that from that samra, what will be formed? Qabiliyyat (potential). And those same namiyat that arose in the form of qabiliyyat, and which went to Shams, via Zuhra and 'Utarid, and came to Qamar, and then after coming here again through the dukh, coming into the diet, and coming to the Imam, and wiladat (birth) happens, through the silsilah of tanasul (procreation), then the child who is born will be the Imam. That is why the Nabi Karim (Noble Prophet) says: `lata'ifu shiy'atina kasa'ifuna wa kasa'ifuna lata'ifuhum` (The subtle bodies of our followers are our dense bodies, and our dense bodies are their subtle bodies). The lata'if of our Shia... Our Shia's lata'if are our kasa'if. Our ruh (souls) are our jism (bodies). And our kasa'if, when we leave this body, we make them into our latif (subtle body). So, this... this... keep this in mind, this is a law. So it is known that after an Imam, there will be an Imam. After a father, there will be a son. Now you understand why after a father, there is a son. In this, it is not a matter of nasl (lineage) in the way that Qabil had a son and the lineage continued. The matter here is that after an Imam, the son of the Imam will be the Imam. There might be ten sons, but the one upon whom he confers it, his son will be the Imam. So it is clear that this chain continued. From Qa'imrud-e-A'zam, the chain started, and it went on, and what happened? One, two, three, four... thousands of Imams passed. And in whose womb did they pass? In the 47,000 years. I told you that the dawr (period) is of 50,000 years, the dawr of kashf, and the first dawr that was, what was it? It was day. It was kashf (unveiling). In the 47,000 years of kashf, many a'immah (Imams) passed. Father after son continued. We don't need to write the names of all the Imams. But if you think about it, their names are preserved in Allah's lawh-e-mahfuz (Preserved Tablet). They must have names. But as I told you, I will tell you the name of the first Imam and the last Imam. The name of the first Imam was Qa'imrud. The first Imam's name was Qa'imrud, and after him were his sons, and after him were their sons, and in this way, the chain continued for 47,000 years. And after 47,000 years passed, the 3,000-year period of fitrat (lethargy) began. And what is fitrat? It is called the period of susti (lethargy). What do we call fitrat in terms of the day? The time of maghrib (sunset). The time of maghrib, what is it? It is a time of a strange twilight. It is a time of a strange melancholy. It is a time of a strange excitement. Melancholy starts to set in. Why? This melancholy is just like the darkness that was covering you there when you were drowning. So this is also a time of melancholy, of darkness, that now night is coming. And before the night, a shadow of the night starts to fall. And there is some day, some night, and you are in a twilight state. It's a time of twilight. And this is called the dawr-e-fitrat. Fitrat means susti. This is a period of susti, and it is for 3,000 years. In these 3,000 years, the Imam is always present, but just as during the day, the da'wat (call) was shining... What happens? During the day, the police do not need to run around so much because there is not so much hooliganism, and pickpockets and rogues do not work. And even animals are hidden in their burrows during the day. But when night falls, what happens? Animals also come out of their burrows, and thieves and robbers also come out, thinking, "It's the cover of night, let's do whatever we want." So all the crimes happen when? They happen at night. So now night is coming, maghrib has started, and now the time of susti has come. And those ahl-e-iman (people of faith), who were believers, susti started to creep into them. What? Now what did they do? "Brother, look, it looks good. Let's put a flower on the picture, what's wrong with that? If we, on our face, on our... if our face is beautiful, what's wrong with having a black beauty spot? It's a very good thing. But where will we put the spot? We will put it where the Hindus put it." They put on a tika, so we will also start putting on a tika. Now these kinds of rasumat (customs) slowly, slowly started to creep in. And you started to move away from your place. Rasumat, waham (superstitions)... what is it? Not to pluck a leaf at night, not to sweep at night, and not to do this and that. Now these things which are women's talk today, in that era, they became men's talk. Now the qiyamats are happening. Superstitions are spreading all over the world. Don't sweep backwards, don't sweep forwards, don't do this, don't do that. If a cat crosses, there will be a commotion. If that happens, there will be a commotion. Brother, what is this commotion about? The commotion is about the salawat. You have completely swallowed that commotion with silence. If the money jingles, it will be known that there is something, some jingle, some commotion. That commotion is completely silent. Brother, for God's sake, bring up the topic of salawat. It seems like you are narrating the salawat to me. Say whatever you want, but for God's sake, the salawat... "Brother, my house is being built." "Don't you have..." All this is fine, but giving money is the worst. So what happens is this. So these superstitions started. The superstitions... strange, strange kinds of superstitions. Now this period of superstitions was for 3,000 years. And 3,000 years passed, and after 3,000 years passed, the last Imam who came... The first Imam, I told you, was Janab-e-Hunayn. ...was Janab-e-Qa'imrud. Now the last Imam, that is, the dawr-e-kashf is ending, and the dawr-e-fitrat is starting... Oh, the dawr-e-fitrat is ending, after the dawr-e-kashf, fitrat came, fitrat ended, and now what is coming? Satr (concealment) is coming. Now, just before the satr and at the very end of the dawr-e-kashf, who was the last Imam? It was Maulana Hunayn. And Hunayn, the name suggests some connection to Hind (India), perhaps they were in India. Anyway, it is not told. But it seems so, that there is some connection to Hind. When all the prophets were related to the Arabs, at least connect Janab Hunayn to Hind. So, Janab Hunayn, you can relate him to Hind. We will also be happy, we give you permission. But Janab Hunayn was the last Imam, and in the time of Janab Hunayn, he saw that now the dawr-e-satr is beginning, and according to the dawr-e-satr, now... a time is coming which is called the darkness of night. Why? The night's darkness, what does it mean? That the fitrat is now over, the susti is over, and the night's darkness is spreading. The dawr-e-kashf is over, that was of 47,000 years. The dawr-e-fitrat of 3,000 years is over. After the dawr-e-fitrat, 7,000 years are beginning, and its beginning starts from where? From Janab-e-Hunayn, who was the last Imam of the dawr-e-kashf. He was the last Imam, and he saw that now the time of night has come, the night has fallen, that twilight is over. Now there is no time for us to appear in the world. Now the time for the sun to set has come, we have to go into concealment. Now we will not appear openly. Why? Because these people have now become very corrupt. Their minds have become spoiled. Their hearts have rusted. Their intellect has been eaten away. And their intellect has become corrupt. Now these people do not know how to respect the awliyaullah (saints of God). If we speak too much, they will stone us. It is better that we remain silent in our place and send someone as a rasul (messenger), someone as a nabi (prophet) on our behalf. This was the matter of risalat (messengership) and nabuwwat (prophecy). And he was the Lord of the time. Janab Hunayn, the Imam of his time, who had come through the chain of son after son, who had started from Qa'imrud-e-A'zam. Janab Hunayn, what did he do? He saw that now there is a need to make someone appear in the world, and there is a need to send someone as a nabiyyun mursal (a prophet sent as a messenger). There is a need to make him a nabi. What is a nabi? One who gives khabar (news). He gives the news of jannat (paradise), warns against jahannam (hell), teaches the shari'ah (sacred law), teaches good morals. Why did this need arise? He saw that now our... if we try to explain, they will not understand. Rather, if a lesser person goes and explains to them in their language, it will be better. This is what he saw. At this time, what happens? If the sun sets, you don't sit in the dark. You either... Allah Ta'ala gives the light of the moon, or you do what? You light a candle or you light a lamp. In the same way, when darkness started to spread, the Lord of the Worlds sent prophets, and the prophets, through the Du'at, took this light from them and began to shine like stars in the darkness. These are the stars of that darkness, which were shining. Do you understand? So now Janab Hunayn saw that now I should make someone a nabi and send him here. What should I do? He looked around in his da'wat-e-sharif (noble mission), and there were many people, whose names were Mahla'il, Dahla'il, Darda'il, Darba'il, 'Azazil. And many such mala'ikah (angels) were there in the darbar (court) of Janab Hunayn, in that da'wat-e-sharif, whom you could make appear, whom you could send. But he saw that from God's side, that he had a brother, who was the king of a small region at that time, and his name was Tanjum. Tanjum the king. He was a king, and his name was Tanjum. And perhaps he was named Tanjum for this reason, that he had a great connection with nujum (astrology), and he was very skilled in the science of stars. For this reason, it might have been so, Allah knows best. But his name was Tanjum, and he was his brother. He was the brother of Janab Hunayn. Maulana Hunayn, who is the Imam of the time, of his era, and who is ending the dawr-e-kashf and starting the dawr-e-satr, Janab Hunayn, his brother was Tanjum. He had a son who was very young, and his name was what? 'Abdullah. His name was 'Abdullah, and he was receiving tarbiyat (nurturing), receiving ta'lim (education). He was reading the basic books of shari'ah, on taharat (purification) and this and that. But the vision of Janab Hunayn was seeing that this child of today can become the nabi of tomorrow. He can be sent as a nabi. So I... sending all these big people will achieve nothing. If I send someone, I will send this child. So now, when he made this decision, to send his nephew, when he made the decision to send Janab 'Abdullah, that he should come into the world as Adam. Adam. Whom do they call Adam? Every person who begins something is called Adam. That is why he is called Adam Smith. This term has become common in the world. Every person who begins something is called Adam. That is why we say Adam-e-kulli. He will be the one to start the dawr-e-satr. So, every person who begins something is called Adam. Since he was the one to start the dawr-e-satr, that is why he was called Adam. Otherwise, Adam, Adam is not a name. His name is what? Janab 'Abdullah. And his father's name is what? Tanjum. And his grandfather's name is Khaujan. And if you want, I can list four or five more generations. And the name of his locality is Zahaka. And the name of the tribe to which he belongs is Zahaka. And where he lived, its name is Shahbaz Badi. And that is a region in Lanka, and in that Shahbaz Badi, that was the region of that time, he lived there. I have even told you who his friends were, who his wife was, what his children were, etc. All these things have been told by us. Nothing can remain hidden. Under the sun, no speck can remain hidden. In the floodlight, everything is clear. Nothing can remain hidden. So it is clear that Janab Adam 'alayhissalatu wassalam, who was Janab 'Abdullah, the gaze was on 'Abdullah, of whom? Of Janab Hunayn. And Janab Hunayn, in the end, what did he do? When he chose him, he said that he is capable of appearing as a nabi, so he told all the mala'ikah, `inni ja'ilun fil ardi khalifah` (Indeed, I will make upon the earth a successor). I want to make a khalifah (successor) on the earth. This is the declaration of Allah Ta'ala which the Quran has mentioned. Now what does making a khalifah mean? Now from khalifah, understand this khilafat (caliphate). This, the khalifah that they become, right? This khilafat. Does a khalifah call himself a khalifah? Khalifah means he wanted to make him his na'ib (deputy), he wanted to make him a nabi. So what did the mala'ikah say? `ataj'alu fiha man yufsidu fiha wa yasfikud dima'a wa nahnu nusabbihu bihamdika wa nuqaddisu lak` (Will You place upon it one who causes corruption therein and sheds blood, while we declare Your praise and sanctify You?). Will you appoint someone who will shed blood? And we are enough for your tasbih (glorification) and tahlil (praise). What was the meaning? The meaning was this: "O Allah, we have studied the sciences of the da'wat so much, we are so learned, we are reading the haqa'iq, we have finished the books of ta'wil, etc. It would have been good if Your gaze had fallen on us. We have served the da'wat a great deal, so please bestow some favor on us as well. You have made us into scattered dust, you have forgotten us. No, you have forgotten us, and whom are you choosing? That Janab Adam, who, poor fellow, is still in ta'wil, and what? He is still in taharat. And if you make him the judge, he will create a mess, and there will be bloodshed all around. Neither will the judgment be a judgment, nor will there be any order in the da'wat. This is also your way. If you have to make someone, make someone from among us." This was the demand of the mala'ikah, which they were making from Janab Hunayn. This is the saying of the mala'ikah to Allah. Now see where Allah has gone, where the mala'ikah have gone, and where their plea has gone. And the Quran Majid is narrating something else, and these Muslims are understanding something else. So, this was the demand of Janab Hunayn, from those of the da'wat, who were called mala'ikah. Mala'ikah is said to a malak, who is appointed to some service. They are called mala'ikah. They were mala'ikah, and among those mala'ikah, there was also 'Azazil. The name of one malak, one angel, was 'Azazil. And what did he say? "You have made the decision. And you want to make Janab Adam, that is, Janab 'Abdullah, your nephew, you have made a firm decision. What is happening? How are you doing this? I am the one who knows the most about the haqa'iq. I am the Mu'allim al-Malakut (Teacher of the Angelic Realm)." This is what Shaytan had said, that "I am the one who teaches the mala'ikah. The Mu'allim al-Malakut." The one who teaches the Malakut. "The one who teaches the haqa'iq, the one who reveals the realities of life is me." And what claim did he make? That "Adam... this Adam, this Janab 'Abdullah, he is created from clay. And I know the science of the flame. And this 'Abdullah is turabi (of dust). He is of clay, meaning he is still reading the shari'ah." He is still reading the laws of the shari'ah. He is within the laws. And you want to make 'Abdullah great, not me? This was his demand. And what happened? What did Allah Ta'ala say? Janab Hunayn said, "The din (religion) is nothing but ta'at (obedience), and you are deviating from my ta'at? I have commanded that you prostrate to Adam." That is, accept Adam. This doesn't mean to keep prostrating. The prostration that we do in namaz, that kind of prostration? Na'uzubillah, na'uzubillah, nothing of the sort. It was about ta'at. "Obey Adam. I have made him my khalifah, my nabi, so obey him." And as soon as the command for ta'at was given, all of them... `illa iblis` (except Iblis)... all of them prostrated, except Iblis. Allah Ta'ala called him rajim (accursed). And he was expelled from jannat. Now what does being expelled from jannat mean? What does it mean? It happens in a second. For a ruhani (spiritual) thing, it doesn't take long. For a jismani (physical) thing, you have to put on handcuffs and put them in jail and do this and that. For a ruhani thing, what is it? He said, "You are out of my... out of the darbar, go," and he went. And he said, "You get out of this da'wat, get out of my jannat." Da'wat is jannat. "Get out of jannat," meaning get out of the da'wat. And he was thrown out from there and told, "You are rajim. You have been cast out from my presence. You did not obey Adam. My obedience is only when you obey Adam." He left. After leaving, now what is the condition? Just as your veins throb, God forbid, if shaytanat (devilry) comes, what does he do? He tries to take revenge. And taking revenge is a thing of great hararat (heat). When the blood boils, then one thinks of revenge, and ways of revenge also come to mind. Shaytan suggests the ways. And what happened there? That Janab Adam 'alayhissalatu wassalam, who was there, for them, first of all, it is to be seen... leave this for a bit, look at this, that Allah Ta'ala says that I created them with both my hands. There you go. The first qiyamah was that Janab Adam was made from clay. Now the second qiyamah is that some water was also mixed into that clay, it became mud. Now the third qiyamah is that he is making him with both his hands, kneading him, Allah Ta'ala. It's a completely nonsensical thing. So what is the point? That there were two hujjat (proofs) with Janab Hunayn. These are his two hands. And what was the meaning of mud? Water is 'ilm (knowledge), and clay is turab (dust), that is, the essence of the mu'min and kafir (believer and disbeliever). It means he was a mu'min. That is, he was a mustajib (one who responds). He had just accepted the da'wat. He was reading about taharat. So, 'ilm should be poured into him so that the two mix, and he is kneaded with both hands and prepared. That is, two ustad (teachers) should be appointed for his education and nurturing, and Adam should be made in such a way that he can appear as a nabiyyun mursal. What we want will happen. And these two started preparing him. Janab Adam was prepared, and those people accepted him. It was the command of Janab Hunayn, how could they deny it? He became a nabi, a mursal, and after becoming a nabi, he started working in the world. Now, he was shown... the zahiri (apparent) qissa (story)... in the Quran Majid, that he is roaming in jannat, and the gardens of jannat... oh, oh, oh, don't even ask. What kind of fruits are hanging? This temptation is arising, "Let's eat this, let's eat that." This pleasure, that pleasure, all these things, and in jannat, raghadan (in abundance), that is, they are roaming around, moving about, and in front of Janab Adam, colorful fruits are hanging. There are gardens, rivers, all this is there. But what is the condition? Janab Adam is feeling wahshat (loneliness). And Janab Adam is all alone. He is feeling wahshat. And due to feeling wahshat, what happened? Allah Ta'ala did what? When Adam started feeling lonely, he created Janab Hawwa by breaking his rib. Look at this, what is the calamity? To present it, they present it like this, that his rib is broken, first Adam is made to sleep. Pictures have even been shown. What more can be said? Adam is made to sleep, then the rib is broken. After breaking the rib, Janab Hawwa is created. This is the condition. God forbid, is Allah Ta'ala doing some kind of tamasha (spectacle)? Breaking a rib, creating Hawwa, what is this? It's nonsensical. No, it was to tell that there are 12 ribs, and from 12, it means there are 12 nuquba (chiefs). There are 12 hujjat, 12 Du'at. These were the 12 hujjat of Janab Adam at that time. From among those hujjat, one rib was broken, that is, one was separated. Breaking means what? That is, one from among them was separated. That is, Hunayn separated one of them and said, "Adam, these hujjat of yours, make one of them your khalifah. Make this hujjat of yours... make him your na'ib, that is, make him your zauj (partner), so that you may have unsat (familiarity) with him." From a wife, a woman, you have unsat. She will become Hawwa. What was the matter? The real matter was that those ribs, from 12 ribs, it means 12 nuquba. There were 12 Du'at. And from them, one was separated. And the one who was separated, his name was Janab Habil. And he was your son. And yet, despite being a son, he possessed more 'ilm than Adam. Adam possessed less 'ilm than him. Adam was less educated than him, Adam was less intelligent than him. You will say, "How did this happen? They are among the nuquba of Adam, and this is an upside-down matter." Sir, don't worry, it happens. So Janab Adam 'alayhissalatu wassalam's son, Janab Habil, he himself, Habil, became the ustad (teacher) of Janab Adam. He was made the ustad. First thing. Second thing, his son was among the nuquba. Third thing, his son became Hawwa. Hawwa is said for being hawi (encompassing). Since he was hawi over the sciences, that is why he was called Hawwa. Otherwise, for Janab Adam to have a biwi (wife) was of no significance. For a biwi to become... what was the point? Zauj, to be a joda (pair). Brother, two students get together and study, they study from him, so that is a jodi (pair). So, "Come on, brother, let's do a study together, let's do this work together." So does becoming a zauj mean becoming a biwi? No. This is not the meaning. There, Janab Adam must have had some biwi, about whom there is no mention in the Quran Sharif, because she was not a sahiba-e-martaba (a person of rank). She must have been, just as people get married. Janab Adam must have gotten married too. She must have been some biwi of his. But the zauj of Janab Adam was who? It was Janab Habil, and he was his son. And despite being his son, he was what? He was made his partner, that "Adam, if you have to learn about 'ilm and you have to take help, take it from Habil." Now, taking Janab Habil, taking his son, he is going, and he is learning. And now Adam 'alayhissalatu wassalam, along with Hawwa, is touring what? The jannat. They are touring the jannat-e-'aliyat (lofty paradises), and fruits are hanging, and they are eating all things, taking pleasure. What is this jannat? What are these gardens? Like our gardens of grapes and apples and oranges? No, these are not gardens. These gardens are not gardens. No, these gardens mean the da'wat-e-sharif (noble mission). And that qutub-khana (library) of the da'wat-e-sharif, in which library there were excellent books, and the command was being given to read those books, that "Read these books, from this you will get pleasure. These are the books, these are the sciences, from which you will also be satisfied." And Janab Adam 'alayhissalatu wassalam, with Habil, was touring, and they were studying the books. Sometimes they would see ta'wil, sometimes shari'ah, sometimes haqa'iq. And they were happy and seeing what kind of sciences, what kind of things Allah has made permissible for me, that is, Janab Hunayn has made permissible for me. Now, they were reading, but Janab Hunayn commanded, "Look, Adam, we know you, how learned you are, how educated you are, what you are. And we also know how much Habil knows. We command you: `la taqraba hadhihish shajarah fatakuna minaz zalimin` (do not approach this tree, lest you be among the wrongdoers). Look, Adam, roam in this jannat, tour everywhere, eat and drink plenty, live very well. These rivers that are flowing, the river of wine, the river of milk, and its river... What are these rivers? You pick up and see, these Chishti, Qadri, this and that, the chains that are going on among the Muslims, this is what is called the rivers of jannat. Where did this talk come from? Whose false interpretation... the Chishtiyyah... No, sir, these rivers of jannat that were there, these were ta'wil, these were haqa'iq, these were the rivers of shari'ah. These were books, these were sciences. And their rivers were flowing. And Adam was told, "Adam, be careful. You can tour the library and look at all the books, you can see everything, but be careful, do not go near this cupboard." `la taqraba hadhihish shajarah fatakuna minaz zalimin` (do not approach this tree, lest you be among the wrongdoers). "You can study all things, but the books... you can see them, but this cupboard which is sealed, be careful, do not touch this cupboard." Now which cupboard must it have been, and what treasures must have been in that cupboard? That it was... Now what happens? The very thing that is forbidden, our inclination towards it becomes greater. And the state of inclination is such that you were forbidden yesterday, and today you are... "Let's at least push the door and see. He is forbidding so much, there must be something to it." If he is forbidding, there must be something to it, and you will clash with it. So the calamity is this. So the condition is that the very thing that is forbidden, the inclination towards it is greater. So here too, Adam gave in to his nature. And Janab Habil, since he knew more 'ilm than Janab Adam, even though he was a son, he was the ustad of Adam. So what did he do? He started telling Janab Adam, "O respected father, we have been forbidden from this cupboard. If we just take a little look, it won't be a big deal." Do you understand? "If we take a little look, it won't be a big deal. Just one book... we have been completely forbidden. So the thing is that... now look, the greed is also for what? The greed is for the pursuit of 'ilm. That is why Janab Amir al-Mu'minin, in one instance in the Balaghat Intiyam, said for Janab 'Abidharr, "This 'Abidharr is very greedy." People asked, "For whom are you saying this, Mawla?" "This 'Abidharr is your slave. And that 'Abidharr, whose every single thing needs to be written with zar (gold), you are calling that 'Abidharr greedy?" He said, "He is greedy in acquiring sciences." You see? How the matter has changed. He is greedy in acquiring sciences. So here too, greed, desire began. And the desire came from whose side? From Hawwa's side. It is said that it is more from the women's side. So it was not a matter of a woman, it was that Janab Habil, who was his wasi (successor), it was he who felt this desire. He said, "We have seen all the books, Janab Adam. If you pay a little attention, a glance can be cast on this cupboard as well." Now, due to their urging, due to some extending of the hand, slowly, slowly, he started to turn towards that cupboard. And the result was that the book was finally taken out. And what was this book? What was this cupboard? Don't ask about that cupboard. The 'ulum (sciences) that were in that cupboard, the haqa'iq that were there, they were related to the faza'il (virtues) of Hazrat 'Ali ibn Abi Talib 'alayhissalatu wassalam. Those were the fazilats, those were the inner, hidden things, which are hidden from thousands of things. They are still hidden from thousands of eyes. No one can understand them. God knows, God and the Prophet know best, God's curse, that they cannot understand those things. All those things are in it. And the secrets of our coming qiyamah (resurrection) were also present in it. Now what did Janab Adam do? He said, "Alright, we have seen all these things, let's take a tour of this as well." As soon as he took out the book... and he was stopped for a reason, that you should not exceed your limit, otherwise... Did Allah Ta'ala want to stop him? No, but the thing is that you love your child very much, but you don't feed him biryani. Why don't you feed him? Because his stomach is not yet capable of it. You want to give him the best of the best. But you will give it to him when he grows up. But for now, if you give him something, you will give him milk. So, in the same way, their nourishment was from other books. He did not want, Janab Hunayn, that they should get these books. And Janab Adam, on the saying of Janab Habil, came and picked up that book. This was "breaking the tree." Go and pick up the stories of the Muslims and see. What is there? It was a wheat plant, eating wheat. What is so special about wheat? We are eating it day and night. At least I am eating it, it has never happened that I missed it. But they are making our father Adam fall because of that same thing. He was stopped, and the sons are eating. Now you tell me. So what a calamity of a thing it must have been. Brother, what's the big deal about wheat? They got some wheat. Brother, they could have taken some other name. No, wheat. So it is known, anyway... there was a lot of talk about wheat, and what happened? They ate wheat, and because of eating wheat, they were expelled from jannat, "Go. Now from you..." So what happened? `fasawwasu lahuma`... and their... now they became 'uryan (naked), Janab Adam and Janab Hawwa. That is, the libas-e-jannat (garment of paradise) began to be stripped away. Now, since there was 'itab (reproach) from Janab Hunayn, the libas-e-jannat was stripped away. What is libas-e-jannat? That is, the flow of 'ilm that was flowing, and the continuous understanding that he was explaining, that method of explaining was lost. The nazar-e-karam (gaze of grace) of Janab Hunayn that was on him, and on which he was... due to which this pebble was also shining, that shine and luster was lost. Now he is explaining, but he cannot explain. He is doing... but Adam is not able to grasp it. He is not able to take it, and the matter is not coming into his grasp. And he cannot explain. This is the stripping of his libas. The departure from libas, the stripping of the libas of jannat is this. And the 'aib (flaw) became apparent, meaning that how deficient he is in 'ilm, it became apparent to all the people of the da'wat. And the poor fellow, in jannat, out of shame... they began to cover themselves, that my 'aib has become apparent. 'Aib has become apparent, meaning that how many weaknesses I have, they have become apparent. This was the stripping of the libas of jannat. And when the libas of jannat was stripped, what happened? Janab Adam and Janab Hawwa were told by Janab Hunayn, "Adam, what was to happen has happened. Now it is better for you to leave this place, go from jannat." That is, "Leave the da'wat-e-sharif, which you were doing while staying in our presence, now leave our da'wat. You go from our da'wat." Before going, what did he do? He was Janab Adam, after all, a nabiyyun mursal. He wanted to do tawbah (repentance), and for tawbah, he looked towards the 'arsh (throne) — the zahiri qissa. He looked towards the 'arsh, and the names of the panjatan-e-paak were seen shining. And he took their wasila (intercession), the name of Allah's panjatan-e-paak. And he started saying, "O Allah, for the sake of these names, forgive me, `innahu huwat tawwabur rahim` (Indeed, it is He who is the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful)." `fa talaqqa adamu min rabbihi kalimatin fataba 'alayh innahu huwat tawwabur rahim` (Then Adam received from his Lord [some] words, and He accepted his repentance. Indeed, it is He who is the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful). Kalimat (words) were cast upon Adam, and he repented with those kalimat, and due to which Allah Ta'ala accepted his tawbah. What were those kalimat? They were the wasita (intercession) of the panjatan. The books that he had seen, he started calling out "'Ali, 'Ali," and started saying, "He is my mugheeth (helper), he is my savior. O Allah, at least take the tawassul of that pure being and forgive me through it." To whom is he presenting this? To the court of Hunayn. In the court of Janab Hunayn, he presented this. And what did Janab Hunayn say? "Alright, `innahu huwat tawwabur rahim`." So Janab Hunayn is the great Tawwab, the Rahim. Allah is Tawwab, Rahim... where will Allah come from? It is Hunayn who is Tawwab, who is the great acceptor of tawbah. And after accepting the tawbah, he said, "Janab Adam, I have forgiven you, but now you are not capable of serving in my presence. It is better that you go from my presence." And so he left from there, and he was cast down. And it is said that he fell in Jeddah, and she fell somewhere else, and he fell somewhere else. Now, what is the meaning of this falling and being cast down? It means that he was sent to the jaza'ir (islands), that "Now go to those islands of taklif (hardship), where many... where the people do not give chanda (donations), where people create difficulties, where the journey is made long, where one has to stay for a long time. Go to this place of all these hardships and there you will have to do da'wat." And do da'wat, then you will realize what the cold water here was and what the hot water is now. Now you will have to go there and work. And then you will realize how much fun you were having while being in our da'wat. Now what will happen when you do da'wat in the jaza'ir? Janab Adam finally had to come. Janab Habil was with you, who was your wasi, your ustad, your 'atalik (tutor). He was always superior to you. The nabi is inferior. Also, understand this. In the same way, every wasi is superior. Now here, it did not happen that there was an election and the wasi was chosen. All the mala'ikah were seated, "Come on, bring the name of the wasi." It did not happen like that. Neither with Adam, nor with Ibrahim, nor with Ya'qub, nor with Yunus, nor with Nuh, nor with any of the 124,000 prophets who passed, with any prophet was there an election, was there this or that, was there democracy, was there this or that, nor were there ballots, nor were there ballot boxes, nor was there a seal, nor were they counted, nor were the votes counted. If they were counted, then where? At the time of our Nabi Karim. And that too, when? When he had not even been shrouded and buried. He had not been shrouded and buried, but in Banu Saqifah, the papers of the khilafat were being flown. The khilafat was being plundered, and the khilafat... it was being said that the khilafat is our right, it is the right of so-and-so, it is the right of the Muhajirin, it is the right of the Ansar. Brother, at least bury the nabi first. Brother, through whose feet's grace this rahmatul lil 'alamin (mercy to the worlds) has come to you, through whose grace you have received Islam, at least acknowledge him. Brother, in whose days there were these things, that they should become prophets. Do you understand? They wanted to become Rasulullah (the Messenger of God). In whose hearts was this thing, that they should become Rasul. That the risalat should come to us. That we should become the Khatim al-Mursalin (Seal of the Messengers). They couldn't become that, so "Alright, if we can't become this, at least we can become the wasi. We can become the wasi-e-Rasulullah." This is how the matter happened. And then the wasi-e-Rasulullah was made in such a way that there was an election. Brother, if an election is so correct, then all the patients should get together and elect a doctor. Alright, if this is the rule in the world, then I also accept it. All the patients get together and elect their doctor, or is the doctor appointed from above? Or do all the students appoint their own ustad? Or tell me, if there are 200... what are they... sheep... goats, then in their minds, there must be some little bit of intellect. If all that intellect is gathered, can one great intellect be formed from it? `Do sad na'l-e ahnin bayad saakht...` as Janab Rumi says. So, democracy is the most jununi (insane) act. There is nothing more worthless in the world than democracy. This is a shaytani phanda (satanic trap). Democracy is a shaytani (satanic) idea, a shaytani thought, and it has been created by Shaytan. This is not a thing. So, the reality was this, that there, the election was done in that way. So, there was no election for anyone. So Janab Adam 'alayhissalatu wassalam, in this way, he became a nabi and came into the world as a nabiyyun mursal. He came as a nabi. What does this mean? Tell me this, what does it mean to come as a nabi? What is a nabi after all? What is this nun, be, ye? What is this nabi? What happened? I don't understand. Nabi, nabi, nabi, we keep hearing. Anbiya, anbiya, anbiya. What is a nabi after all? Nabi is said to be one who gives khabar (news). Brother, if there is no news, then what is the giver of news? What news is he giving? Is he giving news of Allah? Is he telling where Allah is, what he is? No. How is he a nabi? No, all the anbiya were coming to give the news of 'Ali. Amir al-Mu'minin 'Ali, who is in the nisbat-e-'ala (highest relation), in the Tabur, whose point was first of all, they came to give news of him, the naba'-e-'azim (the great news), whom the Quran Majid has called the naba'-e-'azim, whom the Prophet 'alayhissalatu wassalam has called the hablullahil matin (the firm rope of Allah), whom he has called the amir al-nahl (chief of the bees), Abu Turab (father of dust). He was called by thousands of titles, who in reality is the naba'-e-'azim. The greatest news of Allah that is in the world is 'Ali ibn Abi Talib 'alayhissalatu wassalam. So, to give this news, all the anbiya were coming, 124,000. That he is coming, he is coming. That is why Mawla said that in some era I was known by the name of Ilyas, in some era I was known by the name of so-and-so, in some era I was known by the name of Qarrar. So he was telling that his condition had started from there. His manifestation had started from there. That is why the nabi said that if you want to see Adam in his 'ilm, and Nuh in his hilm (forbearance), and Ibrahim in his shaukat (grandeur) and haibat (awe), you want to see them in their condition, and Musa in his haibat, and 'Isa in his zuhd (asceticism), then look at 'Ali ibn Abi Talib. Why did the nabi say this? It was for this reason that all these are slaves of 'Ali. All these who are coming are slaves of 'Ali. That is why he told them. No, the nabi himself knew that he is the one with the nisbat-e-'ala. But they had turned towards the nabi, so he bowed his head and accepted Islam here as well. Otherwise, that 'Ali would never have accepted Islam. What was the need? He was from the nisbat-e-'ala. Why did the one from the nisbat-e-'ala bow down? Because they had bowed down there. 'Ali bowed down, and he recited the kalimah (declaration of faith) of the Rasulullah, that "`ashhadu an la ilaha illallah, ashhadu anna muhammadar rasulullah`." He recited it for this reason. So it is known that this is the story of Janab Adam. If there is a little bit left, I will narrate it, and after that, I will tell you how the era of Janab Nuh came after 1,000 years, and after that, how the chain of nabuwwat was established—Ibrahim, then Musa, then 'Isa, and our Prophet 'alayhissalatu wassalam, how they came. Because if you understand the shari'ats a little bit, then it will be easy for you to understand the ijlas (session) of Janab-e-Qa'im.

I had made a statement before you that regarding the story of Hazrat Adam *'alayhi al-salat wa al-salam*, but I will always want your attention to always keep *Tamur* in consideration. That is the active field, it is the origin, it is the place of the *Masjudin* (those who are prostrated to), and everything… whatever is happening in this universe, who is its axis? It is the *Ka'ba-e-Ruhani* (Spiritual Ka'ba). Just as this is the *Ka'ba-e-Jismani* (Physical Ka'ba), the honor, status, loftiness, delicacy, and comprehensiveness that this Physical Ka'ba has obtained is purely due to that Spiritual Ka'ba, because the complete reflection of that Spiritual Ka'ba is falling upon the Physical Ka'ba. For this reason. So, *Tamur* has the greatest importance, where both *Nisbat-e-'Ala* (the Higher Connection) and *Nisbat-e-Adna* (the Lower Connection) are present. And they, one after the other, their successors become luminous, and in that active field, what happens? *Khilafats* (vicegerencies) are established. To establish *khilafat* means to come to service. They have been appointed to service. Why? Because they had said 'yes' after saying 'no'. After refusing, they... [unclear]... After refusing, they had affirmed. For this reason, service was imposed upon them, that now you have to serve one after the other. And you have to do it one after the other. And what was done? That there, in the *Nisbat-e-'Ala*, this condition was set: that the service you perform, that is established in the same manner, one after the other, you must do it in that way. And now, in whatever way the people of *Nisbat-e-Adna* have been established there, they will be in the same way. But for the *Nisbat-e-'Ala*, what form did *Qudrat* (Divine Power) set here? I have explained its entire chemistry to you, how their body is, what it is. For this reason, *Qudrat* kept this system: that for the Imam, this is the condition. Since he is the guide (*hadi*), the leader (*rahbar*), the master of the universe, the Lord of the Time (*Rabb-e-Waqt*), the God of the Time (*Khuda-e-Waqt*), for him, it is necessary that always after the father, the son... this chain will continue in the same way. And until the world is completely finished, this chain cannot break. It cannot break at all. So, this is a chain that *Qudrat* has established. And the chain of the Prophets (*Anbiya*) has been set in such a way that for them, it is not a condition to have a son after the father. For them, it is that just as *Qudrat* chose whomever it wished, the Imam chose whomever he wished, and made him. But what happens is that, in reality, they are the same ones who are there. You have to keep this in mind. And those who are there, they are called *Muhtajib* (veiled), meaning those who are hidden. And these are called *Hijab* (veils), meaning those who hide. These are called *Hijab*, and they are called *Muhtajib*. Those are the ones who remain behind a curtain; this is the curtain. That is the meaning; these are the words. You understand? So, they are the origin, and they establish an effect of theirs here. And that effect, it is apparent that *Qudrat* also wants them, 'You go into this world and do the work.' And this is also a difficult matter that *Qudrat* has imposed upon them, that you have no choice but to serve. So, if they are to perform the service, how should they do it? So they found a middle path, that we will use an effect of ours, and that effect will be in the form of the *Nafs-e-Hissiyah* (the sensory soul). And the *Nafs-e-Natiqah* (the rational soul) is their deputy. And for the *Nafs-e-Namiyah* (the vegetative soul) and for their body, what arrangement was made? All the *Nafs-e-Namiyah* of the believers, after their death, after their burial, after the three days in the grave, what emerges, that *Namiyah* which is called *Ridiya*, their body will be formed from that *Ridiya*. So, it becomes known that if we see the Imam, then we are seeing ourselves. It is for this reason that the Noble Prophet (*Nabi-e-Karim*) had said that *lata'ifuna*... *lata'ifu shi'atina... wa kas... lata'ifu shi'atina ka-kasa'ifina* (The subtle bodies of our Shia are like our dense bodies). That the subtle bodies (*lataif*) of our Shia are our dense bodies (*kasaif*). *Kasaif* means the body. And I had told you that just as we have power over our clothes, that we can take off our clothes whenever we want and wear other clothes, they have that much power over their bodies. And they have so much power that in a thousandth of a second, they can be somewhere else entirely. It is not known how many there are; it cannot even be estimated. And to understand this, how many Imams changed and what happened and how they changed, then you should see: we go to see a film. Our eyes are on the screen. You, you watch the film. Hey brother, it's loaded in the projector, watch the film! No, you turn your back on the projector. You look towards the screen, because you just have to see the screen. Now what happens on the screen? You should understand that you see a figure. And you started looking at that figure, and now your gaze is fixed on that figure, and it is moving, it is doing some work, or it is saying something, everything is happening. And you are looking at that figure, and you are happy or whatever you are doing, you are doing it. And what is happening behind? That projector, if you go near it and look, you will see that for that same person, reel after reel has passed. A thousand pictures have passed, and there on the screen, you are seeing only one person. It becomes known that it has movement; every movement has a picture, and you are seeing it with that movement. But in reality, what is to be told, the example to be given is this, the example is that there is only one point of comparison. And the point of comparison is only this: that behind the screen, so many have changed, but in front, you saw only one thing. So, in the same way, the Imams (*A'immah*) and the Friends of Allah (*Awliya' Allah*), for them... So, in the same way, the Imams (*A'immah*) and the Friends of Allah (*Awliya' Allah*), for them, you should understand, there are tremendous realities. We are thinking, 'Oh, they have fallen ill!' 'Oh, they are being killed!' Alas! You see, the entire Islamic world... May God ask these people, may God ask the Islamic world, you just reflect that He who, in the Qur'an Majid, stated so explicitly, and on the tongue of the Prophet. One must remember this matter. I am wielding such a big axe now that after this, Islam... no one will be able to stand up. That in the Qur'an Majid, this reality is coming, and He is stating that Allah Ta'ala performed this marvel, that for only one Prophet, He made this statement. He did not say it for all the prophets. But what did He say? He said a strange thing. What did He say? For Hazrat 'Isa, He said that *wa ma qataluhu wa ma salabuhu wa lakin shubbiha lahum* (and they did not kill him, nor did they crucify him, but [another] was made to resemble him for them). I thought that this incident, when Hazrat 'Isa's station comes, I will explain it then. But since the topic has come up, I am speaking. That you did not... Allah Ta'ala says that the people did not kill him, nor did they crucify him, but Hazrat 'Isa was made to resemble another (*tashbih kar di gayi*). Or the people were put into doubt. *Shubbiha lahum* has both meanings: a resemblance was made, and they were put into doubt. The people thought they were giving it to 'Isa, but they were not giving it to Hazrat 'Isa. First point. And the second point is, if they were put into doubt, what does that mean? It means the same thing, that some other person was crucified, he was not. So, they were in doubt about this too. So, whether you take the meaning of doubt or the meaning of resemblance, it is the same thing. So, now you see that when all the Muslims are asked, they say that Allah has clarified about 'Isa *'alayhi al-salat wa al-salam* in the Qur'an Majid: *bal rafa'ahu Allahu ilayh* (rather, Allah raised him to Himself). Allah raised him high towards Himself. So when it is clearly stated, it means he was not crucified. And do you believe that Hazrat 'Isa was crucified? In three sects... people are divided into three classes. One says that Hazrat 'Isa was crucified. The second says that Hazrat 'Isa was not crucified. And one says that Hazrat 'Isa was indeed crucified, but when his body was taken down, there was a spark of life left, and his disciples took him and fled, and went straight to where? To Kashmir. In India's Kashmir they reached. And going to Kashmir, they raised and cared for Hazrat 'Isa, and there Hazrat 'Isa then lived his life and after staying there, you... Now this is the belief of the Qadianis (Ahmadis). There is a reality in this too. There is a reality in that one, and a reality in that one too. But there is some reality, a little bit. But what is the correct matter? The correct matter is this, that now this, which Allah Ta'ala says, that they did not kill him, did not crucify him, then where was Adam killed, brother? Where was Nuh killed? Where was Musa killed? Where was 'Isa killed? No one was killed, no one was buried. Did you understand? By speaking for one Prophet, he has alluded to all the Prophets. For our Prophet Karim, the Seal of the Messengers (*Khatm al-Mursalin*), what will you say? *Hayat al-Nabi* (the life of the Prophet), *Hayat al-Nabi*, they chant this slogan a lot. But do they also understand what is meant by *Hayat al-Nabi*? So, *Insha'Allah*... But you are understanding this matter, that it is a matter of great depth, a very profound matter. That this is that when a person, when for the Prophet *'alayhi al-salat wa al-salam*, Allah Ta'ala is saying, look in the Qur'an Sharif: *innaka mayyitun wa innahum la-mayyitun* (Indeed, you are to die, and indeed, they are to die). O Prophet, you are going to pass away, and everyone has to go from this world. When the Master of the Universe (*Sarwar-e-Kainat*), the Chief of the Prophets (*Sayyid al-Anbiya*), is passing away, then what power does Hazrat 'Isa have? What power does Hazrat 'Isa have? Can he, God forbid, be equal to the Prophet? So what can it mean? It means the same thing, that there is some depth. It is a resemblance (*tashbih*). To inflict such torment on the *Awliya' Allah*... this cannot happen. It is among the impossible things. How can there be torment? Neither illness, nor disease, nor murder, nor plunder, nor neither arrow, nor dagger, nor this, nor that... nothing can happen. Today, the entire Shi'ism that is established, it is on Karbala. This much wailing, this bloody mourning (*khuni matam*) that they do, why do they do this mourning? What, Imam Husayn? The one whose slaves are such prophets... the Husayn whose slaves are such prophets... could they, God forbid, God forbid, kill that Imam Husayn *'alayhi al-salat wa al-salam*?
