Could this Karbala have happened? Today, if this Karbala is taken away from the Shias, then Shi'ism is finished. They are sitting holding onto the entire Karbala, and the Shias are remaining. But what is the reality? But you will say, then what is all this, this Karbala? The grief that we narrate... Of course, we grieve, we do *matam* (mourning). We do *matam* for this reason, look, one must understand the reality properly. We do *matam* for this reason, that the one whom they killed, they killed him thinking he was Husayn. He was not Husayn. But this world thought he was Husayn and killed him. We cry for this reason. If, in reality, God did not want to save him, then they would have actually killed Imam Husayn. But Allah saved him. And with one example in the Qur'an, he clarified the whole matter, solved the entire issue: *wa ma qataluhu wa ma salabuhu wa lakin shubbiha lahum*. Did you understand? Is the point becoming clear? So, in one statement, the entire matter was clarified. Now these are great depths. Then if he is not killed, then how does it happen, what happens, then what about the children, what about them, what about the sick... These are great details. For now, if you suddenly say that I should get everything, it cannot come. But slowly, you will understand. However, you are understanding some part of the matter, that there are some deep matters. Some deep matters. And one is to be an Imam, to be a leader, to become the guide of the whole world, for all people to send blessings and peace upon him, and then for him to be tormented... what, the Prophet *'alayhi al-salat wa al-salam* was tied to a hot stone, stones were thrown at him, this and that was done. God forbid, can such a thing happen to the Mercy to the Worlds (*Rahmat lil 'Alamin*)? Not a chance! The one in whose control divinity is, that servant... you are seeing that the one before whom the entire universe was bowed, that being... could these people inflict harm upon him? Then what happened? Then why did the Prophet say, *ma udhiya nabiyyun mithla ma udhitu* (No prophet was tormented as I was tormented)? If he had not said this, then how would we, as common people, have formed a *sirah* (biography)? How would we receive guidance? For this reason, the Prophet presented the *sirah* of a human being before us. But these are very deep matters. These are very deep matters. This is just the beginning of the time that such things are coming before you, otherwise all these things are hidden secrets (*raz-ha-ye-niha*). This is *'Ilm al-Ladunni* (divinely-inspired knowledge). Very deep secrets. Anyway, for now, I was sitting before you with the story of Janab Adam *'alayhi al-salat wa al-salam*. And it was related to Janab Hunayd, who was your uncle. And he was the Imam of the time, and there in *Tamur*, his point emerged. And first in that era was Janab Hunayd, who came as the Imam. And he appointed his nephew. Now you will say, this relationship... This relationship, these are common things, leave them aside. Leave this matter. It is neither a matter of relation nor of connection. Whoever is worthy, he will come to that place. And you, Janab Adam, who were there... what was his name? His name was Janab 'Abdullah. 'Abdullah was his name, and his father's name was Kanjum, and his grandfather's name was Qauljan. And he was from Shahabad, a resident of an area in Lanka, and Zayqah was the name of his tribe. And he must have had some wife too, Janab Adam. But the Janab Hawwa, Janab Hawwa whose name is said to be your wife, Ummana Hawwa, Ummana Hawwa (our mother Eve), who is that Amma Hawwa? In reality, she is your son Habil, who is also your *wasi* (successor). She is your son Habil, who is also your *wasi* and your caliph, who was made the caliph. And when Janab Adam was being trained, he was studying the *shari'ah*, the *da'wah* was established... the whole... the *dawr-e-kashf* (era of unveiling) was ending, the *dawr-e-satr* (era of concealment) was beginning, and Janab Adam... what happened then? That at that time, Mawlana Hunayd, before his people of *da'wah*... these people of *da'wah* are called *mala'ikah* (angels). *Mala'ikah* means, etymologically, one to whom some task is entrusted is called a *mala'ikah*. *Mala'ikah* does not mean that winged angels are flying around. Yes, the heavenly angels, they are *mala'ikah*. So those who are physical are called *malak*, and the one who... the physical one is called *malik*, and the one who is... is called *malak*. There isn't much difference. And these who were the *mala'ikah*... *wa is qala rabbuka lil-mala'ikati inni ja'ilun fil-ardi khalifah* (And when your Lord said to the angels, 'Indeed, I will make upon the earth a successive authority'). That when Allah Ta'ala said to the *mala'ikah*, 'I want to make my caliph among you.' This was the first voice that echoed. *wa is qala rabbuka lil-mala'ikati inni ja'ilun fil-ardi khalifah*, 'I want to make my caliph on the earth'. Now you see what commotions, what rivers are being made to flow, what speeches, what gatherings... that a caliph is being established, this is... what, Allah's... Allah's representative is being made a human. Look at the personality of a human, and look at the personality of Allah. Where is the connection? What, a caliph is being made? This human who sheds blood, who creates commotion... what, does a human have any standing to become the caliph of Allah? It makes no sense. Then what was the meaning of this, 'becoming a caliph'? 'Allah' there means Janab Hunayd. As I told you, this is a technical term (*istilahi lafz*). Every thing will keep changing. In its own place, it has a spiritual meaning. There, technically, 'Allah' refers to Janab Hunayd, who was the God of the Time. He desired, and he said, 'I want to make my caliph, I want to make someone a prophet and manifest him.' And he pointed towards Janab Adam. Who was your nephew. Now what happened? That when Allah Ta'ala began to prepare Janab Adam, how was the preparation? Allah Ta'ala says about it in the Qur'an Majid, *wa 'allama Adama al-asma'a kullaha* (And He taught Adam the names - all of them). That Adam was taught all the names by Allah Ta'ala. Pick up the commentaries and see. What are all the commentaries filled with? That all the things in the heavens and the earth, the names of all those things were taught to whom? To Janab Adam. Just look at the things, and look at their names, and look at this list... that this is a hat, this is a shoe, this is bread, this is food, this is a curtain, this is a chandelier... these names. Pick up and see the commentaries. So, they say this, that... now if they go into great detail, what do they do? They wrap up their point like this: 'heavens and earth'. What things are there in the heavens and earth? It is just this climate and atmosphere. It is just these things, what else is there? So, the names of all these things were taught. Adam, poor fellow, didn't know. He was told, 'This is a cloud, Adam, this is a pebble, this is a stone, this is bread, this is that, this is a bush...' All this was taught to Janab Adam. When Adam had learned it well... *'allama Adama al-asma'a kullaha*, he learned all the names. Now they were presented... *'aradahum 'alayhim*... and he was presented before the *mala'ikah*, and it was said that, *anbi'uni bi-asma'i ha'ula'* (Inform me of the names of these). O *mala'ikah*, tell me the names. The names that we have told, list those names. *qala la 'ilma lana illa ma 'allamtana* (They said, 'We have no knowledge except what You have taught us'). O Lord, we... *ma 'allamtana illa ma 'allamtana*... our knowledge is only that, O Allah, which you have taught us. Whatever you have taught us, we know that. Now, have you ever seen an exam like this? The *mala'ikah* were not taught. Adam was taught. And then the *mala'ikah* are being asked to tell the names. Is an exam ever like this? The exam happens after the teaching. The poor *mala'ikah*, they were not told. Except for Adam. And the exam is of whom? Of the *mala'ikah*. Let the Muslims answer this. What will they say? And he was asked, 'Tell the names.' So they said plainly, *ma 'ilma lana illa ma 'allamtana*. 'O Lord, whatever knowledge you have given us, we only know that much, we don't know anything besides that'. So Allah Ta'ala said, 'Didn't I tell you correctly that *inni a'lamu ma la ta'lamun* (Indeed, I know that which you do not know)? I know what you do not know'. Look! What anger from Allah! What does this mean? These are all things to be understood. And after that, what happened? When this whole incident took place... *qala lil-mala'ikati sjudu li-Adama* (He said to the angels, 'Prostrate to Adam'). When Adam won and he listed all the names, Allah Ta'ala said... first listen to the story. He... Allah Ta'ala gave the order to the *mala'ikah* for Adam... *sjudu li-Adama* (Prostrate to Adam). 'Prostrate to Adam.' *illa Iblisa aba wa-stakbara wa kana min al-kafirin* (except for Iblis. He refused and was arrogant and became of the disbelievers). And he refused, and... he became of the disbelievers. The one who refused, he was declared a disbeliever, and that's how it happened. This is a strange thing. And all these things... The meaning there is that Adam *'alayhi al-salat wa al-salam* was taught... those 'names' meant the secrets of the *da'wah*. They were the secrets of the *da'wah* which were taught to him. And the matters which are told to those of the rank of prophethood (*nubuwwat*) and messengership (*risalat*), those were taught to him. It is obvious that the *mala'ikah* were not aware of all those secrets. So they said that 'we are not aware of these secrets'. So Janab Hunayd said, 'This is why we say that the one who is worthy has been told, and you do not know'. And now there is a need for the one who knows to always have superiority over the one who does not know. The one who knows has superiority over the one who does not know, always. And he has been chosen for this reason, that he was worthy of it. And you obey him. 'Prostrate' means to obey. The command was to obey. 'Prostrate' did not mean this, to do this prostration. The prostration that is... that is obedience. The command was to obey. 'Obey.' And as soon as the command to obey was given, all the *mala'ikah* said that 'we all prostrated', meaning we obeyed. They said, 'Your command, we accept it with our head and eyes'. You have appointed him, we accept. *aba wa-stakbara wa kana min al-kafirin*. Azazil, who was *Malak al-Mawt* (Angel of Death), who is called *Mu'allim al-Malakut* (Teacher of the Angelic Realm), who had studied the great realities (*haqaiq*), who had said that *khalaqtani min narin wa khalaqtahu min tin* (You created me from fire, and him You created from clay), that I am made of fire and Adam is made of clay. Meaning, I have studied the *haqaiq*, and Adam has studied the *shari'ah*. And you are appointing this *shari'ah*-studying child as a great prophet and messenger, and I was so worthy, I had studied the *haqaiq*... So the Lord of the Universe said, 'The question is not about knowing the *haqaiq* or not knowing them. First was the command to obey. How are you refusing my command?' As soon as he refused the command, he was told, 'Get out from my court. Get out now, *innaka rajim* (you are accursed).' You are the accursed of the *da'wah*. He was expelled from the *da'wah*. From the mission of the *da'wah* and from that place, he was expelled. And that shaytan was expelled, and that shaytan, I am telling you, is a personality. He is a personality. And he was the one who, in the *'Alam-e-Azal* (Pre-Eternal World), was the one who led the group of 'Asir astray. His origin is from there. It was him that *Qudrat* had created. And this was a person named Murrah, and his son was named Harith. I am telling you the name of shaytan. The name of shaytan... his name is Harith, and his father's name is Murrah. This was him. And he did shaytani there, and he came here and did shaytani. And as soon as he did shaytani, he was made accursed of the *da'wah*. Now Janab Adam... now you see, a marvel, that 'he became of the *kafirin*'. *min al-kafirin*. What is the meaning of *kafirin*? *Kafirin* means... *kafir* means one who covers. One who covers. He knew everything, what great status Adam had. But despite that, he covered his status, he hid it. This is the meaning of *min al-kafirin*. You understand? Okay. And then what happened? That Allah Ta'ala says that you... in this garden of paradise, walk, roam, eat the fruits... there are rivers flowing, live with ease and comfort, eat, drink, enjoy. All this that Allah Ta'ala addressed to Adam and Janab Hawwa, and in this way... so Janab Adam, all these things to eat... as I told you, what are these pleasures and all these things? They are books. They are the sciences of the *da'wah*, they are rivers. 'Benefit from these. Benefit from all these things you can eat.' And Janab Adam began to benefit from those things. But what happened? And after that, the command of Allah Ta'ala is coming, look, listen. What is the command of Allah Ta'ala? *wa la taqraba hadhihi al-shajarata fa takuna min al-zalimin* (and do not approach this tree, lest you be among the wrongdoers). 'Look, Adam, do everything, but I am saying this for you and Hawwa'. And who is that Hawwa? The son, Habil, who is your *wasi*. 'I am telling you, beware, do not go near this tree of spirituality, in which the sublime realities are kept'. Those are the hidden secrets of Amir al-Mu'minin. Those are the hidden secrets of the coming Qa'im al-Qiyamah. 'Beware, do not touch these things yet'. 'We want to give you everything, but on its time, not now.' And what happened here? The temptation was so much that Janab Adam and Janab Hawwa... Habil... what did they do? And they ate it. And Allah Ta'ala says, 'If you eat, you will become of the wrongdoers (*zalimin*).' So what happened? Both of them ate the fruit. So now what is it? It is a condition and its consequence. 'If you do this, I will do that.' It means since you did this, I did that. Allah Ta'ala is saying that 'if you eat in this way, you will become of the *zalimin*.' So now, did Janab Adam and Hawwa become *zalimin* or not? And is it obligatory (*farz*) to obey the *zalimin*? Can we, God forbid, obey a wrongdoing prophet? This was the one question... that the great Muslims who had come to Sindh... the questioner asked this question... and they had to flee. This was the question. Tell me. So, the meaning was that there, you will not be among those who do justice (*'adl*). 'Look, it will happen that you will not be able to benefit from those bounties then.' And this is what happened. A command was given for Janab Adam to leave from there. He was with the Imam. He was in the presence of the Imam *'alayhi al-salat wa al-salam*, and Adam was expelled, and his Hawwa, meaning Habil, was also expelled. Now both of them left from there. And they are saying that... mother Hawwa fell in Jeddah, and he fell somewhere on a mountain. What is this... is this some kind of show of throwing from above and a spectacle? These are all stories. Now after that... now this... leaving from there, what happened? They had to come to the islands (*jaza'ir*). The islands (*jazirah*), as you know, I have already told you about the twelve islands where the establishment of faith (*iman*) takes place. And there the people of faith keep being born. They were sent there, that 'go and now endure everything there'. 'Endure hardships, because doing *da'wah* there, doing *da'wah* on the island, is very difficult. The presence of the Imam... there the sun has risen, everything is illuminated, and everything happens by the command of the Imam, and all things are clear.' 'Now this is the darkness of night. The matter of the islands is a very difficult matter. Someone believes, someone doesn't believe, someone is like this, someone is like that... endure the affairs of this tribulation. Now, going there, you people will work in the island, then you will realize.' Adam *'alayhi al-salat wa al-salam* was in the presence of the Imam, but he was removed from the presence and sent to the island. This was the punishment for Janab Adam. And he had to go and work on the island. And he kept working there. Now this... and the one who tormented, who tempted, who did all this, who was he? It was this shaytan. And shaytan... is Azazil, who is called *Mu'allim al-Malakut*, who is the son of a person named Murrah. And he is the same whose origin is from there. He caused mischief there, and he came here and caused mischief and troubled this Adam too. Are you getting the story? So, now when the matter of Janab Adam happened in this way, then Hazrat Adam *'alayhi al-salat wa al-salam*, whose name was Janab 'Abdullah, Janab 'Abdullah established his prophethood and messengership, and as long as your time of service was, you kept serving. Approximately one thousand years had passed. And now, those Imams who were to be in the progeny of Janab Hunayd, were happening one after the other. Their names are also present. Their names are very strange... Farshaj, Yalu... such strange names that you will not be able to understand. Anyway, all such names passed, and all the Imams passed away after Janab Hunayd. Happening, happening, after a thousand years had passed, the Imam who came at that time, what was his name? Mawlana Hud. Hud was his name. A prophet named Hud has also passed. A prophet named Hud has also passed. We are not concerned with that prophet. This is the Imam. And that Imam Hud, who was the Imam of his time, who was from the progeny of Janab Hunayd. He saw that 'I am the Master of the Time (*Sahib-e-Waqt*), the Ruler of the Time (*Aqa-e-Waqt*), the Imam of the Time. Now I need to send a prophet-messenger into the world so that he can go into the world and enforce a *shari'ah* like this, and as a speaking prophet (*natiq nabi*), he can do the work in the world.' So what did he do? He looked in his time and saw, 'Whom should I make now?' So he began to look within his *da'wah*, and looking, he chose one person whose name was 'Abd al-Ghaffar. 'Abd al-Ghaffar was his name. And Janab 'Abd al-Ghaffar, who was of a very old age, was frail. He took this frail elder and said, 'I bestow upon you prophethood and messengership, and now you manifest in the world as a prophet.' So when he came into this world as a prophet... 'coming as a prophet' does not mean coming from above. This whole matter is happening right here. And he came into the world, meaning he came to Sham, or Palestine, or Iraq, wherever he came, and after coming, what did he do? He challenged his people and said, 'Look, I have been made a prophet.' Just as our Prophet gave the command and challenged, in the same way, he said, 'I have been made a prophet. Believe my words, come towards my *shari'ah*, attach yourself to Allah, prepare for the hereafter, turn away from the world.' He began to explain all these things. Now, as soon as Janab Nuh started to explain, what was the situation? The people of Nuh started to argue with him. And this arguing is such a thing... what can be said of a people? Someone instigated them, and the entire people got agitated and started to fight with Janab Nuh. Why? What was happening? In the time of Janab Adam, there were just delusions (*tawahhumat*), only superstitions. But when the time of Nuh came, a thousand years had passed, now symbols (*simbuls*) had been created. Now the inclination towards idol worship had begun. Now the worship of stars had started. Now their inclination was towards such things. And the people of Janab Nuh, what did they do? They started a great commotion and said, 'This is a strange man. He calls us to worship an unseen God.' 'And we will never believe this. We are worshipping our idols with so much effort and worshipping the stars. It is better that we worship these.' As soon as the people started to do this, at that very time, Janab Nuh started to challenge them. And his long and detailed story is present in the Qur'an Majid. If you pick up Surah Nuh and read it, you will find that he tried to call his people, as Janab Nuh says, 'O Allah, the more I call my people near, the farther they run away from me.' 'What should I do, my Allah?' Now to whom is this 'Allah' being addressed? To Janab Hud. Addressing Janab Hud, he is saying, 'My Mawla, what should I do? I am calling them, but my people are not ready to believe.' 'They are not pleased with me. I am tired of explaining to them, but they are not ready to worship you. This people. Now what happened? Janab Nuh... he started to call out so much, he started to lament so much (*nauhe karne lage*), that from his lamentations (*nauhon*), he became Nuh. Did you understand? These are lamentations. From lamentations, Nuh was formed, meaning the one who laments. This was Hazrat Nuh. Otherwise, his name is 'Abd al-Ghaffar. So 'Abd al-Ghaffar, who was known by the name of Janab Nuh, became Nuh by lamenting, lamenting. And he lamented so much that finally, when he saw that the people were not ready to believe, one incident greatly troubled Janab Nuh. One time, Hazrat Nuh was doing some farming. He was farming on a small piece of land. And from there, an old man was passing by, who was carrying his little child in his arms. This story is not in the Qur'an Majid, but its mention is found in other heavenly books. So he was carrying the child and going. As soon as the child saw Janab Nuh, now among the children, what had happened? Janab Nuh had become a plaything and a joke. And to throw stones, to call him mad, to say something or other to him, to call him by some name or other, this had become the pastime of the people, of the children, it had become a game. And he was a frail old man. So the child said to his old father, 'O father, just put me down from your arms. I want to throw a stone at this old man.' So that father said, 'O child, why do you want to throw it now? You are still a child. When you grow up, then you can throw it.' The child said, 'Father, will they even be around until I grow up?' 'They will be finished. My wish will remain unfulfilled, that I couldn't throw a stone. So it's better if I throw it now.' So you see, this was the condition of that people. For this reason, Janab Nuh had become disheartened. He was being stoned, he was being called mad. The Prophet *'alayhi al-salat wa al-salam* was called a poet, a magician, a madman, this and that. This did not just happen to the Prophet; it has happened to every prophet. Hazrat Nuh was also troubled and said, *Rabbi la tadhar 'ala al-ardi min al-kafirina dayyara* (My Lord, leave not upon the earth from among the disbelievers an inhabitant). 'O Lord, now do not leave any of the disbelievers behind. Wipe them all from the face of the earth.' He cursed them. Who? Hazrat Nuh. The extremity of his lament was this, that *Rabbi la tadhar 'ala al-ardi min al-kafirina dayyara*. 'O Lord, do not leave anyone behind now.' 'Do not leave even one of the disbelievers. Wipe them all out, annihilate them.' As soon as this challenge came from Janab Nuh, Janab Hud heard his call and said, 'O Nuh, you have called upon me, so how can I not listen to you? I will definitely listen.' 'It's a good thing, it's a good thing, I am listening to you, and a punishment will definitely befall them. And now a coming punishment will engulf them.' And Janab Hud listened to him. And this was Janab Hud. Look, the first thing you must remember is this, that all the stories (*qisas*) and all the incidents that are in the Qur'an Majid, you should know this about them, that many incidents of Janab Adam, or Nuh, or Ibrahim, or any prophet, have happened in the exoteric (*zahir*) and in the esoteric (*batin*). There are many incidents that happened only in the esoteric and not in the exoteric. There are many incidents that happened only in the exoteric and not in the esoteric. So there are three kinds of incidents. This incident of Janab Nuh, it is an incident that happened in the exoteric and in the esoteric. What happened in the exoteric? That Hazrat Hud gave the command that, 'Nuh, build an ark (*kishti*).' He started to build an ark. Now you see the commotion of the world... 'This ark is coming out, so it's Nuh's ark. That ark is found, it's Nuh's ark. A plank is found there, it's a plank from Nuh's ark.' What will they do with all this? Anyway, Janab Nuh started to build the ark. He built the ark. Now what? He said, 'A flood is coming.' And he said, 'A flood is coming, that's why I am building an ark. Whoever boards it will be saved, and whoever doesn't will be drowned. And for God's sake, you people come into the ark and let me build it.' And Janab Nuh kept building his ark. So it became known that Janab Nuh kept doing a task by the command of his Master. Okay, he kept doing it. So exoterically, this was it. What was it in the esoteric? Hazrat Sam, who is your son, he was your *wasi*. And to accept him as *wasi* and to announce his successorship (*wasayat*)... you did, and you announced that 'after me, my son Sam is the *wasi*'. His brother, his name was Ham. Ham got agitated and said, 'How have you appointed Sam as the *wasi*? This is my right.' A conflict arose between the two brothers, just as it arose there between Habil and Qabil. Adam's two sons, Habil and Qabil. You had made Janab Habil the *wasi*. You had not given the successorship to Qabil, and he became agitated. And what did he do? He presented an offering (*nazar*), and that offering was the sacrifice of a cow. And Habil's was accepted, and Qabil's was not accepted. Upon which, he picked up a stone and hit him, and his head split, and Janab Habil passed away. This is the exoteric story. The esoteric story was that when Janab Adam made Habil, his son, who had also been your teacher, his caliph, then when you took over the caliphate, Qabil could not bear it and wanted to kill you, that he should snatch away that appointment (*nass*) and stop your *da'wah* that was happening. So 'to pass away', 'to kill' means what? To stop from the *da'wah*. To stop from calling towards Allah, this is the meaning. So just as it happened there, in the same way, here Ham, what did he do? He said, 'No, brother. There is no need to kill Janab Nuh.' And he was his own son. And the situation was that Janab Nuh was explaining to whom? To Ham. The disbelieving son. Now what happened when the ark was ready? The exoteric story. Listen to the exoteric story. The flood came, and the flood emerged from the mosque of Kufa. That place exists even today, from where the flood of Nuh emerged. *Tannur*. From that oven (*tannur*), the water came out. And that water is still present today. And after it came out, what happened? It drowned the whole world, that water. And as all... you see that... believe in all things, and the flood of Nuh came. And after the flood came, the ark of Janab Nuh sailed. Now, before the flood of Janab Nuh, a command was given, 'O Nuh, from every pair, you take them here. If all these get drowned, what will remain of creation?' Did you understand? So what did Janab Nuh do? A pair of elephants, a pair of camels, a pair of lions, a pair of tigers, a pair of snakes... all good and bad animals, you gathered them. Now the ark of Janab Nuh is sailing, having gathered all the animals. Does your intellect even accept that he gathered the animals and left? So there, for Janab Nuh, the command to gather the animals was this: 'Look, in your *da'wah*, there are some with an Islamic form and some with a faithful form. Some are a bit exoteric, some are understanding the esoteric very well. Take both of these.' 'This pair-pair, you should keep them here so that from the faithful root, faith may also enter into them.' This was it. 'From your *da'wah*, you should not only take the people of faith into your ark, do not do this. Take the people of Islam too.' And what happens is that what is its pair, its quality (*sifat*) is always there. The quality of bravery that you have, this is your pair. Your pair does not mean that your female, your wife, is your pair. That is just an exoteric pair. But your real pair is your quality. You understand? So... and you see, more than anything else is this matter. Today, all the Muslims believe that he took the pairs and gathered the animals. Okay, fine, he took the animals. Brother, tell me, what was the wisdom in this? Let any Muslim give the answer. What was the wisdom in this, that he took so many animals and wanted to save them, Janab Nuh? Was it by the command of the Lord or not? Yes, brother, it was by the command of Allah, and by his command, he took the pairs. Well, if it was by the command of Allah, then is Allah not *innallaha 'ala kulli shay'in qadir* (Indeed, Allah is over all things competent)? Is Allah all-powerful or not? When he has the power, could he not create them again? Why was this command given, 'Fill this ark and sink the ark with the weight'? Why was the command given? Does Allah not have the power to create them again? And if this ark was sailing for six months, as it is in all the traditions, then how much fodder would be needed for six months? And all animals eat different things. Where did it come from? Is this a matter of some sense? This is not it at all. So the matter was this, that he gathered people from his *da'wah* and set off. And the ark reached Judi, and there you gave the command for a fast, and this is all the exoteric story. The esoteric story is that a crisis came in the *da'wah*, and Ham started to oppose you. Exoterically, when Ham... when the ark was sailing, Ham... you called out to him, he had climbed a mountain. The Qur'an Majid describes this. And you, Janab Nuh, called out, 'O Ham, you come too. Look, this mountain... and he said, 'No, the mountain is enough to give me refuge. You go, with the ark. I am not coming into the ark.' Meaning, he was telling him, 'Nuh, look, accept your brother Sam. He is my *wasi*.' But Ham was not believing. You said, 'Look, if you don't believe, you will be... drowned.' And what happened? Despite being on the mountain, meaning he remained firm in his own knowledge, but he was drowned. Meaning, his knowledge was of no use, and he was not capable of answering anyone. Meaning, he was drowned in his own knowledge. His knowledge was nothing at all. The real knowledge was *'Ilm al-Ladunni*, which was with Janab Sam. This is the incident of Janab Nuh, which happened to Janab Nuh, and Janab Nuh proceeded in this way. So now, in what manner have these people presented this incident? How have the Muslims seen it? They have seen the flood of Nuh in this way, and they have seen the matters in this way, and neither did they understand the *da'wah*, nor the refusal of the *da'wah*, nor the affirmation of the *da'wah*. They did not understand any part of the matter properly. So now, Hazrat Nuh, who had become Nuh by lamenting, lamenting... and Hazrat Nuh, whose name was 'Abd al-Ghaffar, he had reached the limit in his teaching (*talqin*). He was constantly teaching, he was explaining to his community, he was constantly trying to bring them to the right path, but the believers were not believing. But having become weary, what did Janab Nuh do? Finally, you... called for the divine punishment. Due to which this divine punishment came. *Rabbi la tadhar 'ala al-ardi min al-kafirina dayyara*. 'O Allah, now do not leave any of the disbelievers behind.' And thus, the ghat was prepared. What does it mean to 'prepare the ghat'? It means this, that 'O Allah, the forms you have given them, as humans, they are not worthy of being humans now, O Lord.' 'Put them back to death and keep them aside. And now there is no need to bring them into the form of humans. Bring them later. They are not going to be straightened out now.' Allah Ta'ala accepted his word, and they were drowned. So this was the incident of Hazrat Nuh *'alayhi al-salat wa al-salam*, and this was the story of Hazrat Nuh. And Hazrat Hud was the Imam of that time, and the Master of that Time, and Janab Nuh was his... his messenger, his prophet, who came. Now the matters of the initial *shari'ah*... Janab Adam was given the initial *shari'ah* by Janab Hunayd, the Imam *'alayhi al-salat wa al-salam*, his uncle. And he had explained that 'look, you should adhere to all these things.' So the beginning is always unique. It is not that it will be a completely formed shape, just as we have the complete law, the complete forms of worship, and all things, it will be like that. It was not like that. It was an initial form. Perhaps a few things he had told for prayer, for fasting. Fasting was certainly there. In the time of Janab Nuh, there was fasting, and in the time of Janab Adam, there was fasting. And prayer was also present. Prayer is such an obligation of Islam that it has been established from the very beginning. But its forms have kept changing. Its forms have changed in the era of every prophet. We have no mention of what its forms were then. But as we see, in the time of Hazrat 'Isa, there are mentions of kneeling down, so these are forms. And the methods of worship have kept changing. But its complete form came with the Master of the Universe, the Prophet *'alayhi al-salat wa al-salam*, and you codified it and organized the religion. But before that, there was no such situation. But gradually, slowly, the situations developed. So I was telling you that now, in the story of Hazrat Nuh, only one matter remains, and that is his blessed age. Now regarding his blessed age, what Allah Ta'ala has said in the Qur'an Majid, that he was 900 years old... in reality, what is that? Was Hazrat Nuh's age 900 years? You just see, a person's age is 900... and if he goes above 100, they will say, 'May Allah grant him a quick death, that would be better.' What is the use? Neither are the eyes capable of seeing, nor are the intestines capable of digesting. For what reason? So just as this situation... 100-125 years is a lot, take 150 years. Now this age of 900 years, what is the meaning of this? So Allah Ta'ala, why did he mention it? The matter was this: that is your... your era, your period. It is your period, which was approximately a thousand years...

His descendants, whose name, Maulana 'Uzayr's descendant's name was 'Uzr. He was the one who, after him... and the chain continued after 'Uzr. And here, Hazrat Musa had appointed Janab Harun as his khalifa, had made him his vasi, and a strange thing was this, that on several occasions it happened, in the 124,000 anbiya', that the people raised the issue of election and wanted to take the election into their own hands, that we want to elect. This was also spoken of in the time of Hazrat Musa, and they took the election into their own hands. But that was a strange kind of election, that even after holding the election, they... Hazrat Musa had such great influence that they did not tell him their name, but Janab Musa had given them signs. And they held the election, and this incident, they elected the very one whom Hazrat Musa wanted, meaning Harun. Harun, and they were chosen. And after Harun, his descendants, who were... whom... whom Janab Musa had placed reliance upon after him. But after a little while, Janab Musa who... they made his nephew his successor. Now, in this way, the chain of nubuwwat continued in its place, several anbiya' passed, and from above, the chain of a'imma continued, who are the Aqa, who are the Malik, who are the rabb-i dawr, who are the sahib-i waqt, and their chain continued. Maulana 'Uzr came, after him his descendants came. As this chain continued, it reached Maulana Khuzaima. Maulana Khuzaima, who is among the anbiya' of Allah, Janab Khuzaima saw that 1,000 years had passed, but now an even better nabi should be sent, and one who is natiq, and who serves the qiyamullah, and comes to do the work in the world, and he should be a sahib-i kitab nabi (prophet with a book). So Maulana Khuzaima's gaze fell upon Hazrat 'Isa. Now, first of all, the issue is the paida'ish (birth) of Hazrat 'Isa and the wiladat (birth) of Hazrat 'Isa, that matter, that was the most important, for him to be born, then to grow up, to receive ta'lim-o-tarbiyat (education and training), to become worthy of being chosen for the rank of nubuwwat and risalat. This was the biggest problem. Now, the fact of the matter was that at that time, when the era of Hazrat Musa was ending, Zakariyya Nabi, who was a lesser prophet, whose zikr (mention) is in Surah Maryam. Surah Maryam begins with the zikr of Janab Zakariyya. And Allah has praised Janab Zakariyya greatly. A very blessed zikr has been made by Allah in the Qur'an-i Majid of Janab Zakariyya Nabi, that he was such an 'abid-o-zahid (worshipper and ascetic), Janab Zakariyya, that Zakariyya'l-mihrab (Zakariyya of the prayer niche) became famous. The mihrab got its name from him, that he would always remain in the mihrab, engaged in 'ibadat-guzari (worshipfulness) and du'a (prayer) and munajat (supplication). Janab Zakariyya. So, this Hazrat Zakariyya, he was za'if (old), and he had no aulad (children). And he, being related to the Al-i 'Imran, said, "O Allah, I wished I had a son who would be my waris (heir), and who... but what can I do, I have become za'if, and my hair has turned white, and so I... and there is no such thing as having hope for a child now. And my wife has also become old." At that time, Allah gave a nida (call) and said that "Why are you so sad, O Zakariyya? Allah will grant you a ghulam (boy), will grant a son, who will be your successor, and who... " So, Hazrat Zakariyya was given a son, and this very son's name was Yahya. This is the very same Janab Yahya who is buried in the mosque of the Bani Umayya in Sham (Syria), and his tomb is there. And that is such a pak-o-pakiza (pure and holy) mosque that its founders were not such good people, the Bani Umayya, but that mosque is very noble, for this reason that it contains tremendous aasar (relics). Among those aasar, the greatest effect is that Janab Yahya's maqbara (tomb) is there, in the middle of the mosque. And the two minarets you see are where the Ahl al-Bayt were made to stand when they were brought to the court of Yazid. So those places where Janab Imam Zayn al-'Abidin and the other Ahl al-Bayt were brought and made to stand, those places have been elevated. So now, all the ahl al-tashayyu', the Shi'a people, when they go to that mosque, they go to those very places to perform their 'ibadat and pray. And though for us the entire mosque is blessed, those places where the Ahl al-Bayt sat are the most blessed of places. So, the point was that Hazrat Yahya was his son, for whom the command came in the Qur'an-i Majid, "O Yahya, take the kitab (book) with quwwat (strength)." Meaning, you, the kitab that has been given to you, you should establish its shari'at with full power. So, through ilham (inspiration), he was given a kitab, and that kitab was... by Yahya. And because he was not a natiq nabi or a mursal nabi, his zikr is not made with the same frequency as Musa, 'Isa, and Janab Ibrahim. Now, in the matter of Hazrat Zakariyya, it happened that Janab Maryam is mentioned, and she is called ukht-i Harun (sister of Harun). That she was Harun's sister. Now, this is a historical matter, and I don't have the direct reference for what it is, but it's possible she was the daughter of 'Imran. But she had a special relationship with Janab Zakariyya, or it was certainly the case that Janab Zakariyya raised her. He definitely raised and nurtured her. And just as Janab Zakariyya would sit in the mihrab and perform 'ibadat, Hazrat Maryam, when she was born, she was in his care, and so she would also be seated in the mihrab and perform 'ibadat, just like Janab Zakariyya. Now, the fact of the matter is that this Maryam of Zakariyya, who would sit there, read, and pray, she became famous as Maryam-i Zakariyya. And in that same era, there was another Maryam, and she was Maryam-i Magdalaniyyah (Mary Magdalene), who is called... so that Maryam-i Magdalaniyyah was a separate person, and she was... What happened was that Allah, where He intended to describe in the Qur'an, has mentioned Maryam-i Zakariyya but intended Maryam-i Magdalaniyyah. Now, you see, what happens is, as I said, a mughalata (misconception) occurs there. Now you would say, how can this be? But it happens, it is Allah's word. And for this very reason, Allah said from the beginning: `f-as'alu ahl al-zikr in kuntum la ta'lamun` (so ask the people of remembrance if you do not know). Ask the ahl al-zikr if you do not know. If you don't understand, ask the ahl al-zikr. The ahl al-zikr meant the people of the Qur'an, who were the Ahl al-Bayt. They were the Ahl al-Bayt of the Rasul. Meaning, they were the masters of ta'mur (esoteric interpretation). But they didn't try to ask them. They started asking others besides the Ahl al-Bayt of the Rasul, and whoever's qiyas (analogy) came to mind, they explained it in that way. So this was a wrong thing. They were supposed to ask the ahl al-zikr, but they didn't ask. Because of this, they went astray, and the matter became corrupted. In any case, the fact was that in that era, there was a Maryam who was... and she was Maryam-i Magdalaniyyah, whom they call [unclear]. And that Maryam was in her own place. And so... Now, this matter of Hazrat 'Isa, Ruhullah (Spirit of God), whom they call the spirit of God. After all, why? Was he superior to our prophet that he was called Ruhullah? Hey, there was Kalimullah, there was Khalilullah, you could have called them something too. But what was the reason for calling him Ruhullah? The reason was that Hazrat 'Isa alayhi-s-salatu wa-s-salam's mother was not touched by any human. And because she was called the Virgin Mary, and from her, Hazrat 'Isa was born (tawallud), for this reason they say that Allah had infused his nafs (spirit/breath) into her, blew his spirit into her, so he became Ruhullah. So, this is what became famous, and indeed, this was the zahir-i ta'wil (apparent interpretation) because of which he became famous as Ruhullah. And what was the second thing? He was called Masih. Why was he called Masih? Because he used to travel a lot (siyahat). He used to wander a lot, he wouldn't stay in one place, and he would keep moving from here to there, to there, to there. That's why one who travels a lot is called Masih. So Masih was his name, and Ruhullah was his name, Hazrat 'Isa's. And Janab Maryam, from whom 'Isa's wiladat (birth) was to take place, who was she in reality? She was Maryam-i Zakariyya. It is Maryam-i Zakariyya who was a very devout woman and held a very high rank. Just as Maulana Fatima asked Sayyidna Nabi, "My rank, what is it? And you say about Janab Maryam that she was the sardar (leader) of the women of all the worlds, then what is my rank?" She asked Sayyid al-Anam, the master of the universe, "What is my rank?" He said: "She is sayyidat nisa' al-'alamin (leader of the women of the worlds), while Maryam is sayyidat nisa' al-'alam-i ha (leader of the women of her world). Maryam was the leader of the women of her time, you are the leader of the women of all creation." You understand? Now, this Janab Maryam who was the leader of the women of her time, she was Maryam-i Zakariyya. She was of a very high rank ('ali-darja), a very esteemed ('ali-qadr) lady. And it happened to her that the Lord of the worlds sent wahi (revelation) to her. The wahi was revealed in such a way that a farishta (angel) came down with the wahi, and this is mentioned in the Qur'an-i Majid, that the angel came to Janab Maryam and started saying to her, "I have come to you so that a son may be born to you." She said, "What kind of thing are you saying to me? No human has touched me, nor have I... done anything. And how can you say this?" He said, "I am not saying this from myself, I am saying this on behalf of God. I am telling you from the Qur'an. I am telling you this on behalf of God. I have brought this news, this basharat (glad tidings), to you. And Allah wants a son to be born to you, and I have appeared to give you this good news." Obviously, the angel wasn't talking about marrying her or anything, but it was the infusion of the spirit (nafs-i ruh) into Janab Maryam of Janab 'Isa, and that angel gave this good news on behalf of Allah, and Hazrat 'Isa was born (tawallud). And... So what was the real matter? I am now telling you its key. Listen and understand. That she was, in the language you know and understand, an umm-i zakar (mother of the male principle), Janab Maryam was. And in the ta'mur, the station she had, Hazrat 'Isa's, the effect that was falling from there, of the muhtajib (veiled one)... the muhtajib of Hazrat 'Isa... I told you about nisbat-i adna (lower relation) and nisbat-i a'la (higher relation), you should understand that well. The effect of Hazrat 'Isa, that effect was established here. Where? At Maryam-i Zakariyya's. That effect came here. And that effect, obviously, is not something that has to enter the sulb-o-raham (loins and womb). The thing that enters the sulb-o-raham, which one is it? I have already told you that it is our Namiya, which comes out from the father's sulb, and after mingling in the [unclear], after falling, after coming into the [unclear], after mixing, it comes into the mother's womb and is born. So, the thing that comes through the process of tanasul (procreation) is that. But here, the effect that came, the very first effect, was held by Janab Maryam, and she nurtured that effect with her own being. That effect's name is 'Isa. Do you understand? Please pay attention. The name of that effect, for now, if you don't understand, just accept this much: the name of that effect is Janab 'Isa, and that effect was being nurtured (parwarish) by Janab Maryam-i Zakariyya. And after that, when the angel told her, "O Maryam, if people come and ask you where this boy came from, then you say that I am fasting for Allah today." `lan ukallima 'l-yawma insiyya` (I will not speak to any human today). I... `samtum li 'r-rahman` (I have vowed a fast to the Most Merciful). I have kept a fast for Allah, and today I will not speak to any human. So, it used to be a fast of silence. So Hazrat Maryam was instructed by Allah that, "You say that I am fasting today, I will not speak to anyone." And the people will go on their way, you won't need to give any explanation, and Allah will protect you. Apparently, this is the whole story. And that was not a matter of sulb-o-raham, not a matter of wiladat. It was a matter of nurturing an effect. Janab Maryam fulfilled that duty. But then, that thing was handed over to whom? To Maryam-i Magdalaniyyah. Do you understand? It was handed over to Maryam-i Magdalaniyyah. And at Maryam-i Magdalaniyyah's, just as all children are born, in that same way, Hazrat 'Isa was born (tawallud). Where? At Maryam-i Magdalaniyyah's. At Maryam-i Magdalaniyyah's, Hazrat 'Isa was born, just as every child is born. And not without a father, rather her husband, Janab Maryam's husband's name was Yusuf, who was a carpenter. Joseph the Carpenter was there, and he was the husband of Maryam-i Magdalaniyyah. And her son was Janab 'Isa. He was the one who was first nurtured by Janab Maryam-i Zakariyya. Fine. Now when Hazrat 'Isa was born to Maryam here, the community started to gossip. What happened was that she too was commanded to hide her husband's name, and she concealed it... that her husband's name should be hidden. The real matter is what? It is that with us, we often see that if the husband is a very well-known person, the child is known more by his father's name. And if the mother is very well-known, famous, and distinguished, then he becomes known by his mother's name. Like, say, [unclear] Elizabeth's son, is known by her name. Her husband was Prince Philip, nobody knows him by that. It was the same kind of situation here, that the Janab Yusuf was an ordinary believer, a common believer, counted among the common believers, so for that reason he was of no account, he wasn't considered significant. And Janab Maryam was... he wasn't brought into the limelight in any special way. In any case, it was concealed. Now what happened was that the community, you know how women are and how communities are. The community started saying that "how has she conceived? This girl was unmarried, and now a child has even been born, this is a terrible thing, what is this uproar?" And the Qur'an has described this in detail. And the community came and started saying, "O Maryam, your father was not such a bad man, he was a very noble man, a very good man. And your brother, Janab Harun, was also a very good man." The Qur'an is saying this. And all this was there, "So where did this child come from to you? How did you acquire this fault?" Now Janab Maryam said, "What do I know? I will not give any answer today. Yes, you can ask this child, the child will give you the answer." Just as God had instructed her, Maryam-i Magdalaniyyah, she said the same thing. And the community went towards the cradle. They came to the cradle of Janab 'Isa and started saying, "O child, tell us, what your mother is saying, what is the matter?" So the Qur'an testifies, Allah says in the Qur'an-i Sharif, that there in the cradle, the newborn child said, "I am Abdullah, `atani al-kitaba wa-ja'alani nabiyya` (He has given me the Book and made me a prophet)." "I am a servant of God. Allah has given me a book and made me a prophet." This testimony that the child gave, they were astonished. That a newborn child doesn't speak. This child is speaking. And not only is he speaking, the amazing thing is that he's talking like a prophet. He's saying, "I have become a prophet, and Allah has given me a book." It was a very astonishing thing. They expressed their surprise and said, "O Janab Maryam, this is a very strange and wondrous thing. We have never seen or heard such a thing." The whole community left, surprised and bewildered, and Janab Maryam was saved. Now, Hazrat Maryam's condition was that she was hungry, and taking her child, she went outside. And going out, she said, "O Lord, I have come out with my child in search of food." And Allah sent a wahi to Janab Maryam, "You, the date palm that is in front of you, just shake it. Fresh ripe dates will fall for you, `rutaban janiyya`, and from it you can eat your fill and drink its water." "This is your first meal, which you will give to this child." So, she shook the dates down and acquired them from it. The real matter was what? These dates and all were the ma'jizat (miracles) that were for Janab 'Isa, and all these things were happening. And Hazrat 'Isa was now growing up. And as Hazrat 'Isa was growing, over here Janab Zakariyya's son, Janab Yahya, was also growing. Now both of them started to grow. As Hazrat 'Isa grew older, over here Janab Yahya also started to grow. And having grown up, Hazrat 'Isa, before him, he read many books and acquired a lot of 'ilm (knowledge). After acquiring 'ilm, there were indications from the Imam of the Time to Janab 'Isa, "Go, 'Isa, and try to acquire some ta'lim (teaching)." And he went and acquired ta'lim from whom? From Janab Yahya. From Janab Yahya bin Zakariyya, Janab 'Isa acquired ta'lim. And 'Isa kept studying. And Yahya's four years of education were completed. And it's a very strange educational method of his too, that regarding the alphabet 'alif, ba, ta, tha', he asked strange questions: what is before 'alif', what is before 'ba', what is that and that? So, it was a very strange style of questioning and reading, and of Janab Yahya's teaching. In any case, those common things passed, and from that school, as an ustad (teacher), he gave that ta'lim. And when Hazrat 'Isa completed his education in his place... ...then Hazrat Imam, Janab Khuzaima, now gave a nida (call) to Janab 'Isa, "O 'Isa, we were choosing you for risalat-o-nubuwwat (messengership and prophethood), and we saw this 'ilm in you, and we want to make you a sahib-i kitab nabi (prophet with a book) and entrust you with the duties of risalat-o-nubuwwat." This message that Hazrat 'Isa received from Janab Khuzaima... before this, in the incidents, it has been told how a young man goes out to earn his livelihood, and his mother said, "You are becoming old, and now that I am young, I should go and earn something, so that I can make a living..." So he went to an Englishman, who used to dye clothes, and took up a job there. Hazrat 'Isa. And he went to the dyer and said, "I want to work for you." He said, "That's a good thing. I have a job of dyeing clothes." He said, "What is there to do?" He said, "This is the tub, this is the dye, this is how you have to dye the clothes, and here is the dye and all the clothes mixed together, and like this..." Hazrat 'Isa, on the very first day, performed a spectacle: he mixed all the dyes, mixed all the clothes, and then, doing a spectacle, he separated the dye and all the clothes were colored. And that master said, "You, on the very first day, have caused such a loss. I... how will I teach you this trade? After all, what... you have ruined the whole business. The business of dyeing has been turned upside down. After all, what is this?" So Hazrat 'Isa said, "You... if you doubt my skill, then whichever color you tell me, I will give you the cloth in that color." He said, "This cloth was red, this cloth was this, this cloth was yellow." So Hazrat 'Isa would dip it in, and as he pulled it out, the cloth would be colored that way. So this was the first 'ejaz (miracle) of Hazrat 'Isa that you showed. And that dyer was astonished and said, "This is a great miracle-working elder." And after that, these were the initial, initial things, the light that was shining in Hazrat 'Isa, and after that Janab Khuzaima appointed him his da'i and entrusted him with nubuwwat (prophethood). Now, when he was entrusted with nubuwwat, after being entrusted, there is a style of expression. Just like today, how many Muslims are there who call upon Allah with the word "Miyan" (master). Some call him "Tu" (you, informal). This is a style of love. So everyone calls upon Allah in different ways. Some say "Allah Jalla Jalaluhu", some say "Miyan". Some say "are, tu" (hey, you). So, it's a style. In the same way, Hazrat 'Isa had a style, that he would call upon Janab Khuzaima, and how would he call? "O father." "Fadir, Fadir" he would call. "Father, father" he would call. And what did the people understand? That 'Isa is calling that Allah... And what did the people understand? That 'Isa is calling that Allah, who neither begets nor is begotten, he is calling him and saying "father". You understand? And when people would ask Hazrat 'Isa, "Who are you to him?" He would say, "I am his son." It happens that the one who performs `nas` (infusion of spiritual rank) is the father, and the one upon whom `nas` is performed is the son. With us, this system is eternal, it is established from eternity, and it will remain until Qayamat. Always, the one who performs `nas` is the father, and the one upon whom `nas` is performed is the son. He is the sababi (causal) son. Whether he is a nasabi (lineal) son or not is a different matter, but he definitely becomes a sababi son. So when he becomes a sababi son, it was in that sense that Janab 'Isa would say, "I am the son, he is the father. I am his son." He was not saying anything wrong. But what is to be done when the community misunderstands? Hey, good sir. And they would say, "You show great 'ejazat (miracles), you do these things, how are you doing all this?" Hazrat 'Isa wouldn't say much about it, he wouldn't try to make people understand. And when you would go anywhere, as is mentioned in the Qur'an, you would pay attention to the sick and make them well. The abraṣ (leper) and akmah (born blind), as mentioned in the Qur'an, those kinds of patients, incurable patients who were brought, you would place your hand on them and recite a prayer, and they would become well and healthy. And seeing these 'ejazat (miracles), people were becoming believers. And just as every nabi was given some mu'jiza (miracle), so Hazrat 'Isa was given this mu'jiza. And with this mu'jiza, he was doing his work, and people were gathering around him. And they were saying that this person is doing such great work, giving shifa (healing) and making the sick well, what greater work can there be? And they started following Janab 'Isa. In this way, 'Isaiyyat (Christianity) was spreading. And they saw that Hazrat 'Isa alayhi-s-salatu wa-s-salam is doing this work, so they started saying, "Hazrat 'Isa, you sometimes become mustaghraq (absorbed/engrossed), a light descends upon you, what is this matter?" Hazrat 'Isa said, "My father sends the ruh al-qudus (the Holy Spirit) upon me." "He sends down the ruh al-qudus." What is the ruh al-qudus? It is Jibril. It is wahi. Ruh al-qudus, wahi, all these words, what are they essentially? They are different names for Jibril's, the wahi's, various methods. Upon him, through him, those things would come. Janab Khuzaima was in his place, and nubuwwat had been conferred, and the work was continuing. And the most important things that were coming were from the injil (Gospel). The book, the Bible, that was being sent to you, and Janab 'Isa was constantly compiling and transcribing the Bible. And he was telling his people, the hawariyyun (disciples). Who were the hawariyyun? They were Yunus, Andubas, Lut, Fitras (Peter), whom they call Peter, Fitras. And there are many names, who were Greek. These were your hawari, Hazrat 'Isa's, who were with you and would note down those things and obey your commands. But what happened was that, because Allah willed it so, that the book that would remain for all creation until Qayamat, if any book remains, it is the Qur'an-i Majid. Other books, there is not as much need for them for that community, just as you understand, if a person is sick, and the sick person goes to a doctor, the doctor gives him a prescription according to his illness and treats him, and the patient gets well. But that prescription is no longer valid. Now, if another patient comes, say after two years, his illness has changed, a cough has developed, new things have developed, obviously he will write a new prescription. That old prescription will not be effective now, because the illness has increased or changed. If he comes a third time, there will be a third prescription. In the same way, the anbiya' came in their own places to every ummah (community), and seeing the illness of the ummah, these spiritual physicians, the anbiya', would treat them. But here what happened was that these prescriptions kept changing. And the Lord of the worlds had made a promise regarding these prescriptions: `inna nahnu nazzalna 'z-zikra wa inna lahu la-hafizun` (Indeed, it is We who sent down the Remembrance, and indeed, We will be its guardian). "Hey, this Qur'an-i Majid, We have revealed it, and We will protect it." This book would have been erased, God forbid, God forbid, the Qur'an would have been erased, such incidents had happened before. But the Lord of the universe, Amir al-Mu'minin, who were its protectors, they saved it. They saved it and kept it exactly as it was (`min-wa-'an`), without letting any alterations happen to it. Its protection was constantly done by God. `Inna lahu la-hafizun` (Indeed, We will be its guardian), Allah says, "We are its protectors." And He always protected it. But for these other books, there was no such promise of protection. After all, what was the reason for this? The reason was that their planes (dawa'ir), their point of descent (sutur), the place where they descended, was a lower place. This Torah, Injil, Suhuf-i Ibrahim, Suhuf-i Musa, Suhuf-i 'Isa, all these things that were coming were from the lower planes (sutur). But the thing that was coming from the 'aql-i awwal (the First Intellect), from the 'aql-i awwal the thing that was coming, from the sijill-i ilahi (the Divine Scroll), that was the Qur'an-i Majid. The anwar-i jibriyya (the lights of Gabriel) that were coming from it, they were from where? From the 'aql-i awwal. This is a book that will not be abrogated. That is why it was said that this religion will remain until Qayamat. Its naskh (abrogation) is not certain. That's why no one can change it. And that's why Allah took upon Himself the responsibility of its protection. So, the point was that because Allah had not given a guarantee for those, that's why the Bible was not protected and it was changed. And you see today in the [unclear] the matter is that no one can claim that this is the same original Bible that was with Janab 'Isa. No. It's possible that some things are there, but one has to search and find them. There are many interpolations, many things. No one can say. Just as the name 'Aziz, and the name of Allah, and the name of Janab Khuzaima, it cannot be erased. It cannot be, because they themselves say that it is not. So it became known that its protection was not guaranteed. That prescription was for that time, and it ended. That's why that happened, but it's not like that with the Qur'an-i Majid. And until Qayamat, it will remain protected. Now, the matter is that when Janab 'Isa alayhi-s-salatu wa-s-salam was entrusted with risalat, he, as a rasul (messenger), started to preach. And the first thing he preached was about asceticism. That it is better that we leave our homes and become absorbed in the worship of Allah. We should adopt great taqwa (piety). We should be completely detached from the world. And it was a kind of ruhbaniyyat (monasticism), the style he had. Ruhbaniyyat in its true meaning, which is to be completely cut off from the world, it wasn't exactly that. The meaning was that, being separate from home and family, you should worship Allah in seclusion. This is what you were preaching. And you would always say that you should keep yourselves in a state of fasting for Allah and constantly give zakat. He would give great importance to the obligation of zakat. He would command fasting. He would command namaz (prayer), just as namaz was commanded to us. He would teach and definitely perform namaz. This is the preaching you were doing. And the things that were permissible, the things that were forbidden, the matters that were there, these, because for you the era of Hazrat Musa is distant. The era of Hazrat Ibrahim is even more distant. The era of Hazrat Adam is very far away. That's why the details of their shari'at did not reach. But the details of Hazrat Nuh's time reached, that in his time this was permissible, this was not permissible. This is a temporary thing. Permissible and impermissible, I have already told you, that it is connected to different places and times. If those things are there, this will be haram. If those things are not there, this will not be haram. In any case, there are channels, different channels. If it is possible, if God wants to open it, He opens it. If He wants to close it, He closes it. But who knows that it is opened or closed, besides the nabi? The nabi will tell us that this channel has been opened, this channel has been closed. For example, I'll tell you. Today, with you, I will mention such a thing that you will be a little surprised. That you know what things are halal. You know very well. And what things are haram, you know very well. But you know that the rabbit is also halal. You know that people eat rabbit, it is halal. But I am telling you that just now, a matter of a few hundred years ago, it has been made haram, the rabbit. Why? Because within that channel, some such things are coming that it has been said from above, "Look, it is better to stop this." Because we believe in them, `Ati'ullaha wa-ati'u 'r-rasula wa-uli 'l-amri minkum` (Obey Allah, and obey the Messenger, and those in authority among you), so we obey them, and they are telling us that they are seeing certain things in the channel and that's why they... So... you will say, how did this happen? It happens by chance. Things happen in the channel. Sometimes such things come that they see and immediately give the command, and from then on it becomes haram. So, in any case, Hazrat 'Isa alayhi-s-salatu wa-s-salam was saying "father, father," he was calling out to Janab Khuzaima. And Janab Khuzaima, you would remember him, and you would call upon your rabb (Lord), your malik (Master), your aqa (Master), your Imam, and you would call him by the name of "father." Now, the greatest mu'jiza (miracle) of Hazrat 'Isa that happened was raising the dead. That raising of the dead happened in such a way that Sam'un as-Safa was with you, and you, it's a famous story, that when a dead man was brought to you, and people were crying and weeping a lot, that he was young and this happened, he died, and the circumstances are such, how will we manage... In such special circumstances, Janab 'Isa would give them consolation, and he raised that dead man, but in seven days he raised him. It took seven days for you to raise him. You would recite words over him, and after that he would get life, but after seven days he would be raised. Hazrat 'Isa. And this matter, where does it come in history? When the Lord of the universe, Amir al-Mu'minin, a slain man whose head was separate and body was separate, and in Kufa they had buried him, you raised him. Whose name was [unclear] Budrayqa. When you raised Budrayqa, at that time you had said, "O people, that was 'Isa who would raise the dead in seven days, and they would... I am the wasi of the nabi, and I am 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, and I am... from Allah, I have come as a qiyamullah, and I will say 'qum bi-idhnillah' (rise by the permission of God), and watch, he will get up." You hadn't even said `qum bi-idhnillah` yet that he got up and sat down. This is what Hazrat 'Ali had shown, and all the people of Kufa saw it. There are many miracles. And today you have heard the details of the 'Alawite sciences. You have heard all those stories. You have heard all those accounts. You have heard all those details that I have narrated before you regarding Amir al-Mu'minin. There is no limit or count to the Master's words. That is why it has come in the Qur'an-i Majid that if all the trees, all the trees in the universe, are made into pens, and the entire ocean is made into ink, and the words of my Lord are written, the words of my Lord, Allah's words, will not be exhausted. In reality, what is the meaning of "words of my Lord"? Allah, who is that being who cannot be encompassed, what will we say about His essence? Hey, all those things will be contained in the material. And they will be contained in the human potential. And whose is that human potential? It is Amir al-Mu'minin 'Ali's. That your virtues are such. And that is why, regarding the Lord of the universe, it was said... ...that regarding Amir al-Mu'minin 'Ali, if someone praises him, and in front of you people, it is Hazrat Paighambar alayhi-s-salatu wa-s-salam who said it. "Remember, do not belie it if you do not understand it. Do not belie him." You should see the level of 'ilm that if it doesn't enter our understanding, the Nabi's command is to not belie it. It may not enter your understanding. But those are the virtues of 'Ali. Whose virtues can be, O God, whose praises can be? How can there be an appraisal of the Lord of the worlds? From whom can there be an appraisal of the Master of existence? Hey, whose servants, whose slaves, are these anbiya-i kiram, Ruhullah, Kalimullah, Najiyullah, what not... ...he whose slaves they are, what must that Master be like? What must that 'Ali be like? So in any case, that 'Ali was the door to the city of the Nabi's knowledge. So, Janab... Janab 'Isa was constantly with Janab Khuzaima. And if Khuzaima would take anything, from whom would he take it? From that same Lord of the universe, 'Ali. Now, what happened was that when you started to raise the dead, the community saw and were astonished, saying "This is a great miracle, 'Isa. No one has ever done this before. You have even raised the dead." Just as it is in the Qur'an-i Majid, "You have raised the dead." This is a very astonishing thing. And that Janab Sam'un as-Safa, who was standing there, his companions, one of them started asking him, saying, "Sam'un, just as happens with us, to acquire something, we try to ask our close companions, 'Tell us, how did you do it?'" In the same way, he started asking Sam'un as-Safa. "Tell us, what did he recite? What did he recite that caused this dead man to rise?" So just tell us too. And Sam'un said... Sam'un said, "Brother, it is the Ism-i A'zam (the Greatest Name) that he recited. It is the Ism-i A'zam that he recited, that's why this happened." And as you know, in Islam the Ism-i A'zam exists. If someone knows the Ism-i A'zam, he will fly in the air, walk on water, he can do everything if he gains command over the Ism-i A'zam. So Sam'un said, "He has gained command of the Ism-i A'zam." The meaning is that he has become aware of its reality. But in any case, there is blessing in its name as well. And all these things. Now, in all the Islamic books, you pick them up, and in them you'll find: "Ya Hayyu, Ya Qayyum, La ilaha illa anta, fallan, sallallahu 'alayhi wa-sallam, fallan, fallan..." there are tons of Ism-i A'zams written. And it is written that this is the Ism-i A'zam. And other people have said what? "All the Ism-i A'zams our elders have written, let's gather them all in one book." It's better to recite them all, somewhere or the other the Ism-i A'zam will turn up. Somewhere or the other the Ism-i A'zam will come, maybe its effect will happen. So, nothing is gained from these kinds of talks. The reality is, like the naba'-i 'azim (the great news), that the final news, for which 1,24,000 nabi came to give news, that... ...the glad tidings of which 'Isa himself was giving, `wa-mubashshiran bi-rasulin ya'ti min ba'di ismuhu ahmad` (and bringing good tidings of a messenger to come after me, whose name is Ahmad), "I give you the glad tidings of that nabi who is coming after me, whose noble name is Hazrat Muhammad Mustafa, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, and Ahmad Mustafa is his name in the heavens." So "Ahmad" you said. In the same way, the nabi... that nabi who was the naba'-i 'azim, that final news, who was it? It was Hazrat Nabi. In the same way, the Ism in reality, the Ism-i A'zam, who were the Ism-i A'zam? They were Maulana 'Ali. It was 'Ali's name. But what was the meaning of Ism-i A'zam? The meaning was that we are aware of his reality. To be aware of his reality was the meaning. You see, these are the realities that accomplish great tasks. For instance, there was a great elder of ours, whose name was Sayyidna Hasan bin Nuh, he... I have mentioned this before you two or three times about him, Sayyidna Hasan bin Nuh. He, when he went for the ziyarat (pilgrimage) of the Master of the Universe in Najaf and came back, so... ...that elder went for the ziyarat of the Master of the Universe, and reaching there, he stood at the door of the Rawdah (tomb) and recited the ziyarat. And after reciting the du'a, he said to the bawab, the guards who stand there... ...he said to those gatekeepers, "Please open the door for me, I want to perform ziyarat." The guard said, "What are you talking about? You know that it remains closed for months. It is not opened." He said, "Brother, it is my grandfather's grave. Let me perform ziyarat." Have you seen? This is it. This is the fire inside that was burning, the nur (light) that manifested, so his tongue began to speak in this manner: "It is my grandfather's grave." And he... These are nurani (luminous) chains. It is very difficult to understand them. In any case, what he said was not wrong. When he said, "It is my grandfather's grave, open it. I want to perform ziyarat," the guard was astonished. "What a strange thing you are saying. And you look like you are a sayyid from India." So, he was surprised and started to mock him. `Tastahzi'u 'r-rusula 'uzwa` (mocking the messengers...). The Qur'an says that the messengers were mocked. So this is nothing new for our Da'is. Anyway, he was also mocked. And mocking him, he started laughing and jeering. And Janab Sayyidna Hasan bin Nuh began his munajat (supplication). And of the Prophet alayhi-s-salatu wa-s-salam, he began to narrate all the points... ...with wahi. And no one is understanding it, and his eyes are filled with tears. And when he finished his munajat and was in supplication, the lock just fell off. And he went inside with his companions, with the rijal-i yaum who were with him, he went with them, performed the ziyarat, and came out. And there was a great commotion. There was a commotion in Makkah, and it became famous in Madinah too, "Who was he that came, who was he?" There was an uproar, and you left Najran and returned. So, in any case, what I mean to say is that when realities exist, and when they will it, then nature also wills it. `Wa-ma sha'na sha'a Allah` (And what we willed, Allah willed). We will what God wills, and if God wills, we will. Hey, they have willed so much that upon God's will, whatever God willed, they have always willed it. Today the situation is that nature itself is asking, "Now what is your pleasure, tell me." "Now tell me, what is your pleasure? Now we want to see your pleasure." So now, nature is asking for their pleasure. Today this is the state of the raziya-mardiya. So this is the matter. So when he, Janab Sam'un as-Safa, got agitated... in any case, what did he think, what not, he said some things. "I... this is its name, whatever the name was in that language, you taught him the name. And that person memorized it. And running, he said... ...that this is the Ism, this is what it is. He was passing through a jungle, and there he saw a carcass lying there. It was a big carcass. He said, "Let me just try it out on this to see how much of a miracle it is, what it is." And he blew on it. And when he blew, it was actually a lion's carcass. It was a lion's carcass. It was a complete... and suddenly the lion jumped up. The lion became alive, jumped up, and ate him. That is why it is said in the Qur'an-i Sharif, `la tas'alu 'an ashya'a in tubda lakum tasu'kum` (Do not ask about things which, if they are shown to you, will distress you). "Hey, O people, do not ask about such things that if their real answer is given to you, it will become a cause of harm for you." Did you see? That "do not ask about such things that if their answers are given to you, it will become a cause of harm for you. It is a loss for you." "Your answer... you will get the answer, but it will be a loss for you." "So it's better not to ask such a question at all." This was the matter. So in any case, this is an incident, it is a digression. But now Hazrat 'Isa alayhi-s-salatu wa-s-salam, you left from there. People said, "O 'Isa, after all, how will you spend your life wandering like this? It's better that you build some house for yourself and live in it." Hazrat 'Isa said, "If you are making me so weary, then I have no house, no home." He hadn't even married. He said, "Now that you are saying so much, fine, if you are building a house, then build my house in such-and-such place." The place he designated was right on the bank of the river, adjacent to it, a place, and he said, "This place is where a house should be built." They said, "O 'Isa, you have pointed out a place where waves are crashing, and obviously nothing will last there." He said, "What is the use of building such a house that is going to be destroyed, that is going to break and fall? I want to build an eternal house, over there." "What is to be gained from this house? That's why I don't want a house." So he used to give such teachings, Hazrat 'Isa alayhi-s-salatu wa-s-salam. And in your time... ...Allah, just as in the time of Janab Musa, created great hakims (physicians/sages), in your time too, great hakims came. And who were they? The greatest was Buzasif. The great hakim of your time was Buzasif, who was a great hakim. And another hakim came whose name was Zardasht. Zardasht, who the 'Isais, today's Parsis, consider a god and what not. That Janab Zardasht, he was a very great... not only was he a great hakim of that time, but the Imam of the time had chosen Zardasht in his place. And he had said, "I want, O Zardasht, that I am revealing wahi to you, that you now compile a book and write it." So, by the command of the Imam—whoever the Imam of that time was—by his command, Janab Zardasht wrote a book, which is called Nawashir. Nawashir means scrolls. Those words that he had written... ...that book was written on 12,000 cowhides. It was written on 12,000 cowhides, that book, in that era. And that was Zardasht, Janab Zardasht, who wrote that book. And he was a very esteemed elder, and he was. But what happened was... ...that the teachings he was receiving from the Imam alayhi-s-salam, and the 'ulum (sciences/knowledge) he was being granted, in the process of granting that 'ulum... ...it was a natural thing that he could not understand properly. A moment came when those 'ulum were of such a kind, just as Janab Adam was forbidden from going near that granary, perhaps it was the same kind of matter. Bayra-dil-i says that perhaps Zardasht could not understand, and his intellect could not grasp it. "Hey, this... whatever there is, it is the sun, which gives light to all things." The Imam was explaining some other nur (light), and he understood it as the light of the sun. That's it, he got caught up in that nur, nur, nur, and ended up turning towards the worship of the sun, and he went astray and departed. In this way, there are many who were on the path of truth and strayed from the path of truth and departed. So, in any case, in that era, there were also many other hukama (sages). One of them was Noshirvan-i 'Adil. Janab Hazrat Noshirvan-i 'Adil, who was the king of his time, whose justice will be remembered in the world, that Noshirvan-i 'Adil's justice was so tremendous... ...that there was no justice to compare with it. Just like Janab Hatim Ta'i, in whose generosity there was no other generous person, that Hazrat Hatim Ta'i was a Da'i. In the same way, Noshirvan-i 'Adil was also a Da'i. He was a Da'i, with us. And this Hazrat Noshirvan-i 'Adil was also granted great virtue by Allah. In the same way, there was a Da'i in the time of Hazrat 'Isa, in Hazrat 'Isa's time. And his name was Bakht-i Nasr. Bakht-i Nasr, who had built the Hanging Gardens in Babylon, they still exist today. And they say that it's like there is water underneath it, and that garden... ...he had built it, Bakht-i Nasr. He was also a Da'i, and he did the work of compiling. So these are all those personages of the era of 'Isa who passed, and who did great works, Bakht-i Nasr, Noshirvan-i 'Adil. And in the Aywan-i Kisra, the priestesses who were there... the Aywan-i Kisra, which was in Iran, the priests who were there, they used to worship an idol, and they would bow and pray before that idol. So, an elder came there and asked, "O priests, this idol that you are worshipping, whose idol is it that you are worshipping?" So they said, "This is a very beautiful idol, and we are worshipping it. We don't know whose... whether it's an existing human or not, but it's a very beautiful person, and we are worshipping him." It became known, he told them, that this is Noshirvan-i 'Adil whom you are worshipping.
