`Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim` (In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful). He states that: "O servants of God, listen! I am the secret of God in His cities. O servants of God, listen! I am the secret of God in His cities, and His proof (hujjat) over His creation. I am the command (amr) of God and His spirit (ruh). I have established the high and lofty mountains. I have made the flowing springs gush forth. I am the planter of trees. I am the one who fills the fruits with color. I am the one who balances the sustenance of the beings of the worlds. I am the one who raises the dead from their graves. I am the one who sends down the drops of rain and dew. I am the one who bestows light upon the sun, the moon, and the stars. I am the one who will establish the Qiyamat (Resurrection). I am the one who establishes the hours. I am the one whose obedience has been made obligatory by God. I am living, I am not subject to death. I am dead, yet I do not perish."

Allahu Akbar. He then says: "I am the knower of God's hidden secrets. I am the realm of *ma kana sa-yakun* (what was and what will be). I am the prayer (namaz) of the believers, I am the fast (roza) of the believers. I am their Maula and Imam. I am the master of the first resurrection (nashr-e-awwal), the master of the last resurrection (nashr-e-akhir). I am the master of glories (mafakhir) and virtues (manaqib). I am the master of the stars (kawakib). I am the eternal punishment from God for the enemies of God. I am the one who destroys the tyrants (jabbar). I am the master over earthquakes and tremors. I am the one who humiliates the idols. I am the one who has power over the eclipses of the sun and moon. I am the one who, with my sword, destroys the Pharaohs. I am the one whom God established in the shade of His mercy and called creation to obey me. But when I appeared, these people denied me. Thus, God, Jalla Shanahu, states that when he came to them whom they knew, they denied him. I am the `Nur al-Anwar` (Light of Lights). I am the bearer of the Divine Throne (`Arsh-e-Ilahi`). I am the master of the truthful books (`kitabha-ye sadiqa`) with the righteous (`sahibane abrar`). I am the gate of God, which cannot be opened for the liar and the denier, and he cannot taste the pleasure of Paradise. I am the one around whom the angels throng. It was for me that the sun returned twice and offered me salaam. I prayed towards two qiblas with the Messenger of God. I have made two pledges of allegiance. I am the master of Badr and Hunayn. I am the `tajalli` (manifestation) of Tur. I am the `kitab-e-mastur` (inscribed book). I am the `bayt-e-ma'mur` (frequented house). I am the one to whose obedience creation was called. One group denied, and insisted on that disbelief, and that group was transformed (`maskh`). The second group, which accepted my obedience, was saved from my wrath and became close to the court of God. I am the one in whose hand are the keys to Paradise and Hell. I am with the Messenger of God on earth and in the heavens. I am the Messiah, whom the Hand of Power anointed when no spirit was in motion and no soul was breathing. I am the master of the first era. I am the Silent one (Samit) and Muhammad, Sallallahu 'alayhi wa sallam, is the Speaker (Natiq). I took Musa across the sea, and I drowned Pharaoh and his army. I am aware of the lowing of the quadrupeds, and I am the knower of the language of birds. I am the one who, in the blink of an eye, traversed the heavens and the seven earths. I am the tongue of Isa in the cradle, and I am the one who speaks in the tongue of Isa. I am the one behind whom Isa will pray. I take whatever form I wish, according to the divine will. I am the lamp of guidance. I am the key to piety. `Ana al-awwal, ana al-akhir, ana az-zahir, ana al-batin` (I am the First, I am the Last, I am the Manifest, I am the Hidden). I am manifest, I am hidden. I am the first, I am the last. I see the deeds of the servants. I am the treasurer of His earthly and heavenly treasures by the command of God. I am established with justice and equity. On the Day of Judgment, I am the one who gives reward and punishment. I am the one without whose `wilayat` (allegiance) good deeds can be of no benefit. I am the knower of the orbits of the celestial spheres. I am the `Jabbar` (All-Compelling) and `Qahhar` (All-Dominant). I am the measure of the raindrops and the sands of the desert. I am the one who will be killed twice and revived twice, and I will appear as I wish. I encompass all of creation, even though the number of beings in the world is vast. I am their reckoner (`muhasib`), even though their number is immense. I am the one whose `wilayat` a thousand nations denied, and they were transformed (`maskh`). I am the one who will emerge in the future era. I am the one who will defeat the tyrants who remain. I will uproot them from the earth and in the end, I will give them their punishment. I speak in every language. I am the Imam of the Easts and the Wests. I am the elder of the deeds of creation. I am in Muhammad, Sallallahu 'alayhi wa sallam, and Muhammad, Sallallahu 'alayhi wa sallam, is in me. I am the meaning (`ma'na`) upon which no name (`ism`) can fall. I am the `Naba' al-'Azim` (Great News). He can have no equal. I am the gate of forgiveness." And after that, you repeated again, "Yes, yes, I am the gate of forgiveness." Reaching this point, the Maula-e-Kainat said, "`La hawla wa la quwwata illa billah al-'ali al-'azim` (There is no power and no strength except with God, the Most High, the Most Great). O people! There is no power or strength except with God, the Most High, the Most Great. If I did not have the fear that after hearing this sermon, you people would call me one who claims divinity, I would have said much more." Saying this, he ended the sermon, descended from the pulpit, fell into prostration, placed his cheek on the ground, and in that state, his tears were flowing and streaming down.

This is the sermon of Amir al-Mu'minin, in which he has given his best introduction. You see, all of this is the glory of God, but he is not God. As a poet says, "Show your manifestation, O Ali, for the Nusayris you are God. It is impossible for you to be God, but when were you ever separate from God? You are the companion of the prophets, you are the guarantor of the saints. Under the banner of praise, you are the guide of the world. What astonishing honor is yours, in the sight of the One Creator. Somewhere you are the beginning, somewhere you are the end."

In any case, what praise of the Maula and what eulogy can be done? It is not within the power of a human being, and no one has the capacity to even attempt it.

However, a few points must be laid before you. First of all, regarding Amir al-Mu'minin Hazrat Ali ibn Abi Talib, 'alayhissalatu wassalam, we need to know how his blessed birth (`wiladat-e-ba-sa'adat`) took place and where.

You all know that his blessed birth took place in Makkah, inside the sacred Ka'bah. And there, when you were born, at that time Maulana Fatimah bint Asad, Salawatullahi 'alayha, you were performing the tawaf (circumambulation) of the Ka'bah. Labor pains occurred, and seeing no other option, she wanted to enter the Ka'bah, but the door of the Ka'bah was locked. And at that time, you raised your hands and prayed, and at that very moment, God created a crack in the sacred Ka'bah, and you entered through that crack. A new door was made for Haidar, and you entered inside, and there your blessed birth took place.

And as I mentioned to you in detail, that was the `qubbah` (dome) of the `Payghambar-e-Azam` (Greatest Prophet), the `Imam-e-Awwal` (First Imam), what is called `inna awwala baytin wudi'a li-n-nas` (Indeed, the first House [of worship] established for mankind). Where his dome was, where his resting place was, where his birth took place, on that very dome, which was famous by the name of `raqam-e-hamra` (the red stone), and which, perhaps it is still there, we have seen it, that red marble stone is laid there. And at that place, the blessed birth of the Maula-e-Kainat took place.

In any case, they were the `Nur-e-Ilahi` (Divine Light). And you know, I have stated before you in detail that the matter of their body is very unique. It is like our clothes, that is the state of their body. And the Imams do not just have one type of body; rather, just as we have different clothes for summer and winter, they also have three types of bodies. And they are called `nasut-e-tabi'i` (natural physical form), `nasut-e-zilli` (shadowy physical form), and `nasut-e-khass` (special physical form). But for Amir al-Mu'minin Ali, 'alayhissalatu wassalam, this was a special characteristic: that the `nawasit-e-zilliya` (shadowy forms), `nawasit-e-khass` (special forms), and `nawasit-e-tabi'i` (natural forms) of all the other Imams are in their own place, and they are all of the same style. But for Maula-e-Kainat, it was not so. Your `nasut-e-tabi'i`, `nasut-e-zilli`, and `nasut-e-khass` were not only of a different nature, but they were of a different power and strength, and their nourishment and growth were also completely different.

A special thing to say about you is that the Prophet, 'alayhissalatu wassalam, and Hazrat Ali, these were two such beings who were shining in the universe. And you see, as I said to you, both of them, and all the Imams, all the prophets, are veils (`hijab`) for what is in the Taamur. They are the possessors of being (`Ulu an-nazat`), and these are their representatives established from their side. So, where the possessors of being, for whom the Prophet, 'alayhissalatu wassalam, stated that my name on earth is Muhammad, 'alayhissalatu wassalam, and my name in the heavens is Ahmad. In the same way, Hazrat Ali's name there is 'Ayn-e-'Azima (the Great Eye/Essence), and here it is Ali Murtaza. And in this way, you see that when 'Ayn sought its veil here, and when Meem, that is, we also call Ahmad "Meem," Meem-e-Mariamiya, and when he sought his veil here, you should consider that many veils appeared, but from among those veils, the one that was chosen, Meem-e-Mariamiya chose his veil, he chose the highest veil, and that was the personage of Muhammad, Sallallahu 'alayhi wa sallam, the Rahmat al-'Alamin (Mercy to the worlds), who graced the world. But 'Ayn-e-'Azima, when he wanted to choose his representative, that representative... although many representatives appeared before him, he chose the representative who was the most humble (`adna-tarin`), the lowliest (`kam-tar`) representative.

Let me explain this matter with some detail before you. Many veils of 'Ayn-e-'Azima were appearing. One was Amir an-Nahl, one was Abu Turab, one was Ya'sub ad-Din, one was Amir al-Mu'minin, one was Karrar, and in this way there were many veils that were appearing for 'Ayn, but from among those veils, the one 'Ayn chose was the veil of 'Ali'. Why? Because Providence wanted the humblest veil to appear in the world. And you see, the humblest part of the Maula's being came here, and it caused a revolution in the world. That exalted personage became a complete secret. For that exalted personage, the Nusayri sect emerged, who called him God. Either they elevated him so much that they made him God, or they lowered him so much that they made him the fourth. Someone did something, someone said something, but the point is that it became like a partnership property (`sajhe ka maal`). It happened that everyone became devoted to this light of Imamate, but no one could escape mentioning Ali's name. No group or sect of Islam does not believe in Ali. The Sufis also bowed their heads, all the chains that emerged, the Qadiriyya, the Chishtiyya, whatever emerged from Islam, they all bowed their heads at the door of Ali and affiliated their chains with him. So it is known that this was a special characteristic of Amir al-Mu'minin. The Prophet, 'alayhissalatu wassalam, who was the `muhtajib` (veiled one), who is known by the name of Meem-e-Mariamiya or Ahmad, when he chose, sometimes he came as `Ya ayyuha al-muzzammil` (O you who are wrapped in garments), sometimes `Ya ayyuha al-muddaththir` (O you who are covered). Sometimes he came as Ta-Ha, sometimes as Ya-Sin, sometimes as Mukhtar. But the one he chose was the sacred veil of Muhammad, 'alayhissalatu wassalam, and here the Sarwar-e-Kainat graced us.

Now, what is this matter? Just like there is a conference, and you send your representatives to it. You are also a shopkeeper, I am also a shopkeeper. I send my representative, you send your representative. And let's say there is a trade union, and representatives are going there. What do you do? You send your manager or accountant, who does your work, as a representative. I send a clerk who works for me. So both will go and sit, and my representative and your representative, they will have the status of being representatives, but you see that no matter how much, that accountant, in comparison to him, that poor clerk will sit with a certain humility. He will not be able to raise his head too much because he has less knowledge and a lower status. Even though he is a representative. So this was the matter, that it was the firm decision of Providence, Providence had resolved that Ali should bow, Ali's head should bow, Ali should recite the kalima, Ali should bow down before the Prophet, so that there would be no claim of `nisbat-e-a'la` (higher connection), God forbid, and that from a lower connection he would be seen bowing before the being with the higher connection. And this was the matter, that Maula-e-Kainat, from the very beginning, from childhood itself, you made it clear... what is childhood, what is youth, what is old age? For the `Nur` (light), there is no consideration of age, nor of any other thing, no consideration of illness, nor of being killed or plundered. No such thing can even arise. But Hazrat Ali said from there that "I am with you." You prayed, so he prayed with you. You fought, so he fought with you. If you were in battle, he was with you; if you were in assembly, he was with you. So Ali never left the Prophet's side, he was his helper and supporter, and always remained so. So this was the reason. And this was the reason that you, the Prophet, 'alayhissalatu wassalam, came into this world with such great glory and splendor, and became the `Rahmat-e-'Alam` (Mercy to the worlds), and spread over it. And what can be said, that you presented a most definitive book like the Holy Quran, which will remain until the Qiyamat, shining. And along with it, such a great treasure of hadith you left behind that... which, according to Sahih Bukhari, is 6,000 hadiths. That is such a thing, and such a book, that as I have said in passing, it is a book that we would be ashamed to teach. It is such a book that we would be ashamed to read, because it is very easy to read a text, but it is such a strange book that has been written, in which there are hundreds of hadiths that... you cannot read in front of your children, in front of your house. You tell me, such a book, which contains such hadiths, and which is attributed to the name of the Prophet, 'alayhissalatu wassalam, can we say that this book has a rank after the Holy Quran? God forbid, God forbid. Just think about it, and think about the authenticity of those hadiths. Then the amazing thing is that all Muslims agree that we will check it with `ilm al-rijal` (the science of narrators) and verify everything. Alright, let's check with `ilm al-rijal`. What is `ilm al-rijal`? They said we will see in the hadiths who the narrators are, did they ever tell a lie, were they ever punished, were their hands or feet not cut off, did they ever commit theft or treachery? Alright, when they sat down to check with this standard, and started checking with their self-made `ilm al-rijal`, all the hadiths were invalidated. So, you are committing suicide with your own hands. All the hadiths were invalidated, only one hadith remained: `innamal a'malu bin-niyyat` (Actions are but by intentions). Now this is the limit, that you write 6,000 hadiths, and out of them, you keep only one hadith. So, these are not correct things. Quda'i collected 1200 hadiths, which my late father translated as `Jawami' al-Kilam`, which is before you as `Kitab ash-Shihab an-Nabawi`, the translation of which is `Jawami' al-Kilam`. Those are the hadiths that are authentic for us. And the `ta'wil` (interpretation) of that same book, the truths of that book, the Da'i has done in `Ma'un al-Mu'in`, and has explained its truths, what esoteric meanings and lights are hidden in it.

In any case, the long and short of it is that this was to show how the world behaved and how things turned out. In any case, the Prophet, 'alayhissalatu wassalam, you see that he came as the representative of the highest veil, and Amir al-Mu'minin as the lowest. And if God had reversed it, then the divine system would have been different, and God knows what would have become of those who were to become Nusayris, who became famous throughout their lives by the name of `Mazhar al-'Aja'ib wa al-Ghara'ib` (Manifestation of Wonders and Marvels), God knows what they would have become, and what a commotion would have ensued in this world. The Lord of the Worlds did not will it so, and whatever system God wanted, that same constitution remained in effect in the world.

In any case, this was a small corner that had to be explained, that this is how the matter happened. Now, after that, if... that which is worthy of consideration, that most important thing, is the Holy Quran, which was revealed upon the Prophet, 'alayhissalatu wassalam. That book, about which what can I say, it is the constitution of life, in which `wa la ratbin wa la yabisin illa fi kitabin mubin` (and there is no moist or dry thing but that it is in a clear book). There is no dry or wet thing that is not present in this Holy Quran. Just as God has said, `kulla shay'in ahsaynahu fi imamin mubin` (and We have enumerated all things in a clear Imam), we have encompassed everything in a clear Imam. So the Lord of the Worlds, just as He has wrapped up everything within an Imam, in the same way, He has preserved all meanings and implications within this Holy Quran. The one who revealed this most definitive book was the master of the time, the Imam of the time, the God of the time, he was Hazrat Maulana Abu Talib, who was the revealer of this book. The `anwar` (lights) were descending from the circle of the First Intellect (`aql-e-awwal`). I have already told you. It's not a matter of the tenth or anything else. These `anwar` were coming from there, from the circles of the First Intellect, its descent was from there, which is called `Anwar-e-Dhikriya` (Lights of the Reminder). When these `Anwar-e-Dhikriya` were descending, as they say, when these `anwar` began to descend, they came to the first heaven, then the second heaven, then the third heaven. You understand, the first circle... the circles of the intellect, the ten circles I have mentioned to you, when they came into the first circle, they tried to preserve it, they tried to understand it, then they gave it to the ones below, then the ones below took it. Now look, just as if there are many stairs, 200-300 stairs, and you are pouring water from the top, the water from each stair, as it falls down, some water remains on each stair, it gets absorbed, or it ends there. In the same way, this divine word, what can be said of the intensity of its lights? What can be said of the intensity of those lights? And when they were descending, they were being preserved in all the places, in the circles of the dome, their intensity was being reduced, and by and by, they became capable of coming to this earthly plane, and they came upon Hazrat Maulana Abu Talib. And the sacred personage of Maulana Abu Talib, 'alayhissalatu wassalam, was the one who bore this completely, who bore these `Anwar-e-Dhikriya`. And the Islamic world calls him a `kafir` (unbeliever). He was the one who then sent the Prophet as a messenger and prophet, and this most definitive book, just as the Torah was revealed, the Zabur was revealed, the Injil was revealed, the Suhuf of Ibrahim were revealed. All these things came, but their source was the `ashir` (tenth). The source of those things, those coming things, they were coming from their respective Imams, from Maulana Uz, from Maulana Hud, from Maulana Khuzaimah. These were the `Anwar-e-Dhikriya`, they were coming from the circle of the First Intellect, and its descent was from there. And when they came, the Holy Quran states: `anzalna hadhal qur'ana 'ala qalbika fi lisanin 'arabiyyin mubin` (We have sent down this Quran upon your heart in a clear Arabic tongue).

Did you see? Brother, I didn't understand. What kind of eloquence is this? God could have simply said that "O Prophet, we are revealing the Holy Quran to you." "O Prophet, 'alayhissalatu wassalam, we are revealing it to you." This statement, "upon your heart" (`'ala qalbika`), that it is being revealed upon your blessed heart, upon your heart, this is not understood. The mind is the thing for thinking, and what is the need to reveal it upon the heart? This matter is not understood. But in reality, the matter is understood in this way: that there, the "Heart of the Prophet" (`qalb-e-payghambar`) is Amir al-Mu'minin Ali, upon whom this Holy Quran was revealed. You took the meanings, and you took the words. Indeed, both were aware of it. The one who knows the words is also the one who knows the meanings, and the one who knows the meanings is also the one who takes the words. He was not separate from him, this was not separate from him. The prophet and Ali, and the successor and the prophet, they were not separate from each other at all. And in this way, Maula-e-Kainat handled all those `Anwar-e-Dhikriya`, and he did that. And it was you who compiled the Holy Quran. And what is said, that the third caliph compiled it, and after that, what was there, that Quran, the different things and verses that were found written on palm leaves etc., he had them burned. Fine, now all these things, the Shia people object very strongly to them, that burning the pages of the Holy Quran is such a bad thing, this and that. In my view, this is not an important thing. The important thing is that compiling the Quran was not their job. This was Ali's job. This was Ali's job, and just as Ali worked in all the caliphates, he worked at that time too. And you knew that saving Islam was my job. And I have given the example before, that two women came fighting to Hazrat Ali, and they were fighting over a child. That woman says this child is mine, the other says it's mine, both were fighting with each other. Hazrat Ali said, "O Qambar, take the sword, cut it in two, and give one piece to one and one piece to the other." Sir, as soon as you gave the order, that righteous... the one who was its real mother, she started shouting and saying, "Don't kill it, there is no need to cut it in half, give it to her." Even though the child is mine. Immediately, you handed the child over to her. This is the wisdom of Amir al-Mu'minin. Thousands of such wise acts you have done. So this was the matter, that the Maula-e-Kainat, you adopted humility, and you, there, you did this for this Holy Quran, that Hazrat... when you came to Hazrat Uthman and said, "Look, you are compiling the Holy Quran, and since I am the most knowledgeable and the gate to the city of knowledge, I want to give my help." And you accepted it. And you wanted them to accept, and after accepting, you checked the entire Holy Quran well yourself, so that no change could come in it, because God says, `inna nahnu nazzalna adh-dhikra wa inna lahu la-hafizun` (Indeed, it is We who sent down the Reminder, and indeed, We will be its guardian). It was you who had to protect it, and you protected it. Otherwise, this Holy Quran would also have undergone changes, just as everything else changed. The Sunnahs changed, the situations changed, the Shari'ahs changed, the enforcement changed, the law changed, the hadiths changed. What more can be said? And what would have been the delay in this changing? They would have changed this too, but it could not be changed. And the Prophet's successor saw to it. He saw it well, compiled it, and it remained established in its place.

Now, regarding the Prophet, 'alayhissalatu wassalam, this matter that when you were born, at that very time, the Shia gentlemen say that at that very time, the Maula-e-Kainat opened his eyes in your lap and recited the Holy Quran. Oh, what is the matter of reciting the Holy Quran? These are not children, not adults, they are masters of all books. That is why Maulana Amir al-Mu'minin, while giving one of his sermons, you said, "O people! Whatever is in the heavenly books is in the Holy Quran. And whatever is in the Holy Quran is in Surah al-Hamd. And whatever is in Surah al-Hamd is in the Bismillah. And whatever is in the Bismillah is in the 'Ba' of Bismillah. And whatever is in the 'Ba' is in the dot, and that dot is me. `Ana nuqtatu taht al-ba` (I am the dot beneath the 'Ba')." And I have given you many explanations of this, what the dots are in the 'Be' and what they are. In any case, what I have to say at this time is that you described yourself as the dot of the 'Be'. So, the entire Holy Quran has shrunk and, having shrunk from this `Kitab-e-Samit` (Silent Book), it has entered into this `Kitab-e-Natiq` (Speaking Book). That is why you had picked up the Holy Quran and said, `hadha kitabuna yantiqu 'alaykum bil-haqq` (This is our book that speaks the truth to you). When you recited this verse, "This our book speaks true things to you," at that very moment, Maula-e-Kainat picked it up on his head and said, "O Book of God, speak." "O Book of God, what do you want to say?" And after that, you said, "It says nothing at all." At that moment, you, placing the book on your head, said, "`anta kitabullah as-samit wa ana kitabullah an-natiq` (You are the silent book of God, and I am the speaking book of God)." You are the silent book of God. This book does not speak. But I am the speaking book of God.

Now, since people had left this speaking book, this silent book also remained completely silent for them. That's why `wa ma ya'lamu ta'wilahu illa Allah wa ar-rasikhuna fi al-'ilm` (and no one knows its interpretation except God and those firm in knowledge). The Quran clearly states that no one knows the interpretation except God and those firm in knowledge, but these Muslims deny the interpretation. They deny the interpretation itself, saying there is no interpretation. So you consider, how can the Holy Quran not have an interpretation?

So, those... all of those meanings and implications were to be explained by the Maula-e-Kainat. That is why even today, the Islamic world is in the greatest misguidance, that God gives a book and says that this is a guide that we are giving you, `hudan lil-muttaqin` (a guidance for the God-fearing). This is a guide for the God-fearing. And we take God's book and, kissing it, we are reading this verse, and this is the first verse we are reading, that it is a guide. And the situation is that we say `Alif-Lam-Mim` and fall silent and move on. Just translate `Alif-Lam-Mim`. Translate `Kaf-Ha-Ya-'Ayn-Sad`. Translate `'Ayn-Sin-Qaf`. Translate `Alif-Lam-Ra`. Nothing. These are the `huroof-e-muqatta'at` (disconnected letters), dumb letters. Brother, how can there be dumb letters? How can these locks be put? There must be keys to these treasures.

So, in any case, this is the result of leaving the `Ahl al-Haqq` (People of Truth). `Fas'alu ahl adh-dhikr in kuntum la ta'lamun` (so ask the People of the Reminder if you do not know). God had said in the Holy Quran that if you do not know, then ask the people of the Reminder. What is the Reminder? The Holy Quran. Those who have the Holy Quran, Amir al-Mu'minin Ali and his progeny, ask them, and you will know what it is. And you have seen that who became the explainers of everything? It was Maula-e-Kainat, Amir al-Mu'minin, 'alayhissalatu wassalam.

One more special thing to be said is that Maula-e-Kainat, the station he attained at this time, that station is the `rutba-e-tasmin` (rank of eight). What is the `rutba-e-tasmin`? It is a very great and momentous thing that I am explaining to you. It is that after the completion of seven `sidr` (periods of manifestation) and seven `kashf` (unveilings), now the eighth `kashf` that comes, the eighth `sidr` that comes, at that time, your `zuhur` (manifestation) will happen. That `zuhur` has been described as `rutba-e-tasmin`. `Tasmin` means eight. It will be the state of the eighth. Your manifestations have been many. Whenever a `sidr` came, you graced us with your presence. Whenever a `sidr` came, the prophets also graced us. Whenever a `sidr` came, the Master of the Universe also graced us. So now these matters of coming, and the states, how many times you have come, and in what way you have come, that God has stated in the Holy Quran. And where is that statement? It is `fa-bi-ayyi ala'i rabbikuma tukadhdhiban` (Then which of the favors of your Lord will you deny?). The repetition in Surah ar-Rahman, what is this matter that God repeats `fa-bi-ayyi ala'i rabbikuma tukadhdhiban`? Is this done for the sake of melody? Is this sentence inserted for the sake of rhythm? Oh, if He had said it once, the matter would have been understood, that `fa-bi-ayyi ala'i rabbikuma tukadhdhiban`. How many of God's signs will you deny? It would have been done. But there is a purpose in saying it this way. That denying the greatest sign of God is the Maula-e-Kainat. And its repetition is 31 times, and your appearances in the world are 31. And this, we... I have already mentioned that 399 `qawr` (sub-cycles) of the first `mawr` (major cycle) have passed. 399 `qawr` of the second `mawr` have passed. And this is the 400th `qawr`. The first `dawr` (period) of this 400th `qawr` has passed. And this is the end of the `dawr`, and we are sitting at the end of the `dawr-e-sitr` (period of concealment). So now, this... now the `kashf` that is left, that `kashf` has to come. After that `kashf` and `sitr` passes, you will be established at the `rutba-e-tasmin`. In this way, you will attain the `khilafat-e-qa'im-e-muntazar` (caliphate of the awaited Qa'im).

That is, in other words, if there is a being greater than the Prophet, 'alayhissalatu wassalam, and his righteous successor, it is the `Qa'im al-Qiyamah`, 'ala zikrihim as-salam, who is to come. That is his mention. He is the greatest being. He is the `mabda'-e-kull` (origin of all) and `akhir-e-kull` (end of all), in whom everyone has to be absorbed. Everyone is that, and he is the one who will establish the Qiyamat. That is why it was said, `li-man al-mulk al-yawm, lillah al-wahid al-qahhar` (To whom belongs the dominion this Day? To God, the One, the Prevailing). For whom is the kingdom? It is for the One, the Prevailing. So that being is to come, and he is the highest and greatest being, in whom everyone will have to be absorbed.

In any case, I will say two more things about Hazrat Ali ibn Abi Talib, 'alayhissalatu wassalam: his marital state. When he got married, at that time, regarding the marriage, these stories that are narrated, that so-and-so wanted to marry, this one wanted to marry... well, these are just narrations, and it happens as it does. But Amir al-Mu'minin desired it, and the Prophet, 'alayhissalatu wassalam... this was all a divine matter. As I said in yesterday's and the day before's gathering, in the mention of Maulana Fatimah, how Maulana Mahmud came and said that God has performed the marriage. So here too, the Prophet performed their marriage. But what was the nature of the marriage of Ali and Fatimah? What was the spiritual nature of this? What spiritualities were at work behind it? And how did the nikah of Hazrat Ali and Hazrat Fatimah take place?

There are very special points in this nikah. The matter is that for the sake of saying it, we say that Ali came from the house of God and Fatimah Zahra came from the house of the Prophet, and the two were married. But it is not like that. You are seeing that these people are all from the Taamur. And why are they joining in a marital state here? The matter is that the `suwarat` (spiritual forms) that Hazrat Fatimah Zahra had, all of them were the `samra` (fruit) that the Prophet, 'alayhissalatu wassalam, had granted and given. To whom? To Hazrat Fatimah Zahra. The Prophet, 'alayhissalatu wassalam, in the early days of Islam, when he endured the hardships of Makkah and Islam spread, people passed away, their `suwarat` started to be released. The `suwarat` started to gather, and the one who was collecting those `suwarat` was Maulana Salman Farsi, the Bab al-Abwab. He was collecting them. He collected them, and after collecting them... So the matter was that you were the Bab al-Abwab for all, that is, you were the great Bab al-Abwab, but for the secondary things, as I said that Maulana Ali had 12 stations, here too there are many such things with the Prophet. In the same way, those `suwarat` that were there, all of them were being gathered with whom? With Maulana Khadijah. With Maulana Khadijah. Just as you, in your house, give one thing to one child, another thing to another child to gather, a third thing to a third child to gather. They are your own children who gather, you give it to them. In the same way, but this is not a matter of children and women, these are all matters from there. Maulana Khadijah, you gave her those `suwarat`. And Maulana Khadijah, to whom did she hand them over? To her own daughter. To her own daughter, she handed them over, to Maulana Fatimah. That is why the Prophet, 'alayhissalatu wassalam, about his saying, `Ya Umm Abiha` (O mother of her father), which you had said, that "O mother of the father," in this, the intellects of the wise are bewildered. And the Du'at brought this saying for this very reason: `Ummuhu ummuhu ummuha` (His mother, his mother, his mother). My mother, Ali's mother, and Fatimah's mother. The Prophet's noble mother, Maulana Aminah bint Wahb, and Fatimah bint Asad, Maulana Fatimah who was the noble mother of Hazrat Ali, and Hazrat Fatimah's noble mother, Hazrat Khadijah. All of them, what did they become by going there? All of them were Bab al-Abwab, and they became the `haykal` (temple/structure). They went into the `haykal` and became the `qalb` (heart). So this was a special characteristic that Hazrat Fatimah Zahra possessed. That is why you are called `jawharat al-islami` (the jewel of Islam). In our tradition, you are specially called the jewel of Islam, and this state of being the jewel of Islam belongs to Maulana Fatimah, that the collection of Islamic `suwarat` was with you. Because now you are seeing that through a continuous chain, one line of `mustaqarrin` (permanent) Du'at is running, and one line of `mustawda'in` (temporary) is running. In between these, there is a venerable personage, Maulana Fatimah. Here, Providence wants, what the Mashiyyat-e-Ilah (Divine Will), which the Mishkat-e-Nur is saying, she wants to handle all those things, and the Islamic `suwarat`, whatever there were, from the early days of Islam, they were gathered with Hazrat Fatimah Zahra.

Hazrat Ali was the owner of his father's inheritance. Maulana Abu Talib, that entire inheritance, the treasures of all the Imams, were gathered with you, and you entrusted all of that to the Prophet, 'alayhissalatu wassalam, that "O Ali... O Prophet, I am giving it to you." And that night was the night when the Prophet was given this, that was the very night we call the Me'raj. That was the night of the Me'raj, when the Prophet, 'alayhissalatu wassalam, was entrusted with this. And the Prophet, 'alayhissalatu wassalam, when he returned this to Hazrat Ali, that was the day of Ghadir. It was the day of Ghadir that he said `man kuntu mawlahu fa-hadha 'aliyyun mawlahu` (Of whomsoever I am the master, this Ali is his master), and at that time he entrusted it, and you took it. So Ali became the owner of the `mustaqarrin`, and Fatimah became the owner of the Islamic `suwarat`. These are `imani suwarat` (spiritual forms of faith), those are `islami suwarat` (spiritual forms of submission). Now you will understand the difference. Islamic `suwarat` is just adhering to the outward rules of Shari'ah, reciting `La ilaha illallah`, and doing a lot of dhikr, and living according to the outward Shari'ah. To be aware of the inner things, to sit on the `boriya` (mat) and learn from Ali, to know all the truths, how we came, how we will go, how our death will be, how our burial, how our shroud, how we will be raised from our graves—to be aware of all these things, those `suwarat` were the `imani suwarat`. This collection of `imani suwarat` was with Hazrat Ali. Providence wants the union of these two, that both should come together. What will be the result of their coming together? That the Islamic `suwarat` will get some `imani` fragrance, and the `imani suwarat` will get some Islamic fragrance, even though they are `imani` and superior, but they will accept it, and they will live together. This was the union, this was the bond that the Prophet had made. This was the real marriage, the marriage of Fatimah and Hazrat Ali was this kind of marriage. And that marriage, with a mahr of 200 dirhams that the Prophet, 'alayhissalatu wassalam, set, and giving those 200 dirhams, what were those 200 dirhams? Oh, they were all the `rihiyat` (spiritual essences) that he was entrusting. That, just as the apple came from paradise... As I explained about the Prophet's Me'raj yesterday, but where does the Prophet's Me'raj end? What can be said of the Me'raj? `Dana fa-tadalla fa-kana qaba qawsayn aw adna` (Then he drew near and came down and was at a distance of two bow lengths or even nearer). The Prophet reached this station, that he drew so near, so near that the distance became that of two bows or even nearer. And this distance, in reality, that distance of two bows or nearer, this was a mention of the `sufara` (ambassadors). It was a mention of the `sufara`, that both `safirs` (ambassadors), Maulana Abdul Muttalib and Maulana Abu Talib, and the `adhir`, who is Hazrat Abdullah. So this, when the Prophet, 'alayhissalatu wassalam, after going on the Me'raj and returning, people asked, "O Messenger of God, you had the Me'raj, explain some of its reality, what did you see after all?" `Ma zagha al-basaru wa ma tagha` (The sight [of the Prophet] did not swerve, nor did it transgress [its limit]). That in the blink of an eye, these states occurred. What did you see after all? What God says, what did you see, O Messenger of God? So you said, "O people, what can I say? I went into the seventh heaven, and there, when I was journeying through the heavens, I saw on one heaven that there was a crowd of angels." I was surprised and asked, "O brother Jibril," who was with me and was telling me everything, I asked, "O brother Jibril, what is this? Whom are these angels crowding around? What is the matter?" He said, "O Messenger of God, you go and see for yourself." The matter is that all the angels are eager to see Ali. They are eager to see Hazrat Ali, and he is on earth. And the angels are in the high heaven, and they want to always be seeing Ali. So the Prophet, 'alayhissalatu wassalam... Hazrat Jibril said, "O Messenger of God, at that time God commanded an angel to take his form and make it like Ali's, and that angel's form was made like Ali's, and today all the angels are surrounding that angel."

Seeing that scene, the Prophet, 'alayhissalatu wassalam, went on the Me'raj, and when he went and the station of `dana fa-tadalla fa-kana qaba qawsayn aw adna` came, and that station also came where the command to "take off your sandals" (`fakhla' na'layk`) was given to Musa. "O Musa, take off your sandals, `innaka bil-wad al-muqaddasi tuwa` (indeed, you are in the sacred valley of Tuwa)." You have come to the sacred valley. Here, there was no such command for the Prophet. He is the beloved of God, who is coming, and he is going to such a station. But when, after returning, people asked, "What did you see?" you said, "O people, when I wanted to see, and said that something should be seen, I saw only one thing, and that was a hand." And that hand... so people asked, "What was that hand like?" You said, "It was like Ali's hand." They said, "O Messenger of God, tell us this, what was the tone of voice?" The words that God spoke to you, what was that tone? He said, "Brother, the tone was Ali's tone."

So this was the greatness of that `Ayn-e-'Azima`, of that `nisbat-e-a'la`, towards which the Prophet, 'alayhissalatu wassalam, was pointing.

So, in any case, these stories that the chain was shaking, the bed was warm, all these are verbal flourishes. They have no importance. The real things are the scholarly matters, which we have strayed from. So, in any case, this was the state of the Me'raj that I have presented before you and which you have understood. The Prophet, 'alayhissalatu wassalam's righteous successor, he also had to face many difficulties, and you know that there was no one who faced fewer difficulties than you. And those difficulties came to such a point that the world turned away from you, and with the passing of the Prophet, 'alayhissalatu wassalam, everything that the Prophet, 'alayhissalatu wassalam, had entrusted to you, the world denied it, and an election was held, and how the events unfolded, you know it well. But our Du'at say that this was a matter predetermined by God. This was a firm matter, a matter of understanding, and it was a sign to Amir al-Mu'minin that you will have to be `maqhur` (overpowered) in twelve places, you will have to become `ajiz` (humble). Those twelve places where you had to be humble, you had to show humility... Look, for a wrestler to become humble is not an easy thing. Yes, a child, a coward, or someone like that, for him to become humble is a very easy thing. But for a wrestler who has won all his fights and has won in every battle, for him to become humble is not an easy thing. The `sawlat-e-haydari` (Haydar's assault) was something that the leaders of Arabia feared. All of Arabia knew that no sword could match the cut and sharpness of Ali's sword, Zulfiqar, and no speech could stand against that tongue. But despite that, he remained silent. So the matter was that now, here, the things that happened and...

The humility and being overpowered, there were twelve stations where Maula-e-Kainat became humble. The first station where you showed your humility and became humble, that was the first station, the door and house of Fatimah Zahra. That is, when the Prophet, 'alayhissalatu wassalam, was buried and had passed away, now the sun of Prophethood itself had set, what more can be said, it was darkness upon darkness. And now, the opponents made a clamor and came and started to burn the house of Hazrat Fatimah Zahra. And Hazrat Umar was at the front, and others were also there, and they tried to set fire to the door and the house of Hazrat Fatimah Zahra. Although the fire was not lit, an attempt was made to light it, and they wanted to burn the house. This was the first thing, that Maula-e-Kainat was sitting inside and was silent. Your prowess and your honor, you endured it all, and because it was the command to be humble, you were humble. The second time was when that door, Hazrat Umar pushed it, and Hazrat Fatimah Zahra, the lady of paradise, was standing behind it, and it fell on your stomach, while you were pregnant with Hazrat Muhsin. Your third son, Muhsin, was about to be born, and the pregnancy of Hazrat Muhsin, that pregnancy was aborted, and from that, you ultimately passed away later, but that was the illness, that was the pain that continued. So in any case, they pushed that door down. This was the second time that Hazrat Ali adopted silence. The third time was when chains were put on your hands, a rope was put around Hazrat Ali's neck, and a rope was tied and the caliphs pulled, and they took you away and said, "Give us your `bay'ah` (allegiance)." They took him to the valley of Abu Talib. And it was daytime, and it was morning time, when they took him with a rope around his neck and started saying, "O Ali, you will have to give `bay'ah`." You said, "Look, leave me, I don't want to get into any of this, you should just... I will not interfere in your matters." They said, "This cannot be, you have no choice but to give allegiance." You said, "Alright, if you insist so much, then come, I am ready to give you my allegiance." So you gave allegiance to Hazrat Abu Bakr, and you presented your left hand. So they said, "Why don't you present your right hand for the allegiance?" So you said, "I have given my right hand to the Prophet, and I cannot give that hand. Take this left hand." So you gave your left hand, and you gave your allegiance. This was the third time that you were overpowered. After this, that time came when you remained in submission during the time of the first caliph. Another time came when you were in submission during the time of Hazrat Umar. A third time came... the sixth time came when you were under them during the time of Hazrat Uthman. And a time came when Hazrat Umar established the `shura` (council), and in that `shura`, he had commanded that you... I have explained that `shura` in great detail, and there is not enough time to explain the whole `shura`, but he had arranged it in such a way that Hazrat Ali could in no way become the caliph. He was determined that he should not become one, and the `shura` was of six men, and all the arrangements, I have told you in detail, whose relationship was what. And they had already given their opinions. They are forming the `shura` and also giving their opinions. And after that, Hazrat Ali had to participate in the `shura`, so he was overpowered. This was also a time that you had to be overpowered. You had to become humble. After this, that time came when Hazrat Uthman inflicted severe oppression on your companions. Hazrat Rashid al-Hujari, and Hazrat Hatim Tai's son Uday, and all the people, and Hazrat Abu Dharr al-Ghifari, Hazrat Ammar Yasir, all the great companions, he beat them, broke them, burned them, cut them, exiled them, and all these incidents have been narrated to you. But there is no point in mentioning them. In any case, all these things happened, and at this station too, you adopted humility. After this, the time came when the Battle of Siffin took place, and at that time, Amr ibn al-'As, the fox of history, than whom there is no more wicked man, he had given the advice and said, "O Mu'awiyah, what are you doing? You are about to lose now. It is better that you are not like Ali, and your army is not like Ali's believing army. It would be better if, at this moment when you are losing, you raise the Holy Quran on the spears." And at that time, the Quran was raised on the spears, and they raised the same slogan that Hazrat Umar had given: `hasbuna kitabullah` (The Book of God is enough for us). "This book is enough for us." And at that time, the Maula-e-Kainat had said, "O people, the book of God is me, look at me. And look at me, and don't look there. The living book of God is me." `Al-'ilmu la fi as-sutur, al-'ilmu fi as-sudur` (Knowledge is not in the lines, knowledge is in the hearts). Knowledge is not in the lines, it is in the hearts. But they did not listen to you. So this was also a time. And after that, that time came when at Dumat al-Jundal, Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, his... he became the `hakam` (arbitrator), so he was made the `hakam`, and Hazrat Ali was left out. And after that, in Iraq, Abbas... Abbas ibn Sa'd was made the `hakim` (ruler) there, and Amir al-Mu'minin was ignored. So these are twelve occasions when the Prophet, 'alayhissalatu wassalam's successor had to be overpowered, had to be humble. The Prophet, 'alayhissalatu wassalam's Amir al-Mu'minin Ali was the successor of the Prophet, but in reality, he was the heir of his father. He was the heir of Maulana Abu Talib, and the inheritance he received was from Hazrat Abu Talib. That chain of Imamate was continuing uninterrupted. I will take a little more time today, but I want to finish some part of it. So Hazrat Abu Talib, from him it came to Hazrat Ali. Hazrat Ali distributed those `anwar` (lights) among his children, just as Hazrat Ibrahim had distributed between Isma'il and Ishaq. You chose your younger son for Imamate and successorship, and your elder son for Prophethood and Messengership. You chose Hazrat Hasan for this and him for that, but the matter was that the Prophet wanted that just as you, in your lifetime, received the trust of all things and you remained the elder in the time of Hazrat Ali, in the same way, Hasan should also not raise his head before his brother, he should remain with his head bowed before his brother. This is what Providence wanted, the Prophet also wanted it. That is why he had said, `al-Hasan wa al-Husayn imaman in qama aw qa'ada wa abuhuma khayrun minhuma` (Hasan and Husayn are two Imams, whether they rise or sit, and their father is better than them). So he had called both of them Imams. For this reason, the Prophet, 'alayhissalatu wassalam's successor, Hazrat Ali, gave all those things to Hazrat Hasan. And he told Hasan, "When you pass away, give it to Husayn." Now Husayn became the heir of his father. And as I said to you, in reality, the rightful heir after the father is the son. That heir was Husayn. Husayn became the heir. All the `anwar` of Imamate, successorship, Prophethood, and Messengership were gathered with Hazrat Husayn. But a calamity came, that the Lord of the Worlds also willed that some accounts and reckonings that were outstanding from before should be settled. The matter is that some things also come upon the good people. You will say, "How do they come upon the good people?" You think that doing jihad is very easy. Oh, we do jihad on God's command, if we kill someone, what retribution comes upon us? We are just wielding the sword on God's command. He died, so it's good, he died well, he was a kafir, he died, we did jihad. No, no. He certainly died, everything happened, you did jihad, but as he was dying, his heart was pained. Providence wants retribution for that as well. A small retribution for that. And how will that retribution be? If you have also killed, then you will also be killed. For example, killed in what way? Like being hit with a flower stalk. Being hit with a flower is no hit, but the heart of the hitter is satisfied that "we have hit."

For such retributions, they had to be paid. By whom? By Imam Husayn, 'alayhissalatu wassalam. Hazrat Ali had fought great wars, had caused calamities, had turned the right wing into the left, the left into the right. In the heart of the army, Ali was shining with his sword. He had won such battles. In Khaybar, Uhud, Badr, in every battle, you were victorious. But the many people you had killed, all those people who had died, as they were dying, the pain their hearts felt, those things had remained. And those `suwarat` (spiritual forms) had also gathered in their own place. And all of them... Providence wanted all of them to gather. And all of those evil `suwarat`, just as the good `suwarat` had gathered with Imam Husayn, 'alayhissalatu wassalam, because you were the heir of your father. The things that were gathered with Ali, Ali had entrusted to Husayn. All those people who had done jihad, who had brandished the sword, and who had killed the kafirs and the Muslims who had come against them, their hearts were pained. All of their radiant `suwarat` were gathered with Husayn. And those who were dying, whose hearts were pained, all of them were gathered with Shimr Dhil-Jawshan. And Karbala was the stage for this. Karbala was only this event. It was a battle of a short duration, which the Shias narrate in such a lengthy manner, in such a grand manner that if Karbala is taken out of their lives, Shi'ism itself will end. So the matter is that Karbala is very important in this way, that when this battle was being imposed on the Prophet's grandson, Imam Husayn, at that time, angels descended upon you and brought a message and revelation from God, that "O grandson of the Prophet, we want this, God wants this, that if you wish, you will get help. You will get victory. And if you wish, there is also the meeting with God." So "meeting with God" meant that you have to pay the retribution. So the things that have been coming down from your forefathers, do you want to settle them? If so, settle them. Otherwise, how long will that account continue? It will become a long account. If it is settled here, it is good. And if you don't want to, then God is ready to give you help. This was the matter of Karbala for Hazrat Husayn, 'alayhissalatu wassalam. Hazrat Husayn, 'alayhissalatu wassalam, accepted the meeting with his Lord and wanted to settle that account. The ones who were settling the account, from your side, the two biggest reckoners were Hazrat Hani ibn Urwah, Hazrat Muslim, and Hazrat Abbas, your brother. These were the three individuals who settled all these things. And after that, when the Prophet... when Hazrat Husayn was alone, and went before the enemy and stood and recited a eulogy, at that time those people had said, when you asked, "O people, why are you killing me?" those people said, "O Husayn, `bughdan li-abik` (out of hatred for your father), we are killing you because of the enmity towards your father." Those words came to their lips. This was the battle of Khaybar crying out, this was the battle of Badr and Uhud crying out, and all that blood was crying out. And they wanted their hearts to be cooled. And when Shimr... when Khuli ibn Yazid comes, Hazrat Husayn says, "You are not my killer, go back, go back." When Shimr comes, you say, "Move your veil a bit from your face so I can recognize who my killer is." You said, "Indeed, you will have a gap in your teeth, you will have dog-like teeth," and the signs that have been told about my killer, "O Shimr, they are present in you." He said, "I will kill you in a very bad way." Why the signs? What were the signs? Oh, they were seeing all those evil `suwarat`. On this side were the radiant `suwarat`, on that side were all the evil `suwarat`. They killed you, but as I have said, these are people from the Taamur. Oh, Isa was crucified, the Quran is mentioning it, `wa ma qataluhu wa ma salabuhu wa lakin shubbiha lahum` (they did not kill him, nor did they crucify him, but it was made to appear so to them). This is Husayn. Oh, the doorkeeper at whose door is Isa, the doorkeeper is Isa. So you can imagine, how can such a martyrdom of Hazrat Husayn happen? But they killed him thinking he was Husayn. The grief we have to feel, the sorrow we have to feel, the mourning we have to do, is this, that they killed him thinking he was Husayn. In any case, they took out the fever of their hearts, and in this way, they settled their accounts with each other. So in any case, after Karbala, Hazrat Imam Husayn entrusted it to Zayn al-Abidin, Hazrat Ali Zayn al-Abidin to Muhammad Baqir, Hazrat Baqir to Ja'far as-Sadiq. Now this chain of Imamate ran, the chain, and at that time the `hujjat`s, the `du'at`, they were the guardians of Prophethood and Messengership, and they kept it running. Until our 21st Imam came, Maulana Tayyib, who is from the progeny of Hazrat Imam Husayn, Maulana Tayyib, 'alayhissalatu wassalam, who is our venerable Imam. So you, the 21st Imam, saw that now they should go into complete concealment. Just as Husayn was manifest, Hasan was manifest, Ali was manifest, now that time is no more, but now is the time to go into complete concealment. They went into concealment, and after that, all the Imams went into concealment. And they started to make their `du'at` manifest from their side. And from the time of Maulana Dhu'ayb, the chain of `du'at` has been running, which is inscribed in our `sahif-e-maimun-e-marqum`, from Sayyidna Dhu'ayb ibn Musa to Sayyidna Da'ud ibn 'Ajab-Shah. These `du'at al-tayyibiyyin` continued. These are the bearers of Prophethood and Messengership. Even though they are not called prophets or messengers, oh, these are greater than many prophets. The word "rasul" does not come, but they are greater than prophets. Do not consider these `du'at` to be ordinary. Do not think of them as ordinary. These are greater than prophets. And the `anwar` descend upon them. Divine revelation comes to them. This, which we call by the word "ishraq" (illumination). Revelation ended with the Prophet. Messengership ended with the Prophet. Now that name of Messengership and Prophethood will not be used, only the name of `da'wat` (call) and `da'i` (caller) will be used. Now that same chain is running, the luminous chain of `du'at` is running, from Sayyidna Dhu'ayb ibn Musa to Sayyidna Da'ud ibn 'Ajab-Shah it ran. And on this side, from Maulana Tayyib to Sayyidna Ahmad, who was the 35th Imam of Sayyidna Humam, that 35th Imam, it ran till then. This chain ran continuously. The 35th Imam was Maulana Ahmad. You see, some Shias walked with us for some time, they walked till Imam Ja'far as-Sadiq, and after that, the calamity happened that they had appointed their son, Maulana Isma'il, but they said that Maulana Isma'il has passed away, so his other brother, Musa Kazim, became the Imam. So in this way, they also split from here, some changed to Musta'li, some to Nazari, some to Zaydi, some changed at some other place. So in any case, they kept separating from us. The truth continued on its own path. Those who were to turn their faces away from the truth, kept turning. A thousand... until the time of Sayyidna Humam az-Zaman, Sayyidna Sulayman ibn Hasan, came, and you, it was the year 1000 after the passing of the Prophet, 'alayhissalatu wassalam. And Hazrat Sayyidna Humam's time, what can be said of Sayyidna Humam az-Zaman? What mention can I make of that blessed personage? It would require separate gatherings. In any case, he, Sayyidna Sulayman, quddisa llahu ruhuhu, he was the heir of Sayyidna Da'ud ibn 'Ajab-Shah. Until Sayyidna Da'ud ibn 'Ajab-Shah, the era of Muhammad, 'alayhissalatu wassalam, continued. And after that, the `dawr-e-qa'imi` (era of the Qa'im) began. Because for everyone, 1000 years were given. Only Hazrat Isa was given 600 years. Our Prophet was given 1000 years. That 1000 years ended with Sayyidna Humam, and there your era ended. Now the `qa'imi` era began. Sayyidna Sulayman ibn Hasan and the `du'at` who came after him, after him came Sayyidna Ja'far, after him came Sayyidna Mahmud Fahd, after him came Sayyidna Ja'far. Sayyidna Ja'far, Sayyidna Mahmud Fahd, and Sayyidna Ali, and Sayyidna Ibrahim, Sayyidna Hibtullah, this entire chain of `du'at` continued, until today's our Da'i, Sayyidna Husayn bin Hasan bin Abdullah al-Mukrami, 'atala llahu baqahu wa ja'alana fida', are here. And that luminous chain is continuing in its place. Now it is another matter that for their administrative arrangements, they appoint `mansub`s for the administration of the `jaza'ir` (islands/regions), that is a separate thing, but the chain of `du'at` has continued in this way. Those are `du'at-e-mutlaq`, these are `du'at-e-balagh`. There are several types of `du'at`. The chain of `du'at-e-tayyibiyyin` and `du'at-e-qa'imiyyin` you have seen. There are also `du'at-e-qalam` (du'at of the pen) and `du'at-e-sayf` (du'at of the sword). The `du'at` of the sword and the `du'at` of the pen are different. Those who wielded the sword, did jihad, they were the `du'at-e-sayf`. And those who wielded the pen and wrote thousands of books, they were the `du'at-e-qalam`. In the same way, there are types of `du'at`, `munfaridin` (appointed by `nass`) and `ghayr-munfaridin` (not appointed by `nass`). That is, those who are appointed by `nass` and are established, they are `munfarid`. Those who are appointed by `nass` but are not established, they are `ghayr-munfarid`. In the same way, the `du'at` are of types, `mutlaq` (absolute), `balagh` (communicating), and `mahsusur` (confined). `Du'at-e-mahsusur` are those who are confined within a certain city, but their rank is such. `Du'at-e-mutlaq` are those who are masters of the `jazirah` (island/region), one or two. And `du'at-e-balagh` are those, like our Da'i of Yemen, who is Sayyidna Husayn, he is the master of three `jaza'ir`, and he is at the rank of `da'i-e-balagh`.

In the same way, there is another type of `du'at`, which, when Sayyidna al-Bahari came to India, he had made it known at that time, and they are `du'at-e-afrad` and `du'at-e-shumukh`. And among the `du'at-e-afrad` in our tradition, only Sayyidna Sulayman, Sayyidna Ja'far passed, and Sayyidna Ali ibn Hiba passed, and Sayyidna Isma'il ibn Muhammad. These four `du'at-e-afrad` passed. So in any case, you are seeing that their ranks also, according to their own capacity, their `kasb` (earning), their knowledge, have been happening, and this chain of `du'at` is in its own place, and the chain of Imamate is running in its own place. And today's 35th Imam was Sayyidna Humam in his time. After that 35, the chain continued in his progeny. And today's our Imam, Maulana Muhammad ibn Ali, Salawatullahi 'alayh, is our Maula today, our master, the master of the earth and heavens, he is the master of the time, the Imam of the time, the master of the era, and may God continue his blessings and graces upon us all. And you, the station you are at, its knowledge our `du'at` have, and we know, and he is... the curtain cannot be drawn. Whom God protects, who can see him, is the matter. In any case, he is greatly protected, and he has a great court, and it is a great matter. And his station, his residence, his living, all the places, and who are his doorkeepers, who are his servants, how he is protected, his winter stations, his summer stations, all these things are known to us, nothing is hidden from us.

And at this time, our Imam, he is the 48th Imam. From Imam Husayn, 'alayhissalatu wassalam, the chain that is continuing, continuously going through, from Imam Hasan, Imam Husayn, until the 48th Imam who is ours. And you know that after seven weeks, the Qiyamat will happen. Seven sevens are 49. So these are the 48th, so now his son who will be, who will he be? He will be the final Imam. Your son will be our final Imam. And after that, the matter of Qiyamat will begin. And I will give you more details about this. You don't be surprised, but you are the 48th Imam. His son will be Abu al-Qa'im. And his son who will be, he will be Hazrat Qa'im, who is not counted in the lineage. And his `hujjat` who will be, who is in the station of the Prophet, he will be the `hujjat`, and the Qa'im who will be, who will establish the Qiyamat, he will be in the station of Maulana Ali. So just as here there was the matter of the Prophet and Hazrat Ali, in the same way, there will be the matter of Qa'im and Mahdi there, how their manifestation will be, and how it will be. All these details, God willing, will come in the next lesson. And I will also explain something about `jabr` and `qadr` (predestination and free will) and about fate, and God willing, it will reach its conclusion.

A'immah Mustaqarrin or A'immah Mustawda'in... I had explained the silsilah. And that silsilah, from the Qayamat-i A'zam... I, passing through all the periods, from the Qayamat-i A'zam, had started the silsilah. And first, in the daur-i kashf, the daur-i satr, and at the completion of the daur-i satr, I told you that from the Panjatan-i Pak, how imamah and mustawda'iyyat came to them, and in all ages, for every age, as Allah Ta'ala has said, `wa li-kulli qawmin had` (and for every people there is a guide), for every age, there is a guide, a giver of guidance. In every age, a giver of guidance continued to be established, and the A'immah Mustaqarrin were also established by the will of the Maula, and the A'immah Mustawda'in as well. But these silsilahs, they went up to the Payghambar, alaihis-salatu was-salam, and there the nabuwwah ended. And from there, the da'wah began, and that name was changed, and the name of the da'i started to be used. And the hujjat and the du'at began to serve, and the A'immah Kiram were established in their places. And I told you that our 21st Imam, after him, the silsilah of the du'at continued. And I have explained in detail before you regarding that silsilah. But why did Allah Ta'ala keep this silsilah of hidayah in the world at all? What was the need for Allah Ta'ala to have this silsilah of hidayah? You will say that people were gumrah, and they needed hidayah, otherwise what would we have understood? We would not have understood what is halal and what is haram. We wouldn't have understood anything. Because you people know, that's why you understand that because we said labbayk in the other world, we showed nadamah, so here too we showed nadamah, and those who called us, called us, and we accepted. But what needs to be seen is that when the givers of hidayah gave hidayah, did those who were to take hidayah take it? This is the question. The givers of hidayah gave hidayah, and did those who were to take hidayah take it? It doesn't seem so. So, the world remained gumrah. So what does this mean? It means that either, nauzubillah, the givers of hidayah had some deficiency in their hidayah, or they did not guide properly, or they did not give hidayah at all. And those who were to take hidayah, they could not take that hidayah. Meaning, they did not truly take hidayah. The matter is actually that the givers of hidayah, as you have been hearing all the accounts, the givers of hidayah left no stone unturned. They did the royal Imamah from a straw mat. The heavenly kingdom was in their hands. Even if they did not have the apparent khilafah, it did not matter. But they were doing the royal Imamah from the mat, and they were the carriers of the spiritual Imamah, and they consistently, all those things, those points, which I am now explaining before you, a thousand times more was their language, their substance. The anwar-i zakiriyyah descended upon them, the Quran was revealed in their house. They were explaining it and making it understood very well. There was nothing that was not made understandable. But why, then, did that teaching fail? Why did that teaching fail? The matter is actually this: that from their teaching, hidayah was indeed given, but those who did not take hidayah, who turned away from their teaching, only they did not attain hidayah. The clear, logical conclusion is this: that from their teaching, hidayah was being given, but they did not want to take hidayah, and they did not take hidayah. And for this reason, even today, what is it? Do you think that, "Alright, a truth has been revealed, a fact has become known, so we will all accept it"? No. Human nature is of such a kind that it does not accept every truth. It does not take every goodness. It accepts what its heart desires. You understand about namaz, roza, etc., so do you all accept it? You don't accept it. You do it when you want, and when you don't want, you don't do it. So, in the same way, those people, despite being guided, wanted to turn their faces away, so they turned them away. Although you were seeing that it was 'Ali himself, Maula-i Ka'inat himself, who was giving the tafsir of the Quran, solving problems, he was the hallal-i mushkilat. All things... you did it in every khilafah. You did all the work. You compiled the Quran, you told the verses of the Quran, you did its translation, you gave the answers to questions. If this were not so, then Janab-i 'Umar would not have said, `law la 'aliyyul lahalaka 'umar` (Had it not been for 'Ali, 'Umar would have perished). Had it not been for 'Ali, 'Umar would have perished. He would not have said that `'ajzat an-nisa an talidna mithla 'aliyy-ibn-abi-talib` (Women are incapable of giving birth to the like of 'Ali ibn Abi Talib), that women are incapable of giving birth to a person like 'Ali ibn Abi Talib. He confessed. And Janab-i Abu Bakr also did the same. So these ashab, they were from the time of Sayyidna 'Isa. These two, they were from the time of Sayyidna 'Isa, and it was their great desire to become a rasul. It was their great desire to attain the station of the Payghambar, alaihis-salatu was-salam, and they were among his hujjats, among the companions of Sayyidna 'Isa, with Buhayra al-Rahib, and among his companions. But it was their great desire... this is not about Janab-i 'Uthman... these were two. But, despite that, what happened? When they saw that the prophethood of the Prophet could not be attained, and the risalah that you have attained this virtue, they saw that, "Alright, if not this, then at least let's get the wasayah." So anyway, what I am saying to you is that we wanted to remain gumrah, so we remained gumrah. Allah did not want to keep us gumrah. He wanted to give hidayah, and He gives hidayah, and for every qaum, He sends a giver of hidayah. But we did not take hidayah, that is our fault. So, in any case, what needs to be seen is that... in the context of hidayah, the biggest question that comes up is that of qismat and of our taqdir. Now, in this matter, you see that in this whole world, there is no nasl, no color, no qaum, and no place, no [unclear] that does not believe in qismat. Everyone is a believer in qismat. Everyone believes in qismat, that yes, there is qismat, there is qismat. "It was written in our qismat like this," "It is like this in our qismat." Very few, perhaps a handful, will be there who do not believe, but everyone believes that there is qismat, and there is. But what is it? That not everyone relies on qismat. Unfortunately, if anyone does, it's the Muslims. Unfortunately, if there is any qaum in the world that relies on qismat, it is the Muslims. They completely rely on qismat and sit back. And what is the proof of that? That Muslims rely on qismat and are sitting back? If you look, you will find out that Muslims have relied on qismat in such a way that they have placed all responsibility on Allah. That's why they rely on it. They have placed it on Allah, that the source of everything, everything comes from His side. You see, you grab any Muslim and ask, "Well, whatever Allah Ta'ala wills... Whatever Allah Ta'ala commands... Whatever Miyan does..." He who does, Miyan who does... "Brother, this Miyan and Allah, etc., fine, you can call them by these loving names, but what does He do and how does He do it? Do you also do something or not?" "We... we do nothing... Miyan who is the doer, He is the doer, He does it." "Alright, this Miyan does it, Allah does it. So then, how is this?" When they saw that this has now become an internationally accepted principle of ours, they included it in their kalimah tayyibah: `al-khayru washarru min Allahi Ta'ala` (Good and evil are from God Almighty). Good and evil, whatever there is... there are two things... two things... goodness and evil, virtue and vice. There were two things. They said, "Alright, put the responsibility for all things on Allah's shoulders, and we will be saved from everything, that's the best." So on Allah's shoulders... one on the shoulder, nauzubillah, nauzubillah, they put virtue, and on the other, they put vice. They started saying that whatever comes, it all comes from Allah's side. "Brother, if evil comes, it's from Allah's side. If good comes, it's also from Allah's side." Fine, goodness we understand, He is the source of good, but how can this evil be from Him? So now let me ask them a question: "Brother, you... Allah Ta'ala has said this, has He not, that, `A'udhu billahi minash shaytanir rajim` (I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan). Allah Ta'ala says `fasta'idh billah` (seek refuge in Allah), that you should seek refuge from Shaytan, fear his waswasah, and keep yourself in refuge from his whisperings." Has Allah Ta'ala said this or not? "Yes, of course, He has said it, sir. How can you say that? I see it in the Holy Quran everywhere." "So what do you see?" "I see the name on every page, sir. The name of Shaytan al-Rajim is on every page." "Brother, on one page there isn't just one name, but the name of Shaytan is there four or five times." A person was so vexed by this that he erased Shaytan's name. He said, "Four or five names of Shaytan on one page? It would have been better if my forefathers' names were there." He erased the names and wrote his forefathers' names. So now... what can be done? They will be Pathans like that. So anyway, now... Shaytan... when I ask, "Brother, Allah Ta'ala has told you to take refuge from Shaytan, to fear his whisperings, `A'udhu billahi minash shaytanir rajim`... `A'udhu billahi minash shaytanir rajim`... Brother, wherever you are doing a good deed, you are reading it. Wherever there is the command of `fasta'idh billah`, you are following the command." "Brother, what is the need to follow the command? The short answer to this question is, why did Allah Ta'ala create Shaytan in the first place?" Now they are startled. "Sir, how can you... you are challenging the power of Allah Ta'ala." "Sir, I am asking a short question: why did Khuda create Shaytan? If He hadn't created him, this evil wouldn't have come. If the evil hadn't come, we wouldn't have done it, and if we hadn't done it, we wouldn't have been caught. There you go. A clear, logical conclusion. We would not have committed any evil, and the matter would have been settled. So, the fact that Allah Ta'ala created Shaytan became the biggest evil, and because of it, all the problems have arisen." So when Shaytan's existence itself is a [unclear], then the matter is actually that they cannot even comprehend that we have created Shaytan. "He does the evil deed himself and curses Shaytan," it's like that. We have been the cause of Shaytan's existence. And it happened there, as you heard in the original matters, how 'shaytaniyat' came into being and how 'shaytaniyat' proceeded. It's not that Allah Ta'ala, God forbid, created someone as Shaytan, or we named someone Shaytan. There, whoever did what kind of work, that's what happened. Rahman became one of Rahmaniyat, Shaytan became one of Shaytaniyat. Whoever did what kind of work, that was their state. So, fine, this evil was created. So now, the Muslims who say such things, now for that, you should ponder a little: that to attribute every good and every evil to Allah's side, how far is this a correct statement? The matter comes down to this: that the Lord of the worlds, in the Holy Quran, where He has said, there... did He not give us the ability to act in this 'abode of action'? Did He not say that this is the 'abode of action', here you should strive and act, you should try? Look, there is Jannah and there is Jahannam. If you do good work, you will go to Jannah. If you do bad work, you will go to Jahannam. If there were no Jannah and no Jahannam, no goodness and no evil, no afkar and no akhlaq would remain, nothing would remain. When you rely on qismat like this, then nothing will remain. Nothing will last. So then, Allah Ta'ala's saying, you see, in the Holy Quran, where Muslims pin everything on Allah, then why did the Lord of the worlds say this in the Holy Quran: `lay salil insani illa ma sa'a` (And that man can have nothing but what he strives for). That for man there is nothing except what he has strived for. Now, a moment of thought... they fell into thought, why did Allah Ta'ala say that `lay salil insani illa ma sa'a`. Then Allah Ta'ala also says, `dhalika taqdirul 'azeezil 'alim` (That is the decree of the Exalted in Might, the All-Knowing), that these are the decrees of Allah Ta'ala. There can be no questioning of the decrees. Whatever Allah Ta'ala wills, He does. These are matters of His taqdir. So if these are matters of taqdir, and this is so, then it means there is both jabar and qadr. It means there is qismat and also some matters of ikhtiyar. And so this dual state, how is it?
