But Ali is the one who, when he was called Allah, he... said, "Calling me a bandah, say whatever you want to say." That is correct. From an 'itibar. So... the matter of Ali... and in my opinion, you see that... people make progress, they do... whatever... the entire system... in this system of cycles, lakhs and crores of years will pass. Who knows how long life keeps going on, what it is. In doing this, all the people who are there, they keep doing. Now among them, who is the most fa'iz (victorious)? Maulana al-Sa'ins is a great personality, who is everyone's... guardian. Or... who is the founder of the دور (era). But after that, in making progress, the next station is of Maulana Ali. The station of Wasi. So he who made efforts, all the things that do not come into our understanding, he became the most excellent and fa'iz. So there is a saying in Arabic, man jadda wajada (he who strives, finds). That he who tried the most, he moved forward. Man jadda wajada. He who tries will move forward. You see, the one who prays the most will go to Jannat al-Milla (paradise of the community). Not just praying, one has to become worthy of leading prayers. He is made so. Just reading the prayers, everyone does. Becoming worthy of leading prayers. So man jadda wajada, this... for this, no one has made as much effort as Ali. That is why, from the letters of Ali, if you look at the abjad, it is man jadda wajada, the same letters are there. 110. Man jadda wajada. So this... to understand the maratib (ranks)... now this month is of Rajab. It is the month of Maulana Ali. And Rajab is the seventh month. And you are the seventh... wasi (successor). A great haysiyat (status) of yours is in the 'alam. Founder of the Imams. Abu 'l-A'immah (Father of the Imams). The counting of the Imams started from you. We are in this... dawr-e Muhammadi (era of Muhammad). From the lineage of Adam, two ummahs have passed. In the time of Nuh, there were very great people. They would have been. Now you understand that this entire... the ma'lumat (knowledge) will be known. In every era, people are becoming, and moving forward. That was also an ummah, that was also an ummah. But the last ummah that is, it is the essence of everything. That is why the Prophet's... this ummah is the most excellent. Because this verse came down, al-yawma akmaltu lakum dinakum wa-atmamtu 'alaykum ni'mati (This day I have perfected for you your religion and completed My favor upon you). Wa-raditu lakum al-islama dina (and have approved for you Islam as religion). Remember that this is the most excellent ummah. In this, in the dawr-e satr, ummahs have passed. In which cycle we have come, who knows. Whether we are from the fourth, or from the fifth, or from the twelfth, only Allah knows. But we are. We must be somewhere. But even if we have come as an ummati, today we are members of the most excellent ummah. Among those who believe in the Prophet. And the Prophet is the most excellent. The Prophet is the one who attained a very high level. The station of Mi'raj (ascension). The Prophets there had Mi'raj. Many... all had Mi'raj. You hear in the events that Janab-e Musa was on the fourth heaven. But the Prophet reached the seventh heaven. So the seven heavens are seven layers, which the Prophet crossed and went. All this is to be understood. What are the meanings of Mi'raj? What is Mi'raj? I have explained before, the meanings of Mi'raj... that mim is for the Prophet, and... what is it? It is for Ali. 'Ayn is for Ali. Wherever these two words are, mim is for the Prophet, and... 'ayn is for Ali. Mi'raj. And I understand that the Mi'raj that happened, you know the events, that when the Prophet reached the seventh heaven, Ali was already present there. You said, "Brother Jibra'il, Ali is present here before me." Then Janab-e Jibra'il said, "Ya Rasulullah, all the angels, the mala'ikah, had a desire for the didar (vision) of Ali." So Allah Ta'ala created one angel in the form of Ali. So the point is that Ali was present there too. Where the Prophet was reaching, he was... Now look, the Prophet was reaching. Ali was present. So Mi'raj is mim and 'ayn. Mim... it has never happened that where the Prophet is, Ali is not there. We always read salawat on the Prophet and on the Al (progeny) of the Prophet. Until... you cannot leave it out. In the salawat, you take the name of the Prophet, and do not say "wa 'ala alihi." It is necessary that... So the nafs (self) of the Prophet is the being of Janab-e Ali. Remember that mim and 'ayn are so joined that it is ma'a (with). Always together. Mim and 'ayn. And in my opinion, that... the prayers of both of them... you take them out and see. Whether... take the prayer of... all the great Prophets who have passed, who rescued Yusuf from the well? Who took Yunus out from the belly of the fish? Whose boat of Nuh was brought to shore? All these, who was it, who was it, who was it? In which it has come. That Janab-e... Prophet Sallallahu 'Alayhi wa Sallam and Janab-e Ali were there. Who did the guidance of all the Prophets throughout the dawr-e satr, from Adam to here? Who did it? In what names they did it? You will know as you read. So the point is that mim and 'ayn have ruled the entire world. From there to... from Adam to here, their rule has been in place. You can see for yourself. Whose... who did it? Janab-e Prophet... and the... that existed was... So just as Prophet and Janab-e mim and 'ayn, their government was, in the same way, if we... we are in Hindustan. We, with this understanding, that mim and 'ayn have had a crown. No one else in this world has ruled. And this is Mi'raj. For mim and 'ayn to rule, this is Mi'raj. That the Prophet was shown that the seven heavens... what ranks you have been given the excellence of. From the perspective of nubuwwat (prophethood), from the perspective of risalat (messengership), from the perspective of walayat (guardianship of the Prophet), from the perspective of natiqiyat (speakership), from the perspective of mustawda' (trusteeship), from the perspective of mustaqarr (permanent abode)... from what perspective have you been given? To understand this is the excellence of the din. From day to night... Gradually, gradually, if you understand... so the baat (inner meaning) will develop. But I am giving this talk from this perspective, that it is the month of Janab-e Ali. To understand his maratib (ranks). To understand his hijabat (veils). To understand his... to know his qualities. To know his questions. And in practical life, how much he supported the Prophet, and besides that, in the ranks, which ranks you are attaining. And how the Prophet... still, the relative position between them, of the Prophet and Janab-e Ali, to maintain that while going. This is the delicate issue. Which is very... very... it is subtle. Very fine. To understand this. You don't make him bigger than this, nor smaller than that. A little bit here and there, and the matter is over. Then mentally, it is finished. Remember that in din... to understand the maratib is what... is the... Wal-hamdu lillahi rabb al-'alamin. Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim. Al-Fatihah.

Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim. *'ani al-sadiq 'alayhi al-salam ma'na qawlihi 'alayhi al-salam bana Allah al-Islam 'ala sab'i da'a'im, al-wilayah wa hiya afdaluhu wa biha wa bil-wali yusalu ila ma'rifatiha*.

The meaning of his statement is that Islam was established on seven pillars, and *wilayah* is the most excellent among them. And through it and through the *wali*, one reaches gnosis (*ma'rifah*).

*wa Taharah wa-l-salah wa-l-zakah wa-l-sawm wa-l-hajj wa-l-jihad*.

*naqulu wa billahi ta'ala subhanahu inna hadha al-sab'a da'a'im tamthaluha fawa'idu usulihi allati ikhtaradaha Allahu 'ala 'ibadihi*. Now, see, he is explaining it in a different way. That, just as... *wilayah* is there. After the Prophet, there is Janab 'Ali, his... they are. The *wilayah* of *Amir al-Mu'minin* and all the pure Imams (*A'imma Tahirin*).

Now he is saying here that *wilayah* is upon Janab Adam. Because the command for prostration (*sajdah*) was first given there. And for obedience (*ta'at*). Now it will come. Read.

*wa fawa'id usuluhu*. Yes. First is... what is it? There is *wilayah*, then there is *taharah* (purity). After that is *salah* (prayer). The third one.

*wa fawa'idu usulihi allati iftaradaha Allahu 'ala 'ibadihi wa laha fi ta'wil al-batin amsalun 'ala... amsalun*. And... in the esoteric interpretation (*batin*), there is an example. An example.

*wal-wilayah mithluha mithl Adam*. And *wilayah*, its example is like Adam. The example of *wilayah* is like that of Adam, *'alayhi al-salam*. *li-annahu awwalu man iftarada Allahu wilayahatahu*. Because he was the first person whose *wilayah* was made obligatory. *wa amara al-mala'ikata bil-sujud*. And the angels were commanded to prostrate. The angels were commanded to prostrate to Adam.

So, *wilayah* was the first thing established in the world, upon Adam.

*wa lahu bil-sujud. wa-l-sujud wa-l-ta'ah*. And the angels were commanded... Who were the angels? Tell me. Who were these angels that were commanded to prostrate to Adam?

*hudud*. The *mala'ikah* are the noble *hudud* who were in the presence of Janab Hunayd. They are called *mala'ikah*. The *mala'ikah* are not those who are unseen beings... the `*mala'ikah bil-quwwah*` (angels by potential) who were...

*wa-l-sujud wa-l-ta'ah hiya al-wilayah*. And to prostrate and to obey, that was the *wilayah*. *wa la budda li-jami' al-khalq min i'tiqad al-wilayatihi*. And there is no... it is necessary for all of creation to have faith in his *wilayah*. So, *wilayah* started from Adam, *'alayhi al-salam*. Now, regarding Janab 'Ali, we say that because the era (*dawr*) has changed... and it is also necessary, as his successor (*wasi*). But the beginning was from there.

*wa man lam yatawallahu wa lam yuti'hu lam yanfa'hu wilayahatuhu min ba'dihi li-annahu awwalu man awjaba Allahu wilayahatahu*. After *wilayah*, nothing will benefit him, because Allah, the Exalted, made *wilayah* the first thing obligatory. *wilayati min rusulihi wa anbiya'ihi*.

*wa awwaluhum wa afdaluhum Adam*. Adam is the first. They are... this... *wilayah* was made obligatory upon them. First believe in Adam, then you will reach Nuh. So the chain (*silsilah*) of *wilayah* is for Janab Adam.

*wa-l-taharah mithluha mithl Nuh, salawatullahi 'alayh*. Now, see, the interpretation (*tawjih*) is completely different. In another place, in the stages of the embryo (*janin*), what is Janab Nuh? *Nutfa* (sperm-drop). *Sulalah* (extract) is Janab Adam. *Nutfa* is Janab Nuh. *'Alaqah* (clot) is Janab Ibrahim. Remember all of this. The first is... of... is *sulalah*. Now that is from a different perspective, but here he is saying that *taharah* (purity) is Janab Nuh. The connection of *taharah* with Janab Nuh is not immediately understood, but the interpretation is given. Let's see the interpretation, how it is.

*wa-huwa awwalu mab'uthin min qibal Allahi li-tathir al-'ibad*. And *taharah*... an example. Meaning, now... what is it? The rank of Adam, *'alayhi al-salam*, was that of a *Natiq*. But the first of the *Ulu al-'Azm* (Prophets of Firm Resolve) prophets was Janab Nuh. His rank is higher. And in your time, you made *taharah* obligatory upon all servants. Purity from sins (*ma'asi*), and worship (*'ibadah*), to purify the servants... from sins.

...so that the servants are purified of their sins. `*allati iqtarafuha min ba'd Adam*` (which they committed after Adam). Meaning, after Adam, when a long time had passed, many things in the pillars were weakening. As always happens, when an era ends, many people become lazy, they abandon things... like in today's age. That was happening. So Janab Nuh was created, and it started with *taharah*. *Taharah* is done with water. And water came in the time of Janab Nuh. The flood that came. What was that flood? Janab Sam. Janab Sam is your *wasi* (successor). The disobedient nation... he said, "O Allah, drown all these people." This kind of curse comes from prophets, never from an Imam. Because people do not listen. You tried for your entire life, the age of Nuh was long. Common people say he lived for 900 years, but 900 years was his era (*dawr*). His age was 120 years. At that time, when he prayed, water gushed from the *tannur* (oven/source). Meaning, Janab Sam spoke such words of wisdom that all the corrupt people were drowned. Even Nuh's son was finished. So this is *taharah*, see. And after Adam, he was the first *Natiq*. Meaning, after Adam, if there was a *Natiq*, it was Janab Nuh. And he is not just a *Natiq* but also an *Ulu al-'Azm* prophet. *awwal ulu al-'azm min al-rusul*. The possessors of the *Shari'ah*. *wa ja'ala Allahu ayatihi allati ja'a biha al-ma'*. And for you, Allah made signs that the water brought. `*alladhi ja'alat bihi al-taharah*` (with which purity is done). A sign was made for you. When Nuh's name comes, one thinks of the Ark (*safinah*) or the flood. For Ibrahim, it is that he built the Ka'bah. The architect of the Ka'bah is Janab Ibrahim. And here, from one perspective, Janab Nuh is what? Every prophet had a profession. In terms of profession, he was a carpenter (*najjar*), Janab Nuh. But here, the water was made a sign for you. When did the water come? In the time of Nuh. Why did it come? For purification from sins. And that is Janab Nuh.

*wa-l-salah mithluha mithl Ibrahim, 'alayhi al-salam. wa-huwa alladhi bana al-bayt qiblatan wa-l-maqam musalla*. Now see, when an esoteric interpretation (*ta'wil*) is given, the *ta'wil* is not the reality, but it is a path to reach the reality. He has mentioned two *ta'wils* before. Now he is giving this one. This fits perfectly, there is no flaw anywhere. If there is a flaw, it is in your minds, not here. This is also there, that Ibrahim is prayer. Why? The *Shari'ah* essentially begins with prayer. And from Ibrahim, *tawhid* (monotheism) began. This is a very high rank. And another point is that Ibrahim, *'alayhi al-salam*, is in the stage of *'alaqah* (clot). The stage of the human embryo, the real creation, begins from the *'alaqah*.

*wa-huwa alladhi bana al-bayt*. And he was the one who... `*musalla, mithl Ibrahim 'alayhi al-salam, wa-huwa alladhi bana al-bayt wa-l-qiblatan wa-l-maqam musalla*` (a place of prayer, like Ibrahim, peace be upon him, and he is the one who built the House and the *qiblah* and the station as a place of prayer). And you are the ones who built the Ka'bah, the *qiblah*, and the *maqam*... The *Maqam*, you understand, the Station of Ibrahim, where one prays two *rak'at* of prayer. He made the station its... he made it a *qiblah* and he made it a station.

*qala Allahu ta'ala: wa-idh yarfa'u Ibrahimu al-qawa'id min al-bayt*. And Allah, the Exalted, has said that when Ibrahim raised the foundations of the House. *wa Isma'il, rabbana taqabbal minna*. And Isma'il. "Our Lord, accept from us." Meaning, Janab Ibrahim and Isma'il together built the Ka'bah. When? In the time of Adam, by Allah's command, it was built. In the time of Nuh, it was lifted up during the flood. This is a tradition, history. Then who built it? The Ka'bah was broken many times, seven times it has happened so. So the rebuilding that happened after Nuh, Janab Ibrahim built it. Now, in this building, the wisdom is that Janab Isma'il and Ibrahim are called the architects of the Ka'bah. Just as the Prophet broke the idols. The Prophet and 'Ali broke them. But here, Janab Isma'il... one was standing, one was on top of the other, and he was placing the bricks. This act of placing bricks is a physical manifestation, but what were they actually doing, Janab Ibrahim and Isma'il? In their progeny (*dhurriyyah*), after you, Janab Khayzar was appointed, after Khayzar, Nabat, after Nabat, Salama. These are the foundations (*qawa'id*). The chain of Imams that was started, one after the other.

Just as it happened in the time of the Prophet. The Prophet gave the command in his own time. That after me, 'Ali, you are the chief. After you, Hasan. Hasan was sitting there. Hasan will remain the Imam. No one can say anything. And after Hasan, Husayn. And Husayn, after you, this child who is sitting, 'Ali. 'Ali Zayn al-'Abidin. He was five years old. This 'Ali Zayn al-'Abidin will be the Imam. And 'Ali, you will have a son whose name will be Muhammad. You prophesied this. Muhammad al-Baqir. And convey my *salam* to him. What does conveying *salam* mean? That the *suwar al-'aql* (forms of the intellect) were distributed. And the second thing was what? In terms of name. Muhammad, Muhammad. The Imams who have the name of the Prophet, all of them are receiving a special grace (*wasilah*), something. 'Ali is also there. What are the names of the Imams? Look, 'Ali, Ahmad... these are the names that continue. So they don't just appear like that. There are blessings that are being received.

*Isma'il, rabbana taqabbal minna, innaka anta al-sami' al-'alim*. And accept from us, O Allah... for you... you are the All-Hearing, All-Knowing.

*wa-l-zakah mithluha mithl Musa, 'alayhi al-salam. wa-huwa awwal man da'a ila Allahi*. And *Zakah*, its example is like Prophet Musa, *'alayhi al-salam*. He was the first who called to his Lord. `*wa qawluhu ta'ala: fa-qul hal laka ila an tazakka*` (And His, the Exalted's, statement: And say to him, 'Would you [be willing to] purify yourself?'). "Say, that what... I... that you... I purify you." So, for the first time, the command for *Zakah* came in the time of Prophet Musa. This is an example. The example of purification. *Zakah* means to purify. Now, the purification of wealth is different, and *tazakka* is different. *Zakat al-mal*. Now when the explanations of *Zakah* come, look there. In the era of Muhammad, to whom does *Zakah* go? In the time of the Prophet, who was the recipient? `*aqimu al-salah wa atu al-zakah*` (Establish the prayer and give the *Zakah*). Establish the prayer, and give the *Zakah*. Establishing prayer is Janab Prophet. And *Zakah* is 'Ali. If you want to be purified, be purified through the *wilayah* of 'Ali. *Zakah* is superior to fasting (*sawm*). Fasting comes after it. After prayer, if there is anything... it is always `*aqimu al-salah wa atu al-zakah*`. This is... deep matters. Remember all of this.

*wa-l-sawm mithluhu mithl 'Isa, 'alayhi al-salam*. And... see, for everything, there is an example, a story behind it. And fasting is... 'Isa, *'alayhi al-salam*. *wa-huwa awwal man khatabathu ummuhu*. And he was the first whose mother addressed him. The mother... they addressed his mother. Yes. His mother was addressed. *bi-qawlihi: fa-imma tarayinna min al-bashari ahadan fa-quli...* (with His statement: And if you see from among humanity anyone, say...). So Janab Maryam said, "No man has touched me. I will observe a fast of silence." A fast of silence. So fasting began in the time of Janab 'Isa. And that example is given. And in the *Asas* books, this is all there. Who Maryam was, what fasting means, it is... there are extensive explanations. Pages upon pages.

*min al-bashari ahadan fa-quli inni nadhartu lil-rahmani sawman fa-lan ukallima al-yawma insiyya*. That I have vowed a fast to Allah, that I will not speak to any human today.

`*wa-l-hajj*` (And the Hajj). Now it has come at the end. After fasting is Hajj. `*mathaluhu mathal Muhammad, sallallahu 'alayhi wa sallam. Huwa awwal man aqama al-manasik wa-l-sunan bi-sunnatihi*` (Its example is like Muhammad, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him. He is the first to establish the rites and the traditions according to his tradition). And the Prophet... Hajj, its example is Muhammad, *sallallahu 'alayhi wa sallam*. And he is the first who established the rites and the way. Hajj used to happen before as well. Even in the era of *jahiliyyah* (ignorance), people performed Hajj. It's a tradition. The polytheists (*mushrikin*)... Hindus, whoever they were... the idol-worshippers, they also did. They used to circumambulate continuously. They considered the Ka'bah to be a great thing and circumambulated it. Why did they circumambulate? Because there were idols placed inside it. Just like today they circumambulate a temple, there's an idol inside, so they circumambulate. The Prophet removed the idols. When? When the command from Allah came. But the Prophet established the rites (*manasik*). *Manasik* means to recite the supplications (*du'as*), and to remove all the idols. He removed the idols and established the rites. At every station (*rukn*), he recited the supplications. Before this, what used to happen in *jahiliyyah* was that nothing was recited. They just walked around. Like the Hindus who walk around today, they just walk. We don't just walk, we recite supplications. And in a state of nudity (*'uryan*). They used to circumambulate in a naked state. This... see, it will come now. `*wa ghayraha min al-umam tahujju al-bayta fi jahiliyyah wa la tuqim*` (And other than them from the nations, they would perform Hajj of the House in *jahiliyyah* and not establish...). `*wa kanat al-'arab wa ghayraha min al-umam tahujju al-bayta fi al-jahiliyyah*` (And the Arabs and other than them from the nations would perform Hajj of the House in *jahiliyyah*). And they used to perform Hajj in the era of *jahiliyyah*, they did Hajj. And some things... there was no... they did not have... *wa la tuqim sha'a'ira manasikihi*. They would do as they pleased, there was no specific rite. Backwards and forwards, there was no rite. As Allah, the Exalted, says: `*qala Allahu ta'ala 'anhum*` (Allah, the Exalted, said about them...). As Allah, the Exalted, said about them, in His statement: `*wa-ma kana salatuhum 'ind al-bayt illa muka'an wa-tasdiyatan*` (And their prayer at the House was not except whistling and clapping). Their prayer at the House was nothing but... it was irregular, without rules, there was no form of prayer. `*wa-kanu yatufuna bihi 'uratan*` (And they used to circumambulate it naked). And they would do *tawaf* naked, in a bare state. *wa kana awwalu shay'in... na'am, anhu*. And the first thing that the Prophet forbade... Yes. *fa-qala fi 'umratihi allati i'tamara qabla fath makkah*. And he said in his *'umrah* which he performed before the conquest of Makkah... Yes. And... *fa-qala fi 'umratihi*. And he said in his *'umrah*, such that... The conquest of Makkah happened in the 8th year. So first he performed *'umrah*, and at that time he forbade them, that from now on, you will not perform circumambulation in that naked state. `*ba'da an wada'a ahlaha wa hum mushrikun*` (after he had made an agreement with its people, while they were polytheists). They were polytheists. *an la yatufu ba'da hadha al-bayta 'uryanun*. That they should not circumambulate this house after this, naked. *wa la 'uryanatun*. Neither naked women nor men. *wa kanu qad nasabu hawla al-bayti asnaman*. And they had installed idols around the House. They had installed them before. They were already installed. *wa lahum ya'budunaha*. And they used to worship them. *fa-lamma fataha sallallahu 'alayhi wa sallam makkah kasaraha wa azalaha*. And when he conquered Makkah, *sallallahu 'alayhi wa sallam*, he broke them and removed them. Just as the era of polytheism was dominant. And you came and broke them, you and Janab 'Ali. 'Umar did not come, nor did Abu Bakr. You two broke them together. Then, in the esoteric sense, those who had become gods, like Lat and 'Uzza, etc. It is even said that they were personalities. Lat too. When Lat died, because he was a landlord (*jagirdar*), it was a feudalistic civilization. The landlord would feed 50 people. Those people all thought, "He is our provider. Whatever he gives, he is giving it to us." There was no need to earn. We are getting food. When he died, they became troubled. So what to do? They made his idol. Lat, 'Uzza. 'Uzza was a goddess. And Hubal. All these idols were from before the time of *jahiliyyah*. This is a turn of an era, that this happens, and then someone comes to break it. And Janab Prophet and Janab 'Ali came and eradicated all polytheism (*shirk*). Eradicating *shirk* is a great achievement. And in such a place where *shirk* was rampant. Today, if you want to eradicate idolatry in India, what kind of person would you need? Like that, the Prophet came in Arabia. At that time, of the known world, the worst civilization was that of Arabia. And he made those people such that people learned civilization by looking at the Arabs. He changed them so much. The effort of 23 years. *wa kana al-hajj khatimat al-a'mal al-mafrudah*. And Hajj was the last of the obligatory deeds. And now see, obligatory deeds. He has left out *jihad*. The special point is this. *Jihad* is the last pillar. *Jihad* is not an action (*'amal*). It is an action that will be in the hands of Janab Qaim. So the completion of actions is with Hajj. Just as the completion of all the *Shari'ahs* was with the *Shari'ah* of the Prophet. `*al-yawma akmaltu lakum dinakum*` (This day I have perfected for you your religion). So the pillar of Hajj... and another thing is that Hajj and *Jihad* are the last ones, the sixth and seventh, they go together. Just like me and the *Sa'* (the Hour). `*ana wa-l-sa'ah ka-hatayn*` (I and the Hour are like these two [fingers]). We two are like this. I have gone a little ahead. The Prophet says. I have gone a little ahead, meaning my Hajj... my period came a little earlier, and Janab Qaim is coming later. We were both walking together. From the realm of thought (*fikr*). *wa kana salawatullah 'alayh khatim al-nabiyyin wa lam yabqi ba'da al-hajj min da'a'im al-islam*. And after Hajj, nothing remains from the pillars of Islam. You are the last of the prophets. And after Hajj, nothing remained, after... from the pillars of Islam. *ghayr al-jihad*. Except *jihad*. *wa-huwa mithl al-sabi'*. And he is like the Seventh. *wa-huwa mithl al-sabi' min al-a'immah alladhina yakhrujuna sab'a usbu'in al-akhir alladhi huwa sab'u al-qiyamah*. And he is like the seventh of the Imams, who will appear in the seventh week, which is the last, which is the week of the Resurrection. This is from the *Dawr al-Tayyib*, this book. And *Sahib al-Uzbu'*, that is, in the 49th. From the 49th week, the Resurrection will begin. *Sahib al-Uzbu'* will be in the 49th. The seventh week. Read. *Wa in kana li-ghayri ma'nan, fa ma-l-farqu baynahuma wa bayna sa'iri-l-a'fal?* (and if it is without a meaning, then what is the difference between it and all other actions?). Yes. The answer is: *al-jawabu... rataba 'ala usul-ish-shari'ah... rataba... rataba 'ala usul-ish-shari'ah 'ala ma yujibu-t-ta'wil. Wa dhalika ka-l-fardi fi-l-wudu*. Now it begins with *wudu* (ablution), because *taharat* (purification). *Taharat* is general (*'ammah*) and there is a specific *taharat* (*khassah*). And this, in *wudu*, it is explained that through *wudu* itself, one gets entry into prayer (*namaz*). Meaning, if you have performed *wudu* correctly, then your adherence to prayer has begun, understand it to be so.

And *wudu*, in it, what things have been taught?

The *wudu*, which... In this will come that the *farai'dh* (obligations) of *wudu*. The *farai'dh* are separate, the *sunan* (recommended practices) are separate. What has come in the *Qur'an-e Majeed* is the most true (*asdaq*). Meaning, it is the best. And what is it? *Faghsilu wujuhakum wa aydiyakum* (So wash your faces and your hands). You, your... what is it? *Faghsilu wujuhakum*. You wash your faces. Now look, the face is a sign of a person. And it is an identity. The face. Wash the faces. *Faghsilu wujuhakum*. *Faghsilu*, meaning wash with water. You are not to do *masah* (wiping). *Faghsilu wujuhakum wa aydiyakum*. If, instead of *masah*, you did *ghusl* (washing), then your *wudu* is not valid. *Faghsilu wujuhakum wa aydiyakum*. And these two, up to the elbows. This bone must get wet. This hand like this. *Faghsilu wujuhakum wa aydiyakum. Wamsahu...* (So wash your faces and your hands. And wipe...). And do *masah* (wiping). Wipe your heads and your feet.

Instead of *masah*, the common people (*'awam*) wash. It is wrong. Washing is not right. If you have to wash, then wash before the *wudu*. When you make the intention (*niyyah*) for *wudu*, after that, you should do *masah*.

Why should you do *masah*? Because, as I have said before, *masah* uses less water, *ghusl* uses more. So, the limbs that need more water, more should be applied there; where less is needed, less should be applied.

Meaning, regarding *wudu*, you may wash before it or wash after it, it's fine, but it should not happen during the *wudu*.

*rataba 'ala ha-r-rusul 'ala ma yujibu-t-ta'wil* (The messengers established it according to what necessitates interpretation). What is it? The *rasul*... *'ala ma yujibu-t-ta'wil*. *Wa-r-rijlanu mithlun 'ala-l-imami wa-l-hujjat*. Here too, look. These two, just as there is the *Imam* and the *Wasi*... or rather, the *Imam* and the *Hujjat*. And it is not perceptible. Just as if someone is a *mushrik* (polytheist), you find out that it is clear that this person is a *mushrik*. This person is a *kafir* (disbeliever), so he is a *kafir*. But a *munafiq* (hypocrite) is not known. Just as a *munafiq* is not known, similarly, this passing of wind is not known. The person himself doesn't know. Hearing from one ear and letting it out the other is also. The meaning of tunnel is this. *Nafaq*. *Nafaq* is a hole in which one goes and then turns back. That is *nifaq*.

So that... *'an ahl-il-haqq*. See, this... this is what? *taharatu min-al-ahdathi-z-zahirah mithlun 'ala-l-'ilmi-l-ma'khudhi 'an-il-haqq*. And with this, the souls are purified, from sins and beliefs. And from this, our sins and beliefs are reduced, that we are leaving all these things, *shirk*. We... Allah is... *la sharika lahu* (He has no partner). It should be in your mind that *la sharika lahu*. He has no partner. One must be saved from *shirk*.

The highest rank is the *Da'i*. From the *Da'i*, it will go to the *Ma'zuns*, then it will come down, it will come down. So what is it? "In your concealment, the moon (*qamar*) is giving light." Meaning, if the correspondence (*tanazuma*) is that the *Payghambar*, if he is in the position of the sun, then in the position of the moon is Janab 'Ali al-Murtada. These two completed their دورs and passed away. Who is there now? Now there is the *Imam* and the *Hujjat* (*Hujjat* meaning our *Da'i*). The light is coming to them. From them, it is being distributed. The outward is not that... this is a different matter. It is all coming through them. So, "In your concealment, the moon is giving light. And taking brilliance (*ziya*) from you, it is giving light (*nur*)." It is taking *ziya*. The light of the sun is called *ziya*. And what is it giving? *Nur*. The light of the moon is called *nur*. So what the *Da'i* is getting, we don't get that. Meaning, it comes filtered. From top to bottom... The *mustafid* (beneficiary), however much benefit we are getting... The earned (*kasab*) is separate, and the gifted (*mawhub*) is separate. *Mawhub* is a gifted state that comes from above. The rest, whatever is there, is according to one's earning. So you cannot leave *kasab* either. You can't leave *kasab*, nor... *mawhub* is not in your control. Whatever the Giver gave, He gave. But *kasab*... it's not that if you become a great scholar, you put away the books. "I have become a great scholar." No. You have to keep reading. Just as several such great scholars have passed who, until their last breath, said, "I am a student (*talib-e 'ilm*)." So one has to study. You have *kasab* until the last moment of your life. Whether *mawhub* happens or not, as much grace as you have from Allah, that much you will receive.

*Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim*... *Al-Fatiha*.

*A'udhu billahi min-an-naar min-ash-shaytan-il-la'in-ir-rajim wa bi afdhal Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim. Wa-s-salatu wa-s-salamu 'ala sayyid al-mursalin, khatim an-nabiyyin, an-Nabi al-amjad bi-l-Qasim Muhammad. Wa 'ala sahib al-mafakhir wa-l-manasib, imam al-mashariq wa-l-magharib, ghalib 'ala kulli ghalib, Mawlana 'Ali ibn Abi Talib. Wa 'ala mishkat al-anwar, khulasat al-jawharat al-Islamiyyah, Mawlatina Fatima, salamullahi 'alayha. Wa 'ala imamayn al-humamayn wa-s-sibtayn al-fadilayn wa-l-qamarayn al-bazighayn, Sayyidana wa Mawlana Abi Muhammad al-Hasan, wa Sayyidana wa Mawlana Abi 'Abdillah al-Husayn. Wa ba'dahu wahidan ba'da wahid, ila sahib al-'asr wa-z-zaman, mawla al-bakht wa-l-awan, qarin al-Qur'an, Hujjat al-Rahman, Imam al-ins wa-l-jan, yambu' al-fiqh al-zahirah, wa thamrat tilka al-ashjar al-tahirah, Sayyidana wa Mawlana Muhammadin 'Ali, salawatullahi 'alayh. Wa ba'dahu wahidan ba'da wahid ila sahib al-qiyamah, wa sallam 'alayhim ajma'in.*

There are people sitting in the Jamat Khana.

*Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim.*

Respected brothers, as you know, tonight is a very blessed night. And in it, many virtues are combined. You heard the high sermon from Hazrat Qibla, according to the principles of Mufaddal, about what blessings today holds. In today's date and in today's day and night, great virtues have been gathered. It is also the Shab-e-Meraj, it is also the Wiladat of Amir al-Mu'minin, Salawatullah 'alayh, and tomorrow morning, meaning at the time of Zuhr, the Prophet of Both Worlds, the Master of the Universe, Salawatullah 'alayh, was commissioned.

We always read the history of Islam, and we know how Islam began and how Islam started here. May Allah grant us all the ability to know the history of how the Prophet of Both Worlds initiated it in his time.

As Hazrat Qibla told you, what is the blessing of the Ka'batullah, and by what measure is it? The designated spot, which is the Rukhamat al-Hamra, the blessing of that place, where Hazrat Qibla had gone with Baba Hazrat Muqaddas and obtained blessings, very few people are fortunate enough to receive those. This is a very special matter, that whoever goes there knows, whoever has read knows, and whoever is aware knows what its blessings and what its secrets are. What kind of place is it? As Hazrat Qibla told, the dome was built there in the beginning, the beginning of the world started from there, and every Hajj al-Da'iyyah also takes place there. Which part is it, what is it? All these are things to be read. Anyway, leaving all that aside, because I am speaking in accordance with Hazrat Qibla, I am narrating that we have to narrate the historical biography, about how much hardship the Prophet of Both Worlds endured to establish and start Islam.

Your first kalima, which you proclaimed, was that I will continue to do jihad until the people recite *La ilaha illa-llah*. *Qulu La ilaha illa-llah tuflihu* (Say there is no god but Allah and you will be successful). This was the first kalima of Janaab-e-Paygambar, Salawatullah 'alayh. Islam started from here, on the peaks of Faran, and you challenged them at the age of 40, when a person's age of maturity is reached; at that time you recited the kalima. And as you know, the Prophet has said: *Kuntu Nabiyyan wa Adamu bayn al-ma'i wa-t-tin* (I was a Prophet when Adam was between water and clay). I was a prophet even then, when Janaab-e-Adam, Salawatullah 'alayh, was between water and clay. "Between water and clay" means that when he was in the stages of Shari'ah and Ta'wil, I had already become a prophet even then. The rank of a Nabi, while it is very high in terms of the lower ranks, has several ranks above it. A Nabi is a small rank among the foundational ranks, and after that is Risalat, after Risalat is Natiqiyyat, after Natiqiyyat are the Ulul 'Azm prophets, and after that is the rank of Khullat. There are many things that the Prophet of Both Worlds has attained.

So the meaning is that Janaab-e-Paygambar was granted Risalat at the age of 40. And this was the final Shari'ah which you have completed. In the stages of revelation, Janaab-e-Adam is first, and after him is Janaab-e-Nuh, Ibrahim, Musa, Isa, and Janaab-e-Paygambar. Just as from the *sulalah* (essence) it begins, there is *sulalah*, then *nutfah* (sperm-drop), then *'alaqah* (clot), then *mudghah* (lump of flesh), and then *'izam* (bones), and then the stage of *lahm* (flesh) comes. Janaab-e-Paygambar's is the stage of *lahm*. This is the sixth stage. It is the sixth stage, and after it, only the blowing of the spirit remains, and that pertains to Janaab-e-Qa'im, Salawatullah 'alayh. I am speaking very briefly and quickly so that the subject matter which remains is conveyed.

May Allah grant everyone the ability for this. The Meraj of the Prophet that has been described in the Quran Sharif, how did it happen? Whether it was Meraj or the night of Hijrat, or the gathering of Zu 'Ashirah, or the conquest of Makkah, Fath-e-Makkah, all the things that happened to the Prophet, if you look at history, you will find that they happened on a Monday. Monday is specific to the Prophet. In a way, Friday is specific to the Prophet. For example, if Janaab-e-Adam is in the mansion of Sunday, then Nuh is in the mansion of Monday, and in this way, Friday comes to the Prophet. And that is why it is a source of blessing for us that we celebrate Friday, because it gathers (*jama'*). And Janaab-e-Paygambar, who is the future Sahib-e-Nutuqa to come, for Janaab-e-Qa'im, Salawatullah 'alayh, it is the day of Sabt (Sabbath). It is the day of Saturday. Leaving all these things aside, I want to narrate that the simple, straightforward kalima that you declared was: *Qulu La ilaha illa-llah tuflihu* (Say there is no god but Allah and you will be successful). O people, O people of Makkah, O mushrikeen, you recite *La ilaha illa-llah*, you will attain salvation. And at that time, people understood that he is the Prophet of Allah and started reading. They kept reciting *La ilaha illa-llah, Muhammadun Rasulullah*, and you said: *Man qala La ilaha illa-llah dakhala-l-jannah* (Whoever says there is no god but Allah will enter Paradise). Now a large crowd gathered. *yatkhuluna fi dinillahi afwaja* (entering into the religion of Allah in multitudes). Thousands of people joined your ummah and started reciting *La ilaha illa-llah*. At that time, among the mushrikeen of Makkah, those with some sense asked, "O Rasulullah, you have told us a very easy kalima, that people are reciting *La ilaha illa-llah* and going to Paradise." So brothers, there is an Islamic paradise, there is an Imani paradise; there are ranks of paradise. That is why it is called *jannat-e-'aliyat* (high paradises). There are various paradises. Paradise is a relative term; if there is something better than a good thing, that is a high paradise.

In this sense, the meaning of paradise is different. So you said: *Man qala La ilaha illa-llah dakhala-l-jannah*. At that time, people said this has become a very easy kalima, so you said: *Man qala La ilaha illa-llah dakhala-l-jannah... mukhlisan dakhala-l-jannah* (Whoever says there is no god but Allah... with sincerity, will enter Paradise). He will enter Paradise if he recites it with sincerity. Then people asked: *Wa ma ikhlasuha?* (And what is its sincerity?). He said: *Ada'u huquqiha wa ma'rifatu hududiha* (Fulfilling its rights and knowing its limits). Its sincerity is its pillars, meaning all the pillars of Islam, that is, namaz, roza, taharat, hajj, zakat, fulfilling all of these, and along with that, *ma'rifat-e-hudud* (knowledge of the limits/hierarchy). Both were joined together; when they have *ma'rifat-e-hudud*, then they will enter Paradise. Now one point came to mind on this. You see that Allah is the one who corrects it, and Allah is greater than all, and our esteemed Imams who are the center of knowledge, and from there the knowledge spreads, it comes to the Du'at, from the Du'at it comes down, and filtering down, it reaches here. We believers, who are the *khasireen*, whatever we receive, we get those blessings from there, from the Imam of the Time.

So anyway, this is the matter, that *mukhlisan dakhala-l-jannah*. It occurred to me on this, what is the meaning of *mukhlisan*? The Prophet said that whoever recites *La ilaha illa-llah* with sincerity (*ikhlas*). Now what is our sincerity? Sincerity—we do recite with sincerity (*khulus*), so what is that sincerity? You see that we have—you know, those who read the lessons, especially in these days, these three months of Rajab al-Murajjab, Sha'ban al-Karim, and Ramadan al-Mubarak, there are lessons and sermons are delivered. Everyone knows that we have the *surat-e-ruhani* (spiritual form) which is formed from the *suwarat*, and the second thing are the *ruhiyat* (spirits), and the third thing are the *fuzlaat* (base/physical matter). *Fuzlaat* is the lowest thing, organic matter, which is a material thing. How have the means for its elevation, for its progress, been created? For that, it has been told that when a person is placed in the soil of the grave after death, from there his transfer occurs. From the vastness of that grave, which is a place of heat, from there in the heat, whatever his condition is, from there to the *mihrab-e-masjid* (prayer niche of the mosque), which is the mosque of the island, he is brought there. From there to the *miqat*, which is his station. From the *miqat* he reaches the *bata'iq*. From the *bata'iq* he reaches there, to the *mizab-e-rahmat*. These are different ranks, where from *dhakha'ir* they become *khama'ir*, from *khama'ir* they become *zubad*. And in this way, after reaching the *mizab-e-rahmat*, the things that were raised from our 12 islands—the believer's elevation happened from 12 islands, his *fuzlaat-e-muribah*, the *fuzlaat-e-munifah*, whatever was raised, all these things, this is a process, a method of action, that Allah takes one. He takes him and where does He make him reach? *Mizab-e-rahmat* is the real place, the final place, where they become *zubad*. And after *zubad*, they reach up, to the *falak-e-buruj* (sphere of the constellations), which is the eighth sphere. The sphere of Saturn (*falak-e-zuhal*) is the seventh sphere from here, and above the sphere of Saturn is the sphere of the constellations. After the sphere of Saturn, in the sphere of the constellations, these 12 constellations, then those 12 which were the lower strata, the 12 islands from which we were raised, they then go inside those 12 constellations and find dissolution (*tahlil*). Various things happen. There, their purification (*tasfiyah*) happens, and refinement (*tanqih*) happens. Many things happen, there is purification and release (*ifhas*). In this way, as Allah wills, for 30-30 years, one clockwise and one anti-clockwise, they pass 30-30 years, and then that thing comes down. In the vastness of the grave, it takes 280 years, and above it takes 720 years. So in 720 years, your noble substance (*fuzl-e-sharifah*) comes down and finds dissolution. And the natural water-mill of mineral, plant, animal—from there, through dissolution, you come into human form, that your father eats that animal, and from that, the sperm is formed, then we are born after a thousand years. The point is that the 720 years that are spent above for us, in the realm of the constellations, those 720 years are for purification (*tasfiyah*). The meaning of purification is that there your release (*khalasi*) happens. The release of our base matter happens, and it goes and one thing of ours, this, these parts of the body, which are the noble substances, they go and one thing here, the inherent essence (*jawharat-e-gharizi*), it goes from here and turns towards the vegetative soul (*nafs-e-namiyah*) and becomes the vegetative soul. So this is "matter converted into energy." A material thing, it goes and density turns into subtlety. And this is called purification. So we, when we come after being in the realm of the constellations, our release happens. And the Prophet's statement could be this, that from Allah's side it is that, *Wa ma ikhlasuha?* (And what is its sincerity?). You said that sincerity is this, that *ada'u huquqiha wa ma'rifatu hududiha*. All these things that have been imposed on us, that we have to do purification, we have to pray, we have to fast, we have to give zakat, after all these things happen, when we come again, one part will be minus, and if this is not minus, our success is not certain. We will be successful when we are reduced, we will become less, then it happens. Now you see that *khalasa* is its root word, and from *ikhlas* the meaning is from *khalasa*: *khay, lam, sad*. And their numerical values are 720 years. It could be that in 720 years, a perfect human, who is of straight path, who is a standard believer, who acts on the correct scale, of the brilliant Shari'ah, of the constitution of Muhammad, of the charter of life, he goes and becomes complete, and when he comes down, one thing of his is reduced. Anyway, this was one saying of the Prophet, that *wa ma ikhlasuha?* (what is its sincerity?). And its sincerity is what? You said *ada'u huquqiha wa ma'rifatu hududiha*.

Now I turn towards the history of Islam. In the history of Islam, when the Prophet of Both Worlds reached the age of 40, you were offered apostleship (*Risalat*). You were made a Rasul. Otherwise, the Prophet was also a Nabi. And if you read the books of 'Aqa'id, you will find out that just as a human is a child, and from a child grows up and passes through major stages, in the same way, which stages has the Prophet passed through? And he went and reached a throne (*'arsh*). You have attained such a high ascension. Otherwise, among the esteemed prophets, there are many who had an ascension. But the Prophet of Both Worlds, he is the most noble of creation (*Ashraf al-Makhluqat*), and you are what? The most noble of prophets (*Ashraf al-Anbiya'*). You are the leader of the messengers (*Sayyid al-Mursalin*). You are greater than all messengers. The ascension he had, no one else had. You know how the ascension happened. Adam also faced difficulties in his time, they happened in the time of Nuh. If you read the history of Islam, you will find out that at every stage, at every turn in history, if you read the history of humanity, you will see how many difficulties Nuh, peace be upon him, faced. How many... Ibrahim, peace be upon him, spread Tawhid. Ibrahim did. You are in the mansion of *'alaqah*. And the first Tawhid for the masses has spread from the time of Ibrahim. The mansion of *'alaqah*, from there the original, original connection of the sperm is born. Anyway, this is the matter, that how the esteemed prophets have fulfilled their positions, and have gone and a time came when our most noble of prophets, Mawlana wa Sayyidna Muhammad Mustafa, Salawatullah 'alayh, was born, and you honored the land of Makkah. That Makkah, whose land, where the Arabs were ignorant, and naive, they were polytheists, adulterers, obscene. There was no evil that was not in Makkah. But where there were so many evils, there the greatest of prophets was sent, there in the land of Arabia. And you honored such a land, and took it from where to where. You know that he took it from the earth to the throne (*farsh-o-'arsh*). The matter of the throne is that on the night of Meraj, this thing was granted to you. That in your 23 years of effort that you have done, where have you reached? Otherwise, there is also the night of Hijrat, and the conquest of Makkah, and the gathering of Zu 'Ashirah, wherever you see, in the case of the Prophet, it has been told that it was on a Monday that you reached. It happened on a Monday. And I think that Monday is also because our greatest Peeran-e-Peer is the Prophet of Both Worlds. We who call 'Abd al-Qadir Jilani Peeran-e-Peer, what is he? He is one among the *awliya Allah*, who have turned from evil to good. But the Prophet of Both Worlds, who is the most noble, there is no mention of sin there. That Prophet of Both Worlds is our greatest Peeran-e-Peer, that is why the day of Monday was made specific for him.

Hanif al-Kindi narrates that there was a time when Islam was just beginning, I was sitting with 'Abbas ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib in connection with business. 'Abbas ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib is your uncle, the Prophet's, who was approximately of your age, who were young. There, in connection with his business, he was sitting. Islam had not yet begun, the Prophet had not made the announcement, as Hazrat Qibla told, that for seven years you and Ali kept praying. It was just like that, that we were talking, and from behind a curtain, a man came out and went and, facing the qibla, that is, facing the Ka'bah, he prayed. He stood up in the presence of Allah. And then a woman came out from the curtain and she stood behind him. Then a young man came and started praying. When these three started praying, I asked 'Abbas who they were. He said they are my nephews, and their claim is that I am the final prophet, and this is, they are worshipping Allah. At that time, I did not know what Islam was. But when later I was honored with Islam, I started to regret that if I too at that time, when I was talking to 'Abbas, if I had accepted Islam, then I would have been the second after Ali, or the third after Abu Bakr. A person named Hanif al-Kindi said this; it has come in the history of the Siyar.

Anyway, there are many things, that on the night of Hijrat, what things happened. You know that before the conquest of Makkah, how much oppression was inflicted upon the Prophet of Both Worlds. What kinds of torments were given to the Prophet? Every prophet was tormented, but the way the Prophet was tormented, no one else was tormented. And the Prophet, when he was being tormented, thorns were spread in his path. Stones were placed. Entrails were thrown on his head. And you would remove them and then take your path. Anyway, many such things have happened. This oppression that was inflicted, and after that you did not move from your mission. This Islam, whose beginning you have made, you have done it with great effort and hardship.

At that time, this happened, that Islam kept spreading, and leaving the land of Makkah, where did it reach? It reached Andalusia, it reached Iran, and it spread throughout the entire Middle East. Today in the world, there is only Islam and Islam. And it is continuing to grow, and Allah wants that the whole thing should become Islam. So a time will come when there will be only Islam. May Allah grant us the ability that we should know this. That time when the night of Hijrat happened, at that time the accursed ones wanted to... you, that is, many people had already migrated and gone to Madinah Sharif. Now Janaab-e-Ali, Janaab-e-Abu Bakr, and the Prophet of Both Worlds were left sitting in Makkah. And at that time, a call came from Jibril al-Amin, "O Rasulullah, you should migrate to Madinah." Allah will help you. So at that time, Janaab-e-Paygambar on his bed... and this conspiracy was happening. A conspiracy was being hatched. People, a conspiracy was happening, a plot was being made, about how to kill the Prophet. Everyone's decision was made—there are many details, I am making it brief—that everyone said that we, all the young men, one from each tribe should be chosen, and they should attack the Prophet all at once, so that the burden does not fall on any single tribe. Everyone agreed on this. And after that, the Prophet had received the news from Jibril al-Amin that there is an intention to kill you, there is an intention to murder you. So you, there, on your bed, made Janaab-e-Ali, Salawatullah 'alayh, lie down and said, "Wear my green sheet and sleep peacefully here." This is obedience, you see. And Janaab-e-Ali sacrificed himself. He lay down there, he lay down. And the Prophet, in the Quran Sharif, the verse from Surah Yasin, *wa ja'alna min bayni aydihim saddan wa min khalfihim saddan fa-aghshaynahum fa-hum la yubsiroon* (And We have put a barrier before them and a barrier behind them, and We have covered them over, so they do not see). That is, behind them and in front of them, a barrier was placed, and they could not see. He recited the initial verses of Surah Yasin, took a handful of dust, and throwing it on those infidels, on the polytheists, he walked out. At that time, when it was about to be morning, and these people were trying to put their deed into action, at that time a gentleman came and said, "Hey, what are you people doing, what are you waiting for? The Prophet is not there. It is Ali lying here." At that time they were startled, and when they removed the sheet, they saw that Janaab-e-Ali was sleeping. They were very frustrated that "here we thought we were killing the Prophet." See, this is from Allah's side, that how veils have come. *aghshaynahum fa-hum la yubsiroon* (We have covered them over, so they do not see). They could not see. And the Prophet, walking out from there, went to Madinah Sharif. In Madinah, he spread Islam, and then major events happened there as well, and how Islam flourished.

Anyway, the point to be made is that the Islam that we believe in, that Islam is the one which has happened on a large platform. Meaning, the world of Islam that is visible at this time, they believe in Allah, that they believe in Allah and they believe in the Rasul. But the real meaning, the circle of Iman, begins when the appointment (*nass*) was made for Mawlana Ali. The Prophet of Both Worlds was receiving addresses several times that you should appoint your successor. Because many small and big things, the Prophet himself would show them by doing them practically. How should wudu be performed? How should taharat be performed? He would show all this. But from Allah's side, the command came that you should do that work... *Balligh ma unzila ilayk* (Convey what has been revealed to you). O Prophet, do the work that you have to do. Meaning, appoint your caliph. And the Prophet was hesitating, he was hesitating. From whom was he hesitating? From these three gentlemen. Those who sat as usurpers on the caliphate, Abu Bakr, Umar, and Uthman, he was afraid of these three. And when the final Hajj happened, in the year 8, the conquest of Makkah happened. In the year 8, you performed one Hajj, and then in the 9th year one Hajj, in the 10th year one Hajj. The three pillars of Hajj are Qiran, Mufrad, and Tamattu' bi-l-'Umrah. You performed these three Hajjs one year at a time. And the final Hajj, when you were returning after performing the Hajj al-Tamattu' bi-l-'Umrah, at that time the command came that *man kuntu mawlahu fa-'Aliyyun mawlahu*. You, this... the verse of *Balligh ma unzila ilayk* came, that you should appoint your caliph, O Prophet. *Wallahu ya'simuka min an-nas* (And Allah will protect you from the people). This piece was added. That Allah will give you protection, will protect you. When the Prophet got a... peace and contentment, and this promise of protection came from Allah, then you stopped right where you were standing. And you said, "Bring those ahead to the back, bring those behind to the front." See, I am mixing this sermon because today is also Mawlana Ali's birthday. You have already heard about the birth, and you have heard very high sermons. The birth of Amir al-Mu'minin, Salawatullah 'alayh, how did it happen? At what place did it happen? Does anyone have the audacity to be born there? This is a chosen person in the world. See, a chosen person. People in the world progress, they keep moving forward, they keep moving forward. But I think that the pair of Ali that has been joined... Janaab-e-Qa'im is the final... he is the Sahib-e-Nutuqa, the Sahib-e-A'immah, he is the last one. And after them, if anyone has worked hard and tried to move forward, it is Ali al-Murtada. After the Prophet of Both Worlds, the vicegerent of the Prophet, Mawlana Ali, Salawatullah 'alayh, is a great genius, who is worthy of respect for humanity. In the sense that from Janaab-e-Adam until here, there is no such person who has worked harder than him. You sacrificed yourself for the Prophet. And we have a saying in Arabic: *Man jadda wajada* (Whoever strives, finds). He who tries, moves forward, he attains. Now *man jadda wajada*, calculate its numerical value and match it with the numerical value of Ali. Both are 110. *Man jadda wajada*. So I think that the effort Ali made, no one has. We all progress in our own places. The little progress that happens to us, but who is the father of the Imams (*Abu al-A'immah*) and the Imam of the pious (*Imam al-Muttaqin*), his is greater than all, that he... and whose... how did he do it? The Prophet of Both Worlds and Janaab-e-Ali, Salawatullah 'alayh, if you look at the history of humanity, in the prayer of 'Ashura, it says who turned the ark towards Judi? And how did the ark land on Judi? Janaab-e-Nuh's. How did Janaab-e-Ibrahim get salvation from the fire? And how did Janaab-e-Musa happen? Janaab-e-Isa happened, and all, as many Imams... prophets as there are, the salvation they got, they got it from the veils of Janaab-e-Paygambar, Salawatullah 'alayh, and Janaab-e-Ali. We have a special subject on this, that there is a *mukhtari hijjab* and a *karrari hijjab*. The veils of both of these have worked, and every prophet who is among the *mustawda'in*, their salvation has happened from them. So the meaning is that in the history of humanity, from Adam until here, these are two individuals, these are the two luminaries (*nayyirayn*), who have given peace to everyone. From Janaab-e-Nuh until the present world, everyone who has received peace, has received it from them. The *mukhtari hijjab* and the *karrari hijjab* have worked. And who are these two? For the Prophet, the letter *Meem* comes, and *'Ayn* comes for Janaab-e-Ali. We cannot remove *Meem* and *'Ayn*, we cannot separate them. Both are always together (*ma'a*). They are always joined. *Meem* and *'Ayn* are... and *Meem* and *'Ayn*, I think that *Meem* and *'Ayn*, what they have done, no one in the world has done. The veils that they have worked, they are memorable in the world. And this is, *Meem* and *'Ayn*, in a way, for the welfare of the entire world, for the good, and for saving the prophets and messengers, the work they have done, it is their share. And their sovereignty is over the entire world of humanity. Until today, it will continue until the Day of Judgment, their sovereignty. For their sovereignty, we here in Hindustan, we call it their reign (*raj*). This is their reign. The reign of *Meem* and *'Ayn*. And this itself, in our view, is the ascension (*meraj*). The reign of *Meem* and *'Ayn* is itself the ascension. That the Prophet of Both Worlds, who was in the initial stage, the Prophet, that is, in the stage of a Nabi, from Nabi to apostleship, from apostleship he came into *Natiqiyyat*, from apostleship he became the leader of the messengers, became an *Ulul 'Azm* prophet, and then moving forward he became the beloved of the *awliya*. To the point that you have attained those ranks which have not come in the share of others. The Meraj, which has been told, that *Subhana-lladhi asra bi-'abdihi*. It's the 15th Surah. *Subhana-lladhi asra bi-'abdihi laylan min al-Masjid al-Haram ila al-Masjid al-Aqsa, alladhi barakna hawlahu* (Glory to Him who took His servant by night from the Sacred Mosque to the Farthest Mosque, whose surroundings We have blessed). That Allah took him... He is the glorious being. Allah, the Glorious... *Subhana-lladhi*. Glory be. He is the pure and holy Lord, who took His servant at night. Where did he take him? From Masjid al-Haram to Masjid al-Aqsa. Around which there is... the appearance of all signs happens. *alladhi barakna hawlahu*. Around which there is blessing. And remember this, that the meaning of *asra* is to walk. He took him. So the Prophet of Both Worlds, who went from here, from Makkah towards Madinah... towards Aqsa, this is called walking, it is called *asra*. And from there, at Masjid al-Aqsa, on a rock named Sakhrah, from the rock your ascent, your elevation happened, that is called Meraj. And you all know about the Meraj. In every gathering, we hear that the Prophet of Both Worlds ascended to the seventh heaven. No prophet did. Musa also stopped, Isa also stopped, all of them... and there were great demands. Musa said, "How many prayers have been assigned to you?" From 50 prayers, reducing them, the Prophet came down to five prayers. And Musa said, "It seems to me that your ummah will not pray these either." You... he said, "O brother Musa, I am shy before Allah that my ummah will not even pray five times?" And these five prayers, he brought them there. Then it has been told that when you reached there, and at that time, when you reached the station, on the highest throne, and from Allah... *dana fa-tadalla fa-kana qaba qawsayni aw adna* (Then he approached and came closer, and was at a distance of two bow lengths or even nearer). There are very special secrets in this, there are many things in it, that when you reached there, you saw that Ali was sitting there. It has been narrated in the Siyar that Ali was sitting there. You are going on Meraj and Ali is already sitting there. You said, "O brother Jibril, what is this matter that Ali is already sitting here?" So Jibril al-Amin said, "O Rasulullah, the angels had a desire to see Ali. So Allah made an angel in the form of Ali." This is the station of the Prophet of Both Worlds. We can neither diminish them nor exaggerate them. This is a matter of great delicacy. Those who understand, understand, and those who believe, believe, that how these two came together. Where all did they come together? What is the meaning of *Muhammadun wa 'Aliyyun khayr al-bashar* (Muhammad and Ali are the best of mankind)? What is the meaning of *khayr al-bashar*? May Allah grant us the ability to understand it. I want to conclude this quickly so that my point is complete. That the Prophet who was commissioned, yesterday... tomorrow morning. Meraj also happened, you also had the day of commissioning, and the birth of Amir al-Mu'minin also happened. You all know about the birth of Amir al-Mu'minin, that where did it happen? At Mustajar. At Mustajar, the place which is there, there the wall of the Ka'bah split, and there Mawlatina Fatima bint Asad went inside. And when she came out from there, she came out with the child. Many miracles happened, many things are there. The details are so many that several gatherings are required. It is difficult to narrate in one gathering. These three things are included. This is the birth of Amir al-Mu'minin, it is also the night of Meraj, and it is the matter of the Prophet's commissioning, of which we are followers. That the Prophet of Both Worlds was adorned with a crown of prophethood, a crown of apostleship, a crown of everything. The leader of the messengers, the seal of the prophets. You... what did you get in the Meraj? Did it happen physically or spiritually? People to this day are guessing. Great commentators are... guessing what it is. On this matter, the Du'at have revealed a little, and that too is very ambiguous because it is not easy to narrate everything. Everyone is told according to their fortune, that how your ranks, which are the ranks of prophethood, you have traversed them. When you traversed the stages of hierarchy, you were in the ninth rank, then the Surah of Taha came and you were granted the ninth rank. And after that, your station increased even more, and the address of Yasin Sharif you received. Yasin became your address, so at that time you were in the tenth rank. And you have traversed several ranks. In Yasin, *Ya* is separate, *Sin* is separate. How many ranks *Sin* has, I don't want to go into details. But the height of the Prophet of Both Worlds, and the loftiness, is evident from this, that in 23 years, he went from where to where. We are where we are. But the Prophet of Both Worlds went from where to where. He reached the throne. And your rank became that of *Muhammadun wa 'Aliyyun khayr al-bashar*. If you read, you will find out, if you read the books, you will find out that the Prophet of Both Worlds, the *haqa'iq*, and above the *haqa'iq* are the *daqa'iq*, on the *daqa'iq* are the *khafiya-e-'aliyah*, and on that are also the *daqa'iq al-daqa'iq*. Then there is *ifazat*, that a great person, if he says even two words, it is a very venerable thing. They are jewels that are plundered.

Anyway, this is our matter, that it is not the case that, as speeches are given among the public, that the Meraj happened, and the Rasul was made, and the Prophet, a Nabi was made. He was made a Nabi, and he was made a Rasul. If you read what comes in the newspapers, that on the night of Meraj, what happened to the Prophet? And what rank did the Prophet get? So, he was made a Nabi. Then in the line below it says that the Prophet was made a Rasul. They don't know what a Rasul is, nor what a Nabi is. Which rank is of a Nabi, and which rank is of a Rasul. Anyway, Allah has granted wisdom, and to the *awliya Allah* and the Imam of the Time, that our, this Imam of the Time, today it is his blessing that people get the strength to speak. What is that? As I have narrated before, that after the Prophet of Both Worlds, today, the protectors of the Shari'ah of Muhammad are our Imam of the Time, Salawatullah 'alayh, Mawlana wa Sayyidna Muhammadin 'Ali, Salawatullah 'alayh, who is the protector of the Shari'ah. And we are plundering his blessings. Whatever is upon all the people of the Jamat, upon all the great *awliya Allah*, upon the Du'at, upon the ranks, all of them, each according to his capacity, whatever he takes, he takes. And it is that your being, who is the most noble of creation... the Prophet of Both Worlds, Salawatullah 'alayh, after him, who were the sun of the time, and the moon of the da'wah was Janaab-e-Ali, Salawatullah 'alayh, after their... after the departure of both of them, that position, the Imam and his Da'i, they hold it. And the moon of the da'wah are the Da'is, and the Imam is in the mansion of the sun. The spiritual sun. "So you are the sun of the time." I have written a poem: "You are the sun of the time, from you is the light. You are the manager of the world, you are Mount Tur. The manager of the world, you are Mount Tur. And you are hidden. You are hidden, that is, the Imam of the Time is in hiding. You are hidden, but guidance is from you. Though another may publicize, the broadcast is from you. The broadcast is from you. And on the sky of da'wah, there is a net of stars and constellations (*hudud-e-kiram* are present everywhere). The net of stars and constellations. And the light within them is your miracle." These are the blessings of the Imam of the Time. That this skill has been created in us that we can pray. "The net of stars and constellations, and the light within them is your miracle." And after that is: "You gave the seeker the impulse to ask. You gave the seeker the impulse to ask. And then you gave the guide the ability to answer." And then after that is, that at the end I have written that: "In your absence. In your absence, the moon is giving light. In your absence, the moon is giving light. And taking brilliance (*ziya'*) from you, it is giving light (*nur*). Taking brilliance from you... *ziya'* is called the light of the sun, and *nur* is the light which is of the moon." So may Allah grant us the ability to understand that the Da'i of the Time is taking *ziya'* and we are getting *nur*. "Taking brilliance from you, they are giving light." May Allah, the Exalted, grant us all the ability that in these blessed days, which are at the end of Rajab al-Murajjab, and after that is Sha'ban al-Karim, and after that is Ramadan al-Mubarak, may He grant us the ability to do righteous deeds, so that we may be called true believers. *Wa akhiru da'wana an al-hamdu lillahi rabb al-'alamin, wa-s-salatu wa-s-salamu 'ala Rasulihi-l-Karim.* Mashallah. Subhanallah.

Now I am not giving you permission to get up. I will speak for one or two minutes. You will have to take two more minutes of trouble. A little... keep it in one heap.

*Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim.*

Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, has said: *Wa la ta'kulu* (And do not eat). You should not eat. And you are going to eat, arrangements are being made for your eating. You are taking the trouble to eat, Allah's command is *Wa la ta'kulu* (do not eat). You should not eat. Then how are you running to eat? But the discourse does not end there. Where does the discourse end? *Wa la ta'kulu mimma lam yudhkari-smullahi 'alayh* (And do not eat of that upon which Allah's name has not been mentioned). You should not eat that thing upon which the name of Allah has not been mentioned. Allahu Akbar. Now every person should look at himself. When he ate, did he say *Bismillah* or not? This has been made obligatory by Allah in the Quran Sharif, not in one place, but in many places. Now we are going to a feast, we will eat food, we will do... every person should reflect on this action of his, whether he said *Bismillah* or not. The command is *Wa la ta'kulu* (do not eat). That upon which the name of Allah has not been mentioned. This is a command for every child, for every young person, for every old person, for every woman, for every man, this is the command for everyone. Do not eat that upon which the name has not been mentioned. Because when you take the name, the harmful things which are in it, in the food, they move away from you. This is a strange glory of Allah. The harmful things that are in it, you have no idea how the food was made, how the food happened, how the food came before you. What kind of water got into it, what kind of things got into it. Take the name of Allah. *Wa la ta'kulu mimma lam yudhkari-smullahi 'alayh*. Do not eat that upon which the name of Allah has not been mentioned.

A man came to Mawla-e-Ka'inat, Hazrat Ali al-Murtada, 'alayhi-s-salatu wa-s-salam. You have just heard a sermon on the realities of knowledge, so I want to narrate a sermon on the outward as well. His name was Ibn al-Kawwa'. Ibn al-Kawwa' was his name. And he came and said, "O Mawla Ali, you said at night that if you say *Bismillah* and eat, then nothing will harm you... *ma'ahu shay'*... Whoever said *Bismillah* on food, no thing will harm him. I said *Bismillah* on the food at night, but at night I was troubled with a stomachache." So he said, "O hypocrite, *Ya Luka'*... what did you... did you say *Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim 'ala kulli naw'* (on every type)? You ate several types. You ate sweet, you ate sour, you ate bread, you ate rice, and you ate all these things. Did you say *Bismillah* on every type, meaning on every kind?" He said, "No." He said, "This is the trouble." This is the trouble. Allahu Akbar. Look at the sermon of Mawla Ali. What caution should we take? That we should eat by saying *Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim*. Men are also commanded, and women are also commanded. And this is also a command for us, that when we are in a state of impurity, that it is a command that we should not read the Quran Sharif. Such a state arises for men, that they are not in a state of purity. There is no command to read the Quran Sharif. And women are in a state of menstruation, they do not have the command to read the Quran Sharif. So in that situation, what should they do? They should think that we are saying *Bismillah*, we are taking the name of Allah, we are not reading the verse of the Quran Sharif. Men should also think this, and women should also think this. That we are saying *Bismillah*, we are taking the name of Allah, we are not reading the verse of the Holy Quran. This is the command. Which Sayyidna 'Ali bin Sulayman has clarified in his books. May Allah grant us all the ability that whenever we eat or drink any thing, we should eat and drink by saying *Bismillah*. May Allah grant blessing in it. *Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim*.

See, I will tell you one thing. We had gone to Sayyidna Husayn bin Hasan 'Ala al-Qutub. And there, he had called us to eat. All the... people were invited there. So what did he always say? "*Sammu*." When he would call for food, he would say... say *Bismillah*. "*Sammu*" means say *Bismillah*. He would not say "come to eat." He would say "*Sammu*." Say *Bismillah*. This was the way.

With Islam, *da'im* (the permanent one) is with him. Its *ta'wil* (esoteric interpretation) is, and it is different from the other *ta'wil* that others explain. This *ta'wil* is distinct. *As-salah...* The eighth page. Here, "Concerning *Salah*." We have already done *salah*. The *ta'wil* of *salah* is done, so it's *zakat*. We had started *zakat*.

*Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim. Allahumma salli 'ala sayyidina muhammadin wa 'ala aali sayyidina muhammad wa sallim* (In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. O Allah, send blessings upon our master Muhammad and the family of our master Muhammad and grant them peace).

*Wa 'l-zakat hiya ikhraj juz'in min amwal al-aghniya' ila wali al-amr li-yusarrifahu fi 'l-fuqara' 'ala tabaqatihim* (And *zakat* is the taking out of a portion from the wealth of the rich to the one in authority, so that he may distribute it among the poor according to their classes). And *zakat* means to take out one portion from the wealth of the rich and give it to the *wali al-amr* (the one in authority), so that the *wali al-amr* may spend it on the *fuqara'* (the poor) in their various classes (*tabaqat*). Various classes, as it has come in the Quranic verse, that the *yatim* (orphan) is separate, and the *asir* (captive) is separate, the *miskin* (needy) is separate, the *faqir* (poor) is separate. There is a difference between a *faqir* and a *miskin*. There are eight types of people: *faqir*, *miskin*, *yatim*, *asir*, and *mu'allafati 'l-qulub* (those whose hearts are to be reconciled), and the collectors (*'ummal*). All together, they are eight.

So, a *faqir* is one who asks. A *miskin* is one whose condition makes it apparent that he has no money, and he should be given. He is called a *miskin*. And the fundamental principle is that the wealth reaches the leader. The leaders of the *jazira* (region), wherever they are. If the leader of the *jazira* appoints a subordinate, then wherever there are people, the collectors (*'ummal*) are responsible for collection.

And what is its *batin* (esoteric meaning)? Meaning, this is about giving the *zakat* of one's *mal* (wealth). So what is wealth? And its *zakat* is given, so what is its *ta'wil*? See. *Wa fi 'l-batin...* *Wa fi 'l-batin ifadat al-'ulama' al-mufidin 'ilmahum li-man tahta aydihim min al-mustafidin* (And in the esoteric sense, it is the imparting of knowledge by the beneficial scholars to those under their authority from among the students). Now, the *zakat* that is to be given is that those who are beneficial (*mufid*) and can teach should teach those who are under them. And they should bring it forth (*ikhraj karen*). *'Ilm* (knowledge) is considered like *mal* (wealth). Just as they have knowledge, that is their wealth. So the *mufidin* (beneficial ones) are the wealthy ones.

And, meaning, it is an example of this. There should be the imparting of knowledge (*ifadat al-'ilm*), and the beneficial scholars (*'ulama'-i mufidin*) should teach the students (*mustafidin*) under them. *Al-ma'ruf 'amr ilahi*. And they should remain inclined towards them. And how? *Min... min jihatin min fawqihim* (From a direction above them). Meaning, the senior teaches the junior. To whomever permission is granted. Now, *ijazat* (permission) is the real thing.

*Wa 'l-zakat... wa 'l-zakat la yajibu li-man akhrajaha taslimuha ila 'l-fuqara'* (And for *zakat*, it is not obligatory for the one who gives it to hand it over [directly] to the poor). Yes. This is not necessary or obligatory for any person to take out *zakat* from himself and give it to someone. As is done among Muslims, where sarees are distributed, this is happening, that is happening, thousands are being spent. This is wrong. This, the *zakat* must go upwards and then be distributed from above. By *wali al-amr*, it means the Prophet. During the Prophet's time, it was: *khudh min amwalihim sadaqatan tutahhiruhum wa tuzakkihim biha* (Take from their wealth a charity by which you purify and sanctify them). This was the Prophet's command: "Take from their wealth." It's a command form. Don't show helplessness, don't give excuses, but *khudh min amwalihim* (take from their wealth). Take from their wealth so that you may purify them and sanctify them.

So, here too it is the same way, *la yajibu*. So it is not obligatory to teach someone without permission. This is its meaning here. It will come now.

*Bal al-wajib 'alayhi taslimuha ila wali al-amr... wali al-zaman...* Yes. *...li-yada'aha fi mawdi'ihi* (Rather, what is obligatory upon him is to hand it over to the Master of the Age, so that he may place it in its proper place). But it is obligatory for him to give it to the *wali al-zaman* (Master of the Age). That is, the *zakat* to the *wali al-amr*. Yes. So that he may place it in its proper place. Yes. Just as Allah's saying is... *min amwalihim sadaqa... sadaqatan...* He wrote the same verse. He has ended it there. Just as Allah's saying is: "Take charity from their wealth." Yes.

*Fa-dhalika nassun 'ala an yakuna taslimuha ila al-nabi 'alayhi salam... wa man yaqumu maqamahu... maqamahu min al-a'immah* (So this is a clear text that its delivery should be to the Prophet, peace be upon him, and whoever stands in his place from among the Imams). *Maqamahu* means his station. *Maqam al-a'immah*. That *mim* is missing. Meaning, and this is a clear text (*nass*) that it should be given to the Prophet. In the time of the Prophet, to the Prophet. If the Prophet is not there, then who is in his place? The Imams, who are the guardians of the station of the Prophet. They are the guardians of the *shari'ah*. If the Imam is not there, then the *da'i*. If the *da'i* is not there, then those below him. And from those below him, to those below them. As far as the command (*amr*) goes, it goes.

*Min al-a'immah... fi kulli 'asrin wa zaman* (from the Imams... in every era and time). In every era. *Wa dhalika mithlun 'ala an man balagha fi 'l-'ilm manzilatan man yajibu... li-an yakuna mufid li-ghayrihi... lam yajib lahu an yufida mimma 'indahu min al-'ilm...* (And that is an example that for one who reaches a station in knowledge where it is obligatory for him to be beneficial to others, it is not incumbent upon him to impart from the knowledge he possesses...).

And that is an example that whoever has reached a level in knowledge... that is, one sees that he is capable of teaching. Meaning, of taking out *zakat*, of collecting *zakat*. So he is given permission, and he becomes capable of teaching. *balagha fi 'l-'ilm manzilatahu wa an yajib... an yakuna mufid* (he reached his station in knowledge and that it is obligatory... that he be beneficial). He becomes beneficial. So, wherever they give permission, they first give it to the children, "You teach the children." It happens. Slowly, as his rank increases, he becomes capable of teaching the elders.

Giving *zakat*, in the exoteric legal rulings of the *shari'ah*, this is the meaning behind it.

*...min al-'ilm illa bi-idhni wali al-zaman... idh huwa sahib al-'ilm wa khazinuhu* (...from the knowledge except with the permission of the Master of the Age, for he is the owner of the knowledge and its treasurer). Yes. *Wa in fa'ala dhalika... min ghayri amrin, fa-qad ta'adda 'l-wajib...* (And if he did that without an order, then he has transgressed the obligation...).
