The desire that was in our hearts, that was in the minds of the believers, that we do not have any *tafsir* (commentary) of the Holy Quran, that is a wrong notion. It was written 250 years ago. And it has happened before that too, but this systematic book is what Sayyidna Husayn Jalaluddin has written. We couldn't read its translation, so we didn't understand what the meaning of which verse is. Now, wherever the word `ya'ni` (meaning) comes, the real *ta'wil* (esoteric interpretation) has been explained there. Otherwise, the translation has been given.

Go ahead.

*Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim. Wa bihi nasta'in, wa 'alayhi natawakkal* (In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. And in Him we seek help, and upon Him we rely). All praise is for Allah alone, who has opened the locks of difficult sciences for the servants of His saints (*awliya'*), and from their tongues, has revealed the hidden secrets of the Shari'ah. I praise Him and bear witness that there is no god but Him. He is living, magnificent, supreme, and I send blessings upon His messenger Sayyidna Muhammad and his *wasi* and both their progeny, who are the shining stars and constellations of the *deen*. And send blessings upon the Imam of the era, the Master of the Time, who is appointed for the appointed day. And send salutations upon his *hujjat*s and *du'at* who are the pool of his sciences. And the sealed cups of secrets. O group of seekers of the science of reality! May Allah open the locks of deep sciences for me and for you, and may He free me and you from the captivity and shackles of being deaf and dumb. The sciences that Mawlana Imam and his two *da'i*s have explained, you have heard them. From his blessed tongue, those symbols of the Quran were told to you which are hidden from the common people, and which only the people of intellect can understand. Now you will hear those subtle points of that same series which have been connected with it. Allah is the seeker of help from His saints.

Now, Mawlana Imam and his two *da'i*s. The two *da'i*s that Sayyidna Husayn Jalaluddin has mentioned are Sayyidna Ali bin Sayyidna Sulayman and Sayyidna Ibrahim. These were the two *da'i*s in his time. And it is mentioned that this was written by the command of Sayyidna Ali Sahab. Sayyidna Ali bin Sayyidna Sulayman. And when two or three *surah*s were done, after Surah Baqarah, from where Surah Nisa and others came, at that time Sayyidna Husayn said that this will not be possible for me. This work will not be done. It is a very lofty matter. He said, "It will be done by you." Sayyidna Ali Sahab said. He pleaded a lot, but Sayyidna Ali Sahab did not agree. And he said, "This work cannot be done by me." At that time, Sayyidna Ali Sahab commanded his brother Ibrahim to... His brother Ibrahim had a very special rank. He was among the learned (*'ilmiyyin*) and was a great scholar. He has written very special books. So, Sayyidna... his name was Sarim. Sayyidna Ibrahim. He was given the command. So, the two or three *juz'*s, or the three *surah*s, its translation... the *ta'wil* that has been explained is the *ta'wil* of Sayyidna Ibrahim. Remember this. And it is very lofty. In it, the matter of inheritance, how much share should go to whom, all that is explained. Now we are starting the third *juz'*. `Tilka al-rusul`.

This is the exegesis of the third *juz'*. Whoever contemplates and reflects upon it will attain his share of blessings. And its deep, pleasant effects... and debate about the treasures and troves of its subtle meanings.

*Tilka al-rusulu faddalna ba'dahum 'ala ba'd* (Those are the messengers; We preferred some of them over others). These are the messengers, among whom We have given preference to some over others. Meaning, here the Exalted Creator first mentions the messengers, and then He explains that they are not all of one rank. Not all are of one rank. As I have told you, the one... yes. But their ranks are higher and lower.

*Minhum man kallamal laahu wa rafa'a ba'dahum darajaat* (Among them are those to whom Allah spoke, and He raised some of them in degree). Among them, there is one with whom Allah spoke, and He raised the ranks of some. Meaning, Mawlana Imam al-Zaman made Musa his interlocutor (*kalimah*) and, by virtue of being the fourth, He gave him... Now, you should understand that as much of the Holy Quran as has come... the Holy Quran is before us, and in it all the stories, all the incidents, are of the prophets and messengers. There is no mention of any Imam. Why is this? It is because this is the era of concealment (*dawr al-satr*). And in this, the book that has come contains the stories of all the messengers. And how are they? You can take out and read *Asas al-Ta'wil* or read *Qutb al-Najah*. Any book you read, no verse of the Quran tells where the Imam is. But all the things that the people of the initiatory level are doing, whether Da'ud does it or Sulayman does it, Musa does it or Isa does it, or they come before Fir'awn, or Ibrahim... so all the people of the initiatory rank, the command is coming to them from the Imam. And the Imam is hidden. This is the era of concealment. This is our era of concealment. This whole setup, understand it, that in the era of concealment, the Imam will always be hidden, and the *Nabi* (prophet) will be manifest in his time. The *Nabi* is, the *Rasul* is, all of them. And in today's time, after the Prophet, after the Prophet, there is no prophet after me, `la nabiyya ba'di`. The Prophet's saying is that there is no prophet after me. Now, all those who are of lower ranks, we call them *da'i*s. The *da'i* has come in its place. Let's go.

*Wa aatayna 'Isa ibna Maryamal bayyinaati wa ayyadnaahu bi roohil qudus* (And We gave Jesus, the son of Mary, clear proofs, and We supported him with the Holy Spirit). And We gave Jesus, son of Mary, clear miracles, and supported him through the Holy Spirit. Meaning, We gave him the power to explain esoteric meanings clearly, and endowed him with the sum of subtleties, which increased his inner strength and elevated him in rank.

*Wa law shaa'al laahu maqtatalal ladheena mim ba'dihim mim ba'di ma jaa'at humul bayyinaat* (And if Allah had willed, those who came after them would not have fought each other after the clear proofs had come to them). And if Allah had willed, those who came after them would not have fought among themselves after receiving clear signs and proofs. Meaning, if the Exalted One had willed, people would have known the station of the *wasi* (successor) and, after knowing it, would not have fought for the seizure of worldly leadership. And it has always been that the messengers and them have been rejected. In the time of Nuh, you see, in every era. But the real rejection happens with whom? After the *Nabi*, for the *Wasi*. It has always been that the disputes are for the *Wasi*. After the Prophet, the same thing happened as happened in the time of Musa. That is why one of the titles of the Prophet is that he is called the Musa of the era. And Harun is in the place of Prophet Ali. The Prophet himself has stated that, "O Ali, you are to me as Harun was to Musa."

*Wa laakinikhtalafoo faminhum man aamana wa minhum man kafar, wa law shaa'al laahu maqtataloo wa laakinnal laaha yaf'alu ma yureed* (But they differed, and some of them believed and some of them disbelieved. And if Allah had willed, they would not have fought, but Allah does what He intends). But they differed, so some among them believed and some disbelieved. And if Allah had willed, they would not have engaged in fighting. But Allah does as He wills. Meaning, despite the clear proofs, they differed regarding the *wasi* and the *a'immah*. Some accepted, and some denied. If the Exalted One wanted to stop it, this would not have happened. But since He wants to distinguish between the impure (*khabith*) and the pure (*tayyib*), that is why it happened by His will and intention. See, if the bad did not exist, then everyone in the world would be born good. All would become believers. It hasn't happened that way. But it is necessary to separate the impure from the pure. That wherever a messenger has appeared, a friend of Allah (*wali Allah*) has appeared, a bad person has also appeared before them. And this method has always been there. And history has always been repeated. From Adam to here, you read the incidents, in the people of every era, in this way, the prophets have been rejected. They have been tormented. Our Prophet was tormented the most. And for this, in every era, there has been a devil (*shaytan*). Fir'awn came before Musa, Namrud came before Ibrahim. In every era, one devil has been there. And the Prophet says that because his rank was higher, he had two devils for him. Two devils were appointed for you. So see, this is a special matter of ranks. The greater the friend of Allah (*wali*), the more intense his devil, his opposition (*zidd*), will be. So, it has always been intense, and until when has it been? Because... the incident of Adam, if you read it, you will know. The first part is not in front of me, otherwise I would have narrated it to you. Qabil... that in the time of Adam, Harith bin Murrah, who... and Allah said to him, "Go, I give respite to your foot soldiers and cavalry, that you do whatever you want to torment my believers." But those who are the followers of truth, who are steadfast on the true religion, they will never be turned back. It will never happen. And in this way, the world has been repeating. Always, before the truth, an opposition has come.

*Yaa ayyuhal ladheena aamanoo anfiqoo mimma razaqnaakum min qabli any ya'tiya yawmul laa bay'un feehi wa laa khullatun wa laa shafaa'ah* (O you who have believed, spend from that which We have provided for you before there comes a Day in which there is no exchange and no friendship and no intercession). O believers, spend from the provision We have given you, before that day comes in which there is neither trade, nor friendship, nor intercession of any kind will be of use. See, this is the variety (*tanawwu'*) of the Holy Quran, that one discussion has finished, just now the story was of Da'ud and his... of Musa, many things happened, and now a new topic has been brought. This variety of the Quran is what creates a special quality in it. Otherwise, if it were the same boring thing, it wouldn't be good. But we always get new topics. Every verse has its own separate place. O believers, the provision We have given you... this is its translation. The provision that has been given, spend from it. And before that day comes, in which there is neither trade, nor friendship, nor intercession of any kind will be of use. This is regarding *zakat*. That *zakat*, which is obligatory on us, whatever our earning is, the fortieth part of it... one rupee in forty, must be given. This is the purification of our wealth.

Meaning, O you who obey the *wasi* and the *imam*! See, this is the translation of the verse, and its *ta'wil* is this. Meaning, O you who obey the *wasi* and the *imam*, benefit others with the esoteric sciences and true gnosis with which We have endowed you. Before that day of resurrection arrives when the *Qa'im* (peace be upon him) appears and brings the *qiyamah* (resurrection), and the transmission of beneficial knowledge from the *a'immah* and *du'at* to the people also ceases and is stopped. Because that is a day of examination and reckoning, not a day of give-and-take and teaching.

*Wal kaafiroona humuz zaalimoon* (And the disbelievers, they are the wrongdoers). The disbelievers are the very wrongdoers. Meaning, those who conceal the stations of the *wasi* and *imam* and do wrong are the wrongdoers. That's it.

Al-Fatiha.

[recitation of Al-Fatiha]

[concluding remarks and sounds of people leaving]

Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim. *Ya ayyuha alladhina amanu anfiqu mimma razaqnakum min qabli an ya'tiya yawmun la bay'un fihi wala khullatun wala shafa'atun.* (O you who have believed, spend from what We have provided for you before there comes a Day in which there is no exchange and no friendship and no intercession.) O believers, spend from the provision We have given you before that day comes in which there will be no exchange, no friendship, and no intercession that will be of any use.

Meaning: O *walī* and followers of the *A'immah* (Imams), We have blessed you with esoteric knowledge (*'ulum-e-batin*) and true gnosis (*ma'rifat-e-haqiqi*); help others benefit from it before the appointed day (*yawm-e-maw'ud*), that is, before the *Qa'im* ('alayhi afdal al-salah) comes and establishes the *Qiyamah*. And the dissemination of knowledge (*ifadah-e-'ilmi*), the call of the Imams (*da'wat al-a'immah*), and intercession (*shafa'at*) will all be suspended, and the command to halt will be given, because that will be the day of examination and reckoning. It will not be a day for transactions or speech.

Wherever *Yawm* (Day) is mentioned... Wherever the word *Yawm* is mentioned, it refers to the Day of Qiyamah. And that is the hour, and in fact, it has been said in other books that *Yawm* refers to the Day of Qiyamah, and *Sa'ah* too... *Sa'at* means hour. The hour is the final hour, which is the time of the *Qa'im* 'alayhi al-salam ('alayhi afdal al-salam). And in one sense, it has been divided from the time of Adam 'alayhi al-salam, and the final hour comes at the time of the *Qa'im* 'alayhi al-salam. So, the meaning of *Sa'ah* is also that, and the meaning of *Yawm* is also the same, that is, the *Qa'im* 'alayhi al-salam. And the Prophet (sallallahu 'alayhi wa-alihi) says that "I and *Sa'at* were walking together, and I went a little ahead." For instance, you said about the two fingers that two fingers are like this, and I have moved one step ahead. Meaning, the sixth *shari'ah*, that of the Prophet (sallallahu 'alayhi wa-alihi), came first, and after that, the *Qa'im* will come. This is the meaning.

*Wal-kafiruna humu al-zalimun.* (And the disbelievers - they are the wrongdoers.) And the disbelievers are the very ones who are the wrongdoers. Meaning, those who conceal the ranks of the *wasī* and the *A'immah* and usurp [their rights] are the wrongdoers. Yesterday, I explained that there is a difference between *mushrikin* (polytheists) and *kuffar* (disbelievers). The *mushrikin* are those who, before Islam, were the people of Arabia who were engrossed in *shirk* (polytheism), and they had many gods that were worshipped. 360 idols were kept in the Kaaba. And in this way, they were involved in all things like fornication and wine-drinking. After the coming of the Prophet, their condition changed, and those *mushrikin* became Muslims. Becoming a Muslim is one thing, and becoming a *mu'min* (believer) is another. The circle of *iman* (faith) began at the time when the Prophet (sallallahu 'alayhi wa-alihi) appointed his successor (*qa'im muqam*), his *khalifah*. The circle of *iman* is a separate matter. Many people had entered Islam before that, in the thousands. "*Yadkhuluna fi dini Allahi afwaja*" (Entering into the religion of Allah in multitudes). O Prophet, a whole army is coming into your religion. But now, among them, how many are good and how many are bad? Because many did not even get the chance to perform deeds. Today they became Muslims, and tomorrow they went into another battle and were martyred. So, in this way, there are many incidents from which it is understood that the circle of Islam is very large, but the circle of *iman* is small.

And in the *da'im al-islam* it has been explained that there is a large circle, and within it, a small circle is made. The one who is in the small circle is also in the large circle, but the one who is in the large circle is not in the small circle. So the one who is a Muslim is not a *mu'min* until he has firm belief in 'Ali. But those who have *iman* are also Muslims. This has been explained.

Now after this, the verses of *tilka al-rusul* which are there, that is Ayat al-Kursi, which we recite daily. Read its translation a bit slowly, so that it remains in people's minds.

The *ta'wil* (esoteric interpretation) of Ayat al-Kursi. *Allahu la ilaha illa hu.* (Allah - there is no deity except Him.) Allah is He besides whom there is no other object of worship. That is, the *Sabeq-e-Ta'ala* (Exalted Precedent) is that very Allah. This lesson... ...No, based on the lesson... Based on... Based on the extreme longing for the *ma'rifat* (gnosis) of the *Mubde'* (Originator)... of the *Mubde'*... of the *Mubde'*, it is either the ultimate... or the ultimate bewilderment of the... See, here, this *Allahu la ilaha illa hu* is actually related to *Shahida Allahu... Ashhadu an la ilaha illa Allah* (Allah witnesses... I bear witness that there is no god but Allah), as we recite. So, *Shahida Allahu annahu la...* Allah has testified that there is no deity except *Hu* (Him). *illa hu*. So, in common language, this is what it means: Allah has testified that there is no god except *Hu*. Well, no one gives their own testimony. Its meaning is that the meaning of *Hu* is separate, and Allah is separate. Allah has testified that there is no deity except *Hu*. And *Hu* is "that one." If you reverse *Hu*, it becomes *woh* ("that one"). "That one" means the one who is in the heavens, the Lord of the Worlds, who is the *Mubde'-e-Ta'ala* (Exalted Originator). The day before yesterday, I explained that there is a difference between *Mubde'* and *Mubda'*. If you put a *zer* (vowel mark) under the *dal*, *Mubde'* is the *Mubde'-e-Ta'ala* who created the heavens and the earth, who created the spiritual realm. And *Mubda'-e-Awwal* (First Originated), *Mabda'*, that is the *Mubda'*. *Mubda'* is different, *Mubdi'* is different, *Mubda'* is different. *Mubda'* refers to the *'aql-e-awwal* (First Intellect), who was the first to profess the *tawhid* (oneness) of the Lord of the Worlds. And its meaning is, that is, the *Sabeq-e-Ta'ala* (Exalted Precedent). I have explained this before, that *Sabeq-e-Ta'ala* means... The meaning of *Sabeq-e-Ta'ala* is that it refers to the *'aql-e-awwal* (First Intellect). *'Aql-e-awwal*, *mawjud-e-awwal* (first existent), *wujud-e-awwal* (first being), *sabeq-e-awwal* (first precedent)—all these refer to the *'aql-e-awwal*. This is a being who has encompassed the entire universe. Meaning not just the world, but all the realms (*'awalim*). That is why it is *Rabb al-'alamin* (Lord of the worlds), not *Rabb al-'alam* (Lord of the world). *Alhamdulillah Rabb al-'alamin* (All praise is for Allah, Lord of the worlds), meaning there are many realms. How many are there? There is the spiritual realm (*'alam-e-ruhani*), the realm of creation (*'alam-e-khalq*), the physical realm (*'alam-e-jismani*), the psychic realm (*'alam-e-nafsani*), the realm of life (*'alam-e-hayat*). There are many realms. If we go into its details, then where the realm of creation begins, where the realm of intellect (*'alam-e-'aql*) is, where the luminous realm (*'alam-e-nurani*) is... all these things. So, among them, the very first being who professed the *tawhid*... if you don't understand this, you won't understand anything. That the *'aql-e-awwal*... the *ma'dhuniyyat* begins from this very point. That the *Mubde'-e-Ta'ala*, who created, created countless beings (*jawads*). He created them all at once. He created them in one go. This is the beginning of the *ma'dhuniyyat*, that Allah Ta'ala created the luminous forms (*ashbah-e-nurani*) in the state of a form (*shibh*), meaning it was a form like the letter *alif*, a human form, but it was luminous, spiritual, and holy. Those beings were countless, meaning there was no count. And only Allah knows the number of His soldiers. How many they were in number. So, the luminous forms were created in a realm, and out of them, the first one to profess the *tawhid* of the Lord of the Worlds was him. And how did he do it? This is the biggest issue and the greatest *tawhid*, that he did it without a teacher (*mu'allim*) and without an inspirer (*mulhim*). Without a teacher. There was no one to explain it to him at that time. Nor was there any *mulhim*, meaning one who gives inspiration. He did it on his own. That is, and look here, it is because of the extreme longing for the gnosis of the *Mubde'*, or extreme bewilderment. Out of bewilderment, he suddenly began to do it, thinking that there must be someone who sustains me. And the first declaration of *tawhid* he made was this: "Neither was I created by myself, nor did I create my own kind. Neither can they create me, nor can I create them. Rather, our creator is someone else."

This is the first sign of *tawhid*. And this *tawhid* which is our special chapter, from which the *ma'dhuniyyat* begins, *tawhid* has three components. One is *tajrid* (abstraction/stripping away), another is *tanzih* (declaring transcendence), and the third is *tawhid*. *Tawhid* means to affirm the oneness of the *Mubde'-e-Subhanahu*, that no one else has the power to create. And for this, what is needed? *Tajrid*. *Jard al-ilahiyyah* (stripping away divinity). *Jard al-ilahiyyah* means he separated all of his own kind from divinity, saying that there is no power in them to create, except for Him. This is called *tajrid*. *Jard*. And there are many meanings to it, I don't want to go into the details now. *Tanzih*. The second word is *tanzih*. *Munazzah 'an al-sifat* (transcendent above attributes). He separated the *Mubde'-e-Ta'ala*, who created the spiritual realm, from attributes. He stripped him, separated him, made him transcendent. Making him transcendent means from attributes. Attributes apply to created beings, not to Allah. So the Lord of the Worlds is far above this. Now the *Asma' al-Husna* (The Most Beautiful Names) that we recite, Ya Allah, Ya Rahman, Ya Rahim, all these attributes are all attributes. So we are told from the beginning that these are all names of Allah. It's correct. But these are not the names of Allah, rather they are of Allah's special angels (*mala'ikah*) upon whom these names are bestowed. How so? For example, Ya Qadir, Ya Ghafur, Ya Rahim. All of these... *Ghafur* means the forgiver, *Sattar* means the concealer of faults. So you, even a small... you too have concealed the faults of many people. You have forgiven many people. So you have become *Ghafur*? So you are also *Ghafur* and Allah is also *Ghafur*? This cannot be. That is why the name we give is... we never give the name Ghaffar. It is *'Abd al-Ghaffar*. It is *'Abd al-Qadir*. All of Allah's 99 names, *'abd* (servant) comes with them. Names like Qadir and so on are not given. It is *'Abd al-Qadir*, *'Abd al-Ra'uf*—all these names are given. So the meaning is that *munazzah 'an al-sifat* (transcendent of attributes)... from attributes... stripping him of attributes. This is the second thing. And the *tawhid* of *Rabb al-'alamin*, that there is no deity but Him.

And this is... what did he say? Now here, the meaning of *Allahu la ilaha illa hu* is *Shahida Allahu annahu la ilaha illa hu* (Allah has witnessed that there is no deity except Him). I bear witness that... meaning Allah has witnessed. *Shahida Allahu... la ilaha illa hu.* That there is no deity except *Hu*. That *Hu* is... the meaning of *Hu* is that strange scene where there was nothing, from non-existence, from *'adam*, He brought it into existence. And he created the luminous forms in thousands, lakhs, crores, countless, innumerable, and immeasurable beings.

So remember that the spiritual realm is a special one, which is also called the realm of intellect (*'alam-e-'aql*). It is also called the spiritual realm. And after that, the realms that exist, their names are different. From where the division has occurred, from where the matter of believing came. Now look, this thing is that whatever we are reading is this: *Allahu la ilaha illa hu*. Allah is He besides whom there is no other object of worship. That is, the *Sabeq-e-Ta'ala* (Exalted Precedent). Who is the *Sabeq-e-Ta'ala*? The *Sabeq-e-Ta'ala* is He. He is *Ta'ala* (exalted), very high. He is far above us. He is the first veil (*hijab-e-awwal*). He became the veil of the *Mubde'-e-Ta'ala*. The moment he professed the *tawhid* of *Rabb al-'alamin*, he became distinct from all the realms, and he was elevated. And his state was such that it was so... I mean, first he was a luminous form, and then the light began to increase. It increased and increased so much that those below fell into bewilderment. In seeing him, they became bewildered. And from that, the guidance, they say, and the *ma'dhuniyyat* which begins, it starts from this very thing. That the beings below, however many there were, thousands and lakhs, at that moment their gaze fell, "Oh, who is this whose light has become more than ours? He was just like us." So, the *'aql-e-awwal*... now people are bewildered about him. So in one sense, the meaning in our tradition is that the *'aql-e-awwal* himself has been called Allah. So Allah is... the meaning of Allah, look in the *Munjid*, look in the dictionary, the meaning of Allah is that about whom one feels longing (*shawq*) or about whom one is bewildered.

So look here, its meaning is the extreme longing for the *ma'rifat* (gnosis) of the *Mubde'*, or the state of being drowned in extreme bewilderment. What is it? It is Allah, derived from *waliha*. Allah is derived from *waliha* or from *aliha*. Or from *aliha* or from *yaliuhu*. Because... ...the *Mubde'-e-Ta'ala*, neither can any indication be made towards Him, nor can any attribute be applied to Him. The prayer that we offer, all of it is offered to the *Mubde'-e-Ta'ala*. It is not for anyone else. Meaning, among the created beings, from the *'aql-e-awwal* down to here, the prayer is not for anyone. We know, in terms of association, that today is this day, this is for Mawlana 'Ali, this is for the Prophet, this month is like this. But the prayer that is offered is only for the *Mubde'-e-Ta'ala*. If it is directed away from Him, it is not a prayer at all. So remember that the one who is the true master, the Lord of the Worlds, the creator of the spiritual realm, He is the *Mubde'-e-Ta'ala*, for whom the word *Hu* has been used. And only an indication can be made. Look, it is an indication. So no indication can be made... no kind of indication we can make that He is in the sky, on the earth, He is not here, He is in the valley, He is not on the mountain. It cannot be anything. Wherever He is, there Allah is. So remember this, that Allah is *Khabir* (All-Aware) and '*Alim* (All-Knowing). The entire Quran is filled with this, that Allah Ta'ala is also *'Alim*, He is also *Basir* (All-Seeing), everything is in Him. So what this means is that all the names we take, the *Asma' al-Husna*, they are Allah's special representatives. Now, Ya Qadir, Ya Ra'uf, Ya Ghafur, these names that are being taken, which beings do they apply to? We don't have knowledge of that. So the *du'at* say that if you don't know the specifics, then understand that all these things apply to the *'aql-e-awwal*. That the *'aql-e-awwal* is that being who encompasses everything. And above him is only the *Mubde'-e-Ta'ala*, who created the spiritual realm. Neither can our thoughts reach him... these are the sentences of the oath. The oath that is taken, its secrets are given. That neither can our inner sight (*basirat*) reach him, nor our outer sight (*basarat*), nor can our thoughts reach him. We cannot see with our eyes. We can only believe. And how do we believe? Well, *ma'rifat* (gnosis) is not possible. The *ma'rifat* of Allah, the *Mubde'-e-Subhanahu*, who created the spiritual realm and the... the spiritual realm... how can we have *ma'rifat* of him? So for *ma'rifat*, it has been said that *ma'rifat* is simply not possible. Just be helpless. *La tujasirunnahu al-khawatir.* (Thoughts do not venture towards Him.) Our hearts cannot have notions. No thought can enter our hearts. Remember this, that we can believe. So what is there for that? That we should just affirm. That He is, that's all. And point the finger and say *Shahida Allahu annahu la ilaha illa hu.* (Allah has witnessed that there is no deity except Him.)

*Al-Hayy* (The Ever-Living). Alive. *Al-Hayy*, He is alive. This is an indication towards the *Sabeq-e-Ta'ala* who is the source of eternal life. Now look, all the attributes are for him, they are being applied to the *Mubda'-e-Awwal*, and they are for the *Sabeq-e-Awwal*. *Al-Hayy*, He is alive. This is an indication towards the *Sabeq-e-Ta'ala*, who is the source of eternal life. All life forms emerged from him. In recognizing him... "Hey, these were our companions, how did he become so luminous?" And it has been said that the light that started to form in them... the light and radiance... in the revelation... kept increasing. It increased so much that the people below were bewildered. They became so low that he became the *Sabeq-e-Ta'ala*, and he was given the rank of *'aql-e-awwal*. Now look, in the realm of intellects, you all keep reading the *ma'dhuniyyat*, you know it happens every year. This *'aql-e-awwal* has gone up to the tenth intellect (*'aql-e-'ashir*). *'Aql* (intellect)... the meaning of *'aql* is "to tie." To tie, to keep something in control. The camel that is there, a stake is driven for the camel, and it is tied with a rope, and the camel can only roam in the area it covers in a circle. It cannot go beyond that. So that is called *'aql*. So this *'aql* is... that *'aql*, if our intellect works, it will work only according to our understanding. If we show excessive cleverness, we will become foolish. So remember, the intellect has a restraint. That is why it has been said that those who act presumptuously, they become foolish and do not keep their intellect in check.

*Al-Qayyum* (The Self-Sustaining). He is established. Meaning... *Al-Hayy al-Qayyum*. He is also *Qayyum*. He is established. Meaning all the realms... ...the helper of all the realms. Now, all the support (*ta'idat*), whatever we understand, that we are getting support, where is it from? We get support from the *Da'i* of the time. Where does the *Da'i* of the time get it from? He says from the Imam. Where does the Imam get it from? He says from the *Qawa'im*. Where do the *Qawa'im* get it from? From the *Jusus*. Where do the *Jusus* get it from? From above. It goes on and on up to the *Sabeq-e-Ta'ala*, and it is the *Sabeq-e-Ta'ala* who is the helper of all. The one who gives help is him. Meaning, the helper of all the realms is him.

*Wala ta'khudhuhu sinatun wala nawm.* (Neither drowsiness nor sleep overtakes Him.) *La ta'khudhuhu sinatun wala nawm.* *La ta'khudhuhu sinatun wala nawm.* Neither... Now look, we recite this daily, five times we recite it. And what is the verse? *La ta'khudhuhu sinatun wala nawm.* Neither does drowsiness overcome him, nor sleep. We fall asleep while listening to the lecture. The lecture is going on, and it's a human nature that you listen to a lecture for some time, and then your mind gets tired, and you fall asleep. This has been observed. So what is the matter? Neither does sleep ever overcome him, nor... a jolt. Drowsiness. Drowsiness comes. Meaning, in giving help... ...laziness does not come to him, nor... Now look, the meaning... its real *ta'wil* (esoteric interpretation) is. This we were just reading the translation, that neither drowsiness overcomes him, nor sleep. Meaning, he never shows laziness in giving help. The one who is receiving it, is receiving it from there. It is coming from above.

*Lahu ma fi al-samawati wa ma fi al-ard.* (To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth.) The heavens and the earth, whatever is in them, is His. Yes. Meaning... the manifest and the hidden, He is the master of it all. Yes. Now see, this has many meanings. Two or three lines of the translation are coming. That He is the master of the manifest (*zahir*) and the hidden (*batin*). He is of the heavens and the earth. The heavens, meaning the seven heavens, and the seven earths have been created. Adam, Nuh, Ibrahim, Musa, 'Isa, and the Prophet, and our coming *Qa'im*, who is the seventh. So these seven *Nutuqa'* are in the station of the heavens, and their *Wasīs* are in the station of the earth. And it is also related to the noble *da'wat*. Two meanings. The heavens and the earth, whatever is in them, is His. Meaning, of the manifest and the hidden. You have been hearing from two perspectives, in the morning lesson and in the evening lesson, that He is the master of the manifest (*zahir*) and the hidden (*batin*). The manifest is a separate thing, the *tanzil* (exoteric revelation), and the *ta'wil* (esoteric interpretation), He is the master of both.

*Man dhalladhi...* *Man dhalladhi yashfa'u 'indahu illa bi-idhnihi.* (Who is it that can intercede with Him except by His permission?) Whose power is it that without His permission... Whose power is it that without His permission, one can intercede in His presence?

Meaning... His *Bab-e-Ta'li* (Gate of the Follower), besides him... no one can intercede. Look, *Bab*. There is *Bab*, and above it, *Ta'li* is also written. The *Ta'li* is the same... the *Ta'li* is the being of the *Munba'ith-e-Awwal* (First Emissary). That if... where... you have read the *ma'dhuniyyat*, you have seen it. I don't know if the *ma'dhuniyyat* has happened here or not. But when the *'aql-e-awwal* was established in his rank, the veil of... he became the veil of God. He became the greatest veil. At that time, his joy and his... was such that his radiance increased so much that the people below fell into bewilderment. Now, in that, it has been explained that only two individuals moved forward. This is a special topic of the *ma'dhuniyyat*, it is a topic of *tawhid*, that when the *'aql-e-awwal* took the lead, after that, two individuals arose, two forms arose. And in that, one is the *Munba'ith-e-Awwal* and one is the *Munba'ith-e-Thani*. *Munba'ith* means the one who rises, rising. One is the *Munba'ith-e-Awwal* and one is the *Munba'ith-e-Thani*. Two arose. Now, the meaning of two arising is that even today, if you look at numbers, after one, it is always two that comes. Take out all the books, wherever... all the languages in the world, all of them, after the singular, the plural comes. After one, the plural form comes. Except for Arabic, in which there is also a dual (*tathniyah*). *Tathniyah* means two, dual. So what this means is that the greatest system of Allah was that of the *'aql-e-awwal*, and after the *'aql-e-awwal*, two forms arose. And both of them tried. And how did they try? That... neither do we, from ourselves... create all these, nor do they create us. They first affirmed one thing. The second is that he preceded us in this... in professing *tawhid*. They acknowledged the rank of the *'aql-e-awwal*. They affirmed it. That both of them did it. Both of them, if you read, you will find out that both of them affirmed that the *'aql-e-awwal* is better than us. And we are moving forward by looking at him. So see, the first one was without a teacher, without an inspirer. Here, both of them moved forward by looking at him, in the *tawhid* of God. This is the second chapter.

But what was the difference? From here, see, the separation began. The system of the world that was disrupted and the opposites that were created below, they were created for this very reason. What happened? That among them, one did not pay heed to the second. The two who had risen, one's gaze was lofty and one's was base. So the lofty one was... the second person... both had risen in rank. But the rank was... he was given one, and the second one, his... had a delusion of equality (*wahm-e-masawat*). "I am equal to him." The one above is bestowing a gaze on someone, and you are saying I am also... This is what happened there. And what happened? The *Munba'ith-e-Awwal*, who was the first... whose gaze was lofty, and the gaze... the meaning of gaze is very deep, chapter after chapter is on it. How much can be explained? That his gaze was, but the second one said that I believe in Allah, I believe in this *'aql-e-awwal* who is superior. But I don't believe in him, because he was with me, we are both equal. Just this... the delusion... and that is why in Sayyidna Ghulam's book, if you read, you will find out that delusion, envy, greed, all these are bad habits. They are the "mothers of sins" (*ummahat ma'asi*). The sin is... which is a sin, among them, this is also one. To have a delusion. Delusion that we are both one. This is wrong. No one is equal. "*Faddalna ba'dahum 'ala ba'd*" (We have preferred some of them over others). Each one is given preference over another. So what this means is that there, the second intellect, the mistake it made was this, that "I and he are equal." As soon as... he stagnated. He stood still. He stopped. And the *Munba'ith-e-Awwal* became the veil of the *'aql-e-awwal*. When this happened, a change occurred in the realm. You read in the *ma'dhuniyyat* the subjects and its... listen to the cassette, you will find out. That in the two, one became superior, who is called the *Munba'ith-e-Awwal*. Now the *Munba'ith-e-Thani* stopped. But the realm was a realm of liberty, a realm of freedom. At that time, all the intellects moved forward. And how many were there? Seven intellects moved forward. Seven intellects moved forward, and seven and these two became nine. And after that, the one who was the *Munba'ith-e-Thani*, whose gaze was base, he realized that "I was up there, how did I come here?" And at that very moment, he thought that "No, I have to ask." So the one who was the eighth... ninth form, the ninth intellect, in the circle of the intellect, there were thousands of people, thousands of forms. He asked the last person of the ninth circle, "What is my mistake? I was there, how did I come here?" At that time, his request was forwarded upwards. And it reached the *Munba'ith-e-Awwal*. And he said that this mistake was of equality. It was the delusion of equality. As soon as he found out, he repented. Look, repentance... he repented. And as soon as he repented, his repentance was accepted, and he became the tenth intellect (*'aqil-e-'ashir*). The nine intellects had already been formed, this is the tenth intellect. And he is the tenth intellect who created the entire world. The town planner of the entire world is the tenth intellect. *'Ashir*. *'Ashir*, *'ashir*, we who... recite in the prayers, he is the tenth intellect, his rank... So remember that this is a summary of the *ma'dhuniyyat*, which is the realm of intellects. This is... it's very long. I am just giving brief indications. But it's very big, how the forms were created, what they did, and what kind of gaze there was, what it is. *La ta'khudhuhu sinatun wala nawm.* (Neither drowsiness nor sleep overtakes Him.) Neither drowsiness overcomes him, nor sleep. Meaning, the helper is not lazy. *Lahu ma fi al-samawati wa ma fi al-ard.* (To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth.) The heavens and the earth, whatever is in them, is His. Meaning, in the manifest and the hidden. The manifest and the hidden. Now the manifest and the hidden began. The lofty gaze and the base gaze. Everywhere, this is what it is, the lofty gaze and the base gaze. The one who has a base gaze should understand that the one with the lofty gaze is superior. This... this should be accepted. *Man dhalladhi yashfa'u 'indahu illa bi-idhnihi.* (Who is it that can intercede with Him except by His permission?) Whose power is it that without his permission, a request can be made in his presence, an intercession can be made? Meaning, now see, the *Ta'li*. The *Ta'li*. The *Ta'li* is clapped with two hands. The *Munba'ith-e-Awwal* and the *Munba'ith-e-Thani*. Or the *Ta'li* has become. The *Ta'li* is what? It is the being of the *Munba'ith-e-Awwal*, who became the veil of the *'aql-e-awwal*. And from here, he became the next, the follower. He became the one who follows. And besides him, no one can intercede. The *Munba'ith-e-Awwal*, besides him... meaning, only within his circle can you... all our requests that go, we think that they reach the Imam of the time here. But in reality, the circle goes up to there, up to the *Munba'ith-e-Awwal*. He is the master of all.

Now, it has been explained that the *'aql-e-awwal*, who did it without an inspirer... this is a special thing to understand, that the *'aql-e-awwal* who did it without a teacher and without an inspirer, he was removed from the circle. He was made higher. And the circle of unity (*da'irah-e-wahdah*) was made. *Wahdah* means he is the one and only being, that is the being of the *'aql-e-awwal*. That's it, it ends there. With the *Munba'ith-e-Awwal*, there are a few. And with his third intellect, there are more. In the fourth, there are more. The soldiers of Allah, I mean, the army, only Allah knows how many there are. It was divided into seven circles. And for this reason, seven heavens were made. And in this way, down to the realm of the human being. So, the *Munba'ith-e-Awwal*, he is the Holy Presence (*hadirat al-quds*). The Garden of Abode (*jannat al-ma'wa*) is near the Holy Presence. And here in our world, he is the Imam of the time, and then his... who is it? The Gate of Gates (*Bab al-Abwab*). The Gate of Gates is the Garden of Abode (*jannat al-ma'wa*), which is near the Lote-tree of the Utmost Boundary (*sidrat al-muntaha*). Remember this, this is of the world here... the state.

So now it is being said here that besides his *Bab-e-Ta'li*, no one can intercede. *Munba'ith-e-Awwal*, it is written here. *Ya'lamu ma bayna aydihim.* Read, brother. *Ya'lamu ma bayna aydihim.* (He knows what is [presently] before them.) He knows those things which are before them. Meaning, the *du'at* of the *A'immah*... and their *hujjat* (proofs), who are the manifest representatives in the heavens and the earth, he knows them. *Wa ma khalfahum.* (And what will be after them.) And those who are behind or after them. Meaning, those who will be established in their ranks after them, their successors (*khulafa'*). Yes. *Wala yuhituna bi-shay'in...* Now, the same thing happened in that realm. In the realm of intellects, when seven intellects were formed, after the seven intellects, 82 intellects were formed. This is all a very subtle matter, it might be difficult to understand. But this is it, that 82 intellects were formed after that. And this, Sayyidna Hasan Khan, who is... 'Abd al-Malik, he has explained it with great clarity, how in the realm of intellects, seven were formed, and then seven went up from below. And then seven *Nutuqa'* were formed. Then seven opposites were formed. And this is our count, meaning, that is, we carry around the 28 letters. From *alif* to *ya*, there are 28. In the 28, there are four pieces of seven each, or two of fourteen each. So remember that all this, until we understand it, the *ta'wil* will not be understood, and if the *ta'wil* is not understood, the realities will not be understood. *Ya'lamu ma bayna aydihim*, meaning the *du'at* and *hujjat* of the *A'immah*, who are the manifest ones in the heavens and the earth, the representatives. *Wa ma khalfahum*, and those who will come after them, meaning those who will be established in their ranks, their successors. *Wala yuhituna bi-shay'in min 'ilmihi illa bima sha'.* (And they encompass not a thing of His knowledge except for what He wills.) And the people... people cannot be aware of any part of his knowledge, except for that much which he wishes. Meaning, it is in the authority of Allah that... here, what is written? It is in the authority of the *Sabeq-e-Ta'ala* that how much knowledge is given to you. It is not in anyone's authority. We, the... what is it for us? That the acquired intellect exists, and the innate intellect exists. Now, the common people know, neither the scientists know, where the intellect is. Where is the intellect? What is the innate intellect called? And what is the acquired intellect? Is it in the brain or in the heart? Now, you can look it up, you can ask a philosopher or a scientist. I don't want to speak today, tomorrow, God willing, we will do it, it has become too much. Go on, tomorrow, God willing, I will explain. *Wala yuhituna bi-shay'in min 'ilmihi illa bima sha'.* And those people cannot be aware of any part of his knowledge, except for that much... as much as he is made aware of. Meaning... Meaning, the *A'immah*, *hujjat*, and *du'at* all know from his knowledge only as much as he has taught them. Yes. *Wasi'a kursiyyuhu al-samawati wa al-ard.* (His Throne extends over the heavens and the earth.) His throne has spread over the heavens and the earth. Meaning, the throne, whose representative is the *wasī*, it is dominant over the *A'immah* and the *hujjat*. *Wala ya'uduhu hifzuhuma.* Now, there are many things in this, I don't want to make the discussion long now. Otherwise, what is the meaning of the throne, whose... the *wasī* of the Prophet, who is dominant over the *A'immah* and the *hujjat*. What does dominant mean? Mawlana 'Ali (sallallahu 'alayhi), who is the *wasī* of the Prophet, Mawlana 'Ali (sallallahu 'alayhi), he is the father of the Imams (*Abu al-A'immah*). He is the leader of the pious (*Imam al-muttaqin*). He is the leader of the radiant ones (*qa'id al-ghurr al-muhajjalin*). And from where the noble *da'wat* begins, he is the *wasī* of the Prophet. And all the Imams who are coming, from Mawlana Hasan to the present Imam, all of them are veils (*hijab*) of Mawlana 'Ali. They are veils. Now to understand this, let's leave this matter, it's enough. This is... it has been said... what has been said? "Paradise lies at the feet of the mother." "Paradise lies at the feet of the mother." What does this mean? "Paradise lies at the feet of the mother," have you understood? What does it mean? A dutiful one... his ethical advice, all this is in its place, that one should also have love for the mother, and one should also have affection for the mother, and one should also obey the mother. But... "Paradise lies at the feet of the mother," what does it mean? So it has been explained in other books that this is a saying of the Prophet, that "O 'Ali, I and you, O 'Ali, are the two fathers of the believers (*abawayn al-mu'minin*)." "I and you, O 'Ali..." ...are the parents of all believers. So, the father is you, and the mother is Mawlana 'Ali (sallallahu 'alayhi)'s being. Now see, this is a point to understand. Should one love the father or the mother? What does nature say? Love is for the mother. And for this reason, the *wilayah* (love/allegiance) of Amir al-Mu'minin has been made obligatory. The *wilayah* of the Prophet, has it been mentioned anywhere? That if there is no love for the Prophet or if he is not obeyed, then we are not even Muslims. But after becoming a Muslim, until... the *wasī* of the Prophet, 'Ali al-Murtada (sallallahu 'alayhi), there is no love for him... without the *wilayah* of Amir al-Mu'minin, neither your prayer, nor your fast, nor your pilgrimage, nor your zakat, nothing is valid. So what this means is that in religion, the ranks that are there, or the believers, or the respondents, whatever they are, for every one of them, in the rank of the mother is the being of Mawlana 'Ali. At the feet of the mother is... what is it? Paradise. At the feet of the parents... the common mother, you obey her anyway, and your love for her awakens, everything is there. But the real mother is Mawlana Amir al-Mu'minin (sallallahu 'alayhi)'s being. And his feet are from Mawlana Hasan to here, to the 48th Imam. They are the feet (*khudum*). Whose love has been made obligatory. You cannot leave a single Imam. All of them, you have to remember them by name, so that our prayer is complete. So, feet means this.

Another example is also there. I will just mention it. More than just reading... that wherever analogies (*tamthilat*) have been given, to understand religion, that *Allahu nur al-samawati wa al-ard.* (Allah is the Light of the heavens and the earth.) Allah is the light of the heavens and the earth. So what is the earth, and what are the heavens? The earth is the being of Mawlana Amir al-Mu'minin (sallallahu 'alayhi), and the heavens are the being of the Prophet. This is the second example. The third, what is it? ... The sun and the moon. Who is the sun of the religion? The spiritual sun is the being of Mawlana the Prophet. And Mawlana 'Ali is the moon of the *da'wat*. So what this means is, how will you interpret the sun? How are you saying that... the Prophet is in it? How... how will you say this? So it has been explained that where... it has been explained that where... where the mention of the sun has come in the Quran, there... there it has been explained that "*sirajan wahhaja*." (a burning lamp). "A lamp that is blazing." Blazing means it is giving light, it is giving heat, it is giving warmth. "*Sirajan wahhaja*," this is the attribute of the sun. And when the example of the Prophet is given, there it is said "*sirajan munira*." (a luminous lamp). He has also been called a lamp. So both became lamps. That is why we say that the spiritual sun is the Prophet, and the spiritual moon is Mawlana 'Ali (sallallahu 'alayhi)'s being. Now you see that we... can we sit in the light of the sun? You sit for two hours, your life will be at risk. The commands of the Prophet, the religious obligations, fasting, praying, doing this, doing that, you get tired of it. But we have to believe in it because it is the Prophet's... all these commands have come through revelation. But if you see this in an example, not the sun, you sit under the moon. You sit in a moonlit night, you can sit for hours. You benefit from it. Because the Prophet is in the station of the sun, so his light is called *ziya'* (radiance). The light that is self-generated is called *ziya'*, and the light that is borrowed from others is called *nur* (light). So the light in the moon is borrowed, it is taken from the sun. The Prophet... it is taken from him. And Mawlana 'Ali says that "I learned a thousand chapters of knowledge from the Prophet, and from each thousand, a thousand more chapters opened up for me." So what this means is that the Prophet gave, and 'Ali took. So you... you also, here in the world, science tells us that all the light in the moon is a gift from the sun. So the spiritual sun is the Prophet, and the spiritual moon is Mawlana 'Ali (sallallahu 'alayhi). And that is why we... divine sciences, or lordly sciences, which are the streams of Mawlana 'Ali, which are his sciences, his realities, we can listen to 'Ali's for hours. There is difficulty in the commands. "Hey, the fast has become 14 hours long, it has become 16 hours long, so-and-so happened, how to give this much zakat, so-and-so." All these are difficulties. So the matter of the sun is different, and the matter of the moon is different. So the three examples are, the sun and the moon are on the Prophet and 'Ali. The parents, the father and mother, are also them. And the third is this... what is it? The heavens and the earth. The heavens are the *Nutuqa'*, and the *wasī* of the Prophet is... he is. God willing, if there is another discussion, I will explain it.

Now one thing remains, that is the intellect. Where is the intellect? You should find out where the intellect is. Science says one thing, geographers say another, philosophers say another, that it is inside the brain. And we have to think about something, so the brain has to be used. And for us, what do the *du'at* teach? That the intellect is in the heart as well as in the brain. The intellect. But there is a difference between the two. One is the acquired intellect (*'aql-e-muktasib*), and one is the innate intellect (*'aql-e-gharizi*). The innate is a different thing. Acquired, grasping power. The child slowly learns and grows, that is related to the brain. And for us, the structure of the Imam of the time, the *haykal-e-imami*, inside it, who is in the station of the brain, who is in the station of the heart, all this needs to be known. God willing, when the opportunity comes, I will explain. Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim... ...Al-Fatiha.

...to the Imam of the time, and the da'wah of the Imam of the time is the da'wah of the Wasi. So, from this perspective, if you look, the da'wah of the Wasi is the da'wah of the divine religion, and there is no compulsion to enter it. La ikraha fi al-din (There is no compulsion in religion). This is the statement of Allah Ta'ala, and its explanation, that is, with the word 'yani' (meaning), is the ta'wil of the Holy Qur'an which Sayyidna Husayn Husamuddin stated. qad tabayyana al-rushdu min al-ghayy (the right course has become distinct from the wrong). Hidayah (guidance) has become clear from zalalah (misguidance). Meaning, the distinction between the station of the Wasi and the station of the Zidd has been established. fa man yakfur bi al-taghuti wa yu'min billahi... The station of the Zidd... who was the Zidd of the Wasi of the Prophet, Maulana Ali Salawatullah 'alayh, it has become known from them who is right and who is wrong. fa man yakfur bi al-taghuti wa yu'min billahi (So whoever disbelieves in Taghut and believes in Allah). The person who rejects the Taghut and brings iman (faith) in Allah... yani (meaning) the one who rejects the Zidd al-Awwal (the first opponent) and accepts the Wasi. Ji. fa qad istamsaka bi al-'urwati al-wuthqa (has grasped the most trustworthy handhold). So he has grasped the strong rope of Allah. Look, this, this is: he rejects the Zidd al-Awwal. As I have mentioned before, if one is to come to the da'wah of the Wasi, meaning to accept the wilayah of Amir al-Mu'minin, then one must also perform bara'ah (disassociation) from those who are against him. Until there is bara'ah, it cannot happen. It should be in the heart, whether it is expressed by the tongue or not. Meaning, in the era of taqiyah, it is not necessary. But the bara'ah should be from one's heart, that 'we do not accept them'. The Khalifah, the true janashin (successor) of the Prophet is Maulana Ali Salawatullah 'alayh, who was raised in Ghadir Khumm. So the meaning is that the one who was made [successor] in Ghadir Khumm is the true janashin. The one whom the people made is not the true janashin. And what happened at the time of the Prophet's passing, you all have heard in the majalis that at the Prophet's final moment, it became very difficult. Janab Ali and Janab Fatima were sitting beside him, and all the people were holding a committee, having a meeting there. At Saqifah, which is behind the Masjid al-Nabawi, there. That when the Prophet passes away, and the situation is such, what should we do now? Who will lead the prayer and who will be the leader? So all that meeting was happening, and in the midst of it, Janab Umar, who is the Khalifah Thani, he said to Abu Bakr Sahib, the Khalifah Awwal, that 'bring, extend your hand, I will give you my...' ...I do it. Then place a piece of them on every mountain. Then call them. Look, the incident is like this, that they will come running. Four of them will come running. Now, you cut up the birds, put four pieces, and place one piece on each mountain, and then call out. They themselves will come flying. What is the meaning of this? If this is the meaning that the world understands, which is explained in the Qur'an Sharif, then there is no meaning. It is not understood. Until its ta'wil is explained. Yani (meaning)... Yani (meaning), send them to different places and spread them out separately. Then command them to invite towards you. They will immediately say 'labbayk' (at your service) to your command. And will quickly be engaged in spreading your da'wah. wa a'lam anna Allaha 'Azizun Hakim (And know that Allah is Exalted in Might and Wise.). And know that Allah is All-Powerful, All-Wise. Yani (meaning), the Wasi has no nazir (equal) or mathil (peer), and is Hakim (wise) in his actions. mathalu alladhina yunfiquna amwalahum fi sabili Allahi ka mathali habbatin anbatat sab'a sanabila fi kulli sunbulatin mi'atu habbatin (The example of those who spend their wealth in the way of Allah is like a seed [of grain] which grows seven spikes; in each spike is a hundred grains.). Those who spend their wealth in the way of Allah, their example is like that of a grain which grows seven ears, and in each ear, there are a hundred grains. 'Baal' means the ears that come out of the wheat, that. Now you have heard the lesson of Hazrat Da'i, how there are benefits of Zakat. If you spend in the way of Allah, how much benefit there is. The meaning of Zakat is 'safai' (cleanliness). It comes from 'zakka'. So what is the meaning? And its, the meanings of Zakat are told to be very high. That Zakat is the rank after namaz (prayer). It is not fasting. Fasting comes later. Aqimu al-salata wa atu al-zakat (Establish prayer and give zakat). So, establish prayer and give Zakat. So Zakat is... for Janab Ali Salawatullah 'alayh, and Salat is for the Prophet. Meaning, follow the Prophet's shari'ah and 'Ali's ta'wil. Aqimu al-salata wa atu al-zakat. Zakat is a very special thing, that out of 40 rupees, take out one rupee. The wealth you have, to take out 1 for 40 from it, your wealth does not decrease. Rather, that 1 for 40 is Allah's right. If you do not give, your 39 are ruined. And if you give, then the 39 become pure. So this is the concept of Zakat. And Sayyidna Husayn... Isma'il bin Hiba, Allah Ta'ala says to him, he says that by giving this, your wealth does not decrease. And by not giving, there is no... it doesn't happen that your wealth increases. So the meaning of this is that wherever... and it has been told from your side that wherever there is loss for the mumineen in the dry land and the sea, it happens for this reason, that they do not give Zakat fully. They do not give it fully. They give, but less. And for that, the narration of Maulana Ja'far al-Sadiq that you heard just now, how an old woman comes and troubles a man. Suhayl was his name. And he... started to complain, came to Maulana Ja'far al-Sadiq and said, 'Look, an old woman comes to me at night, she scares me. And I am worried.' So a friend of mine said, that friend came and said that my friend has this thing. So Maulana Ja'far al-Sadiq said, 'Ask him, to whom does he give Zakat?' He asked. He said, 'I will ask tomorrow and tell.' The next day he came and asked. He said, 'I take out 1/40th. What do you do with the 1/40th?' He said, 'I take it out and distribute it with my own hands.' He said, 'This is the reason she troubles you.' That it should go up in the da'wah. It should go to the Imam of the time. If there is no Imam, then to the Da'i al-Mutlaq. If there is no Da'i, then to those who are great, it should reach there. From all places, it comes up, and then from up, it is distributed. Among whom? Eight people. The names of the eight people are all given. That how, they who are the great ones of the da'wah, they distribute it. So the names of all are given. That there is ibn sabil, 'amilin, and besides that, poor, needy, orphans, captives, and on whom a case is running, or understand, who are in such... difficulties, have committed a murder. To such people it is given. And besides that, one is also mu'allafat al-qulub. Mu'allafat al-qulub means to win over hearts. To win over their hearts, the great ones of the da'wah also send something to them. And it happens that in the Da'wah Sharif, in many places, such people who want to harm the da'wah, it is given to them so that they remain quiet, that is called mu'allafat al-qulub. Yani (meaning) those who try to establish the position of the Sahib-e-Haqq and are like the Natiq, in whose daur (era) there are seven Imams, and under each Imam, there are one hundred Hudud. Wallahu yuda'ifu li man yasha'u wa Allahu Wasi'un 'Alim (And Allah multiplies [His reward] for whom He wills. And Allah is all-Encompassing and Knowing.). And Allah, for whomever He wishes, increases. And Allah is All-Encompassing, All-Knowing. Yani (meaning) Sabiq-e-Tala, among these servants, whomever's ranks He wants to increase, He increases it according to their capacity and ability. And Sabiq-e-Tala has this power. And He also knows to whom more should be given. Bas. Sabiq-e-Tala is who? The dhat (essence) of 'Aql-e-Awwal. Sabiq-e-Tala is the dhat of 'Aql-e-Awwal. We, about Mubdi'-e-Tala, neither our thoughts go there, nor our eyes go there. So whatever is, it starts from 'Aql-e-Awwal. And between 'Aql-e-Awwal and Mubdi'-e-Tala, there is only one thing that is created, and that is the Kalimah. It is the Kalimah, that is, the Amr-e-Ilahi (Divine Command). And it is the hukm (command), that it comes out. So from 'Aql-e-Awwal, things emanate downwards, and in the 'alam-e-jismani (physical world), they reach the Natiq of the daur, who is the Prophet Salawatullah 'alayh. So from there, to whomever they wish, they give. And after Janab Prophet, it comes to Janab Wasi. After the Wasi, the Imams begin. So the Imam is the muhafiz-e-shari'at (guardian of the shari'ah). The real responsible one for the shari'ah is him. We are doing it according to our own capacity. But the real muhafiz is the person of Janab Imam. Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim. [Du'a in Arabic] al-Fatiha.

Baqarah, 158. This is page 26. 159.

Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim (In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful). Ya ayyuha-lladhina amanu (O you who have believed)...

`wa asabahumu l-kibaru wa-lahu dhurriyyatun du`afa'u fa-asabaha i`sarun fihi narun fahtaraqat. Kadhalika yubayyinu llahu lakumu l-ayati la`allakum tatafakkarun` (and old age befalls him while he has weak offspring, and a whirlwind containing fire strikes it [the garden] and it is burned. Thus does Allah make clear to you His verses that you might give thought).

And old age befalls him and his offspring are weak, then a fiery whirlwind comes into the garden and the garden is burned. In this way, Allah makes the signs clear to you.

This has been mentioned before, and this is always mentioned in the events of Karbala, that Islam is a garden planted by the Prophet. It is the garden of Islam. And in it there are various things, just as there are in a garden. And... Yezid is a fiery whirlwind that came and turned it to ashes. `Fahtaraqat. Kadhalika yubayyinu llahu...` (so it was burned. Thus does Allah make clear...). This happens when `asabahu l-kibru` (old age befalls him), meaning its gardener, who is the guardian, when he becomes old, then his offspring are made weak. And after that, it is mentioned that the garden was burned and turned to ashes. This, in the events of Karbala, this comparison is often read.

This matter was completed yesterday. It's finished.

`Ya ayyuha-lladhina amanu anfiqu min tayyibati ma kasabtum wa-mimma akhrajna lakum mina l-'ard` (O you who have believed, spend from the good things which you have earned and from that which We have produced for you from the earth).

Meaning, O followers of the wasi, you... seekers... those esoteric sciences, pure esoteric things... Its translation... Leave the translation... they have left it blank... The translation has been left out, it's blank. Because "meaning" is the actual `ta'wil` (esoteric interpretation).

`Ya ayyuha-lladhina amanu anfiqu min tayyibati...` (O you who have believed, spend from the good things...). O people, whatever sustenance you receive, take some out from it so that... which is a thing that grows from the earth, so that you may give it. But what is its meaning? They start with "meaning." Meaning...

O followers of the wasi, you must teach the seekers those esoteric sciences, the pure esoteric things, that you have derived from exoteric knowledge. And also benefit [others] with what We have given you from the knowledge of the wasi.

Meaning, where there is a matter of `ta'wil`, `ta'wil` is given. And where there is a matter of translation, the translation is told. It should be both exoteric and esoteric. The esoteric sciences emerged from Sayyidna 'Ali, `salawatullah 'alayh`. And explain it. To whom? To your `mustafidin` (seekers). ...esoteric sciences... read it. And whatever We have given in exoteric knowledge, meaning the knowledge of the Prophet, the knowledge of `tanzil` (revelation). A continuous point is being made: `tanzil` is the Prophet's part, and the knowledge of `ta'wil` belongs to Sayyidna Wasi. And from the knowledge of the `wasi`, whatever We have given you... Read it. And from the knowledge of the `wasi`... And... And from the knowledge of the `wasi`, whatever We have given you, also provide benefit with it. Yes.

`wa-la tayammamu l-khabitha minhu tunfiquna wa-lastum bi-akhidhihi illa an tughmidu fih. Wa'lamu anna llaha ghaniyyun hamid` (And do not aim toward the defective therefrom, spending [from it] while you would not take it [ yourselves] except with closed eyes. And know that Allah is Free of need and Praiseworthy).

And do not even touch an impure thing to spend in the way of Allah. You must not touch an impure thing. Meaning, look, `tunfiquna` comes for `zakat`. Money that is `haram` (forbidden) should not go into `zakat`. You have been hearing this for two or three lessons, how Sayyidna Isma'il has explained the reasoning of `zakat`. And various things have been explained. That the `zakat` which is one rupee that you take out from forty, those thirty-nine become pure for you. And if that one rupee is not taken out, then those forty become spoiled. And Sayyidna Isma'il says that where there is theft or, you can say, loss, whether on land or at sea, all of it happens because of not paying `zakat` properly. Remember this.

...in a state where you yourselves would not take it... When you yourselves don't take it, then how can you give that same money to elders? When you yourselves... to give it... you hesitate. Don't even touch it. In a state where you yourself are not willing to take it, then how do you give it to others? For this...

...except that you overlook it. And know that Allah is free of need, Praiseworthy.

Meaning, that knowledge which is based on doubt, do not teach it. Especially when you yourself do not accept it or believe in it. Then why teach it to others? ...except that you cursorily study it. In it... So the knowledge that is wrong... knowledge is of two types. For example, knowledge is an example of water. So water is sweet and it is also brackish. The knowledge of the river has salt mixed in it, so it is brackish. So what is in this world, brackish knowledge is more, and pure knowledge, or you could say, sweet knowledge, is less. Which is told on behalf of the `Awliya Allah`. So don't even touch that either. And don't... do that. The thing which is based on doubt, do not teach it. When you teach it... Today, you see on TV, `hadith-e-sahih` (authentic traditions), `hadith-e-gharib` (unfamiliar traditions), all are being narrated daily. And whether the `hadith` is authentic or not, it is not known. But they give arguments from it. So there are several types of `hadith`. One is `hadith-e-sahih`, one is `gharib`, one is `mashhur` (famous), one is `qudsi`, and one is `mawdu`' (fabricated). `Mawdu`' means fabricated, meaning which has been created. And they are full of such `hadith`. The `sittah` which is... the `sihah sittah` (six authentic collections)... six hundred thousand `hadith` have been fabricated. Now they are taking them out from it. They are refining it, as to which is authentic, which is `gharib`, and which is this.

...especially when you yourself do not accept it or hold that belief. Then why teach it to others? Except that you cursorily study it. Do not ponder over it, nor consider it worthy of attention. And know that the wasi is free of need from the deniers and is praised by the obedient.

`Ash-shaytanu ya'idukumu l-faqra wa-ya'murukum bil-fahsha'. Wallahu ya'idukum maghfiratan minhu wa-fadla. Wallahu wasi'un 'alim` (Shaytan threatens you with poverty and orders you to immorality. But Allah promises you forgiveness from Him and bounty. And Allah is all-Encompassing and Knowing).

Shaytan threatens you with poverty and commands evil deeds. And Allah promises to forgive you on His behalf and to give you more. And Allah is vast, All-Knowing. Meaning, the Second Opponent frightens you that, remember, if you follow 'Ali, you will be deprived of the gnosis of the religion, as if it were in his possession and property. And then he says, "Come to our side, we are the `Khalifat al-Muslimin` (Caliphs of the Muslims)." ...have been made. Follow us, which is entirely an evil deed.

So look, the Second Opponent. You all know who the Second Opponent is. And he is the one who brings the thought that "We are the `Khalifat al-Muslimin`, come this way. Don't go towards 'Ali." Now look, what this wrong thing is for: he frightens with poverty. What is it? Shaytan... you... Shaytan. You understand Shaytan to be Harith bin Murrah, who was the Shaytan in the time of Adam. So he is the total Shaytan, of the entire era of `sitr` (concealment). And his disciples have existed in every era. In every era, those who teach evil deeds are the Shaytan... his disciples. So in every era, after him there is Qabil, there is Namrud, there is Fir'awn (Pharaoh), there is Haman, there is Shaddad, and there are many such people who are all... teaching... who are... calling towards the wrong path. Now see, the one who only frightens with poverty. "Man, what is this? I pray from morning to evening and my condition is not good. And those who do pray, look at their condition, how Allah blesses them." So in one era, it has come in a book that Sayyidna Sulayman Saheb... his grandfather, Sayyidna Yusuf bin Sulayman. In his time, where he used to lead prayers in Sidhpur, there a person was very poor and was very punctual in his prayers. And he was always regular in his prayers. A time also came when he was overcome by greed. "Man, what is this, so many people come to the mosque, they are much better than me, and I am so punctual in my prayers. I remain a poor man." Some thing should come. Now Shaytan possessed him. Which Shaytan? The Second Opponent. He said, "Man, this is not right." Now it came to be known that in a few days, his condition began to change. What changed? That he would come to the mosque and sell `miswak` (tooth-sticks). Miswak. In that era, whatever the currency was, `rupiya` or `anna-pai`, he would sell them. And he would give it to the person next to him... "I have `miswak`, it has come from the Imam al-Zaman (Imam of the Time)." And from Imam al-Zaman! They would immediately take it. The person next to him took it, the third one took it, the fourth one took it. And five rupees, two rupees, whatever it was... Daily, his condition started improving. As it improved, his clothes changed, his place changed, his house changed, all things changed. And he became very... quite... wealthy. A time came when a person... in that era, for travel... they used to walk from one village to another. A gentleman was crossing through the jungle. He saw that the same gentleman had also arrived there at the time of `maghrib` (evening prayer). And from the front, a woodcutter is cutting `miswak` and bringing it. He is bringing a bundle. And this person, by giving five or ten rupees, bought the entire bundle. Bought the bundle. And brought it... and sold it. He came and informed Sayyidna Yusuf. "My lord, this is what's happening." When Sayyidna Yusuf found out... "Alright, is that so?" He called him. He called him and said, "Brother, it seems your connection with the Imam has been established. We are `da'is` (missionaries), we have no such connection." Although Sayyidna Yusuf did have a connection. In your time, Mahmud... came, in the recent era. Anyway, so he said, "Brother..." He asked, "This is a strange thing, that you have reached... you are a `da'i`, you are this, of the Imam al-Zaman, but you have the grace of Allah, that from the Imam al-Zaman, `miswak` comes to you." `Miswak` is a special thing, and people like it. One after another... He said, "You... this is a great thing for you." He said, "No, there is no such thing, sir." "No, if there is, then tell me, brother. We will also benefit." "We don't know that such things can come from the Imam." When he was compelled more, or he was asked with some stratagem, at that time he said, "Yes, sir." As soon as he confessed, he [Sayyidna Yusuf] was standing, and he kicked him in the chest. And he went and fell far away. At that time, he got angry. "O deceiver, you practice deceit? You deceive the `mu'minin` (believers)?" At that time, he confessed, "Yes, I had a way, I used to do this, and I... out of greed... did this." So he started doing all this. So, after that, he gave the order, "Whosever money you have taken, return it to all of them." Now his condition changed, it kept changing. Whatever he had taken from people, he returned it all, and he came back to the same state of poverty. So this state of poverty, Shaytan frightens with it. And what does he do? He directs attention towards evil deeds. And Allah promises you forgiveness from Himself and to give more. And Allah is vast... Meaning, giving is in Allah's hands. Sustenance is not in anyone's hands. Sustenance is only in Allah's hands. We think that we are working in a bank, we are farming, we are doing this, we are doing that, we are getting money from there. You are not getting anything from there. The Giver is sitting above. So there are four things that are exclusively for Allah, for no one else. And what are those four things? `Al-Mulk Lillah` (Sovereignty belongs to Allah). The whole world, the whole earth, is Allah's earth. It is not anyone's earth. "This is my field, this is my house, this is my so-and-so." It belongs to no one. Everyone is going to go into two yards of land. Nothing belongs to anyone. Everything belongs to Allah Ta'ala. So, `al-mulku lillah`. And from the mouth of Sayyidna al-Qa'im, `salawatullah 'alayh`, this will emerge, `Liman al-mulk?` (To whom belongs the sovereignty?). `Al-mulku lillahi l-wahidi l-qahhar` (Sovereignty belongs to Allah, the One, the Prevailing). Sovereignty is for the One, the Prevailing, it is for Allah Ta'ala. This is the first thing, sovereignty. The second thing is `Al-Rizq 'ala Allah` (Sustenance is upon Allah). Sustenance is upon Allah. It is on Allah. How much to give to whom, wherever it reaches, his sustenance reaches him. So sustenance is Allah's responsibility. Every... rich and poor, and... poor, sick, whoever gets two grains, he is alive with that. So `al-rizqu 'ala Allah`. What is the third thing? `Al-rizqu 'ala Allah`, `al-mulku lillah`... and the third thing is... `Al-mulku lillah`... `Al-Amru Lillah` (The Command belongs to Allah). The command... The quality of giving commands, except for Allah, belongs to no one. We think that he is giving the command, so we have to obey, he is giving the command, he is an elder, so-and-so. Who gives the command to the elders? The One above gives. It goes up to the Imam, and from the Imam, it goes further up. So `al-rizqu 'ala Allah`, `al-mulk` is for Allah Ta'ala, and `al-amru lillahi ta'ala`. And what is the fourth thing? The fourth thing... `Al-'Ibadah` (Worship). The `ibadah`. Worship, `sajdah` (prostration). `Al-'ibadatu lillahi faqat` (Worship is for Allah alone). Worship is only for Allah Ta'ala. It is not for anyone. We think that we know the `mansus` (designated successor) very well, I know more than you, I pray a lot of... you should keep the `mansus` in your mind. But at the time of prayer, when the intention is made, it is only for Allah Ta'ala. `Lillahi faqat` (For Allah alone). That Allah who is the creator of the spiritual realm, we pray for Him, who is not visible, neither do thoughts reach Him, nor do our eyes reach Him. Nothing reaches Him, it is for Him we pray. So `al-'ibadatu lillahi ta'ala`.

And the Wasi, `alayhi al-salam`, gives you the promise, "Come, submit to me. Your sins will also be forgiven, and your ranks will also be elevated." The Wasi is the possessor of vast knowledge. He encompasses all ranks and is aware of all sciences.

`Yu'ti l-hikmata man yasha'. Wa-man yu'ta l-hikmata fa-qad utiya khayran kathira. Wa-ma yadhdhakkaru illa ulu l-albab` (He gives wisdom to whom He wills, and whoever has been given wisdom has certainly been given much good. And none will remember except those of understanding).

Allah grants wisdom to whom He wills. And he who is given wisdom has been given great wealth. No one understands it except people of intellect. Meaning, the Wasi teaches esoteric knowledge to whom he wants. And whoever receives esoteric knowledge from the Wasi, in reality, has received a very great wealth. These matters and symbols, no one understands them except the possessors of esoteric knowledge. Because esoteric knowledge is the essence and summary of exoteric knowledge.

It is he who has the appreciation for it. Those who have an appreciation for esoteric knowledge, they will understand. He who knows the value of sweet water will not go near salty water. Even though salty water is much more abundant in the world and... Look, an example from years ago, it has been 40 years... When I used to teach in Kuwait. So at that time, in conversation, I said that at night when I go, I have a book of `haqa'iq` (realities), a book of `ta'wil`, I read a little and go to sleep. So the questioner asked, it's been years, "Why do you do this?" I said, "It's a habit of mine that I fall asleep with it..." and it's... If you read a book of philosophy or some literary piece, you will fall asleep immediately. If you read an interesting book, you will keep reading it all night. The thing you don't understand... So the sciences of `haqa'iq` are not easy, they are a hard nut to crack. As much as I read... I keep reading... so after that... whatever my habit was, I told him. He said, "What is the purpose of this, sir?" I said, "Look, it's like this: in the world, from morning to evening, the media is working, you are reading newspapers, watching TV, meeting people, meeting good people, meeting bad people, listening to everyone's talk. Various things are happening." And so... But, now look, the exercise for the body... the body is separate and the soul is separate. The nourishment for the soul and the nourishment for the body are different. For the body, to be healthy, the exercise that is done, in it cycling is mentioned, so-and-so is... In that era, I gave the example, I was 40 years old then. That, "You do these things, but the best exercise is considered to be swimming, that `tayrna` (swimming) is the best, because the whole... all your limbs work." So I said, when you go to the sea, to the ocean, and swim, you swim for as much as you want, you swim for two hours. But when your father or elder says, "Come out, it's been a long time, two hours have passed." You say, "Alright, I'm coming." It takes time to come out, but as soon as you come out, you first take a shower. You will bathe with fresh water, and then you will come out. "Why is this? You were in the water for two hours." "You were in the water for two hours." So I said, "This... the body is getting sticky. The pores are... getting..." I said, "I take a shower and in five minutes, it's done." What it means is that our whole day, whatever we hear, our minds get polluted. Some things... at night, when we read... the knowledge of the `din` (religion), which is correct knowledge, we should read it, so that our minds become clean. Then he understood.
