And as this was happening—one group going this way, one group going that way; those who see goodness and those who run after `amileen` (sorcerers)—while this was happening, suddenly `satr` comes. And the birth of Janab-e-Adam 'alayhis-salam happens. The `dawr-i satr`, meaning as soon as `maghrib` time ended, the night came. And the time of night is called `satr`. So `kashf` is the time of day. So `kashf` and `satr` are just like we see night and day. Night is `satr`, day is `kashf`. And in between, there is a twilight (`jhutputa`). So now it's time for `maghrib`. "Let's go, it's getting dark, it's getting dark." That is the `dawr-i fatrat`. This, night and day, just as you cannot change it... this is a law (`nizam`) of Allah. `Lan tajida li-sunnatillahi tabdila` (You will never find in the way of Allah any change). It is the `sunnah` (way) of Allah which will never be changed. And it will continue to run. So the `sunnah` is Allah's `sunnah`. It is not the Prophet's or anyone else's, that it should be changed. Rather, this is the `sunnah` of Allah. `Wa lan tajida li-sunnatillahi tahwila` (And you will never find in the way of Allah any alteration). And this is Allah's `sunnah` in which there can be no alteration. So it's not this either, but with night and day, just as we cannot change it, so too we cannot change `kashf` and `satr`. After `kashf`, `satr` must come. And after `satr`, `kashf` must come. It will keep running. How many eons and ages have passed, but it is the same. And then the days change, moments change into days, days change into years, centuries pass. After centuries, a `dawr` comes. Several `dawr`s make up a `qawr`. Several `qawr`s make up a `mawr`. So this world is very old, it is continuing, and in it the periods of `dawr` and `qawr`, the durations that have been told by the `awliya Allah`, will continue to run.

So the mistake that happened from us, you forgive that. Meaning, they implore their Lord, the Wasi 'alayhis-salam, that in inviting towards you, the shortcoming (`kotahi`) that occurred from us, and in explaining your station, the mistake (`bhool`) that occurred, and the inattention (`be-tawajjohi`) that was shown, do not seize us for that. O Allah, do not hold us accountable for the mistake we have made. Rather, you show your mercy and... By whom is this happening? In the general Qur'an Sharif, it is from Allah, but the `ta'wil` is what? Janab-e-Ali, salawatullah 'alayh. Now, for the sake of Ali, why? This Sayyidna Husayn [bin 'Ali] has written, that wherever the word "Allah" appears, if you see the first `para` (part), what is the explanation of `Alhamdulillahi Rabbil 'Alamin`? What is the explanation of `Bismillah`? What is `Ar-Rahman Ar-Rahim` called? All of this... I have taught this lesson, but I am saying that there are different explanations. Now, from this perspective, it is seen that this Surah al-Hamd is very special, because in it, all things have been told, from whom the matter has come, from where it has emerged. Why? Because you recite Yasin Sharif daily, you recite it every week, you recite it on Fridays. And what is in it? `Yasin`. Yasin is one of the names of the Prophet. Just as I said, the collections of 9,000 years are Janab-e-Prophet. And that is why what happened? The Surah Taha was revealed. The `Ta` of Taha is the ninth degree. It has nine letters. That is why the Prophet is the possessor of 9,000 years of collections. And you had completed nine ranks. But after that, a person does not sit in silence, but keeps striving. When the Prophet reached the tenth station, at that time the chapter of Yasin Sharif was revealed. The `Ya` of Yasin indicates that he reached the tenth degree. So in this way, there is a difference between the two. And Maulana Ali, salawatullah 'alayh, is the possessor of 10,000 years of collections. 10,000 years. And which ones? In their `istiqrari` (established) forms. The forms, the collections, which are not in the Prophet's share, but in... But we cannot lower the rank of the Prophet. If you make them equal, even by a hair's breadth, then you deviate from monotheism (`tawhid`). So one has to be very careful in explaining this, what the rank of the Prophet is. If the Prophet's rank was not clear, Ali would not have been `mamdud` (extended). So here in this world, Ali came in the form of `hijabat` (veils), and that too, your `ayn-i 'azima` (great essence) is `muhtajib` (veiled). His final `hijab` came. The lowest (`adna`) `hijab` came. And the Prophet's was the middle (`darmiyani`) `hijab`. If the middle `hijab` had not come and the final `hijab` had come, then Ali would never have been `mamdud`. It has been explained. [unclear] You have heard it from Baba Hazrat. That the final `hijab` in which... the `hijab` of Janab-e-Ali came. This is a track, a path, that Allah Ta'ala does this within `satr`. Wasi. Everywhere it is wasi, wasi. You see, the era of Musa, Harun's name does not come up as often. Yusha's doesn't. Habil's doesn't. When Adam is mentioned, Adam, Nuh, Ibrahim, Musa, 'Isa. What is the status of these people? Why are their names famous in the world? The era of Ibrahim, the era of Musa, the era of 'Isa. But the `mustaqarr` (permanent) Imam of their time, that Imam is very high. He is above them. By his command, these people were made. Who made Nuh 'alayhis-salam? Who made Nuh 'alayhis-salam? Janab-e-Hud. Hud was the Imam of that time. And Adam 'alayhis-salam was made by Janab-e-Hunayn. And the Imam of Ibrahim 'alayhis-salam's time was Maulana Salih. Maulana Salih. And for Janab-e-Musa, it is Janab-e-'Ud. `Alif`, `dal`. And for Janab-e-'Isa, it is Maulana Khuzaymah. These five who passed, these five `nutuqa` (Speaker-Prophets) who are very high... they are very high. These five whose names we take, Adam, Nuh, Ibrahim, Musa, 'Isa, how many are they, including the Prophet? Six. These six are `nutuqa`. Not `Ulu 'l-'Azm` (Possessors of Firm Resolve) prophets. `Ulu 'l-'Azm` prophets start from Nuh. So Adam was removed from the `Ulu 'l-'Azm` prophets. It is said about them in the `du'as` you write in books, that they did not have `Ulu 'l-'Azm`. It started from Nuh. So Nuh is the first among the `Ulu 'l-'Azm` prophets. And after that, of a higher rank than them is Janab-e-Ibrahim. Then Musa, then 'Isa, then Janab-e-Prophet. These five, the prayer we are offering, the five daily prayers we are offering, are incumbent upon these five. There are many subtleties, but remember for now that the five `nutuqa` or the five `Ulu 'l-'Azm` prophets, our prayers are incumbent upon them. Now, in this, the special point is that the prayer is `salatan mawquta` (a prayer at a prescribed time). The prayer is a prayer to be offered at its time. If you start praying the `zohr` prayer at 10:30, and people are watching, what is he praying? There is no prayer at 10:30. And if you pray without its time, then it has no significance. So the significance of time is great. The significance of time is there. So the times of prayer, just as we are careful about the time, that `zohr` has happened or not, or the sun has set or not, as we are careful, the times of prayer are greater than the prayer itself. Why are they greater? I have said this many times. The times of prayer are greater than the prayer because the prayer is from the side of the servant, and the times are sent by Allah. From above, the openings that open, the windows that open in the heavens, from there blessings and mercy descend. So that is from Allah's side, so the requirement of its time is greater. And incumbent upon the time are their followers (`motabe'een`), who are the concealed Imam, who is the Prophet. Nuh 'alayhis-salam is a prophet. So Janab-e-Hud sent the Prophet... sent Nuh. Wherever you see, the command came, "O Nuh, build an ark." From whose side did it come? From the side of your `muhtajib` (veiled one), the Imam of that time. And the Imam, who was he? The seventh Imam. And a very high Imam. So Janab-e-Hud, from his side there were signs. Then in Janab-e-Ibrahim's time, the matter that happened, Salih was your father, and it was a different matter there, in Janab-e-Ibrahim's case. Ibrahim is in the lineage of the prophets' forefathers, and he is the son of Janab-e-Salih. That is why Janab-e-Ibrahim's rank is what? It is not just that he was a prophet, or a messenger, or a `natiq`, or an `Ulu 'l-'Azm` prophet. He was a prophet, he became a messenger, after messenger he became a `natiq`, after `natiq` an `Ulu 'l-'Azm` prophet, and after that he attained the rank of `khullat` (friendship). `Ibrahim khalilullah` (Ibrahim, the friend of Allah). And `Ibrahim alladhi waffa` (And Ibrahim who fulfilled). Ibrahim is the one who completely fulfilled his loyalty. And after that, what happened? He attained such a rank that you, it's as if from a narrow-gauge, you went to a broad-gauge. So what does that mean? That you, from the rank of prophethood (`nubuwwah`), moved to the rank of Imamate (`imamah`). `inna ja'iluka linnasi imama` (Indeed, I will make you an Imam for the people). We have made Ibrahim an Imam. So Janab-e-Ibrahim became an Imam, and after that, he kept progressing, the ranks of Imamate, in which there are the higher ranks, after Imamate there is `imamat-i ruhani`, `nafs-i ilahi`, and after that he progresses. So which rank did you attain? This is what needs to be recognized. The `hudud` (ranks), the `hadd-i ali` and `hadd-i adna`, whoever they may be, recognizing their station is our `tawhid` (monotheism). That is why what do we do? We say, `Allahumma thabbitna 'ala ta'atillah wa ta'at-i rasulihi wa ta'at-i imam-uz-zamanih wa hudud-id-dinih` (O Allah, keep us firm in the obedience of Allah, and the obedience of His Messenger, and the obedience of the Imam of the time, and the `hudud` of the *din*). O Allah, keep us steadfast in what? In the obedience of Allah, in the obedience of the Messenger, in the obedience of the Imam of the time. This is all completely equal. But in the `hudud` of the *din*, there is a problem. There, we do not fully obey. We leave some `hadd`, we elevate some `hadd`, we lower some. This `ghulu` (excess) and `qulu` (deficiency), I mentioned yesterday too, that `ghulu` and `qulu` are both wrong. So what is here? "Do not seize us." A request is being made to Janab-e-Wasi. We are asking Allah. Look, you show your mercy, a shortcoming has occurred from us, we are servants, we are human, and we are statues of forgetfulness. You forgive us, only you can forgive. "Do not seize us." O our Lord... now what does it mean? O our Lord, in the `da'wat`, the sin we have committed from deficiency, do not place its burden upon us. Do not place the burden of this sin upon us. Do not place it upon us as it was placed on those before us. Because with Amir al-Mu'minin, it is... Recite it. ...that collection of subtleties (`lata'if`) of the predecessors (`sabiq`). ...the collection. who had guided the rebellious ones. And they gathered in your presence and became one with you. Now, with Amir al-Mu'minin, such a matter began, that with Amir al-Mu'minin, which collections gathered? From here, three came, from there three came, from there three came. There are very special matters, which collections gathered with you. You became `istiqrari` (established), not `istida'i` (initial). And that is why the perfections (`kamalat`) manifested, the miracles (`mo'jizat`) also manifested, which were... such miracles that had never been seen before, those were... to change the form (`hayyat`) of a human being... the form of a human being, an ordinary person cannot change it. But Maulana Amir al-Mu'minin did it. His grace (`karam`) was such that he changed the form of a human. One of them, you were sitting and he was passing by on the road, and two men were arguing. I have told this before. Two men were arguing. And one was saying, "I am right," and the other, "I am right." You were asked, and you said that this one is right, and this one is wrong. As soon as someone was called wrong, he started to get flared up, as it happens today in our disputes. "No, I am right, I am right." You are giving the wrong judgment. He was saying this to Amir al-Mu'minin, "You are giving the wrong judgment." He was with Amir al-Mu'minin. So at that time, you said, "Whatever I am doing, I am doing it with the gaze of Allah, and it is correct." He did not agree. And he started speaking with some intensity. So at that time, with you were 'Ammar Yasir and many other people, a group, who were walking behind you. So you said, "O man, what I am saying is correct." He did not agree, and the dispute grew, it increased. He was arguing with Amir al-mu'minin. So at that time, you said that, "O Allah, turn this person into the form of a dog." "Turn him into the form of a dog." And the people who were watching, who were all walking along, they saw that his form changed, and he became a black dog. When he became that, the other friend who was with him, who were arguing with each other, he became worried. "What has happened? He was my friend, we had a dispute..." And he immediately fell at your feet, saying, "You have mercy on him, do this, do that." Everyone saw your miracle. And after that, you said that, "O Allah, Lord, I take the intercession of Adam 'alayhis-salam, I take that of Nuh 'alayhis-salam, Ibrahim, Musa, 'Isa, all the `nutuqa`, I take their intercession, that you return him to his original form." That is, the form he had before, return him to that. Then he returned to his noble human form. This happening, changing into the form of a dog, and then returning to the noble human form, is not an easy task. So that happened. As he turned from a dog back into a human, and as soon as he returned, he fell at your feet, saying, "A mistake was made by me. You are giving the correct judgment." When they saw this, all the `hawari` (disciples) who were there, among them was 'Ammar Yasir. 'Ammar Yasir is one who comes in our `mamsulat`, for `zohr`. So 'Ammar Yasir said, "O Maula, this is your grace, what a strange thing it is that you take a person and his form... from a human form, you change it into the form of a dog, an animal, and you see that there, Mu'awiyah, what is he doing with you?" Mu'awiyah is showing such force, and what-what is he doing? So everyone who was listening was listening. That Mu'awiyah, where is he? He is sitting in Sham (Syria). And you are in Kufa. So at that time, you said, "O 'Ammar, do you want to see my power, do you want to see my strength?" Just then, you said, "O..." he took his mother's name. "Son of these, come here. Come here." And at that time, it is said that a piece of cloud came, and Mu'awiyah, from up there, fell down with a thud. And he came and stood in front. And after that, you said that he, the Prophet's... did he obey the command, or did he not? He told me to become the successor. You all... the extent to which he had to speak, he kept saying all of it, that it was like this, like that, he denied this, he denied that. And he kept listening in silence. When the people saw that Mu'awiyah had been summoned from Sham to Kufa. And he fell in front of them. And silent, no answer. After that, you said that, "O Allah, I want this one to... his place of abode... which was his previous place, send him there." He went straight from there to Sham, where the court was. He had been snatched from the court. And then he sat back in the court. Now, when he came to the court, a gap of 5-10 minutes had occurred. So people were worried, "Where had he gone?" He had suddenly disappeared. So at that time, what came from Mu'awiyah's mouth was, "People, be quiet. 'Ali had summoned me." Like that, the special people who were there, he told them. That this matter should not go out of this room. That 'Ali did this, this. So miracles of this kind, 'Ali's... 'Ali can do them, no one else can. So here too it is the same, that wherever the word "Allah" has come, there this is. We recite Yasin. `Yasin`. Yasin is a title. We recite Yasin Sharif daily. After `Yasin`, it is `wal-Qur'an-il-Hakim` (By the Wise Qur'an). Brother, Yasin is a part of the Qur'an. It is a surah. But we recite Yasin, then we recite with a `waw`. And the Wise Qur'an. What does that mean? Yasin means Janab-e-Prophet, and the Wise Qur'an is Maulana Ali, salawatullah 'alayhi'z-zat. You are the `Qur'an-i Natiq` (Speaking Qur'an). And the rank of `Qur'an-i Natiq` is very high. The `Qur'an-i Samit` (Silent Qur'an) is in our hands. And we think that this is the source of our guidance. But what is the reality behind it, the inner meaning (`batin`)? It is the `Qur'an-i Natiq`. This does not speak... this is `samit`. It is not a speaking Qur'an. We derive its meanings. As we read the translation, we do this. But who is the real speaker? The `Qur'an-i Natiq` is Maulana Ali's person. He himself says. You see the sayings (`irshadat`) of the Prophet, "I am this, and 'Ali is this." "I am the warner, and he is the one who gives glad tidings." "I am like this, and he is like that." "I am the `Bi'r-i Mu'attalah` (unused well), and he is the `Qasr-i Mashid` (lofty palace)." Many examples are given by Janab-e-Prophet. But here what is it? You said that the `Qur'an-i Natiq`... what is the matter? So that... Allah Ta'ala has already clarified it in the first verse. How? `Alif Lam Mim. Dhalikal-kitabu la rayba fih` (Alif, Lam, Mim. That is the Book, wherein there is no doubt). `Alif Lam Mim`. If you ask a Maulvi about `Alif Lam Mim`, what is it? They will say these are `muqatta'at` (disjointed letters), only God knows. We don't know what `Alif` means, what `Lam` means. We have books on it, what they mean. But after `Alif Lam Mim`, it is `Dhalikal-kitabu la rayba fih`. That book in which there is no doubt. Now, we are reading this, we are Muslims, we are believers, and every Muslim also knows and believes this. So, this is in our hands and we have it. Then why is Allah Ta'ala saying `dhalikal-kitab la rayba fih`, there should be no doubt in it? That book. This is not the book. `Hadhal-kitabu la rayba fih` is not there. `Dhalikal-kitab`. How is this? Those who know, they know the difference between `hadha` and `dhalika`. The difference between "this" and "that". For "this", `hadha` comes, and for "that", `dhalika` comes. So here, Allah Ta'ala... there can be no mistake from Allah Ta'ala. In `wahi`, there is no mistake. It is in our understanding that there is a mistake. So what is it? The difference between `hadha` and `dhalika` is that `dhalika` came for the `Qur'an-i Natiq`. And its example is that Janab-e-Wasi himself was sitting, when he had become Amir al-Mu'minin. And the Qur'an Sharif was placed there. So you wanted to make it clear that the `Qur'an-i Natiq` is my person. In what way? That you said, `hadhal-Qur'an...` `nuzila minallah` (This Qur'an... was revealed from Allah). It was revealed from Allah. They said, "We affirm it." We affirm that it is revealed from Allah. This is. So you said that... you took the Qur'an Sharif and placed it on your head and said, `unthukiya kitab` (O Book, speak). "O Book, speak, talk. Speak out." Talk. Now this Qur'an Sharif, if 'Ali had said it and wanted it, it would have started speaking. But it was not 'Ali's will. It is `samit` (silent). This Qur'an is `samit`. So you said... so people started asking, "How will this talk, O Amir al-Mu'minin? This is just pages of the Qur'an." So you said, "Yes..." You placed it on your head and said, `hadha Qur'anun samit wa ana kitabullah-in-natiq` (This is a silent Qur'an, and I am the speaking book of Allah). I am the speaking book of Allah. Now you consider this. I am the `Qur'an-i Natiq`. I am the Qur'an, but `natiq`, the speaking one. Now look, the Qur'an Majid has been here for 1400 years, it is in everyone's hands. It has come and it is continuing, in the hands of the people. But Janab-e-Amir al-Mu'minin came and went. 1400 years have passed. So is it this or is it that? Will you say this 'Ali or that 'Ali? That one was far. It refers to something far. That 'Ali who was in the time of the Prophet, `dhalika` comes for him. So it means that no one is doubting this. The one they are doubting is the `mutahayyirun` (the bewildered), meaning about the `wasi` of Allah, they have doubts. They have doubts about him. It is in him: `dhalikal-kitab`. Not `hadhal-kitab`, `dhalikal-kitab`. So there are matters like this, that to 'Ali's... just as we have read before, "Do not fail to make 'Ali's station clear." Always keep making it clear. This is... the love of 'Ali, if it is not in the heart, then there is nothing. Nothing at all. Neither the prayer is correct, nor the fasting is correct, nor anything. Nothing is correct. You see, `aqimus-salata wa atuz-zakah` (establish the prayer and give the zakat). What is the esoteric meaning of prayer and what is the esoteric meaning of zakat? If you don't understand this or that, and you are just praying. But `aqimus-salata wa atuz-zakah`. You establish the `da'wat`. This `da'wat`, the shari'ah of Muhammad, salawatullah 'alayh, is a constitution for life (`dastur-i hayat`), a beacon of guidance (`manjur-i hidayat`), which has been sent from Allah's side. If you don't accept it, it's over. So this beacon of guidance is in our hands, every one has brought it, a brochure... and brings their plan of action. But the real thing is that to believe in the `wasi` of the Prophet is the sign of entering the circle of faith (`iman`). That is why the circle of `iman` began when the Prophet appointed his `wasi`. Before that too, there were... Salman Farsi and others all knew. But they were in a hidden state. Although he is a `sahabi` (companion), and the others are also `sahabi`. But those who had faith were believers, and those who were hypocrites were hypocrites. And I have already told you what the difference is between a `munafiq` (hypocrite), a `mushrik` (polytheist), and a `kafir` (disbeliever). All this has been going on for several days. So remember that if we are praying, we are praying `lillahi faqat` (only for Allah). Allah, who is `mujarrad` `subhan`, we pray for Him. But to make clear the stations (`maqamat`) of the Prophet and the `wasi`, the `awsiya Allah` (successors of Allah), and to be aware of them. That is, is Janab-e-Mu'id greater or is Maulana Tayyib greater? If you don't know, then you are ignorant (`be-bahra`). Become aware of this. What is Maulana Mu'id's rank, and what is Janab-e-Maulana Tayyib's rank? What is Maulana Muhammad bin Isma'il's rank? Maulana Muhammad bin Isma'il, who is the seventh among the `A'immah-i At-har` (Pure Imams), his rank is the highest. Although he was the possessor of only one `hujjat`. So all these things are the ways of the *din*, the ways they run. If you don't understand this, and don't brush up on it, then you will be left behind. That the *din*... just the rulings... you prayed, you fasted, and you broke your fast at the right time, you ate `sahri` at the right time. This is not it. Why is `sahri` eaten at that time? Why is the fast broken? What does breaking it mean? What is the meaning of `Eid al-Fitr`? Why is it that after 30 fasts, suddenly in the morning, `iftar` is done? All these things have esoteric interpretations (`ta'wilat`) behind them. And `ta'wilat` is a bridge that leads to the realities (`haqa'iq`). Until we master the `ta'wilat`, we are not capable of understanding the `haqa'iq`. Alhamdulillah Rabbil 'Alamin (Praise be to Allah, the Lord of the Worlds). [Du'a in Arabic]

Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim. The interpretation of Surah Al-Imran, its ninety-nine secrets, and the explanation of some high mysteries. Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim. Surah Al-Imran, it is said that it is after al-Baqarah. It is the Surah. Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim. Alif Lam Mim. In the beginning, in the first part, the shara'... Alif Lam Mim is what went in the beginning, in Surah al-Baqarah. It is a Surah of that type, and after that, those who have read the panj... are seeing it, that after Surah Fatiha, it begins with Alif Lam Mim. So, the way the Qur'an-e-Majid began, its interpretation has already been given. The meaning of Alif Lam Mim has already been told. Bismillah. Allahu la ilaha illa hu al-hayy al-qayyum (Allah - there is no deity except Him, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of [all] existence). Meaning, besides sabiq ta'ala (the first exalted one), in all the worlds, there is no ilah (god) or ma'bud (worshipped one). He alone is the markaz (center)... markaz-e-hayat (center of life) and is the one who sustains everyone. Look, here the thing to understand is, what is an ilah called, and what is Allah called? An ilah is something that is made by one's own hand. That is, within creation. Now, those who practice idol-worshipping or other things, they are all man-made gods. There was a time when humans, when civilization had not yet arrived, before Maulana Ibrahim salawatullah 'alayh or after him, at that time, a human would worship whatever he feared. Whether it was the sun, the moon, the stars, or snakes, scorpions, etc. - whatever he feared, that is what was worshipped. So, the meaning of worshipping is that they were afraid. So much so that in pre-Islam, before the coming of Islam, the environment that existed, it was also present there. Every single one... It has been said that Abu Jahl, Abu Lahab, etc., who was Abu Lahab? The Prophet's uncle. And Abu Jahl was the one who supported him. Both were shaytans (satans). Although, what was Abu Lahab? He was the son of Janab 'Abd al-Muttalib. But just as the uncle of Sayyid al-Salimain was bad, so too was the Prophet's uncle bad. His name was Abu Lahab. The Prophet says that every nabi (prophet) was given an opponent, meaning a shaytan. Every nabi has a shaytan. You know, who was it for Musa 'alayh al-salam? Fir'awn (Pharaoh). Who was it for Ibrahim? Namrud. In this way, in every era, there has been a shaytan. But the Prophet says that for me, there are two shaytans. So the higher the rank of the Prophet, the greater the waliyullah (friend of God) will be, the more formidable the shaytan will be. So now what is it? Here, from ilah, it means a man-made god. That we make it from matti (clay) and worship it, or any other creature. But Allah, for whom is He? He is the rabb al-'alamin (Lord of the worlds). Rabb al-'alamin is the creator of many worlds. The 'alam-e-ruhant (spiritual world), the 'alam-e-jismani (physical world), the 'alam-e-'uqul (world of intellects), the 'alam-e-khalq (world of creation), the 'alam-e-jinnat (world of jinn), the 'alam-e-hayat (world of life). That is why what has come in the Qur'an-e-Majid? Alhamdulillah rabb al-'alamin (Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds). That He is the creator of many 'awalim (worlds). So this is the muntaha-i-subhana (the ultimate glorious one). Now, what is it here? We have already studied about the muntaha before, that we can neither think about it, nor do thoughts go there, nor does our heart accept it, nor does our 'aql (intellect) go there. So now what is it? In all the worlds, there is no ilah, meaning ma'bud (worshipped one). Ilah. Because about whom are we talking? Meaning sabiq... sabiqa. Sabiq ta'ala is that first being who was the first to profess the tawhid (oneness) of rabb al-'alamin. Meaning, sabiq ta'ala is 'aql-e-awwal (the first intellect). So it is about them that even they are ilahs, meaning they are created, they are makhluq (creation). So there is no ilah except for rabb al-'alamin. He is the markaz-e-hayat (center of life). Meaning, now this is the praise of sabiq ta'ala, that he is the markaz-e-hayat. I have told you all before that all the ta'idat (supports) that exist, we think they are coming from the one above. Where does the one above get it from? From their senior. Where do they get it from? From an even greater senior. So much so that it reaches the Imam. The Imam receives it from above, from the 'awalim, from other places, and then, going on and on, the matter reaches sabiq ta'ala. Sabiq ta'ala means 'aql-e-awwal. He is everything. He is the maujud-e-awwal (the first existent), he is the sabiq-e-awwal (the first precedent), he is sabiq ta'ala, he is the wujud-e-awwal (the first existence). And he is 'aql-e-awwal. These are all their... The sifat (attributes) that exist, they can all be applied to him. Now, what was discussed before this? Four or six days ago? That the asma' al-husna (most beautiful names) which we read in the sahifa, like ya Qadir, ya Ghafur, ya Rahim (O Powerful, O Forgiving, O Merciful) - these are all attributes. They are attributes. The meaning of Qadir is one who possesses power. The meaning of Ghaffar is one who forgives. The meaning of Sattar is one who conceals faults. The meaning of Ra'uf is one who removes things, removes impurities, removes everything. Each one has a meaning. The meaning is a sifat (attribute). So Allah Ta'ala is pure of attributes. What do we call it? Munazza 'an al-sifat (transcendent above attributes). Remember this. Remember this word. Munazza 'an al-sifat. No attribute applies. Neither Qadir, nor Ghafur, nor Rahim. That is why what do we do? Whoever's name we give, we give 'Abd al-Ghaffar, we give 'Abd al-Qadir. There will be no name Qadir. This is all the name of Allah. So the meaning is that 'Abd al-Ghafur, 'Abd al-Ghaffar, 'Abd al-Sattar - all these names are special servants of Allah, they are mala'ika (angels), and in relation to them are the asma' al-husna. So the asma' al-husna that we hear, that Allah has ninety-nine names. But upon whom are those ninety-nine names? They are special mala'ika of his. But we do not recognize them, which mala'ika they are. Because the ninety-nine are in sets of thirty-three, three of them, just like our tasbih is formed. In which 'alam (world) are they? In the 'alam-e-'uqul, in the 'alam-e-hayat, in the 'alam-e-meherbani. We do not know this. So what do we do? We apply all these attributes to 'aql-e-awwal. Sifat. Apply that, and that is permissible for it. Because what is above it? It is the muntaha-i-subhana, about which we cannot think. La tudarrikuhu'l-qawatir (thoughts cannot grasp Him). Our hearts do not have خطور (khutur - passing thoughts). We cannot even think about it. The greatest of men, even 'aql-e-awwal is perplexed. And regarding 'aql-e-awwal, those below are perplexed. So every great person, the ones below him think, "How did such power come into him?" So every person looks up to the one above him. That is why it is said that every person has a had-e-'ali (high guide). And the had-e-'ali is everything. Through him, all things are distributed, are received. Nuzila 'alayka al-kitaba bi'l-haqqi musaddiqan lima bayna yadayhi (He has sent down to you the Book in truth, confirming what came before it). He revealed the kitab-e-barhaqq (the true book) upon you. Now, with whom is this address? Which confirms... With the nabi salawatullah 'alayh. Which confirms what came before. That is, the wasi (legatee) who is deserving of the daraja-e-wasa'it (rank of intermediaries), you have been commanded to establish him. He sent down the book upon you. The book was sent down. What? The book was sent down upon the Prophet. The entire Qur'an came. Now, the nur-e-Qur'an (light of the Qur'an) that came, that is, the Qur'an-e-Majid in our hands, in what form did it come? It came in the form of wahi (revelation). And in what way did it come? In the form of nur (light). Now, the common explanation is that, and what the history tells us is this: that the Prophet's chest was split open, from it the qalb (heart) was taken out, it was washed, and it was purified, and after that, Allah Ta'ala blew wahi into it, wahi was placed. This is the common explanation. But what is it really? It came to you in the form of nur. Which we cannot understand. The one who diluted it is the nabi salawatullah 'alayh. That he, in the form of a book, in the form of words, the words that are there are these, the meaning is with the Prophet. The words in which he expressed it, that became the Qur'an for us. So now what is it? That He sent down the book upon you. 'Alayk al-kitab bi'l-haqq (upon you the Book in truth). With truth. He sent down the true book upon you, which confirms what came before. What does it confirm from before? That book states that the Tawrat (Torah) was also correct. The Injil (Gospel) is also correct. The Bible is also correct. And the Suhuf-e-Ibrahim (Scrolls of Ibrahim) are also correct. The Zabur (Psalms) is also correct. Upon whom did the Zabur come? Upon Da'ud 'alayh al-salam. Da'ud 'alayh al-salam. Now what is it? That all these books were revealed from Allah. Then why do we give importance to the Qur'an, that the Qur'an Sharif is the greatest of all? Why is that? Because it has a special meaning. That there are various circles in the 'alam-e-azal (world of pre-eternity), that is, the 'alam-e-ruhani (spiritual world). From there, things come down in the form of nur and in the form of blessings. So in it, the Tawrat and the Injil... upon whom did the Injil come? Upon our 'Isa. The Tawrat came upon Musa. The Zabur came upon Da'ud. These and the Suhuf-e-Ibrahim are also there. All these things have emerged from the circle of 'aql-e-'ashir (the tenth intellect). Except for the Qur'an. The Qur'an-e-Majid has come from 'aql-e-awwal, which we are discussing, sabiq ta'ala. It has come from there. So, will the thing that has come from a higher place be greater or not? The meaning is that it is greater. So, the Prophet confirms it, so we also confirm it. But by 'book', I told you yesterday, what is the book? The Qur'an. The Qur'an Sharif. That is why, Ya Sin wa'l-Qur'an al-hakim (Ya Sin. By the wise Qur'an). When we read Ya Sin, the Qur'an is the book. It is the book that is revealed from Allah. And what is the real book? It is the wasi-e-paygambar (legatee of the prophet). It is 'Ali Murtada. And that is why what is it? It confirms. That is... now look, 'that is' the meaning. That is, the wasi who is deserving of the daraja-e-wasa'it, you have been commanded to establish him. He confirms with the shari'at of zahir (exoteric law), its batin (inner meaning), its ta'wil (interpretation), and its haqiqat (reality). Yes. The wasi-e-paygambar is the same as the Qur'an-e-Natiq (the Speaking Qur'an). I have told you this before. And this is the book. The meaning is that your Qur'an has been revealed, meaning 'Ali has been entrusted to you. And 'Ali is the one who will explain the batin (inner meaning) of the Qur'an-e-Majid. Nabi salawatullah 'alayh never explained it. Whatever verses there are, their explanation... you cannot show it anywhere. No book can show it, no question and answer can show that nabi salawatullah 'alayh only gave the explanation. What kind of explanation? In the hadith-e-mubarak (blessed tradition). All the hadith that have come, they are in the form of explanation. That's it. It came from the Prophet's mouth. And the beauty of the Prophet was this, rather it is a great miracle. It is that the Prophet himself narrated the hadith, and the Prophet himself narrated the Qur'an. But the Prophet was truthful and trustworthy. Therefore, when the Prophet said this is the Qur'an, it is the Qur'an. This is the hadith, it is the hadith. It came from one mouth. But the hadith is a different thing, and the Qur'an-e-Majid is a different thing. Meaning, the wasi who is deserving of the rank of wasa'it, you have been given the command to establish him. He confirms the zahir shari'at (exoteric law) with its batin ta'wil (esoteric interpretation) and haqiqat. This is the right of Janab 'Ali. And I am explaining further that Janab 'Ali has the right to give its ta'wil. Wa anzala al-Tawrata wa'l-Injil min qablu hudan li'l-nas wa anzala al-furqan (He sent down the Torah and the Gospel before this, as a guide to the people, and He sent down the criterion). Now look, the same thing came. For the guidance of the people... For the guidance of the people, first the Tawrat and the Injil were sent down. Yes. And the Qur'an was sent down. That is, the zahir shari'at, Tawrat, and its 'ilm-e-batini (esoteric knowledge) is the Injil. Now look, as the stages progress, Musa 'alayh al-salam came two and a half thousand years ago. Before the Prophet, six hundred years ago, Janab 'Isa came. So the era had moved forward. Just as today we understand that compared to before, the whole world has become enlightened, all things are known, everything has been revealed. In the same way, the Tawrat that came upon Janab Da'ud... Janab Musa, if we consider it the zahir shari'at, then its essence or its good or its batin is the Injil. And the batin of the Injil will now be the Qur'an-e-Majid. And then the Tawrat and then the Injil were revealed, and the Qur'an was revealed. That is, that is... those people who have an affinity for the kalimat-e-hikmat (words of wisdom), he taught them. And this same practice has happened in previous eras as well. In previous eras... yes, it has happened in eras. And then the Furqan was revealed. That is, he made the maqam-e-wasa'it (station of intermediaries) clear. There's a lot to understand here. If you go deep into it, there are many things. That the prophets who have passed, the nuteqa who have passed, each one had a wasi. Janab Musa had Harun, Janab Ibrahim had Janab Isma'il, each one had one. But a final nabi came, the Khatim al-Anbiya' (Seal of the Prophets). And what is he? Sayyid al-Mursalin (Master of the Messengers). The Seal of the Messengers. His person came. So the wasi who came was the greatest of all. Just as the Prophet is the Ashraf al-Anbiya' (most noble of prophets), so is Janab 'Ali salawatullah 'alayh the Ashraf al-Awsiya' (most noble of legatees). The one who has an affinity for him was taught, and this happened in previous eras as well. Before this also, this sitr (veiling) came. When did it come? Before kashf (unveiling). Before this was kashf. Meaning, a period of 50,000 years passed. And after the period of 'arsh passed, then sitr came. So sitr comes, just as after night comes day, and after day comes night. In the same way, after kashf comes sitr, after sitr comes kashf, after kashf comes sitr. This... you cannot change this. Just as we have no power to prevent night from coming after day, and for it to remain day. It can't happen. Or for it to remain night after night. After six hours, the sun must rise. This is the system of Allah. And it's an automatic system. No one can change it. So just as this cannot be changed, in the same way the ayyamullah (days of God), which are special days, meaning the era of kashf, which is 50,000 years long, that comes first, the time of day. Then comes the period of sitr. Sitr is 7,000 years long. It began with Adam. Now, we are not finding the previous book, we are searching for it here, it is not being found. In it is the story of Adam 'alayh al-salam. So that if that is known, you will know how the world began and what the status of Adam 'alayh al-salam was, and how in the time of Adam 'alayh al-salam, the shaytan misled people. And he is still misleading them. All those who go astray, they are all disciples of 'Arith bin Murra. 'Arith bin Murra, this is the shaytan from the time of Adam 'alayh al-salam. He was given a moment of reprieve from Allah. Why? Because he said, "I am a mu'ahid (monotheist). I believe in you, I believe in Allah Ta'ala. But I did not obey your command." So he who did not obey the command, did not obey it. But he had a whim, he had a qiyas (analogy). Because awwalu man qasa Iblis (the first to use analogy was Iblis). That he was the first to make an analogy. Whatever thing you surmise, that it should be like this, it should be like that. Who are you to change the system? The ones who change it are the prophets or those below them. You have no authority. So the one who first made a qiyas, in religion, was 'Arith bin Murra. 'Arith bin Murra is the shaytan of our era of sitr. He who did not accept Adam. When Allah Ta'ala said, what is it? Inni ja'ilun fi'l-ardi khalifa (Indeed, I will make upon the earth a viceroy). That book is not available, but I have to tell you. That Allah Ta'ala, what did he say? Inni ja'ilun fi'l-ardi khalifa. All the mala'ika were sitting, and you said, "I want to create a khalifa (viceroy) on the earth." Meaning, ja'ilun fi'l-ardi khalifa. At that time, all the mala'ika were present. At that moment, all of them said, "We are following you, we are prostrating, we are bowing to you, we are doing this and that. We are glorifying you. And you are creating a human being?" Khalifa means fi'l-ardi khalifa. Ard, ard means on the earth. On the earth, a viceroy. What is this? At that time, Allah Ta'ala said, "Inni a'lamu ma la ta'lamun (Indeed, I know that which you do not know)." That's it. This command was given, and from that time, the angels were taken aback. Now, there are great meanings to it, but there isn't enough time to go into its details. That how can angels make a mistake? Mistakes are made by humans. Why did these angels object? They used their tongues. That we are lacking in our prostrations? That you are creating a human? And what did they say? The verses of Alif Lam Mim have passed. That what will he do? He will fight on the earth, he will cause discord, he will shed blood. All these things. At that time, Allah Ta'ala said, "Inni a'lamu ma la ta'lamun (Indeed, I know that which you do not know)." That's it, the matter was closed. And now those angels were perplexed. And they were ashamed, and they made a mistake. What did those angels do? They were taken aback, that we have made a great mistake. After that, Janab... Allah created the form of Adam. Now there is a whole explanation of this, it is very long, but I will tell you briefly that Allah Ta'ala created the form of Adam. And what did he do? This is the translation of the verses of the Qur'an Sharif. But the real meaning comes later. That he created the form from what? From clay and water. Because nothing is made from clay alone. A form is not made. Until water is mixed in it. Mixing water, he made it, and after that, he blew his ruh (spirit) into it, Allah did. After blowing it, he told all the mala'ika to prostrate to Adam. So the prostration is not like the prostration we do. The definition of prostration is different. This prostration is the sajda-e-ta'zimi (prostration of respect). Which is to bow in the manner of ruku' (bowing), in front of someone, to follow, to obey. So all of them... what was said? Allah Ta'ala said, "Usjudu (prostrate)." Prostrate to him. Then what happened? All the angels, fa-sajadu (so they prostrated). All the angels prostrated. Illa Iblis (except for Iblis). Except for Iblis the accursed. Aba wa'stakbara wa kana min al-kafirin (He refused and was arrogant and became of the disbelievers). He refused, disobeyed, and became one of the kafirin (disbelievers). This is the first chapter after your Alif Lam Mim. Hudan li'l-muttaqin alladhina... after that. The meaning is that the angels made a mistake, and after that, this one... which angel was this, who... Iblis? He was the teacher of all of them. He taught everyone. He was the mu'allim-e-malakut (teacher of the angelic realm). He was the greatest. Because he was coming from the era of kashf. But when the time for testing came, the time for the exam came, "Prostrate to him." He did not do it. That's it, the matter was closed. And he was called Iblis the accursed, and after that... So now here, many questions arise in common language, because if you go among the common people and they hear all this, what meaning will they take from it? That Allah Ta'ala... what is Allah? He is the one who, with kun fa-yakun (Be, and it is), it happens. He said "kun" (be) and fa-yakun (it is), the world was created. Then what was the need to make a form of Adam from clay and water? What does it mean, from clay and water? If the form of Adam is made from clay and water, then we too are Adam's... are humans. We should also be made from clay and water. We are not like that, we are from flesh. So what is the meaning of this? It's a matter to understand, but it becomes very long. But I will hint at it, that by clay and water, it means that by clay is meant the knowledge of shari'at (law), and by water is meant the knowledge of ta'wil (interpretation), which we are reading. Ta'wil. By giving the knowledge of ta'wil and clay, meaning shari'at, he prepared him. Whom? Adam 'alayh al-salam. And when he was prepared, then he blew his ruh (spirit) into him, meaning the haqa'iq (realities). The books that are higher than this, the knowledge of haqa'iq was given to him. When he had read the haqa'iq, then it was said, "Now obey them. They are your seniors, obey them." So all of them, fa-sajadu illa Iblis (so they prostrated, except for Iblis). All the people prostrated, except for Iblis the accursed. Aba wa'stakbara wa kana min al-kafirin. He is the one... So when this had happened, then the angels realized, "Oh, what is this?" That we are prostrating, and this shaytan has not done it. We have made a blunder. We should... Allah is commanding us to prostrate, and we are being impertinent. That are we not enough for your praise and glorification... for your prostration? So at that time, they realized that we have made a mistake. Now we must ask for forgiveness. This is the first forgiveness in the world. That they, the mala'ika, what did they do? Now they started to circle around the 'arsh (throne). To appease Allah Ta'ala. See, this is the translation. To appease Allah Ta'ala, that, "Forgive us, we have made a mistake, we have been impertinent, and so on." And they are circling. In this circling, the चक्कर (chakkar - turns) they made, Allah Ta'ala liked this manner. If you have to ask for forgiveness from someone, and they have turned their face away, then as they have turned their face, you also turn. Just as we do the tawaf (circumambulation). Just like that. They kept turning. And until they were forgiven, they kept turning. When Allah Ta'ala liked this manner, He said, "Now go and build a house for Me on the earth. And whoever commits a sin, let him go to Makkah Sharif and do its tawaf. In the tawaf, the supplications they make, you read them in zahir (exoterically), but what is the real meaning of it? That you are asking for forgiveness for your sins. And make seven rounds." This is the matter. Now, the meaning within it is that Allah Ta'ala did not come from above. Allah said, Allah said, "What is it?" Inni ja'ilun fi'l-ardi khalifa. Did Allah Ta'ala get up from there and come? It can't be. Then, "with both my hands, I made..." This is the phrasing of the Qur'an Sharif. Now, if you ask the common people, what does it mean? Does Allah have two hands? Does Allah have a tongue, with which he is speaking? It can't be. So then what is the meaning of it? I have said in Baroda every year, I teach this lesson. And I have said it here many times, and in other places too. That Allah Ta'ala neither has a tongue nor this. Then what is its meaning? Its meaning is that Allah Ta'ala, just as we... four... we are reading. That by Allah is meant the Imam of that time. The Imam created Janab Adam. The Imam, who? Maulana Hunayd salawatullah 'alayh. Maulana Hunayd is the last of the era of kashf and the beginning of the era of sitr, in between, you came. And you gave the command, "Now prostrate to Adam." And my... this lineage will continue. Because until now, in the era of kashf, the Imam was present. It will come in A'ina. The Imam, when they are present in... that is, in life and visible, that is what we call the era of kashf. And what is the era of sitr called? When the Imam is hidden. In that way, just as when the sun is visible, we call it day, and when the sun is not visible, it is night. So now it is the period of night. So in this regard, Maulana Hunayd salawatullah 'alayh had given the command. So, to make him from clay and water, I have told you, with both his hands. What are the two hands? They are your two hujjat (proofs). Whatever work a person does, he does it with two hands. So your two helpers, your two fathers, the zahir and the batin, with them he prepared you. Whom? Adam 'alayh al-salam. This is the incident of the first Alif Lam Mim that has passed above. In it, what is the meaning of Alif, Lam, Mim, that will be told when it comes. And then the Furqan was revealed. That is, the one possessing the maqam-e-wasa'it was made clear. The one who is a distinguisher and a differentiator between truth and falsehood for the believers and the hypocrites. Inna alladhina kafaru bi-ayatillahi lahum 'adhabun shadidun wa'llahu 'azizun dhu intiqam (Indeed, those who disbelieve in the verses of Allah will have a severe punishment. And Allah is Exalted in Might, the Owner of Retribution.). Those who disbelieved in the verses of Allah, for them is a severe punishment. And Allah is All-Powerful, the one who takes revenge. That is, those who denied the a'imma (Imams), they will be brought down from their ranks. And no one can overcome the command of sabiq ta'ala. On the command... on the command... No one can overcome the command. No, they can't. Look, a'imma. A'imma is the plural of Imam. One after another, wahidan ba'da wahidin wa ladan 'an waladin (one after another and a son from a father). The shart we read, it is necessary that we read wahidan ba'da wahidin wa ladan 'an waladin. One after another, and a son after a father. It must be a son after a father, it cannot be anyone else. Whether the son of a da'i is a da'i or not, that's a different matter. Whether the son of a mansus is a mansus or not, that's a different matter. If he is worthy, he will become one. But it must be the son of an Imam. It cannot be anyone else. So this path, Allah Ta'ala has set it. It has been coming for ages. What is it called? Wa lan tajida li-sunnatillahi tabdila (and never will you find in the way of Allah any change). This is such a sunnah (way) of Allah that will never be changed. Let lakhs of years pass, let crores of years pass. But a son after a father, a son after a father will happen. Even now, when the era of kashf begins, when sitr ends, this same lineage... who? Who is the last one? Janab Qa'im. After the Mahdi, the Qa'im will come. From the progeny of the Qa'im, the era of kashf will begin. And when the era of kashf ends, then the era of sitr will begin, it will begin from their sons. So, wahidan ba'da wahidin, wa ladan 'an waladin, this sequence will never be broken. Wa lan tajida li-sunnatillahi tahwila (and never will you find in the way of Allah any alteration). In it, there will never be any alteration, any deviation. Remember that the one who denies the a'imma, among the mustawda'in... now it will not be understood what the mustawda' is. Now that will come, the mention of it will come. What is the difference between a'imma and mustawda'? It will come now. In a couple of sentences. That is, those who denied the a'imma and were brought down from their ranks. What happened? They didn't accept Hasan. Sulh had to be made. Imam Husayn, a great personality, the very embodiment of faith. There was no one like him in that era when Karbala happened. But they didn't accept, they didn't accept. In the mustaqarr imams, your rank is very high. The beloved son of Maulana 'Ali. But they didn't accept. So at that time, what is it? And on the command of sabiq ta'ala... now they will be thrown down from their ranks. The one who does not accept the Imam, will be thrown down. What does thrown down mean? It means he has left the hand. He has left the hand. Now what is he? He has become one of the opponents, and then slowly, slowly he will be put into the 'adhrat, he will go into the 'adhabat, there will be the punishment of safra, these are the levels, and while going through the levels, he will go down. They don't throw anything down all at once. Allah Ta'ala, he lowers it slowly, gradually. He will put him in the 'adhrat, then he will go to the 'adhrat, then there will be the punishment of safra. These are the levels, and he has been told. He is the one who takes revenge from the rebellious. Rebellious, rebellious like Namrud was, Haman is, Shaddad is, Fir'awn is. What did Fir'awn say? Ana rabbukum al-a'la (I am your lord, most high). I am your lord. Rabbukum al-a'la. And what happened? He drowned. He was finished. He was washed away in the storm of dharat, finished. How? The river Euphrates, which you were told about, in the river Nile, he was, in it the entire army... if you read it, then the inner meanings will be known, that what does the Nile mean, what does drowning in the water mean, Musa 'alayh al-salam crossed over and Fir'awn was finished. How? If you read all that, you will understand. Inna Allaha la yakhfa 'alayhi shay'un fi'l-ardi wa la fi'l-sama' huwa alladhi yusawwirukum fi'l-arhami kayfa yasha'u la ilaha illa huwa al-'aziz al-hakim (Indeed, from Allah nothing is hidden in the earth nor in the heaven. It is He who forms you in the wombs as He wills. There is no deity except Him, the Exalted in Might, the Wise.). Nothing is hidden from Allah, neither on the earth nor in the heavens. He is the one who fashions you in the wombs of your mothers as He wills. There is no god but Him. He is the All-Powerful, the All-Wise. That is, nothing of the esoteric and exoteric knowledge is hidden from the wasi. Look, now he is the one who, in a hidden way... Nothing is hidden from Allah. This is the translation. That everything from the heavens to the earth, Allah is All-Aware, he knows. But what is written below? Look, Mulla Amir Sahab has translated it, absolutely exactly. Every single letter, every word is special. What is it? That from the heavens to the earth, nothing is hidden... nothing is hidden from Allah. You, in your heart, think of anything, whether it is good or bad, He knows everything. He is All-Aware. So, Allah is All-Aware. Because He is the creator of everything. But what is the meaning here? He is the one who, in the wombs of mothers, fashions your form as He wills. So who is the mother? And besides Him, there is no other god. He is the All-Powerful, the All-Wise. That is, nothing of the esoteric and exoteric knowledge is hidden from the wasi. The wasi knows. You will say, "I am praying, I am doing this and that, I am praying with great sincerity." Your hadd-e-'ali goes up, hadd-e-'ali, hadd-e-dani, hadd-e-'ali goes up. The Imam knows how you are praying. Are you praying for show? Are you praying with humility or not? You are standing there, doing the tasbih, saying, "This is all a show." Show. Show business, this is. This should not be. You should speak with humility. No one is great before Allah Ta'ala. He is the greatest. Allahu akbar. He is the greatest of the great. Remember that those who pray for show, I have written about them that they are such that their face is not towards the qibla, but they have turned back and are praying, "Look, people, I am praying." This is the prayer of show. And there are such people among the common folk, you go and see. They just stand there. The whole surah is finished, in the Tarawih. And how is the Tarawih? You know how it is. In Tarawih, here our hafiz are all very learned, they are like that. I was in Kuwait, and we would... the munshis would come to teach the children. They were very good, they were hafiz, and they taught well, they did things. Once I asked him, the children had come to be taught, I said, "Which mosque are you teaching in these days?" He said, "Ibrahim Sahab, the first mosque where I used to teach, I have left it. Now I am in another mosque." I said, "Why?" He said, "This is a strange matter with these Arabs. Here, where they used to teach, there was no hafiz nearby. So I was called." So I went, and I was teaching. So before that, the sahibs who were there, how did they used to teach? Behind them, some people were standing. And this sahib is leading the prayer, he is reciting the surah. So he was not a hafiz. In front, the Qur'an Sharif is placed on a stand. He is looking at it and reciting. He said, "I left it. I am a hafiz. I will not teach in that place. I have left and am teaching in another mosque." So there are such people too. That it is a matter of show. So whether it is the prayer of show, or the fast, or the hajj, or the zakat, or anything, it is not accepted. Remember this. With humility, bowing down and speaking. Not with the power of speech. Allah is the greatest. The great one knows you. How you are. So remember this. He is the one who, in a hidden manner, arranges the ranks according to His will. Yes. Besides Him, there is no other god. 'Ali knows. Every Imam knows. And who is every Imam? They are all veils of 'Ali. So 'Ali is the most knowledgeable. The wasi-e-paygambar, before him no one can... that's it. It's finished. That Allah has such a wasi that he is the Ashraf al-Awsiya' (most noble of legatees). In the era of sitr, from Adam until here, no such wasi has been created. It is the naba' al-'azim (great news). And he is the imam al-muttaqin (imam of the pious), the qa'id al-ghurr al-muhajjalin (leader of the radiant ones). Who? 'Ali Murtada. 'Ali Murtada is his name. What is 'Ali? To know that, you will... ten lifetimes will pass. You have to know what 'Ali is. Who is the a'imma-e-azima? Who is amir al-nahl? Who is Murtada? Who is Mujtaba? What is Taha? What is Ya Sin? To understand this, it is a very difficult thing. That is why the Qur'an Sharif is not for everyone. It is not something they can understand. Those who think that we have done the tafsir (exegesis), we are translating the Qur'an Sharif, very correct... আরে (are), translation is translation. Translation is not the meaning. The meaning is a very distant thing. You are just polishing the shell. You have not reached the essence inside. The meaning is that there are many things that are very hidden. If they were not hidden, then these phrases would not come: 'afalata'qilun ('do you not use reason?'), 'afalatubsirun ('do you not see?'). O people, do you not do a close review? Do you not use your intellect? What is the matter in this? That you are running like a sheep, that one after another you are just reading the verses. With great khirat (melodious recitation) you are reading. You go and see. Do you understand the meaning? The khirat is very good. So khirat, or reading, is a fann (art), not 'ilm (knowledge). 'Ilm is a different thing. 'Ilm is the hidden meaning inside, which our awliya' Allah will tell us. And who has told the awliya' Allah? Maulana Ja'far al-Sadiq, and all the a'imma, the 'ilm has been distributed from them. They have told us. They are the ones who have the right. Fa's'alu ahl al-dhikr in kuntum la ta'lamun (so ask the people of remembrance if you do not know). Ask the ahl al-dhikr (people of remembrance) if you do not know something. Now who are the ahl al-dhikr? Those who are sitting, with their pillows, and are in meditation, they have become the ahl al-dhikr. Wrong. The ahl al-dhikr are those who are the ahl al-bayt (people of the house). The ahl al-bayt-e-kiram who are there, they are the ahl al-dhikr. He is unparalleled and is All-Wise. Huwa alladhi anzala 'alayka al-kitaba minhu ayatun muhkamatun hunna umm al-kitab wa ukharu mutashabihat (It is He who has sent down to you the Book; in it are verses that are precise - they are the foundation of the Book - and others are allegorical). Yes. It is He who has revealed the book to you, from which some verses are muhkam (clear and precise). They are the umm al-kitab (mother of the book). And others are mutashabih (allegorical). Yes. In it, there are some clear, distinct, firm verses, in which no doubt is created. They are the essence of the book. And others are not doubt-creating. No... Yani... they are doubt-creating. They are doubt-creating. That is, sabiq ta'ala commanded you to establish the wasi. That is, from the zurriyat (progeny) of the wasi, they are the a'imma whose ranks are muhkam (firm). That is, they are mustaqarr (established). They are the ones who are worthy of the imamat-e-mustaqarra (permanent imamate). And others are mustawda', in their ranks. The whole matter is now clear. The whole matter has come out. I had just told you that the difference between mustawda' and mustaqarr, this is it. That the a'imma... the mutashabih, it is said that Maulana 'Ali was asked, "What do you know?" He said, "I know which verses are mutashabih and which are muhkam. Which were revealed in a valley, and which on a mountain. Which came in a mosque, where. You know all things." The speaking Qur'an is you. So now here too, what is it? That all the a'imma are a'imma. From Imam Hasan until here. But you know the maratib (ranks), what is the rank of Hasan and what is the rank of Husayn. Mustawda' are of a lower rank, who are caretakers, who are temporary, or you can say they are trustees. But the mustaqarr imams are different. Maulana 'Ali had two sons, both were rightful Imams. Al-Hasan wa al-Husayn imamani (Hasan and Husayn are two Imams). Qama aw qa'ada wa abuhuma khayrun minhuma (whether they rise or sit, and their father is better than both of them). The Prophet says that after me, both are Imams. Mama haq hain (they are my rightful Imams). Imam ke baad ma (after the Imam, ma). Two Imams, true. Whether they rise in their right or they sit. Now look, who is sitting? Janab Hasan. Whose name came? Al-Hasan. Not al-Hasan wa al-Husayn. Al-Hasan wa al-Husayn imamani. The name of the elder brother was taken first by the Prophet. And al-Hasan wa al-Husayn imamani, qama aw qa'ada. Whether they rise or sit. Now, in the context of function, the rank of qama was given to Husayn. And qa'ada, meaning to sit, who is sitting? Janab... they relinquished their right. Maulana Hasan. So Janab Hasan is the mustawda' Imam. And Janab... the mustaqarr Imam, meaning the lineage that fought, son after father, that is Husayn after Janab 'Ali. Remember this. And then Zain al-'Abidin, then Janab Baqir, then Janab Ja'far al-Sadiq, then Maulana Isma'il, then Muhammad bin Isma'il. This continued. That is why the eleventh Imam, Imam Mahdi came. After that, the Qa'im came. And now the Mahdi is also to come. In all of these, who is mustawda' and who is mustaqarr? If you know that, then you have the correct madhhab (school of thought) in your mind. How is the arrangement of the Imamate? So, the mustaqarr Imam is the one who is son after father, and upon whom the burden of the Imamate is placed. He is made. How? Now, if I read a little, it will be understood. I want to finish, but that matter is not being completed. They are worthy of the imamat-e-mustaqarra. And others are in the ranks of the mustawda'. And they are very similar to the a'imma-e-mustaqarrin. So much so that people mistook them for the mustaqarr Imam. Its reason is something... The purpose is to fulfill some religious aspect. Fa-amma alladhina fi qulubihim zayghun fa-yattabi'una... Look, they are similar. How are they similar? Musa al-Kazim. He came in opposition to whom? Seventh Imam, Ja'far al-Sadiq. Then Isma'il, the sixth Imam. And Musa al-Kazim, the brother. So, all the exoteric things were given to Musa al-Kazim. He knew the exoteric, he knew the esoteric. He had the accounts, and so on, it was given to him. He is great. And he thought that I am everything. Ja'far al-Sadiq had two sons. So Musa al-Kazim, all the Shia people started to accept him. Musa al-Kazim. And who was the real master? Maulana Isma'il salawatullah 'alayh. And then there are great incidents, if you read the sirat, you will understand, that in Kufa, Janab Isma'il, his opponent, who was their opponent? Walid was his name. He was a very bad person. He was inclined towards the Bani Umayya and the Bani 'Abbas. He was very much after your life. So Maulana Ja'far al-Sadiq gave the nass to Janab Isma'il and he himself went into the veil of hijabat. A person who makes one Imam, another Imam, he should go away. He did not go, that's why he is alive. So what is the meaning of this? If that meaning is understood, then you are a mu'min (believer). Otherwise, you are nothing. You need to understand that Maulana Ja'far al-Sadiq was not there. When the command came from Ja'far al-Sadiq, "Come, O people of the city, see, my son has been martyred." The body was lying there. The body remained in Kufa, and people were coming, they circled, they saw the body, they went. They came, they saw, they went. For the raj'at-e-din. So all this has happened in the time of the a'imma. It is the miracle of Maulana Ja'far al-Sadiq that you did this and you saved Janab Isma'il. In place of Isma'il, who worked? The hijabat. If the reality of hijabat is understood, it is an ocean. To cross that ocean is not easy. If the hijabat is understood. And then Janab Isma'il immediately made his son, Isma'il... Muhammad bin Isma'il, the seventh Imam. A very great Imam. So, there was Ja'far al-Sadiq, then Muhammad bin Isma'il. All the hijabat came, and then it happened. This is the arrangement for saving. So at that time, people thought that Musa al-Kazim is everything. In this way, in the future, a mutashabih... this is the mutashabih. That the muhkam... muhkam are those who are the mustaqarr imams. And some are for show, the Imam. How? I will finish in one sentence. That the Karbala incident happened, and the war took place. After the war, all 72 people were martyred. Some were left, children, women who were left, the caravan returned, plundered. So in it, one grown man was left, and he was Maulana Zain al-'Abidin. Zain al-'Abidin is the real Imam. Of whom? The son of Janab Husayn. Maulana Zain al-'Abidin is the greatest. He returned alive. Now, at that time, there was no telegraph, no communication, nothing. So in Karbala, everyone was martyred. So at that time, Muhammad al-Hanafiyyah was made the mustawda'. His brother. Muhammad al-Hanafiyyah. A step-brother. So now the looted caravan that came, when it reached Madinah, then it came to the river... So when it came to Kufa, then it was known. So Muhammad al-Hanafiyyah, he himself is not saying that I am the Imam. You are saying, "You are the Imam, you are, you are." All the people are saying, "You come, he is just sitting there." It is possible that I am the one. Because everyone was martyred there. So Maulana Zain al-'Abidin could also be. So when Janab Zain al-'Abidin arrived, परेशान (pareshaan - distressed). So what to do? He himself, if ten ignorant people are saying that you are the Imam, and no one else is left, they are all finished, so it is all true. But it is not the truth. So Maulana Muhammad al-Hanafiyyah also started to think that it is possible that I am the Imam. So at that time, he... the Imam is such a personality where all the surah come together, where all the ruhaniyat (spirituality) is, that. So he didn't receive anything. So whatever they had, just like Da'ud had it. In that way, the dawa'at was going on. Now his rank is great because he... no mistake was made by them, but by their hijabat. So at that time, Maulana Zain al-'Abidin came and saw that, "The Imam, I have returned, and all these people are accepting him." He was their uncle. So what did you do? You took a bottle of 'itr (perfume) and poured out all the 'itr. After pouring it out, the empty bottle, in which only the fragrance remained, he sent it to the dawat. That's it. As soon as he saw it, he understood that whatever I had, has all gone from here. He immediately asked for forgiveness and everything was done. So it happens like that. That there too, Muhammad al-Hanafiyyah came in the mutashabihat. Then Musa al-Kazim came. And in the future, Maulana Mustali, who is our nineteenth... the night that comes, he is its Mansus. Maulana Musta'li. A very great Imam. His... the one who was his... his brother. The son of Mustansir. He was Nazar. Agha Khan. The one who came out from Agha Khan, he... they became Nizari. They became Nizari or Agha Khani. So Nazar was also like this. All the exoteric government was given to him. By his father. But he is making his son his Imam. Do you accept the Imam or do you accept the king? And the people went astray in this very thing. The Nizari sect became separate. Here, the Shia became separate. So we are the ones who have been coming down from above, and in between, great sects have separated from us. The last sect is this, of the Saudis, which we have started. So in this religion, there is such division. They meet and then they separate, they meet and then they separate. This is the demand of the era of sitr. All these... the corruption of faith, the badness of character, the lack of discipline, all this is included in it. Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim. O Allah, for the sake of Sayyidna Muhammad, and for the sake of Sayyidna 'Ali... Al-Fatiha.

Right, the bedsheet... Ibrahim Bhai... Yes... A little bit forward... please move a little bit... 41... 41? One page, before this page... 48 is the last... 41... yes... this lecture was given before, on the 7th... yes, yes... Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim. That... yes... *huwa alladhi* (He is the one). A little bit of it was done... Bismillah al-Rahim. Speak a bit louder. Slowly, slowly, read. *huwa alladhi* (He is the one). Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim. *huwa alladhi yusawwirukum fi al-arhami kayfa yasha'u la ilaha illa huwa al-'aziz al-hakim* (He is the one who shapes you in the wombs as He wills. There is no god but He, the Exalted in Might, the Wise). This is not it. *huwa alladhi anzala 'alayka al-kitaba minhu ayatun muhkamatun hunna ummu al-kitabi wa ukharu mutashabihatun* (He is the one who has sent down to you the Book. In it are verses that are precise—they are the foundation of the Book—and others that are allegorical). Yes, this is it.

The translation of the *ayat* is: It is He who has sent down the Book to you. From it are some *ayat* (verses) that are clear, distinct, and firm, in which no doubt is created. They are the essence of the Book. And others create doubt.

I also explained yesterday that *ayat muhkamat* (clear verses) and *ayat mutashabihat* (allegorical verses) are of two types. Their meaning is that *muhkamat* refers to the *A'immah mustaqarrin* (permanent Imams), where the son becomes Imam after the father. The second type is *mustawda'* (trustee/temporary), whose mention will come later. *Mustawda'* are caretakers; they are given a trust which they then return to its owner. That is... that is... And its *ta'wili ma'ne* (esoteric meaning) is, that is, *Sabiq Ta'ala* has commanded you to appoint a *wasi* (successor). That is... *minhu*... and from the *ayat* "*minhu ayatun muhkamatun*," the meaning of *minhu* is, that is, from the progeny of the *wasi* are those *A'immah* whose *maratib* (ranks) are *muhkam* (firm), meaning *mustaqarr* (permanent). These *mustaqarr* Imams cannot be changed. It is a condition that the son comes after the father. The *mustawda'*, however, can be anyone who is worthy; they become the *mustawda'* to whom the trust is given.

*Muhkamat* is a separate thing, and *mutashabihat* is a separate thing. *Mutashabihat* means those that resemble each other. They are also elders, these are also elders, but the difference is that one is a *mustaqarr Imam*, who is son after father, *wahidan ba'da wahidin* (one after another). And I said yesterday and the day before that this is a *sunnah* (practice) of Allah, not of the Prophet, it is the *sunnah* of Allah, which never fades nor is it altered. *wa lan tajida li-sunnati Allahi tabdila* (And you will never find in the way of Allah any change). Allah has set a path that after one Imam will come another Imam, *wahidan ba'da wahidin*. This has been going on for years, not just centuries, but for millions of years. This era will never be overturned. *wa lan tajida li-sunnati Allahi tahwila* (And you will never find in the way of Allah any alteration). Neither will there be any alteration in it, nor will there be any change. This is the *sunnah* of Allah. Since when? If one *karr* is, say, 16,000 crore years, and if we take one *dawr* on a smaller scale, a *dawr* is, say, 4 lakh years. In 4 lakh years, the son must become [Imam] after the father, that's it. Whether you are in *satr* (concealment) or *kashf* (manifestation), whichever. After *kashf* comes *satr*, after *satr* again comes *kashf*. But after an Imam, an Imam will come. When the current *dawr* of *satr* ends, the *Qa'im al-Salam* who will come, from his progeny, Imams will be born, and they will be the Imams of *kashf*, the first Imams. It has been explained who they are, what they are, everything has been told.

*Minhu*, that is, from the progeny of the *wasi* are those *A'immah* whose *maratib* are *muhkam*, that is, *mustaqarr*. They are the ones worthy of the *imamat-e-mustaqarra* (permanent Imamate). And the others are in the *maratib* of *mustawda'*, and they are very similar to the *A'immah-e-mustaqarrin*, so much so that people mistake them for the *Imam-e-mustaqarr*. The reason for this is to fulfill some worldly objectives.

You see, sometimes there is an expediency (*maslahat*), there are certain things. Just as I have explained before, and it will probably come up again, that *Mawlana Imam Husayn*, when he was leaving, when he departed from Madinah, he left his uncle, *Sayyidna Muhammad bin Hanafiyyah*, as his representative (*qaim maqam*). And when they returned—that is, when the entire caravan was finished, and *Sayyidna Husayn* and his family had all passed away or were martyred—*Mawlana Zainul Abideen*, who was the Imam of the time... because you hear in the accounts of Karbala that in the final moments, *Mawlana Zainul Abideen* also wanted to sacrifice himself for his father, just as *Mawlana Ali Akbar* and *Ali Asghar* had done. At that time, the *Imam*—*Mawlana Husayn*—stopped him. When he took a spear and came out of the tent, saying, "I too will be martyred for my father," *Sayyida Zainab* stopped him, and *Sayyidna Husayn* came and said, "What are you doing, Ali? My *Imamat* will be established through you. Meaning, you are the remainder." And he gave him his testament (*wasiyyat*), and handed over some weapons. He wanted to hand them over—as is mentioned in the common *sirat* (biographies)—but his breath was leaving, and he became the Imam of the time. After that, *Imam Husayn* passed away, was martyred. And after his martyrdom, *Imam Zainul Abideen*, with the looted caravan, came to the court of Ubaydullah ibn Ziyad, and from there to Yazid's court, and then he went to Madinah. He performed the *ziyarat* of the Prophet. After that, a rumor spread that *Muhammad bin Hanafiyyah* was the Imam. This gave rise to the Hanafiyya sect. We also, out of *taqiyya* (precautionary dissimulation), call ourselves Hanafi, and we do so for this reason. Because he was an elder, and it wasn't his claim, but people started saying, "You are the Imam, since that caravan has been finished." It wasn't known who would return from Karbala. So at that time, it was the Hanafiyya. Now, we narrate in our *'aqa'id* (creeds) how the confusion with *Muhammad bin Hanafiyyah* was cleared; that is a separate matter. I explained it yesterday. But the deviation did not originate from *Muhammad bin Hanafiyyah*; rather, people were saying it, and there was malice in their hearts. What did *Mawlana Zainul Abideen, salawatullah 'alayhi*, do? He took a bottle of *'atr* (perfume), took out the perfume, and sent the empty bottle to his uncle. That's it. From this gesture, he understood and immediately apologized, and all matters were settled.

The point is that *Muhammad bin Hanafiyyah* was a *mustawda'*. He was a *mutashabihat*. He was such an elder that he was also considered to be the Imam, that he was worthy of becoming the Imam. Being worthy of becoming an Imam is not how it works. Worthiness is for the ranks below, like *da'i*, *ma'dhun*—these are based on worthiness. But for an Imam, the son of the Imam must be the one. If there are four sons, one of them will be it. Not all four sons will be. For example, *Ali Akbar* had to be martyred, *Ali Asghar* had to be martyred, and *Sayyidna Abbas*. All of them who were there, the progeny of *Sayyidna Ali*, were not meant to be the Imam. We, out of respect, call *Imam Abbas*, *Mawlana Abbas*, because his rank is very high. But the real Imam is *Mawlana Husayn, salawatullah 'alayhi*, who is the *mustaqarr Imam*, the son of *Mawlana Ali*. And *Sayyidna Hasan* was a *mustawda'*. And in this way, *Muhammad bin Hanafiyyah* is one, and then it is said that at the time of the sixth Imam, there was another schism, another dispute. And who came? Musa Kazim came. At that time, *Mawlana Ja'far al-Sadiq* had given him all the *zahiri* (exoteric) things. Giving *zahiri* things is one matter, but the *batini* (esoteric) reality is to establish the *hudud* (ranks), which is a different matter. *Zahiri* things—many things, properties, whatnot, accounts—he gave it all. Just as Nizar was given. Who was Nizar? The son of *Mawlana Mustansir Billah*. *Mawlana Musta'li, salawatullah 'alayhi*, was made the Imam. But Nizar claimed, "I am the Imam." This is the Nizari, Aga Khani [line]. And in this way, this has happened in many places, where someone was made a *mustawda'*. Here too, someone was made a *mustawda'* on a smaller scale: Dawood. And what did he do? He committed betrayal (*khayanat*).

So, in these high ranks, betrayal doesn't happen, but doubts arise. That's why it is called *mutashabihat*.

Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim. *fa-amma alladhina fi qulubihim zayghun fa-yattabi'una ma tashabaha minhu ibtigha'a al-fitnati wa-ibtigha'a ta'wilihi* (As for those in whose hearts is deviation, they follow that which is allegorical, seeking discord and seeking its interpretation). Yes. Its translation of the *ayat* is: Those in whose hearts there is a flaw, they follow the *mutashabihat* from this Book. The purpose is to stir up *fitna* (discord) and to seek *ta'wil* (interpretation).

That is, those people... This is a complete *ayat*. Those in whose hearts there is... how is it? Previously in Surah al-Baqarah, what was said? *fi qulubihim maradun* (In their hearts is a disease). In the first *sipara* (part of the Quran)... *fi qulubihim maradun fa-zadahumu Allahu* (in their hearts is a disease, so Allah has increased them [in disease]). And Allah is increasing it. When malice enters their hearts, or bad things, Allah increases it even more. "Do as much as you want." Then you will taste the punishment. *Fi qulubihim maradun fa-zadahumu Allahu*. Allah increases it. And... just as there was a respite there, in the time of the *Ahl al-Bayt*, for *Sayyidna Adam*'s companions, there was one here too for the first Caliph, the second Caliph. They all had a respite. They used to see the Prophet, they used to do everything. And they knew the ranks of Ali. But just... their claim, the claim of the common people, was that the Prophet's house—since Nabi *sallallahu 'alayhi wa alihi* became the Prophet—this is the house of prophethood (*nubuwwat*). How can it also be the house of *Imamat*? The *Imamat*... "we will choose, we will do it." The *Imamat* won't come from this house. That's why they didn't accept Ali. And after Ali, malice towards Hasanayn, malice towards Hasan, malice towards Husayn, this whole thing... This is the progeny of Shams, Abd Shams, who was he? Sayyidna Hashim's brother. The sons of Abd Manaf. The animosity started there, 100 years before, when *Sayyidna Hashim* and *Abd Manaf*... Abd Manaf was a great Imam. His sons were Hashim and Abd Shams.
