So it means... only three `jazira`s of ours are currently active. Yemen, Hindustan, and Sindh. These three `jazira`s have always been fertile. And they have remained so because the `jazira` of Yemen is the highest `jazira`. Why is it the highest? Because Makkah and Madina are in it. Makkah Sharif and Madina Sharif are both in it, so the `jazira` of Yemen... I mean, we are taking it like this... that is an island. In terms of `jazira`... Mawlana Idris has made it like this. Otherwise, in terms of area, that part is included in Yemen. So, because of the greatness of Makkah, it has been given that rank, that the `jazira` of Yemen is the most superior. And that is why, in today's time, whom we call `da'i`, in the time of Bani Isra'il, they were called `nabi`. As many prophets (`nabi`) as passed, 1,24,000 prophets passed, until today. Now you will say, where will we get the count? We can't even count 1220. Where will we get 1,24,000 from? So it means... from Adam 'alayh al-salam till here, all the venerable `hudud` who were the `du'at` of that time, they had the rank of `nabi`. Whom we call `da'i`, today our `du'at` have that same form. And in other books that you are reading, the names are given, the cabinet that is with the Imam, the `du'at`... their names are given. And the names that have come in the Qur'an, among the 1,24,000, are the most excellent names, the highest prophets. And among them too, there has been a division of `Natiq` prophets, and a division of `Ulu al-'Azm` prophets. Among the `Ulu al-'Azm` prophets, two prophets are the highest: Janab-e-Ibrahim and Janab-e-Paygambar. And in that, the most noble, `Sayyid al-Mursalin`, Janab-e-Paygambar (S), is called the highest prophet in the whole world. Now, what is `nubuwwat`, what is `risalat`, what is `wasiyyat`, what is `imamat`, what is `qa'imiyyat`... we have to understand this. The topic for two or three days is this: we, who are called `mu'minin`... after this, I will directly start the `ma'ad` of the `mu'min`. I mean, we are going into the `mabda'`. So... we, who are called `mu'minin`, a `mu'min` is one who is observant of prayers, and follows all of Shari'a. When a person takes the `'ahd`, he doesn't become a `mu'min`, but becomes a `mustajib`. A `mustajib` is a rank of the `mu'min`. It is the first rank. That you have taken the `'ahd`. You haven't done any `amal` yet. It is the first rank. Then as the days pass, his progress is known to him and to Allah. How will it be? When the ten ranks of the `mu'min` are completed, he is brought to the rank of the `hudud`. Now how will he be brought? The Mawla's gaze will fall on him. That is not our work. The Mawla's gaze will fall, and he will come to the rank of the `hudud`. When the ranks of the `hudud` are completed, he will go to the rank of `mukasir`. From `mukasir`, there is `madh'un`. `Madh'un`, then `da'i`, then `hujjat`. And in these, there are ten ranks each. Until the ten ranks are passed, a `madh'un-e-mahdud` cannot become a `madh'un-e-mutlaq`. Then the ten ranks of `madh'un-e-mutlaq`, i.e., of the `mansub`. `Madh'un-e-mutlaq` means the master of two `jazira`s. `Mahdud` is lower than that. So the `madh'un-e-mutlaq`, until then he cannot reach the rank of `da'i`, until he passes those ten ranks. That is why with us, there is a very subtle point, but it is that `du'at` can tell that when a `mansub` passes away, to which rank he has been promoted. After becoming a `madh'un`, there is also progress. After becoming a `madh'un`, according to his deeds, two ranks, four ranks, six ranks... he passes to the rank of... To the extent that where his `inzimam` (joining) has happened, that is also all mentioned in our books. It's not a small matter, but it is higher than our standard. Anyway, that he... the ten ranks of the `mu'min`, then the `hudud`, `mukasir`, then `madh'un-e-mahdud`, `madh'un-e-mutlaq`... in between there are others, `da'i-e-ihlal`, `da'i-e-ihram`... there are many such things. And going, the `da'i-e-mutlaq`, he is the one who is the master of our three `jazira`s. Now, here a subtle point has come, because this is a matter in front of us... our Sayyidna is present, so we must understand this, our duties. Sayyidna 'Aliqadar, whether he is the previous one, or the current one, or the future one... so this...

There is no difficulty, that is why I am teaching. And then Allah Ta'ala makes them say that... makes one say, that *dhalik al-kitab la rayba fih* (that is the Book, in it is no doubt). So what will be its meaning? So why is Allah Ta'ala making me... forcing me to read more? When it has already been taught that this is the thing, that there is no doubt in it, so then you should read it. So there is no doubt in the promise of Allah Ta'ala. We are Muslims, we are *mu'mins* (believers), we don't have any doubt at all, so why is this written? Anyway, leave that. *Dhalik al-kitab la rayba fih*. There, the word that has come is *dhalika*. *Dhalika* means 'that'. Those who know a little bit of basic Arabic, a little, they know *hadha* means 'this' and *dhalika* means 'that'. This and that. So 'this' is used for *hadha*. When the book is right in front of you, which you can see, which is on the desk, then will this be said, will 'this' be used or 'that' be used? You tell me. The near pointer which is there, in Urdu or in English... 'this' will be said or 'that' will be said? 'This' will be said. What should be said for 'this'? *Hadha kitabun*. And there, it is not said that, it is *dhalika*. No one can tell its reason. For 1400 years it has been written as *dhalika*, so what is its meaning? Anyway. So, what do the commentators do? I didn't understand it, but in a book... Abul Kalam Azad and great... are sitting. And what did they do? They translated it as: 'This is that book.' This is that book. This is that book, in which there is no doubt. Like, there is no... any doubt. So, what will be its meaning? That *dhalik al-kitab*, we believe that what is written is correct, and its meanings need to be understood. If it is not understood, it means our minds have a flaw, Allah Ta'ala's... there is no... one cannot have any doubt. In the word of Allah Ta'ala, there is not even a mistake of a single *zer*, *zabar* (vowel marking). A word is a different matter. And if a word with a *zer*, *zabar* is wrong, then one cannot even be called a *mu'min* (believer). There are some instances where if you put a *zer* instead of a *pesh* (vowel markings), then it becomes *kufr* (disbelief). I will tell you. Anyway. This, see, what is meant by *dhalik al-kitab*? The commentators did not understand it. But we have... in the first *sabaq* (lesson) of *Kitab al-Mabda'* it is written that 'this' should be there, 'that' should not be. Now, listen to what Mawla 'Ali said. [unclear] Go back. When, during the time of 'Uthman, the Quran was being compiled, a person from his clan... was sitting. He had a Quran compiled five times. And he said, "*Hadha kitabullah*" (This is the Book of Allah). This is the Book of Allah. He had it said. Then, during the time of 'Uthman, this is the book of the Prophet. So someone there said, "What about that book?" The father's book. *Untuq*, he said, 'you speak'. Meaning, O Messenger of Allah, O Prophet, what about my father's book? Now you tell me, what book is in the *satr* (concealment)? Which Quran Shareef is written on paper? The Quran Shareef is the word of Allah. He recited it three times before the people, "Speak, O book. Speak, O book." The words were not spoken. After that, he showed the book, the Quran Majid, and silenced everyone. He said that, "*Hadha kitabullah al-samit, wa ana kitabullah al-natiq*" (This is the silent Book of Allah, and I am the speaking Book of Allah). This is the speaking book of Allah and that is the silent book. So now, Janab-e-'Ali, that is the *Kitab-e-Natiq* (Speaking Book). And where is he written? Far, far away. The *Kitab-e-Natiq*, the person of Janab-e-'Ali *salawatullah 'alayh*, was born 1400 years ago. And he was also the *Qur'an-e-Natiq*. Now you tell me, *dhalik al-kitab la rayba fih*, so whose proof will this be? That book... this book is not... in the Quran... there is no doubt in it, everyone does it. The doubt is in whom? In 'Ali. The doubt is in the station of Janab-e-'Ali. For this reason, *dhalik al-kitab*, there should be no doubt in him. And he who is far, 1400 years ago, we cannot say 'this' to him, we have to say 'that'. That's it. Anyway, these are... there are many things where we... from two things... he can learn his lesson. This which is in the world of Islam... is so much that it is about Hadiths, and it is within the narrations, there are many things. I will, *insha'Allah*, slowly explain it. Today, I have to explain a very important thing about our prayers (*namaz*). Our prayer which we perform, the Fajar prayer which has two *rak'at*s of *sunnah* prayer... two *rak'at*s are for our Imam, and after that, two *rak'at*s are prayed, so four *rak'at*s are completed. The rest of the thing that... he has also done. The prayers which are imposed, from the side of Allah Ta'ala, those are the *fara'id* (obligatory) prayers, which are 17 *rak'at*s. 17 *rak'at*s. Fajr has two, Zohr has four, Asr has four, Maghrib has three, and Isha has four. These are the *fara'id* (obligatory prayers). These we... it is a must for us. It is absolutely necessary. Every day, these 17 *rak'at*s should be performed. After that, *sunnah*s are there, which are just below the *fardh* (obligatory). Like, it has its place. Its rank is after that. The rank of *sunnah*. So *sunnah* has this rank, below the *fardh*, and *nafil* and *tatawwu'* are of a lower rank than that. And what is its reality? That these are kept as *mansulat* (attributions). The meanings are behind it. Usually, in Zohr, we pray four *rak'at*s. In Zuhr, before the *fardh*, we pray six *rak'at*s. All of these have their *manzilat* (stations). And according to their station... which is... which *manzilah* is higher, which one is lower. Which... Anyway, the prayer that we are commanded to do is of five times. These cannot be missed. This is... say, a syllabus that this many *rak'at*s in a day must be completed. As long as your life is, if this decreases, then in the Imam's presence, the *mu'min* is considered a sinner. Now this which we... we pray... prayers. These are prayed at *Zohr* (noon)... in the afternoon. *Asr* is the time after that. And *Maghrib*, which is the evening... when the darkness begins to set. And *Isha*, which is in the middle of the night, at that time. *Fajr*, which is in the morning. So, just as there are many *mansulat*, as you have read, that Mawlana Dr. Saheb has said that the *tahajjud* (late-night prayer) is not just one, there are many *tahajjuds*. In the same way, there are many *mansulat*. As you know, our five times are attributed to the five prophets. Nuh, Ibrahim, Musa, 'Isa and the Prophet. They are attributed to the five. I am telling you this so that you remember and always keep it in mind. And it is in this way. You see, this is the period of *fikr* (contemplation), which we call the time of night. And this is the day... after the evening, night comes, and after that, the dawn breaks... that when the sun is setting, we will call it night, and when the sun is rising, we will call it day. This is the word. Now, we will apply the sun to this: when the Imam is manifest (*zahir*), it will be the time of *dhikr* (remembrance). And when the Imam is not manifest, we will call it *fikr* (contemplation). This... darkness and light... it is like that. Now, the first prayer which was made obligatory on us, in the world of Islam, the first time the Prophet prayed was the *Zohr* prayer. He prayed the *Zohr* prayer for the first time... So *Zohr* has four *rak'at*s. There are four *rak'at*s of *Zohr*, and on the Prophet... Muhammad... Muhammad has four letters. On the four letters, Mim, Ha, Mim, Dal, on that the four *rak'at*s are a proof. It is a proof. I am telling you the *ta'wil* (esoteric interpretation). The reality is much deeper. It cannot be understood. But this *ta'wil* is a middle, a bridge, which we... to reach the reality, we use this. This is... those four letters of Muhammad, it is a proof on that. And what did the Prophet do? The first prayer he prayed was the *Zohr* prayer in the world of Islam. And the sun of the Prophet, when it rose, it shone upon the entire world. In the whole world, it was proclaimed that such a person has been born in Arabia, whose glory is very great, and everywhere... even the emperor of Rome was trembling. Iran, and other places, even in Andalusia... the embassies and all the emperors of that time, they were all surprised that who has been born in Arabia. So when the sun of prophethood shone... in the same way, it was shining at that time, as the sun shines at the time of noon. At noon, when it moves a little from the meridian, then our time for *Zohr* begins. This is the time when the sun is shining brightly, so that is the time of light, and that is our *Zohr* prayer. Now, what is the real meaning of prayer, I will tell you after this. See, prayer is... first I will... prayer that we perform, that is... as I told you, that we... on the command of Allah... we perform two, four, four *rak'at*s. But we... what reward do we get? What is the thing that is received as a reward? The reward is this, that at those times... at those times, because it is written everywhere, it probably comes at the time of *Maghrib* prayer... *kitaban mawquta* (prayer at fixed times). That this is... the prayer is a *salat al-mawqudah*, it comes that it is a fixed prayer. It should be prayed at this very time. If you pray in the evening, it becomes invalid. So, at the times they pray, in the world, at the time we are bowing and prostrating, the surface of the world, *falak-e-muhit*... on the *falak-e-muhit*, there are such issuing gates. There are... openings, windows. From the spiritual world, from where... There, from there, *suwarat* (spiritual forms) from the spiritual world descend at that time when our prayers are. So remember that the times are always greater than the prayer. The times of prayer are greater than the prayer itself. Remember this. Because prayer comes from our side, and the times come from Allah's side. So from above, at the time when these issuing gates, meaning the streams of reward, or the blessings that are in them, these things descend, meaning *suwarat* descend. When *suwarat* descend, at that time in the world, it is its time. Today, our watches have been made, everything is fixed. In those days, what was it? They would put a stick and see if the sun had passed the zenith or not, all these things had to be seen. Now everyone knows when the time of *Zohr* is and how much it is changing. So whenever from above, the time of its descent happened, that time became our *Zohr* time. Our *Zohr* time is not connected with it, rather we are subject to it, from above. So this is... they open at the time when our *Zohr* time is. And... this is also a matter, that ordinary Muslims pray five times, and we pray three times. What is the reason for this? That we combine *Zohr* and *Asr*, and we combine *Maghrib* and *Isha*. Why is it like this? They should be prayed separately. So we pray this for the sake of necessity, and the second thing is that the gate that opens for *Zohr*, it remains open for two and a half hours. The *suwarat* descend. Meaning, if at 12 o'clock, for example, it is the time of *zawal*, then until 2:30, the time for *Zohr* is there. And the time for *Asr* begins from 1 o'clock. So in its shadow, the gate for *Asr* opens. And it remains until when? Until 5 o'clock. Meaning, five o'clock means one and a half hours before *Maghrib*, or one hour before. When the sun, its entire disc is finished, it turns yellow. When it turns yellow, then the time for *Asr* is finished. You should pray before that. So we can pray like that too. There is no restriction for us that you pray *Zohr* and then leave, and at 2:30 or 3 o'clock you pray, there is no difference. It is such that when one comes to the mosque, at the time of congregational prayer, we pray them combined. So, what it means is that at the last time of *Zohr*, the time for *Asr* begins, so we pray them combined. And the same is for *Maghrib*. But what is with *Maghrib*? Among all the prayers, it has a very short time. It should be finished in 15 to 20 minutes. That is why we get up after praying the *sunnah*, because the *tatawwu'* (voluntary prayer) is not there for *Maghrib*. It is not written anywhere in the *sahifah* that there is a *tatawwu'* for *Maghrib*. We can pray it later. The *sunnah* should be prayed with the *fardh* (obligatory prayer). Otherwise, if you go to drink tea, it will be late. So the time for *Maghrib* is 15 to 20 minutes. And *Isha*... that is *Isha-e-Akhirah* (the final night prayer). When the night becomes dark, then the time for *Isha* begins, and it lasts until 12 o'clock. Now look at its *mansulat* (attributions). And when is *Fajr*? At *sahari* (pre-dawn meal time). After *sahari*, its time begins, and it ends before the sun rises. So, this is... in the *mansulat*, I told you for *Zohr* that it is *mansul* (attributed) to the Prophet, the *Zohr* prayer. Because the sun of the world... the sun of the world, as it shines, in the same way, the sun of prophethood was also shining at that time when this prayer was made obligatory. Similarly, there is the *Asr* prayer. The *Asr* prayer comes after *Zohr*. And in the same way, after the Prophet, Janab-e-Qaim's arrival is there. Janab-e-Qaim, who is to come, he is the *mansul* of our *Asr* prayer. And the *Asr* prayer is what? *Asr* means... *'asir* means juice. The essence of something, a sherbet. So the essence of something is called *ras* (juice), or if you say sherbet, and in Arabic, it is called *'asir*. From *'asir*, *asr* is derived. *Asr* is called the era, and it is also called the essence. So the essence of the world, the essence of the entire world is the person of Janab-e-Qaim, so *asr* is *mansul* to him. And *Asr* has four letters, in the same way as *Qaim* has four letters. And just as after Janab-e-Qaim, no new *shari'ah* will come, when Janab-e-Qaim *'alayhi al-salam* comes, then prayer and all these things will be finished. And after that, the *dawr al-kashf* (period of unveiling) will begin. Just as the prayer is lifted, in the same way, after the *Asr* prayer, there is no command to pray. You put your hand on your head and recite the *du'a*, after that, there is no *du'a* to recite, and the prayer is finished. Then at the time of *Maghrib*, you have to pray. This is Janab... this is the *Zohr* prayer and the *Asr* prayer. Now after this, see that after the *Asr* prayer... meaning after the light, suddenly the darkness of the night does not come. Rather, the evening comes first. Which we call twilight, or when it gets dim, we call it evening. That the sunlight has finished and now the sunset is happening. At that time, we are commanded to pray the *Maghrib* prayer. So this is the time when Janab-e-Paygambar's eye was closing, Mawla 'Ali's time was coming. So at that time, this Janab-e-'Ali *salawatullah 'alayh* is in the place of *Maghrib*. And *Maghrib* has three *rak'at*s, just as 'Ali has three letters. And now, let me also add this, if you remember, that the four *rak'at*s of *Zohr*, what are its *mansulat*? The entire four *rak'at*s are on the Prophet. And the *Zohr* prayer is also *mansul* to the Prophet. But if we individually dissect it, then the first *rak'ah*, second *rak'ah*, third *rak'ah*, fourth *rak'ah*, what are these? So the first *rak'ah* and the second *rak'ah* in which we recite two *surah*s, that is on Janab-e-Paygambar and his successor. The first *rak'ah* is on him, the second is on the successor. And the third and fourth are on both of their *Bab*s. This is the custom. And similarly, *Asr* is on Janab-e-Qaim and his successor, and both of their *Bab*s are in the third and fourth *rak'at*s. Now, Janab-e-'Ali *salawatullah 'alayh*'s... the *Maghrib* prayer is *mansul* to him. So Janab-e-'Ali and his successor are the first and second *rak'at*s. And the third *rak'ah*, a single *rak'ah* is for both of their *Bab*s. It has been kept. This is the special glory of *Maghrib*. And its gates, which are there, open for a short time, so 15 to 20 minutes are kept for it. It is called *manfas*. These are issuing gates, from above, from *'alam al-arwah* they come out. And when they emanate *suwarat* (spiritual forms) upon us, our prayer becomes a prayer. If someone sees, then our prayer is considered a prayer. Meaning, the *suwarat* from *'alam al-arwah*, which are in an abstract form, they cast their gaze upon us. That is why we... as it is written in *da'a'im*, and in the *sahifah*, that even if you are in the jungle, you should call the *adhan*. It is written that the angels are all present. So what does it mean? It doesn't mean the angels have wings. Those *suwarat* descend at this time. And from this, our prayer becomes a prayer. This is all a matter of secrets, but it is also a matter to be understood, that how this emanation of *suwarat* happens. And especially, whose name we take, meaning that Mawlana Fatimah is *mansul* to *Shab-e-Qadr*. Now, who is the 21st for? Who is the 23rd for? And who is the 17th for? Who is the 19th for? Who is *Laylat al-Milad* (the night of the birth) for? Every single one has a *mansul*. I, as the night comes, on that day, I will narrate it. Now after this, this *Isha-e-Akhirah*. After *Maghrib*, when the period of Janab-e-'Ali passed, and how much did it pass? A very short period. Three caliphates passed for 30 years. And after that, Janab-e-'Ali had to become the caliph in the end, so his caliphate was very short. It is just like the period of *Maghrib* is short. And after that, it went on, and evening came. Meaning, in Islam, an evening and a darkness started to come. As it went on, it happened that now the time for *Isha* began. Now, just as *Isha* is a deep night, in the same way, when in the world, the sun has completely set. Because at the time of *Maghrib*, even if the sun has set, there is still a little bit of light. Even though the sun has set, there is still light. But at the time of *Isha*, that twilight also ends, the redness ends. After that, there is the command to pray. And this is what happens, that we pray *Isha-e-Akhirah* in the complete darkness of the night. This darkness is what? That after Mawlana Tayyib *salawatullah 'alayh*, all the Imams went into complete concealment. Not a single one was known, where they are, what they are, except for the *du'at*. So that era, which is the period of *satr*, from Mawlana Tayyib until Janab-e-Hujjat, the whole night that we are passing through, how many? Where are we passing through? This is the 21st, and today is the 48th. This long period that has passed... this is not one *mansul*, there are many *mansulat*. So the Imam of the time of every era, on him, the *Isha-e-Akhirah* is *mansul*. If you were born 100 years ago, the Imam of that time was the *mansul*. Today, in whichever era we are, our Imam is the *mansul*. This is what? The *Isha-e-Akhirah*. And this period is long for this reason, that from Janab-e-Tayyib until here, it is a complete dark night. Now when this *Isha-e-Akhirah* ends, as it goes on, at 2 o'clock, 3 o'clock, 4 o'clock, now the time of twilight came and the *Fajr* prayer is near. So this time of twilight is... Hazrat Dai Saheb and the *mansus* before him have stated that the time of twilight has also ended. Meaning, we have passed *Isha-e-Akhirah*, rather, according to the demands of the time, the arrival of the *Qaim* is so near, the period of *qiyamah* is so near, that we have also finished the stage of twilight. When did this happen? That Sayyidna Wafi Ahmad, and Mawlana Zuhayr ibn Musa, and Ibrahim Hamidi, these who passed, they are the *mansul* of that period. And after that, as time went on, when the time for the *Fajr* *adhan* will come, that will be the time when Janab-e-Mahdi will arrive. Now this is the time of light. Just as it was the Prophet's time, this is M-H-D, this is also M-H-D. That is Muhammad, this is Mahdi. So when the period of Muhammad *sallallahu 'alayh* ended, now Janab-e-Mahdi's period will be such that in the world, there will be such a proclamation that no one in the world can equal him. And it will be such that, like suddenly, the dawn spreads. It has been said, I, in the last *sabaq*s, about Janab-e-Mahdi and Janab-e-Qaim, and how the field of *qiyamah* will be, what it is, all the details will come in the last *sabaq*s. Janab-e-Mahdi's period will be such a commotion in the whole world, and what will happen? That the light will be at random. It will be at once. It will be sudden, it will be unexpected. So for that, in the Quran Shareef, a verse has come: *baghtatan* (suddenly). For the *qiyamah* (resurrection), two signs have been told. One is that it will be *baghtatan*, and one will be *yawm-e-ma'lum* (a known day). The one that will be *baghtatan* is the arrival of Janab-e-Mahdi. And *yawm-e-ma'lum* is the *qiyamah*, meaning the arrival of Janab-e-Qaim *salawatullah 'alayh*. So the *qiyamah* when Janab-e-Qaim will come, all its things are written. They exist. But when Janab-e-Mahdi will come, no one knows. His arrival is *baghtatan*, it will be completely at random. So how will he come at random? For that, there must be a resemblance. And I am telling you from the beginning that *as-salatu mi'raj al-mu'min, 'ala mithal al-khilqah* (Prayer is the ascension of the believer, in the likeness of creation). The creation of religion is on the likeness of creation. And what is its likeness? That it is... there, when in *Fajr*, you stand on the terrace, when at the time of *Fajr*, there is talk of the sun rising, suddenly there will be light. As you watch, the whole thing will spread. You can observe it. In the same way, Janab-e-Mahdi *salawatullah 'alayh*... in the whole world, through television, everyone will know that someone has been born. And he has come like this. So today, for us, television etc. are providing this facility, that everything will be known. A new file is opening, a new one is closing. So we are doing this. We are creating relationships, we are making them less, we are increasing them. So increasing means that you close ten files, so you open twenty new files. It is going on. This is going on in the world of rebirth. We are coming as humans, we are coming as *mu'mins*. We are taking the oath. We are becoming *mansub*, *dai*, *hujjat*, up to the *bab*. But with that, the accounts are also opening. And if we don't remain with them, then we are not even born here. We are born in the heavens. And in the heavens, there are *du'at*. In the heavens also there are *du'at*. But such *du'at* who do not have *kisass*. And they are called *hujjat-e-layl*. And they are of a high rank. But here, they have come. So it is not that the *du'at* here, the *ma'adhin* here are of a low rank. Their rank is higher than there. Some are also such that our... the *hudud* in our group, they are of a higher rank. But they have *kisass*. They have *kisass*. What can be done? They are human. And this cycle is going on, it's going on. Whenever the *qiyamah* comes, the small *qiyamah* is separate, the big *qiyamah* is separate. I have told you that the *qiyamah* of *satr* is separate, of *kashf* is separate, the *qiyamah* of the period of *kashf* and *satr* combined is separate, then the *qiyamah* of the period is separate, then after that, the *qiyamah* of death. And with the *qiyamah* of death, the entire account will be settled. That how many are in the *barzakh*, as they are progressing, the small sphere we say that a *mu'min* progresses, where does he go? The sphere of *jadd* became his, it's over. That's one life. Now he will progress from there, he will go to another sphere, one plus one will happen. There, up to the *Bab*, everyone will gather. And one will become a *barzakh-e-'ali*, for example, the *Bab* of the time of the Imam. From there, to the Imam's presence. Now such Imams, how many have there been in 4 lakh years? The points have changed. So each one has such a large store. So after every seven, then after seven more, then the 7000-year period of *satr*. Then the 57000-year period. In this way, gathering, it becomes one *kawn-e-a'zam*, whose duration is what? It is 16000 crore years. 4 lakh *dawr*s... 4 lakh multiplied by 4 lakh. One... one *dawr* is of 4 lakh years, so 4 lakh such *dawr*s are placed, so that becomes one *kawn-e-a'zam*. One *kawn-e-a'zam*'s duration is 16000 crore. Such big, big... huge structures exist. They are structures. Where are they? Allah and His Prophet know. These nebulae that are there, this entire space that is so vast, this universe we are seeing, and Allah is what? *Rabb al-'alamin* (Lord of the worlds). It is said *al-hamdu lillahi rabb al-'alamin*. This universe is not just one, there are hundreds of such universes roaming around. The universe is separate, we are talking about our world. The universe is very big. There are waiting rooms. Which in Arabic we call *barazikh*, or *barzakh*. They go and stay in one place. Such are *sawa'id* that come and fill it. Then there are *qawa'im*. A *qaim* is, from the point of view of the Imams, he has a partial authority. The Imam is a complete authority. From our point of view, the Imam is a complete authority. But from the point of view of the *qaim*, he is a partial authority. Such are *qawa'im* that when they come into being, they become a partial authority for them. And in the end, when death comes to everyone, then the biggest of them all comes. And that discussion will come, that how in the end, it will be, how the end of death will be, there is a whole... a book has been filled, that how... He is the master of the time. It is a very long duration. We cannot even calculate it. Neither the calculator can do it, nor... on the computer, on the IBM, when they did it on the computer, then the calculation came. That one death's duration... I mean, put 25 zeros after it. That is what we have on the television screen... it doesn't come. On the television screen, it is... and that you... I have calculated it 14-15 years ago. When the new... the IBM had come. This earth which... in which everything is progressing, in the same way, the moon, sun and other planets, is there some similar concept of progress there too? No. Only on Earth. So just as some people went to the moon and from there that soil and that... some things were also brought here. So they have brought them, but the things for which the account is there, from above, something has to come down, it will come, it is by the power of Allah. But it is not that any human lives there or anything. It is only on Earth that it has been kept. And from here itself, they will sprout, from here itself they will grow. So the progress is on the moon too. So the progress is on the moon too. The moon is what? The moon is a big store of the *nafsiyyin*. It is of the *nafsiyyin*. And those things are coming down and... as I have told you that the moon and the sun are two big factories. And they are not doing just one job, like giving light, it's not like that. Rather, they are doing many other things. The moon and the sun, or say every planet has three parts. Three. On a chart you have seen, in science books you will read, that there are three parts. One is the outer surface, which we see. And inside it, there are its subtleties. And inside the subtleties, there is one... the center point, that is the actual seed-world. From where the work happens. And here, as science also says, that there is a center core, and around it, there is helium gas, or say the... the gases that fill it. And the thing around it, the surface, that is called *satah* (surface), or *madar-bandh* (orbit-bound). And that is the crust, which we see. And how was it made? I have told you before this, that in the beginning, a cycle of ice happened from above. When the *falak al-muhit* spun, and inside it, all the small ones started spinning, so the first light that came from above, of every sphere... because they were also *mawjud*. They were *mawjud*. So these spheres are very special parts of the *nafsiyyin*. They were so good, not like ours, that they could not come into the world of density. They were not visible, they were like a complete fog. So that light, throwing it from above, after throwing it, it struck here... the surface of the earth. After striking, it rebounded. It bounced from here. It went up so fast that what it had to take from the earth, the dense things, taking them from here, it went straight up. And going there, a circle was formed of it. And that became the *satah* (surface). It became that. If that was not formed, neither the moon would be visible, nor the sun would be visible. Absolutely... then a second time, the *du'at* say that then another time the light was thrown. And the light was thrown again, so its power was less. And it went and... these spheres which are there, of fire, water, air and earth, it reached here and the spheres were formed. It could not reach above. The Bermuda Triangle... The soil that he brought... what are its... So those are... The soil he brought, that... he said this much that he brought it from the moon. Now he has brought it or not, it is his secret. But if he has brought it, then on the moon... it is...

The knowledge of who the *Hajj ‘Ali* is, is not known to anyone. This is a special arrangement from Allah, so that it is not known to anyone who his *Hajj ‘Ali* is. Otherwise, what would happen? One would sit at their feet, saying, "You are everything," "I will not leave you." And such incidents have also occurred in the past, among the *salaf*, that, well, regarding the *Hajj ‘Ali*, no one has any knowledge. They are not told, nor is it revealed. And what happens? We, the *jazira* that we belong to in our *‘aqidah*, the *jazira* we are in, or the three *jaziras* whose *maliks* they are, all those many, many *jaziras*, their *Hajj ‘Ali* is the same one. For this reason, their *ta‘zim* (respect) is necessary upon us. Otherwise, we are not bound to show *ta‘zim* to anyone, because the *Hajj ‘Ali* is not known. Now, look, in this… [Audience member asks a question, inaudible] ...then we don't know who the *Hajj ‘Ali* is… So, it's not like that. We have been told, the *Wali Amr* has told us that these are the senior ones, after them are these senior ones, and after them are these. We are to follow (*ittiba'*) that order, that's it. The *Hajj ‘Ali* is not known. It's possible that the *Hajj ‘Ali* is sitting in Najran. It's possible that the *Hajj ‘Ali* is sitting in Sindh. They can be anywhere. Only the Imam has this *khabar* (knowledge). And if he wishes to inform, then the *da‘i* can have this *khabar*. And for this reason, the *rutbas* (ranks) are changed, they are replaced. Anyway, the point is that regarding this concept of *Hajj ‘Ali*, I want to narrate an incident. The three *da‘is* that we are studying in history, one of whom is Sayyidna Qadi al-Nu'man, who, along with Maulana Mu‘izz, three or four, you served during the time of the Imams. You were the *Qadi al-Qudat* (Chief of Judges), the Chief Justice of your time, the greatest *qadi* you are considered to be. And in your *nasl* (lineage) too, there have been three or four *qadis*, who have been *Qadi al-Qudat*. Your status is very high. Our, that is, the special books of our *deen* (religion), *Da‘a’im al-Islam*, *Ta’wil al-Da‘a’im*, *Mukhtasar al-Athar*, and this *Asas al-Ta’wil*, all the *fundamentals* books of the *shari‘ah* were written by Sayyidna Qadi al-Nu'man. And his status is so high that during the time of Maulana Mu‘izz *salawatullahi ‘alayh*, when you saw, Maulana Mu‘izz, that the influence of the Maliki, Shafi‘i, Hanbali, and Hanafi schools of thought was growing a lot, at that time he said, "O Nu'man, you too should codify our *shari‘ah*."

Now, that's a special rank. Maulana Mu‘izz's rank was special, he was the seventh *da‘i*, and he held a *natiq*-like status, which is why he said this. Well, that's a separate matter, that he gave the order, and Sayyidna Qadi al-Nu'man began to write. After writing it, when he brought it, at that time he was told, "I have brought this book, please look at it." And he saw the book, and on it, he gave a certificate that this achievement of the *qadi*, this achievement of the *qadi*, this *Da‘a’im al-Islam* that he has written, is greater than all the deeds of the *ummah* (community) until the Day of Judgment. My *ummah*, that is, the *mu’minin* (believers), all the achievements of the *mu’minin*, all their deeds, as many as there will be until the Day of Judgment, this one achievement of the *qadi* is greater than all of them. In terms of greatness. What does this mean? That is, by reading *Da‘a’im al-Islam*, we are performing deeds. Whatever deeds we are doing, we are reading *Da‘a’im al-Islam*. Anyway, the point is that a certificate was given to you, that the deeds that will be done until the Day of Judgment, this is greater than them. Now, this Qadi al-Nu'man, whom we can call *Rasulullah* (Messenger of Allah) — in what way *Rasulullah*? That he is the messenger of Allah's proof, Maulana Mu‘izz *salawatullahi ‘alayh*. You are studying not just the *shari‘ah* but other books as well, from which it is known where the word *Rasulullah* is used. So, he was a very great personality, that Qadi al-Nu'man *salawatullahi ‘alayh*. What happened? At one time, you used to live in Qahira (Cairo). In Cairo, you fell ill. Sayyidna Qadi al-Nu'man became sick. And he was the *Qadi al-Qudat*, the Chief Justice. Now, at that time, the government was of Maulana Mu‘izz. So all the prominent people, ministers, and others, all the people came to inquire about the health of Sayyidna Qadi al-Nu'man, that the Qadi has fallen ill. All the great, prominent figures came. Now, when he got well, the period of illness was over, he came to the Imam. The Imam asked, "How is your health? What's the matter?" He inquired about his well-being. And after that, he said, "O Qadi, who all came to your side to inquire about your health?" "Who all came, the prominent ones?" So he said that so-and-so came, so-and-so minister came, so-and-so great person came. He named everyone. He said, "Everyone came, *illa Ja‘far*" (except for Ja‘far). "Except for Ja‘far, everyone came." And the Imam is raising his inner state through his speech. The Imam is the one who can access it, to see what is in their minds. Just as Maulana 'Ali has said, that he sees up to seven generations if there is a *mu’min*, so was the power of Maulana Mu‘izz. When he asked who all came, he said, "Except for Ja‘far, everyone came." He said, "Alright." And after that, he sat for a while, took out a book, and gave it to Sayyidna Qadi al-Nu'man. Now, Qadi al-Nu'man began to look. He was a scholar. He looked and started praising it, "Maulana, this is *Kalam al-muluk, muluk al-kalam* (The speech of kings is the king of speech). What can I say about your words? It contains the best of the best things." And he began to praise it greatly. When he praised it too much, he took it from his hand, and he said, "*Haza min maulak Ja‘far*" (This is from your master, Ja‘far). "This is written by your master, written by Ja‘far."

At that moment, he was shocked. "*Haza min maulak Ja‘far*" (This is from your master, Ja‘far). At that very moment, he fell at his feet, Sayyidna Qadi al-Nu'man. He understood. He was made to have the *ma‘rifat* (gnosis) of the *Hajj ‘Ali*. That if someone is greater than me, it is him. He had the rank of a *Bab al-Abwab*, Ja‘far. Ja‘far bin Mansur al-Yaman, who, from Qahira, turned the *Dawat* and turned it in Yemen. So he, Ja‘far bin Mansur al-Yaman, was a very high-ranking person. Though in the government, he was made a *qadi*, and these were senior, and they did great work in the apparent *Dawat*. But in the esoteric *Dawat*, the one who was the chief was Sayyidna Ja‘far, Ja‘far bin Mansur. He said, "*Haza min maulak Ja‘far*." At that very moment, he fell at his feet, asked for forgiveness, that he had made a mistake. And the *qadi* got up right away and kept searching in the streets of Qahira. And he found out where Ja‘far bin Mansur al-Yaman lives. He found out in the streets that he lives in such-and-such a house. He went at night and knocked. As it happened, he was there. He knocked. From inside, an old man came out, Ja‘far bin Mansur al-Yaman. He was old. He asked, "Who has come?" He said, "The *qadi* has come." And as soon as he met him, he fell at his feet and asked for forgiveness for the mistake he had made. So this, I have to tell you, is how the mistake against a *Hajj ‘Ali* is forgiven. So for us, we haven't been told who the *Hajj ‘Ali* is, but a hierarchy of ranks has been established, where the Imam makes the *da‘i*, the *da‘i* makes the *ma’dhun*, the *ma’dhun* makes the one below him. So our job is that as far as we have to follow, we should follow. *Wa akhiru da'wana an al-hamdu lillahi rabb il-'alamin, wa salatu was-salamu 'ala rasulih il-karim. Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim...* [Arabic prayer]... *Al-Fatihah*.
