So anyway, I have explained a sequence, that just as we understand that all these things exist, in the same way, other people also inhabit the world. Brother, now you have explained all these things of principle. But what will be the fate (*hashr*) of these people? How will that be? I will finish in ten minutes. That those who are *ghair-e-haqq* (not on the path of truth), what will happen to them? So you see, I have already told you that whoever has not taken the covenant (*ahd*), we will call them *ghair-e-haqq*. Whether they are Muslim, Dawoodi, or anyone else. They just haven't taken the covenant. They are outside of this circle of ours. As for them, their creed (*aqidah*), some of them have a slightly better one, while some are completely finished. Like today in Karachi, what kinds of people there are. The Shias' punishment (*azab*) is better... all are different, but from our perspective, all are wrong. Wrong. So if they are wrong, they will also receive punishment accordingly. Today, look, we believe that greater than one's mother and father are the parents, the brother, they believe in the Imam, they believe in the Imam, there is a whole dynasty of them. And the greatest Imam is Janab-e-Ali. After the Prophet. Now, there are many others with ranks greater than him. If you want to understand in the realm of *haqaiq* (realities), you will have to contemplate much more. But these things that are there... now, a *da'wat-e-haqq* (call to truth) is also running, and a *da'wat-e-zalal* (call to error) is also running. There is a call that misguides. For example, as we understand, it is that of the Dawoodis. Perhaps their people number in the thousands, but they are wrongly misguiding people. So is this *da'wah* of ours correct or not? You think with your own intellect (*aql*). So those who are wrong, it is necessary for them to receive punishment. Here, if the court (*adalat*) does not give punishment, that is a different matter. But His court is greater than all. There, punishment must be given. So after *inteqal* (passing away), meaning after dying, remember this, that we are transferred (*muntaqil*). We go to someone who is higher than us. That is why it is said, we are being transferred (*muntaqil*), meaning *inteqal* is happening. But not every person who is undergoing *inteqal* is dying or being finished. He dies, meaning it is his ruin. He is being corrupted. So how does he go? He is given punishment. So the system (*nizam*) of Allah Ta'ala is that the punishments, He does not just throw them down all at once from above. Rather, gradually, He takes him down in descending order. He will be removed from human faculties (*insani khawas*), then he will emerge from the animal [realm], then he will emerge from the vegetable (*nabat*) [realm], then he will emerge from the mineral (*ma'dan*) [realm]. So now look, those people who are other than us, wherever they may pass away, no matter where they are from. The first level (*darka*), it is called a *darka*. There are ten more minutes. The first *darka* is that of humanity. Sudanese, Somalis, Ethiopians, all these people who are black, they are all from there. They will be put into that very [level]. Although they have human faculties. I have told you that he goes down gradually, he doesn't go down all at once. So now they have been locked (*qofal*), a lock has been put, that now they are not going to turn back and come again. They are going to fall down. Now when their *darka*—that is, when that finishes... How many *darkat* are there? This is seven in number. Seven. From man down to mineral. Seven. Within every seven there are 70 *qamis* (forms). 70 *qamis* means, shape. If I wear this, it is different. If I wear pants and a shirt, I will look different. And if I wear a *doongi*, I will look different. These are all different shapes.

...meaning there are 70 levels, and in 70 centuries, there are 70 links. Meaning, if they come as a moth it's separate, if they come as a pigeon it's separate, if they come as an animal, a fox, it's separate. These are all separate shapes. So the first level is that of humanity. The second level is that of the sloth bear, bear, and chimpanzee. As many monkeys as there are, all are in that... The third level is of the beast. The fourth is that of reptiles. As many reptiles... The fifth is birds. Birds. So the fifth level, you see, birds, we think they are good. They are worse than beasts. In descending order, it is the fifth level. The sixth is that of vegetation, plants. And the sixth level, the final level, which is the seventh, is minerals. This sulphur, etcetera, these things, petroleum, etcetera. What is this thing? They are all for punishments, in *zakat*. So this whole system, these people reach up to the seventh level. After going up to the seventh level, then for them, if the punishment is over... Because the sentence, just as they announce in the High Court that for so many days, six months, they must be kept. After six months, a pardon is necessary. Then their... coming and telling them to do *tawba* (repentance), now finish it, from now on we won't steal. So similarly, Allah Ta'ala brings them. Some are brought after three levels, some are brought after four, some after seven. The one who went up to the seventh level, for him, one more punishment is designated. And that is the punishment of the North Pole and South Pole. This is why today you say that in America, sir, whether it's this stone or gold, these regions of the North Pole and South Pole are bad regions. These are regions of cold. There, a part of *jahannam* (hell), you could say, has been kept. There is an intermediate section. The final punishment, and the lesser punishment, the punishment in between them is the North Pole and South Pole. The penguins at the North Pole and South Pole, the sea horse, the whales, all of these are in punishments. All are in punishments. You see, the sea horse, when it is at the freezing point, if it opens its mouth, it cannot close it. If it were given a tongue, it would say, "For six months I have kept it open like this." I cannot close it because it is so cold. So these are punishments. And after that, this punishment also lasts for 5,000, 10,000, 20,000 years. Because I just told you the duration, that after 10 comes 1,000, after 1,000... God knows where the birth of the time of the pool is. When this punishment of the peripheries is over, then even after that, if someone's term remains, that the punishment is still pending, then they are given the punishment of stone. And this is the final punishment, and it is a third-degree punishment. With us, what happens? First, a thief is not put in jail. First, they are kept in custody, after that, they are put in a lock-up. Then tomorrow, there will be a court appearance. There is a hearing. You will pass that hearing, you were an accused until now, now you have become a convict. Then you will be given the punishment. It is the same with this, that now, that time comes when the entire periphery is completely finished, and now, after that, the man will come who is to give the decision. And everyone is waiting for him, his name is Qa'im. Qa'im Alayhissalam will come, and he, he is a... He is the one who will fix the court. And the grand proceedings will start. As soon as Janab-e Qa'im comes, before that—now, Qa'im is such a high-ranking official of Allah, before him, many people will come. Suppose Manmohan Singh has come here, and he is going to give a speech here. Then before him, 10 very big people will come. [unclear] will come, then after him, this one will come, that one will come.

When the Chief Justice comes, then the Prime Minister comes. So, in the same way, we have great *awliya'* who are coming in the final era. And when *Janaab-e Qa'im* comes, on that day, what will happen is that punishments will be given in full. And the final punishment will be meted out. And where will that happen? In the plain of Mina. Yes, the plain of Mina, there, there it will happen. When *Janaab-e Qa'im* comes... where does he emerge from? From a village. Before that, *Janaab-e Mehdi* will come. I am not describing that in detail, I am just establishing the point. *Mehdi 'alayhi as-salam* will come. And he is the paternal cousin of *Mehdi 'alayhi as-salam*. Just as the *Paygambar* and *Janaab-e 'Ali* were, in the same way, *Mehdi* and *Qa'im* are. They are cousins. *Mehdi* means, it is an ascending order of that same *Paygambar*. He has come. And *Janaab-e Qa'im* is in the line of *Janaab-e 'Ali*. So when *Janaab-e Qa'im* comes, where will he come from? There is an area in Yemen. From there he will emerge and go straight to Madinah. From Madinah, he will then go to Makkah. Arriving in Madinah, he will visit the grave of *Janaab-e Paygambar* there. Because these are his ancestors. They are all there. He will perform *ziyarat* there. After performing *ziyarat*... Look, you're not getting bored, are you? The discussion is long... these are the very last things, which are very special things. You go and perform *ziyarat* in Madinah. The *Paygambar's* grave is called the Dome of *daan-e sakina*. Next to it is Abu Bakr, and over there is 'Umar. You don't accept this. And they are wrong. Those who corrupted Islam... the internal corruptions in the religion are many. We don't even speak of those things. But the apparent corruptions are that the position that was *Janaab-e 'Ali's* was not given to him. Things that should not have been done were done. So, both of them are next to the *Paygambar*. Why are they there? If you are so close to the religion, then how can these two corruptions be there? This... this is the point. So, look. Just as there is the star Mushtari... have you heard of Mushtari? Jupiter. Jupiter is the most auspicious star. Before it is Saturn. And after it, over here, is Mars. Mars... it is between Saturn. In the same way, the *Paygambar* is flanked by one who is Mars and one who is... Now, I am just giving a simile. If I explain the other thing, then I will have to explain many things about what happens there. Anyway. So, he will come... *Janaab-e Qa'im* will come, and after arriving, he will offer *salam* there, just as we offer when we go for *'umrah*. After offering *salam*, he will order, "Open this grave." As soon as it is opened for him... and he is the one who will pass judgment on the entire world. At that time, both of them will emerge, alive. It is stated. Those who are there will see it. Our age will not reach it, you people will see it. That they will be brought out alive. And they will be crucified. The gallows will be erected. And then from there, he will come... he will come here. Where? To the plain of Mina. First, they will come to Makkah, perform *tawaf*, recite the required *du'as*, and do that. The entire caravan with him... how many men will be with him, who they will be, all of this has been written down in the books. There will be 313 men with him. Three hundred and thirteen men. He will be the 314th. He will emerge from there and go to Mina. How far is Mina? Four kilometers from Makkah. Four kilometers. They will go there. And...

Asghar, Manhar. Manhar is where the zabihat (ritual slaughter) is done, the qurbani (sacrifice) is done. We sacrifice goats, and we sacrifice cows. We also sacrifice camels and... cows. There, I myself have gone many times, for 30-35 years I have been going. At that time, earlier there were small, small gates. Now that the Saudi government has received money, they have made such huge gates. This is Bab al-Ghanam (Gate of the Goats). Meaning, when you go inside, it is filled with goats. You have to sacrifice them... This is Bab al-Baqar (Gate of the Cows). A very large gate... and smaller... dawa'iz... This looks like the preparation for that time has started. The entire system has been established by Allah Ta'ala. When Sayyidna al-Qa'im goes with his qafila (caravan), he will go there... they will reach... and until that time, those who are to receive punishment, whether they are in Argentina, or in Canada, or in Venezuela, or, you can say, in Dubai, wherever they may be, they will be hypnotized, all of them will be brought. Where will they come? First they will come to Jeddah. From Jeddah, straight to Mina. Whoever is to be met. There are some very bad people, stubborn people. They will all come. And Sayyidna al-Qa'im... will give the order, "Slaughter them." So those, these big 'nots', the big ones, who are the big ones? Fir'awn (Pharaoh). Namrud (Nimrod). Habil... Qabil (Cain). And the big ones: Yazid, who killed Imam Husayn, or the one who killed Sayyidna Ali. These big ones, Qa'im alayhis salam himself will... nahr (slaughter) them, like a camel is killed. Then, the great du'at and anbiya (prophets) and such people will be there. They will be told, "You... you do it." And after that, the smaller people are... they will be slaughtered like goats. So all the people who are to receive punishment will receive it there. And this is a third-degree punishment. The rest of the people who have committed minor mistakes will be spared. Then their... will be taken away. Then the da'wat will be presented to them. If they accept, fine, if not, then... But this, this azab (punishment) is a very terrible azab. When they are cut, their blood will flow. I have already told you about the blood, the signs of Shaq and all that. Blood... blood will flow. The entire plain of Mina will be filled with corpses. At that time, Sayyidna al-Qa'im... you haven't understood the whole theory yet. As much as I can explain in... how many hours has it been? Two and a half hours. And... the part about ma'ad is still remaining, but this is for our... for the mo'min jama'at (community of believers) to understand. But now this is... however many corrupt people pass away... just as our ruh (spirit) departs—the ruh has different types—similarly, they have only one ruh, a corrupt one. Ruh al-Khabitha (the Vile Spirit). Whose? Those people, whether they are Hindu, or Muslim, or... who are corrupt. Theirs... the sun... sorry, the moon... from the surface of the moon, there are two invisible stars. Ras and Dhanab. Which are called Rahu and Ketu in the common language. Chehra TV... Ketu... Andhrim... in cinema they do it... so that is Rahu and Ketu. There are two. And the du'at say that it is in the form of a snake. It has a head and it has a tail. The tail is very corrupt. So the very, very corrupt people, their Surat al-Khabitha—Surat al-Khabitha means their invisible form, their ruh—is locked up there.

The *sar* is there, in which the foul odor is less. It is a completely peaceful place. And we cannot see it. If we could see it, it would destroy it. And Allah does not want to destroy it. That is why it is not visible. This is the state of their *Surat al-Fadilah*. When these corpses are created, then that *Surat al-Khabitha* will be given the command of *Qiyam* to come down. That *Surat al-Khabitha* will come in your form. It is said, in your form. Its entire shape has been given there, what its form will be. Coming down, they will burn their own bodies. So what will happen from the burning? All the corpses will burn up and the foul odor and all that will start. And right now the foul odor is less. As soon as this happens, Allah Rabb al-‘Alamin will command the water that, "Rain!" Water will rain, there will be rain. On top of the rain, these corpses that are there, if they were dry, it would be another matter. As soon as the water falls, the foul odor will start. The ultimate punishment. That entire field will be filled with foul odor. At that time, the winds will be commanded to remove this filth. Just as we... someone, a person takes it out or flushes it out, similarly the winds will take the entire debris and go to a place which is called Jahannam, *patal*. The *patal* which is below you is the *patal*. So the mouths that are formed for it, the *minawazi* is there. From there, it will go down. When the entire debris goes down, this is a third-degree punishment, which is called *‘azab-i akbar* (the greatest punishment). And the Du‘at say that we don't even like to describe it. We don't want to explain it. So they will go down. When they go down... as soon as they go down, by the power of Allah, they will again become people. But what kind of people will they become? Someone with four hands, ten heads. Just like today, idols are made for us... all such ugly forms will be there. Now, I look at you and I see one. But if I have four eyes, and you also have four, what will I see? That four are standing in front of me. So they will start hitting. They will hit me, and I will hit them. So it is stated there, the Du‘at say, that going down, there will be so much heat, don't even ask. And in it, they will be hitting each other. And I hit, the one in front was finished. He hit, this one was finished. As soon as they fall, they will stand up again. So for this it has come in the Qur’an Sharif, *la yamutu wa la yahya* (he will neither die nor live). They are neither alive nor dead. They will stand, they will hit, they will fall. So for how long will they fall, for how long will it go on? One *parardha* year. 16,000 crore years will be spent in this. This whole thing is going on below. Below the... below the earth, this will happen. The Qa'im, *alayhis-salam*, will come and settle the account. Now whether this Qa'im or the one after this Qa'im, whenever it happens, it is an accounting of an era. This is our system. But the system above this is that we who are *mu'min* (believers), who are good, will be in the TV, will be watching, that one after another they are being killed. Our... [unclear]... this body that we are carrying... that you, with your intellect, have understood this *mazhab* correctly or that correctly. But your body is also listening. It is also understanding. It is praying *namaz* with you, or bowing to someone, or giving *salam* to someone, or you are giving it *zakat*. So it is also obedient to you. It also has to get a reward.

Your spirit also has a paradise... so what is its reward? The reward of each one is its paradise. For this reason, when we... it ends further on, we say in paradise... may Allah grant paradise. We say 'in paradise' [singular]. But what comes out of the mouth sometimes? May Allah grant *jannat* (plural). *Jannat*. There are many paradises. So is *jannat* one, or one or ten? The meaning is that the paradise of your spirit is separate, the body's is separate, the rational soul's is separate; all these are categories. So that is how such a world is running. Many such things, after crossing over... came into the category of *du'at* (summoners). From *du'at* to Imam... from Imam to Imam... from Imam... up to seven Imams... it happens up to seven. The seventh Imam... the complete *da'wah* (mission) of the six... The details that were prepared with us regarding things reached up to the seventh Imam. So from seven, it became 49. Increasing like this, to the point where everything was left behind from this world. The meaning is that the story is this: we who have fallen from above, have come down as human... from here we have to go again. So may Allah Ta'ala give us such ability that according to humanity, according to the *shari'ah*, according to our *'amal* (action)... so *'ilm* (knowledge) and *'amal* (action), there are two things. You learned, but did not act. Neither prayed *namaz* nor this... so there is no benefit. Or you kept acting and you don't know anything, so for what reason are you doing it? So *'ilm* and *'amal* are two wings. So Hazrat Sadiq Sahab, our pride... [unclear]... he said that, in the wings... O Allah, he was a poet, give so much strength in the wings that we may reach the *nasheman* (nest). A *nasheman* is the nest of every bird. It roams the entire world, but at night it goes and sits in its *nasheman*. Give so much strength in the wings that we may reach the *nasheman*. Meaning, in our *'ilm* and *'amal*, give us such... uh... stability that we may reach there, to that *nasheman*. It has been a long time since the home was left behind. Because thousands, crores of years have passed since we were made human and sent from there. From here, we have to go again. When you go there, Allah Ta'ala has said that many things... *ya ma'shar al-jinn wal-ins* (O company of jinn and men)... more dangerous than *ins*... *ya ma'shar al-jinn*... it starts from here. So, O company of humans and jinn... *an tanfudhu min aqtari 's-samawati wal-ardh* (that you pass beyond the zones of the heavens and the earth). If you wish, you can exit beyond these heavens, meaning the sky and the earth, go above. You cannot reach... *illa bi-sultan* (except with authority). Except that you have some *sultan*. *Sultan* means king. What is the king? The Imam. There is one such Imam who can take everyone from anywhere to anywhere. So what are we doing right now? We are making progress... will fast too... doing so, we reached the Imam. From the Imam then to the greater Imam... to him, to the *Qayim* (the Risen One). The *Qayim* of the *Sidrah* (Lote Tree) is separate, of the *'Arsh* (Throne) is separate, of the *Kursi* (Footstool) is separate, of the *Lauh* (Tablet) is separate, of the *Qalam* (Pen) is separate. All of these, however many there are, are all making progress in their own places. You came from here to here. Suppose you came into the second [grade]. So it won't be that you are... uh... middle... middle school used to be when one passed the seventh [grade]. So this is a relative position that you are changing. But what will you call progress? What will you call the true paradise? That which goes from here to the sky. So, *ya ma'shar al-jinn wal-ins in istata'tum an tanfudhu min aqtari 's-samawati wal-ardh fanfudhu. La tanfudhun...* (O company of jinn and men, if you are able to pass beyond the zones of the heavens and the earth, then pass. You will not pass...). Hey, try and see. You cannot go. Except that your... So we have been told that even if you have the *sultan* of *qawr*, if you have passed in *qawr*, you have been seated in that very place. But you could not go there. Until the *qayim* of *mawr* comes. You know the duration of *mawr*. The master of *mawr*, he will take the entire *qalb* (heart/essence) from here and pierce the sky. Where will he go? Where he is... in a luminous form.

When one is left, there are two people, Muminji is here. The rest are coming. If the rest of the people had come, there would have been a good exploration. In one sitting, this much becomes... it's difficult. No, it's not difficult, is it? No, meaning for me there were some new things that... It's related to what came before. They will say what are the nine, what are the seven, what is the da'wah after that... Today's science also... everything... what I have written from a scientific perspective, as I will explain to you... for a week, it's like a single day... No, insha'Allah. Is there a CD? Yes, I have seen it on CD too, there are many things... but... You have to listen and also watch, audio-video. It's a good thing. We study one or eight subjects. Computer engineers also come. They know engineering, they only study mechanical. With us, it is that we study more subjects. After knowing these haqā'iq, there is an increase in [understanding of] every subject. We are studying. Now this, the increase is not scientific. It is due to knowing these haqā'iq. I'll give a small example. Before I go to the khutbah... there were two things I didn't do. I didn't celebrate birthdays either. And the second, from going on leave... after going, I would not turn back and praise anyone. This is the way of the English... that I have come here to Hyderabad... the heat is intense, there are mosquitoes, I am eating mangoes... they do this wrong, the ones who ask... Once I was talking with the staff, and they asked, "Why don't you celebrate birthdays?" Every staff member's birthday is celebrated... they celebrate colleagues' birthdays... you don't celebrate the birthday. But now I also have to give an answer as to why I don't celebrate it. The conversation started, and it ended this way... later... 'Do you celebrate a birthday, or do you celebrate your delivery date?' What does that mean? So, celebrating a birthday is very difficult for me. Which day should I call a birthday? What you are celebrating is the delivery date, the day you came out... For the birthday, now, scientifically that... yes, that one. I couldn't explain it to them, brother. They weren't getting convinced. It is that which... have been explained well, or understand that... they are doctors also. No, it's not like that. Science will have to accept all these things. Now look, one thing you... [unclear]... I'll give an example. You will have to accept everything I am saying. So with us, the example... I have also removed water, and... So with us there is samāwāt and arḍ (heavens and earth). In samāwāt is āsmān (sky). Āsmān and... We have sent down water from the āsmān. Below is the zamīn (earth). So from the sky to the earth, everyone knows this. What is the meaning of this coming in the honorable Qur'an? Its meaning is... āsmān... It also has a bāṭin (inner meaning). The sky, just as there are seven [skies], in the same way, there are seven Nāṭiqs. Adam, Nuh, Ibrahim, Musa, Isa, [unclear]. There are seven Nāṭiqs.

He makes the rain fall upon his earth, that is, upon the Janab-e-Wasi. Harun, in the same way that the matters of Musa's shadow come, Harun would bring it. So where did Harun get inspiration from? He would get it from Musa. Because he is receiving it from the prophet, Janab-e-'Ali. And from 'Ali, all of us are taking it, up to everyone. So these things, where is it being received from and where are we delivering it to? So this... so what is the earth? The existence of every imperfect thing is the earth.

Now you... I had reflected on it. It is written in it... it is written with us that everything has to return to its origin. *Kullu shay'in yarji'u ila aslihi* (Everything returns to its origin). It has to return to its origin. This is our... Now you, from this soil, for the listener, if I pick up one thing and throw it, wherever it is, it will go to the earth. Everything that goes will go towards the earth. Except for when you stop it like this... I'll throw this, it came here and stopped. It's not on the earth, is it? So this is, you are stopping it by force.

Meaning, against nature, you built a roof, and it came and fell on it. Otherwise, if the roof were removed a little, you would fall down and go towards the earth. So the point is that by force, today the era, everyone... now what is the earth?

It is the example of Hazrat 'Ali. You should remember this. Now, in the same way that there is Janab-e-'Ali and the earth. So within the earth, there is a special gravity. Force of... there is power. There is a force of gravity within the earth, which is pulling everything. So we also have it like that, that in 'Ali there is a special force that is pulling everyone towards him.

Now we are wandering by force. We are within our respective boundaries now. As soon as the boundaries end, we will go straight towards 'Ali. So the whole world has to come towards 'Ali.

And regarding this very thing, it has been told to us that a *maulana* went to study with Zain al-'Abidin, in connection with that matter... even before him. So he said, what is the meaning of this: *yaliju al-jamalu fi sammi al-khayati* (the camel entering the eye of the needle). That a camel passing through the eye of a needle. Explain this. So he couldn't explain it.

He was new. Then you explained that brother, its meaning is this: the camel is a large structure. And the eye of a needle is very small. This entire world is an example of the camel's structure. And the eye of the needle is our Ahl-e-Shari'at. That every single person, at some point or another, when its time comes, it will come and exit from there.

So now, from that perspective, from the perspective of the force of gravity, everything has to return towards 'Ali. *Kullu shay'in yarji'u ila aslihi* (Everything returns to its origin).

So this... now I have many examples of this...

You were surprised. It is written down, we can’t prove it now, but the proof will come. When it happens, you will see. You can see it. So, this is the kind of situation it is. Whatever is known, will come from khamir (leaven). For example, to make dahi (yogurt), a little khamir is added to the milk. The next day the whole pot becomes dahi. So, khamir... That khamir is the khamir of nadamat (regret). The khamira (leavened dough) of the Dahriyya (materialists)... the khamir of nadamat. That is taken and what is gained through it, its connection with the muhtaj (needy one) happens, and that is what they name qadim (ancient/eternal).

In the same way, as you are giving... so this is the... So these are the three types of nafs: namiyyah (vegetative), hissiyah (sensory), and natiqah (rational). The three nafs are for one person.

Now your question was, that it was about this… this… uh… Nasut-i-taba'i, Nasut-i-dhilli... This is a question… uh… that unless you understand all of it, it is not easy to understand.

So, Nasut-i-taba'i, what is that? Nasut-i-dhilli, what is that? Nasut-i-khass, what is that? And there is Nasut-i-kulli. And besides this, there are other things as well. Nufus (souls), their types, as we are understanding that our three nafs are namiyyah, hissiyah, and natiqah. There are three. According to our current knowledge, there are three. Meaning, if you do further study, or do some research, or read books, then there is a nafs-i-ilahiyyah (divine soul), there is a nafs-i-qudsiyyah (holy soul), and many others which are with the Imams or with the buzurgan-i-din (great ones of the faith). Those nufus are there. This is to be remembered. So we don't need that, that has nothing to do with us.

In any case, Nasut-i-taba'i... This Nasut, what is its meaning? This is a term in philosophy, it means the jismani kaifiyat (bodily state), the paikar (form). And Lahut is that which is not visible. Nasut is visible, Lahut is not visible. So the Imam, the Imam is visible, but Imamat is not visible. This is a simple thing to remember. Imamat is not visible, that's why it is connected to the suwar (forms). And this Nasut is the Imam who is visible, that's why his... he is Nasut, and the nafs... from it... is formed. This is the Rij'iyyah. So what is the Rij'iyyah? The Rij'iyyah is the three things you said just now: nafs-i-namiyyah, nafs-i-hissiyah, and nafs-i-natiqah. So where does Rij'iyyah come from in this? After the passing of a human and after he is buried, after three days, what happens to him is that after his death and after he goes into the grave, his nafs-i-rij'iyyah, this nafs-i-namiyyah, is called… baqaya-i-shar'iyyah (legal remnant). Baqaya-i-namiyyah (vegetative remnant). With the namiyyah, he is buried. And this is our biggest helplessness... that we think that after death, our body becomes dust to dust, that earth mixes with earth. It is not so. Because all of us sitting here are sinners, there are some flaws. So our entire nafs-i-namiyyah does not perish. The hissiyah (sensory soul) departs. For some, even the hissiyah does not depart. For some, both the namiyyah and the hissiyah depart. So for each, it is according to how they have lived their life, just as they find it, so it is. So after death, when they are put in the grave, at that time it has been told that the nafs... in the body... the connection with the nafs-i-namiyyah remains. This nafs-i-namiyyah undergoes tarqi (ascension/purification), it is purified. And how is it purified? Every higher thing pulls the lower thing. Or the lower thing is pulled towards the higher. So what does that mean? That the nafs-i-natiqah... see, the nafs-i-natiqah that we received at the time of the 'ahd (pledge), that "Brother, this is our madhhab (faith)," "This is..." "We have this belief," "This is our Imam-i-zaman..." These are all the beliefs we have, this is what will save us. And what does this do? That all the life we have lived, and we are praying `namaz`, doing all this, doing that, so we are doing it under that. So that is a sayiban (guardian) for us, that is the nafs-i-natiqah. It is not connected with our... with our body. The nafs is separate but it has a connection with the suwar. So this all, it influences our hissiyah. "Look brother, the time for `namaz` is here, get up." "Do that." So this, this is what happens. So all the life that passes in good a'mal (deeds) of ours, what happens later? At the time of death, the natiqah, it wants to pull the hissiyah along with it. That now I am not a permanent resident here, I am not a thing of this place. I am from the world of command (`alam-i-amr`). So now I will make the hissiyah like myself as well. So how much of it becomes like that? That is up to you. How you have lived your life, how you have prayed `namaz`, what it is. It slowly, slowly... the hissiyah... however much it becomes pure... Suppose you say... out of 100 parts, 50 parts have been pulled away. The remaining 50 parts are left behind. People who have bad habits, or have illnesses, or have bad habits, or talk about drinking things, or something... so how can their hissiyah be pure? So it gets left behind in the grave. Now what is the case with some? That those who have lived good... lives, their nafs-i-hissiyah gets pulled up. The namiyyah remains in the grave. The namiyyah is adna (lower). So just as the nafs-i-natiqah pulls the hissiyah, it tries to pull the namiyyah as well. Every higher one pulls the lower one. So how much does it pull? That is up to you. So what usually happens, it has been seen, in today's age or in the past ages, or in the time of our... that is, the time of the hudud, that is, that some of this namiyyah... the hissiyah departs in any case, but some of the namiyyah remains behind. Whether it is 25, 50, out of 100. How many, we don't know. That baqaya-i-namiyyah (remnant of the vegetative soul), that too has to make tarqi (ascend). But when? After undergoing saza (punishment). And what is the punishment? That he is put in the grave. A human who has become completely lifeless, if you bury him, that's fine. But he has a nafs-i-namiyyah in him, and you are burying him. Is it a matter of taklif (pain) or not? And this is what is called 'adhab-i-qabr (the torment of the grave). The torment of the grave is this very thing. That with it... the `namaz` of Wahshat al-Qubur (loneliness of the grave) that is prayed, or the talqin (instruction to the deceased) that is given, is for this very purpose. What is that? That only... for our, that is, for the mu'minin (believers), it is a great rahmah (mercy) from Allah Ta'ala that there is 'adhab (torment) for only three days. For three days, they are in the torment of the grave. And they are freed from it and depart. The remnant that was there, the remnant could have departed earlier as well. Now look at the... a janazah (funeral procession) that takes place, or whatever... so when it is taken for burial, some of the buzurgan-i-kiram (great ones) have said to lift from the feet. That is, go from the feet's side. And not to walk in front. When the janazah goes, don't walk in front. Because the Rij'iyyah is there. Our elders don't let us get close, "Hey, go back, go back, the children... go back." The janazah is going. So what happens? For the buzurgan-i-kiram, it departs at that very moment. It departs even before reaching there. But for some, after they are buried, a little baqaya-i-namiyyah remains. And when it departs after three days, its name is Rij'iyyah. And the Rij'iyyah becomes Nasut.

Now Nasut, its types were told just now. It has three types. There is taba'i, there is dhilli, and there is khass. These are the three main ones we have. So the taba'i Nasut that is formed... Nasut means what? The jism-i-Imam (body of the Imam). The body of the Imam has to be formed. So why does the body of the Imam have to be formed? Because the Imam has no body. The Imam is a nuri makhluq (luminous creation). He is just coming here to us, to free us, he is coming as our hadi (guide). He is a being of that place. So how will he come? When he is there, and they are nuri (luminous) beings, they are all in the 'alam al-arwah (world of spirits). They cannot come here. But it is also necessary for them to come. They cannot come, and it is also necessary for them to come. If they don't come, how will we find guidance? An Imam must be there, right? So how? So a rule was made by Allah Ta'ala that the asl paikar (original being) is there, that is, the asl muhtajib (original veiled one) is there, its hijab (veil) comes here. A partaw (reflection), a sayah (shadow) of it, comes into the world. And its name is hijab. And it is experienced. So the hijab, how will it be given a body? It has no body of its own. Where will it come from? The nufus of all the mu'minin, its body is formed from them. So what does that mean? That our nufus and their jism are of the same jawhar (substance). Our nafs, a mu'min's nafs, whether you consider it high or low... in comparison to the people of the world, our nafs is very good. And it becomes the Imam's body. So what is the relationship between us and the Imam? Our Rij'iyyat, our nufus, are their jism. That's why they say, "Kasayifuna lata'ifuhum" (Our crude things are their subtle things). Our crude things are their lata'if (subtle things). The crude things of the mu'min are their lata'if. The subtle things of those people are our jism. So it is the same...

Now Nasut-i-taba'i, Nasut-i-dhilli, Nasut-i-khass. The mu'minin are in India, in Pakistan, in Yemen, here, there, believers are everywhere. So are all believers pure? Pure means, are they completely... pious... in their form? No. There are those who follow the usul (principles), there are those who pray `namaz`, there are those who do tasbih (glorification), there are all kinds. Young, old, all are included. Now, in comparison to them, the hadarat (pure beings) who are with the Imam, the mu'minin who are there, they too will pass away. They are much better than us. Because they do not have fisad (corruption). We have fisad. Fisad means... that fisad came, you got a cold. You got a fisad, your nose is running. You got a fisad, you got an abscess. You got a fisad, your finger got cut. You got a fisad, your nose started bleeding. All these things that are with us are fisad. Fevers, habits, all these things, diseases, these are... They don't have anything there. They are free from fisadat. That's why they were born there. And in terms of darajat (ranks), it's not that they are higher in rank. Here, people can be much higher in rank. There are manasib (dignitaries), there are hudud (ranks), they are higher. But whether they are manasib or da'is, here, diseases occur. They are born there, so there are... Now, why is that? Because there is less connection with the world. One has to earn a living, do this and that, get called here and there. They just sit, eat, drink, pray `namaz`, do this, do that. So there is less attachment to the world. They become detached. When they have nothing to do with the world... So this is the world of fisadat, this is our world. And fisadat is a universal matter. That no one is free from it. A da'i is not free, an... Except for the Imam, among the hudud-i-din, whoever they are, they all have fisad. If there were no fisad, they wouldn't be born here. They would be born there. In hadarat. So the mu'minin who were born in hadarat, they are also there. So what happened now? There are two groups. I told you, right? Three. Three. So the mu'minin here... Now let's not categorize the mu'minin. Which mu'min is what, how many... he is a `mulla`, he is this... no. A mu'min. Because sometimes a `mulla` is not an asl mu'min (true believer). It's understandable. The mu'min-i-haqiqi (true believer) is one who... even after being this, to be a mu'min-i-kamil... there is a special darajah (degree) of iman (faith). You will say, "I have confirmed with the tongue, so it's done." But have you done it with your whole being? You haven't. So even after that, there are stages of iman. Anyway, for now, remember this, that all the mu'minin in the jaza'ir (islands), in the jazirah (peninsula), that is, India, Pakistan, Yemen, and all these places, our own relatives, they pass away, so their rij'iyyat are what become the Nasut-i-taba'i. Because Nasut-i-taba'i is the adna (lowest) Nasut of the Imam. And we are the lowest, from the jaza'ir. Now, the second group that is there... the afadil (virtuous ones) from here... Every mu'min and da'i is not at the same level. There is a da'i, there are manasib, there are hudud, there are those who are attached to the hudud. Now, someone whose rank is not that of a bab, but is a hujjah... or those who are of a higher rank, they and the mu'minin from there... where? From the hadarat. They form the Nasut-i-dhilli. Nasut-i-dhilli. Dhill means shadow. And the third is, the du'at from there... The da'is, manasib, and hudud from here who are of a higher rank, whom we think are... and the mu'minin from there. This is the Nasut-i-dhilli. It can be back and forth. A mu'min from there can also come, who is very perfect. He is not a `mulla` at all. And the third is the Nasut-i-khass, which is the afadil who are there in the hadarat. There are 12 da'is, right? In that, there are 4 hudud-i-da'iyyah. And there are also hudud-i-qudsani there. There are many. As Sayyidna Dhari used to say, there are thousands of my... it comes to my mind... mu'minin there. Thousands. It's not that there are few. And very pure, like that. No. So this third category is the Nasut-i-khass. Which is very high.

Now this Nasut is the Imam's qaida (base). The one formed from us is the Imam's khitta (part). That is the Nasut-i-taba'i. That is the very taba'i that we see. The Imam we meet, in Kufa, in Madina, this and that... Imam Husayn is coming and going. All of this... I am telling you in a summarized way, its details are many. This is, these are what? They are the Nasut-i-taba'i. The Nasut-i-dhilli is not visible. It is formed from higher-ranking people. And the ones there who are... mu'minin, they are free from fisadat. So it's Nasut-i-dhilli. That Nasut-i-dhilli is controlled by the Imam's mother. Every Imam's mother is the holder, or she controls it. So you have to remember, every Imam's mother is the one who controls the Nasut-i-dhilli. Because the wife of one Imam is the mother of the next Imam. This is the rule.

The third is the Nasut-i-khass. Which is very high. Sayyidna Hasan 'Ali used to say that its imtihan (test) doesn't even happen in the world. We can neither perceive it nor... just what can be... So let's leave aside the Nasut-i-khass. The Nasut-i-dhilli is not visible to us. The Imam's mother has a connection with it, when it has to be, the connection happens, that is a special matter. The Nasut-i-taba'i is the main thing. Taba'i means natural. The natural... Now, that Nasut-i-taba'i also has types. What is in it? Because the Nasut-i-taba'i is that which... the `rij'iyyat` of the mu'minin, formed from them... So that too is... just as the Imam is, so it is. Like Mawla 'Ali is, like Mawlana Muhammad ibn Isma'il is, like the other... whatever... جتنے بھی جتنے جو عقید... वो इतना ऊंचा उनका जो है, नासूत-ए-तबई बनता है, कि जो है, हमको दिखाई देने के काबिल नहीं होता। So that Nasut-i-taba'i is also of such a high level that it is not visible to us. The believers of the jaza'ir, Makkah, Madina, who are... there are very good believers there... so theirs is not visible. And if it has to be seen, then what to do? So they take on hijabat (veils), degrees. They wear them. And they take one hijab. So that by taking it, they become visible to the eyes of the one in front. Meaning, they come to eye level. If not, then another... degree is taken down. So this time, I am going into a lot of detail, but I'll... summarize it. That the Nasut-i-taba'i is... of Sayyidna 'Ali was... higher than the Nasut-i-khass of other Imams. Nasut-i-khass. Nasut-i... of Mawla 'Ali was that high. Nasut-i... So you are seeing him? How is he being seen? So the Nasut-i-taba'i that he is speaking with... the Nasut-i-taba'i... one Ayah is being recited, it's going on. Every person, every mu'min, is hearing all the private matters. He's not there. Rather, Sayyidna 'Ali, in the morning, went out on a tour and said, "I prayed the Fajr `namaz` in Madina, behind this one." He goes to another city, he says, "I prayed the Fajr `namaz` behind that one." A third city... five men standing in the same place said, "We prayed behind 'Ali." So it was just to show his station, "Look, how many hijabs I can be in." The Imam has one thousand hijabs. He has one thousand hijabs. He doesn't have them. But he has the power to take on one thousand hijabs. And this... the prophets, from our own understanding, from our own studies, from that, it is that... the prophets, the anbiya', they have three hijabs that are main. Main means, they are generally there. Prophets have... Ali has... these... So those who have a Hijab-e-Hijab-e-Tanasul. And then, there are other types of hijabs as well. Are you understanding? So Nasut-i-taba'i... Nasut-i-taba'i is like Sayyidna 'Ali's. Since you're not able to see him... you are a king of the whole world... that your Nasut is so high that you are not capable of being seen. So what should it be like? So one... the first veil of tanasul (procreation) was taken. Tanasul, from generation. That through wives and children you spend your life, that is one veil of tanasul. That tanasul is also so high that it is not visible. So another veil was taken. That veil is also high... not visible. So then a third veil was taken. So the one who was seen in Kufa, the one who was seen, was the Hijab-e-Hijab-e-Tanasul. Not taba'i, not dhilli, not khass. It's not that. So they had to lower themselves this much so that people could receive guidance, could do... What do you think, that the... [unclear] hello? Yes. It's that Mawlana 'Ali's... was the Hijab-e-Hijab-e-Tanasul. And there is a book of hijabs, which is Sayyidna 'Ali ibn Dhiyab's, it says where the hijabs are, what they are, since when they were, when they came into this world, and what is the Hijab-e-Muhtajib, what is the muhtajib (the veiled one), what is the muhtajib's work, all these things. Muhtajib means the one who is your asl (origin). Here you came as 'Ali Murtada. But there you are the 'Ayn-i-'Adhimah. 'Ayn, they say, from 'Ali, it is 'ayn. And we... sometimes we explain it by saying 'ayn means it will be understood from this. Mim means the Prophet's name will be understood from that. So the 'Ayn-i-'Adhimah is... that is the being there, and his partaw (reflection) that came here is 'Ali Murtada. And 'Ali Murtada was also so high that he had to take on hijabs. Some were called Abu Turab, some were called Mustafa, some were Abu Turab, many of your names, the titles you have, Abul-Hasan... these are all within the hijabs. And even the Prophet's. Muddaththir is separate, Muzzammil is separate, Taha is separate, Yasin is separate... all... as Sayyidna Ja'far used to say, these are all hijabs. So anyway, this is one issue, so I told you that there are three... uh... Nasuts and there are three... types of each. And besides this, there is one more Nasut, its... to go into its details is not necessary... Nasut-i-kulli. Nasut-i-kulli is... it is not for everyone. Among the Imams, those who are of a very high degree, for them... that is, the khulasa (essence) of 10-12 Imams, when it comes out, it is given to that great Imam. And it is called kulli.

So sir, this Lahut which is not visible...

So the ruh of the Imam is... And it is formed from our suwar. So that... the Imamat... No, Lahut is the asl paikar (original form). Our suwar ascend and become Lahut. They don't... it's not that our ruh goes up. So one Rij'iyyah is one paikar of an Imam. And the Imam is a separate thing, Imamat is a separate matter. Mawlana Ja'far al-Sadiq... was the son of his father. But until nass (designation) happened to him, you couldn't consider him an Imam. He remained a son. Like other... there are many. 'Ali Akbar, 'Ali Asghar... are they Imams? We say Imam Asghar, Imam... but that is out of respect. They are not Imams. The Imam is only Mawlana Zayn al-'Abidin. So the one who receives nass, that attachment happens. So this suwar that we have... as I explained, this Rij'iyyah, its parts depart from the body and after being buried in the grave, after three days, they depart. And after departing, where do they go? To the qamar (moon). From the qamar, to Zuhal (Saturn), from Zuhal to Zuhra (Venus), from Zuhra to Shams (Sun), from Shams to Mushtari (Jupiter), from Mushtari to Mirrikh (Mars), and after that, it goes to the qalam (pen). After the qalam, it goes to the kamil (perfect). There it stays for a period. Until the Imam desires that "Now that son of mine should be born, who is to be the Imam." There were many sons. Mawlana 'Ali had several sons, Mawlana 'Abd al-Muttalib had several sons. But the son who is fit to be the Imam, he is the one whose time is to come. So according to that, a... a movement starts, that from the moon... all the Rij'iyyat gather. From all over the world. Now, our world is Yaman, Sindh, Hind, it has become very small. Because we don't even know if there are mu'minin in other places. But if there are mu'minin in the 12 jaza'ir (islands), then there are many Rij'iyyat. And they stay there. And when the Imam decides that "Now that son of mine should be born, who is to be the Imam," a movement occurs in the higher realms. From where? A command comes from 'alam al-amr (world of command), a movement occurs in 'alam al-hayat (world of life), and then, coming here, a movement occurs in this moon. And that... those... namiyyah, its parts, in the form of water or in the form of juice, these are the two things, they enter into a pure fruit. The three fruits, right? Grapes, pomegranate, and apple. The fruits of Paradise. They permeate into them, and he himself eats them and gives them to the Imam's wife to eat. So that apple is not just an apple. It is a good thing. Now you will say, "Hey, it's just a thing, so why...?" Just as for a sick person, you bring juice, so you bring juice in a glass, the glass should also be good. So in the same way, there, that thing... which is the apple, it is the container, like a container. The thing permeates into it. And the Imam eats it, specially. And then after that... his wife eats it. And from the union of both, that Imam is then conceived. So their conception is also completely different. Not every son is born this way. But this Imam who is to be born, his chemistry and his physics are different. And this is how he is conceived. Then after that, there are other matters. For the duration of the pregnancy, his wife keeps receiving madad (sustenance) from there. And she... for nine months, so that after that the child is born. So this is... of whose? Of our... uh... Rij'iyyat. But the suwar, this thing, the original concept is that we are doing this, these activities, praying `namaz`, listening, doing, all this is under our hissiyah. But our natiqah, under which is our 'aqidah (belief), or our tasawwur (conception)... the tasawwur of all is... that tasawwur we are taking and going. And when death occurs, whatever our mind has worked on, our tasawwur, that... after death, it becomes our hadd-i-'ali (higher rank). A suwar-i-ruhaniyyah (spiritual form) is created. I am not going into detail, there are many things in it. A suwar is a... a suwar is just an appearance, a form that is created. And a suwar can be of two types. One type is suwar-i-'amali (form of deeds), one is suwar-i-'ilmi (form of knowledge). Now I am not getting into their types. When is the suwar-i-'amali created? When is the suwar-i-'ilmi created? And how does it get nourishment? But... that's a detail. But it is that both things... if you are only praying `namaz` and doing... and you don't know what the reward is. Or you don't want to know what the Imam is. Some are like... one is that he wants to know a lot. That I should know everything, do this, do that... but he doesn't pray `namaz`. So the outward and the inward, both things must be there. Action and knowledge, both must be there. So to study and to learn. When this happens, both are the wings for flight. For flying. And with that, the suwar-i-'ilmi is also formed and the suwar-i-'amali is also formed. It goes and connects with your... now the Imam has... the entire... their count is with the Imam. `Ind Allahi Ilm`. He has a special register, that "You travel in a plane, wherever you go, or stay at work, wherever you are, but your seat with the Imam is what?" What number is it? The Imam knows it. We say, "It's with Allah." Allah has made the Imam-i-zaman the... he is the controller. So your number is 24. So there is one below you, 23. And 25 is above you. So you are in the hadd-i-'ali (higher rank) of the one who is lower than you. And you are the hadd-i-adna (lower rank) of the one who is above you. So for everyone, hadd-i-'ali, hadd-i-adna, hadd-i-'ali, hadd-i... it keeps going. All the way to the top. And this is the system. This is what is most disliked by the Wahhabis, the hadd-i-'ali, hadd-i... That one is the hadd-i-'ali of another. You don't even know. You are sitting here, and your hadd-i-'ali is in Yemen, or it is in... That someone is lower than you, whether in the `mufid` ranks, or among the `bab` ranks, or among the `du'at` ranks, or we don't know where. So what happens is that this hadd-i-'ali, hadd-i-adna... so hadd-i-'ali... it goes on. When your death occurs, your... nafs-i-namiyyah and nafs-i-hissiyah are left behind. The nafs-i-namiyyah becomes Rij'iyyah. Or the hissiyah also joins it. Hissiyah joins the natiqah and it departs. It becomes pure. Plus your a'mal (deeds). `Namaz`, `roza`, `hajj`, `zakat`, all that you did, charity you gave, good character you displayed... all these things become one... a thing is formed. Its name is suwar. And this suwar goes to our hadd-i-'ali. Whoever it is, you don't need to know. Nor do you need to know. You should know that I have a hadd-i-'ali and a hadd-i-adna. And there is no distinction between men and women in this. Anyone can be. The hadd-i-'ali of a da'i can be a woman. There are so many high-ranking ones. So now what is it? That they have reached there. To the hadd-i-... So he too has a nafs. Who? The hadd-i-'ali. And he is alive. Your death has happened. You are finished. You are gone. Your suwar-i-ruhani has been created. Now what will happen with his nafs? He too has a suwar. Which is higher than you. So the suwar of the hadd-i-'ali, your suwar goes and joins his suwar. It becomes double. So what happens? 1 + 1 happens. So does it stay there permanently? No, the suwar joins. The nafs becomes its mujawir (neighbor). The nafs has a chance of getting corrupted. The suwar doesn't. Once the suwar becomes good and your death occurs, you go and join them. And that... it keeps going up. But its nafs can get corrupted. So this nafs is its mujawir, mujawir means it stays in the neighborhood. But with the suwar, it becomes mutajawiz (intertwined). Mutajawiz, like... isthimad ہوتا ہے, to meet happens, like that. So that stays until his death. Mujawir. If his death also happens with a good end, then their suwar and your suwar join and go to a third one. From the third to the fourth. From the fourth... Now, you don't even know where it is going, where it is going. And it goes on and on, the one who is the great one of the jazirah (peninsula), it goes up to him. These are stations. It also happens in the mawaqif (stations). There is also an Imam in the mawaqif. That's why their importance increases. But there, it's on a smaller scale. From there, one mufid of the jazirah, the great ones of the jazirah, it is necessary to go to them. What comes to them? Your thing. Your milkiyyat (possession). It goes to them, that's why they are called malik (owner). The owners of the jazirah. That our possessions are with them. And then they go... the great ones of the jazirah, they go and join the da'i. So who became the asl malik (original owner)? That's why they are called Malik-i-Jami'. They are the owners of everything. Our... from there, the chain goes up. So we don't need to think that much about it. It goes to the hudud, from the hudud to the suwar, from there to the du'at, all this... there are many stages. And after that, there is the Bab al-Abwab. Bab (door), is the door to the suwar. The first bab, the second bab, the third bab, there is Lahat, there is Bath, there is Musalsal, there is Indamaji, there are four types of abwab. These four types of abwab, after passing through them... And Bab al-Abwab is the door of all doors. You have many doors, this door is the main one. Close this, and the whole house is closed. Open this, and everything is open. So Bab al-Abwab is... the bab is Bab al-Abwab. And with him... these things reach. Whose? The suwarat of the 12 jaza'ir. That's why their... rank is so high, and their power is... that... the one who is with the da'i, the one who is with the manasib, and the one who is with the bab, how high does it become? That the suwarat of the entire jaza'ir are gathering with him. What power he would have. He is called Fasl al-Khitab (the decisive speech). Bab al-Abwab is Fasl al-Khitab. That whatever comes out of his mouth, it happens. When the Bab al-Abwab has this state, what is the state of the Imam? The Bab al-Abwab has been established by the Imam. So it is... Bab al-Abwab... The Bab al-Abwab collects... that... in three jaza'ir... Yaman, Sindh, Hind, these are the da'is. Then three jaza'ir's are taken. Then three jaza'ir's... that is, there should be four da'is and 12 jaza'ir. The things of the 12 jaza'ir are collected. They are collected and reach the Bab al-Abwab. Now he has the authority. What thing? The suwar-i-ruhani. The namiyyah is separate, the Rij'iyyah is separate... it's with the Imam. This suwar is formed. Suwar... with the Bab al-Abwab. Now, when it is said that "Now the Imam will go to the dairah (circle)," that the suwar stays with them, at their... that is, the suwar is formed. The suwar becomes one. Suwar is singular, suwar are plural, as in majmu'a (collection). It goes and the suwar becomes one with him. And after that, with the Bab al... Now, he stays there. Until when? Until the Imam declares that "Now my son... will become the Imam." The Imam has been born. The son has been born. And after 10 years, 20 years, 25 years... he has to be given nass. There is no specific age for them. It can happen anytime. Mawlana Tayyib's was 4 years. So now, when the Imam's time to go is appointed, then he will go. Meaning, both are lazim o malzum (inseparable). That you have made the son, when it is necessary for your own departure. At that very time, the transfer happens. You will find that it takes one to one and a half minutes. Death occurs. So he... establishes the Imam. He gives nass, which is something visible... it's a thing in front... but to hand over the trust... to hand over what? To hand over the Imamat. A son is... Mawlana Ja'far Sadiq are there, Mawlana Zayn al-'Abidin are born, now Imam Husayn has to hand it over to them. So what is he handing over? The suwarat of the entire 12 jaza'ir are with the Bab al-Abwab. He has to take it from the Bab al-Abwab first. So as soon as he took it from the Bab al-Abwab... the Bab al-Abwab's departure is necessary. Because his duty is over. The thing he had to give, he gave. Finished. So the suwar of the Bab al-Abwab no longer remains. And the Bab al-Abwab's death happens at the very last moment, because the entire jaza'ir is supported by him. He is the biggest authority. So now what happens? That Nasut is not, or Lahut is... remember this, that its form is like our human one. That is, it's not that Nasut is... Imamat and... its form is... Lahut is also completely human. Human form means invisible. Hands, feet, all things are there. So all those things, your... your... are against the feet, they are against the hands, they are against this... the feet are against the feet, the hands are against the hands, the hair is against the hair, the nails are against the nails... all are separate. After they are collected, they become one. But the Bab al-Abwab is the biggest authority, he is against the qalb (heart). Now those places are empty. The whole haykal, what they call haykal... haykal, Lahut, Imam, all three are one. So what is Imamat, what is haykal, what is... So we say haykal. Why do we say haykal? Haykal means a big... a very big thing. Structure. A big... So that thing, from the Bab al-Abwab... the Imam says, "Now I will give it to my son." The shehzada (prince), tomorrow he will become the badshah (king). I am giving it. So he takes it from the Bab al-Abwab and gives it. As soon as he gives it... and as soon as he takes it from the Bab al-Abwab, his departure happens. Departure means he himself goes and sits against the qalb. And the whole jism (body) becomes complete. It was not complete. And what does the Imam do? Seeing that, he gives it to his son. That is to do nass. Just as Imam... Husayn, what happened in the end? In the tent, Mawlana Zayn al-'Abidin... the spear was brought... he said, "Oh nephew, you will be the one through whom my lineage will continue. Why are you coming here?" "Stay back," he said. "Oh 'Ali, you stay back." And after that, he handed over his weapons. You have... many things, he gave nasihat (advice). What was the nasihat? He was doing nass. That... he handed over the asar-i-imamat (relics of Imamat). He gave it all to him and... he passed away. So after that, within one to one and a half minutes, the father's departure is necessary. Because as soon as the Imam is made, a shehzada has become a badshah. So what will the badshah do? He has to step down, right? So he immediately steps down. So he is called muqim. Muqim-i-Imam. Meaning, the one who establishes. The one who establishes the Imam. He has his own tarqi (ascension). His jawar-i-rahmat (proximity to mercy) is a separate station, a separate way he goes. And one Imam, two Imams, three Imams, four Imams, this is all a chain. Six Imams pass. The seventh who comes, he will be sab'awi (related to the number seven). And as soon as the seven are complete, he collects all six. This is the chain. You should know this much.

Yes. This Bab al-Abwab's khalq (creation) comes into the haykal. So the coming Imam's khalq... becomes the Imam's haykal. The khalq of the Imam's haykal, the khalq becomes... becomes the haykal. Yes, yes. And there are many subtleties in it, that one Imam's departure happens, so where does his khalq go? His things are collected. Imamat... Mawlana Sulaiman also says it, his khalq is also there and it is also in the body of his father. There are many things. Now, he is at a higher stage. It won't be easy to understand. There are many things. One Imam's departure happens, so his... things, are divided into five parts. And they go to different places. To the coming Imam, to the... some things go to the heavens, some things... remain with the mu'minin. Where, where it is... there are several parts to it. That's outside of our... stage. What I was explaining was that...

This is the `mas'alah` of our `i'tiqad` (belief). That, al-hamdu lillahi rabb il-'alamin (praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds). Praise is for Allah alone, who is the rabb (Lord) of the 'alamin (worlds). Rabb al-'alamin. Then what? He is Ar-Rahman (the Most Gracious), who is Rahman and also Rahim (the Most Merciful). Then Malik-i-Yawm al-Din. He is the master of the Yawm al-Din (Day of Judgment), that is, of Qiyamah (Resurrection). This whole thing has come from the `madhhab`. And after that, what is there? Iyyaka na'budu (You alone we worship). We worship only You. Wa iyyaka nasta'in (and You alone we ask for help). And we seek help only from You. Ihdina al-sirat al-mustaqim (Guide us to the straight path). Oh Allah, guide us to the straight path. Sirat alladhina... that path... whose path? An'amta 'alayhim (upon whom You have bestowed favor). Those on whom You have bestowed Your favor, Allah has. They are the mu'minin. The an'amta 'alayhim are the mu'minin, they are the nabi'in (prophets). Ghayr al-maghdubi wa al-dallin (not of those who have evoked [Your] anger or of those who are astray). Not of the maghdub (those who have earned anger), and not of the dallin (those who are astray). The dallin are the Jews and the Christians and all these others, who believe in Allah, believe in oneness, but they don't have the correct belief, they are dallin. And ghayr al-maghdub are the mushrikin (polytheists). Those who are completely atheists or don't believe in Allah. To them... The whole surah is that...

Someone gave me a Farsi `risalah` (treatise). It was an old Shia book on medicine. Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq's, Imam Baqir's... for this disease, this... but what was written in it was that one... one such person was there who... Musa Kazim, their Imam, Musa Kazim... but he quoted a Farsi ayah. For traveling. So... can we follow such a thing? Because he quoted a Farsi ayah, but the one from whose mouth it came out, he is not... correct. I don't understand that.

Yes, there is. It's difficult. Because whether it is Musa Kazim or other Imams, Imam Taqi... their... read the history, read the Tibb-i-Ma'sumin (Medicine of the Infallibles). In that, Mawlana Ja'far al-Sadiq's and Mawlana Baqir's are many. The vegetables and fruits and such things of that time... how to get benefit from them. Those are correct. Now about them, Imam Taqi, Naqi, they are all in their progeny. So many things have come from their forefathers. So some things are correct, some are not. If you want to believe, believe. But these are things of medicine... you are giving them to doctors, giving them to others, consulting with Hindus, what's wrong with taking their things? But with the belief that this is... it doesn't align with us. And yoga... What's wrong with doing yoga? There's no harm in it at all. See, the mind is exercised and the body is exercised. The body also needs to be kept active. It has to be done. So what's wrong with it? Many lectures... if I give a lecture, you will go to sleep. But... 12 of you are ready. For me, it's not. So it is that... see, 'ilm (knowledge) is like water. Now see, a ta'wil (interpretation) is coming out. 'Ilm is like water. The properties that water has, 'ilm has. All of them. As it has been told in the `dawr` (cycle)... there is no contradiction in it at all. So water always comes from top to bottom. 'Ilm also always comes from top to bottom. From a lower place to a higher place, it never goes. From higher to lower. From top to bottom. And it comes to the heart of the `mu'min`. If we want to take water from bottom to top, we do it by force. That is, by unnatural means we take it up. That is, by force. So it is the same way, you, the `jumhur` (general populace), say, "Brother, you are a `mulla`, this is your speech..." You have no right. The 'ilm from the lower is not given to the higher. From higher to lower. This is the way of the `dawr`. Then the one who is the man, who has the 'ilm, he will give it to the ones below him. So this chain, this is the way of the `dawr`. Now see the parallel in this. I always give this example. The Prophet. The Prophet is the founder of the whole of Islam. Your `da'wat` is also his, all the `shari'ah` (law) is brought by him. So the 'ilm of the `shari'ah` is a separate thing, the 'ilm of `ta'wil` is a separate thing, and the 'ilm of `haqa'iq` (realities) is a separate thing. The Prophet did not do `ta'wil`. He brought only `haqa'iq`, that is, he brought the `shari'ah`. Tanzil (revelation). Now see, there is a special term we have, Tanzil. Tanzil means... the Qur'an Sharif was revealed upon your qalb (heart). But you did not do the work of explaining it. So what happened then? The Prophet is the master of Tanzil, the master of `ta'wil` is Mawlana 'Ali. Whatever he learned, he learned from 'Ali. The Qur'an Sharif came, `Bismillah`... "I have heard it from you." This is the greatest blessing. That no one could bear it. The mountains would have crumbled, if the Qur'an was revealed upon the qalb... if it had been revealed upon a prophet other than the Prophet, or upon someone else, the mountains would have crumbled. Who were the mountains? They were Salman, they were Miqdad, they were 'Ammar... the qalb of none of them had the power to bear the prophet. So the prophet... Now the prophet is such a mashrab (source/fountain). Mashrab means a place to drink, a place to drink water... so that he is wasi' (vast). See, he is like the whole sea. He is like the ocean. The Prophet has been compared to the ocean. The Prophet is an ocean of 'ilm. That is, he is wasi' and he is deep. Now in that, who will come to drink water? Animals, birds, all come to drink. And who were the Prophet? Not just for the mu'minin. He is the nas... he is the Rahmatun lil-'alamin (mercy to the worlds). He has come as a mercy for the worlds. Not just for the mu'minin, or for the Muslims... for the whole of humanity he has come as a mercy. So this is the explanation. Now the water, what kind of water is it, of the ocean? It is salty water. It is not sweet water. So the salty water, the hadiths, this and that... you read the hadith, you can read it. It is an English book... there is... but its explanation, what is its... its explanation, one is a superficial one... there is a deeper one. A very... its... behind it is a lot of meaning. A lot of... there are subtleties in it. For example, `b` is `ali`. So its meaning will be told. The hadith has many such things that are beyond your understanding. In writing, it is such that... the prophet explained it in everyday language. But it is very deep. So its `haqa'iq`, what Sayyidna Hasan and Husayn say... so we don't have a connection with them. Sayyidna Hasan and... so it is that the prophet is like the ocean. And our Imam, 'Ali, peace be upon him... Mawlana 'Ali... he is like a well. He is like a well. From a well... you can't go and drink water. You have to work hard to draw it out. To draw it out with a `dol` (bucket). So the `du'at`... I was about 55 years old when I read this. Mulla Muhammad Ali... that is, in '52, '53 I read it. So what did they write, Sayyidna Nizar, that a `dol` is tied and water is drawn out. If someone has to drink water, a `dol` is tied. How much comes in a `dol`? Several gallons of water come. So the `dol` is... Abu Mus'ab, and Bab al-Abwab, and others... are the `dol`. From there, you don't drink the water from the `dol` either. Rather, what do they do? They put it in big vessels. They are called Awani-i-Kabirah. Awani means vessel. Big vessels. From big vessels, to small vessels. A big vessel is like a `lagan` (large basin). You can't drink from that either. So to smaller vessels. From smaller vessels to even smaller ones, until it comes to your tank, comes to the `surahi` (earthen pot), comes to the glass, and then you get it. So these things, so what happens is that the natural way for a person to drink water is not like this. Water is taken... in the villages, you see, they are like this. Here... culture has increased so much that... from the tap, in the glass... just from how many paths... how many mediums have come? So they are all hadd-i-'ali. At various places... it passes through Mawlana Husayn's, then it is read by the `mufid`, then the `da'i`, then... it goes through this, this, this, and comes to you, these two hands. And these two hands are your `ma'dhun` and your `mukasir`. A `ma'dhun` who is a `mansus` (designated) `ma'dhun`. He comes from the right hand. And those who are of a lower rank, they come from the left hand. It is from these two hands that you get the `da'wat`'s nourishment. So, `mukasir`... and not `mufid`. So `mufid` is not there. And you don't have that much... so `ma'dhun` `mukasir`, it has been told... Now see, we do the whole `wudu` (ablution). Whether it is `masah` of the ears, or `masah` of the nose, it is done with these two palms. Is it or not? It is done with two palms. The whole... `masah` of the head is happening, this is happening, that... so each thing, in its explanation, in its `ta'wil`, `haqa'iq` have been explained, and `tanazil` has been explained. That what do they mean? Why is `masah` of the nose... water is put into the nose, what does it mean? `Masah` of the head... Now `masah` is separate, washing is separate. "wa-ghsilu wujuhakum wa aydiyakum" (and wash your faces and your hands) "wa-msahu bi-ru'usikum wa arjulakum" (and wipe over your heads and your feet). Two things are for `masah`, two things are... we do how much `wudu`? Seven parts. Four are primary. So the four things are, two are `masah` and two are washing. A command from Allah Ta'ala. Later, the `du'at`, the Imams, have added... `masah` of the ears, of the nose, these are... so they are... Now the things for `masah`, what are they? They are the head and the feet. In `masah`, less water is used. In washing, more water is used. So the head, from the front to the back, is `masah`. `Masah`... from the front. Yes. So there are two `masah`s and two washings. In `masah`, less 'ilm is there. Now see, I am going into a bit of detail. The Qur'an Sharif is there, so that is from our Imam's time, that the Qur'an Sharif is on the qalb of the Prophet. That... the qalam, the first that was made... the qalam... So, it is that... there is a small thing. It is given by one who is the creator, Rabb al-Sudur. So he gives the authority, that is our qalam. So from the qalb of your Prophet... it came out from there. It became a circle. All the books of the world, that is... the divine books, Zubur, Torah, Injil, they came out from where? Their source is the qalb of the Prophet. But the Qur'an Sharif is the only thing that came out from the qalb of the Prophet. This... there is a saying of Sayyidna Ja'far that was revealed just now... they don't even tell it. Now it has... the `dawr` is... the Prophet's saying is... that is the qalb of the Prophet. That is `da'ira-i-wahid`. `Da'ira-i-wahid`... from that, a single qalb of the Prophet. Yes, but there is no circle there. The circle starts later. So what is the significance? That the Prophet is the only one... the Qur'an Sharif has been revealed upon him. Now see, I am telling you a couple of things that are not commonly... so that you understand. That the anwar-i-dhikriyyah (lights of remembrance) were revealed upon the qalb of the Prophet. Anwar-i-dhikriyyah is also a name for the Qur'an Sharif. Anwar-i-dhikriyyah. The anwar (lights) of dhikr (remembrance). That is, of what is repeated, or what is always said... anwar-i-dhikriyyah. Now these anwar-i-dhikriyyah were revealed on the qalb of the Prophet. So what did the Prophet become? A dhikr. The anwar were revealed on the qalb of the Prophet, so you became a dhikr. Did you or not? You became a dhikr. Now there is a famous verse here, that... what is it? "fas'alu ahl al-dhikr in kuntum la ta'lamun" (So ask the People of Remembrance if you do not know). "You ask the ahl al-dhikr (people of remembrance) if you do not know something." So now people have been searching till today, who are the ahl al-dhikr? So I am saying this, that when the Prophet became a dhikr... when the Prophet became a dhikr, then the ahl al-dhikr, who are they, the Ahl al-Bayt (people of the house), or not? The Ahl al-Bayt are the ahl al-dhikr. So "fas'alu ahl al-dhikr in kuntum la ta'lamun." You ask the ahl al-dhikr if you do not know. A couple of such things I have collected so that... people can... to make them understand. And the other things are, as your father has said... there are... their books are more than ours, we have less. There are... `ta'wil`'s... when the division happened, at that time there was a lot of knowledge, and a lot... the books that were there in today's time, the books that are there... `hakayiq` are there, `ta'wilat` are there... So we have categorized them, that `ta'wil` is what, `hakayiq` is what. `Hay` is for `haqa'iq`. `To` is for `ta'wil`. `Shin` is for `shari'ah`. `Sin` is for `siyar`. `Kaf` is for `kuzh`. `Alif` is for `hizin`. These books. And then there is the period, that whether it is from the time of the Qaimiyyah, that is, from the time of Sayyidna 'Imad, or is it from the time of Sayyidna Tayyib al-Dawr. If it is from the Tayyibiyyah `dawr`, then they write `To-il`. So that we know that this is from the Tayyibiyyah period. So this is... they are categorized. You take out any book, by looking at the book I can tell you that this is... because now there is a lot going on. The number of `to-il` books is very large. `Hay` is less. `Haqa'iq`... of Tayyib is... `hay-to-il`. `Hay` is written. And if it is only `hay`, then you will understand it is... as if... Sayyidna Dhari... Sijina... Ra'ani... these... their books are there. So they write `hay` for `haqa'iq`. `To-il` for `ta'wil`. `Hay` for `haqa'iq` in the Tayyibiyyah period. Hay. So, the books that are stolen, or the `firqah` divided, they were seized, we didn't get them. They got a lot. They were seized. A lot of such... the `haqa'iq-i-tayyibiyyah` books are many, and `hay-to-il`'s books... `hay-kat-ki` a book... Sayyidna 'Imad's, there is only one book, `hay-kat`. And `hay-kat`, if I read it, I get a headache. Sayyidna 'Ali was... Asrar-i-Hayat... there are many books. So it is that there are many books of the Tayyibiyyah period.
